project.status: source version 1.1.0; Atari STE/Mega STE conversion with joystick-only flight controls
project.notes: Identity: Reverse-engineered reimplementation of Brøderbund’s 1990 Amiga Wings of Fury for Atari STE/Mega STE. A substantial C++ game implements original flight model, enemies, weapons, all 15 maps, front end, saved games and drawing on AGT, with Amiga-format decoders and conversion scripts plus 68k disassembly/decompilation research. Classification: Inspected actual ~7400-line native game source with fixed 12.5Hz original-model logic, original-address table references and MiNT/AGT hardware integration. Fifty-one recorded input test flights documented. MIT covers conversion’s own code/tools/tests/docs; original Brøderbund assets/program, derived graphics and AGT diff excluded. Repository contains original/derived game materials; no blanket open-license claim. Source CPU: Amiga original 68000 program, assets and disassembly are inputs. Target CPU: Atari STE/Mega STE native m68k output; macOS/Linux build hosts kept separate. Build: Needs patched AGT master a155d41, m68k-atari-mint GCC4.6.4/binutils/MiNTLib, Python/Pillow, make and shell; release scripts generate floppy/hard-disk packages. No build performed; all build/runtime/byte-exact flags remain unknown. No candidate software was compiled or executed; build/run/play/byte-identity flags remain unknown. Runtime profiles: Upstream states STE/Mega STE, 2MB+, 50Hz colour monitor, floppy or hard disk. Source/reported tests inspected only, no independent play. AI: README says conversion code written by Claude in Claude Code; pinned commit contains Claude Opus 5.5 co-author trailer. Relationships: Uses dml’s Atari Game Tools with repository-local patch; derived from Amiga version, not Apple II source lineage. Evidence: https://github.com/theimann/wings-of-fury-atari-ste/blob/c6fd48298109b5148dd4837aadb0e78082cbc2a7/README.md https://github.com/theimann/wings-of-fury-atari-ste/blob/c6fd48298109b5148dd4837aadb0e78082cbc2a7/game/wof.cpp https://github.com/theimann/wings-of-fury-atari-ste/blob/c6fd48298109b5148dd4837aadb0e78082cbc2a7/game/Makefile https://github.com/theimann/wings-of-fury-atari-ste/blob/c6fd48298109b5148dd4837aadb0e78082cbc2a7/docs/BUILDING.md https://github.com/theimann/wings-of-fury-atari-ste/blob/c6fd48298109b5148dd4837aadb0e78082cbc2a7/reverse-engineering/notes/player.md https://github.com/theimann/wings-of-fury-atari-ste/blob/c6fd48298109b5148dd4837aadb0e78082cbc2a7/tools/hunk.py https://github.com/theimann/wings-of-fury-atari-ste/blob/c6fd48298109b5148dd4837aadb0e78082cbc2a7/tools/iff.py https://github.com/theimann/wings-of-fury-atari-ste/blob/c6fd48298109b5148dd4837aadb0e78082cbc2a7/LICENSE https://github.com/theimann/wings-of-fury-atari-ste/commit/c6fd48298109b5148dd4837aadb0e78082cbc2a7 Source version 1.1.0 changes flight to joystick-only because Atari ST keyboard handling drops some three-key combinations; deck menus, takeoff and restart retain keyboard controls, and a Mega STE Ctrl+Q path is fixed. The README explicitly requires Atari STE or Mega STE, at least 2 MiB, a 50 Hz colour display, joystick port 1 and floppy or hard disk. Version 1.1.0 is recorded as source state rather than a published GitHub release because no matching release was available when checked. Evidence: https://github.com/theimann/wings-of-fury-atari-ste/commit/dbe8a3a63863b16952905c0410ded3ab00465f5d https://github.com/theimann/wings-of-fury-atari-ste/commit/9390713ecd21e191e6e6ef67c2e06f5f6f732f0b https://github.com/theimann/wings-of-fury-atari-ste/blob/9390713ecd21e191e6e6ef67c2e06f5f6f732f0b/README.md

runtime_profiles.name: Linux x86-64 command-line runtime
runtime_profiles.notes: Current CI builds the release executable on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and executes vamos comparison and interpreter/JIT fixtures. No minimum RAM or Linux release is established.

runtime_profiles.notes: Current CI log identifies aarch64-apple-darwin and passes unit/end-to-end guest fixture execution. No minimum RAM or macOS release is established.

project.status: v0.11 published; sanitizer tracks exec.library allocation lifetime and catches guest use-after-free
project.notes: Wine-style host runtime for classic AmigaOS m68k command-line tools: interprets guest instructions (optional m68k-crate trace JIT) and reimplements OS library calls in Rust. No Kickstart ROM is needed for normal use. It is generic development/analysis tooling, not a native reconstruction of a specific game; graphics, custom chips, Workbench GUI and games are explicitly out of scope. Linux/macOS build and guest execution are corroborated by current CI logs; published Windows x86-64 binaries compile but Windows/Wine runtime remains unverified. Interpreter/JIT parity covers six fixtures; comparison with vamos includes three documented known divergences, so it is not universal compatibility proof. The math-library shims now return comparison/test results in both D0 and 68k condition codes, matching the documented ROM calling behavior needed by SAS/C's scmieee.lib; before the fix, SAS/C double comparisons appeared equal and exp() overflow checks returned HUGE_VAL. Evidence: https://github.com/sidick/volamos/commit/de321627fd5f1c16ca6cc76020222d7f3c18d564 exec.library SetFunction now installs executable guest JMP entries, returns a synthesized callable stub for the previous host-backed handler, supports hook chaining and restoration, and is covered by an end-to-end guest test. The patch is deliberately limited to one guest invocation and does not emulate AmigaOS-wide persistent hooks. Evidence: https://github.com/sidick/volamos/commit/018fd8f047d27fa3f85948b1595f44acf3f6f596 v0.10 incorporates non-AUTOINIT disk-library loading and the MakeLibrary/AddLibrary/InitStruct/MakeFunctions exec paths. Current main also adds opt-in CLI handling for UAE's formatted debug port at $BFFF00 and Emu68's byte debug port at $DEADBEEF, routing guest diagnostics to stderr without claiming broader GUI/custom-chip emulation. Evidence: https://github.com/sidick/volamos/releases/tag/v0.10 https://github.com/sidick/volamos/commit/2ee28f5f2759a9ea5096ba7f0068c4ec4cf94011 https://github.com/sidick/volamos/commit/359f762476c061b3b487cdcaf1dc86acdc786dd9 https://github.com/sidick/volamos/commit/fcec136d6f7f416b89af11d6bb76f6c89c96a8f5 v0.11 publishes aarch64 Apple/Linux and x86-64 Windows/Linux archives. Current sanitizer work extends exec.library Allocate/Deallocate handling: allocations become uninitialized, frees become unaddressable/freed, and live MemChunk headers remain addressable to avoid false positives. It can catch guest use-after-free and optionally uninitialized reads, but deliberately has no redzones, so one-byte overruns remain outside the stated coverage. Upstream reports 1,109 workspace tests passing; real gcc/sc binary checks were not run and trap-level end-to-end tests substitute. The implementation commit explicitly credits Claude Sonnet 5. Evidence: https://github.com/sidick/volamos/releases/tag/v0.11 https://github.com/sidick/volamos/commit/e5a44e39cf91e92d1350fcb898e224db363fd589

project.notes: Identity: Rust high-level runtime implementing classic Mac Toolbox/OS managers and 68k/PPC application loaders so original Macintosh applications can execute without a Macintosh ROM or installed System. Classification: Inspected CODE 0/A5 jump-table parser and per-manager trap dispatch implementation. Scope includes broad applications and games, so it is not a per-game CPU wrapper. Browser catalogue entries are part of the same runtime project rather than separately reconstructed games. GPL-3.0-or-later runtime; bundled font files/compatibility data have separate OFL notices, documented in LICENSING.md. Source CPU: Documented source/input platforms: Macintosh. Processor scope: m68k, PowerPC. Target CPU: Documented output/support targets: macOS, Linux, Windows, Web. Processor scope: ARM64, x86-64, WebAssembly. Build: Cargo package requires Rust 1.93 and registry dependencies including m68k, ppc, stuffit and graphical/audio crates. Native release instructions cover macOS/Linux/Windows; browser is a workspace member. User supplies original app/resource forks or archives; no ROM/System image dependency. No candidate code was compiled or executed. No candidate software was compiled or executed in this pass; build/run/play/byte-identity flags remain unknown. Runtime profiles: README lists native x86-64 and ARM64 releases, Linux glibc 2.35+ and ALSA runtime. No complete RAM or minimal processor model established. AI: Bounded README, source metadata and tip-commit inspection found no explicit development-AI attribution. This does not establish non-use. Relationships: 68k and PPC execution cores are Cargo dependencies, while Toolbox/OS manager reimplementation is project-specific. Do not label it original recovered Apple OS source. Evidence: https://github.com/benletchford/systemless/blob/28dffcaac3fef67b277ccfac280a3ca3988753e1/README.md https://github.com/benletchford/systemless/blob/28dffcaac3fef67b277ccfac280a3ca3988753e1/Cargo.toml Current main labels CPU-only baselines separately from GPU qualification while preserving the same guest/page sweeps and pixel comparisons, so CPU results cannot be mistaken for GPU coverage. QuickDraw and QD3D now reuse bounded compute bind-group slots and invalidate them when scratch storage grows. The reviewed commits include explicit Claude Opus 5.5 co-author attribution; these are upstream test/implementation receipts, not an independent run. Evidence: https://github.com/benletchford/systemless/commit/e847c8506e5f701fcaa657c3c65372de8e39ef30 https://github.com/benletchford/systemless/commit/e4e590d010b0fbc685a59869ec7a52ef7aa3e9df https://github.com/benletchford/systemless/commit/a42eee8225905be448d4e412b665921eade9263d

project.title: mz800emu
project.display_title: mz800emu — Sharp MZ-800/700/1500 emulator and debugger
project.status: active; frame-synchronized GUI/MCP memory search, freeze and write-origin analysis added
project.notes: Open-source Sharp MZ emulator with cycle-accurate Z80A execution, chip/peripheral emulation, a built-in debugger and an MCP bridge exposing screenshots, coverage, profiling and analysis controls. Primary docs provide Linux, Windows and macOS build paths; no minimum host CPU or RAM is stated. Claude client configuration documents a supported integration, not evidence that AI authored the project. Current main saves hidden Z80 MEMPTR, interrupt, EI-delay and T-state state plus CTC, scroll, VRAM-wait and floppy-controller state; it safely adapts RAMdisk/IDE8 snapshot loads. Debugger/MCP fixes expose all 532 expanded memory regions, keep debugger reads from firing guest watchpoints, correctly stop temporary run-to breakpoints and record the instruction bytes actually fetched by self-modifying code. Evidence: https://github.com/michalhucik/mz800emu/commit/1f477d90e2efd6808253c1c3d5f31fa56f465570 https://github.com/michalhucik/mz800emu/commit/a5726b9658d10b4412cf4a28bc212a78351f28a4 Current main adds frame-boundary-synchronized memory search across user RAM, logical Z80 space, VRAM, extension banks, RAM disks and other writable memory, with numeric/string types, filters, undo/redo, candidate actions, freeze controls and write-origin inspection. Matching MCP tools expose searches and freezes for automation, and the same change fixes the missing second half of PEHU 512 KiB memory. A maintained locale catalog at the reviewed commit explicitly names Claude Code as Last-Translator, correcting the prior no-evidence AI audit while keeping attribution limited to that content. Evidence: https://github.com/michalhucik/mz800emu/commit/0e4967ca56d162bcd2dc3607ebab986f9e029e78 https://github.com/michalhucik/mz800emu/blob/0e4967ca56d162bcd2dc3607ebab986f9e029e78/src/locale/de/LC_MESSAGES/mz800emu.po

project.status: v0.9.6; runnable multi-format interactive-fiction and disk-image interpreter
project.notes: Runnable Rust terminal interpreter for Z-machine, Glulx and Scott Adams formats, with loaders for original ADF, ST, D64, DSK and other disk images, automapping and artwork rendering. v0.9.3 moves new installations to platform-standard data folders, adds a migration command and Glulx border defaults, and bounds runaway stories plus damaged media/image/audio handling. This is historical story/media format implementation, not a claim of recovered game source. v0.9.5 adds game-probed automap exits and non-cardinal room placement, Scott Adams autocomplete, and single-pass/lazy media reads that reduce a documented 354 MiB CD launch from repeated full-image reads to about 27 MiB. It also corrects narrower-window save restoration, multi-command mapping and platform data-folder migration. The following unreleased compass styling is not promoted into the release status. Evidence: https://github.com/sharkusk/lanthorn/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md https://github.com/sharkusk/lanthorn/releases/tag/v0.9.5 v0.9.6 publishes Linux x86-64/aarch64, macOS universal and Windows x86-64 archives. Current main prevents modal dialogs from being hidden under full-screen artwork by using terminal-protocol-specific fallback behavior for sixel/iTerm2 and Kitty graphics, and replaces fixed PTY test delays with content-based staging; the commit reports the affected test dropping from roughly 37 seconds to 2.5 seconds. These commits explicitly credit Claude Opus 5.5. Evidence: https://github.com/sharkusk/lanthorn/releases/tag/v0.9.6 https://github.com/sharkusk/lanthorn/commit/b7145309bb2eff33a57482a945c85d118b3c17ef https://github.com/sharkusk/lanthorn/commit/48a8228875ec20efa5a73266785cd42b88ce60c5

project.title: ghidra-retro-machines
project.display_title: Ghidra Retro Machines — bank-aware loaders and retro CPU languages
project.status: Active; address-masked indexed writes now resolve at effective targets with 35-ROM NES regression coverage
project.notes: Ghidra extension for banked C64/C128/PET PRG and NES iNES analysis, with SPC700 and 65C816 language variants. The current NES pass bounds split low/high pointer tables by the next section gap: Dodge shrinks from 64 to 26 entries, River City Ransom from 64 to 27 and Mega Man 2 from 255 to 15. Upstream reports build-and-test SUITE OK and 29 NES baseline passes plus the three corrected fixtures. Existing 65C816 oracle-defect guards and language limitations remain; these gates show bounded analysis improvements, not universal correctness. The reviewed commit explicitly credits Claude Opus 5.5. Evidence: https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/6556e84ff267a0c96e7c89c5dbe2d3c3777d2aad The next analyzer pass extends RAM save-slot proofs across admitted cross-function jumps and narrowly recognized save-helper calls, while preserving conservative abandon rules and declining unresolved overlay-bank cases. Upstream reports 33 NES tests passing; the separate Dragon Power symbol-output flap remains documented. Evidence: https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/3f983b0189e67e2f8337804e0c2beb46c5483d44 The latest bank-analysis passes persist provenance for analyzer-created overlay references so later rounds retract stale targets without deleting user-owned references, and remove fall-through code only when a conditional branch is provably taken and no flow, entry point, function or user label preserves the old path. Upstream reports deterministic NES corpus updates and passing synthetic/JUnit gates; these are bounded analyzer-correctness receipts, not universal decompilation correctness. Evidence: https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/475eeadd4fb50ad045bd8e01dd428243279bfe2d https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/1251af61b1d65c8849bc90795d186ee274938db4 The newest passes write jump-table overrides once a containing function exists, eliminating first-reference analysis-order sensitivity, then remove the default single-thread pin while retaining GRM_THREAD_PIN=1 as a diagnostic. Upstream reports byte-identical results across all 34 NES fixtures at 12, 4 and 2 threads plus passing synthetic gates; this is bounded corpus determinism rather than universal analysis correctness. The reviewed commits explicitly credit Claude Opus 5.5. Evidence: https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/2a15e0df8abeeccc0842b212a00e1d08d2316e41 https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/48c66e952687ddaa24979626263f9b24dbd6b11d Current main fixes a dataflow join across a cross-function predecessor edge so a shared-store tail can retain the correct save-slot proof. Castlevania III now forks bank_5116 for banks 7 and 30, reduces warnings from 15 to 14 and raises bank comments from 171 to 172; the other 34 NES rows remain byte-identical and build-and-test reports SUITE OK. Adjacent fixes discard partial states that violate overlay invariants or flow into a differently occupied overlay, retry isolated flaky corpus rows, handle ROM paths with spaces and synchronize a 6510 illegal-instruction definition. These remain bounded analyzer/corpus receipts. Evidence: https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/101dc785283b69672728d98a318af579d2f5f7ff https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/9ab5515 https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/2950474 Current main corrects indexed writes under address masking by decoding at the effective target rather than the operand base. Five new tests pass; upstream reports build-and-test SUITE OK, 35/35 NES real-ROM corpus rows passing without blessing and byte-identical Bandai goldens. The commit explicitly credits Claude Opus 5.5; the results remain bounded analyzer regressions rather than universal correctness. Evidence: https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/8bef37250f5fa012f96753884da2cf5db28ab1c4

project.notes: Active investigation of the ZX Spectrum 48K Fairlight II completion bug. Current work maps the C0-FF room-bytecode opcode table, direct and lookup-based operand encodings, room-renderer flags and dynamic-object formats. New analysis documents the 3D engine and its relationship to Fairlight I, then compares 48K/128K bugs and quirks: a Part 2 completion defect, 128K sprite-direction behavior, health underflow/wrap, magic-carpet redraw/use behavior and unusual exits. Supporting captures are repository evidence, not a runnable reconstruction or build claim. events.title: Memory Search: find a variable by narrowing candidates (GUI and MCP)
events.message:
Memory Search: find a variable by narrowing candidates (GUI and MCP)

New debugger window Memory Search (Debugger -> Memory Search, Alt+Shift+E)
finds where a program keeps a value - lives, score, a timer - the way a
cheat search does: take a sample, let the value change in the program,
keep only the positions that changed the same way, repeat.

- Spaces: User RAM (default), Logical Z80, VRAM, MemExt banks, RAM disks,
  all writable memory. Over 4 MiB only with "Allow large space" (32 MiB).
- Types: u8, s8, u16, s16, u24, s24, u32, s32 (LE/BE), packed BCD, digit
  strings (raw 00h-09h, ASCII, Sharp MZ display code, leading spaces).
- Filters: equal, not equal, less, greater, between, increased /
  decreased (by N), changed (by N), unchanged, bits under mask - against
  a value, the previous or the first sample; Not, Undo / Redo (with the
  reference samples), preview of the filter.
- Samples are taken by the emulator thread at a frame boundary (at once
  when paused), so all regions come from the same moment; the emulation
  loop is unchanged.
- Candidate actions: Show in Memory Browser, Add to Watch, Add write
  breakpoint (zone RAM / VRAM framebuffer / PEHU bank with bank offset),
  Freeze at current value, Who wrote this byte?, Copy address, Eliminate.

MCP: emu_memsearch_start / _filter / _sample / _undo / _redo / _list /
_eliminate / _close (the list gives each candidate's CPU address and a
ready write breakpoint for emu_bp_create_with_init) and Freeze Bytes over
MCP: emu_freeze_add / _remove / _list. Agent recipe:
emulator://docs/memsearch_workflow.

Fixed: with a PEHU memory expansion the Memory Browser, Freeze Bytes and
emu_regions_list / emu_region_read showed only the first half of the
512 kB (PEHU banks 20h-3Fh were missing).

Docs: debugger/memory-search.md, mcp-server/tools-overview.md; the
display code table of the agent document sharp_display_code was
corrected (space 00h, digits 20h-29h).

events.title: sanitize: extend heap detectors to exec.library Allocate/Deallocate (#83, Tier 1) (#166)
events.message:
sanitize: extend heap detectors to exec.library Allocate/Deallocate (#83, Tier 1) (#166)

* sanitize: extend heap detectors to exec.library Allocate/Deallocate (#83, Tier 1)

A successful Allocate now marks its returned block Uninit in the
sanitizer shadow map, and Deallocate marks the freed block Unaddressable
with PoisonReason::Freed -- the same states execmem's poison_allocation_edges/
poison_freed_block already apply to AllocMem/AllocVec. This matters because
a C program's malloc (libnix and newlib alike) takes a few big blocks via
AllocVec and then sub-allocates from its own pool with Allocate, so most of
a real C program's heap traffic was previously invisible to --sanitize.

Unlike AllocMem's free list (host-side, invisible to the shadow map),
Allocate/Deallocate's free list lives in guest memory and is read/written
through the same checked AddressSpace path a guest access uses. Poisoning
a freed chunk's entire extent naively would poison its own live
mc_Next/mc_Bytes header too, and the very next Allocate/Deallocate call
that walks past it would then trip a violation against the allocator's
own bookkeeping -- not a guest bug. Fixed by always keeping a MemChunk
header that remains (or becomes) part of the live free list shadow-Valid,
via a new exempt_chunk_header helper, called before any checked write to
such a header (a checked write to an already-poisoned byte is recorded as
a violation, not healed). A dedicated test
(malloc_pattern_allocate_free_then_reallocate_smaller_causes_no_false_positive)
exercises exactly this and caught a real ordering bug during development
(exemption was originally applied after the write instead of before).

Tier 2 (redzones around the returned block, to catch overruns) is
explicitly not attempted here -- it would change the guest-visible pool
layout, a separate, bigger decision per the issue.

No real m68k-amigaos-gcc/sc toolchain was available in this environment,
so the C-fixture and false-positive sweep against real gcc-built/pLhA/
PhxAss/sc binaries from the issue's checklist were not run; the new
trap-dispatch end-to-end tests are the substitute coverage here.

1109 tests pass workspace-wide (was 1102 on main).

events.title: grm-egw, grm-bow: decode an addr_mask latch's indexed write at its effective target
events.message:
grm-egw, grm-bow: decode an addr_mask latch's indexed write at its effective target

Under an addr_mask (Bandai FCG), neither writesInRange tier could judge an
indexed store. The operand tier knew only the base and declined. The reference
tier looked authoritative but was the base decoded too:
MosConstantReferenceAnalyzer replaces the computed reference with a base one on
a known index (grm-egw), and stock const-prop parks an unknown-index access at
the base. That was wrong in BOTH directions -- STA $8000,X with X=8 (the PRG
register) was missed, and STA $8008,X with X=1 (an IRQ register) latched
prg_bank, the false-latch half grm-egw did not name.

Now, under an addr_mask, an indexed operand is decoded only at
StoredValueScanner.effectiveOperandTarget (same hooks as the bus-conflict AND,
RegisterEnv.NONE since the mechanism match is cached by address); an
unresolvable index declines. The write itself is still established as before
(true store, or a write reference in range for an RMW). Boards without an
addr_mask are untouched.

Five new MemoryLatchStrategyProgramTest cases, each failing on the old code:
refless resolvable store, base ref hiding a PRG write, base ref latching a

events.title: Unattended runs: --headless ends by itself with an exit code and a result file
events.message:
Unattended runs: --headless ends by itself with an exit code and a result file

For CI and scripts without an MCP client, the emulator in --headless can
now end by itself when a condition is met, write the result to a JSON file
and return an exit code.

    mz800emu --headless --speed max --run-mzf test.mzf \
             --exit-on-pc 2000h --fail-on-pc 2100h --timeout-seconds 30 \
             --automation-dir out

Exit conditions
- --exit-after-frames N - after N emulated frames (code 0)
- --timeout-frames N / --timeout-seconds S - safety timeout in emulated
  time (code 2)
- --exit-on-pc ADDR[,skip=N][,code=C] and --fail-on-pc ADDR[,skip=N] -
  when the CPU executes an address (code C / 1)
- --exit-on-write ADDR[=VAL] and --exit-on-out PORT - when the program
  writes to a memory address or an I/O port; the exit code is the written
  value (or code=C)
- --bpt FILE - a breakpoint set; any breakpoint with the new action
  "exit" ends the run
The first condition met wins. The --exit-on-* options can be repeated.
An unattended run neither loads nor saves the breakpoints and variables
saved from earlier sessions, so leftovers from the GUI cannot change the
result.

Exit codes: 0 success, 1 test failed, 2 timeout, 3 error of the emulator
or of the options (only when an unattended-run option is given; otherwise
an invalid option returns 1 as before), 64-255 free for codes reported by
the program.

Result
- --result-json FILE or --automation-dir DIR (result.json + screen.png):
  reason, exit code, trigger (breakpoint, option, hits), time (frames,
  GDG clock ticks, emulated seconds), registers, raster position,
  SHA-256 hashes of RAM, MemExt, VRAM, PCG and the screen, artifacts.
  Written also on a timeout or an error. Two runs with the same options
  give the same hashes.
- --exit-screenshot FILE, --exit-snapshot FILE - final screen and state.
- Video recording and audio capture are finished whatever the exit code.
  Before, an exit with a non-zero code skipped this cleanup, and on
  Windows an exit after an error in --headless waited 5 seconds; it no
  longer waits.

Breakpoint actions
- stop ["message", args] - stop the emulator, optionally with a message
  (log and stop in one breakpoint)
- exit <code> ["message", args] - end the run with an exit code. In the
  GUI and in an MCP session the emulator only pauses: emu_run reports
  stopped_by "exit" and the paused event has reason "exit" with exit_code.

Time conditions and the result file also work in a build without the
debugger; --exit-on-*, --fail-on-pc and --bpt need the debugger.

Documentation: docs/en/mcp-server/headless-mode.md (Unattended runs),
docs/en/debugger/breakpoints/action-dsl.md, MCP document
emulator://docs/unattended_runs.

events.title: ui: hand Qt the desktop entry's base name, not its file name
events.message:
ui: hand Qt the desktop entry's base name, not its file name

0.10.0 prints a warning on every start of an integrated install:

  QGuiApplication::setDesktopFileName: the specified desktop file name ends with
  .desktop. For compatibility reasons, the .desktop suffix will be removed.

The block exists precisely to avoid a per-start warning for no benefit — it locates
the installed entry first and stays silent when there is none — and it defeated
itself by passing the file name. setDesktopFileName() takes the entry's base name;
Qt strips a ".desktop" suffix itself and says so when it has to.

Found by running the published 0.10.0 AppImage under X: the state CI never runs,
because the AppImage is verified by extracting it, not by starting it.

Verified against the dev binary with XDG_DATA_HOME pointing at a tree holding
applications/pist.desktop: the warning printed before the change and does not now,
and an install with no entry stays silent as before.

events.message:
grm-8x6f: an ambiguous code-prefix cut still cuts the trailing non-code run

megaman2 92e4 kept its 15th case (bdb5, $ff filler) not because the
cases were out of table order -- they are not; bdb5 is entry 14 -- but
because real entry 10 (e6b5, opening on undefined opcode $04) fails to
decode. grm-0pen's codePrefix saw the first failure at 10, case 11
decoding again, and kept everything as ambiguous.

codePrefix now falls back to cutting the trailing run of non-decoding
cases when the first-failure cut is ambiguous. Nothing follows that run
to vouch for it, which is why a first failure on the last case already
stood unconfirmed. Still a refinement only (shortens an already-capped
list, bytes only). The EOL comment names the new cut separately
("trailing targets that do not decode as code"), and JumpTableProbe now
prints each switch's [JumpTableBound] comment.

check nes: only two rows moved, both reviewed.
- megaman2: 92e4 drops case_14 (bdb5), 15 -> 14 entries.
- cv3: bank-4 table a04f (switches 9e22, 9ea0) drops entries 29..32,
  33 -> 29 each; those point into an adjacent a1xx pointer table, not
  code. Entries 18..28 still do (they pseudo-decode): grm-6j5q.

The redesign's cards are the only way a person picks a template, a size, a palette or
a theme, and nothing tested them: the existing template case drove the hidden combo,
so a card wired to the wrong entry would have shipped silently.

Three cases, each asserting what the dialog produces rather than which member was set.

on disk in a temporary directory; New Image's four size cards and its palette cards
move the spin boxes and `paletteKind()`; and Settings' theme and shortcut cards save
the value they name. The cards carry no object names: the New File and New Image ones
identify themselves by the property they hold, the Settings ones by their caption,
which is what a person reads before clicking.

events.message:
ui: the review's fixes before 0.10.0

From an independent review of the redesign (PR #27):

- The QA checklist sent the tester to the bottom dock group for Find in Files; it
  moved beside Project files, so §3's Activate line named a dock that is not there.
- The New Image dialog's "Saved in …" note was computed once, from the directory it
  started in, so Browse… to another folder made it name somewhere the file would not
  be written. It follows the field now.
- The dock re-grouping hid already-hidden tabs first — a no-op, with a comment that
  claimed an ordering guarantee. It hides the visible tabs with the raised one last,
  which is what the comment said and what the list order already did.
- The first-run Setup dialog asked for 760×720 with no screen clamp — the trap
  SettingsDialog records for a 768 px screen at 125–150 % scaling.
- The welcome column's 440 px minimum became the window's minimum: with the factory
  docks it left PiST unshrinkable below about 1100 px. The words wrap; 320 is enough.
- The welcome rows could not be reached by keyboard and drew no focus state. They
  take focus now and paint a ring.

Deliberately not changed: the welcome plate stays at 1.4 MB (a palette-quantised
copy is 7.8× smaller, but banding needs an eye on a real display); the swatch numbers
living only in tooltips and the two owners of the bold dock-tab style are design
notes, not defects.

events.title: RAM Write Log - who wrote this byte?
events.message:
RAM Write Log - who wrote this byte?

A new debugging tool records the writes into memory while a program runs
and answers "which code wrote the value at address X?" - also for a byte
that was overwritten long ago - and "which code writes into this area?".

What is recorded for every write:
- the address of the instruction that wrote (for an accepted interrupt the
  return address the CPU pushed),
- the CPU address and the physical memory cell (RAM, MemExt, VRAM with the
  MZ-800 plane, PCG on the MZ-1500, ROM = write dropped),
- the old and the new value, the time (start of the writing instruction,
  the same clock as the Trace Suite) and the source: instruction,
  interrupt, debugger, breakpoint poke, freeze, tape (CMT hack) or program
  load (one summary record per block).

The same CPU address can be RAM now and VRAM after a banking switch; these
are separate cells with their own history. The last writer of every cell is
kept even when its record was already overwritten in the ring buffer.
Writes that did not change the value are recorded but hidden by default.

GUI
- Debugger -> RAM Write Log: start / stop / clear the log (range of CPU
  addresses or all memory, ring or fill mode, size), "Who wrote" query with
  the last writer and the write history of a cell, table of the newest
  writes.
- Memory Browser: right-click a byte -> "Who wrote this byte?".

MCP
- emu_ramlog_start, emu_ramlog_stop, emu_ramlog_clear, emu_ramlog_status,
  emu_ramlog_who_wrote, emu_ramlog_writers; the records are read page by
  page with emu_trace_read, channel "ramlog". Recipe for AI clients:
  emulator://docs/ramlog.

Breakpoints
- Actions ramlog_start [from, to], ramlog_stop, ramlog_clear; expression
  function lastwriter(addr).

Command line / configuration
- --ramlog-mode off|window|always, --ramlog-ring, --ramlog-capacity,
  --ramlog-lo, --ramlog-hi and the [RAMLOG] section of the INI file.

Performance (MZ-800, MAX SPEED, two test programs): recording one byte or
one 4 KiB page costs about 4-12 % of the emulation speed, all memory about
11-20 %, while a MEM_W breakpoint with a continue action on the same byte
costs about 17-27 %. With the log off the emulation speed does not change.

Available on MZ-800, MZ-700 and MZ-1500. Documentation:
docs/en/debugger/ram-write-log.md.

events.title: dos.library: OpenFromLock, ChangeMode (#159) (#162)
events.message:
dos.library: OpenFromLock, ChangeMode (#159) (#162)

Tier 2 of the dos.library LVO gap scan from #156/PR #161: cheap but
needing a small refactor first, as tracked by #159.

- OpenFromLock: splits DosState::open's "resolve a name through the Vfs"
  half from its "open a host path per access_mode and register a
  FileHandle" half (now open_resolved), so OpenFromLock can skip
  straight to the latter using a lock's already-resolved
  (host_path, amiga_path) from doslock::LockEntry. On a successful
  open the lock is relinquished via the existing unlock() path (matching
  the autodoc's "should not be UnLock()ed or used again"); a failed
  open leaves it untouched. Always opens the existing file read+write
  (MODE_OLDFILE-style) regardless of the lock's shared/exclusive access
  -- treating an exclusive lock's "NEWFILE-like" wording as a license to
  truncate would destroy a file that necessarily already exists.
- ChangeMode: this runtime has no real concurrency to enforce (same
  posture as the semaphore/AddTask stubs), so it just validates the
  referenced lock or filehandle exists (per CHANGE_LOCK/CHANGE_FH) and
  reports success, updating LockEntry::access for debuggability on the
  lock side (there's no equivalent field on HostHandle::HostFile worth
  adding for the filehandle side).

events.title: fix(core): pause-lease holders on two threads take turns with the machine (beads-nhfy) (#135)
events.message:
fix(core): pause-lease holders on two threads take turns with the machine (beads-nhfy) (#135)

* fix(core): pause-lease holders on two threads take turns with the mac…

…hine (beads-nhfy)

Every CpcPauseLease holder that found the runner idle went ahead, so two
holders that change the machine could do so at once from two threads: the
text IPC loading a snapshot beside a rebuild on the main thread, a KCPC
reset beside a DevTools disc format.

An idle lease now claims the machine, per thread, and a holder on another
thread waits for it within the lease's bound and fails closed (not idle)
when it is not let go. Nested leases on one thread do not wait for
themselves, and the frame runner inside its own turn never waits. A
PauseOnly lease that never calls wait() (window screenshot) pauses without
taking the machine.

The one cooperating pair, IPC `profile load` holding a lease while the
main thread rebuilds under its own, lends the machine for the length of
that wait (CpcPauseLease::lend()); without it the rebuild waited for the
IPC thread until the bound ran out and the command timed out.

events.title: demo: the tour, a first-run doorway and a Demo button
events.message:
demo: the tour, a first-run doorway and a Demo button

Polish for 0.10.0: the demo becomes the way to see the release.

`demo/hello.s` is now a complete little GEMDOS program written so each feature has
something to bite on — labels and equates for completion and the palette, all three
traps (GEMDOS, BIOS, XBIOS) for the hover card and the reference dock, a word to
watch by name, and a loop with a labelled breakpoint — with comments that name, line
by line, what to try in the IDE. `demo/hello.hooks.lua` is the project's stop hook:
it logs every stop, counts stops in the guest's own memory (a fresh Lua interpreter
per stop means nothing carries over in Lua), reads `counter` by name on the second
stop and pokes its low byte, and asks to continue once the program has counted its
last round. `hello.pistproject` points at it with `hooks.enabled`.

Three doorways: the toolbar's Demo button (the Atari mark, disabled when no demo is
reachable), File ▸ Open Demo Project, and — in `main()`, when the app is started with
no file and there is no last document to reopen — the demo opens itself. That last
one is application policy rather than window behaviour: a window built by a test must
still start empty, and the first version of this put it in the window's constructor
and took `tst_gui` and `tst_remotecontrol` down with it.

A doorway can be handed a *project* path — the welcome rows always are, from
`demoProjects()` — and `openPath()` shows a project file as its JSON. `MainWindow`
now derives the source beside it (`<project>.s`, the rule `openProject()` already
used inline), and both the welcome rows and the Demo button open that. That is a
pre-existing bug fixed, not merely used.

Packaging: the demo's authored files install to `share/pist/demo` (a whitelist, so
build output cannot ride along); `demoProjects()` searches it beside the installed
prefix as well as the source tree; and the AppImage, the deb/rpm private prefix, the
macOS bundles and the Windows archives all carry it — each checked against the
install that path actually runs.

Tests: `tst_gui` gains `theToolbarOpensTheDemo` — present, enabled exactly when a demo
is reachable, and it opens `hello.s`, asserted by the tab's title and by its text
being assembly rather than JSON — and the fresh-session completion case now picks the
editor it opened rather than the first one, since a window can hold more than one.

events.title: Put newlib's headers in sys-include before configuring newlib
events.message:
Put newlib's headers in sys-include before configuring newlib

newlib 4.6's configure checks the preprocessor by including <limits.h>
with the installed cross compiler. gcc's build leaves only the amigaos
header copies in sys-include, whose limits.h and assert.h include
newlib.h and _ansi.h from libc/include, so the check failed. On Linux
the host /lib/cpp fallback hid it; the macOS build stopped there since
the newlib merge. The old newlib 3.0 configure never ran the check.

The two rsyncs move from the libc.a rule into a _headers stamp that
both the configure and the build rule depend on.

events.title: Run the Mac II family and the Portable at 15.6672 MHz
events.message:
Run the Mac II family and the Portable at 15.6672 MHz

The CPU and the bus of the Mac II family and of the Portable run from
C16M, 15.6672 MHz, not 16 MHz. Give their buses that frequency, which
also makes the VIA clock of the Mac II exactly every 20 bus cycles and
derives the recovery time of the SCC and the clock of the SWIM from it.
On the Portable, whose VIA clock already came every 20 bus cycles, the
SWIM took 16 MHz, which made the tachometer and the bit rate of the
drives 2.1% slow against the VIA (#385).

ASCTester on a IIx then reads the first half empty interrupt 255.3
samples after the first write, as a real IIci and LC 475 (255.2), where
it read 256.3. The sample period of the ASC stays 35.15 VIA ticks, as
its rate is still divided into the bus frequency, where the hardware has
35.2.

Functional change, to match the hardware more closely: the Mac II
family and the Portable run at 15.6672 MHz. The compact Macs are
unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: Give each bus its own frequency
events.message:
Give each bus its own frequency

The frequency of the bus when the overclock is turned off was the one of
the Macintosh II for all the models.

Instead, give each bus the frequency of its real hardware, as a constant
behind a bus_frequency() accessor, and use it for what depends on it:
the default when the overclock is turned off, the clock of the SWIM, the
recovery time of the SCC, and the VIA clock of the Mac II. The field
holding the frequency of the bus, which includes any overclocking, is
renamed to act_bus_frequency.

set_bus_frequency() is renamed to set_overclock() to avoid confusion.

The VIA is passed the bus frequency and uses this at its clock source.

No functional change: all the buses keep 16 MHz for now, we'll adjust
them in subsequent commits.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: Run the compact Macs at 7.8336 MHz
events.message:
Run the compact Macs at 7.8336 MHz

A cycle of the compact Mac bus is a cycle of the CPU, which runs at C8M,
7.8336 MHz: the E clock comes every 10 cycles and the video, at C16M, is
ticked twice per cycle. Give the bus that frequency instead of 16 MHz.

The SWIM took 8 MHz, which made the tachometer and the bit rate of the
drives 2.1% slow (#385). It now takes the frequency of the bus. The VIA
keeps its speed, as it is converted against the same frequency, and an
overclock entered in MHz now means the same on a compact Mac as on the
other models.

Functional change, to match the hardware more closely: the compact Macs
run at 7.8336 MHz, and their floppy drives with it.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: ASC: give the sample period in C16M cycles
events.message:
ASC: give the sample period in C16M cycles

The Apple Sound Chip plays a sample every 704 cycles of C16M (15.6672
MHz), 22254.5 Hz, the rate the Guide to the Macintosh Family Hardware
gives for the sound of the Plus and SE, which comes from the same clock.
ASCTester measures 35.2 VIA clock cycles per sample (C16M / 20) on a
IIci, a LC 475, a LC II and a LC III. The Mac II and Portable buses
divided a rate of 22257 Hz into the bus frequency, which gave 703 cycles
of a 15.6672 MHz bus, 35.15 VIA clock cycles.

Give the period in C16M cycles instead of a rate, and count it against
the bus frequency, so that the sound keeps its pitch when overclocking
as before.

Functional change, to match the hardware more closely: the sample
period of the ASC is 704 C16M cycles on the Mac II and the Portable.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>

events.title: dos.library: ExamineFH, DupLockFromFH, ParentOfFH, GetCurrentDirName, SetFileSize, SplitName, SetProgramName (#161)
events.message:
dos.library: ExamineFH, DupLockFromFH, ParentOfFH, GetCurrentDirName, SetFileSize, SplitName, SetProgramName (#161)

Follow-up to codewiz's newlib-porting feedback that volamos 0.10 aborts
on ExamineFH/MakeLink/GetCurrentDirName/DupLockFromFH/ReadLink/
ParentOfFH. Implements the six genuinely cheap ones from that report
(all but MakeLink/ReadLink, tracked separately in #160 along with the
other, more involved gaps found while scanning the rest of the LVO
table), plus two more from that same scan: SetFileSize and
SplitName/SetProgramName, which needed only a small refactor
(OpenFromLock/ChangeMode, tracked in #159) or none at all.

Each reuses existing infrastructure rather than adding new capability:

- ExamineFH/DupLockFromFH/ParentOfFH read the host path every open
  FileHandle already carries (a new third field on HostHandle::
  HostFile, alongside the amiga_path NameFromFH already used) and
  call straight into Examine/Lock's own fill_fib/new_lock -- the same
  data a LockEntry already carries for a real Lock, just sourced from
  an open file instead.
- GetCurrentDirName is a thin wrapper around Vfs::cwd(), the same
  state CurrentDir() already maintains.
- SetFileSize is a few lines of std::fs::File::set_len.
- SplitName is a pure string function, no different in kind from the
  AddPart/FilePart/PathPart already in dospath.rs.
- SetProgramName is the inverse of the already-implemented
  GetProgramName, replacing the cli_CommandName BSTR.

ym2612: Modulation

Initial modulation is implemented for the ym2612:

 - Each channel's output is calculated and store in the operator state,
   so that it can either be used for audio output or to modulate other
   operators.

 - The algorithm_modulators table is added, indicating for each
   algorithm which operators are modulated by one another.

 - The sum of modulating operators is added to the phase when updating
   an operator's output.

Not implemented yet, but a part of how modulation should work:

 - Delays caused by operator order (1-3-2-4)

events.title: NetPrefs: At boot switches the whole Wi-Fi block
events.message:
NetPrefs: At boot switches the whole Wi-Fi block

The Installer starts a Wi-Fi interface from a block in S:Network-Startup:
"If EXISTS ENV:Sys/Wireless.prefs", WirelessManager under Status/If WARN,
EndIf, with the interface's AddNetInterface inside the If (Raspberry Pi,
or a secondary card) or on the line after the EndIf (a PC Card as the
primary).  At boot handled only the AddNetInterface line: off left
WirelessManager starting, and on, for a block written commented out,
brought back the line alone, so the card started without joining
(refs #307).

np_wifi_switch() finds the block for the interface and adds or strips one
';' on each of its lines, so off and on round-trip byte for byte, a
second tick changes nothing, and a WirelessManager line the Installer
wrote commented out keeps its own ';'.  Every other line is copied as is.
tests/tools/run-netprefs.sh gains the wifiboot group: off, on, off on a
Pi block and on a PC Card block, each compared with the whole file.

events.title: Installer: an older WirelessManager of the user's is kept, not started
events.message:
Installer: an older WirelessManager of the user's is kept, not started

A user's C:WirelessManager or SYS:C/WirelessManager (WM_USER) was kept
and S:Network-Startup started it, whatever its version.  On an A1200 with
prism2.device 2.9 that copy was WirelessManager 1.3: it never scans and
loops on "Disassociation notification" at a whole CPU.  The archive ships
1.5 (third_party/wirelessmanager, pinned by tools/fetch-wirelessmanager.sh).

Version <copy> 1 5 FILE answering WARN marks it older (WM_OLD): it stays
where it is, byte for byte, and the archive's copy goes beside it -- the
drawer layout's own C, or the AmiNetXDuo drawer in the system layout --
and is the one S:Network-Startup starts and S:AmiNetXDuo-WiFi records.
A copy with no version string, or 1.5 and newer, is kept and started as
before.  One radio still gets one supplicant: the lines start one copy,
and WM_ELSEWHERE still comments them out.

run-workbench.sh -w userwmold plants a C:WirelessManager carrying
"$VER: WirelessManager 1.3": kept, the archive's beside it, started.

An interface file with CONFIGURE=NONE and CONFIGURE6=OFF, started by

frames.  ami_ns_interface_add_locked()
turned OFF into AUTO for every caller.  That default was meant for

interfaces.c and ipv6_link_test.c already pass AUTO themselves; the
interface-file path (NETCTRL_INTERFACE_ADD, netstack_interface_start)
lost the file's OFF to it.  Removed: the file's CONFIGURE6 now holds, and
ami_ns6_configure_interface() leaves the interface without IPv6.

An A1200 with a Netgear MA401RA (MANFID $000B/$7300, a prism2.device card)

events.title: DHCP: DISCOVER backoff stops at 8 s, so a late Wi-Fi join leases (refs #306)
events.message:
DHCP: DISCOVER backoff stops at 8 s, so a late Wi-Fi join leases (refs #306)

The stack does not hear a Wi-Fi association: nothing in src/sana2 asks a
driver for S2EVENT_CONNECT.  An unassociated card (prism2.device,
anxwifipi.device) drops every frame, so the DISCOVERs sent before the join
are lost and NetX Duo's SELECTING backoff (4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 64... s,
nxd_dhcp_client.c:5607) decides when the next one goes.  With the
interface brought up before the key is entered, the 30 s bring-up wait
ends on a link-local address, and the lease came up to 65 s after the
join; ping said "network unreachable" in between.

NX_DHCP_MAX_RETRANS_TIMEOUT 8 s in the port's nx_user.h: the backoff goes
4, 8, 8... and the lease follows the join within one retransmission.  RFC
2131 4.1 sets 64 s as a maximum.  NetX Duo itself is unchanged.

tests/tools/wifigate.c is the repro: a unit in front of the A2065 that
drops every write until it associates and answers S2_ONEVENT and the
signal as prism2.device 2.9 does; run-wifigate.sh associates it 70 s after
AddNetInterface and wants the lease within 15 s (nightly).

  tests/tools/run-wifigate.sh -A 70 -L 15
  origin/main: lease_after_assoc_s=59 verdict=FAIL
  this branch: lease_after_assoc_s=3  verdict=PASS (with -R 20:
               route_after_rejoin_s=0)

events.title: 実装: CALL・USR・DEF USR・VARPTR（l4-t4 第1段）
events.message:
実装: CALL・USR・DEF USR・VARPTR（l4-t4 第1段）

根拠は仕様 l4-program 第4.24節（測定 l4-t4 第1回・追補1〜3 → 796255b・87602a1・e2ebde7）。
- CALL は数値変数の番地で呼び、引数の変数の格納場所を HL（第1）・DE（第2、文字列は3B記述子）で渡す。
  引数が無いとき HL は本文の現在位置、第2引数が無いとき DE は自作の作業域を指す（未規定・RAM 内を指すようにした）。
- USR の入口 A は型コード、整数・単精度は HL+0、倍精度は HL−4 からの作業域（スタックに8B）、文字列は DE が固定 RAM の記述子
  （MM_USR_STRING_DESC）。呼び先が書き換えた値を戻り値にし、戻り型は渡した型。DEF USR0〜9 の表はヒープのレコードに初回だけ確保。
- VARPTR は格納場所を符号付き16ビットで返す。自作は短い文字列をレコードに直接置くため、VARPTR・CALL に渡すときは3B記述子の形に直す。
- 自作判断: 番地 0・FFFF の CALL/USR は実行せず ERR 5（公式は制御が戻らず未確定）、CALL の実引数は0〜2個、VARPTR(#…) は固定の負番地、
  配列要素の VARPTR は実際の要素を指す（公式の不一致は理由未解決で、期待値から外してある）。
配置: main 0x7667〜0x78F8（658B、残り 221B）、bank3 481B（残り 90B）、bank0 316B（残り 154B）。bank1・bank2（BSAVE/BLOAD 用）は未使用。
照合: tools/l4_mlcall_measure.py check --results で第1回＋追補1 61/61・追補2・3 18/18（実装前は 19/61・2/18）。
自己検査: ext_bank・main_sub_link・m6ib 全腕ビルド・SQR 陰性対照・l4_deffn・l4_memdyn・l4_strfunc・l4_strcmp・l4_dim・l4_deftype・l4_mlcall（全ラウンド）・l4_bsave が終了0。run_all は未実行。

events.title: MCP: read the audio capture from memory (summary, PCM window, paged records)
events.message:
MCP: read the audio capture from memory (summary, PCM window, paged records)

The audio capture now also keeps its data in memory, so an MCP client can
analyse the sound without access to the capture files (also over a
network connection), while the capture runs and after it ends, until the
next capture starts.

emu_audio_capture_start - new parameters (memory is on by default via MCP;
the menu and the command line keep the old behaviour):
- memory: keep rings of PSG writes, channel level changes and per-frame
  summaries;
- pcm: PCM rings of the reference render and/or the audio output path
  (default ["reference"]);
- memory_minutes, pcm_seconds: ring lengths.
A capture into memory only (all files off) creates no folder.
emu_audio_capture_status reports the capture number (segment), the start
time, the channel names and the memory rings.

Reading:
- emu_trace_read channels audio_psg_writes (every PSG write, with Hz and
  note for a new tone divider), audio_levels (every level change of a
  channel) and audio_frames (one row per audio frame: level changes, time
  with level > 0 and RMS level per channel, RMS and peak of the reference
  and of the audio output). Same cursor/filter/character budget contract
  as the trace channels; new filters channels and reg.
- emu_audio_capture_summary: silent and sound spans, per-channel
  statistics, notes played by the PSG (replayed from the writes and the
  PSG state at the capture start), a histogram of the speaker edge
  intervals with a tone / 1-bit PCM estimate (explicitly a heuristic), and
  the delay and difference of the audio output against the reference
  (found from note onsets and volume changes; flagged when only a steady
  tone makes the delay undeterminable).
- emu_audio_capture_pcm: a short PCM window as WAV or raw base64,
  resampled by averaging (analysis preview); 44100 Hz stereo returns
  exactly the samples of reference.wav / sdl.wav.

The pitch and note computation is now shared by the PSG Audio Scope, the
PSG window and the MCP summary (no change of the displayed values).

No change in the emulation hot path: the memory is filled by the existing
capture hooks, which run only while a capture is active.

Documentation: Audio capture, MCP tools overview, and a new agent guide
emulator://docs/audio_capture_read.

events.title: grm-jt7s: bound a jump table indexed by a keyed linear search
events.message:
grm-jt7s: bound a jump table indexed by a keyed linear search

megaman PRG_LO_B5::99b5 dispatches through a search over 3-byte
(id, lo, hi) records:

  9998 LDY #$2d / 999f CMP $99bb,Y / BEQ 99ab / DEY x3 / BPL 999f /
  LDY #0 / 99ab LDA $99bc,Y / STA $04 / LDA $99bd,Y / STA $05 /
  99b5 JMP ($0004)

Nothing bounds Y for the decompiler at the switch, so it read the loads at
stride 1 (256 cases, 184 distinct targets) against 16 records and 9 real
handlers, and every JumpTableBound extent rule declined: the real cases
are every third one, which no prefix cut can express. Stock laid the
over-read, including garbage like c953 ASL $bd falling into a BRK.

New SearchLoopDispatch reads the index set the code states: the values
LDY #n / DEY x k / BPL holds while bit 7 is clear, plus the LDY #imm
fallback falling into the join. Guards keep the claim exact: the join to
the switch is straight-line, writes no Y and is entered only by that
fall-through and the one search branch; the loop body is entered only at
its head, and the head only from its BPL and the run down from LDY #n.
Each target is read from the two table bytes at that index, and every
one must be a case the decompiler also read, so the rule can only shrink
a table. JumpTableBoundAnalyzer tries it ahead of the extent rules (not
for cross-bank tables) as Rule.SEARCH_LOOP, skipping the codePrefix
refinement, which has nothing to refine in an exact set.

check nes: only megaman moves. 99b5 is "bounded 256 -> 16 entries (index
from a keyed search loop)", carrying the 9 hand-traced targets. Instruction
census A/B against HEAD: 23 lost, all over-read garbage (the c953 and fe2f
BRK runs, BRK-ended decodes at a9c5/a9f4/aa23, lone ORA/AND/RTS bytes); 125
gained, all real code: 109 in the search handlers 99eb-9aea and 16 at
c93c-c961 that the c93e/c953 garbage had overlapped. Bank comments that
named FUN_c53d by a stock over-read label (caseD_a4) now name the function,
and 9a5f gains one.

  megaman: refs.intoOverlay.intraOverlay 1699 -> 1673, instrs.inOverlay 7722 -> 7816, bankComments 114 -> 115, symbols 216 -> 233

Realrom-Bless: megaman

events.title: fix(sdisc): a Silicon Disc enabled at run time is fitted on the board (beads-t9vs) (#134)
events.message:
fix(sdisc): a Silicon Disc enabled at run time is fitted on the board (beads-t9vs) (#134)

* fix(sdisc): a Silicon Disc enabled at run time is fitted on the board…

… (beads-t9vs)

`config set silicon_disc`, `sdisc load` on a disabled disc and the DevTools
Enabled checkbox only flipped g_silicon_disc.enabled. The board gained (or
lost) banks 4-7 only at the next rebuild, so on a 128K machine the CPC's
bank 4 was still expansion bank 0 while `sdisc status` said enabled.

subcycle_bridge_silicon_disc_fit() fits the disc on the running board
(Machine::enable_silicon_disc, then the battery buffer into banks 4-7) or
takes it out (the board's copy back to the buffer first), and sets the host
flag to match. All three paths call it under the lease they already take;
the DevTools checkbox now goes through sd_with_machine() like Save, Load
and Clear instead of writing the flag from the render thread.

events.title: Installer: a PC Card Wi-Fi gets WirelessManager again (refs #307)
events.message:
Installer: a PC Card Wi-Fi gets WirelessManager again (refs #307)

#261 removed the bundled prism2.device and, with it, every path that made a
PC Card the Wi-Fi.  A card set up as PCMCIA "Something else" with the
user's prism2.device became a wired eth0: S:Network-Startup started the
interface and nothing started WirelessManager, so the card never joined.

The installer still does not supply prism2.device.  It recognises the
user's Wi-Fi driver instead:

- InstallNetProbe CARD wireless: the card in the slot is 802.11 by its
  identity (netprobe_pc_wireless(): a Prism2 2.9 MANFID, a Linux 802.11
  PC Card MANFID or a wireless FUNCE), or prism2.device owns the slot.
- prism2.device in DEVS: or DEVS:Networks, or such a card, preselects the
  PCMCIA family and "Something else" with the driver's name.
- PCMCIA "Something else" with prism2.device, or any driver for a card
  that says 802.11, is the Wi-Fi when the Pi Wi-Fi is not selected:
  WirelessManager, Wireless.prefs and the S:Network-Startup block as for
  the Pi, and no Pi firmware.  The pre-#261 rules come back with it: one
  Wi-Fi at a time, a primary card starts outside the Wireless.prefs
  guard, "Keep it" finds a kept card from its live DEVICE
  (InstallWiFi PRISM2).

run-workbench.sh gets -w prism2/prism2pi/prism2keep back, with the user's
prism2.device staged from the asset store, and run-all.sh runs them with
cnetkeep as PCMCIA_WIFI, PCMCIA_WIFI_PI, PCMCIA_WIFI_KEEPIT and CNET_KEEP.

events.title: editor: seed the completion candidates where the window starts, not at the first build
events.message:
editor: seed the completion candidates where the window starts, not at the first build

Reported from a real session: typing `mov` offered nothing. The window's candidate
list was assigned only inside `rebuildProgramMap()` — after a build — so a project
that had never been assembled pushed an *empty* list into every editor, and the
vocabulary, which does not depend on the build at all, was simply missing until
then. It is seeded in the constructor now; a build only *adds* the label and equate
candidates on top of it.

The suite stayed green through both of this feature's failures for the same reason:
the completion case used a standalone editor whose candidate list the test seeded
by hand, so nothing covered the window's own editor in a fresh session. `tst_gui`
now has `windowCompletesBeforeAnyBuild` — a source opened in a window, nothing
built, `mov` typed into its editor — which fails if the vocabulary is not already
there.

events.title: fix(kcpc): a write beside readers is taken at the frame boundary, not under a lease (beads-df1x) (#133)
events.message:
fix(kcpc): a write beside readers is taken at the frame boundary, not under a lease (beads-df1x) (#133)

* fix(kcpc): a write beside readers is taken at the frame boundary, not…

… under a lease (beads-df1x)

While clients read a running machine, REGS_SET and MEM_WRITE no longer let
a boundary pass and then take a pause lease (two to three frames each, and
a pause that took the frames the reads were waiting for). They are queued
at the gate behind the reads (Gate::at_boundary()) and the runner makes
them at the same boundary, where the lease would have made them too. With
nobody reading, or on a paused machine, the lease is kept: it waits for no
boundary at all. "Reading" is a read waiting, or one served in the last
four boundaries (Gate::reading()).

Three 64 KiB readers and a writer: paced 19-20 -> 41-48 writes/s, reads
112-119 -> 117-152/s; unpaced 146-174 -> 2728-2803 writes/s and 637-860
-> 2731-2807 frames/s. Write-only and no-client rates unchanged.

events.title: editor: draw the completion list inside the editor, and let Tab ask for it
events.message:
editor: draw the completion list inside the editor, and let Tab ask for it

Reported: the list does not open while typing. It did — offscreen. The list was
QCompleter's popup, a Qt::Popup, i.e. a surface of its own, placed with
move(mapToGlobal(caret)). Under Wayland a popup is an xdg_popup the compositor
positions *relative to its parent*, so a global move is not honoured and the
surface can be dismissed on show; the offscreen platform every test uses has no
compositor, so isVisible() was true there while nothing appeared on screen.

The list is now a QListView child of the viewport: drawn inside the editor
wherever the editor is, positioned in the viewport's own coordinates, below the
caret when it fits and above it when it does not. Two consequences come for free —
the keys never leave the editor, so a headless run and a real one take the same
path (the eventFilter that existed only to catch a popup's keys is gone), and the
two QCompleter quirks the code used to work around go with it: nothing is left to
hide its own popup on the next keystroke, and nothing is left to place it at the
widget's bottom edge.

Tab now asks for the list when it is not showing: on a word with candidates it
opens it, preselected; on a shown list it takes the candidate, as before; at the
start of a line, inside a comment, or on a word nothing knows, it still indents.
A click in the text dismisses the list, because the caret has moved away from the
word it was offering.

Tests: the completion case now types two characters in a row and asserts the list
stays up — the assertion whose absence let this ship — pins that the list is a
child widget rather than a popup window, and covers Tab opening the list mid-word,
Tab taking the candidate, and Tab still indenting at a line start and in a comment.

events.title: fix(cpu): keep a keyboard reset hold across a forced CPU board reset (#2473)
events.message:
fix(cpu): keep a keyboard reset hold across a forced CPU board reset (#2473)

With the multithreaded CPU and a board that turns a RESET instruction into
a full CPU reset (Blizzard PPC), m68k_reset() on the CPU thread cleared
SPCFLAG_CPUINRESET and the pending keyboard reset, so the CPU kept running
while Ctrl+Amiga+Amiga was held.

On the CPU thread, m68k_reset2() now keeps a keyboard reset that the CPU
thread has not taken yet and holds the CPU again. Resets on the main thread
still drop it.

events.title: MCP: read Trace Suite records and the Event Viewer page by page
events.message:
MCP: read Trace Suite records and the Event Viewer page by page

New MCP tools emu_trace_status and emu_trace_read let an MCP client read
the recorded trace directly, without parsing the chunk files:

- Channels: cputrack, iorqlog, intlog, hwlog, marklog and the Event
  Viewer ring (eventlog).
- Works while recording runs. Records that are still only in the RAM
  buffer are readable too, so a short run returns data without saving
  first. After emu_trace_stop the last recording stays readable until
  the channel is started again.
- Cursor paging (next_cursor, end_of_data); a cursor from an older
  recording returns an error starting with "segment_replaced:".
- Decoded rows by default, with a character budget per page (max_chars,
  default 20 000) and column selection; format raw_b64 returns the raw
  records for scripts.
- Server-side filters: PC range, port / direction / type, chip, marker,
  time range; max_scan keeps a filter that matches nothing from scanning
  forever.
- cputrack rows carry the disassembly decoded from the recorded bytes,
  the symbol and the time in GDG ticks since emulation start.

cputrack record format v2 (manifest "event_record_version": 2):
- byte 11 (previously reserved) holds the standard T-states of the
  instruction;
- a record with insn_length 0 is an accepted interrupt (PC = handler
  address, byte 11 = acknowledge T-states), so the record time can be
  reconstructed exactly from the chunk anchors also with interrupts on.

Documentation: Trace Suite, MCP tools overview, cputrack format and a
new agent guide emulator://docs/trace_read. The documentation now calls
the recording manifest by its real file name <name>.json (it said
meta.json).

No measurable performance change in MAX SPEED, with or without cputrack
recording.

events.title: fix(cpu): keep a keyboard reset hold across a RESET instruction (#2472)
events.message:
fix(cpu): keep a keyboard reset hold across a RESET instruction (#2472)

With the multithreaded CPU, Ctrl+Amiga+Amiga pressed while the CPU thread
waited for the chipset reset of a RESET instruction was lost: custom_reset()
cleared SPCFLAG_CPUINRESET and the keyboard reset sequence, so the CPU kept
running while the keys were held and releasing them did not reset the
machine.

When a keyboard reset is pending, the main thread now keeps the sequence
state across that chipset reset and holds the CPU again, so the CPU thread
takes the deferred keyboard reset and release resets the machine.

events.title: grm-jt7s: a late jump-table override retracts stock's over-read cases
events.message:
grm-jt7s: a late jump-table override retracts stock's over-read cases

megaman2 92e4 was bounded 255 -> 15 by override, and the decompiler honoured
it (FUN_925b decompiles with 10 distinct cases), but the listing still held
stock DecompilerSwitchAnalyzer's over-read: 224 COMPUTED_JUMP refs, one
switchD_92e4::caseD_<n> label per case, and the disassembly at each target,
e.g. da2b ORA ($00,X) falling into a BRK at da2e, all inside FUN_925b's body.
Stock runs first and the override lands late (the order the
jumptablebound-late-override-load-bearing memory says must stay), and only
the pin-by-references path ever replaced the switch's references.

After writeOverride succeeds, JumpTableBoundAnalyzer.retractStaleCases now
removes each ANALYSIS computed-jump ref whose target is not a kept case
(matched by offset, so an overlay retarget of a kept case stays), removes
stock's ANALYSIS case label there, clears the code from that target when
nothing else reaches it (DecidedBranchAnalyzer.deadCodeStart plus
ClearFlowAndRepairCmd, the same guard and command), and recomputes the
function body.

check nes: it fires at one site in the whole tier, megaman2 92e4 (213
retracted, flow cleared from 61). 34 rows unchanged. megaman2's bank
knowledge sharpens because the stale case refs were false flow joins:
cc43 "prg_bank=14?" with assumed bits becomes a fully known prg_bank=14,
cbc7 now knows mirroring.1, and 2 more refs are retargeted into overlays.
Probed after: 92e4 carries 10 distinct targets, the same set the decompiler
recovers, and da2b/da2e are no longer instructions.

The kept 15th entry (bdb5, $ff filler) is a separate bound defect: grm-8x6f.
megaman 99b5 (no rule bounds it) stays open on grm-jt7s.

New test: JumpTableBoundProgramTest.lateOverrideRetractsStockOverReadCases
runs stock DecompilerSwitchAnalysisCmd first, then the analyzer; it fails
with the retraction disabled.

  megaman2: refs.intoOverlay.retargeted 71 -> 73

project.notes: Maintained Jaguar and Jaguar CD libretro emulator continuing the original Virtual Jaguar lineage. v3.8.0 adds cartridge mirroring, BIOS-mode startup corrections, HLE DSP interrupt timing, a default-safe 68000-only blitter timing option, GameDrive SD-card support and savestate v17 with backward loading. The README and release workflow explicitly publish x86, x86-64, ARM, arm64 and WebAssembly variants across desktop, mobile and console hosts. Release notes distinguish headless-only verification and preserve known JaGol/JaguarDemos regressions, so playable remains unknown and no universal compatibility is claimed. Claude Opus 5.5 is explicitly credited on the release-notes commit; configuration-only Copilot evidence is retained separately. Evidence: https://github.com/libretro/virtualjaguar-libretro/blob/master/README.md https://github.com/libretro/virtualjaguar-libretro/releases/tag/v3.8.0 https://github.com/libretro/virtualjaguar-libretro/commit/e166e0e1fd36d87d85cf16a81db119bb14c0225b v3.9.1 restores Xenowings audio through netlist-derived DSP store/divide behavior, corrects 33-bit RISC division, broadens GPU idle-loop fast-forward without changing the tested corpus hashes, makes the 68K GDB stub usable by stock gdb, and corrects twelve homebrew/demo load routes. The release publishes a broad architecture matrix, including Windows ARM64 and signed/notarized macOS downloads; known timing, shader-CI and Windows-signing limits remain explicit. change_details.before: Maintained Jaguar and Jaguar CD libretro emulator continuing the original Virtual Jaguar lineage. v3.8.0 adds cartridge mirroring, BIOS-mode startup corrections, HLE DSP interrupt timing, a default-safe 68000-only blitter timing option, GameDrive SD-card support and savestate v17 with backward loading. The README and release workflow explicitly publish x86, x86-64, ARM, arm64 and WebAssembly variants across desktop, mobile and console hosts. Release notes distinguish headless-only verification and preserve known JaGol/JaguarDemos regressions, so playable remains unknown and no universal compatibility is claimed. Claude Opus 5.5 is explicitly credited on the release-notes commit; configuration-only Copilot evidence is retained separately. Evidence: https://github.com/libretro/virtualjaguar-libretro/blob/master/README.md https://github.com/libretro/virtualjaguar-libretro/releases/tag/v3.8.0 https://github.com/libretro/virtualjaguar-libretro/commit/e166e0e1fd36d87d85cf16a81db119bb14c0225b
change_details.after: Maintained Jaguar and Jaguar CD libretro emulator continuing the original Virtual Jaguar lineage. v3.8.0 adds cartridge mirroring, BIOS-mode startup corrections, HLE DSP interrupt timing, a default-safe 68000-only blitter timing option, GameDrive SD-card support and savestate v17 with backward loading. The README and release workflow explicitly publish x86, x86-64, ARM, arm64 and WebAssembly variants across desktop, mobile and console hosts. Release notes distinguish headless-only verification and preserve known JaGol/JaguarDemos regressions, so playable remains unknown and no universal compatibility is claimed. Claude Opus 5.5 is explicitly credited on the release-notes commit; configuration-only Copilot evidence is retained separately. Evidence: https://github.com/libretro/virtualjaguar-libretro/blob/master/README.md https://github.com/libretro/virtualjaguar-libretro/releases/tag/v3.8.0 https://github.com/libretro/virtualjaguar-libretro/commit/e166e0e1fd36d87d85cf16a81db119bb14c0225b v3.9.1 restores Xenowings audio through netlist-derived DSP store/divide behavior, corrects 33-bit RISC division, broadens GPU idle-loop fast-forward without changing the tested corpus hashes, makes the 68K GDB stub usable by stock gdb, and corrects twelve homebrew/demo load routes. The release publishes a broad architecture matrix, including Windows ARM64 and signed/notarized macOS downloads; known timing, shader-CI and Windows-signing limits remain explicit. project.status: v0.14.1 published; RESTORE now produces one deterministic NMI pulse per press with checkpoint-safe held-key state
project.notes: Headless C64/1541/1581 reverse-debugging runtime used by C64RE. v0.12.9 makes an execution breakpoint on the first interrupt-handler instruction fire, persists interrupt-entry stops through checkpoints, and aligns step, step-over and step-return behavior around IRQ/NMI and RTI with VICE monitor expectations. ROMs remain user-supplied; no host CPU or RAM minimum is stated. Evidence: https://github.com/Jondalar/TRX64/releases/tag/v0.12.9 https://github.com/Jondalar/TRX64/commit/db224337d341 https://github.com/Jondalar/TRX64/commit/1e6f73894427 https://github.com/Jondalar/TRX64/commit/212ebaf46857 TRX64 0.13.1 publishes Linux, macOS and Windows archives for x86-64 and ARM64. Development immediately after the release makes until and stepOver honor caller-supplied cycle budgets and changes instructionsElapsed from a mislabeled cycle total to a true retired-instruction count, with real-binary and headless tests. This is upstream evidence only; the tracker did not execute the archives. Evidence: https://github.com/Jondalar/TRX64/releases/tag/v0.13.1 https://github.com/Jondalar/TRX64/commit/86658ec6c62d44470c942ccfaf482f527b449891 Development head models Action Replay V5/V6 banking, freeze NMI timing and cartridge RAM/state. Upstream daemon tests mount four real-image variants as CRT and raw BIN, freeze and resume a BASIC counter without corrupting underlying RAM, restore frozen checkpoints/dumps and reproduce the same-cycle trace across fresh daemons; copyrighted images remain outside the repository and absent corpora skip. Evidence: https://github.com/Jondalar/TRX64/commit/cd97c39d9997c475213bb834ea36f4b08c103084 https://github.com/Jondalar/TRX64/commit/efbb280be0aed77e63942c322029753c3b30376a v0.14.1 changes RESTORE from a held NMI line to one deterministic pulse per press, preventing a held key from blocking CIA2 NMIs and preventing checkpoint restore from creating a phantom NMI. The release republishes Linux, macOS and Windows archives for ARM64 and x86-64; no CPU-generation, RAM or OS minimum is stated. Evidence: https://github.com/Jondalar/TRX64/releases/tag/v0.14.1 https://github.com/Jondalar/TRX64/commit/fc8a3aa3dc2e6b8ba52930154cb039ed799ced0d

project.title: PUAE Debugger
project.display_title: PUAE Debugger — Amiga source debugger & profiler
project.status: active; v1.0.0 package exposes VS Code/DAP debugging plus a headless MCP emulator and profile-analysis server
project.notes: Amiga debugger/profiler built around the WinUAE-derived PUAE core. Supports Hunk/ELF debug information, source and instruction breakpoints, data watchpoints, reverse execution, CPU/DMA profiling, Copper/blitter inspection, memory reconstruction, standalone DAP use and headless MCP-driven emulator inspection. Current main documents the packaged puae-debugger MCP server, which analyzes saved profiles and boots the WinUAE-derived PUAE core headlessly under Node for program injection, memory, screenshot and profiling workflows. Per-project MCP configuration keeps copyrighted Kickstart paths in user environments. The repository explicitly identifies the integrated emulator as PUAE/WinUAE-derived; this closes the relationship audit without treating those ancestors as duplicate tracker records. Evidence: https://github.com/grahambates/vscode-puae-debugger/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/grahambates/vscode-puae-debugger/blob/main/package.json https://github.com/grahambates/vscode-puae-debugger/commit/38cd4bbaa6ae0612b965947e0ba036904406b1ee

project.title: prog8
project.display_title: Prog8 — 6502 and 68000 development language
project.status: active; distributed compiler available while m68k remains experimental and gains Copperline/Vamos execution paths
project.notes: Structured low-level language/compiler for 6502-family computers and 68000, with experimental Amiga 500/1200 targets; README says the m68k targets are not yet production-ready. The current README documents official runnable compiler distributions, source builds and explicit 65xx/m68k output targets. IR format 8 now uses word-packed byte/bool/word argument slots and four-byte long/pointer/float slots across the experimental Amiga 500, Amiga 1200 and QEMU m68k targets. This does not promote the m68k targets to production-ready or establish target-machine RAM minima. Evidence: https://github.com/irmen/prog8/blob/master/README.md https://github.com/irmen/prog8/commit/0b902f06b55356b76b0c0f5fee5e207a87c33dfc The experimental Amiga 500/1200 targets now stage generated programs for a Copperline execution path under -emu, while -emu2 retains the headless Vamos path. The change does not make the m68k backend production-ready or establish minimum Amiga hardware. Evidence: https://github.com/irmen/prog8/commit/16f7d588a78042622eb00510d2847e8d2472a940

project.title: mz800emu
project.display_title: mz800emu — Sharp MZ-800/700/1500 emulator and debugger
project.status: active; current main completes hidden CPU/peripheral snapshot state and hardens debugger/MCP tracing
project.notes: Open-source Sharp MZ emulator with cycle-accurate Z80A execution, chip/peripheral emulation, a built-in debugger and an MCP bridge exposing screenshots, coverage, profiling and analysis controls. Primary docs provide Linux, Windows and macOS build paths; no minimum host CPU or RAM is stated. Claude client configuration documents a supported integration, not evidence that AI authored the project. Current main saves hidden Z80 MEMPTR, interrupt, EI-delay and T-state state plus CTC, scroll, VRAM-wait and floppy-controller state; it safely adapts RAMdisk/IDE8 snapshot loads. Debugger/MCP fixes expose all 532 expanded memory regions, keep debugger reads from firing guest watchpoints, correctly stop temporary run-to breakpoints and record the instruction bytes actually fetched by self-modifying code. Evidence: https://github.com/michalhucik/mz800emu/commit/1f477d90e2efd6808253c1c3d5f31fa56f465570 https://github.com/michalhucik/mz800emu/commit/a5726b9658d10b4412cf4a28bc212a78351f28a4

project.title: konCePCja
project.display_title: konCePCja — CPC/Plus emulator and IPC debugger
project.status: v6.4.2 published; protocol-v0 debugger and deterministic media-writeback/IPC regressions continue on main
project.notes: CPC/Plus and GX4000 emulator with sub-cycle hardware models, flux-image decoding, an integrated debugger and TCP/headless automation. Beyond v6.4.2, the new protocol-v0 binary frontend on port 6545 implements HELLO/PING/MACHINE_INFO, register and memory reads/writes, PAUSE/RUN/RESET/STEP control, run-state queries and subscribed pushed events. Its design includes a 4096-entry lock-free event ring and controller lease; reviewed commits add server skeleton, reads, writes/control and run/events in successive tested slices. These are upstream implementation receipts, not an independent run by the tracker. No minimum host CPU/RAM was stated.
