project.status: v2.1.1 published after full-script/MCP field testing on VICE 3.10; post-release media and snapshot safeguards continue on main
project.notes: General-purpose TypeScript C64 reverse-engineering toolkit controlling stock VICE and integrating disk/BASIC/static-analysis/assembly/equivalence workflows. package.json now declares 2.0.0 and publishable CLI/MCP/host bins, while the primary roadmap explicitly leaves npm trusted-publisher setup, the v2.0.0 tag and verification of the published package open. C64RT_TRACE adds per-process JSONL field traces for host requests, VICE lifecycle, MCP calls, native tool runs and stderr without exposing the trace to the agent. Node.js 24+, VICE 3.9+ and user-supplied ROMs remain prerequisites; no host CPU/RAM minimum or independent execution is established. Evidence: https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/blob/main/package.json https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/11987768d056 https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/5ceac29bb61b Current M14 work now generates byte-identical ACME source from an unpacked image or PRG, curated knowledge and Ghidra instructions; an optional loader is run in VICE and checked at the recovered entry state. The documented ten-stage workflow adds explicit acceptance criteria, exit checks, deliverables and coverage reporting. Release comparison can attach first-access/runtime-change evidence to differing bytes, single-release separation reports unpack/access/reachability provenance, and platform symbols can be exported as an ACME include. These are upstream live-tool checks rather than an independent tracker run, and they do not close the separate npm publication gate. Evidence: https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/8e2bbb5a106c2fe339bc2f1aaaa8d02b414a1341 https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/18bc1327744db353667cabf39d81ed373effe078 https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/b80796c63719f7eeb4fd694afd689fe5a926cd8b https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/1c0070e068b719314a4ee47b56de189916b0a6d6 https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/ad164faf2354087ee3c0f7bd8d9e52c36a367fbc M17 now captures CIA timer latches and interrupt masks that ordinary register reads cannot recover, programs generated loaders to restore the reachable timer state, and compares counters, latches, controls and masks at the entry jump. An upstream live test distinguishes the repaired loader from one without CIA restoration. The host also records each skill-script operation and outcome while keeping verbose MCP/VICE tracing opt-in. These are upstream tests; no local VICE run was performed, SID voice 3, TOD phase and interrupt flags remain documented limits, and the npm publication gate remains open. Evidence: https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/5cdc74d5226db7d8123ca782cfb6e9a36a11ee8b https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/15a3bb8f331d0fe8d81976400c04a4e632813b06 M23/M24 now let execution traces continue while recording observations/history, generate linked source maps and program reference pages, and route evidence-producing agent run files into owned run directories. The Bruce Lee acceptance reports 70 reference pages, 1,227 entries, 21 decoded tables and deterministic second-pass linking; these are upstream field-run receipts and do not close the separate npm publication gate. Evidence: https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/4c209ab6e79cbb0a34e3b818bf33d8b6fb92f0ba https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/7a45b671dc7b6efc1f0c6b905e57ae1839a8ce3a https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/9caaff4bf206b429d389fcdf5e94d42919600cd9 v2.1.1 closes the previously open publication gate and reports a real-project field pass covering every script command and MCP tool on VICE 3.10. It hardens JAM state, snapshot failures, drive-side stops, static/provenance analysis and preflight validation; current main additionally rejects malformed media before VICE can reinterpret it, stops an in-flight autostart before snapshot restore and exposes the documented $A000-$BFFF VICE memory-map flaw. These are upstream field and regression receipts, not a tracker-side VICE run. Evidence: https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/releases/tag/v2.1.1 https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/eb69c523cc34f88e9c2aa5e23f3139306ed6bb5b

project.notes: Emulates CPC 464/6128, Plus and GX4000 with per-model CRTC/Gate Array timing, disc and tape support, a debugger and embedded RASM. Inspected src/core includes Z80, CRTC variants and debugging code. README calls expansion hardware and UI work in progress; SHAKER compatibility is upstream's claim. v0.4.0 adds host-backed M4 TCP/DNS/server and plain-HTTP operations, a folder-backed FAT16 IDE/CF interface for SYMBiFACE II/III, and LambdaSpeak 3 Epson/DECtalk command handling using host voices. The release documents tests with Duke's TCP/telnet examples, SymbOS and LambdaSpeak software; these upstream compatibility claims were not independently reproduced. Evidence: https://github.com/WacKEDmaN/CPCSyntaxError/commit/c909c7f7e465dc54640248cbd91a4d78a1c45656 v0.5.0 adds guided and manual RAM cheats, CDT/TZX tape recording and turbo loading, HFE read/write, IPF read support, image writeback, a 300-rpm real-time floppy model, Multiface II, RS232C endpoints and folder-backed M4 DSK images. The bundled IPF decoder retains its non-commercial licence; upstream compatibility tests were not independently reproduced. Evidence: https://github.com/WacKEDmaN/CPCSyntaxError/commit/35ca66c5bb974eb0b1113e08980ea166cf93362a v0.6.0 adds successful CI builds and release assets for Windows x64, Linux x86-64 and universal macOS arm64/x86-64, plus monitor H/V hold controls and Compendium-backed CRTC sync timing. Upstream explicitly says the Linux and macOS packages were not yet desktop-tested. Evidence: https://github.com/WacKEDmaN/CPCSyntaxError/commit/2b74f27e5c466376321eb7aa6587d994e08a6670 https://github.com/WacKEDmaN/CPCSyntaxError/releases/tag/v0.6.0 https://github.com/WacKEDmaN/CPCSyntaxError/actions/runs/38114012270 v0.6.3 adds a CRT slot mask for colour monitors, scanlines for green/grey displays and controls for strength, stripe width and orientation. It also splits Media into Disc, Tape, Cartridge and Snapshot windows and keeps ROMs separate. Release assets remain Linux x86-64, macOS universal and Windows x64; no new minimum CPU/RAM claim follows from the packaging. Evidence: https://github.com/WacKEDmaN/CPCSyntaxError/releases/tag/v0.6.3 https://github.com/WacKEDmaN/CPCSyntaxError/commit/f87aa174c50c6bb56a2e8c3ca4b4ddbaa7650f4a The v0.6.5 development commit adds exact machine snapshots with instruction-stamped input replay, backward debugging and last-write lookup, a triggered one-microsecond logic analyser, raster-I/O overlay and fast-path optimizations. Upstream reports SHAKER's 2,166 screens remain byte-identical and CPC 6128 speed rises from 2.2x to 5.7x real time; unsupported expansion-card rewind and disk writes remain explicit limits. Evidence: https://github.com/WacKEDmaN/CPCSyntaxError/commit/4d4ada0808299b90dbb3fdc44bf70e9977dc7f4c v0.7.0 publishes Windows x64, Linux x86-64 and macOS universal packages and adds persistent nine-slot snapshots with undo, MJPEG/ZMBV/WAV recording at CPC cadence, a CALL/RST/interrupt profiler, graphics-memory inspection, model/locale-specific on-screen keyboards and configurable digital/Plus-analogue controllers. Publication does not establish a host CPU-generation or RAM minimum, and the tracker did not execute the packages. Evidence: https://github.com/WacKEDmaN/CPCSyntaxError/releases/tag/v0.7.0 https://github.com/WacKEDmaN/CPCSyntaxError/commit/51413b6986ff1793bc5b577a1069b3d7cd426b52

project.status: v8.4.0 published; development head adds authenticated local Windows IPC and repairs threaded JIT/reset behavior
project.notes: General-purpose UAE/WinUAE-derived Amiga machine emulator. v8.4.0 publishes Windows ARM64/x86-64, macOS universal and Linux ARM64/x86-64 assets, establishing upstream compilable and runnable variants without establishing minimum hardware. The release adds ZZ9000 AHI/SANA-II/SDK/MHI/MPEGA/image/ZZPlay support, optional external MiniGL and dma-buf paths, relative media paths, cartridge and .A1000 ROM handling, runtime GL fallback, Raspberry Pi 4 drawing improvements, ARM64 JIT fixes, FreeBSD amd64/aarch64 CI and broad networking/display/input/libretro/Android corrections. m68k remains the guest CPU; ARM/x86/RISC-V/LoongArch are host families, not guest minima. External Kickstart ROMs and game media remain outside the GPL source grant. No independent execution or equivalence test was performed. Evidence: https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/releases/tag/v8.4.0 https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/blob/master/README.md Post-v8.4.0 development fixes apply RetroArch auto-loaded save states only after the emulated CPU loop is active, correct CIA-B time-of-day increments in fast and programmed-sync paths, preserve open-file keys across host renames, honor cache-inhibited pages in 68030/68040/68060 fast-cache paths and restore USE_PPC=OFF linking. These are source-level fixes on current main, not a new published release or independently executed verification. Evidence: https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/71ac39e07d339d9d8e296e15db79642e6ab5619a https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/3b5e647578e667adff3a88ef9557e2f3702b8ebe https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/bdc870008140cff3dbbb4379df94aa92d7322e27 Current main ports WinUAE's optional loopback GDB remote server, disabled by default and unavailable with the threaded CPU, with m68k registers, physical RAM/ROM, stepping, breakpoints, watchpoints and memory-map support. A separate MacPorts integration covers Apple Silicon and x86 hosts and explicitly credits ChatGPT for substantial assistance; this extends the AI record without implying whole-project generation. Evidence: https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/4faddbe399757a663fb3f2e8dc4be678eda96d4d https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/831f13e71ee6e872d6d3570f2c23068493d0dd15 Development head now honors database-requested 68040 AGA configurations, disables cycle-exact mode when requested, aligns Android previews with the launched CPU/FPU configuration and follows with 68030 database handling. project.notes: Ambermoon v1.21 now ships AM2_CPU and the loader built from Jurie Horneman's original source plus restored missing kernel, 3D-renderer and music-player parts and subsequent fixes. The release fixes plain-68000 odd-size decompression and several memory, loader, conversation and gameplay faults; the tools release workflow publishes Windows, Linux and Amiga artifacts. These are upstream source-build/release claims, not an independent rebuild or byte comparison. Evidence: https://github.com/Pyrdacor/Ambermoon/commit/faca6448dea37b24d59a161d4680583822812d7b https://github.com/Pyrdacor/Ambermoon/releases/tag/game-v1.21 https://github.com/Pyrdacor/Ambermoon/releases/tag/tools-v1.18 The current release baseline is Ambermoon v1.22 and Tools v1.19. Development head adds the separately titled AmbermoonImageEditor paint program for PNG, BMP and Ambermoon Amiga graphics and wires it into the Windows, Linux and Amiga tool-package workflow. It remains a component of the repository's versioned Ambermoon tool suite rather than a separately released project, so no duplicate project record is added. Evidence: https://github.com/Pyrdacor/Ambermoon/releases/tag/game-v1.22 https://github.com/Pyrdacor/Ambermoon/releases/tag/tools-v1.19 https://github.com/Pyrdacor/Ambermoon/commit/ebaf2d63b05ee718b97a61f531a2c6c00857b399

project.display_title: 3Dvibe64 — Commodore 64 graphics engine SDK

runtime_profiles.name: Q8 accelerated-emulation qualification
runtime_profiles.notes: Upstream recommends Q8 only above 20 MHz. v1.8.0 reports Turbo6510 64 MHz measurements on public PAL cube scenes: Mode 2 precise/hybrid 23.70/25.05 FPS, Mode 5 27.00/27.45 FPS, and distant-cube Mode 7 standard/fast/fast+LOD 3.10/6.95/11.50 FPS. These are scene-specific emulator measurements, not minima, general guarantees or physical-hardware qualification. The v1.10.2 stable qualification additionally reports Mode 4 stock/turbo results of 0.649958/30.186113 FPS with defaults and 0.749952/38.484510 FPS with arithmetic, camera and visibility experiments; Mode 7 defaults report 0.044442/3.091013 FPS and arithmetic+UV 0.061107/3.703647 FPS. These remain emulator measurements, not physical-hardware or minimum-machine claims.

project.status: 1.12.0 source SDK published on main; source-only Windows/VICE qualification, with Linux and physical hardware still unverified
techniques: SID bank and zero-page wrapper generation
project.notes: Source SDK for eight C64 graphics modes: polygon rendering and a distinct Mode 8 2.5D DDA bitmap renderer. PowerShell/Python scene builders emit 6510/6502 assembly for 64tass. v1.8.0 adds opt-in gradual Mode 7 texture LOD, optional Q8 hybrid line rasterization for Modes 1/2/5 and safe presentation for Modes 1–7; legacy geometry, standard texture quality, precise raster and LOD-off remain defaults. Upstream reports all 22 public tests passing and bounded Turbo6510 64 MHz scene measurements, while explicitly stating that real hardware has not been tested. Code/data remain PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. Codex usage guides document downstream SDK use, not development-AI authorship of the engine. v1.9.0 adds an explicit experimental Normalized16 build and bounded signed-16 geometry generators while preserving the Q8 defaults unless the optional hook is selected. Native benchmark and qualification tooling are included; this does not change the recorded physical-hardware limitation. Evidence: https://github.com/Librologica/3Dvibe64/commit/562f3c314314abce8de7c30786843c2435b00e94 https://github.com/Librologica/3Dvibe64/commit/6ea4d7cf99513d9714407ea938aed06b8d55d4bc v1.10.2 promotes the qualified development line to a stable source SDK without changing default runtime options. Its optional Q8 arithmetic, UV, camera-table and visibility experiments remain disabled by default; upstream reports PAL-emulated Mode 4 and Mode 7 measurements, complete source/package regeneration gates and Windows/VICE qualification, while explicitly leaving Linux and physical hardware untested. Evidence: https://github.com/Librologica/3Dvibe64/releases/tag/v1.10.2 v1.11.0 packages 794 source files, 34 English/Italian manual pairs and 41 release gates, including 15 byte-identical checkpoint rebuilds. events.title: fix(core): the quit dialog also asks about an unsaved Symbiface IDE image (beads-nfz8) (#132)
events.message:
fix(core): the quit dialog also asks about an unsaved Symbiface IDE image (beads-nfz8) (#132)

* fix(core): the quit dialog also asks about an unsaved Symbiface IDE i…

…mage (beads-nfz8)

The quit dialog (native and ImGui) only looked at driveAltered(), so a
Symbiface II IDE image the CPC had written to was never mentioned, and
the ImGui "Quit anyway" wrote everything back although its text said the
changes would be lost.

The bridge now mirrors the board's IDE-dirty flag into an atomic at each
frame boundary (subcycle_bridge_ide_altered(), beside driveA.altered), so
the main thread never reads the board. A quit-only predicate,
quitLosesWrites(), counts it; the dialog text names the disc, the IDE
image or both (koncpc_quit_unsaved_message()). "Quit anyway" in either
dialog drops disc and IDE writes alike; every exit nobody was asked
about still writes both back. driveAltered() is unchanged and keeps
gating the reset and Options restart prompts.

events.title: WF1772IP: force interrupt from idle restarted the last command (#24)
events.message:
WF1772IP: force interrupt from idle restarted the last command (#24)

The IDLE state started a command on the bus write (CMD_WR) while the
command register still held the previous command. A force interrupt
written while idle therefore restarted the last command (after a reset a
restore with spin-up, busy until 6 index pulses), and the next command
was ignored. EmuTOS detects a drive with D0 + restore, so it found no
drive A: with "Real floppy drive as A:".

The fix is applied by tools/wf1772_ce.py (FIXES) before the clock enable
conversion; run_wf1772.sh compares against the original with the same
fix (--fix-only), works with the LLVM build of GHDL and checks a force
interrupt with no command running.

tests: add ImageInUseError to the fuse_mock driver_runtime stub

fuse_fs imports ImageInUseError from driver_runtime, but the fuse_mock
stub of amifuse.driver_runtime only defines BlockDeviceBackend. A test
that first imports amifuse.fuse_fs under the fixture fails with
"cannot import name 'ImageInUseError'". The full suite hides this
because other modules import fuse_fs during collection, but
test_fuse_stat_mode.py, test_status.py or a single fuse_fs test fails
when run on its own.

Add ImageInUseError to the stub as an OSError subclass, like the real
class. The real class cannot be re-exported from the fixture: some test
classes replace amitools and amitools.fs with mocks before fuse_mock
runs, so driver_runtime does not import there.

Fixes #102

software: Show the network stack in the system software overview

Add a Network row after Graphics. It names the running TCP/IP stack
from what it left in the library list, without opening
bsdsocket.library, which would start Roadshow or make Miami go online:

- Roadshow, TheWire13 and the UAE bsdsocket.library by their library ID
- Miami and MiamiDx by the version of the miami.library they create
- Genesis by its genesis.library over an AmiTCP kernel
- AmiTCP by its library ID

TheWire13's library ID carries the version of its bsdsocket.library,
which TheWire13 releases number separately (1.9.0 comes with 4.4.0),
so it is named as such: "TheWire13 (bsdsocket 4.4.0)".

Roadshow and TheWire13 keep bsdsocket.library in LIBS:. When no stack
runs, read that file and show the stack as not running, for example
"Roadshow 1.15 (not running)" or "TheWire13 (not running)". A string
that one read cuts off is carried over whole to the next. Skip the
check when every LIBS: directory is on a floppy.

The overview holds seven rows. Show Active ROM only when a ROM update
replaced the Kickstart, and let the overview scroll like the software
lists when a PPC board still adds an eighth row.

events.title: software: Show the Miami release from its program's $VER
events.message:
software: Show the Miami release from its program's $VER

Miami and MiamiDx were shown with their miami.library version, such
as "Miami (miami 15.0)", since neither library ID names the release.
Both programs build miami.library from an InitStruct table that points
the ID at a string in their own data hunk, and the release is in the
$VER in their code hunk: "Miami 3.2b", "MiamiDeluxe 1.0c".

Find the process whose program segments hold the ID string, a CLI's
command or the segment list in pr_SegList[3], and take the release
from that program's $VER. Show "Miami 3.2b" or "MiamiDx 1.0c", and the
library version as before when no program holds the ID. Only segments
that lie within one of Exec's memory regions are read, in Forbid().

Miami itself exits on this OS 3.2.3 test setup, so this was tested in
WinUAE with a program that lays out miami.library and its $VER the
same way, started with Run and from WBStartup.

events.title: fix(core): a walk that sees a breakpoint stop always finds its hit (beads-1meo) (#131)
events.message:
fix(core): a walk that sees a breakpoint stop always finds its hit (beads-1meo) (#131)

* fix(core): a walk that sees a breakpoint stop always finds its hit (b…

…eads-1meo)

step to onto a breakpoint of the caller's own at the target now and then
answered ERR 409 stopped-elsewhere with PC=target in its own trailer.

The walk learns of a stop two ways, without the pause mutex: the latched
hit and the announced stop. cpc_commit_breakpoint_stop() announced the
stop before it latched the hit, and the walk looked for the hit before it
looked at the announcement. A stop that became visible between the two
reads was taken for an arrival by PC with no hit; the IPC side tells an
arrival onto its own breakpoint by the hit it was handed, so it answered
stopped-elsewhere.

Latch the hit before the announcement, and read the announcement before
looking for the hit, so a stop the walk sees always comes with its hit.

events.message:
fix(sdisc): save, load and clear act on the disc the CPC is using (beads-mtfy) (#130)

* fix(sdisc): save, load and clear act on the disc the CPC is using (be…

…ads-mtfy)

The board keeps the Silicon Disc in its own expansion RAM (banks 4-7).
g_silicon_disc.data is only what a build loads and what a rebuild copies
back, but the IPC `sdisc save|load|clear` and the DevTools Silicon Disc
window worked on that buffer alone: a save wrote what the disc held at the
last rebuild, and a load or clear never reached the running CPC (and was
overwritten by the board's copy at the next rebuild).

subcycle_bridge_silicon_disc_copy_out()/copy_in() now address the disc the
CPC sees: the board's banks while it has one fitted, else the host buffer.
The IPC commands and the DevTools window call them with the machine held
still and alone (a pause lease, change_alone), and read or write the file
outside the lease. Nothing is added per frame.

test_sdisc_commands_reach_the_running_machine: a Z80 program writes bank 4
and another reads bank 5 through the real banking; on master the save holds
0000 where the CPC wrote 5AA5, and after a load the CPC reads 0000, not 3CC3.

events.title: fix(ipc): the frame-step counter has an owner; a second starter is refused (beads-y3tm) (#129)
events.message:
fix(ipc): the frame-step counter has an owner; a second starter is refused (beads-y3tm) (#129)

* fix(ipc): the frame-step counter has an owner; a second starter is re…

…fused (beads-y3tm)

There is one frame-step counter, shared by the text IPC (step frame,
wait vbl, a key tap's hold, frames dump) and KCPC's STEP frames. Arming
it was a blind store, so a text command sent during a KCPC frame step
replaced the count and the KCPC step ended when the text one did.

arm_frame_step() is now a claim: under a small owner mutex it refuses
(returns 0) while a step runs, else returns the new step's ticket.
Waiters wait on their own ticket and cancel only their own step, so a
waiter whose step just ended can no longer wait on, or disarm, the next
owner's. The text IPC answers ERR 409 frame-step-busy; KCPC answers BUSY.

events.title: grm-q4ga: a call cannot return into base bytes its bank does not hold; read the switched-in copy's table
events.message:
grm-q4ga: a call cannot return into base bytes its bank does not hold; read the switched-in copy's table

deadly_towers' last lone BRK (PRG_ALL_B2::85a9) came from bank-0 code at
847e: LDA #3 / JSR $fc2a / JSR $86c5 / JMP $85a9. fc2a switches the
32KB window to bank 2 and dispatches through a table, and every bank-2
handler returns through fc54, which stores bank 0 before its RTS. The
engine cannot see that restore, so bank 2 flowed into the JSR's
fall-through, and every later base reference was retargeted into bank 2.

1. BankDataflowEngine.returnsElsewhere: a call's base-space fall-through
   is reached by RTS, which lands on whatever the live bank holds there.
   mapsElsewhere's same-window exemption is right for sequential flow,
   but not for a return. When the state pins the window to an occupant
   whose bytes at the fall-through differ from the base instruction's,
   that state cannot hold there. The edge is kept but its state is
   forgotten. Dropping the edge instead left everything after a far call
   unvisited (instrs.inOverlay 4549 -> 1393). Byte-identical copies (code
   duplicated in every bank) still keep the state.

2. That bug had been how deadly_towers reached its banks. Base JSR $fc15
   sites, carrying a wrong bank-N state from the previous far call, were
   retargeted into the overlay copies PRG_ALL_Bn::fc15, which read their
   own bank's table. With the state fixed, the base trampolines read the
   tables themselves, and JumpTableBoundAnalyzer's cross-bank refit
   (grm-pwuh) declined them. It re-read the BASE routine's operand
   ($8000) in the switched-in bank, while each bank's copy reads its own
   table (bank 2: LDA $8035,X). New BankContext.switchedInCopyTableShift
   walks the run's indexed table loads beside the copy's
   pseudo-disassembled bytes and returns the operand shift when every
   pair agrees. crossBankTable reads the table there, and the load tables
   the extent rules measure against move with it. Base fc27/fc3c/fc51 now
   resolve to bank 1/2/3's real handlers (fc3c: 6, the grm-0pen count).

deadly_towers, checked against the ROM and an InstructionCensus A/B with
HEAD:
  - B2::85a9 gone; 8484/84b2 JMP $85a9 keep only the base ref (RTS).
  - Overlay BRKs 113 -> 1. Interior-target warnings 33 sites -> 5 (the 5
    were present before: wrong-bank decompiler reads left beside a
    cross-bank pin).
  - 863 overlay instructions lost, 58 gained. Every lost run checked was
    reached only by the bug or by garbage: B1::fc15/fea8 and B2::fda4
    from base calls under the wrong state; B1::fcfa (reset copy) only
    from COMPUTED_JUMPs out of garbage BRKs; B1::8818 and B1::86c5 are
    bank-0 subroutines decoded over bank-1 data (SBC/ORA runs). The gains
    are bank-1/3 handlers named by the now-correct tables.

nesintrawintest: the fixture switched its own window to bank 2, then
expected bank 2 to persist at 8008 after JSR $8010, while bank 2 held 00
there (the RTS lands on a BRK). Bank 2 now carries the same window code,
as a real ROM would; $8010 still differs, which is what the fixture
tests. All its criteria pass; golden re-blessed for the new ROM identity
plus bank 2's now-real JMP $800B.

Gates: build-and-test check SUITE OK. realrom check nes: 34 pass,
deadly_towers blessed below (genuine diff, 0/3 solo reruns match the old
golden; two full runs give identical dumps). CrossBankJumpTableProgramTest
gains 4 tests (shift, disagreeing loads, analyzer follows the copy,
returnsElsewhere).

  deadly_towers: refs.intoOverlay.retargeted 529 -> 55, refs.intoOverlay.intraOverlay 1578 -> 1171, instrs.inOverlay 4549 -> 3744, bankComments 199 -> 186, symbols 260 -> 223

events.title: test(kcpc): a controller gives control back before it closes (beads-5t1v) (#128)
events.message:
test(kcpc): a controller gives control back before it closes (beads-5t1v) (#128)

* test(kcpc): a controller gives control back before it closes (beads-5…

…t1v)

controller() in test_kcpc.py closed its socket and the next controller()
sent HELLO at once. The server frees control when the old connection's
reader reads EOF, but that EOF and the new connection's HELLO reach two
different reader threads with nothing ordering them, so the HELLO could
win and be made an observer: "control was not free" (seen once in
test_subscribers_do_not_change_what_the_machine_computes under -H).

The server cannot do better: a close is not a message it can answer.
CONTROL release is, and its reply comes after control is free. The
helper's client now sends it on leaving its with-block (unless the test
closed the connection itself or the core ended it), so the next
controller() always finds control free. No polling.

test_each_controller_finds_control_free opens 200 controllers back to
back on one core.

* test(kcpc): a core that quit may abort the release on Windows (beads-…

…5t1v)

Windows reports a send or read on a connection the quitting core dropped
as ConnectionAbortedError (WinError 10053), which the helper did not
catch: MSVC UI-free failed test_quit_during_a_walk and
test_chip_get_matches_the_text_ipc. Catch ConnectionError, the base of
the broken-pipe, reset and aborted errors.

A restore right after c64_autostart was overwritten when the autostart went on. A broken .crt or .t64 loaded as a PRG and reported success. events.title: test(rom): wait for the IPC server's port instead of a fixed 200 ms (beads-00tl) (#126)
events.message:
test(rom): wait for the IPC server's port instead of a fixed 200 ms (beads-00tl) (#126)

* test(rom): wait for the IPC server's port instead of a fixed 200 ms (…

…beads-00tl)

RomSlotsTest started its IPC server and slept 200 ms, and send_command
read port() once before its connect retries.  On the MSVC Win32 runners
the listener has taken longer than 200 ms to bind (run 38255585417:
the first test ran at 32.396, "IPC: listening on port 6543" at 32.408),
so the first shuffled test read port 0 and spent its whole 1 s budget
connecting to port 0.

The suite and send_command now wait for port() > 0 (up to 10 s), the
way IpcServerTest's fixture already does.  A new test sends a command
the moment a fresh server is started; it fails on master.

project.notes: Identity: Binary patch and link-time override layer that adapts the stock Amiga UNIX SVR4 2.1c kernel from its original 68020/68030 MMU assumptions to 68040/68060 processors. The substantial assembly implements page-table/HAT translation, exception and cache handling, boot/runtime changes and support glue; this is not a complete recovered kernel distribution. Classification: Inspected actual HAT assembly with original addresses and documented 030-to-040 descriptor conversions. Extensive diagnostic/test and contract documentation; hardware acceptance claims are upstream reports only. MIT for new code/modifications. Original AMIX is proprietary and supplied by user. Motorola packages retain separate terms and NetBSD-derived algorithms BSD notices. Source explicitly acknowledges identical one-line vendor ABI macros. Source CPU: Original binary input is AMIX for 68020/68030. Target CPU: Native output is AMIX kernel for 68040/68060, including LC060 support; build host is Linux. Build: Linux shell orchestration requires a repaired m68k-cbm-sysv4 cross toolchain, GNU m68k tools, licensed stand/unix input and checksum-pinned NetBSD 10.1 source tarball. No build performed; all build/runtime/byte-exact flags remain unknown. No candidate software was compiled or executed; build/run/play/byte-identity flags remain unknown. Runtime profiles: Upstream reports real A3000 040/060 boot-to-login, X11/RTG and network operation; experimental preservation work, not production-supported. Large native 68020 assembly implementation includes Z80 execution, VDP timing/sprites, cartridge mappers, FM sound, menus and save support. Classification: Actual main assembler documents Z80 cycles, PAL/NTSC scanline timing, V9958 behaviour, mapper handling and split sprite snapshots. Generic multisystem emulator, not a game-specific CPU wrapper. No broad main-code license found. README says original author granted community-update permission; that is not an OSI license. emu2413 FM instrument data carries separate MIT terms; system ROM/data rights distinct. Source CPU: Emulated input machine is Z80 MSX family, not m68k; m68k is implementation/output CPU. Target CPU: Native assembler minimum 68020, practical baseline documented 68030/50. Build: vasm2.0f+ Motorola assembler; build.sh uses Devpac-compatible m68020 Hunk executable output and a configurable Windows vasm path. Release/test scripts use WinUAE. No build performed; all build/runtime/byte-exact flags remain unknown. No candidate software was compiled or executed; build/run/play/byte-identity flags remain unknown. Runtime profiles: Beta release. Low-end goal 68030/50 with fast RAM; faster accelerators support FM/60Hz modes. Upstream WinUAE/openMSX regressions not run. events.message:
測定: l4-t4 追補2・3 の結果（USR の数値の引数の置き場と戻り値）と期待値

公式ROMで追補2 15腕・追補3 3腕（＋較正）各2走、全走が関門通過・2走一致。USR の入口で自作の機械語が RAM を走査した。
入口 HL は型によらず同じ番地。整数・単精度の引数は HL+0（2B・4B）、倍精度は HL−4 から8B。
12345 系・23456 系・25000 系で同じ番地に1件（整数 12345 だけは ASCII 一致で多数→追補3で 25000 に替えて確定）。
置き場を書き換えて RET すると USR の戻り値がその値になる（整数・単・倍）。戻り型は渡した型と同じ。文字列は DE が記述子。
追補1で HL±32 に見つからなかったのは、戻ったあとに照合したため（戻った後の評価で上書き）と整合する。
期待値 tests/conformance/expected_l4_mlcall_usrarg.tsv（18腕）。公式自身 18/18、現行の自作は 2/18（較正のみ）。

project.status: v8.4.0 published; development head expands the WinUAE-derived remote GDB monitor and debugging surface
project.notes: General-purpose UAE/WinUAE-derived Amiga machine emulator. v8.4.0 publishes Windows ARM64/x86-64, macOS universal and Linux ARM64/x86-64 assets, establishing upstream compilable and runnable variants without establishing minimum hardware. The release adds ZZ9000 AHI/SANA-II/SDK/MHI/MPEGA/image/ZZPlay support, optional external MiniGL and dma-buf paths, relative media paths, cartridge and .A1000 ROM handling, runtime GL fallback, Raspberry Pi 4 drawing improvements, ARM64 JIT fixes, FreeBSD amd64/aarch64 CI and broad networking/display/input/libretro/Android corrections. m68k remains the guest CPU; ARM/x86/RISC-V/LoongArch are host families, not guest minima. External Kickstart ROMs and game media remain outside the GPL source grant. No independent execution or equivalence test was performed. Evidence: https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/releases/tag/v8.4.0 https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/blob/master/README.md Post-v8.4.0 development fixes apply RetroArch auto-loaded save states only after the emulated CPU loop is active, correct CIA-B time-of-day increments in fast and programmed-sync paths, preserve open-file keys across host renames, honor cache-inhibited pages in 68030/68040/68060 fast-cache paths and restore USE_PPC=OFF linking. These are source-level fixes on current main, not a new published release or independently executed verification. Evidence: https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/71ac39e07d339d9d8e296e15db79642e6ab5619a https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/3b5e647578e667adff3a88ef9557e2f3702b8ebe https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/bdc870008140cff3dbbb4379df94aa92d7322e27 Current main ports WinUAE's optional loopback GDB remote server, disabled by default and unavailable with the threaded CPU, with m68k registers, physical RAM/ROM, stepping, breakpoints, watchpoints and memory-map support. A separate MacPorts integration covers Apple Silicon and x86 hosts and explicitly credits ChatGPT for substantial assistance; this extends the AI record without implying whole-project generation. Evidence: https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/4faddbe399757a663fb3f2e8dc4be678eda96d4d https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/831f13e71ee6e872d6d3570f2c23068493d0dd15 Development head now honors database-requested 68040 AGA configurations, disables cycle-exact mode when requested, aligns Android previews with the launched CPU/FPU configuration and follows with 68030 database handling. IPC was redesigned to keep up to 16 clients across frames, bound per-frame work, cap requests at 64 KiB and queue replies without blocking the emulation thread. These guest CPU selections are emulated configurations, not Amiberry host target CPUs or minimum machines. No tracker-side WHDLoad or IPC run was performed. Evidence: https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/5dc6c79f956b4a76b793cbc957242cb65345fed7 https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/69b4be8173 https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/2685d3e774cbdd3c99db0cee66aa6836642ed36c Development head ports WinUAE monitor extensions for AmigaDOS entry stops, Exec task controls, exceptions, DMA/range watchpoints, guest diagnostics, input, screenshots and frame checkpoints. Follow-up fixes bound replies, preserve resets, report checkpoint write failures and safely disassemble at memory-bank ends. This is source-level development evidence, not a new v8.4.0 release or an independent run. Evidence: https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/42335beeafe955c81df4dec31dd508867a6b3b4d

事前登録追補: l4-t4 追補2 — USR の数値の引数の置き場を入口で走査する

追補1は USR から戻ったあとに BASIC で HL±32 を PEEK しており、引数の作業域は戻ったあとの評価で

件数と最初の4件の番地、入口 HL との差を記録する。引数は式（12000+345 等）で作り本文・変数に値を出さない。

資料（マニュアル類）は読まず、置き場は測定だけで決める（引数の受け渡しの説明は作業域の番地＝(b) を含みうるため）。

events.title: fix(cpu): stop keyboard reset racing the multithreaded CPU (#2470)
events.message:
fix(cpu): stop keyboard reset racing the multithreaded CPU (#2470)

A keyboard reset (Ctrl+Amiga+Amiga) ran custom_reset() on the main thread
while the CPU thread kept running 68k code, so the chipset and the autoconfig
state were reset under a running CPU. With the multithreaded CPU and a hard
drive, repeated keyboard resets during boot crashed Amiberry (segfaults in
expamem_map_filesys(), the JIT and the UAE boot ROM), and runs that did not
crash logged CPU halts.

- cpu_keyboard_reset() replaces the custom_reset() and cpu_inreset() pairs in
  the keyboard reset code. While the CPU thread runs, it only records the
  request and raises SPCFLAG_CPUINRESET.
- The CPU thread starts the chipset reset from its reset hold through the
  existing custom_reset_cpu() handshake, so the main thread resets the
  chipset while the CPU thread waits.
- The deferred chipset reset keeps the keyboard reset sequence, which
  custom_reset() would clear, so releasing the keys still resets the machine.
- On key release, the full reset in m68k_go() runs after the CPU thread has
  stopped, instead of an extra chipset reset under the running CPU thread.
- A full CPU reset drops a request that the CPU thread did not take.

The non-threaded CPU keeps its existing behavior.

events.title: 測定: l4-t4 第1回＋追補1 の結果（CALL・USR・VARPTR・BSAVE・BLOAD）と期待値
events.message:
測定: l4-t4 第1回＋追補1 の結果（CALL・USR・VARPTR・BSAVE・BLOAD）と期待値

公式ROMで第1回 66腕・追補1 31腕、各2走。不明3腕（CALL -1・65535・未定義変数＝制御が戻らない）以外は関門通過。
CALL は変数番地だけ実行（定数は ERR 2）、レジスタ破壊後も復帰、49152.4 は丸めて実行、65536 は ERR 6、文字列は ERR 13。
引数つきは HL が第1引数の値、DE が第2引数（文字列なら記述子）を指す。
USR は入口 A が型（整数02・単04・倍08・字03）、文字列は DE が記述子。USR10 は ERR 2、未定義の番号は ERR 5。
数値の引数 12345 は HL/DE/BC の ±32 に無く、置き場は追補2で測る。
VARPTR は負の値（番地 0x8000 以上）で、格納形式は既知の符号化と一致、x% と y% の番地差は 6、未定義変数は ERR 5。
BSAVE は種別 0x01、本体の先頭に開始番地・終了番地+1（各2B下位先）、4バイト目から中身。BLOAD は既定・再配置・,R が成立。
誤り: ファイル無し 53、長さ0 5、長さ省略 2、bload 単独 22、ドライブ9 70、文字列番地 13。
第1回の bsave は両ドライブを空データディスクにしたため全腕 ERR 33 で無効（追補1で構成を直した）。
期待値 tests/conformance/expected_l4_mlcall.tsv（61腕）・expected_l4_bsave.tsv（14腕）。公式自身 61/61・14/14、現行の自作は 19/61・4/14。

events.title: Phase 240: the A4000's memory map and the AGA palette - v0.11.97
events.message:
Phase 240: the A4000's memory map and the AGA palette - v0.11.97

The emulated machine now has the reference's memory: 2 MB chip RAM at 0,
8 MB 32-bit motherboard fast RAM ending at $08000000 (priority 30,
"expansion memory") and 16 MB Zorro III RAM at $40000000 (priority 20).
Both fast regions carry their MemHeader at their start, as AddMemList()
lays them out (SysInfo: lower bound $07800020; BlitzBasic2 "Largest Mem"
16383K as on 3.1).  Programs, stacks and AllocMem() memory lie above the
ROM as on the reference.

Host: lxa_memmap.h holds the RAM regions and lxa_ram_ptr()/lxa_ram_avail()
for every host access to emulated RAM (display planes, DOS buffers,
relay strings, BltClear, copper, coverage bitmap).  The Zorro II space
above chip RAM is empty.  exec's RemTask() validates task pointers with
TypeOfMem() instead of a 24-bit range.

DisplayInfo: every mode has the 24-bit AGA palette (PaletteRange 65535,
8 bits per gun; probe graphics/modedb extended and re-captured; DPaint
shows "256 of 16777216" and "[8:8:8]").  ModeNotAvailable() is complete
for the AGA machine (no DI_AVAIL_NOCHIPS case).

Fish Password loop no longer takes the stack-overflow path (removed from
MEMORY_DEPENDENT); Fish Window calls through the vector at $100 and is
memory-dependent.  The expansion tests keep their Zorro II board images in
chip RAM (expansion.library reads boards above 16 MB as Zorro III).

Goldens re-promoted: SysInfo (gadget flags now match), BlitzBasic2 (memory
ignore region gone), DirectoryOpus (status line shows CHIP/FAST/TOTAL;
amounts and clock owned by Phase 264), DPaintV (ShowSelected string and
History widths owned by Phase 256).

docs: record the reference authoring — sheet §2 delivered

The sheet's §2 becomes the delivered record in its own convention: status, what was
built and what the gate asserts. It also loses the claim that the instruction table
holds 233 mnemonics — it holds 123, and the TOS table 111, which is what the counts
in the new text use.

README names the two fields in the reference bullet; ARCHITECTURE's `ui/` row says
the dock shows them; AGENTS gains a lookup row for the reference itself (the tables,
their dock and their authoring gate) and lists `tst_reference` among the suites; PLAN
§6 records the feature as delivered and §9 the finding behind it — an example is a
sentence about the assembler, so the assembler is what decides whether it is true,
and 234 of them cost half a second to check.

events.title: editor: give the reference an example and a typical use for every entry
events.message:
editor: give the reference an example and a typical use for every entry

Sheet §2 (docs/glm-features.md), re-scoped 2026-10-17 to the reference itself:
`Used in:` went with the teaching layer's rethink, so the two fields that remain
are the ones that stand on their own.

`InstructionInfo` and `OsCallInfo` gain `example` and `typicalUse`, both last in
the struct with default member initializers so the tables' existing brace lists
keep compiling (PLAN §11). The dock renders both under the summary and flags.

The authoring rule is mechanical rather than aspirational, and `tst_reference` is
where it lives: every entry of both tables carries both fields; every example
assembles under vasm inside the one wrapper the test documents (`start`, `msg` and
`buffer` are the only context an example may assume, so a fragment that drifts
out of the assembler's grammar fails the suite rather than shipping as prose); an
instruction's example starts with the mnemonic it belongs to and a call's makes
that call's own trap; and a `typicalUse` is one line, at most 120 characters,
ending in a full stop. The gate reports every unfinished entry at once, because
the list of them is what the authoring work is done from.

Authored in two passes over the tables: 123 instructions and 111 calls. Each
example was assembled by the same vasm invocation the test runs before it was
committed.

events.title: RTG display database: uaegfx modes, monitors and BestModeIDA (Phase 241) - v0.12.0
events.message:
RTG display database: uaegfx modes, monitors and BestModeIDA (Phase 241) - v0.12.0

With RTG enabled (LXA_RTG=1, lxa --rtg, lxa_config_t.rtg) the display
database lists the 57 modes of an emulated Picasso96 uaegfx board after
the native ones, with DisplayInfo/DimensionInfo/MonitorInfo/NameInfo,
ModeNotAvailable, FindDisplayInfo, OpenMonitor and one MonitorSpec per
resolution in MonitorList, all equal to the rtg reference profile
(tests/probes/rtg/modes, golden captured with lxaprobe).  The host owns
the RTG mode table (src/lxa/lxa_rtg.c, EMU_CALL_GFX_RTG); the ROM only
hooks the display-database entry points.  suite-ref runs probes marked
'rdd: profile rtg' on the rtg reference profile.

Also fixes two GCC 16 warnings (const strchr result, unused variable).

events.title: docs: scope sheet §2 to the reference itself — Example and Typical use, no Used in
events.message:
docs: scope sheet §2 to the reference itself — Example and Typical use, no Used in

Decided 2026-10-17: the `Used in:` cross-link is dropped, because it only means
something if there is a teaching layer and the teaching layer is going back for a
rethink. The other two fields stay, and with them §2's dependency on `lessons/`
goes: the reference should say what an instruction is *for* and show it, whether
or not anything teaches it.

The section is renamed from "L4 reference authoring" to "Reference authoring" —
L4 named a level of the teaching layer, which is exactly what it no longer has
anything to do with — and the same name is used in PLAN's feature list and the
README's index. The "Never state a wrong thing to be complete" discipline is
rewritten for the two fields that remain: `flags`' rule (say nothing rather than
something wrong) governs them too, and an empty `Typical use` is a fact the test
records rather than a gap to fill with filler. §2 is now unblocked: PLAN's scope
note no longer waits on the teaching-layer PR.

Phase 240: the FPU starts in its reset (null) state - v0.11.96

As on the reference 68040 a task that has not used the FPU finds it in
the null state (FSAVE frame 0) and after FPU instructions in the 68040
IDLE state (0x41000000); probe exec/fpu checks both.  SIGMAth2, whose
ButtonClickInteraction corrupted the free list with null frames on the
68882 frames of Phase 237e, passes with the 68040 frames.  FSAVE and
FRESTORE accept all control addressing modes ((An), (d16,An),
(d8,An,Xn), absolute) instead of stopping the emulator.

events.title: spec 914 D5: sources of different dialects build together
events.message:
spec 914 D5: sources of different dialects build together

assemble_source takes units: each is built by its own assembler, in dependency order (uses); what a
unit defines is read back from its label table (64tass -l, KickAssembler -symbolfile) into one neutral
list (name, address, scope) and handed to the units that use it as equates in THEIR dialect, through a
wrapper that includes the equates before the unit's own file. No source is translated or edited; a
foreign unit is registered with its dialect and its sha256 is checked unchanged after the build. A
label a unit uses that none of its uses exports, and a circle of uses, are refused by name.

An explicit C64RE_64TASS_BIN / C64RE_KICKASS_JAR is a pin: that file or none, instead of quietly
building with another one.

events.title: spec 914 D2-D4, D6: one resolver, one listing lookup, the proof on the record, no default dialect
events.message:
spec 914 D2-D4, D6: one resolver, one listing lookup, the proof on the record, no default dialect

D2  resolveDialect(): the call's assembler=, the file's record, the project's preference; nothing else.
    disasm, disasm_prg, disasm_raw, run_prg_reverse_workflow, run_payload_reverse_workflow and
    disasm_menu take assembler=; a dialect the call names is remembered on the file's record.
D3  listingFor(): one lookup for the listing of some bytes (record first, the names the renderer has
    always used for a project that never registered it); the "Run disasm" task names the bytes
    (listing-exists), the annotation status reads either comment syntax, the status table, the index
    walker (walkAsm is gone), list_artifacts, prompts, steering and doctrine say "the listing".
D4  the rebuild proof assembles with the assembler the listing is written for (no silent fallback; a
    missing one is said by name), writes the verdict onto the listing's record with the listing's hash,
    and stamps the head in the listing's own comment syntax. The temp PRG is named from the stem.
D6  there is no default dialect: project_init and agent_onboard require the choice, an old project is
    asked at its next agent_onboard, a render that resolves to nothing is refused naming how to set it.

The existing scripts name a dialect in their fixtures; the ones that compare both dialects of one set
of bytes render twice.

Document the call contract in every skill, and test that docs and scripts agree

Every SKILL.md with scripts has one Calling the script section and one
Project folder section, word for word. The docs name the new commands,
options, ranges, step forms, result shapes, exit codes and errors. Fixes:
coverage evidence names the map by its path at the import, c64-source writes
l_17e2, static-analysis hands source generation to c64-source, type and press
behave as written in recordings and scenarios, the emulator remedy names the

(one JSON error, exit 2, nothing on stderr), finds bare throws in all code
that a script reaches, keeps the shared sections identical, and checks every
command and option that a SKILL.md names. The bare throws left in that code

events.title: docs: restore the sheet's feature sections, and say how they were lost
events.message:
docs: restore the sheet's feature sections, and say how they were lost

`docs/glm-features.md` lost sections 2 to 6 in one edit: the change that recorded
sheet §6 as delivered searched for the first "### How to start" in the file, and
§1 has one — so everything after it was cut, and the result was committed and
merged before anyone counted the headings.

The file is restored from the commit before that edit and the §6 record is
reapplied with the search scoped inside §6. All six sections and their statuses
are back, including the two features this branch had already delivered.

The trap is general enough to be a rule (PLAN §11): these documents repeat their
headings by design — one "How to start", "What exists" and "Tested" per feature —
so a rewrite must anchor inside the section it is rewriting, and the only cheap
check afterwards is counting the headings.

presses again at the same read. c64run registers SHIFT alone and the up arrow,
and speaks protocol 2.

fix(core): exit puts a zipped disc's written-back DSK on the Recent list (beads-8c1o) (#127)

* fix(core): exit puts a zipped disc's written-back DSK on the Recent l…

…ist (beads-8c1o)

A GUI exit with code 0 saved the config in cleanExit() before
doCleanUp() stopped the runner and wrote the discs back. A disc read
from a .zip is written to a DSK beside the archive and that DSK is
staged for the Recent list, as on an eject; at exit nothing applied the
entry after the save, so Recent kept the archive.

doCleanUp() now saves the config itself, after the write-back, and
applies the staged Recent entries first. Which exits save and which
write back is unchanged.

events.title: ui: edit a floppy image's own contents — Delete, Rename and New Folder in the pane
events.message:
ui: edit a floppy image's own contents — Delete, Rename and New Folder in the pane

Sheet §6 (docs/glm-features.md). The whole-file primitive was already there
(`floppy::updateImage`); the pane's menu stopped at Copy/Cut/Paste, so an entry
inside a disk could not be dropped, renamed, or organised into a folder without
copying it out and rebuilding the disk by hand.

Three operations on `floppy::Transfer`, beside the transfers it already owns and
behind the same confirm/resync preamble:

- `removeEntries()` is the `removals` argument alone; a chosen folder takes its
  subtree, which is the writer's own rule for a removal.
- `renameEntry()` reads the entry out and re-adds it under the new root in the
  *same* `updateImage` call that drops the old paths — one atomic rebuild, so a
  folder and its contents move together and a failure leaves the disk as it was.
  Renaming to the name it already has is nothing to do rather than a collision.
- `makeDirectory()` adds an `isDirectory` item with no contents.

Two decisions worth keeping. A name the disk already shows is refused, not
numbered: `updateImage` numbers a colliding addition, which is what makes a paste
never overwrite and is exactly the wrong answer for a rename, which would
silently become NAME(2) while the pane showed what was asked for. The comparison
is the display spelling the pane shows — the 8.3 conversion is internal to the
writer — so an entry whose stored name field differs from its display name can
still collide, and that is documented at the function rather than left to be
found. And the listing is taken *after* the confirm question, never before,
because `confirmTargets` re-reads the drives once every question has been
answered: a directory listed earlier can already be stale.

The menu (`FileBrowser::onFloppyContextMenu`) gains Delete… / Rename… / New
Folder…: Delete and Rename need a selection, Rename needs exactly one entry
(renaming a set is not something a pane can mean), and New Folder lands in the
directory that was clicked, exactly as Paste does. Delete asks first; Rename and
New Folder take their name from a dialog that refuses an empty name or one
containing "/", because the controller answers a bad name with a silent Invalid.

tst_gui asserts the image rather than the rows: delete removes both the pane's
row and the `listRaw` entry, rename moves both and `readFileRaw` still returns
the bytes the entry was written with, New Folder exists as a directory in
`listRaw`, and both refusals leave the image byte-identical.

events.title: spec 914 D1: the renderer builds a listing structure, one emitter per dialect writes it
events.message:
spec 914 D1: the renderer builds a listing structure, one emitter per dialect writes it

The renderer used to build KickAssembler text and a second pass pattern-converted it into
64tass. It now builds ListingLine records (label, instruction with operand, data directive,
comment, equate, relocation block) and emitListing writes them in one dialect: a render writes
exactly ONE file. convertKickAsmToTass is gone. disasm-prg/disasm-raw take --dialect (else the
output name decides: .asm KickAssembler, .tas/.tass 64tass; a name that says neither is refused);
disasm-menu gains 64tass through the same structure. The equate/undefined-symbol backstops scan
the structure instead of the finished text.

Checked against the old pipeline on 342 real invocations of the existing e2e corpus: the
KickAssembler text is identical, the 64tass text identical once comments are set aside.

events.title: debug: watchpoints that are named, not addresses
events.message:
debug: watchpoints that are named, not addresses

Sheet §5 (docs/glm-features.md). A watchpoint could only be a raw address, and
GEMDOS picks the load address afresh on every run — the interface a breakpoint
got, the watchpoint never did. It can now be asked for by label:

- `Watchpoint` carries the `symbol` it was asked for by and a `resolved` flag.
  `label()` names what was asked for (`watch counter.l`), and the *stored*
  watchpoint never keeps a resolved address: the resolved copy the panel is
  handed for a run has it, so the address a previous run worked out has nowhere
  to live — the failure the sheet called the most confidently-wrong panel in the
  IDE.
- `planWatchpoints()`, beside `planBreakpoints()`, resolves a name through
  `labelAddress()` — the one rule a hook script's `sym()` and the remote
  `breakpoint <label>` verb already use — afresh at every arm, after `info
  basepage` has delivered the live bases. A named watchpoint is therefore pending
  until then, and a pre-bases arm skips it rather than arming `$0` (the vector
  table, which would fire at once); a raw address still arms before the program
  has loaded, because an address means the same thing either way.
- Run ▸ Add watchpoint takes `label|address` with an optional `.b`/`.w`/`.l`.
  The remote verbs are the set/clear pair `watchpoint <a|l>` — which now answers
  with what it watches and where it landed — and `clearwatchpoint [a|l]`, never a
  toggle; the MCP tools follow, `pist_watchpoint` taking `address` or `label` and
  `pist_clearwatchpoint` marked destructive with the other state-rewriting calls.
- A name that resolves to nothing, to an equate, to a symbol with no source
  position or to one that emits nothing is refused naming it and saying which of
  those it is. A name the build has wins over a token that merely looks like hex,
  so `watch deadbeef` watches the label when the program has one.

tst_debug pins the plan with no emulator; tst_gui the text form, the refusals,
the pending panel row and the clear counts; tst_remotecontrol the verb's replies;
tst_mcp the two tools and the whole catalog. tst_emulatorhost proves the label
path against the machine: the plan resolves `val2` through the build's symbols
and the session's own live bases to the address the program's data really has,
and that command is what stops the run.

Three things were found by running rather than reading (PLAN §9): the label
alternative of the width-suffix regex was greedy and swallowed `.w`/`.l`, so
`counter.l` resolved as a name that does not exist; a single-line reply's text is
an interface, and two existing tests had pinned `ok` exactly; and a two-argument
`QString::arg(QString, QLatin1Char)` has no overload in the Qt 6.8.1 the CI
pins (6.10 grew one), so it is the chained form.

as {out, bytes, sha256}. platform decode refuses an unknown register instead

events.title: gui: Draw tight text through a squeezed copy of the UI font
events.message:
gui: Draw tight text through a squeezed copy of the UI font

TightText() composed every glyph row in C into a Chip RAM template,
which takes about 7.5 ms per label on a 68000. Let the ROM's Text()
draw the line instead, through a copy of the UI font whose advances
are limited to the tight width and whose space has the caller's width.
The copy shares the glyph data and kerning with the original font and
only adds a table of advances, about 450 bytes per space width plus a
shared table of zero kerning for fonts without one.

Fonts with colour or tags, soft styles, extra spacing, COMPLEMENT and
INVERSVID keep using the existing composer, as does the MMU list with
its erased spaces.

On a 68000 A500 the speed panel labels take 43 ms instead of 120 ms and
a main-view redraw drops from about 606 ms to 527 ms. The rendering is
identical except where a glyph's eighth column touches the next one,
such as the slash in "N/A", which now keeps that pixel.

events.title: Give action steps the inputs of the MCP tools, and add press
events.message:
Give action steps the inputs of the MCP tools, and add press

A step is { kind: input } with the fields, ranges and defaults of the tool
that does the same: write = c64_memory_write {address, data}, registers =
c64_registers write values, type = c64_keyboard {mode, text|bytes}, runUntil =
c64_run_until {target, timeoutFrames}. Names work in every steps file. type
fills the KERNAL keyboard queue in every engine; the new press pushes matrix
keys and only the replay core has it, so VICE steps refuse it with the remedy.
The scripts install without packages, so host-client/steps.ts checks steps
without zod; src/mcp/inputs.ts holds the tool schemas, and inputs.test.ts
checks that both take and refuse the same inputs. c64_registers takes read
and write. readActionSteps replaces three steps-file readers.
events.author: Henrik Olsson

events.title: fix(cpu): restore multithreaded JIT performance (#2469)
events.message:
fix(cpu): restore multithreaded JIT performance (#2469)

Threaded JIT throughput:
- The threaded CPU now handles SPCFLAG_CHECK through the shared reset/halt
  code. The flag used to stay set after the boot RESET and end every JIT
  block.
- The CPU thread gets its own JIT budget, so compiled blocks chain instead
  of returning to the dispatcher.
- Idle interrupt polls no longer take the shared flag exclusively, and the
  thread-ID lookups are cached.

Threaded CPU correctness:
- Only the main thread publishes the interrupt level, before it raises
  SPCFLAG_INT/DOINT, and the CPU thread clears the flags before reading it.
  A stale level caused about 2400 spurious interrupts per second on an idle
  AROS boot.
- SPCFLAG_BRK no longer ends the CPU thread; setting a breakpoint froze the
  emulation. Exactly one thread handles each BRK.
- The CPU thread semaphores are created fresh for each run, so
  custom_reset_cpu() waits for custom_reset().
- An accelerator CPU fallback restarts the CPU loop instead of leaving the
  chipset running with no CPU.
- SPCFLAG_CHECK is cleared before the halt state is read, the CPU thread
  waits during a keyboard reset hold, and it no longer writes INTREQ for
  SPCFLAG_UAEINT.
- Freezer cartridges, MMU, cycle-exact and CPU fallback configurations run
  the CPU on the main thread; fixup_cpu() checks the threaded option after
  the other CPU options are final, and the GUI matches.
- SPCFLAG_BLTNASTY is not raised for the threaded CPU.
- The unused register batch and IO queue are removed; their flush could drop
  writes.
- If the CPU thread cannot start, the CPU runs on the main thread.

editor: complete, jump and explain from one candidate list

Sheet §4 (docs/glm-features.md): the console had QCompleter completion and the
editor had none, which is backwards. All three surfaces now read one list of
candidates - the assembler's own vocabulary plus the build's labels and equates
- so the popup, the palette and the hover cannot disagree about a word:

- Tab (or Ctrl+Space) completes the word at the caret: prefix matches before
  mere substrings, case-insensitively; Tab/Return take the candidate, Up/Down
  walk the list, Escape dismisses it, and a comment or a word already typed in
  full is offered nothing. QCompleter supplies the model, the popup and the
  filtering; the prefix, the keys and the placement are the editor's.
- Ctrl+Shift+O (Search ▸ Go to Symbol…) is the same candidates as a jump list
  over the build's symbols, filtered as you type; Enter opens the definition's
  file at its line, and the filter's Up/Down walk the list.
- A hover card at the pointer gives a mnemonic the reference's summary and
  condition-code flags, a TOS call its name, meaning, prototype and pushed
  arguments, and a label where the build put it - and nothing at all for a
  directive or a word nothing knows, the refusal the reference already keeps.

The reference dock and the hover card share editor/CursorReference, the dispatch
the dock used to inline, so a line cannot mean one thing in the panel and another
in a tooltip. The word it returns comes from asmlex's token alphabet now, so a
label keeps its underscore.

tst_completion drives the vocabulary, the ranking and the resolver with no window
and no emulator; tst_gui pins all three surfaces. Two Qt traps that cost a
measurement each - a completer attached to a widget that is not a QLineEdit hides
its own popup on the next keystroke, and its popup sits at the widget's bottom
edge - are recorded in PLAN §11.

events.title: ui: find in files — a project-wide search that counts with the editor's scan
events.message:
ui: find in files — a project-wide search that counts with the editor's scan

Sheet §3: search was per-document only, and a project-wide one has to count the
same way or it looks like it is lying. So the scan is shared rather than
re-implemented — `editor/FindScan.{h,cpp}` now holds `FindOptions`, the
whole-word filter and the 2000-hit cap, and `CodeEditor::collectMatches` calls
it — and the dock is a view over a walk that reports results as it finds them.

`ui/FindInFiles` is that walk: the project directory, files in path order,
skipping what `isSearchableFile()` refuses (executables, objects, disk and
still-image formats, ROM images, vasm listings; unknown files with a NUL byte;
hidden directories; oversized files) and counting what it skipped, because the
header has to say so. It is chunked on this thread by a 10 ms tick budget rather
than threaded: no dock here walks a directory off the GUI thread (the one QThread
is a modal setup dialog that cannot be cancelled) and Qt6::Concurrent is not
linked, and chunking makes "a new query replaces the running one" a state change
instead of a race.

`ui/FindInFilesView` is the dock beside Problems: the query, the find bar's two
options, results grouped by file with each match's span painted in the colour the
editor uses for its own hits, a header stating hits, files *searched* and files
skipped, and a `navigate` callback the window implements as "open the file, go to
the line, select the match" (`CodeEditor::selectSpan()` — the one new editor
entry point). F4/Shift+F4 tour the list while it has focus, claimed through
ShortcutOverride rather than bound as a second shortcut: F4 is already the
diagnostics tour, and two shortcuts on one key make Qt fire neither. Its sizeHint
is deliberately a strip, because the factory layout sizes the bottom group from
its docks' hints and that group is meant to stay short — the first version of it
failed the layout test, which is how the invariant was found.

The window asks a new `projectScopeDirectory()` for the scope, which the Git panel
now shares, so the two cannot disagree about what "the project" is; and it adds
Search ▸ Find in Files… (Ctrl+Shift+F) plus the dock's View-menu entry.

Tests: `tst_find` (new, no window) pins the shared scan's counting and cap and the
walk's skip list, cap, summaries and cancellation contract — and caught the
negative-`from` bug in the line lookup while being written. `tst_gui` pins the
dock against a fixture tree: rows by file with their line numbers, the header's
counts, F4 crossing into the other file and selecting the match, F4 still the
diagnostics tour when the editor has the focus, and a second query leaving nothing
of the first. The five existing find-bar tests pass unchanged, which is what the
extraction had to prove. Full local suite green.

events.title: test(pacing): a host stall no longer fails the paced-sleep test (beads-7ik5) (#124)
events.message:
test(pacing): a host stall no longer fails the paced-sleep test (beads-7ik5) (#124)

* test(pacing): a host stall no longer fails the paced-sleep test (bead…

…s-7ik5)

EmuFramePacingTest.PacedFramesReportTheirSleep failed once on the macOS CI
runner with fast frames and almost no sleep (2.87 ms of 27.4 wanted). The
cause is the test, not FramePacer: a host that holds the thread up for tens
of ms while it is awake lets the deadlines pass, and drift correction then
rightly sleeps that much less. Freezing the test process for 60 ms at random
moments reproduces it on master (2 of 300 runs, the same signature).
FramePacer::stopped() is not on this path: the bridge start and the unpaced
frames before the paced ones both clear it.

The sleep is now measured up to five times and must exceed half the
headroom once; a counter that loses the sleep fails every attempt. Each
attempt also checks what no host can change: the four paced frames span at
least the three 60 ms of deadlines, and the reported sleep fits inside that
window.

events.title: Add cycle-exact save states
events.message:
Add cycle-exact save states

C64.saveState() serializes the whole machine into a tagged chunk
stream and restoreState(from:) continues from the same clock cycle,
mid-instruction and mid-rasterline. Chunks cover the CPU, memory and
CPU port, VIC-II with line buffers, sprite shifters and traces, SID,
both CIAs, the IEC bus, Kernal trap channels, the cartridge with its
bank and RAM state, the 1541 with VIAs, RAM, head state and GCR disk,
the high-level drive channels and DOS RAM, and the tape unit. Mounted
media are embedded; ROMs are not. Every chunk body must be consumed
exactly, arrays are length-checked and enumerations range-checked.

Each chip records its reflected stored-property count next to its
save code and a test compares the two, so new fields cannot be left
out of the format silently.

The app adds File > Save State / Load State (Cmd+Shift+S/L), Quick
Save / Quick Load (Cmd+Option+S/L) in Application Support, drop
support for .s64 files, and a status-bar message.

Tests prove a fresh machine and a rewound machine continue cycle for
cycle identically to the uninterrupted run, with and without ROMs and
with the compatibility true drive running; the cartridge and disk
round-trip; corrupt files are rejected. The Release regression slice
across the touched chips passes 1,046 tests.

events.message:
fix(log): one log line is one locked write (beads-2qcw) (#123)

* fix(log): one log line is one locked write (beads-2qcw)

The LOG_* macros already formatted each line into one buffer, but wrote it
into std::cerr/std::cout with no lock, from the Z80, render, IPC, telnet,
M4 HTTP and KCPC threads at once. ThreadSanitizer reports that as a data
race on the stream (libc++ __pad_and_output, two KCPC connection threads
logging 'client N connected/disconnected').

log_write_line() in log.cpp now writes the finished line and flushes under
one mutex shared by every macro. The lock is only taken for a line that is
really written: LOG_VERBOSE/LOG_DEBUG still test log_verbose (and compile
away without DEBUG) before anything is formatted.

test/log_test.cpp installs a stream buffer in std::cerr that sees two
writers inside it at once; 8 threads x 20 LOG_INFO lines. Fails on master
3/3, passes with the fix.

events.title: RunCommand: overlay the calling process instead of a nested Runtime (#157)
events.message:
RunCommand: overlay the calling process instead of a nested Runtime (#157)

* RunCommand: overlay the calling process instead of a nested Runtime (fixes #8, #156)

RunCommand ran the invoked seglist through the same brand-new
Runtime/CpuCore/FlatMemory System()/Execute() use, which is correct for
those two but wrong for RunCommand: real AmigaOS runs it as a
subroutine in the caller's own process, inheriting (and propagating
back) the same CPU register state, including FPCR/FPSR -- the concrete
repro in #156 is a newlib test that depends on exactly this.

The "genuine architectural extension" a prior design pass thought this
needed already exists: ContinuationStack::trampoline (built for
OpenLibrary's real-library init vectors) lets a handler run a guest
subroutine and get control back through the ordinary dispatch loop, no
CPU reentrancy required. run_command_handler now resolves the entry
point straight from the already-loaded seglist bytes in guest memory
(no re-read from disk), carves a stack from the caller's own heap
(same bookkeeping StackSwap already does), and trampolines to it.
FPCR/FPSR need no explicit handling at all: they're plain CpuCore
fields nothing else touches, so running the child on the same cpu/mem
inherits and propagates them for free.

System()/Execute() are unaffected. Found along the way:
fixtures/runcmdtest.s kept its seglist BPTR in D1 across the call,
relying on a comment that was only true under the old implementation --
fixed to save it on the stack instead, matching real hardware (no
register is safe across a real RunCommand call).

* Fix cmdline_pos leak across RunCommand, remove dead seglist_host_paths

Fable's review of the overlay implementation found a real bug:
DosState::cmdline_pos (ReadArgs's cursor into the command-line buffer)
was saved/swapped/restored for cmdline itself but not its paired
cursor, so a caller that had already called ReadArgs on its own
command line left the child's ReadArgs starting mid-buffer (often past
the end), silently parsing it as empty. Fixed by resetting it to 0
alongside the cmdline swap and restoring the caller's value in the
continuation; added a regression test that fails without the fix.

Also removed DosState::seglist_host_paths, write-only dead state left
over from the old RunCommand implementation (its only reader was the
resolve_and_run_command this PR already deleted), and tightened the
two FPCR unit tests' marker values to the exception-enable byte
(bits 8-15) instead of bits real FPU silicon masks to zero, so they
can't start failing (or silently proving nothing) if the m68k crate
ever adds real FPCR masking.

events.title: docs: record the stop hook's agent surface, and why its event is its own
events.message:
docs: record the stop hook's agent surface, and why its event is its own

The sheet asked for "a `hook` field on the published `stopped` event". §10 now
records why that is not implementable — the run happens after the stop is
published, by design (D1), because it reads registers that must be real first —
and what happened instead: a `hook` event of its own, emitted before the continue
policy so the wire order is stopped → hook → running. §11's failure table says
who learns what now that a watcher is listening, §12 names each new case, §13
marks L3 implemented, and §17 closes: L1, L2 and L3 delivered. §5's D5 and §15's
open question stop posing as future work as well — the per-breakpoint script
landed in L2, and the correlation question is answered as far as the wire goes
(order plus PC; no stop id, said rather than implied).

README documents the verb, the tool, the event's fields and its read-only
annotation; ARCHITECTURE's hooks paragraph says the runner is readable from
outside; glm-features §1 no longer says L3 remains, and PLAN.md §6 summarises the
phase while §9's ledger carries the departure rather than absorbing it.

events.title: control: report the stop hook to an agent, as a verb, a tool and an event
events.message:
control: report the stop hook to an agent, as a verb, a tool and an event

L3 of the stop hook (docs/stop-hooks-plan.md §10): an agent that drives the IDE
over remote control can now see what a hook it never watches for itself ran.

`hook` answers with a block of JSON — {enabled, path, autoContinue, last} — built
in RemoteStateAdapter from the same StopHookRunner::LastRun that renders the
dialog's sentence, so the two cannot come to disagree: that record is now the
run's fields, and lastRunSummary() is one rendering of it. `last` is always
present and `ran` is what says whether a script has run at all this session, so a
consumer tests a field rather than the existence of a key. `pist_hook` serves the
same over MCP — mapped and framed from the shared verb table, listed read-only,
and returned in structuredContent as well as text.

The run reports itself in a `hook` event rather than as a field on `stopped`: the
script runs *after* the stop is published, because it reads registers that must be
real first (D1), so at publication time there is no outcome to report. It is
emitted before the continue policy, so the wire order is stopped → hook → running,
and carries `<status> file=… line=… writes=… logs=… pc=… [message=…]` with the
status one of ok, timeout, error or norun — the last of which is what keeps an
unreadable script from looking like one that raised. That line is
hookEventDetail(), in the hooks module rather than in the publishing widget, so
the format an agent codes against is pinned by a test instead of drifting.

Tests: tst_stophooks pins the record and asserts the event line whole for a
success, plus the difference between a raising script and an unreadable one;
tst_remotecontrol asserts the verb's shape with no project at all; tst_mcp pins
the tool catalog whole (a dropped tool breaks an agent silently) and asserts the
mapping, framing and parsed fields. Full suite green, and the path was smoked
against a real session: `pist_run` through `pist-mcp`, then
`event stopped pc=… | event hook ok file=hello.hooks.lua line=-1 writes=1 logs=1
pc=…` on a watcher, with `pist_hook` returning that same run's numbers.

events.title: Debugger and MCP fixes
events.message:
Debugger and MCP fixes

- A stop on a temporary breakpoint (Run to cursor, Step over a CALL,
  emu_run_until_addr, emu_step_out) now emits the "paused" event with
  reason "run_to". The stop also happens when a breakpoint with an unmet
  condition sits on the target address; previously the temporary
  breakpoint was skipped there.
- All memory regions are listed and accessible, including in the Memory
  Browser, diff, snapshot and byte freeze. Previously the list was cut at
  128 regions in MCP and at 512 in the GUI, and a fully expanded MZ-800
  has 532.
- Memory reads and writes made by the debugger itself no longer trigger
  MEM_R/MEM_W breakpoints. This covers the disassembler, Memory Browser,
  byte freeze, emu_mem_read, emu_mem_write and emu_region_write. The
  breakpoint action "poke" still triggers MEM_W breakpoints.
- In MZ-700 mode, showing 0E000h-0E008h in the debugger no longer affects
  the emulation (for example, it no longer advances autotype).
  0E004h-0E006h now show the 8253 counter values.
- Breakpoint expressions have two new identifiers: InsnPC (address of the
  current instruction) and FrameCycle (GDG ticks since the start of the
  frame).
- The MCP trace tools and the breakpoint action "trace_start" can now
  control the "marklog" channel.
- emu_history_get returns a position taken at the same moment as the
  returned lines.
- emu_event_poll accepts waits longer than 30 s.
- cputrack records instruction bytes as the CPU fetched them, so
  self-modifying code is logged correctly. Recording with cputrack is
  about 12 % slower; emulation without diagnostics runs at the same speed.
- Documentation fixes: [addr]! in expressions, trace_reset, where the
  "log" action writes in pipe mode, and the GDG to CPU clock ratio
  (5 on PAL, 4 on NTSC).

events.title: fix(ipc): config set crtc_type|silicon_disc holds the machine still (beads-7h32) (#122)
events.message:
fix(ipc): config set crtc_type|silicon_disc holds the machine still (beads-7h32) (#122)

* fix(ipc): config set crtc_type|silicon_disc holds the machine still (…

…beads-7h32)

The text IPC's `config set` called ipc_config_set() on its server thread
with no pause lease, so `crtc_type` (Machine::set_crtc_type) and
`silicon_disc` (silicon_disc_init + ga_memory_manager) changed the CRTC
device and the banking while the frame runner could be mid-frame, or
beside a machine rebuild. KCPC's CONFIG_SET already wrapped the call in
a lease of its own.

ipc_config_set() now takes an IpcConfigHold: with Lease it holds the
machine for those two keys itself (CpcPauseLease, change_alone(),
restore_run_state()) and answers NotIdle when it cannot, which the text
IPC reports as ERR 409 z80-not-idle; KCPC passes Caller, since its
CONFIG_SET already holds the machine alone, so the lease is never taken
twice. Validation stays outside the lease; the other keys are unchanged.
