events.title: feat(repl): the banner names the build, the heap, the collector, the JIT state and the boot image
events.message:
feat(repl): the banner names the build, the heap, the collector, the JIT state and the boot image

The right column beside the lambda used to carry two facts: the version
and the OS.  It now answers what a user asks first when the REPL comes up
on an Amiga, and what a bug report needs:

    AmiLisp v0.12
    Common Lisp for AmigaOS
    68020+ FPU, 8M heap, Immix GC, JIT
    booted from amilisp.img

The CPU segment tells the soft-float, FPU and PowerPC binaries apart
(__HAVE_68881__ is what -m68881 defines), the GC segment says Immix,
generational or mark-sweep, the JIT segment reports THIS run ("JIT off"
after --no-jit; absent on a build without a native backend), a wide-string
build adds "unicode", and the boot line names the restored image file --
"embedded image" for a delivered executable -- or says "booted from lib/
(no image)".  image.c keeps the staged file's base name before it frees
the path (cl_image_restored_name).

The art is unchanged and stays ASCII (the Amiga console draws Topaz); the
text column is padded to a fixed width so the lines align.  "AmiLisp v"
and the exact "Type (quit) to exit." line stay, since test_executable.sh
and test_repl_values.sh key on them.

tests/test_banner.sh (in make test) pins: the heap figure follows --heap
in --heap's own spelling, "JIT off" follows --no-jit, the boot line names
an explicit and a discovered amilisp.img, the column alignment, no banner
in --batch / --non-interactive.  Cross-compiled soft-float and FPU=1 to
check the per-build branches.

events.title: feat(ipc): add Windows named-pipe transport
events.message:
feat(ipc): add Windows named-pipe transport

Amiberry's IPC control endpoint on Windows is the byte-mode named pipe
\\.\pipe\amiberry (further instances amiberry_1..amiberry_9). Connect
with the proactor loop's create_pipe_connection behind the existing
reader/writer interface, so every command path works unchanged;
ERROR_PIPE_BUSY is retried inside the connect timeout and a brief
grace retry covers transient FILE_NOT_FOUND while Amiberry rotates its
listening instance.

Discovery and is_available() list the pipe namespace instead of probing
with os.path.exists, which opens a client connection to a pipe; the
per-command preflight is skipped on Windows, where the connect itself
reports a missing pipe. A non-proactor loop raises an explicit,
actionable IPCConnectionError. Unix behavior is unchanged.

events.title: fix(disk): an exit nobody is asked about writes a disc's unsaved writes back (beads-lgul) (#111)
events.message:
fix(disk): an exit nobody is asked about writes a disc's unsaved writes back (beads-lgul) (#111)

* fix(disk): an exit nobody is asked about writes a disc's unsaved writ…

…es back (beads-lgul)

doCleanUp() joined the frame runner and then called dsk_eject(), which only
queues the eject for a frame that never comes, and subcycle_bridge_stop() is
not called on exit. So IPC quit, SIGTERM/SIGINT, --exit-after,
--exit-on-break and a scripted KONCPC_EXIT all dropped a disc's unsaved
writes.

Every exit nobody was asked about now writes each disc back to its own file
through the eject's write-back (subcycle_bridge_write_back_discs(), so a disc
from an archive goes to a DSK beside it). Only a user shown the
unsaved-changes dialog who answered "Quit anyway?" with yes leaves them
unwritten (koncpc_quit_writes_back_discs()).

events.title: feat(ipc): support IPC control on Windows via a named pipe (#2466)
events.message:
feat(ipc): support IPC control on Windows via a named pipe (#2466)

* feat(ipc): support the IPC control interface on Windows via a named pipe

Windows builds forced USE_IPC_SOCKET off because the transport was a Unix
socket, and CPython on Windows cannot open AF_UNIX sockets anyway. The
listener is now a byte-mode named pipe, \\.\pipe\amiberry (amiberry_1..9
for further instances), driven with overlapped I/O from the same
non-blocking per-frame service loop. Request handling is shared with the
POSIX socket, which keeps its behavior.

The pipe rejects remote clients and its DACL grants access only to the
account Amiberry runs as. tools/ipc_client.py opens the pipe on Windows with
a 5 s read deadline and identification-level impersonation.

* test(ipc): add a behavioral test for the IPC transport

Starts headless emulator instances and checks, over the Unix socket or the
Windows named pipe: in-order replies to pipelined requests, a second
controller served while the first stops reading, oversized requests
refused, abandoned connections freeing their slots, half-close on Unix, a
second instance on its own endpoint, and QUIT answered before exit. Runs in
tests/run_tests.sh and on the Windows x64 CI leg.

events.title: Disassemble Cyberun from its tape, with how it works, the planet, its graphics, animations, sounds, bugs and pokes
events.message:
Disassemble Cyberun from its tape, with how it works, the planet, its graphics, animations, sounds, bugs and pokes

scripts/build_cyberun.py loads the tape by simulating the real LOAD, so
the game's own loader moves the block to $5C80 and undoes its nibble
shift, then maps the code by playing it in SkoolKit's simulator --
through the menu, every control method, long flights, an empty tank,
game over, two players and staged scenes put by the game's own restart
(the launch through to the next planet, part deliveries, every add-on,
tours of the caverns) -- and follows branches out of what ran, out of
the game's tables of entry points and out of the jumps it patches into
itself (READ_EDGES). 10745 of 11340 instructions ran. The build fails if
any executed address lies in an entry typed as data.

All 42240 bytes from $5B00 are in 900 entries, every one titled,
described and labelled; the listing reassembles byte for byte and writes
back the snapshot it read, with 0 warnings. The annotations now decide
where entries are (sna2ctl's guesses are dropped inside each), checked by
ctl_tools.py check --new-entries. cyberun_data.py lays out the map,
tiles, objects and pick-up places record by record at build time and
draws every graphic into its entry with the game's own routines.

Six page modules build the HTML: how it works (eight pages with worked
examples), the planet (the whole map drawn by the game's renderer,
checked against its own first screen), tiles, objects and pick-up
places, landscape pieces, sprites, object types, add-ons, the panel, 28
animations, every sound recorded and matched to its routine, and bugs,
pokes (each tried against the same trial without it) and facts.

notes/cyberun/ has the working notes. Corrections found by running the
game are logged in them, among them two reversals: the missiles' target
table is not off by one, and stage 0's infinite-lives poke (62671,0)
runs the game-over sequence at every death; 62671,183 is the one.

No game bytes are committed: the listing, pictures and sounds are built
locally into game_disassembly/ and published only on gh-pages.

events.title: strips: HAM-aware HAM6 swap planner with register-lifetime refinement
events.message:
strips: HAM-aware HAM6 swap planner with register-lifetime refinement

The HAM6 strips planner ranked candidate swaps with a SET-only centroid
proxy and DP-checked only the top 5, often all on one register. It now:

- pre-screens (register, colour) swaps by the HAM error a SET of that
  colour removes over the next three strips, charging pixels that SET
  the old register value with their best fallback (another register,
  the new colour or a MODIFY of the previous output);
- draws candidates from the source and pre-dithered pixels of those
  strips (colours can be loaded before the strip that needs them) and
  the centroid of the strip's worst-encoded pixels;
- DP-verifies the top 24 (at most 4 per register) per slot;
- refits each written colour (mid-line MOVEs and the values this row's
  hblank already writes) over its register lifetime with an exact
  RGB444 search, kept only when the row DP error drops. Values alive at
  the row end that already match the next row's entry stay fixed.

Measured and dropped: a beam over slot decisions (+0.06 S2 for 1.7x
time) and an hblank-restore gate (no row needs more than 12 of the 13
restore writes).

Ordered dithers now bias the HAM6 strips targets as in plain HAM
(ham::ordered_dither_target, shared with the HAM encoders); before they
were ignored. Plain and sliced HAM6 output is unchanged.

HAM6 strips now report useful mid-line swaps per line, like the other
strip variants. output-score-ham6-strips floor 74.4 -> 75.2 (makena now
76.48).

S2 (--chipset ocs --mode ham6 --sliced --strips), before -> after:
fromthe 72.17 -> 73.43, lovers 73.48 -> 74.78, macaw 73.46 -> 74.53,
space3 70.12 -> 71.89, makena 75.69 -> 76.62, maui 76.79 -> 77.62,
photo 65.96 -> 68.58.

events.title: strips: HAM6 swap scoring resumes the DP and runs candidates in parallel
events.message:
strips: HAM6 swap scoring resumes the DP and runs candidates in parallel

A mid-line swap at slot s changes only the pixels from strip s+1 on, so
each candidate's row DP now resumes from a beam checkpoint at that strip
instead of re-encoding the row prefix (ham::score_scanline_dp_per_strip_from,
same expansion order and pruning, so the error is exact). The surviving
candidates of each slot are scored with pipeline::parallel_for and the
first strict improvement in rank order wins, so the choice does not
depend on the thread count.

Output is byte-identical to the previous planner (full hash matrix at
8 threads and with hardware_concurrency() forced to 1). HAM6 sliced +
strips wall time on 8 cores: 17-86 s -> 7-28 s per image.

events.message:
grm-gipk.3: resolve task-table dispatch (JMP (P) reloaded from a slot table)

megaman3's RESET ends in a cooperative task scheduler whose START path is
fedf JMP ($93), with $93/$94 reloaded from the X-indexed slot table
$82,X/$83,X immediately before the jump. No straight-line walk reaches the
site with the pointer known, so the main task ($C8D0) and the whole
fixed-bank game were never disassembled (grm-gipk.1).

IndirectJumpConstantPointerAnalyzer gains a task-table mode: when the site's
own run loads both pointer bytes as LDA base,X / STA P from one slot, the
targets are the constant ROM pointers some walk leaves installed in that
table (walks start at runs that store to P or index-store into the table).
Table sites are remembered and re-resolved when later code feeds them, so
tasks installed by newly reached task bodies cascade.

megaman3 re-blessed: fixed-bank functions ~10 -> 67, bankComments 19 -> 50,
retargeted refs 2 -> 50. Banked game code is still unreached because the
FUN_ff6b shadow banks are not recovered (grm-mej.27). check nes: other 34

events.title: copperhf: refuse OpenDevice on an empty unit with TDERR_BadUnitNum
events.message:
copperhf: refuse OpenDevice on an empty unit with TDERR_BadUnitNum

The boot ROM's Open vector answered a unit with no drive behind it,
an empty slot or a unit number past CHF_UNITS, with IOERR_OPENFAIL.
scsi.device answers an unanswered target with TDERR_BadUnitNum, and
bus scanners depend on the difference. HDToolBox 3.1 opens every SCSI
address and LUN in turn (unit LUN * 10 + address) and reads -1 from
OpenDevice as "the driver cannot be opened at all", setting a flag
that ends the whole scan. With copperhf it therefore listed nothing
when unit 0 was empty, and never got past unit 0 when it was present,
because unit 10 (target 0, LUN 1) is the next unit it probes. The
A2091 with both the Commodore and the bundled open ROM lists the same
drive layout correctly.

Open now fails with TDERR_BadUnitNum (32). Requests that reach the
doorbell for an absent unit keep IOERR_OPENFAIL; only Open changes.
HDToolBox 3.1 now lists drives on units 1-6, and HDToolBox 3.2, which
already scanned past -1, is unchanged.

The ROM is rebuilt with the pinned gcc-v16.2 image. That tag was
re-pushed after the ROM was last committed, so the whole image
differs, not just the changed store; a clean rebuild of the previous
source gives the same size (5244 bytes) and code layout.

Add a chftest_m4 subtest that opens an empty slot (unit 2) and unit
10 and expects TDERR_BadUnitNum. It fails against the previous ROM.
Update docs/internals/copperhf.md and copperhf_board.h.

events.title: cyc: a ROM read override, so a trusted mod can patch what the CPU reads
events.message:
cyc: a ROM read override, so a trusted mod can patch what the CPU reads

A Game Genie code changes the VALUE the CPU reads at a ROM address, which is how
it patches a game's own code without rewriting the image, and it is the one cheat
primitive this backend could not express: cyc_mod_peek() reads WITHOUT
intercepting, and the compiled-code write watch (hw_code_watch) only sees
stores. A trusted mod wanting to honour such a code had nowhere to put it.

Two sites, and both are needed. hw_bus_read() covers a byte the recompiler left
computed at run time; hw_read_rom() covers one it folded to a constant, and the
folded ones are the majority: counting over one game's generated cycle code
(mapper 1, 128 KB PRG) gives 1405 cpu_read() against 3327 cpu_read_rom(), so
70% of PRG reads would be invisible to a hook on hw_bus_read() alone. Both
already called hw_cart_cpu_read_snoop(), which is why these are the two lines to
change.

What this cannot reach, and no read hook can: what the recompiler has already
turned into C. An opcode is a goto and an address operand is a compile-time
constant (recompiler/src/cyc_codegen.c), so a substitution changes the constants
a game compares against and the data it reads out of a ROM table, and cannot
retarget an instruction. A caller that needs to change WHICH address is read
has to change the code generator, not this.

Blast radius: none for a game that has not asked for one.
cyc_mod_rom_read_overrides is NULL until cyc_mod_set_rom_read_override() is
called, and hw_rom_read_override() returns early on it, so the cost on the
hottest path in the machine is one load and a branch. Overrides are host policy
rather than machine state and are not serialized into a save state, which is
the right way round -- a state records the machine, and an override applies to
whatever machine is loaded -- and matches cyc_mod_set_ppu_write_hook, which is
host policy for the same reason.

Verified against a game-side consumer of the new API, on a mapper 1 title:

- with nothing registered, a 600-frame run is byte-identical to the same build
  without this patch: the total cycle count, the native share, and a per-frame
  hash of the registers, CPU RAM, palette and OAM all compare equal.
- an override reaches a FOLDED read: an entry at an address whose byte the
  recompiler folded to a constant changes guest state against a stock control
  over the same 300 frames.
- the two spellings of one substitution agree: setting an address/value pair
  directly, and deriving the same pair from a Game Genie code, produce
  byte-identical output over 300 frames.
- setting and clearing at run time take effect from the next frame in both
  directions, so a host can toggle one without a reset.

The substitution is applied after hw_cart_cpu_read_snoop(), so an override wins
over the board. A cheat the mapper can undo is not a cheat.

events.title: window: drop a worker frame the window has resized past
events.message:
window: drop a worker frame the window has resized past

Resizing the main window on Windows could hang Copperline and slow the
whole host until the process was killed (reported on Win11 with an AMD
GPU).

The present worker plans each frame on the main thread and presents it
later. On Windows the main thread pumps the modal size-move loop while
the user drags an edge, so the window changes size under frames still
queued for the worker. wgpu picks Vulkan first there, and the driver
answers VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR for a swapchain whose extent no longer
matches the window. pixels 0.17.2 retries that acquire in a loop with no
bound, reconfiguring from its cached surface size, which only the main
thread can update, and only after reclaiming the GPU side. The worker
rebuilt the swapchain at the stale size forever while the main thread
waited in PresentWorker::reclaim to apply the Resized event: the window
stopped responding, and the swapchain churn starved the GPU driver. This
is issue #362's loop again, now on a thread the corrective event cannot
reach. Single-threaded present never hit it on Windows, since the window
can only change size while that same thread pumps messages.

Each PresentJob now carries the surface size it was planned for, and the
worker compares it with the window's live size before acquiring. A job
whose window has moved on is dropped: it was drawn for the old geometry
anyway, and the Resized behind the change reconfigures the surface on the
main thread for the next frame. On macOS the worker must not call winit,
and the Metal layer never reports a resized surface out of date, so it
presents as before.

The race between that check and the acquire is closed by patching in
upstream's bounded retry (parasyte/pixels#462, unreleased): pixels gives
up after one reconfigure and returns GetSurface(Outdated). That error is
logged at debug as a dropped frame on both present paths; other present
failures stay errors. The patch is a revision-pinned [patch.crates-io] in
the root, player and fuzz workspaces, allowed in deny.toml, to be removed
once a pixels release includes #462.

COPPERLINE_THREADED_PRESENT=0 or WGPU_BACKEND=dx12 avoid the hang on
builds without this fix.

events.message:
markdown.datatype 0.1b2: big files on small Amigas

Laid out a part at a time with md_render_range (TextTools cdf1bb3), cut
where blocks end; a part that does not fit is retried smaller; if memory
still runs out, what fitted is shown with a note, not an empty window.
Lean pens under 3 MB (one piece per table row), long-lived memory from
the top, a 16 KB stack. Whole and part-by-part layout compared on five
real READMEs: identical except blank rows in a list over 16 KB. Stock
A600 (1 MB, 3.1): 7.7 KB README fine, 96 KB shows 593 rows and the note.

events.title: RESTORE key drives the NMI line (one NMI per press)
events.message:
RESTORE key drives the NMI line (one NMI per press)

session/key_down "RESTORE" (what a scenario's `I hold / start holding the
key "RESTORE"` sends, now or at a cycle) only went into the held-key set:
RESTORE is not in the matrix, and INT_SRC_RESTORE was never set, so no NMI
was ever taken.

The core now samples the keyboard's RESTORE state every cycle, like the
expansion port's lines, into INT_SRC_RESTORE. As in VICE, key down asserts
the source and key up releases it; the edge-triggered NMI makes a held key
one NMI. A press queued for a cycle is seen from that cycle.

Test: tests/restore_key_nmi_gate.rs (held = one NMI, release, second press,
queued press at its cycle). Fails on main, passes with this change.

events.title: fix(gui): a Run the user asks for is not dropped under another actor's pause lease (beads-jlbg) (#101)
events.message:
fix(gui): a Run the user asks for is not dropped under another actor's pause lease (beads-jlbg) (#101)

* fix(gui): a Run the user asks for is not dropped under another actor'…

…s pause lease (beads-jlbg)

cpc_resume() does nothing while any CpcPauseLease is held. The GUI's Run
actions resumed with it, so a Run that arrived while a KCPC client was
writing memory, or the text IPC held the machine for a `reg set`, was lost:
the machine stayed paused and nothing said why.

They now use cpc_run(), which records the run for the lease chain, so the
machine runs when the last holder lets go (unless somebody stops it first):
the command palette's Pause / Resume, dbg_run_pause_toggle() (DevTools
toolbar and Disassembly window), F5 in DevTools, the Resume (Esc) button,
closing the pause menu, closing Options (commit and revert), cancelling the
quit confirmation, the auto-pause resume on focus gain / mouse enter, and
the M4 web interface's pause toggle. With no lease held cpc_run() and
cpc_resume() do the same thing, so a single actor sees no change.

The text IPC's `screenshot window` paused and resumed by hand with
was_paused, the pattern beads-mk1w removed elsewhere: announced to every
subscriber as a stop and a resume, and its resume was dropped the same way.
It now borrows the machine under a lease and ends with restore_run_state().

Left alone: the shutdown path's cpc_resume() (the Z80 thread's loop tests
the quit flag whether paused or not, and the process is on its way out),
dbg_step_in()'s branch for a machine without the board, and the text IPC's
test-only `wait pc` fallback.

* test(m4): a reset an M4 test queued is not run by the next suite that…

… drains (beads-jlbg)

M4HttpTest.ConfigCgiCpcReset and ResetQueuesDeferred leave
g_m4_http.pending_reset set: the fixture cleared the queued requests in
SetUp only. When the shuffle ran one of them last, and the suite before
GuiRunUnderLeaseTest, AnM4ResumeIsNotLostToAnothersLease's drain_pending()
ran emulator_reset(), which dereferences the video plugin the test process
never creates (video_set_palette(): vid_plugin->set_palette). That is the
segfault of the Linux job, seed 33333; the same seed crashes on macOS.

M4HttpTest now clears what it queued in TearDown, and the lease fixture
clears every request drain_pending() serves, not only the pause toggle.

events.title: feat(kcpc): media, snapshots and configuration over the binary protocol (beads-rcyq) (#102)
events.message:
feat(kcpc): media, snapshots and configuration over the binary protocol (beads-rcyq) (#102)

* feat(kcpc): media, snapshots and configuration: MEDIA_*, TAPE_CONTROL…

…, SNAPSHOT_*, CONFIG_* (beads-rcyq)

Slice 9 of the binary protocol on port 6545: the nine requests a remote
GUI needs on its one connection.

- MEDIA_INSERT, MEDIA_EJECT, TAPE_CONTROL run the loaders of slotshandler
  under a pause lease, alone, and apply the bridge's queued swap before the
  lease is let go: the machine holds the medium when the reply is sent, and
  every EVT_MEDIA_CHANGED of the request names it and follows the reply.
- A disc insert ejects the outgoing disc first, so a disc with unsaved
  writes is written back to its own file. Every other load path names the
  new file first and writes the old disc into it (beads-11us).
- A cartridge insert re-attaches the image to the board, resets the
  machine, and puts the previous cartridge back when the new one is refused.
- MEDIA_INFO and CONFIG_GET are read through the machine gate and pause
  nothing.
- SNAPSHOT_SAVE and SNAPSHOT_LOAD are SNA, through snapshot_save() and
  snapshot_load(); a load is announced as EVT_RESET.
- The text IPC's `config get|set|apply` becomes one table of keys
  (ipc_config_get/set/apply) that both servers call; its replies are
  unchanged. CONFIG_APPLY uses the main-thread rebuild and names itself in
  EVT_MACHINE_CHANGED.

The document is brought in line with what the loaders do: no write-protect
flag (the FDC has no switch for it), no cartridge eject, a snapshot never
rebuilds the machine, TAPE_CONTROL moves the deck under its lease.

* test(kcpc): the controller takes its EVT_CONTROL_CHANGED before an ob…

…server joins

events.title: Match 165 more functions byte for byte and write 24 hidden ones
events.message:
Match 165 more functions byte for byte and write 24 hidden ones

Thirteen parallel passes over the game core and the ix library, each
judged by compiling one unit and comparing every function's whole span
(code, switch tables, padding) with the original at 64 symbol offsets.
CL 4.20 breaks register ties by symbol index, so a function counts as
matched when it is exact at some offset; the real offsets are solved
once global ownership is reconstructed.

- 165 functions that were exact at no offset now are: types (short
  returns, unsigned short parameters, signedness), operand and statement
  order, loop shapes and switch layouts. None regressed.
- 24 hidden functions: code nothing references, so Ghidra never made it
  a function, but which sits inside the original's .text and moved every
  later address. Among them SendMonoDebugCommand3, FreeAllPilotTalk,
  FindNavMapLabelAtPoint, the near-heap helpers, ConvertSphericalTo-
  Rectangular, the DIB width/height getters and several empty hooks.
  0x4404B0, first taken for one, is RecRoom's switch table; the
  function behind it starts at 0x4404E0.
- Header corrections: return and parameter types the callees' own code
  proves, InitFullScreenViewport as __stdcall (it ends in RET 8), and no
  volatile where the code reads a global only once. SeedRandomFromClock
  takes its argument through an unnamed prototype parameter: a named one
  is one more symbol in every unit, which moved detect_collisions.

make report: 1,509 functions, 1,164 byte-exact (from 1,028), 107 of a
different size (from 133), net drift -182 bytes; 1,287 at 100% mnemonic
similarity, 62 below 90%. make verify and the SDL build pass.

events.title: Move the NewtonScript time base to 2024, so the Newton sleeps again
events.message:
Move the NewtonScript time base to 2024, so the Newton sleeps again

NewtonScript seconds counted from 2008 wrapped on 2025-01-04 (30-bit
integers). SetSysAlarm() alarms landed in 1993, fired at once and were set
again every few milliseconds. CyclePower() found the alarm message on
gNewtPort and cancelled every power-off. The base is now 2024-01-01, good
until 2041-01-04.

The emulated RTC on Windows no longer uses an epoch 150 days and one hour

The inert-command allowlist did not converge: git runs aliases, heredoc
substitutions hid commands after separators, and quoted text faked a

words still count only when they could yield finding.mjs or --request, so

for spelled markers, so a single-quoted '/tmp/$SPEC.md' no longer adds an

events.title: Amiga output: -o x.idx writes raw chunky indices
events.message:
Amiga output: -o x.idx writes raw chunky indices

--help and the README document .idx as raw chunky indices (1 byte per
pixel, scan order, no header), but in Amiga modes -o x.idx wrote a PNG
and, since 106e5b56, exits 64. write_amiga_output now writes it.

Every Amiga path builds the bundle from bitplanes, so the .idx bytes are
decoded from them: each pixel's bitplane value (bit k = plane k), at the
image's own width and height. That is the palette index in plain,
sliced and strips modes, the HAM control + data bits (the same values
the batch atlas path decodes), and the combined PF1/PF2 value in DPF.
Lores strips viewers fetch an extra word and shift the planes 5 px;
that happens only in the .cpp writer, so .idx is unshifted.
--transparent-output-slot applies, as documented.

There were four copies of the .idx writer: --output-each, its duplicate
in the joint-palette block, and --output-indexed in the EHB and plain
paths. They and the new branch now share write_idx_file; bytes and
status lines are unchanged. A failed --output-indexed open now exits
73 (cannot create) instead of 1.

Tests: amiga-output-idx checks byte count = width * height and known
bytes for plain, sliced, strips and HAM6, and that -o .idx matches
--output-indexed. check_strips_replay.py --check-idx (DPF default,
lores d3, EHB default, HAM6 default) requires each .idx byte to be the
bitplane value the replay renders that preview pixel from.

events.title: Judge an expanding command by an inert-command allowlist, not execution vectors
events.message:
Judge an expanding command by an inert-command allowlist, not execution vectors

Chasing execution vectors missed an assignment prefix (`A=1 $N $F $R`),
an expanded executor (`n{o..o}de $F $R`) and markers with attached
redirections. A command without any expansion character is still decided
by its loose view. An expanding one is a possible deposit when an expansion
could assemble a marker around literal text, or when any simple command in
it - $(…), backtick and unquoted-heredoc substitutions included - does not
start, past NAME=value prefixes, with a literal inert word (echo, printf,
cd, ls, cat, git, grep, head, tail, wc, pwd, test, [, date). Words now also
split at redirection and control operators. Records the round-2
do-not-merge review verdict.

Count a whole-word $ expansion as a deposit only beside an execution vector

Denying every non-canonical command with a $ or backtick expansion in a
chat session blocked ordinary work such as `echo $HOME` or
`cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"`. Such a word now counts as a
possible deposit only when the command can run it as a script or flag:
node, npx, bash/sh/zsh, eval, source or `.`, exec, xargs, env, or an
expansion in command position. Without one, only an assembly around

events.message:
Lores strips: exact 8-px grid and a black frame with colour 0 unlocked

The viewer now shows the lores-strips bitplanes 5 px left of the
standard placement (one extra fetch word: DDFSTRT $30, BPLCON1 $BB,
BPLxMOD -2, DIW H $7C/$BC). With gate 0x3C, copper MOVE k then lands at
exactly x = 8k: 40 slots, x = 0..312. With standard placement no gate
reaches x = 8k (8k-13/-9/-5/-1 for 0x38/0x3A/0x3C/0x3E). Gate 0x3E with
a 1-px shift gives the same grid, but there the 41st MOVE crosses the
line end and lands one copper cycle late (x=324).

COLOR00 is the border colour. With --no-lock-color0 it now stays black
outside the picture: hblank never writes it, slot 0 (x=0) loads the
image colour, a MOVE at x=320 restores black, and the frame-start
palette has COLOR00 black. With the lock on, COLOR00 is black already
and none of this is emitted.

The chain always runs past the end of its line, so lores rows have no
end-of-line WAIT (on line 255 one would be checked on line 256 and stall
the copper). Hblank cap measured on Copperline (320x256, depth 4):
14 MOVEs with the lock on, 13 with the restore MOVE; one more delays the
chain and the late end cascades into the next line.

ScapSlotTable gains end_of_line_wait and display_shift_px; cheader
applies the shift to the viewer and documents it in the .h. The api's
line-start palette snapshot includes lores slot 0 (x=0).

rows, the issue command (both locks) and the debug pattern at depth 1
and 4 all show 0 image pixels differing from the preview and no

events.title: Serial drivers: don't overrun the receive DMA
events.message:
Serial drivers: don't overrun the receive DMA

The serial drivers wrote everything they read from the host into the
receive DMA buffer, also past the count NewtonOS gave it (mRxDMADataCountdown),
overwriting bytes NewtonOS had not read yet. A host sends faster than a
serial line: over TCP a whole MNP frame (up to 256 bytes) arrives at once,
so a frame that came while the buffer was partly full was broken, and the
Newton asked for it again and again (NCX's incremental backup stopped at
the soup info it sent).

Now the drivers read no more than receive DMA can take (RxDMARoom()), leave
the rest in the socket, pipe, or PTY, don't wait for input while there is
no room, and wake up when NewtonOS starts receive DMA again (the count
register, kSerCmd_RxCtrlChanged). All four drivers: TCP client (POSIX and
Windows), named pipes, PTY, BasiliskII. Tested on macOS with the TCP client
(NCX backup); the Windows side builds untested.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.message:
Add opt-in public CIA conformance runner

PublicCIAConformanceTests runs the exitcode programs from the CIA
section of the pinned VICE-testprogs revision, one C64 per program,
sequentially, with results reported through $D7FF. The fetch script
makes a sparse checkout of only the CIA directory into ignored .build.
Environment variables select subsets, cap cycles, and write a
tab-separated scoreboard.

First sequential Release scoreboard, repeated once with identical
per-program results: 143 programs complete, 53 pass, 78 fail, 12
upstream-expected failures. TESTING.md records per-program failure
reasons and CompatibilityStatus.md lists the open CIA defects. No CIA
behaviour is changed by this commit.

events.title: Add warp mode, game controller input, and selectable VIC palettes
events.message:
Add warp mode, game controller input, and selectable VIC palettes

Warp mode drops frame pacing on the emulation thread and mutes the
speaker; leaving warp discards the stale audio queue and waits for a
fresh startup fill. Toolbar, Emulation menu (Cmd+Shift+W), status bar,
and inspector expose it.

Game controllers route through the GameController framework. The first
controller follows the joystick routing preference and a second takes
the other port. Controller state is merged with the keyboard joystick
ports so either input works alone; CIA1 now reads the merged ports.

Settings > Display selects between Pepto (C64 Wiki, the previous fixed
table), Pepto PAL (VICE), and Colodore palettes with a swatch preview.
The table swaps between frames on the emulation thread.

Regressions cover merged joystick ports reaching CIA1, muted-speaker
silence and resume, and palette presets reaching VIC output. No VIC,
CIA, SID synthesis, or drive timing changes.

events.title: Drop the approval guard's shell parsing that the canonical-line gate made dead
events.message:
Drop the approval guard's shell parsing that the canonical-line gate made dead

With every non-canonical possible deposit denied up front, the precise
parse only ever sees one plain simple command. The tokenizer loses its
heredoc body scanning, operator splitting and backslash handling outside
double quotes; continuation joining, redirection detection and comment
handling go entirely. A re-parsed string argument (bash -c '...') is
checked against the same canonical rule before it is scanned. Tests for
shapes the old parser handled one by one now assert the single
non-canonical denial instead.

events.title: Deny a possible request deposit that is not one plain canonical line
events.message:
Deny a possible request deposit that is not one plain canonical line

The approval guard now builds a loose view of the command (quotes,
backslashes, backslash-newlines, backticks and $ removed). When that view
mentions finding.mjs or --request, the command is a possible deposit and
the precise title/approval judgment runs only if the raw command is one
simple canonical line: no newline, no unquoted shell metacharacter, every
quoted string a whole word, no $ or backtick inside double quotes. Any
other possible deposit is denied in a chat session with a reason naming
the plain --spec-file/--why-file form. This closes the quote-split flag,
continued heredoc terminator and attached redirection shapes without
extending the tokenizer. The hook wrapper skips on the loose view, and the
stand-down text names the Write-tool file route instead of a heredoc.

events.title: Βήμα 145: ο παίκτης κρατά την όχθη για τις αντλίες — καμία μέτρηση με νερό κάτω από 20, ο 1048 0 στους 64
events.message:
Βήμα 145: ο παίκτης κρατά την όχθη για τις αντλίες — καμία μέτρηση με νερό κάτω από 20, ο 1048 0 στους 64

Στο g144b το νερό του 1048 0 έμεινε κάτω από 20 σε 35 μετρήσεις από το
sol 47, με 34 αποίκους και τρεις αντλίες. Το g144 είχε χάσει εκεί 23 από
αέρα. Ξαναπαιγμένο ως το sol 42, από εκατό όχθες ως τα 40 tiles χωρούσαν
αντλία μόνο δύο: οι θόλοι του big είχαν πιάσει όλη την όχθη δίπλα στο
σκάφος, και οι άλλες όχθες δεν είχαν δομή ως τα 12 tiles.

Αλλάζει μόνο ο παίκτης (tools/play.py, σχέδιο big, Game.keep_shore). Το
παιχνίδι είναι του βήματος 144, byte προς byte. Από τους δεκατέσσερις
αποίκους ο παίκτης κρατά μία θέση αντλίας:
- περνά τον κανόνα του bd_res, και μια αντλία τη φτάνει τώρα;
- είναι όσο πιο κοντά γίνεται στις αντλίες που έχει;
- κανένας θόλος, δομή, διάδρομος ή μονοπάτι δεν τη σκεπάζει, ούτε το
  μονοπάτι της.

Μετρήθηκαν έξι παραλλαγές σε 24 κόσμους × 60 sol:
- Επιλογή με το έδαφος μόνο: ο C0DE 1 έμεινε στο νερό 5.
- Κράτηση από την αρχή: πήρε γη από τον πυρήνα, μέσος στο sol 40 15,2
  αντί για 17,1.
- Χωρίς το μονοπάτι: ο C0DE 2 έχασε τη θέση στο sol 45.
- Η τελική (g145f):
  - νερό κάτω από 20 σε 0,0% των μετρήσεων (g144b 0,5%);
  - μέσος 25,1 στο sol 60 (25,0) και 16,5 στο sol 40 (17,1);
  - 16 θάνατοι (18), κανένας από αέρα ή δίψα;
  - ο 1048 0 στους 64 με πέντε αντλίες (38).
Ως τους δεκατέσσερις και οι 24 κόσμοι παίζουν ακριβώς όπως το g144b.

Οι δοκιμές του παίκτη (noroom, outside, brokenop) περνούν. Το DESIGN.md
γράφει το §10.1 «Water kept, at milestone 145», μια σημείωση στο εύρημα 4
του βήματος 140, και μια λυμένη γραμμή στο §15.

CPC-palette version: MODE 2, 27 colours as 1 x 2 dithers (sh build.sh cpc: lander-cpc.ssd)

The "Amstrad CPC palette": every colour with red, green and blue each off, half or
full, made on a plain BBC as two of MODE 2's eight colours, one on even lines and one
on odd (two MODE 2 pixels one above the other are about square), a half channel lit
on one line of the two (the brighter halves first, each to the darker line so far).
The renderer is the NULA version's, at full resolution: the boxes' even and odd
bytes simply differ now.  proto/nula.py: variant() (NULA=1 or CPC=1), the 20 colour
entries the game uses each given a different CPC colour by the nearest assignment
overall (scipy's linear_sum_assignment), the map's colours as entries.  land.s and
game.s: .ifdef NULA becomes MODE2 but for the palette (CPC: VDU 20, MODE 2's own
colours); nula.inc is mode2.inc.  build.sh cpc; test/identical.sh checks all three
discs (MODE 1 and NULA unchanged); every test passes for all three versions.

events.title: Deny a request whose command carries a redirection, and read continuations joined
events.message:
Deny a request whose command carries a redirection, and read continuations joined

Any redirection, here-string or heredoc word in the simple command of a
finding.mjs --request makes its deposit untitled, so it is always denied; a
heredoc that ends the command stays allowed as finding.mjs's documented
stdin route. &> and >&N are read as redirection words. Bash text is also
scanned with backslash-newline continuations joined, and the deposits of
both readings are judged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: Keep redirection operands and heredoc continuations visible to the approval guard
events.message:
Keep redirection operands and heredoc continuations visible to the approval guard

The << and <<< operators (with an fd prefix) stay words, so a here-string or
heredoc operand can never become a title or approval; {fd} redirections count
as redirections too. Backslash-newline continuations in an unquoted heredoc
body are joined before the substitution check, as bash does.

events.title: ym2612: Sort out ranges and volume level
events.message:
ym2612: Sort out ranges and volume level

Parts of the implementation started tables borrowed from the ym2413
implementation, and to account for different ranges a fixed attenuation
was added to log_carrier_value.

This patch updates that:
 - Exponent table stays the same (remove todo)
 - Exponent lookup shifts left by an extra bit, doubling the range
 - Sine table and lookup stay the same (remove todos)
 - eg_level ant total_level have 6 fractional bits. Left-shift them to
   give a log_carrier_value that has 8 fractional bits matching the sine

   to be implemented for the 2612, but will be done later on as this may
   also tie in to algorithms with more than one operator contributing to
   the output.
 - Channel-6 DAC mode shifted to the same range as the FM channels.
 - Scale the ring-buffer range based on the maximum amplitude of a
   single channel exp lookup.

events.title: docs: plan scripted stop hooks — the trigger, the runner and the API
events.message:
docs: plan scripted stop hooks — the trigger, the runner and the API

docs/stop-hooks-plan.md is the plan of record for glm-features §1, grounded in the
transport's actual code. It revises the sheet in two places: the hook fires on the
published stop (after the register batch) rather than on raw stoppedChanged(true),
where the state is a batch stale and the entry dump may still be printing; and the
engine is an L0 measurement rather than a settled pick — Lua stays on record, with
QJSEngine as the default candidate because the packaging evidence is the fallback
case the sheet named (no vendoring mechanism in the tree at all, and the shipped
licence set is derived from the linked artifact, which a static Lua is invisible to).

The runner's discipline is the substance: queued invocation so its read-back nested
loop is outside the transport's single-entry drain (inside it, the response could
never be parsed — a hang, not a stall), and scripted writes must complete before a
script's continue(), because resume() prunes everything without keepOnResume and a
write queued in the same frame would be dropped silently.

glm-features §1 and PLAN §6 point at it.

events.title: VideoNULA version: MODE 2, sixteen flat 12-bit colours (sh build.sh nula: lander-nula.ssd)
events.message:
VideoNULA version: MODE 2, sixteen flat 12-bit colours (sh build.sh nula: lander-nula.ssd)

The renderer is unchanged: it still works in MODE 1's pixels, 256 across, four a
byte; each MODE 2 pixel shows the even one of the two it covers, so only the masks
(land.s's PM: MASKB, MASKN, LM, PIXM and the immediates; shipgen's KTN) and the
colour bytes (landgen's dither_bytes: solid MODE 2 bytes) change.  proto/nula.py
holds the palette (black, three seas, the pad's grey, seven lands, four ship
colours: each the average of the dither it replaces; land.py's LAND and SEAC
shortened to fit), the mask rule, a 3 x 7 font for the readout and FUEL, and the
build check.  LANDS resets the NULA, sets its palette mode and colours, then
rewrites the ULA's control byte and an identity palette (harmless with a NULA,
MODE 2's own colours without).  game.s: dots and the map marker in the MODE 2
pixel they fall in, the fuel bar's and the map's bytes in NULA colours.

The tests take NULA=1 and check the same reference in MODE 2's bytes; all pass
(landsoak's every soak, shipbtest's 832 drawings, gametest).  build/variant names
the build in build/ and the tests refuse a mismatch.  The MODE 1 disc is
unchanged (identical.sh checks both discs).

events.title: Stamp the original link time into WC1.EXE
events.message:
Stamp the original link time into WC1.EXE

LINK 4.20 writes the current time into the PE file header and cannot be
told otherwise, so every build differed from the original there. The
link rule now stamps the original's TimeDateStamp, 0x32480D3C
(1996-09-24 16:33:00 UTC), with bin/stampPeTimestamp.py. The image has
no checksum or debug directory, so that is the only copy of the time.

With this, the PE headers differ only in fields that follow the layout:
section sizes and addresses, the entry point and the directory
addresses.

events.title: Move the Mac ship unit's functions into ship.c
events.message:
Move the Mac ship unit's functions into ship.c

The Mac build's symbols name the ship unit's functions in order, from
initialize_object through your_afterburner, and they map one for one
onto 0x41DEE0-0x4219BF in the Win32 build. Our tree spread that run
over three files: its first 15 functions sat in disk.c, its last 14 in
logic.c. check_for_lost_control was already in ship.c, so ship.obj and
disk.obj interleaved, an order no link line can reproduce.

ship.c now owns the whole run, disk.c ends at 0x41DEDF and logic.c
starts at 0x4219C0. The rebuilt .text loses 80 bytes of drift there,
and one more function compares byte for byte. ORDER.md also records
mathutil.c's real range, which overlapped disk.c.

events.title: Assemble the raster library from its original source
events.message:
Assemble the raster library from its original source

The raster library was hand-written assembly, rebuilt until now as naked
C functions around inline assembly. That could not reproduce it: its 98
shifts and rotates by one use the D1/D0 encodings, which CL 4.20's
inline assembler never emits, and it keeps tables in its code segment.

src/raster.asm is now its source. bin/extractRasterLibrary.py extracts
it from the retail executable and checks that UASM, a MASM-compatible
assembler added as a submodule and built by make, reproduces every byte
and relocation. The linked library matches the original exactly: code
0x439C40-0x43F635 and data 0x46E69C-0x47008B. The source is plain MASM
6: .model flat, c, whose 4-byte aligned _TEXT and _DATA fit where the
original placed them; all 962 jumps left for the assembler to size; and
MASM's add esp, -N frames.

Where the library starts and ends:
- FillRasterBytes (0x439C10) is compiled C. CL 4.20 compiles
  memset(destination, value, length) to its exact bytes. The mov edi, edi
  before and after it is the NOP padding CL adds after every optimized
  function, not a hot-patch entry, so the library starts at 0x439C40.
- All 1,291 core functions are 16-byte aligned. The only INT3 fill in the
  core is LINK's after the library, which ends unaligned. raster.obj sits
  between screens.obj and killbrd.obj, and its .data between the screens
  literals and the kill board tables.

The library gains DissolveRasterClip (0x43F1AE) and its LFSR tap table,
which the inline version lacked. Its cosine and IFF tables move from
.rdata back into .text. .text is now 0xD70 bytes short of the original,
down from 0x1640.

The SDL build keeps the portable routines, and globals.c defines the
library's data only for that build. The audit config records the one
initialized global the C audit no longer sees. binary-comp now
inventories .asm sources, so the report covers the library: 1,485
functions compared, 1,186 at 100% (from 1,181), 77 below 90%
(unchanged). All 58 library functions and FillRasterBytes are exact, and
make verify passes.

and in FS-UAE on OS 3.2.1 (020) and Workbench 2.05 (68000), from C and
ARexx. ARexx takes a function library's result from A0: the entry

events.title: Strips: plain OCS lores, 1-4 bitplanes, 8-px slot grid (#12)
events.message:
Strips: plain OCS lores, 1-4 bitplanes, 8-px slot grid (#12)

With at most 4 lores planes the copper owns every even DMA cycle, so a
mid-line COLOR MOVE lands every 8 lores px. New kStrips4bplLores table,
calibrated on Copperline (A500 OCS, 68000) with --strips-debug:

- MOVE k lands at x = 8k-13/-9/-5/-1 for gate 0x38/0x3A/0x3C/0x3E.
- 39 slots from gate 0x3E: preload at x=-1, then x = 7, 15, ..., 303.
  A 40-MOVE chain from 0x3C or later ends after the line wraps, so the
  line-255 end-of-line WAIT (VP $FF) is checked on line 256 and the
  copper stalls for the rest of the frame.
- Hblank reset cap 13 MOVEs: 14 delays the chain by 2 CCK and the late
  end cascades into the next line.

The DPF planner becomes encode_strips_indexed<kBaseColors>, driven by an
IndexedLayout row (slot table, register mapping, hblank cap). DPF keeps
its register layout and output; lores uses COLORk directly. A full
hblank reset is used while it fits the cap, else the partial reset.
Lores pixels may use COLOR00; mid-line MOVEs avoid it under
--lock-color0. The EHB stripe debug generator takes the table and depth
so lores --strips-debug reuses it.

One StripsVariant table (mode, dpf -> slot table, label, CLI name)
replaces five copies of the table/label ternary in api.cpp and main.cpp.
run_pipeline's strips dispatch becomes an if-chain. Gates widened in
api.cpp, main.cpp and the web UI; strips dither defaults for lores reuse
the DPF row.

DPF, EHB and HAM6 strips .png/.h/.cpp outputs and CLI text are
byte-identical to the previous build. Every lores configuration tested
(depth 1-4, --slice-changes 7, 256 rows, --no-lock-color0) matches the
png2amiga preview pixel for pixel on Copperline.

Tests: lores strips smoke/content, depth-5 rejection, api-equiv, and
check_strips_replay.py lores cases (depth 1-4, budget, +/-1 px shift,
tall, no-lock). api_pipeline_smoke takes --slice-changes like the CLI.

events.title: grm-v60: resolve far-call trampolines into the destination bank's overlay
events.message:
grm-v60: resolve far-call trampolines into the destination bank's overlay

New FarCallTrampolineAnalyzer handles the switch / JMP (P) / restore
trampoline (wizwarr ff69 -> ff83 JMP ($001b)). Per call site it takes
the pointer's low byte from the caller's register (Y), the bank from A
(through BIT-skip hidden entries, decoded from bytes without touching
the listing), and the high byte from a write-once RAM constant -- one
direct store in the whole program, mirror copies of the same
instruction in other bank overlays counting once. Owner ruling: that
rule is accepted only when every target lands on a JMP/JSR abs entry in
the destination bank; otherwise the site is declined with a NOTE.
A COMPUTED_CALL goes on the JMP (P) site, the target is disassembled in
its overlay, and BankContext gains resolveUnder/switchedByEntry.

wizwarr: instrs.inOverlay 0 -> 3964 (58 call sites, 24 vector slots in
PRG_ALL_B1..B3, 0 declined); golden reviewed and re-blessed. Other 34
NES rows byte-identical. build-and-test.sh check SUITE OK; 9 new JUnit
tests (baseline, idempotence, mirror copies, five negatives).

events.title: fix(zz9000): fix SDK media and audio issues found in ZZPlay guest testing (#2465)
events.message:
fix(zz9000): fix SDK media and audio issues found in ZZPlay guest testing (#2465)

- Read media DECODE flags from offset 12 of the command payload, after the
  64-bit value. Reading them at offset 4 refused ZZPlay's late-frame skip
  flags, so switching to fullscreen stopped playback with "bad request".
- Keep FLAC and Ogg Vorbis input in the session's input ring until it is
  decoded, and count only decoded input as consumed, as the card does. A
  feed is refused only when the ring has no room. ZZPlay's on-card output
  waits on that count and gave up after a second.
- Answer BUSY instead of NEED_INPUT when an FFmpeg session has all its
  input and EOF but has not produced the next frame yet. ZZPlay treats
  NEED_INPUT after EOF as a truncated file.
- Let the FFmpeg worker demux up to 1 MiB of video ahead of its frame
  queue, like the card's video FIFO. A VOB carries audio up to ~0.7 s
  behind its video, and stopping at three frames starved it.

events.title: Rebuild the LZO decoder and file module as the original linked them
events.message:
Rebuild the LZO decoder and file module as the original linked them

The decoder was an /Od function around an __asm block, not a naked one.
The compiler supplied its prologue and the jump to its epilogue, and
ALIGN 4 directives in the block account for the nop and lea ecx,[ecx]
padding inside it; MSVC 4.20's inline assembler pads one- and three-byte
gaps exactly that way. Rebuilt that way, the decoder matches the
original's 0x16E bytes.

In WC1 and WC2 alike, INT3 padding to a 16-byte boundary follows the
decoder, which is how LINK pads between objects. The file module was a
separate object, and it begins with two empty, unreferenced functions
we were missing. They are named ix_file_init_hook and
ix_file_shutdown_hook by analogy with the other ix modules. Move the
file wrappers to ixfile.cpp and give each object a library of its own,
the decoder's searched first. One library holding both pulls the file
module first, because the streamer needs it before the thread needs the
decoder.

The CRT now sits at one constant offset from the original: all 338
functions with a known address are displaced only by the 0x1640 bytes
the core is still short.

make audit-addresses; make audit-compiler-glue; make modern.

The README treated 0x40CB20 (jmp GetJoystickButtons) and 0x434D10

They are ordinary functions: MSVC 4.20 compiles a C function that
returns another call's result, with the core flags, to the same

ReadJoystickButtons is unreferenced, like its neighbour

short and is what PlayScrambleHangarScene calls. The original takes
(RandomWord() + 3) % 4, the signed modulo its code computes, where we
had folded the expression into `dec al; and al, 3` (89.83% -> 94.35%).

FID_conflict, strchr among them, and make verify-calls drops calls into
unnamed library code. A wrong CRT call therefore passed every gate:
RewriteDiskFileGraphicsExtensions called strrchr where the original
calls strchr.

name those functions under calls.known_crt from the matched members:
the two identical copy routines are memmove (0x44D6C0) and memcpy
(0x44EA10, the one realloc and fwrite use), remove and _unlink are told
apart by their position in unlink.obj, and strchr follows its internal
label. Calls into them are now checked; the FID_conflict mismatches in
DebugOverlayConsole::Scroll, DosMemcpy and the joystick calibration
code resolve, and four calls to _exit surface.

events.title: Restore the code the original's CRT order exposed
events.message:
Restore the code the original's CRT order exposed

With the link line reproduced, LIBCMTD members land in the order the
code first references them, and the original's order disagreed with
ours in four places:

- RewriteDiskFileGraphicsExtensions calls strchr, not strrchr.
- DebugOverlayConsole::Scroll calls memmove, not memcpy. The two CRT
  copies are byte-identical; the one realloc and fwrite call is memcpy.
- SetDiskFileNumber (0x41D9B0) was missing. This unreferenced helper
  writes a two-digit disk number into a file name's extension, or uses
  the graphics mode's letter when the name has none. Ghidra had merged
  it into PromptInsertNumberedDisk, and it is the original's first
  caller of strchr.
- ix_file_write (0x46173E) was missing. It wraps fwrite, which is why
  fwrite.obj is linked.

The report compares mnemonics only, so both wrong calls scored 100%.
The two new functions match exactly. All 338 CRT functions with a known
original address now fall into two runs at constant offsets from the
original: the first-pass members, and those after the LZO module, whose
inline-assembly decoder encodes 0x20 bytes shorter than the original.

The two new declarations in the shared headers shift CL 4.20's register
allocation in units that never use them. MinInt and MaxInt in geom.c
trade places between 100% and 83%, depending only on how many
declarations are added. In total 1,176 of the 1,480 functions match
exactly and 73 score below 90%, against 1,168 and 77 before.

Validation: clean make WC1.EXE; make report; make verify, whose data
audit now compares all 1,021 globals with no mismatch; make sort; make
audit-addresses; make audit-compiler-glue; make modern.

events.title: Reproduce the original link line
events.message:
Reproduce the original link line

LINK 4.20 lays out library members in the order their symbols are first
needed, so the retail executable's CRT order, call thunks and import
tables record how it was linked. Link the same way:

- No /ENTRY. LINK then adds WinMainCRTStartup after the command-line
  objects, and wincrt0.obj follows strncmp.obj as in the original,
  instead of leading the CRT.
- Import libraries in the original descriptor order (kernel32, user32,
  gdi32, advapi32, winmm), with dsound and ddraw after the ix libraries,
  whose members their call thunks follow.
- ixlog.obj as the last command-line object: its CRT references precede
  the entry point's. The rest of ix comes from libraries, one per source
  tree its assert paths name: Streamer, win95\dsp and sound. Searched in
  that order they reproduce the exact member order. The LZO and file
  module is a fourth library searched before them, so it is pulled only
  on the second pass, after the RtlUnwind thunk, as in the original.
- The game calls strupr, itoa, ltoa, ultoa, filelength, cprintf and chdir
  by their old names, resolved through OLDNAMES; the original pulls
  their CRT members only on the second pass. The SDL port maps the old
  names to its existing shims, and binary-comp verifies them as aliases
  of the CRT entries.

All seven import tables now match the original's order, including every
KERNEL32 entry, and so do the ix members and the call thunks. docs/ORDER.md
records the evidence.

Validation: clean make WC1.EXE; link order compared with the original's
CRT, thunk and import order; make report and make verify; make modern.

events.title: ui: drop the scratch guard that never fired, and let the rescue close on one answer
events.message:
ui: drop the scratch guard that never fired, and let the rescue close on one answer

The review of this change, each item checked against the tree:

- `documentVanished()`'s guard on `paths::sessionBaseDir()` was dead code. An
  extracted floppy document lives under `paths::documentExtractDir()`, which
  Paths.h documents as deliberately outside the session tree so a sweep cannot
  delete the file behind an open tab — and the extract prune runs at startup, aged
  by the newest activity inside each directory, so it cannot take one mid-session
  either. The guard, its comment and the sentence in ARCHITECTURE all claimed
  otherwise; all three are gone.

- The delete rescue's "Close tab" went through `closeTab()`'s unsaved-changes
  offer: a second modal for a decision the user had just made, whose "Save" would
  recreate the file they deleted and whose "Cancel" would make "Close tab" close
  nothing at all. `closeTab()` takes `promptToSave` now, and the rescue passes
  false — its own prompt is the question.

- `DocumentWatcher::setPaths()` re-adds a path the owner still holds, so that
  path's reported-gone flag has to be cleared with it: a file that came back and
  was then deleted again would have had that deletion swallowed, which is exactly
  what the flag exists to prevent.

- The image-include template said the exported palette is 32 words and put the
  first sprite block at `$0040`. The palette block is `kMaxActive` (16) words —
  32 bytes — so the block after it starts at `$0020`, and the comment says the
  size in bytes now. The GEMDOS template's breakpoint hint named "the `move.w`
  below `message`", a line that does not exist; it names the Crawcin line.

- `WelcomeView::applyAppearance()` joins the other panels', so a theme switch with
  the welcome view on show re-inks its fixed labels rather than leaving the old
  theme's greys behind.

events.message:
tests: write the source a test opens, instead of borrowing one

statusBarShowsCaretAndBuild opened the suite's scratch source (m_source) without
writing it, so it only worked when an earlier test had left that file behind. Run
on its own — which the CI workflow does for a failing suite's functions, one at a
time, to get readable output — openPath's "could not open" is a modal with nobody
to dismiss it, and the test hung until the loop timed out (looking like exit 127
rather than the hang it was).

The test now writes the file it opens, like the other tests that need a source.
Checked the whole list of tests this branch touched by running each one on its
own: all sixteen now pass standalone.
events.author: idontwantyourspamthanks

events.title: ui: a document is a file — New File creates one, and zero documents is a welcome view
events.message:
ui: a document is a file — New File creates one, and zero documents is a welcome view

Every editor tab is now bound to a file on disk: the untitled assembly buffer is
gone as a document state (docs/untitled-plan.md). An .s file exists to be
assembled from disk next to a .PRG, and everything PiST anchors to it — the
build's output paths, the line map, breakpoints (file:line), the blame lane, the
floppy write-back, remote control — is anchored to a real path, so a buffer
without one could not be assembled at all. All three phases of the plan land
together: removing the buffer needs its replacement (the welcome view) in the
same stroke, and the stats and disk-change work sit on the same model.

The swap (plan §4, §5, §8)
- File ▸ New File is a transaction. NewFileDialog over the widget-free
  NewFileSpec validates as it is typed — empty name, a path-shaped or GEMDOS-
  reserved name, an existing target are refused with a sentence; a name longer
  than GEMDOS' 8.3 only draws a note — and creates the file through
  files::write() before anything is opened. Four templates (FileTemplates):
  blank, GEMDOS hello, keyboard/input, image-include.
- The sidebar's New File… runs the same dialog rooted where the user
  right-clicked (FileBrowser::newFileRequested). FileBrowser::createFile is gone
  with its post-hoc validation, and the created file is opened and revealed
  rather than created and forgotten.
- WelcomeView fills the central area whenever zero documents are open: recent
  files, the demo projects on a first run, Open/New actions, toolchain and ROM
  readiness with Setup…, and a small usage shelf. The central area is a
  QStackedWidget (centralPages) whose page 0 is the tabs and page 1 this view —
  there was no zero-document destination before.
- File ▸ Close File (Ctrl+W) and Close All: the tab's × was the only route to
  zero documents. closeTab() returns false when a save was cancelled, so Close
  All stops where the user stopped.
- addEditorTab()/addImageTab()/CodeEditor::displayName() assert a path, and the
  17 filePath().isEmpty() guards in MainWindow.cpp collapse to six: two
  assertions and four image-tab or settings cases (an *image* may still become
  path-less when an import has no file of its own — the deliberate asymmetry).
  Build/Run can no longer skip a focused buffer silently.
- RemoteControl's `save` reply loses its "an untitled document can't be named"
  framing — the document always has a file, so the failure is the write.

Stats (plan §6)
- settings:: counters (sessions, builds, runs, files opened, first-launch date)
  and a last-session summary flushed once at teardown, local to the user's
  QSettings like everything else there. The shelf orients; it is not a
  dashboard.

Disk changes (plan §7)
- DocumentWatcher (support/) watches every open document's path. saveEditor()/
  saveImage() re-arm it after PiST's own staged write. A deletion either closes
  an unmodified tab (the sidebar's own delete — that gesture already asked) or
  offers Close tab / Save a copy… / Cancel; Cancel keeps the buffer bound to the
  name it had, and a later save writes the file again. A deletion under
  paths::sessionBaseDir() is ignored: an extracted floppy document's file is
  PiST's own scratch copy, and sweeping that directory is not the user's file
  vanishing.
- A rename fans out through followRenamedFile(): the open editors and images,
  the breakpoint store's base-name keys (pist::renameFile, unit-tested in
  tst_debug), the sibling .pistproject, settings::renameSource() for the
  last-source pointer and the recents, and the blame lane.

Corrections found while implementing (docs/PLAN.md §9, not silently absorbed)
- The .pistproject has no sourceFile key; the project file is named after its
  source (settings::projectFileFor), so a rename moves <base>.pistproject.
- Breakpoints are in-memory only — src/debug/ has no store — so the rename
  migration is in-process, and the unit test pins the pure transformation.
- The ImageEditor's path-less scratch comes from importFile(), not a region
  extraction, so the plan's non-goal was narrower than stated.
- Measured (untitled-plan §11): on Qt 6.10.2 / Linux 7.0.0 a staged temp-file
  rename over the watched path does not drop the QFileSystemWatcher watch and
  emits no change signal. DocumentWatcher::rearm() is therefore defensive rather
  than load-bearing on that pair; tests/tst_watcher.cpp pins what the design
  needs — a deletion after a re-arm is still reported.

demo/spritedemo/ is tracked with this change: the welcome view's demo row and
the image-include template both refer to it, and ARCHITECTURE.md already
described it while it lived only in the working tree.

events.title: support: report a deletion once, and let the geometry test follow the platform
events.message:
support: report a deletion once, and let the geometry test follow the platform

CI's Windows leg found two more things a Linux run cannot:

- Qt raises the same deletion twice there (the test expecting one report out of
  two deletions saw two), so a watcher that trusted it would tell the owner twice
  about one file going away — and the owner's answer is a modal prompt. The
  watcher now remembers the paths it has already reported gone, and forgets that
  when the owner says the path is live again (`addPath()`, `rearm()`) or the file
  reappears: one report per deletion, whichever platform raised it.

- The offscreen plugin restores the saved geometry with a frame the first window
  never had (measured: 1016×700 restored from 962×700 on the Windows runner,
  exactly on Linux), so the round-trip assertion allows that margin. What it
  still pins is that the saved size comes back at all, rather than the factory
  1280×860.

The Windows measurements join the ledger (docs/PLAN.md §9) and the watcher's
paragraph in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

events.title: tests: pin the window's geometry portably, not to a pixel request
events.message:
tests: pin the window's geometry portably, not to a pixel request

windowGeometryPersistsAcrossRestart asked the window for 760×700 and asserted it
came within 80px of that. The offscreen plugin nudges a requested size and clamps
it to the screen, and the virtual screen is not the same size on every leg of CI
(Windows is the leg that failed), so the assertion was pinning the platform.

The contract is the geometry the user set surviving the restart, which the second
half of the test asserts exactly. Around it, the first window now has to be at
least its own minimum, no larger than the screen, at least the size requested
where the screen and the minimum both allow it (so a resize dropped on the floor
still fails), and smaller than the factory 1280×860 (so the persistence check
cannot be pinning the default). Each failure prints the sizes it saw, instead of
a bare "returned FALSE".
events.author: idontwantyourspamthanks

events.title: support: keep the owner's watch set, and let the geometry test follow the platform
events.message:
support: keep the owner's watch set, and let the geometry test follow the platform

Two things CI's Windows leg found that a Linux run cannot:

- QFileSystemWatcher keeps reporting a path that has been removed from its own
  list while another file in the same directory stays watched (measured on the
  runner: deleting a `forget()`-ed path raised fileChanged for it, so the test
  expecting exactly one report saw two). The document model relies on forget()
  being final — that is what keeps a closed tab, and the sidebar's own delete,
  quiet — so DocumentWatcher now holds the paths the owner asked for and filters
  reports against that set. paths() reports the owner's set too, since a path
  whose watch Qt dropped is still one the owner asked for.

- windowGeometryPersistsAcrossRestart required the window to be no larger than
  the screen, which is not a contract: Windows' offscreen plugin takes the dock
  layout's preferred 962×700 rather than the 760×700 request, where Linux takes
  the request (and clamps it to the screen). What the test pins is now what it is
  named for — the size the window ended at is the size it comes back as — plus
  that the window is at least its own minimum, that the request is honoured where
  the screen and that minimum allow it, and that the resize reached the layout at
  all (below the factory 1280×860). Every failure prints the sizes it saw.

events.title: fix(ci): build the macOS chdman universal and SDL-free (#993) (#994)
events.message:
fix(ci): build the macOS chdman universal and SDL-free (#993) (#994)

The jagcd-tools-macos chdman linked /opt/homebrew/opt/sdl3/lib/libSDL3.0.dylib
by absolute path (MAME's default macOS OSD is sdl3, and every tool links its
ocore), was arm64-only, and carried minos 26.0 because MAME sets no deployment
target. It would not launch on a Mac without Homebrew's sdl3, on any Intel Mac,
or on anything older than macOS 26, which broke jagcd-to-chd for most users.

macOS now builds with OSD=mac, MAME's native Cocoa OSD (ocore_mac is POSIX file
I/O plus system frameworks). Only the chdman project is built, from genie's
Makefile, once per architecture in its own BUILDDIR, then lipo'd;
jagcd-chd-check is built universal too, and both target macOS 11.0. The runner's
SDL is uninstalled before the build, and a new step after signing fails the job
unless both files have arm64 + x86_64 slices, link only /usr/lib and /System,
have minos 11.0, and chdman prints its banner with no Homebrew sdl3 present
(also under Rosetta when the runner has it). The macOS ccache key gets its own
prefix so the new objects are saved.

Closes #993

project.notes: Headless C64/1541/1581 reverse-debugging runtime used by C64RE. v0.12.9 makes an execution breakpoint on the first interrupt-handler instruction fire, persists interrupt-entry stops through checkpoints, and aligns step, step-over and step-return behavior around IRQ/NMI and RTI with VICE monitor expectations. ROMs remain user-supplied; no host CPU or RAM minimum is stated. Evidence: https://github.com/Jondalar/TRX64/releases/tag/v0.12.9 https://github.com/Jondalar/TRX64/commit/db224337d341 https://github.com/Jondalar/TRX64/commit/1e6f73894427 https://github.com/Jondalar/TRX64/commit/212ebaf46857 TRX64 0.13.1 publishes Linux, macOS and Windows archives for x86-64 and ARM64. Development immediately after the release makes until and stepOver honor caller-supplied cycle budgets and changes instructionsElapsed from a mislabeled cycle total to a true retired-instruction count, with real-binary and headless tests. This is upstream evidence only; the tracker did not execute the archives. Upstream daemon tests mount four real-image variants as CRT and raw BIN, freeze and resume a BASIC counter without corrupting underlying RAM, restore frozen checkpoints/dumps and reproduce the same-cycle trace across fresh daemons; copyrighted images remain outside the repository and absent corpora skip. Evidence: https://github.com/Jondalar/TRX64/commit/cd97c39d9997c475213bb834ea36f4b08c103084 https://github.com/Jondalar/TRX64/commit/efbb280be0aed77e63942c322029753c3b30376a

project.status: DOS reconstruction playable; native x64 title text/GRCG paths have bounded differential parity while whole pictures and physical timing remain open
project.notes: Identity and classification remain a PC-98 reconstruction of Touhou 4 with a separate unfinished Linux/Windows x64 port. The current native producer reports 545 programs at b4519b50, 84 GNU and optimized-UBSan build programs, and 82 passing CTests. Upstream now retains 544 original controls and exercises 30 seeded saves/restarts, 24 score and 24 complete Ending registration routes plus eight Extra routes per compiler; independent component images and eight default Demo profiles also pass. These are bounded upstream receipts, not whole-game, physical-scanout or Windows acceptance. Other waits, malformed-score unsafe graphics, real active-PMD timing, broader gameplay and Windows remain open. No safe minimum physical PC-98 or x64 host CPU/RAM profile is stated. Primary commits continue to identify gpt-6.1-sol. Evidence: https://github.com/N0zoM1z0/th04/commit/a80ce900f1a4db8084768be074c73efdb644a977 https://github.com/N0zoM1z0/th04/commit/db797001d42f1ff3298a87dd4e6d33bdb2dfb775 https://github.com/N0zoM1z0/th04/blob/main/README.md Current main pairs the reconstructed and original MAIN programs for 8,000 updates including a real Continue/resumed-gameplay route. Upstream reports matched consumed input, 36 compared fields, 3,042 RNG calls, nine pools and 22 states, while retaining 263 post-reset input differences and making no whole-campaign, Windows or physical-timing claim. Evidence: https://github.com/N0zoM1z0/th04/commit/07f69d3d6c01c3319b9865357f4420120c2f4b85 The native title pass now matches 8,000 title-state boundaries, three complete text rows and ordered BB calls; component checks cover 7,895 cases at each of two loads with complete TRAM and four GRCG planes. A preserved 43-frame one-pixel negative demonstrated that text agreement alone missed graphics phase, and the latest correction withdraws a false phase inference while retaining the natural-picture gap. project.notes: Identity: The creator’s repository contains eight native Apple II games, including original Arkabreakout/ChromaBreak and ports of POM1 games. Reviewed concrete Arkabreakout gameplay assembly, Snake C implementation, ChromaBreak bootstrap/build, and Chess documentation. This is one repository-level collection record, not eight inflated entries. Classification: Native Apple II source collection and ports. Arkabreakout assembles a standalone BRUN binary and DOS 3.3 disk; ChromaBreak builds a ProDOS system file. The bundled a2run/a2shot emulator code serves tests and is not embedded in the games. LOGO, demos and generic dev tooling are incidental to this game-scoped record. Source CPU: The README and Snake header identify POM1 Apple-1/GEN2 versions as predecessors, and Chess documents reused POM1 rules code. Those predecessor files were not independently inspected, so no source CPU is inferred from the target assembly or Apple-1 label. Target CPU: Arkabreakout’s game.s explicitly specifies NMOS 6502 and contains native gameplay assembly. ChromaBreak’s Makefile passes --cpu 65c02; boot.s starts with a 6502 CPU probe and then selects .setcpu "65C02", rejecting an NMOS IIe. These establish separate 6502 and 65C02 outputs, not a single machine minimum. Build: The reviewed game Makefiles invoke ca65/ld65 or cl65 and construct bootable DOS 3.3/ProDOS disks. The README claims deterministic rebuilds and emulator-based tests, but those claims were not independently reproduced; byte_exact remains null. Limitations: Static primary-source review only. No candidate code, build, emulator, gameplay, hardware test or byte comparison was executed; all independent build flags remain null. Runtime profiles: Upstream describes II+ 48 KB/DOS 3.3 for Arkabreakout/classic ports and enhanced IIe or IIc 128 KB/ProDOS for ChromaBreak, with keyboard/paddle or AppleMouse controls. The bootstrap explicitly rejects NMOS machines for ChromaBreak. These are source/author requirements, not independently verified runnable minima. Limitations: Profiles preserve directly observed requirements/author claims only; no independent runtime hardware validation was performed. AI: The latest commit explicitly includes Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>; the same named tool is present in the inspected recent commit sample. This is development-AI evidence, separate from the chess opponent AI. Relationships: The README and source headers explicitly derive the classic games from VERHILLE Arnaud’s POM1 work. Chess credits cc65-Chess for board/piece art and its Apple II port, but identifies its engine as POM1 rules code; this is not another copy of the already catalogued cc65-chess-stewbc-native. GPL-3.0 code, Skinner Microban levels, CC-BY-3.0 sprites and separate Apple ROM/DOS rights are disclosed. No blanket original-authorship or permissive-license claim is made. Normalized roots were screened programmatically against prior-roots.json before file review; current catalogue titles/subjects were checked for aliases. This is bounded lineage review, not proof of complete originality. The root README states Apple II+ 48 KB or //c with mouse or joystick; this is an upstream requirement, not an independent run. Evidence: https://github.com/habib256/pom2games/commit/76e48cf163cfcc52b2c99a9533f4875fd257ca8e https://github.com/habib256/pom2games/blob/9b83dc0c9f56c11a19c02a25fe78e2f5c492e8ea/README.md The repository now includes MCS, a Music Construction Set-inspired two-staff HGR editor with speaker playback, save/reload support and its own build/test target, and Arkabreakout has expanded to 60 sectors with joystick, paddle and AppleMouse II control. Evidence: https://github.com/habib256/pom2games/commit/e58ca7f35a89 https://github.com/habib256/pom2games/blob/main/README.md The collection now includes an in-progress Wilderness: A Survival Adventure reimplementation based on analysis of external WOZ/A2R images: SMALLDOS layout, parser vocabulary, TOPO maps and the SURV3D view were documented, while a new 6502 terrain renderer is compared bit-for-bit with a Python reference on fixed and randomized inputs. The original images remain out of git. Evidence: https://github.com/habib256/pom2games/commit/996971397f77a62c49aef92890dac1d69b5cc338 https://github.com/habib256/pom2games/blob/main/wilderness/docs/ANALYSE.md Neowilderness now ships a 140 KiB Disk II edition for enhanced Apple IIe/IIc 128 KiB and an 800 KiB XL edition for Apple IIe with a 3.5-inch controller or SmartPort-capable IIc/IIc Plus. The latest lot adds ROM-probed crafting, shelters, weapons/tools, persistent fire-until-DOUSE behavior, visible animals and MouseText XL pages; the README continues to document remaining work. The commit explicitly credits Claude Opus 5.5. No disk image was booted by the tracker. Evidence: https://github.com/habib256/pom2games/commit/f07e562562ab46127de6b99f2b3bc2cd8edca605 https://github.com/habib256/pom2games/blob/main/neowilderness/README.md NeoWildernessXL now carries joystick-driven menus, persistent OBJECTS hand/pack selections, quantified water/equipment transactions and a separate TMAP pre-game archipelago program. Upstream reports make test-xl across 21 scripts plus 96 TMAP archipelagos; the tracker did not boot the image, and the existing 128 KiB/storage profile is unchanged. Evidence: https://github.com/habib256/pom2games/commit/d1b369198dbeb50be199be735d1831ca4d417f71
