project.status: active; M23/M24 add evidence-bearing traces, generated source maps/reference docs and field-run acceptance while the 2.0.0 publication gate remains open
project.notes: General-purpose TypeScript C64 reverse-engineering toolkit controlling stock VICE and integrating disk/BASIC/static-analysis/assembly/equivalence workflows. package.json now declares 2.0.0 and publishable CLI/MCP/host bins, while the primary roadmap explicitly leaves npm trusted-publisher setup, the v2.0.0 tag and verification of the published package open. C64RT_TRACE adds per-process JSONL field traces for host requests, VICE lifecycle, MCP calls, native tool runs and stderr without exposing the trace to the agent. Node.js 24+, VICE 3.9+ and user-supplied ROMs remain prerequisites; no host CPU/RAM minimum or independent execution is established. Evidence: https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/blob/main/package.json https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/11987768d056 https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/5ceac29bb61b Current M14 work now generates byte-identical ACME source from an unpacked image or PRG, curated knowledge and Ghidra instructions; an optional loader is run in VICE and checked at the recovered entry state. The documented ten-stage workflow adds explicit acceptance criteria, exit checks, deliverables and coverage reporting. Release comparison can attach first-access/runtime-change evidence to differing bytes, single-release separation reports unpack/access/reachability provenance, and platform symbols can be exported as an ACME include. These are upstream live-tool checks rather than an independent tracker run, and they do not close the separate npm publication gate. Evidence: https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/8e2bbb5a106c2fe339bc2f1aaaa8d02b414a1341 https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/18bc1327744db353667cabf39d81ed373effe078 https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/b80796c63719f7eeb4fd694afd689fe5a926cd8b https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/1c0070e068b719314a4ee47b56de189916b0a6d6 https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/ad164faf2354087ee3c0f7bd8d9e52c36a367fbc M17 now captures CIA timer latches and interrupt masks that ordinary register reads cannot recover, programs generated loaders to restore the reachable timer state, and compares counters, latches, controls and masks at the entry jump. An upstream live test distinguishes the repaired loader from one without CIA restoration. The host also records each skill-script operation and outcome while keeping verbose MCP/VICE tracing opt-in. These are upstream tests; no local VICE run was performed, SID voice 3, TOD phase and interrupt flags remain documented limits, and the npm publication gate remains open. Evidence: https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/5cdc74d5226db7d8123ca782cfb6e9a36a11ee8b https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/15a3bb8f331d0fe8d81976400c04a4e632813b06 M23/M24 now let execution traces continue while recording observations/history, generate linked source maps and program reference pages, and route evidence-producing agent run files into owned run directories. The Bruce Lee acceptance reports 70 reference pages, 1,227 entries, 21 decoded tables and deterministic second-pass linking; these are upstream field-run receipts and do not close the separate npm publication gate. Evidence: https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/4c209ab6e79cbb0a34e3b818bf33d8b6fb92f0ba https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/7a45b671dc7b6efc1f0c6b905e57ae1839a8ce3a https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/9caaff4bf206b429d389fcdf5e94d42919600cd9

project.status: active; current main adds authenticated DM1 PC champion-selection regressions and input-to-present instrumentation
project.notes: Clean-room Dungeon Master-family engine using authenticated original media. Current primary documentation records bounded startup/runtime coverage for DM1 on DOS, Atari ST, Amiga and FM Towns; CSB on Amiga, Atari ST and FM Towns; and DM2 on DOS, Amiga, FM Towns and Macintosh. The latest receipts correct DM1 Amiga HD and DM2 FM Towns boot assertions and expand the cross-game startup matrix and diagnostics. These source-owned handoffs do not establish full campaign, save, display or audio parity; Nexus and Theron's Quest remain explicitly bounded, with authentic level/campaign consumers still incomplete. Evidence: https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/blob/main/docs/PROJECT_STATUS.md https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/7791b08de76e https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/17a20bdb465e The newest authenticated-media pass discovers the DM1 Amiga 3.6 archive from configured data roots, covers its root-menu scan, records an Amiga startup-media matrix and wires DM1 PC34 soundtrack selection to WAV playback. These remain bounded startup/audio receipts rather than full-game parity. Evidence: https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/d3b50c77c364455674d783c6bf4d4755777dbc44 https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/ec51d5c1b2f58b51b235fc2145abb384d55b597c https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/da1e85756e618dd321ec42257cb31afbb2b341d1 v3.0.376 receipts now cover DM1 Amiga 2.0 resume, the published Linux x86-64 AppImage under QEMU on an ARM64 VM, and the DM2 FM Towns selected-hero HUD icon sourced from authenticated interface data. They do not establish native x86-64 hardware, physical input, aura/panel completion or full visual parity. The release also publishes Android and iOS arm64 artifacts; publication alone is not runtime verification. Evidence: https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/releases/tag/v3.0.376 https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/e0cf778c39b039918d6b1ae1ebf18e23ec423b1a https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/f0c58017d243551f9dbf30ae5b28fb25172bd10e https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/1be613b14f3cef9e2323a3e2b6ed840e13f6c480 Current-main receipts add native Mac mini M4 DM1 title/door pacing into runtime and authenticated FM Towns startup checks for DM1, CSB and DM2. A four-run French Atari ST test also narrowed an earlier no-output incident to a plausible uninitialized-menu fallback, while explicitly leaving historical causation, physical input, display/palette and audible-speaker parity open. Evidence: https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/7256c2f693a8f2a609ebccfcb687f5e1f8c00868 https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/47bc75ce1f897306e74d2e79a0c053209684edd9 https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/3b729320e80658a8eae965f11c1b5f1bd880f5a3 Current-main Amiga work now paces DM1 A20 palette fades and title zooms against absolute 20 ms source deadlines rather than adding host VSync latency. An authentic Amiga v2.0 native Cocoa run on a Mac mini M4 completed the five-fade title in 1,698 ms (366 ms zoom, 500 ms hold, 166 ms final fade); this does not establish HiDPI/pixel parity or beam-line 152 timing. The authenticated Japanese FM Towns CSB save regression now asserts restored map 0, party position 13,13, direction 1 and four champions through direct launch and the live menu-resume route. Evidence: https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/1538eeab7f46d6318be1c6cd89a55a9edc6d5d87 https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/1d3f8e34d62d0cd9b95d74d9fd33b1bb35eb1a6e https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/087aed4bf4b977cb30805152519c82860ff2ed20 Current-main receipts add an authenticated DM2 Amiga viewport gate, bounded DOS viewport/HUD checks and a locked three-draw fresh-weather RNG bootstrap. Separate native Mac M4 tests keep live Retina input unresolved despite controlled 2x/mixed-geometry tests, and real-media startup reruns use dummy video/audio, so they do not establish physical display, input or speaker parity. A separate authenticated PC 3.4 path decodes the LZEXE-packed DOS selector preview. Targeted source-lock/native-build checks pass upstream, but the author explicitly retains original-frame comparison and full cross-platform visual parity as open. Evidence: https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/9a2b86019bfcd6bd513213bc21cd402a4f5adaf0 https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/2a85ec7e1801b58d22232fa11ccc5f18a0e9bd0d https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/41b103f29b4d7439d7445fb4e3578f9985e5cfab https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/3085c2f6d56e8088279b5207bfd46744a1dbbd24 The Apple IIGS path now decodes original dungeon worlds, graphics, startup/font, creature/effect metadata and sound, launches authenticated worlds through the CLI/M12 path, and connects native IIGS mirror recruitment. Primary recovered documentation explicitly identifies hidden Apple IIGS graphics.dat code as 65C816 code, supporting the added source architecture. Current changelog receipts also cover stereo DOC effects, Hall progression, inventory transfer, food use and carrying capacity; wall damage, sensors and full sound/presentation parity remain open. No Apple IIGS minimum RAM or host profile is inferred. Evidence: https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/26f1361e5b3d18512db35b7b0791b84f4e4385da https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/9a7458e5fc0b0f019cbe4284bd9d68384050a56b https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/blob/439213c5ba9fbd79d0753d6143a3b86ff9f0d90f/reference/dmweb-community-docs/html/community/documentation/dungeon-master-and-chaos-strikes-back/graphics.dat-hidden-code.html The DM1 PC34 path now preserves the original status-box priority over overlapping ready-hand zones, verifies consecutive champion switches with authenticated data and prevents held-key selector skips. Debug traces separately measure queue, source-outcome and present-return timing while explicitly marking physical scanout unmeasured. project.display_title: Carmageddon — incremental DOS executable reconstruction
project.status: Active function-by-function Carmageddon reconstruction; DrawLine2D is exact and FollowCheatyPath is behavior-equivalent
project.notes: Buildable native Carmageddon reimplementation that replaces original DOS executable assembly with C function by function. Historical Watcom symbols exist but do not match released-code positions. Current CI builds and tests Windows x86/x64, Linux x64/arm64 and macOS x86_64/arm64 variants; no minimum host hardware is documented. The latest reviewed commits report exact reccmp matches for GetGraphicsOptions, ChangingView and drpixelmapcopy, demonstrating incremental function parity rather than whole-program completeness or playable parity. Evidence: https://github.com/dethrace-labs/dethrace/commit/ff723168a9b458252ce40bb6e0ceb008cb4dcc35 https://github.com/dethrace-labs/dethrace/commit/80898db36d16d584d50789a9f8d05cdf2ed8458f https://github.com/dethrace-labs/dethrace/commit/d5b90d885b298c9ca338c9060468f899ca095fab Four merged reconstruction PRs add SwingCamera, ObjectGrooveBastard, PathGrooveBastard and FunkThoseTronics. PathGrooveBastard reports a 100% match; the other PRs distinguish equivalent/effective behavior from lower similarity percentages, so they are not described as byte-exact. Each PR explicitly labels the work AI generated and records time/token totals, establishing AI use without identifying a model or tool. Evidence: https://github.com/dethrace-labs/dethrace/pull/1191 https://github.com/dethrace-labs/dethrace/pull/1192 https://github.com/dethrace-labs/dethrace/pull/1193 https://github.com/dethrace-labs/dethrace/pull/1194 Current main adds a 100% reccmp match for DrawLine2D and a separately qualified behavior-equivalent FollowCheatyPath result. The latter is deliberately not promoted to an exact or whole-executable claim. Evidence: https://github.com/dethrace-labs/dethrace/commit/d16bdad486c66fd77e7ac69231526ea22c3df753 https://github.com/dethrace-labs/dethrace/commit/50c1e867f2d4d44224d3f527f70ffd7f1c93614e

project.status: active; v0.6.5 development head adds deterministic rewind/input movies, logic analysis and raster-timing diagnostics
project.notes: Emulates CPC 464/6128, Plus and GX4000 with per-model CRTC/Gate Array timing, disc and tape support, a debugger and embedded RASM. Inspected src/core includes Z80, CRTC variants and debugging code. project.title: Copperline
project.display_title: Copperline — Amiga emulator & reverse debugger
project.status: active; Fat Gary warm-reset semantics now preserve COLDBOOT state across RESET while restoring it only on power-on
project.notes: Cycle-driven Amiga emulator with reverse stepping and source debugging. Native screenshot capture preserves original pixels before presentation effects, and memory-write output follows WinUAE conventions. WASM board plugins can now opt into manifest-scoped persistent-resource writes; upstream tests cover capability denial, bounds, reset/cache coherence and host-file write-through. Current main preserves AGA Alice's hard $D8 bitplane-fetch stop, weaves both chipset fields into full-height native interlaced screenshots and persists menu-only settings without discarding launcher-less keys. A second change adds CYL.SIDE display plus WinUAE/FS-UAE floppy sample-set playback while serializing mechanism events so save states, run-ahead and netplay checksums do not depend on installed host sounds. These are targeted fidelity/tooling improvements rather than universal compatibility proof. Evidence: https://github.com/CopperlineHQ/Copperline/commit/9e8359ea6cce6fc5e5028d1f4e31b960b53f7da6 https://github.com/CopperlineHQ/Copperline/commit/c3220bc325d68f85a5730b50627ef419879b19a2 The Fat Gary model now keeps COLDBOOT clear across keyboard/CPU warm reset and sets it only on power-on, matching the documented WinUAE behavior and preserving A3000/A4000 Kickstart state such as boot-menu choices, residents and recoverable RAM disks. Chip-, bus- and CPU-level regressions cover the path. Evidence: https://github.com/CopperlineHQ/Copperline/commit/535fb60a828d88c292935c536b269ac512d301af

runtime_profiles.name: C64RE workbench
runtime_profiles.os: Node.js 22 or newer; TRX64 0.13.1; user-supplied Commodore ROMs
runtime_profiles.notes: No minimum host CPU or RAM is stated.

project.status: source/package 0.9.1; every e2e/smoke/test/probe script is gated or carries a reasoned exception, and gate execution is parallelized
project.notes: C64 forensic and semantic-disassembly workbench. The Node.js 22+ application verifies reconstructed assembly with byte diffs and now pins TRX64 0.12.9 with user-supplied ROMs. The current changes use execution breakpoints for reachability claims, prevent duplicate equate definitions in relocated listings, preserve byte-identical rebuilds, and scope negative knowledge claims to their owning evidence coverage. A separately running C64 Ultimate bridge exposes the TRX64 wire protocol to multiple clients; hardware execution remains gated on a successful emulator run of the same bytes. Evidence: https://github.com/Jondalar/C64ReverseEngineeringMCP/commit/669c1346e4ec https://github.com/Jondalar/C64ReverseEngineeringMCP/commit/74fe38185ca5 https://github.com/Jondalar/C64ReverseEngineeringMCP/commit/cbfcadbf92b3 https://github.com/Jondalar/C64ReverseEngineeringMCP/commit/f68fe3d28d92 The current platform pass adds explicit VIC-20 and TED-machine tags, Plus/4 BASIC 3.5 listing/tokenization, VIC-20/TED BASIC-stub recognition and signature-based raw-cartridge placement. Follow-up fixes emit outside-image addresses as equates and place names inside relocated blocks at the defining instruction while preserving every reference. Evidence: https://github.com/Jondalar/C64ReverseEngineeringMCP/commit/38f1292610839c16db44f06a565a0ee4e49693f5 https://github.com/Jondalar/C64ReverseEngineeringMCP/commit/86f2e560ae1608c751018daac2abf2af5c63120e https://github.com/Jondalar/C64ReverseEngineeringMCP/commit/be6a640cbcd7d217562502fdd3b28f7cb613af52 The source/package version is now 0.9.1 and pins TRX64 0.13.1. Subsequent fixes keep a hand-written knowledge/NEXT.md byte-identical across step recording and sandbox completion, while human zero-page labels suppress redundant KERNAL/BASIC platform hints without changing reconstructed bytes; upstream reports its 126/126 gate for both changes. No local package or Neuromancer/IM2 fixture run was performed. Evidence: https://github.com/Jondalar/C64ReverseEngineeringMCP/commit/829f623063d6da0abdef9f228abd613324e8c4ae https://github.com/Jondalar/C64ReverseEngineeringMCP/commit/82e1341556341e74644d876ed50f07c4736ae761 https://github.com/Jondalar/C64ReverseEngineeringMCP/commit/ec27379fe04a90c8a1cd3abb854b0b427aefee5a The repository now statically requires every e2e/smoke/test/probe script to be in the gate, reached from one, or carry a one-line exclusion reason; 96 formerly orphaned scripts joined and the exception list is empty. A bounded worker pool adds per-step logs/timings and limits concurrent runtime services while preserving serial setup and final leak checks. Missing ROMs, daemons and local-only samples skip loudly. Evidence: https://github.com/Jondalar/C64ReverseEngineeringMCP/commit/8b09b50a5aec44d9b56017a7890f0ac4f415aaaa https://github.com/Jondalar/C64ReverseEngineeringMCP/commit/c66d81639073b40d09abc447848b346fcfb556ac

project.status: v8.4.0 published; development head expands the WinUAE-derived remote GDB monitor and debugging surface
project.notes: General-purpose UAE/WinUAE-derived Amiga machine emulator. v8.4.0 publishes Windows ARM64/x86-64, macOS universal and Linux ARM64/x86-64 assets, establishing upstream compilable and runnable variants without establishing minimum hardware. The release adds ZZ9000 AHI/SANA-II/SDK/MHI/MPEGA/image/ZZPlay support, optional external MiniGL and dma-buf paths, relative media paths, cartridge and .A1000 ROM handling, runtime GL fallback, Raspberry Pi 4 drawing improvements, ARM64 JIT fixes, FreeBSD amd64/aarch64 CI and broad networking/display/input/libretro/Android corrections. m68k remains the guest CPU; ARM/x86/RISC-V/LoongArch are host families, not guest minima. External Kickstart ROMs and game media remain outside the GPL source grant. No independent execution or equivalence test was performed. Evidence: https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/releases/tag/v8.4.0 https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/blob/master/README.md Post-v8.4.0 development fixes apply RetroArch auto-loaded save states only after the emulated CPU loop is active, correct CIA-B time-of-day increments in fast and programmed-sync paths, preserve open-file keys across host renames, honor cache-inhibited pages in 68030/68040/68060 fast-cache paths and restore USE_PPC=OFF linking. These are source-level fixes on current main, not a new published release or independently executed verification. Evidence: https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/71ac39e07d339d9d8e296e15db79642e6ab5619a https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/3b5e647578e667adff3a88ef9557e2f3702b8ebe https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/bdc870008140cff3dbbb4379df94aa92d7322e27 Current main ports WinUAE's optional loopback GDB remote server, disabled by default and unavailable with the threaded CPU, with m68k registers, physical RAM/ROM, stepping, breakpoints, watchpoints and memory-map support. A separate MacPorts integration covers Apple Silicon and x86 hosts and explicitly credits ChatGPT for substantial assistance; this extends the AI record without implying whole-project generation. Evidence: https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/4faddbe399757a663fb3f2e8dc4be678eda96d4d https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/831f13e71ee6e872d6d3570f2c23068493d0dd15 Development head now honors database-requested 68040 AGA configurations, disables cycle-exact mode when requested, aligns Android previews with the launched CPU/FPU configuration and follows with 68030 database handling. IPC was redesigned to keep up to 16 clients across frames, bound per-frame work, cap requests at 64 KiB and queue replies without blocking the emulation thread. These guest CPU selections are emulated configurations, not Amiberry host target CPUs or minimum machines. No tracker-side WHDLoad or IPC run was performed. Evidence: https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/5dc6c79f956b4a76b793cbc957242cb65345fed7 https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/69b4be8173 https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/2685d3e774cbdd3c99db0cee66aa6836642ed36c Development head ports WinUAE monitor extensions for AmigaDOS entry stops, Exec task controls, exceptions, DMA/range watchpoints, guest diagnostics, input, screenshots and frame checkpoints. Follow-up fixes bound replies, preserve resets, report checkpoint write failures and safely disassemble at memory-bank ends. This is source-level development evidence, not a new v8.4.0 release or an independent run. Evidence: https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/42335beeafe955c81df4dec31dd508867a6b3b4d

project_inventory_sync: give a CRT manifest without an image link its .crt back (#132)

The manifest repair of 128c48ec re-labels a manifest.json that an older extract_crt
left as a prg disasm-target, but the same damage had dropped the record's
sourceArtifactIds. Spec 909 mints a cartridge only from a crt-manifest that names
its image, so that cartridge was never registered, and disasm filed its banks under
the project's other cartridge as "the project's only cartridge".

- the repair also links a crt manifest with no cartridge-image source to its image,
  found by bytes: every chip file must equal the image at the chip's offset + 16
  (two images with the same header name and size are told apart); none or more
  than one match -> no link, never a guess

events.title: main: Check Workbench for RTG without opening it
events.message:
main: Check Workbench for RTG without opening it

In AUTO display mode open_display() called LockPubScreen() on
Workbench and the default public screen to see whether they use RTG.
On a floppy boot Workbench is still closed, and LockPubScreen() opens
it, which takes about 44 KB of Chip RAM just before xSysInfo opens its
own screen. Look the screens up in the public screen list instead.

A closed Workbench on a Picasso96 or CyberGraphX system will open on
the graphics card, so when rtg.library or cybergraphics.library is
loaded and no Workbench is open, still open it to check, as before.

On a 512 KB A500 with Kickstart 3.1 or 3.2.3 the floppy failed with
"Could not open screen". Together with skipping mmu.library on a 68000,
it now starts in 8 colours.

events.title: hardware: Skip mmu.library on a 68000
events.message:
hardware: Skip mmu.library on a 68000

A 68000 or 68010 has no MMU, but both identify.library and xSysInfo
loaded mmu.library whenever SetPatch had run. That library takes about
50 KB, and on a 512 KB Amiga with Kickstart 3.1 or 3.2 the floppy then
could not open its screen. Check AttnFlags before opening it, and update
identify to do the same and to skip openpci.library, which a 24-bit
CPU cannot use either.

On a 512 KB A500 this leaves about 53 KB more Chip RAM free before the
screen opens. A 68030 still loads mmu.library and reports its MMU.

does, so every built-in board is found regardless of its ID.

events.title: mmu/68k: $400000..$F9FFFF and writes to $0..$7 bus-error; a fault while stacking a group-0 frame halts the CPU
events.message:
mmu/68k: $400000..$F9FFFF and writes to $0..$7 bus-error; a fault while stacking a group-0 frame halts the CPU

Matches Hatari's ST map (memory.c memory_map_Standard_RAM with TOS at $FC0000, no IDE):
$0..$3FFFFF stays void/MMU-aliased, everything from $400000 to the cartridge port is
BusErrMem, and SysMem_*put bus-errors any CPU write below $8 (previously a generic
failwith that killed the run). A bus or address error while EnterGroup0Vector pushes its
frame is a double bus fault: Cpu.Halted is set, Step() idles deaf to interrupts, and the
loop detector no longer aborts on the frozen state. A fault pushing an interrupt frame now
takes vector 2/3 (and normally halts) instead of escaping Step().

Gates: verify 5000000 PASS; 30M diskless, pm142/rand1 and pop/game_start snapshots
byte-identical to the pre-change build; selftest 1000051 pass, 0 wrong, 9 skip.
PowerMonger byte6 36/38/42 (pm156 b6_NN_0): the record read at $1162e hits $00f95600 and
bus-errors before the illegal word at $11640; the game's vector-2 handler ($112a:
clr.l $2c1ba / rte) returns to the stacked fault address, re-faults 1389 times walking
SSP down to $14, and the frame push to $6 double-faults: CPU halted, no TOS bombs.

events.title: report: Write reports in English regardless of the catalog
events.message:
report: Write reports in English regardless of the catalog

A report mixed languages: its section labels were fixed English, while
the values came through the catalog, so a German system wrote "Keine"
and "K.A." between English labels. Reports are read by other people,
usually in issues and forums, so they are now English throughout.

get_string() returns the built-in text while a report is being
written. Strings that detection stored for later display (model, CPU,
FPU, MMU, clock, mode, card slot, graphics system and the benchmark
comment) are now stored as built-in text and translated when the GUI
shows them, so the report never meets a translated value and the GUI
keeps its language. The MMU list keeps its translated lines for the
GUI and records which catalog string each came from, so the report
builds the page-size and hint lines again in English.

The CPU revision stores nothing when unknown instead of a translated
"N/A", which the display code compared against the English literal.

events.title: feat(ipc): expose the GDB monitor commands over the IPC socket (#2464)
events.message:
feat(ipc): expose the GDB monitor commands over the IPC socket (#2464)

* feat(debug): export gdb monitor commands to host callers

Add gdb_monitor_command() so a host caller can run the same text as GDB
monitor without a client. step-over and checkpoint are refused because
they complete inside the GDB stop loop.

* feat(debug): keep monitor stops when no gdb client is connected

Watch, exception-mask, and process-break hits enter the native debugger
instead of being dropped, and the stop reason is kept for the host. A
GDB connection is refused while IPC monitor state is installed, so detach
cannot clear it.

* feat(ipc): add a MONITOR passthrough to gdb monitor commands

MONITOR runs the host monitor entry point and returns result lines as
fields. State changes require pause or a stopped debugger. step-over,
checkpoint, and input sequence are refused and name the IPC command to
use instead. DEBUG_STATUS includes the monitor stop reason.

* fix(ipc): arm breakpoint tracing when a condition changes

condition add and condition remove now call debugger_breakpoints_changed(),
the same helper SET_BREAKPOINT uses. While the native debugger is stopped
that helper leaves trace_mode alone; debug() rearms TRACE_CHECKONLY from
enabled breakpoint slots on the way out. While paused it arms or disarms
tracing immediately, so a condition installed during PAUSE fires after
RESUME. Clearing the last condition does not drop a console process
breakpoint's TRACE_CHECKONLY.

* fix(debug): refuse GDB attach from live IPC monitor state

gdb_monitor_ipc_active() now reads the monitor object instead of a flag
written only after an IPC command. A process-break hit clears process_armed
inside check_stop and does not send another command, so the old flag kept
refusing GDB after the one-shot was gone.

* fix(debug): keep console process tracing when monitor trace ends

history off and process-break clear call debugger_sync_monitor_trace()
even when that monitor feature was already off. Clearing TRACE_CHECKONLY
whenever no breakpoint slot is enabled also dropped the console process
breakpoint, which uses the same trace mode with processptr or processname
and no bpnodes slot. Other trace modes were already left alone.

* fix(debug): keep the no-client stop check visible to WinUAE merges

The process-break check and the memwatch stop text were changed without
an AMIBERRY guard. A later WinUAE merge can replace those lines and drop
the native-debugger stop. The non-Amiberry side keeps the original
gdb_server_connected() test.

* fix(ipc): clear the debugger stop reason when execution resumes

DEBUG_CONTINUE, DEBUG_STEP, and DEBUG_STEP_OVER now clear reason=. Without
that, a watch stop left T05awatch: in DEBUG_STATUS after continue, because
debug() is not entered again. The docs name the awatch, watch, and rwatch
prefixes and state that reason= is empty unless stopped=1.

* fix(debug): report a condition stop in DEBUG_STATUS

A condition uses the breakpoint table, so the native stop had no monitor
reason text. Record the slot as T05breakpoint:N so a condition installed
over IPC is visible in reason= while stopped=1.

* docs(debug): correct watchpoint limits and the detach clear list

A watchpoint range must end at or below the limit, which is $01000000
with 24-bit addressing, not $7FFF0000 unconditionally. The 64 KiB cap
holds for GDB data watchpoints, watch range, and dma-watch; watch add
takes sizes of 1, 2, or 4 bytes. Restore and detach also clear
conditions, history recording, the watch event log, and held input.

* fix(ipc): count captured output and held input as IPC monitor state

A GDB detach clears everything in the shared monitor object, but the ownership check only looked at armed state. Guest-output records kept after 'guest-output off', and keys or controls held by 'input event', did not block a GDB connection, so its detach dropped the records and released the input. The check now covers everything detach() clears except the last captured exception record. docs/ipc.md lists the commands that release each kind of state.

* fix(ipc): report reason= only while the debugger is stopped

Only the step and continue requests cleared the saved stop text, so leaving the debugger through DEBUG_DEACTIVATE or the console left an old reason in DEBUG_STATUS. Emit it only when stopped=1.

* fix(ipc): recompute trace from every source and keep input out while GDB owns the monitor

debugger_breakpoints_changed() cleared TRACE_CHECKONLY when the last breakpoint slot went away, even with history recording or a program-entry break still armed, so removing a condition (over MONITOR or CLEAR_BREAKPOINT) silently stopped both. It now recomputes trace from all sources: breakpoint slots, the console process breakpoint, and monitor history and entry breaks; MONITOR calls it after every state change, which replaces debugger_sync_monitor_trace().

input event and input release were still accepted while a GDB client was connected, so IPC could hold a key that the client's detach would then release. Both are now refused like the other state changes.

* fix(ipc): answer IPC while GDB has the CPU stopped

gdb_server_stop() loops on gdb_server_poll() and the message pump and never returns to handle_events(), so read-only MONITOR queries and status commands got no reply until GDB resumed the guest. The loop now also services IPC, as the native debugger wait already does. State changes stay refused while a GDB client is connected.

* fix(ipc): reject control bytes in MONITOR commands

Control bytes in MONITOR arguments could bypass refusal checks because
monitor_refusal compared the full std::string while gdb_monitor_command
received c_str() and truncated at NUL. Reject bytes below 0x20 in
HandleMonitor before the refusal check, and pass const std::string& to
gdb_monitor_command so both sides inspect identical bytes.

* fix(ipc): isolate monitor condition slots from IPC breakpoint commands

IPC SET_BREAKPOINT and CLEAR_BREAKPOINT operated on raw bpnodes[] slots
without awareness of monitor condition ownership. Skip condition slots
during auto-allocation, reject explicit requests for a slot holding a
condition, and leave condition slots untouched during CLEAR_BREAKPOINT
ALL or CLEAR_BREAKPOINT <addr>.

* fix(ipc): refuse state saves while the CPU is stopped by the debugger

Taking SAVESTATE or QUICKSAVE while the CPU is stopped in debug() (either
via a GDB stop or a native debugger stop) produces a corrupted state file
that loops on JIT fault redirection upon restore. Refuse both commands
while debugger_is_stopped() or gdb_server_halted() is true, and direct
callers to resume or PAUSE first so the save occurs at a frame boundary.

* fix(ipc): reject file paths exceeding MAX_DPATH

IPC handlers taking file paths (HandleLoadState, HandleSavestate,
HandleScreenshot, HandleInsertFloppy, HandleInsertCD, HandleLoadConfig,
HandleInsertWHDLoad) copied client strings into fixed MAX_DPATH buffers
or downstream functions expecting bounded paths. Reject paths of length
MAX_DPATH or greater with an error before attempting any copy.

events.title: image: Add Apple2 .nib, .nic, .dsk, .do and .po images
events.message:
image: Add Apple2 .nib, .nic, .dsk, .do and .po images

Two nibble formats and three sector formats of the Apple2 and Agat
world, in src/image/apple2.c.

.nib holds 35 tracks of 6656 GCR bytes as the Disk II controller reads
them, the common format of disk dumps. The format has no room for the
sync bytes' trailing zero bits, so the host's controller aligns on the
data instead and keeps the alignment through the all-ones gaps, which is
how such images have always been emulated.

.nic is the format of the SDISK// emulator, common on the Agat: 35
tracks of 16 blocks of 512 bytes, the first 416 bytes of each block one
sector as a ready bit stream with its sync bits, the rest zero padding. A
track streams as its 16 sectors back to back, the same 6656 bytes as a
.nib track, so one handler serves both, reading whole blocks and copying
their 416 bytes into the bit-cell ring.

A sector image's 16 sectors of 256 bytes per track stream as the .nic
blocks of the same disk would, made as the track is read: the self-sync
bytes, the address field with volume 254, which the image does not
keep, and the 6-and-2 data field. A .do is in DOS 3.3 order and a .po
in ProDOS order; a .dsk is in DOS 3.3 order unless block 2, where
ProDOS order puts the volume directory, starts as a ProDOS volume
directory's key block, so that renaming the file overrides a wrong
guess. 35 to 40 tracks are taken, and the 128-byte trailer naming the
disk that some Agat images end in, which is left as it is.

All of them stream their bytes as 4us bit cells with the generic
raw-bitcell flux code. In Apple2 mode the formats are told apart by
extension alone, from the list apple2_image_type[], which also names
the type on the display; image_valid() leaves a sector image of other
than 35 to 40 tracks out of the list, as it does an HFE above 1.25 MB,
so that the 840K disks of the Agat do not show there, and the scan's
log line counts both.

Writes decode the sampled bit cells back into nibbles the way the
controller does, eight bits from a 1 bit on, the zeros between them being
the sync bits, and collect them in the staging buffer, which keeps 8 KB
ahead of the volume cache for this, until the write is complete. Then
they go into a .nib track at the byte where the write began, around the
track's end if need be, a track written whole being cut at the track's
length as HFE does; and into the fixed places of the .nic blocks: an
address field, D5 AA 96 and four 4-and-4 pairs, names its sector in the
third pair, and a data field, D5 AA AD and 343 nibbles, goes to the
sector of the address field before it in the same write, or, for the
usual sector write by DOS, to the sector the write began in. That keeps
the image as the SDISK// tools expect it. Blocks are read, patched and
written back whole. In a sector image each data field whose nibbles and
checksum are good goes into its sector; any other is dropped with a log
line in the format of the other sector images, which shares their
string.

After the .nib handler of Oleg Odintsov's Gotek firmware 307 for the
Agat, the gotek-sa390 project of https://svn.code.sf.net/p/agat-hardware/code,
which mounted the images writable and dropped the writes.

events.title: ui: decouple the edit caret from the program counter
events.message:
ui: decouple the edit caret from the program counter

Pressing Run moved the caret to the program's first line: the entry stop was
handled like every other stop, and the editor followed the PC into the file with
gotoLine() — caret, centred view and focus. Every later stop did the same,
including a breakpoint firing while the user was typing. The editor now marks
where the machine is and leaves the caret alone unless it has been handed over
(docs/cursor-plan.md is the spec of record for the behaviour).

  - MainWindow gains the ownership state: m_pcFollow (the user has given the
    caret to the PC), m_pcPlaced (the session's first stop is a *placement*, not
    a movement — marker and chips only), and m_pcFollowInProgress (the guard that
    keeps the follow path's own caret move from reading as the user taking the
    caret back). All three reset in clearSessionViews, so a session ends with no
    claim on the caret.
  - locationFromPc() therefore splits in two. A placement or a released stop sets
    the marker through setExecutionMarker(), which clears it on every other open
    editor so a marker always means "the program is here"; a following stop opens
    and raises the PC's file and moves the caret under the guard. A file the PC
    walks into is no longer opened on a stop the user did not claim.
  - Three engage affordances, one behaviour (followExecution()): Run ▸ Follow
    Execution (checkable — the tick *is* the ownership), a click on the session
    chip, and a click on the ▶ the gutter paints on the marker line. Every other
    caret movement releases the claim through the same cursorPositionChanged;
    Run to Cursor releases explicitly, being a caret gesture that moves nothing.
  - CodeEditor gains followExecutionLine() — no focus, and it scrolls only when
    the marker's line is not already on screen — beside the unchanged gotoLine(),
    which stays the user navigation. The gutter reserves a column for the ▶ and
    reports its click as executionMarkerClicked(); setCurrentExecutionLine() now
    repaints the gutter itself, which the follow path used to do by scrolling.

Verified against real Hatari sessions: seven new tst_gui tests (the placement
leaves caret/scroll/focus, a passive stop moves the marker only, all three
affordances, following moves the caret without taking focus, a caret move
releases, following across files opens and raises only while claimed, an unmapped
PC clears the marker), each of which fails on the pre-change tree — three of them
behaviourally, the rest on the affordances not existing yet. A render test pins
the wedge's column against the click test that finds it, which needs no emulator
and caught the lane-relative paint bug. Full suite green.

Docs: the plan's §9 ledger records the reversal, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md documents the
model, and the README, AGENTS.md and the stale code/test comments that claimed the
old behaviour are rewritten in the same pass.

events.title: Fixed cmdline args to main() so argv[0] == NULL.
events.message:
Fixed cmdline args to main() so argv[0] == NULL.

Several applications have been ported to KOS that have either asserted
or have otherwise bitten us due to attempting to dereference the argv[]
array passed to main().

Yes, an argc of value 0 is valid; however, argv[argc] is REQUIRED by the
C, C++, and POSIX specs to ALWAYS be a NULL value, such that argv[] is a
NULL-terminated array of C strings, which can be iterated over without
even inspecting argc.

1) init.c
    - Modified arch_main() to properly pass a NULL-terminated array of
      pointers-to-C-strings via a compound literal.

events.title: tests: Add unit tests of image handlers and floppy code, built and run on PC
events.message:
tests: Add unit tests of image handlers and floppy code, built and run on PC

The tests compile firmware sources as they are, with ffemu's host-build
headers, and drive them against a USB drive in RAM holding a FAT16
volume: an image is mounted by image_open(), its tracks are read by the
handler into the bit cell ring, as the floppy code reads them, and
written from bit cells put into the write ring. The floppy code itself
runs on a board of the tests' own: register blocks in memory, a clock
that moves only when a test moves it, software timers, and interrupts
that run when a test runs them. A host on that board writes as it does
on the cable: it asserts WGATE when its start comes round past the
index, gives a flux reversal on WDATA for each 1 cell, and releases
WGATE after the last one, while the board plays the timer and DMA that
capture WDATA and runs the main loop until the write is in the image.
No firmware source is changed: tests/harness.c and tests/floppy_env.c
stand in for the rest of the firmware, and tests/ft_main.c, on the
host's C library, runs the tests and gives the firmware its cancellable
calls.

A failed check names its expressions and their values; for memory, the
first differing byte, with the 16 bytes around it on both sides. The
firmware's console output of a failed test follows.

The 19 tests cover:
- IBM PC 720K and 1.44M raw images, their MFM tracks decoded back into
  sectors; read from mid-track with a seek between each two reads, and
  fragmented, with and without the fast-seek table of the floppy code's
  size; sectors written at the start, the end and the middle of a track
  and on two tracks, and a data field with a wrong CRC;
- TR-DOS .trd images, their geometry from the info sector of a made-up
  disk: double-sided 640K and single-sided, a file shorter than its
  disk, an odd number of tracks, and sectors written at both ends;
- an MFM HFE written at a byte and across two of its blocks;
- the flux intervals that a handler gives for its bit cells, against
  those the cells stand for at its cell length, for an IBM PC image and
  an HFE;
- the head stepped by STEP and DIR for a Shugart host, not while
  deselected, within the cylinder limits;
- three sectors of an IBM PC 720K image written by flux on WDATA
  through the floppy code, on two cylinders and both sides, the host's
  clock 0.7% slow and each reversal up to a tenth of a cell early or
  late;
- the firmware's CRC-16, snprintf() and filename_extension().

A read from within a sector's data regenerates the sector whole, its
CRC included; a start within the CRC itself leaves it wrong in that
first revolution, when no host can read the sector, so those 32 cells
are not compared.

The disks are made up by the tests; none comes from a real disk. The
board's arena is about the RAM that an STM32F105 leaves the firmware,
and each test starts with no image inserted.

"make tests" builds them and then runs them if their program has
changed since they last passed.  This behaviour is also integrated
into plain "make", alongside building the firmware and ffemu; a
failing test fails the whole build.

Speed pass, logic analyser, timeline, input movies, raster overlay (0.6.5)

Speed (the same emulation: SHAKER 2.7, 2166 screens, byte-identical;
every check passes; frame hashes equal):
- the GATE ARRAY and the monitor take a character's 16 Pixel-M2 in one
  step when no event is in them (CtmMonitor::quietRun);
- getenv no longer read once a monitor line; scan-line records reused;

  lightgun mode not copied each character; FDC and DAC idle fast paths;
  breakpoints not looked up when there are none.
- 6128 core 2.2x -> 5.7x real time. Unlimited speed: 30 ms of frames a
  picture, no wait for the display; slot mask and blur on threads.

Drive stop: a disc of more than 43 tracks is in an 80-track drive (stop
82), so Batman Forever's one-disc version reads past track 42.

Logic analyser window: HSYNC, VSYNC, C-SYNC, DISPEN, INT and more, the
CRTC counters, MA, PC and the AY channels, a sample a microsecond, with
triggers. It records only while its window is open.

Timeline: exact snapshots of the machine (each chip copied, restored in
place) and every input, stamped with its instruction. Rewind (Ctrl+Left),
and in the debugger Back, Frame back, Run back and Last write.

Input movies (Machine > Movie): from power-on, every input; played back,
the same run, checked every second.

Raster timing overlay (Debug menu): a tick where each OUT was made.

Soft slot mask: a CRT pattern as ACE-DL draws a CTM.

events.message:
Gate: a worker pool, a log per step, timings; steps are tagged in gates.yml

scripts/gate.sh keeps reading gates.yml as the single list, and hands it to scripts/gate-pool.mjs. A comment tag above a step (# gate: parallel | runtime, ignored by CI) marks it as safe beside others; untagged is serial. Parallel steps run in a pool of min(6, cpus), runtime steps (daemon or server on a free port, own TMPDIR and C64RE_STATE_DIR) at most 3 at once, longest first by the last run's timings; serial steps run before and after, the leak check stays last. Each step logs to its own file, printed whole when it ends; the first failure stops new launches and names the step. The gate runs ensure-built instead of rebuilding, prints the ten slowest steps and keeps the timings. GATE_JOBS=1 is the old serial run.

events.title: Bound monitor history replies before the remote packet limit
events.message:
Bound monitor history replies before the remote packet limit

history read accepts up to 128 entries. With large register values the JSON reply can pass half the GDB packet size, and Session::command() then answers E01 for the whole command. Stop before the limit and report "truncated":true. Entries are collected from the newest backwards so a truncated reply keeps the most recent instructions, and are still returned oldest first.
events.author: midwan

events.title: Report checkpoint save failures
events.message:
Report checkpoint save failures

finish_checkpoint() inferred success from the frame-save flag and savestate_state, but save_state() ignored write and close errors, so a failed write still answered OK and left a truncated file. zfile_fclose() now returns write and close errors, save_state() fails on them, and savestate_check() keeps the result for the checkpoint completion.

save_state() also left savestate_state at STATE_SAVE when the file could not be opened, so debug() returned early on every frame and savestate_check() retried the save forever; the checkpoint never completed. Clear the state on every failure path.
events.author: midwan

events.title: Disassemble instructions that end a memory bank
events.message:
Disassemble instructions that end a memory bank

disassemble_line() required 32 readable bytes after the PC, so monitor disasm and step-over failed for code in the last 31 bytes of RAM or ROM, such as a NOP in the last word of chip RAM. Scan the 22 bytes of the longest 68k instruction instead, refuse any I/O byte so the disassembler never reads hardware registers, and accept the result only when the decoded instruction lies in readable memory. With 2 MB chip RAM, a NOP at $1FFFFE now disassembles, while a JSR at $1FFFFC whose operand runs past the end of chip RAM is still refused.
events.author: midwan

events.title: Match memwatch ranges against every byte of an access
events.message:
Match memwatch ranges against every byte of an access

memwatch_func() tested the first byte of every access, the second byte only for word accesses, and the third and fourth bytes for longword accesses, so a longword access at A never matched a range that covers only A+1. Use a plain interval overlap test. A monitor range watch on byte 5 now records the Kickstart's longword reads of ExecBase at address 4.
events.author: midwan

Preserve guest output truncation across the 1024-byte boundary

GuestOutput treated a captured string of exactly 1024 bytes as truncated. uaelib also copied the guest message into a MAX_DPATH buffer. MAX_DPATH is 1000, so a longer message was cut at 999 bytes and the truncation flag stayed false.

events.message:

events.title: Compact: tick the video and the bus up to the next event
events.message:
Compact: tick the video and the bus up to the next event

After each CPU instruction, the bus catches its devices up with the
cycles the CPU just spent. The compact bus did this one cycle at a
time: for every cycle it moved the video beam two dots (one at a time),
counted the E clock, checked for blanking edges, and ticked the SCSI
and SWIM by one cycle. That loop took around 40% of the host time when
emulating a Plus, while most of these cycles change nothing.

Advance by as many cycles at once as possible instead, up to the next
point where something can happen: an E clock edge, where the VIA is
ticked, or the start or end of a horizontal or vertical blanking
period, where interrupts, the sound and PWM samples, the mouse and the
frame rendering are handled. The steps still add up to the cycles the
CPU spent, so the devices end up at the same point as before. The video
skips to the next blanking edge in the same way instead of moving one
dot at a time.

The machine state is unchanged: save states taken along floppy boots
of the Plus, SE and SE FDHD, and along a flux image boot on the Plus,
are identical to before. The Plus boots to the Finder more than twice
as fast.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: renderer: skip frames the frontend has not picked up yet
events.message:
renderer: skip frames the frontend has not picked up yet

On every emulated vertical blank, the video devices convert the whole
framebuffer to RGBA and the ChannelRenderer allocates a new buffer.
When running faster than real time, most of these frames are replaced
before the frontend shows them: at 10-20x speed that is 600-1200 frames
per second for a 60 Hz display, and 9-26% of the host time depending
on the model.

Add Renderer::frame_wanted(), false while the last frame sent through
the channel has not been taken, and only render on vertical blank when
a frame is wanted. Explicit renders (blanking, state load) still
always happen.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>

events.title: SWIM: handle all the bit cells and flux transitions in a tick
events.message:
SWIM: handle all the bit cells and flux transitions in a tick

Swim::tick(ticks) advances the floppy emulation by `ticks` CPU cycles.
The Compact Macs call it once per cycle, but the Mac II and the
Portable call it once per bus sync with all the cycles since the
previous one, often 10 to 50 cycles at a time and sometimes more.

On bitstream tracks, a new bit comes off the disk every ticks_per_bit
cycles (a 2 us bit cell, about 31 cycles on a Mac II). Each tick() adds
its cycles to a counter, but only took one bit off the disk when the
counter passed ticks_per_bit, even when the cycles were enough for two
or more. For instance, a tick of 70 cycles on a Mac II should shift two
bits into the IWM; it shifted one and left the other in the counter, to
be shifted on the next tick(). Until the counter catches up, the data
the CPU reads from the IWM is behind where the disk is. The ISM
(SuperDrive MFM) code had the same problem.

On flux tracks, a counter holds the cycles until the next flux
transition. When a tick() went past the transition, the transition was
handled and the counter reloaded with the next interval, but the
cycles of that tick() past the transition were thrown away, so every
later transition happened that much later than it should. Each
transition also gets a small pseudo-random timing jitter computed from
the cycle count, which was the count at the end of the tick() rather
than at the transition.

Handle every bit cell and flux transition that falls within the
ticks, each at its own cycle, so that one tick() of N cycles gives
exactly the same result as N tick()s of one cycle.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>

table has a section of its own and comes first as before.

events.title: build: edit vasm's arguments per build mode, default release to -devpac -nosym
events.message:
build: edit vasm's arguments per build mode, default release to -devpac -nosym

The assembler command line was fixed: `-quiet -Ftos`, with one trailing "extra
args" list. Issue #7 asks for an editable command line and control over
optimisation; the reported "wrong PRG without -devpac" is vasm's default
optimisation.

There are now two editable argument lists, Debug and Release, each with a reset
to defaults:

  - Debug: `-quiet -devpac -opt-x+` — Devpac compatibility (which disables
    optimisations) plus the DRI/GST symbol table the debugger reads, with
    full-length names.
  - Release: `-quiet -devpac -nosym` — the same Devpac build with the table
    stripped. `-nosym` is redundant with `-devpac` (both set vasm's
    `no_symbols`) but states the mode's intent and survives the `-devpac` being
    changed.

`-devpac` drops the DRI/GST symbol table, so a debug build has to put it back;
Devpac's `-opt-x+` does exactly that (verified on vasm 2.0f, and Hatari's
`symbols prg` loads the resulting table). `-opt-d+` restores it too but truncates
names to eight characters; `-monst` does not restore it at all. Keeping `-devpac`
in both lists means one source assembles to the same code in either mode.

This changes the default for existing projects too: the migration applies the new
lists to a project that only carried the old `extraArgs`, so a source that
assembled under plain Motorola syntax now assembles in Devpac compatibility
mode. That is the fix, but it is a behaviour change on upgrade, noted in
docs/PLAN.md §4.1 and the README.

The Build toolbar button is a split button — click builds debug, the arrow offers
Build Release — so the release build is reachable without a second,
near-identical icon. The Build menu also gains "Build Release"; Build (F7),
Run (F5) and the remote `build` verb stay on the debug list.

PiST still owns the structural arguments (the output format, -I/-D/-L/-o and the
source file). Their order is built by `vasmAssemblerArguments()` and pinned by a
test in tst_parsers: vasm takes the last `-F`, so the managed format must follow
the project's own flags, or a stray `-F` could change the output module the
launch depends on.

The project file schema is bumped to version 2: version 1's "extraArgs" migrates
into the debug list, and a newer build refuses the file rather than dropping the
lists.

events.title: gary: keep COLDBOOT across the reset line
events.message:
gary: keep COLDBOOT across the reset line

Fat Gary's COLDBOOT flag ($DE0002 bit 7) is a power-up latch. Early in
every reset, A3000/A4000 Kickstart tests it and then clears it. If it
reads set, the reset code clears $4 and cold-starts, rebuilding ExecBase
and dropping everything a warm reboot carries over: KickMemPtr and
KickTagPtr residents, the capture vectors, a recoverable RAM disk.

Gary::reset() rebuilt the chip through Gary::new(), so the keyboard
reset and the CPU RESET instruction both set COLDBOOT again, and every
reboot on a Gary machine came up cold. A user-visible casualty is the
Kickstart 3.2 boot menu. It applies a chosen boot device by calling
ColdReboot() and carrying the choice across in that warm-reset state,
so on an A3000 the machine always booted the highest-priority device,
whatever was picked. Gayle machines were not affected.

The /RESET line now leaves COLDBOOT alone. A new Gary::power_on_reset(),
called from Bus::power_on_reset(), sets it again for a power cycle.
TIMEOUT and TOENB are still cleared by the reset line, as before. This
matches WinUAE, which sets gary_coldboot only on a hard reset.

Add regression tests at the chip, bus and CPU levels. The CPU test
clears the flag, executes RESET and reads it back the way Kickstart
does. Update the Fat Gary section of docs/internals/peripherals.md.

events.title: Action Replay V5/V6: the cartridge, the freeze machinery and its state
events.message:
Action Replay V5/V6: the cartridge, the freeze machinery and its state

CRT type 1 (and a 32 KiB .bin) mounts as an Action Replay: a port of VICE's
actionreplay.c with its four ROM banks, 8 KiB RAM at ROML and in the IO2 page, the
$DE00 register (lines, bank, RAM, kill, freeze release), mode $22 and the IO1 read
that rewrites the register with the phi1 byte.

The freeze is shared machinery: a cartridge can hold /NMI, has a freeze button that
takes effect on the cycle of the press (no random delay), asserts NMI and three
cycles later runs its own freeze and the PLA follows. The cartridge's NMI joins the
expansion NMI source; a read with a side effect re-runs the PLA; the cartridge sees
the real phi1 byte instead of $ff. Peeks never fire a read side effect.

State: registers, lines, NMI, a pending press and the cartridge RAM ride the
checkpoint and the .c64re dump (RAM as a byte node; older checkpoints still load).
The RAM is not a writable image and is never written back into the .crt, and the
read-set lane does not count it as ROM payload.

`cart button freeze [cycle]` in the monitor, `cart/button {button, cycle?}`, and a
`freezer` object in the cart status.

`media/mount` takes `cart_type`, so a raw .bin (an Action Replay is 32 KiB) can be
mounted in the daemon; it had no door and read as a PRG. The ultimax open windows
read the VIC's phi1 byte as VICE does, instead of $FF.

Daemon tests: the real V5 PAL/NTSC/5.1a and V6 images mount as .crt and .bin and boot to
their own start-up screen; a BASIC counter is frozen, the NMI is taken through the
cartridge's vector in ultimax, the freezer menu is on screen, F3 returns to the program
with the counter running on and the RAM below it unchanged; a checkpoint and a .c64re
dump taken while frozen restore the menu, the registers and the cartridge RAM; the same
press on the same cycle is the same run (and the same trace) over two fresh daemons; a
peek does nothing. The spec is closed with its decisions, including the hazard of VICE's
mid-instruction switch.

events.title: Action Replay: switch to ultimax when the CPU takes the NMI, not 3 cycles after
events.message:
Action Replay: switch to ultimax when the CPU takes the NMI, not 3 cycles after

VICE runs the cartridge's freeze three cycles after the NMI goes up (c64cart.c:1369-1372),
which lands under whatever instruction is in flight: a JSR into BASIC lost its operand
fetch to the open bus and about 3 % of presses on a BASIC loop broke the program. Owner
decision 2026-10-16: the freeze now runs from a hook in the CPU core at the NMI sequence's
$FFFA fetch, after the PCH/PCL/P pushes, called from the plain NMI path and from the
IRQ/BRK path when an NMI took the vector over. The press is still on its exact cycle and
a pending freeze is still part of the cartridge's state (checkpoint, .c64re).

Tests: 0 broken of 62 presses on a BASIC loop and of 62 on a KERNAL-calling loop on the
real V5 PAL image; a synthetic ROM with operands in $A000 and $E000+ survives a press on
200 consecutive cycles and on every cycle around an IRQ entry. Spec, archive decision and
FEATURES record the deviation.

events.message:
fix(review): a refused save is a note; an overtaken action commits nothing; collection-time research skips fail the run

The branch's code review found five defects and fixed them, each with a test seen red on
the code before:
- TerminalSession.save shows a save the engine refuses (StateSchemaError) as
  session.save_failed and play goes on, as it does for an OSError.
- step checks the action's owner again before a nested sub-state's lookup and before the
  commit, so an action suspended at a prompt while another config loads raises
  StaleConfigError instead of committing against the new config.
- The research guard counts a skip raised while a module is collected; a test pins that
  the real suite registers the guard.
- The typed x8 weight is normalized under an exact context, so a weight of more than 28
  digits is stored as typed, not rounded up.
- A shell's options are checked by the key a menu picks them by (their own, else their
  position): an unkeyed option past the ninth, or a key that is another option's position,
  is refused at load.

Docs: the engine_api reason for staying at 2; schema 3's typed keys in the freezing
learning; line references in two learnings replaced by symbol names. The review's
deferred items are recorded in the next slice's basis.

events.title: fix(display): merge WinUAE NTSC, vblank and PCem fixes (#2462)
events.message:
fix(display): merge WinUAE NTSC, vblank and PCem fixes (#2462)

* fix(pcem): stop skipping pixels in 15-bit lores SVGA modes

Port of WinUAE 5f5c809c ("Fix 15bit lores PCem/86box RTG boards"). The non-remapped 15-bit lowres renderer reads two source pixels per iteration but advanced the source index by four, so every other pixel pair was dropped. The remapped path already stepped by two.

* fix(display): restore vblank line tracking and make filter blanking a setting

Port of WinUAE 2ab1c5ac ("Fix filter border blanking and make it optional").

- update_agnus_vb() records the vblank start/end lines from linear_vpos
  again instead of linear_vpos_start (partly reverting 985b93c9), and
  custom_trigger_start() no longer adds one to linear_vb_offset. The extra
  line moves into set_custom_limits()' vertical start instead.
- set_custom_limits() loses its "blank" argument. Blanking of the region
  outside the filter's crop rectangle now follows the new per-filter
  gfx_filter_blanking setting (default off), which check_custom_limits()
  also honours.

Amiberry's renderers only ever call set_custom_limits(-1, -1, -1, -1), so
the crop rectangle is never narrowed and the blanking setting has no
effect here. The gfx_filter_blanking key is saved and parsed inside the
GFXFILTER blocks like upstream, and the GFXFILTER-only rule that derives
it from gfx_filter_autoscale is not ported: Amiberry parses
gfx_filter_autoscale outside GFXFILTER, and setting blanking there would
only stop explicit gfx_filter_*_border values from being blanked.

* fix(display): move the AGA long-strobe correction to the line end

Port of WinUAE 9c56300a ("Fixed NTSC fix"), which follows up 1380a678.
On AGA lines after a long strobe (overscan mode up to "overscan"),
get_line() no longer subtracts two from the starting pixel counter.
set_pixtotal_max() lowers the line's maximum pixel count by one instead.

events.message:
drive-mechanism trace: find the sector under the head once per track, not on every drive instruction

The armed head-position sample rescanned the GCR syncs of the track on each
drive instruction (about 98 percent of the run in the profile). The sync marks
of a half-track and the header each one leads to are now kept per half-track
and per image generation, so a head write, a step, an attach or a restore
rebuilds them and every other call is a binary search. The answer is the same
at every head position; captures are byte-identical apart from the file's
creation time.

events.title: Windows RTC: fix 64-bit overflow in QPC to nanosecond conversion
events.message:
Windows RTC: fix 64-bit overflow in QPC to nanosecond conversion

rtc_now_ns() and throttle_get_ns() computed ticks * 1e9 / freq, which
wraps 64 bits every 18446744073 ticks (1844.67 s at the usual 10 MHz
QueryPerformanceCounter frequency). The returned time then jumped
backwards, the wall-clock RTC next-pulse deadline stayed in the future,
and the 50 Hz interrupt stopped. SINTRAN's clock froze and every
timeout with it, which stalled HTTP and FTP transfers (reported
16-OCT-2026 against 1.0.22 on Windows with rtc = wall).

Add src/ndlib/qpc_time.h with qpc_ticks_to_ns(), which splits the
counter into whole seconds and a remainder before scaling, and use it
in both Windows clock functions. Non-Windows hosts use clock_gettime
and are unchanged.

Add tests/test_qpc_time.c (CTest qpc_time_tests): exact values at the
old wrap boundaries for six QPC frequencies, a monotonic walk across
the boundaries, the 100 ns step at 10 MHz, and a negative control that
shows the old formula still breaks there.

events.title: A game is mapped by its moves: runtime_state_map and c64re state map
events.message:
A game is mapped by its moves: runtime_state_map and c64re state map

- runtime_state_map / `c64re state map <file.json>` (one function): from an anchor file, a breadth-first search over
  the bytes you name as the key and the moves you list (stick directions, fire, "nothing", keys), on one machine of its
  own. Each state is reached by restoring its checkpoint (pinned; one the ring refuses goes to a file), a JAM is a crash
  state named by its PC, a goal stops the search at the shortest path, caps on states / runs / depth / the sandbox budget
  stop it and say which. A description is checked before any machine starts; the key is checked against what the project
  has read (the call's project_dir goes to the check). A jam report at a PC that holds no JAM opcode is not a crash.
- The map is kept in the project graph (state_map, game_state, MOVES_TO, STARTS_FROM, CONTAINS, SAVED_AS), found by
  graph_find and project_search, and answered from the graph on the same call again; the goal (and with save_states
  every state) is written as an anchor file.
- e2e:912 (gates.yml): the maze is assembled in the test from its own 64tass source; S1-S6, S4 skipping loudly on a
  runtime that lacks the checkpoint-restore fix.
- Taught: agent-doctrine section, playbook "Map a Game by Its Moves", runtime-sandbox recipe, wiki page Mapping-a-Game
  (linked from Home and Trying-a-Fix), setup line; the tool is in the default tools and the sandbox parity table.
- Spec 912: status BUILT on spec/912, section 5, board row.

events.title: deps: move zip to 9.0.4, every 8.x release is yanked
events.message:
deps: move zip to 9.0.4, every 8.x release is yanked

zip has yanked its whole 8.x line (and 9.0.0 to 9.0.2) over the
security fixes in 9.0.1 to 9.0.4. cargo deny now fails every shipped
graph on the locked 8.6.0, and the fuzz job's fresh lockfile cannot
resolve zip at all.

Move the core requirement to 9.0.4 and pin Coppersynth at its zip 9
merge (CopperlineHQ/Coppersynth#11), which required zip 8. The root,
browser, player and libretro lockfiles move to 9.0.4. The root also
picks up zip 9's default-feature dependencies (zstd 0.14, lzma-rust2
0.22, ppmd-rust 1.5) through Coppersynth's build script, as it did
for 8.x.

zip 9 makes ZipFile::name() fallible, since decoding a member name
can fail. The WHDLoad package reader treats a name that does not
decode like one that leaves the archive: it is skipped, and the
warning shows the raw name lossily. The zipped-soundfont lookup skips
such a member as well.

events.title: Banked overlay write and read for every banked cartridge mapper
events.message:
Banked overlay write and read for every banked cartridge mapper

runtime/overlay_run and sandbox patches can now put a byte into any bank of
Normal 8K/16K/Ultimax, Magic Desk, Magic Desk 16, Ocean, GMod2, MegaByter,
C64MegaCart and GMod4 (and a locked self-configuring cart), not only EasyFlash.
The patch goes into the stored bank image and never through the flash command
state machine, so it sets no dirty flag and bumps no persist generation.
A checkpoint restore re-attaches the cart from its original bytes, which takes
the patch back; a test proves it for each family.

events.title: palette_pairs: parallel refit trials, hoisted per-call work
events.message:
palette_pairs: parallel refit trials, hoisted per-call work

joint_refit, refine and refine_ehb encode and S2-score each candidate
palette one after another; refine_with scores the same start once per
search and both results again at the end. Same choices, less work:

- encode_all: a pass's candidates are encoded and scored in parallel
  (pipeline::parallel_for), then chosen in input order as before. Only
  where the encoder is safe to call concurrently (new trailing
  `concurrent` argument; the dither::apply and EHB diffuse callers pass
  true, thomson_palette_refine keeps the serial default).
- refine_with: one PrecomputedSource and one start score shared by both
  searches; refine_search returns its final score instead of a rescore.
- refine: one dither::PrecomputedImage for all trial encodes.
- joint_refit: the 5x5 blurred sRGB source is built once, not per
  iteration; a step equal to the other step, or to the current palette
  after a kept iteration, is not encoded (it cannot be kept).
- proposals: source conversion once per call instead of 9x per pixel;
  the 256-entry weight array is reset per active entry instead of
  zero-filled per pixel. Both colour spaces run in parallel.

Byte-identical PNG/IFF/raw/pi1 output (clang and GCC 16). Wall, median of
3, fantasy1.jpg / DIV2K 0256: lores d5 0.41 -> 0.19 / 0.36 -> 0.19 s,
vga-12h 1.57 -> 0.61 / 1.29 -> 0.57, stf-low 0.31 -> 0.14 / 0.23 -> 0.15.
WASM (node) fantasy1: lores d5 0.49 -> 0.22, vga-12h 1.95 -> 0.70.

events.title: lores sliced: resumable, batched DitherWindow trials
events.message:
lores sliced: resumable, batched DitherWindow trials

The dither-checked planner (e5322d36) re-dithered rows y-4..y+8 from
scratch for every candidate swap. Same decisions, less work:

- dither::DiffuseRows / DiffuseState: diffuse_raw_buffer split into a
  per-row step with copyable state (diffuse_raw_buffer is now start() +
  row() over all rows). Optional whole-image source conversions
  (DiffuseSource) and a per-entry sRGB in PickResult::chosen_srgb skip
  the per-pixel source and chosen-colour transcendentals.
- DitherWindow keeps the incumbent's trace: rows above y are dithered
  once per row; a trial resumes from the saved state at the first row
  whose picks can change; raw and blurred are ordered sums of
  non-negative row terms, so a partial sum that already fails rejects.
- Trials run in parallel batches (pipeline::parallel_for, up to 8): the
  planner lists the next proposals as if each were rejected, scores
  them against the same incumbent and applies the first kept one.
  The incumbent's own rows from y on run with the first batch.
- find_best_swap caches per-slot centroid reductions between scratch
  refreshes (they do not depend on the excluded set).
- pick_palette_index_with_ostro: distances first, then a min
  reduction; same index, best and second distance as the strict-<
  scan. nearest_palette_index skips the second distance for the
  window, whose diffuser reads only the chosen colour.

Byte-identical PNG and IFF output (clang and GCC 16). With the next
commit (palette refit), wall, median of 3, fantasy1.jpg / DIV2K 0256:
OCS lores d5 --sliced 3.66 -> 1.02 s / 1.36 -> 0.53 s; AGA 6.31 -> 1.62
/ 4.01 -> 1.30; lores-lace 10.24 -> 2.60 / 4.12 -> 1.19. WASM (node)

events.title: cpu: bump m68k to 0.14.6 for the LC/EC060 PCR
events.message:
cpu: bump m68k to 0.14.6 for the LC/EC060 PCR

m68k 0.14.6 models the FPU-less MC68LC060/MC68EC060 PCR: with no FPU
fitted, reset loads identification $0431 (the full MC68060 is $0430)
and DFP is held set against MOVEC writes, so software that clears it
can no longer enable an FPU the part lacks. The 060's FBcc, FScc,
FDBcc and FTRAPcc now also take the FPU-disabled exception while DFP
is set, ahead of reading any extension word, as the other FP opcodes
already did.

Copperline sets the core's fpu_present from the config before its
reset, so `fpu = false` on a 68060 picks up the new identification
with no code change. Add a regression test for the PCR identification
and DFP hold across MOVEC writes and resets for both parts, and drop
the documented $0430 / writable-DFP gap from docs/internals/cpu.md.

Bump all five lockfiles that pin m68k; 0.14.6 has the same dependency
set as 0.14.5, so only the version and checksum change.

events.title: One feature file takes a fix from an anchor to a verdict: engine and doors
events.message:
One feature file takes a fix from an anchor to a verdict: engine and doors

- An anchor is a mark and a file: runtime_anchor_set also dumps the machine to knowledge/anchors/<name>.c64re
  (drop deletes it), `Given the mark` starts a private machine from that file exactly where it was dumped,
  and `And I set the anchor "<name>"` makes one from a boot with no session.
- `And variant "<name>" assembles "<path>" at [roml|romh bank <n> ]$<addr>`: the baseline and each variant run on
  a private machine of their own from the same origin, up to four at once; the code is written in after the
  origin is loaded and before the first step. A wait that does not happen is a FAIL of that run.
- The Then lines decide PASS/FAIL per run; the memory a variant changed besides is listed as side effects.
- runtime_feature_run and `c64re scenario run` are the same function (exit 0/1/2 as the file says).
- A candidate is the record of a feature run (history, per-variant verdicts, choice); old records still read.
- Removed: runtime_candidate_create / _variant / _run / _patch / _remove_patch and the old runner.

events.message:
Βήμα 140: πάνω από τους τριάντα τρεις — ο παίκτης γεμίζει μεσαίους θόλους, και σταματά μόνο η χαλασμένη μηχανή

Ο παίκτης ζήτησε να συνεχίσουμε. Κανείς δεν είχε παιχτεί πάνω από τους 33,
οπότε το σενάριο έπαιξε 60 sol στους ίδιους 24 κόσμους. Με τον παίκτη του
139, 14 αποικίες από τις 24 είχαν πεθάνει ως το sol 60 (383 θάνατοι, 354
από πείνα): έχτιζε μόνο μικρούς θόλους, μία μηχανή ο καθένας, σε 14 tiles
από το κέντρο, και ο επόμενος θόλος τροφής δεν έβρισκε θέση.

Ο παίκτης (tools/play.py, σχέδια big*· το tweak nogrow τα σβήνει):
- γεμίζει πρώτα μια ελεύθερη υποδοχή μεσαίου θόλου (Game.fill)· μεσαίοι
  θόλοι από τους 14 για τροφή, βιομηχανία, κοιτώνες, ανταλλακτικά, μικρός
  όπου ο μεσαίος δεν χωρά· ψάχνει σε 14, 20, 26 tiles·
- δεύτερο Control κοντά στο ταβάνι· θόλος για ένα υλικό που πέφτει·
  πλοία μόνο όταν τα υλικά και το νερό δεν πέφτουν ή φτάνουν για πέντε sol·
- κρατά 30 μέταλλα από τους 14 (όχι για οξυγόνο, νερό, δεύτερη πόρτα)·
  ανταλλακτικά ξανά· δεύτερο airlock στους 16· μεσαία αποθήκη από την πέμπτη.
Μετρημένο (g60m, 24 κόσμοι, 60 sol): 18/24 ζωντανές, 13 πάνω από είκοσι,
ως 49 (64 στη g60b), μέσος 18,1, 148 θάνατοι (11 εισβολείς, 102 πείνα).
Οι g60f, g60g, g60m είναι σχεδόν ο ίδιος παίκτης: 21,1, 20,5, 18,1.

Τι βρήκε στο παιχνίδι:
1. Γεμάτη αποθήκη σκοτώνει: σταματούν οι κήποι και το VITROMEAT, και αν
   λείπει ένα από άμυλο/λαχανικά/κρέας τα γεύματα σταματούν και τίποτα δεν
   αδειάζει την αποθήκη (g60f: 7 αποικίες, 88 θάνατοι). Ο παίκτης διάλεξε
   «μόνο ό,τι λείπει»: ~30 bytes, μετά από βήμα μνήμης (141, μετά 142).
2. Μία χαλασμένη μηχανή σταματούσε όλο τον θόλο: διορθωμένο εδώ (κάτω).
3. Ως 8 θόλοι ενός είδους (ROOM_MAX): ο παίκτης διάλεξε να μείνει, γραμμένο.
4. Το νερό τελειώνει όπου δεν χωρά άλλη αντλία· ένα airlock είναι ένας
   μετεωρίτης από τη σφαγή· ο πάγος κρατά περίπου δεκαοκτώ (32% έδαφος)·
   στο x4 οι πενήντα τρέχουν 3,65 αντί για 3,97.

ΣΤΑΜΑΤΑ ΜΟΝΟ Η ΧΑΛΑΣΜΕΝΗ (η επιλογή του παίκτη, src/jobs.asm): ως το 139 το
jp_one ζητούσε σε κάθε επίσκεψη τη Repair, την έβρισκε ήδη στον πίνακα και
γύριζε, χωρίς Operate· οι χειριστές έφευγαν να φάνε και οι άλλες τρεις
μηχανές ενός μεσαίου θόλου σταματούσαν (1048 3: τριάντα νεκροί δίπλα σε
184 άμυλο, 157 λαχανικά, 99 κρέας). Τώρα ΕΝΑΛΛΑΞ: ο δείκτης EC_JDOME τρέχει
0-255, ο θόλος τα έξι χαμηλά bits, το bit 6 το σάρωμα· στα ζυγά η Repair,

events.title: fix(gui): apply Chipset Extra changes on hard reset (#2459) (#2461)
events.message:
fix(gui): apply Chipset Extra changes on hard reset (#2459) (#2461)

Changing Chipset Extra and then pressing Reboot never applied the new
value. The core copies most chipset flags from changed_prefs into
currprefs as it runs, but not cs_compatible and a few others. WinUAE
applies those by copying every setting into currprefs when its GUI asks
for a hard reset. Amiberry dropped that copy for #1068. Each GUI open
then copied currprefs back over changed_prefs, so the Chipset panel went
back to the old model while Advanced Chipset kept the new model's flags.

Copy cs_compatible, cs_rtc_adjust, cs_cdtvcr, cs_resetwarning,
cs_ciatodbug, cs_1mchipjumper and cs_bkpthang into currprefs in
target_reset() when the reset is a hard reset, so every hard reset path
applies them. Keep their pending values when the GUI refreshes from
currprefs, so the GUI shows what the next hard reset will apply.

HelperDiscovery.findCallEdgeWrappers accepts a body-closing plain JMP as

relay or one-instruction thunk the strategy's arm scan

events.title: ASC: support FIFO status writes to retrigger interrupts
events.message:
ASC: support FIFO status writes to retrigger interrupts

Now this is a nasty convoluted one:

On the Mac II with the AMU (no PMMU), SwapMMUMode switches the MMU mode
with VIA2 port B bit vFC3.

Any access to port B clears the VIA's CB1 flag, which is the ASC interrupt,
and since CB1 is edge triggered and the ASC holds its line until the status
is read, the interrupt is lost for good. The ASC still has the FIFO status
bits set but the interrupt is lost at the VIA level.

SwapMMUMode works around it: after the switch it reads the ASC FIFO
status which releases the interrupt line to the VIA, and if any flag is
set, ORs it back into the register so the ASC interrupts again. This
new edge then gets caught by the VIA which sends a new interrupt to
the CPU.

Our model stored the value on a write but without raising the interrupt,
so the interrupt was well and truly lost, causing the remaining occasional
sound related hangs we observed on the Mac II.

This fixes it by raising the interrupt again on a write of non-zero flags.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>

events.title: Checkpoint restore carries the CPU jam: a restore from a jammed machine runs again
events.message:
Checkpoint restore carries the CPU jam: a restore from a jammed machine runs again

A checkpoint never recorded the jam, and restore_cpu never cleared it, so after a
restore from a jammed machine every session/run reported `jam` at whatever PC the
restored CPU stood on — though the CPU ran. The jam is CPU state like the registers:
capture writes `cpu.jammed` (only when set, so every other checkpoint is byte-identical
and an older one reads as not jammed), and restore sets it on both cores.

Regression test: the steps of GitHub #12 on the reporter's maze program — restore runs,
a real JAM after a restore or an undump still reports its own PC. Fails before the fix
with the reported values (c64Cycles 3100060, jam.pc 2073).

Fixes #12

events.message:
fix(flatpak): use the runtime's FFmpeg and libwebp (#2460)

#2458 added libwebp and FFmpeg modules to the in-repo Flatpak manifest. They are not needed: the freedesktop 26.08 SDK the manifest builds against already ships FFmpeg 8 (libavcodec 62) with the FLAC, Vorbis, Opus, VP8/VP9, MPEG-1/2, AC-3, MP1/2/3 and DVD/S16LE PCM decoders the ZZ9000 needs, and libwebp 1.6 with libwebpdemux. The modules were also unbuildable: their commit fields named the annotated tag objects, not the tagged commits, so flatpak-builder would reject both sources. The manifest is back to the module list the Flathub manifest uses.
