project.notes: Cross-platform image/asset converter for Amiga, Atari ST/STE, IBM PC, C64, Genesis, SNES Mode 7, Game Boy Advance, Sega Master System/Game Gear, Amstrad CPC/CPC Plus, Thomson and Commodore TED targets. v1.109.0 (25 September 2026) added SMS/GG and CPC/CPC Plus output modes with packed-output round-trip tests. The README documents native CMake builds, a WebAssembly web app and pre-built desktop releases; standard x86-64 binaries require AVX2, while a compatibility build is provided for older x86-64 CPUs. The latest Amiga conversion pass fixes a locked-black palette seed that could duplicate black and drop the final colour, using shared unlocked-slot filling for copper and EHB paths. OCS low-resolution d5 sliced dithering was retuned on 34 images from 1.0/0.10 to 0.72/0.35, then checked on a separate 21-image set where sliced S2 mean rose from 50.47 to 56.89 versus 55.39 for plain output; EHB results were unchanged. These are upstream image-set metrics, not universal quality guarantees. Evidence: https://github.com/tinic/png2amiga/commit/64a1844fa1cd7d207a1bd80be71865dcc0648f19

runtime_profiles.name: MegaST v1.1 on MEGA65 R6
runtime_profiles.notes: Primary README reports stable real-hardware R6 operation with floppy/hard-disk images, TOS 1.04, named games and additional tester-reported TOS/game configurations. Requires an SD card, tos.img and user media. No 45GS02 requirement or guest ST-RAM size is treated as a host CPU/RAM minimum. v1.1 additionally verifies the read-only internal 3.5-inch drive with an original Jim Power disk.

runtime_profiles.name: MegaST v1.0 on MEGA65 R3/R3A
runtime_profiles.notes: The dedicated R3/R3A core keeps 512 KiB of guest ST RAM in FPGA block RAM because HyperRAM is too slow for cycle-exact timing. Upstream reports R3A operation including hard-disk images. Viking and STEroids modes are unavailable. The 512 KiB value is guest configuration, not host minimum RAM.

project.status: v1.1 stable; R6 internal 3.5-inch drive support verified read-only; R4/R5 remain untested
project.notes: Ports the tracked MiSTer AtariST/MiSTery core to MEGA65 with MiSTer2MEGA65. Its machine wrapper, SDRAM/ACSI controller, native keyboard, TOS loader, RTC, video scaling and virtual-drive integration establish a distinct target port rather than a mirror. Version 1.0 is the first stable release. Primary documentation reports real R6 operation, tester-reported R3A hard-disk support, TOS 1.62 and named games; R4/R5 and several optional devices remain untested. The R3/R3A core keeps 512 KiB of guest ST RAM in FPGA block RAM because HyperRAM is too slow for cycle-exact timing; that is not a host RAM minimum. Releases through 0.4.10 could damage hard-disk images when writing. v1.0 restores remembered media, centres additional HDMI modes and ships distinct R3/R3A, R4, R5 and R6 core files. TOS and user media are required; EmuTOS ships in release archives, while proprietary Atari TOS remains separate. AUTHORS identifies the FX68K cycle-accurate 68000 CPU. The output is an FPGA bitstream/framework integration, not a program targeting the MEGA65’s default 45GS02 CPU, so no target CPU is inferred. GPL v3 aggregate includes upstream GPL v2-or-later and FX68K GPL v3 components. Selected implementation commits explicitly credit Claude Opus 5.5; that wording is retained as repository attribution only. No synthesis, simulation, ROM execution or hardware testing was performed here. Evidence: https://github.com/freemchr/MegaST/releases/tag/v1.0 https://github.com/freemchr/MegaST/blob/master/README.md https://github.com/freemchr/MegaST/blob/master/doc/DEVELOPMENT.md https://github.com/freemchr/MegaST/blob/master/AUTHORS https://github.com/freemchr/MegaST/commit/63c86eddc8ed7922474d41469d420b72406eee2b https://github.com/MiSTer-devel/AtariST_MiSTer https://github.com/gyurco/MiSTery https://github.com/sy2002/MiSTer2MEGA65 https://github.com/ijor/fx68k v1.1 makes the MEGA65 internal 3.5-inch drive available as Atari ST drive A in read-only mode. The implementation covers the WD1772 command set and copy-protected layouts up to ten sectors and 82 tracks; read assist retimes pulses and retries a CRC-failed sector for up to 15 revolutions. Upstream tested the path on R6 with an original Jim Power disk that booted and loaded without errors. The internal-drive path remains untested on R3/R3A, R4 and R5, and stcfg expands to 104 bytes. Evidence: https://github.com/freemchr/MegaST/releases/tag/v1.1 https://github.com/freemchr/MegaST/commit/1f057d4d5505edd1b0964554feb1dde47048c2dc

project.status: v0.57.2 Atari 2600 emulator/debugger with published Linux, Windows and dual-architecture macOS builds
project.notes: High-accuracy Atari 2600 emulator with developer debugger, mapper support and a distinct ARM coprocessor debugger. Current ARM fixes correct ASR zero/immediate and variable shifts, carry/sign extension, SMUL/SMLA, saturation, alignment and bitfield masks; these are bounded coprocessor-correctness changes rather than universal compatibility claims. Release v0.57.2 publishes Linux amd64, Windows amd64, macOS Intel and macOS Apple Silicon packages. The build workflow sets macOS deployment targets 10.11 for Intel and 11.0 for Apple Silicon; no RAM or CPU-generation minimum is stated. The README identifies Stella as a visual and format/reference source, not as a fork or derived code base. Searches of current code and commit history for Claude and ChatGPT found no development-AI evidence, so AI use remains unknown. No package was independently executed. Evidence: https://github.com/JetSetIlly/Gopher2600 https://github.com/JetSetIlly/Gopher2600/releases/tag/v0.57.2 https://github.com/JetSetIlly/Gopher2600/blob/master/.github/workflows/build.yml https://github.com/JetSetIlly/Gopher2600/commit/ca1e5ec

project.title: ghidra-retro-machines
project.display_title: Ghidra Retro Machines — bank-aware loaders and retro CPU languages
project.status: Active; conservative overlay/dataflow fixes and repeatable 34-ROM NES corpus analysis
project.notes: Ghidra extension for banked C64/C128/PET PRG and NES iNES analysis, with SPC700 and 65C816 language variants. The current NES pass bounds split low/high pointer tables by the next section gap: Dodge shrinks from 64 to 26 entries, River City Ransom from 64 to 27 and Mega Man 2 from 255 to 15. Upstream reports build-and-test SUITE OK and 29 NES baseline passes plus the three corrected fixtures. Existing 65C816 oracle-defect guards and language limitations remain; these gates show bounded analysis improvements, not universal correctness. The reviewed commit explicitly credits Claude Opus 5.5. Evidence: https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/6556e84ff267a0c96e7c89c5dbe2d3c3777d2aad The next analyzer pass extends RAM save-slot proofs across admitted cross-function jumps and narrowly recognized save-helper calls, while preserving conservative abandon rules and declining unresolved overlay-bank cases. Upstream reports 33 NES tests passing; the separate Dragon Power symbol-output flap remains documented. Evidence: https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/3f983b0189e67e2f8337804e0c2beb46c5483d44 The latest bank-analysis passes persist provenance for analyzer-created overlay references so later rounds retract stale targets without deleting user-owned references, and remove fall-through code only when a conditional branch is provably taken and no flow, entry point, function or user label preserves the old path. Upstream reports deterministic NES corpus updates and passing synthetic/JUnit gates; these are bounded analyzer-correctness receipts, not universal decompilation correctness. Evidence: https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/475eeadd4fb50ad045bd8e01dd428243279bfe2d https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/1251af61b1d65c8849bc90795d186ee274938db4 The newest passes write jump-table overrides once a containing function exists, eliminating first-reference analysis-order sensitivity, then remove the default single-thread pin while retaining GRM_THREAD_PIN=1 as a diagnostic. Upstream reports byte-identical results across all 34 NES fixtures at 12, 4 and 2 threads plus passing synthetic gates; this is bounded corpus determinism rather than universal analysis correctness. The reviewed commits explicitly credit Claude Opus 5.5. Evidence: https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/2a15e0df8abeeccc0842b212a00e1d08d2316e41 https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/48c66e952687ddaa24979626263f9b24dbd6b11d Current main fixes a dataflow join across a cross-function predecessor edge so a shared-store tail can retain the correct save-slot proof. Castlevania III now forks bank_5116 for banks 7 and 30, reduces warnings from 15 to 14 and raises bank comments from 171 to 172; the other 34 NES rows remain byte-identical and build-and-test reports SUITE OK. Adjacent fixes discard partial states that violate overlay invariants or flow into a differently occupied overlay, retry isolated flaky corpus rows, handle ROM paths with spaces and synchronize a 6510 illegal-instruction definition. These remain bounded analyzer/corpus receipts. Evidence: https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/101dc785283b69672728d98a318af579d2f5f7ff https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/9ab5515 https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/2950474

runtime_profiles.name: Fantasm CLI and Python API

project.status: v1.3.0; active Python 3.12+ multi-target disassembly/reassembly toolkit
project.notes: Consolidated CLI/API for managing annotated 6502 disassemblies across versions, including round-trip verification with BeebAsm; can use Dasmos or py8dis drivers. Fantasm 1.2.1 replaces line-regex annotation discovery with AST parsing for both py8dis and dasmos drivers, makes syntax errors explicit, and adds comment-placement/content checks including copied-version, byte/address, branch-phrasing and code-read-as-data diagnostics with false-positive suppression. Evidence: https://github.com/acornaeology/fantasm/commit/7c8b51870d2c817d8e2d20e70c7a5259b6b6bb2b https://github.com/acornaeology/fantasm/commit/2b0cf0947c4f2d7329ca3bc918a5ea11ca459554 https://github.com/acornaeology/fantasm/commit/9f2734b37f5015221b34554d7e9b748a05fcf39f Fantasm 1.3.0 adds target and layout abstractions through [layout] and [[targets]], explicit existing-project adoption, .inf parsing for DFS/ADFS/Stardot conventions, configurable verification, verify --all, environment variables and per-target driver working directories. The tracked acorn-nfs reconstruction now explicitly requires Fantasm 1.3.0. Evidence: https://github.com/acornaeology/fantasm/commit/b9286c31a80ff68050cd878d6c61feee39cb569e https://github.com/acornaeology/fantasm/commit/08cbb841

project.title: Dethrace
project.display_title: Carmageddon — incremental DOS executable reconstruction
project.status: Active function-by-function Carmageddon reconstruction; new groove/camera routines include exact and behavior-equivalent matches
project.notes: Buildable native Carmageddon reimplementation that replaces original DOS executable assembly with C function by function. Historical Watcom symbols exist but do not match released-code positions. Current CI builds and tests Windows x86/x64, Linux x64/arm64 and macOS x86_64/arm64 variants; no minimum host hardware is documented. The latest reviewed commits report exact reccmp matches for GetGraphicsOptions, ChangingView and drpixelmapcopy, demonstrating incremental function parity rather than whole-program completeness or playable parity. Evidence: https://github.com/dethrace-labs/dethrace/commit/ff723168a9b458252ce40bb6e0ceb008cb4dcc35 https://github.com/dethrace-labs/dethrace/commit/80898db36d16d584d50789a9f8d05cdf2ed8458f https://github.com/dethrace-labs/dethrace/commit/d5b90d885b298c9ca338c9060468f899ca095fab Four merged reconstruction PRs add SwingCamera, ObjectGrooveBastard, PathGrooveBastard and FunkThoseTronics. PathGrooveBastard reports a 100% match; the other PRs distinguish equivalent/effective behavior from lower similarity percentages, so they are not described as byte-exact. Each PR explicitly labels the work AI generated and records time/token totals, establishing AI use without identifying a model or tool. Evidence: https://github.com/dethrace-labs/dethrace/pull/1191 https://github.com/dethrace-labs/dethrace/pull/1192 https://github.com/dethrace-labs/dethrace/pull/1193 https://github.com/dethrace-labs/dethrace/pull/1194

project.status: active; v0.6.3 adds CRT masks and reorganized media/ROM management across existing host packages
project.notes: Emulates CPC 464/6128, Plus and GX4000 with per-model CRTC/Gate Array timing, disc and tape support, a debugger and embedded RASM. Inspected src/core includes Z80, CRTC variants and debugging code. README calls expansion hardware and UI work in progress; SHAKER compatibility is upstream's claim. v0.4.0 adds host-backed M4 TCP/DNS/server and plain-HTTP operations, a folder-backed FAT16 IDE/CF interface for SYMBiFACE II/III, and LambdaSpeak 3 Epson/DECtalk command handling using host voices. The release documents tests with Duke's TCP/telnet examples, SymbOS and LambdaSpeak software; these upstream compatibility claims were not independently reproduced. Evidence: https://github.com/WacKEDmaN/CPCSyntaxError/commit/c909c7f7e465dc54640248cbd91a4d78a1c45656 v0.5.0 adds guided and manual RAM cheats, CDT/TZX tape recording and turbo loading, HFE read/write, IPF read support, image writeback, a 300-rpm real-time floppy model, Multiface II, RS232C endpoints and folder-backed M4 DSK images. The bundled IPF decoder retains its non-commercial licence; upstream compatibility tests were not independently reproduced. Evidence: https://github.com/WacKEDmaN/CPCSyntaxError/commit/35ca66c5bb974eb0b1113e08980ea166cf93362a v0.6.0 adds successful CI builds and release assets for Windows x64, Linux x86-64 and universal macOS arm64/x86-64, plus monitor H/V hold controls and Compendium-backed CRTC sync timing. Upstream explicitly says the Linux and macOS packages were not yet desktop-tested. Evidence: https://github.com/WacKEDmaN/CPCSyntaxError/commit/2b74f27e5c466376321eb7aa6587d994e08a6670 https://github.com/WacKEDmaN/CPCSyntaxError/releases/tag/v0.6.0 https://github.com/WacKEDmaN/CPCSyntaxError/actions/runs/38114012270 v0.6.3 adds a CRT slot mask for colour monitors, scanlines for green/grey displays and controls for strength, stripe width and orientation. It also splits Media into Disc, Tape, Cartridge and Snapshot windows and keeps ROMs separate. Release assets remain Linux x86-64, macOS universal and Windows x64; no new minimum CPU/RAM claim follows from the packaging. Evidence: https://github.com/WacKEDmaN/CPCSyntaxError/releases/tag/v0.6.3 https://github.com/WacKEDmaN/CPCSyntaxError/commit/f87aa174c50c6bb56a2e8c3ca4b4ddbaa7650f4a

project.status: v0.60 beta; native Lynx tracker release with dense-pattern timing fix and real-hardware verification
project.notes: Original Lynx homebrew music tracker, not reverse-engineered or RE-derived. Upstream documents a native 65C02 .lnx build, real-hardware validation, four-channel Mikey synthesis, streamed PCM kits, EEPROM persistence and ComLynx/MIDI bridging. v0.60 fixes cumulative tempo slowdown in dense four-channel LFSR patterns by queuing/catching up VBlank work instead of silently discarding ticks; SAVE/LOAD remains deliberately nonqueued. Upstream reports at least 20 aligned stress passes where the old path reached 16, a passing full ROM/editor/audio/save/MIDI/sync suite, production .lnx assets and successful real Atari Lynx verification. Persistence still requires a full 2 KiB 93C86-compatible EEPROM: RetroHQ GameDrive is verified, while 128-byte ElCheapoSD storage cannot save. runtime_profiles.name: Q8 accelerated-emulation qualification
runtime_profiles.notes: Upstream recommends Q8 only above 20 MHz. v1.8.0 reports Turbo6510 64 MHz measurements on public PAL cube scenes: Mode 2 precise/hybrid 23.70/25.05 FPS, Mode 5 27.00/27.45 FPS, and distant-cube Mode 7 standard/fast/fast+LOD 3.10/6.95/11.50 FPS. These are scene-specific emulator measurements, not minima, general guarantees or physical-hardware qualification. The v1.10.2 stable qualification additionally reports Mode 4 stock/turbo results of 0.649958/30.186113 FPS with defaults and 0.749952/38.484510 FPS with arithmetic, camera and visibility experiments; Mode 7 defaults report 0.044442/3.091013 FPS and arithmetic+UV 0.061107/3.703647 FPS. These remain emulator measurements, not physical-hardware or minimum-machine claims.

project.status: v1.11.0 stable source SDK; Windows/VICE qualified, with Linux and physical hardware still unverified
project.notes: Source SDK for eight C64 graphics modes: polygon rendering and a distinct Mode 8 2.5D DDA bitmap renderer. PowerShell/Python scene builders emit 6510/6502 assembly for 64tass. v1.8.0 adds opt-in gradual Mode 7 texture LOD, optional Q8 hybrid line rasterization for Modes 1/2/5 and safe presentation for Modes 1–7; legacy geometry, standard texture quality, precise raster and LOD-off remain defaults. Upstream reports all 22 public tests passing and bounded Turbo6510 64 MHz scene measurements, while explicitly stating that real hardware has not been tested. Code/data remain PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. Codex usage guides document downstream SDK use, not development-AI authorship of the engine. v1.9.0 adds an explicit experimental Normalized16 build and bounded signed-16 geometry generators while preserving the Q8 defaults unless the optional hook is selected. Native benchmark and qualification tooling are included; this does not change the recorded physical-hardware limitation. Evidence: https://github.com/Librologica/3Dvibe64/commit/562f3c314314abce8de7c30786843c2435b00e94 https://github.com/Librologica/3Dvibe64/commit/6ea4d7cf99513d9714407ea938aed06b8d55d4bc v1.10.2 promotes the qualified development line to a stable source SDK without changing default runtime options. Its optional Q8 arithmetic, UV, camera-table and visibility experiments remain disabled by default; upstream reports PAL-emulated Mode 4 and Mode 7 measurements, complete source/package regeneration gates and Windows/VICE qualification, while explicitly leaving Linux and physical hardware untested. Evidence: https://github.com/Librologica/3Dvibe64/releases/tag/v1.10.2 v1.11.0 packages 794 source files, 34 English/Italian manual pairs and 41 release gates, including 15 byte-identical checkpoint rebuilds. Its billboard, door, material, animation, static-lighting, portal-visibility, shared-Q8-mesh and room-group features remain bounded by the release documentation; the release ships source only, without compiled PRGs, demos or media, and qualifies Windows/VICE rather than Linux or physical hardware. The release commit is explicitly authored by the GitHub account Codex, which establishes AI-tool attribution without quantifying contribution. Evidence: https://github.com/Librologica/3Dvibe64/releases/tag/v1.11.0 https://github.com/Librologica/3Dvibe64/commit/fd7cdcafb452407faf29bd5a2115998b2a998f8d

Measured on this branch and on main alike: the held kneel's shins lie on
the ground (lowest shin -0.021 to -0.007 figure units) and every
transition frame touches it (lowest -0.11 to +0.03). The kneel-transition

events.title: npm scripts: no >/dev/null, which npm's cmd shell on Windows cannot run
events.message:
npm scripts: no >/dev/null, which npm's cmd shell on Windows cannot run

Seven package.json scripts silenced gen-tool-surface-inventory.mjs with
>/dev/null. npm runs scripts through cmd.exe on Windows; cmd answers "The
system cannot find the path specified." and the script fails, so
scripts/gate.sh stopped at step 10 (check:doc-capability-claims).

The generator takes --quiet instead, and check:npm-scripts-portable (a
gates.yml step) fails when a script redirects to /dev/null again.

events.message:
e2e-disasm-family: section 7 tests the returned listing path with isAbsolute

The disasm tool reports an absolute native path. The test took only a path
starting with "/" as absolute and joined a Windows C:\ path onto the project
dir, so section 7 opened a doubled path (ENOENT) and the harness aborted.

events.message:
Emulate the ZZ9000 firmware's WebP, FLAC, Vorbis, WebM and MPEG-2 services (#2458)

* feat(zz9000): emulate the firmware's WebP, FLAC, Vorbis, WebM and MPEG-2 services

The ZZ9000 firmware now advertises WebP stills and animations, FLAC and
Ogg Vorbis audio streams, WebM (VP8/VP9 with Opus/Vorbis), MPEG-2 Program
Stream (AC-3/LPCM/MP2) and Matroska media, per-stream audio gain,
card-DDR media preload and a console encoder. Bring the emulated SDK
mailbox up to that protocol so current ZZPlay, zz9k-view and the
picture/sound DataTypes work the same way as on the card.

- Audio: per-stream gain (0x0515) and codec-aware BeginEx (0x0516) for
  MP3, FLAC and Ogg Vorbis. FLAC and Vorbis are decoded incrementally
  with FFmpeg as the guest feeds them; play sessions open the host
  stream at the decoded rate and channel count.
- Images: WebP stills through every image output mode and WebP
  animation sessions (next/present/retire/restart) on YUV422CGX
  surfaces, using libwebp with the firmware's limits.
- Media: FFmpeg worker per session for MPEG-2 PS/VOB, WebM and
  Matroska, streaming through a bounded input queue with cumulative
  accepted-byte progress, YUY2 packing with interlace blending and
  half-size packing, and the firmware's status pages. MPEG-1 stays on
  pl_mpeg. AX audio binding stays unadvertised.
- Memory: card-only media allocations up to 64 MiB on Zorro III,
  MEM_FILL and MEM_COPY, MEMORY_OPS advertised.
- Console encoder service (0x8200) with RFB tile output.
- Zorro II aperture-info handshake and layout query used by current
  zz9k.library builds.

Capability bits and service flags are advertised only for the code
compiled in. USE_FFMPEG (FFmpeg 5.1+) no longer depends on
USE_VIDEOGRAB, USE_WEBP is new, and the Windows vcpkg manifest, CI and
Linux/macOS/FreeBSD packaging gain FFmpeg and libwebp.

* fix(zz9000): snapshot the console framebuffer on band 0 of every pass

The console encoder copied the framebuffer only when it reconfigured, so
ordinary incremental passes compared against a stale snapshot and sent
nothing after the first keyframe. Like the firmware, band 0 now takes
the snapshot on every pass, a new geometry voids it, and a same-geometry
reset keeps it.

* fix(zz9000): pad FFmpeg audio packets and keep half-size rows on whole pairs

FLAC and Vorbis packets went to FFmpeg from unpadded vector storage, and
the FLAC parser read straight from the input queue, which is erased
before a returned packet is sent. Packets are now copied into padded
AVPackets and the parser reads a padded copy.

Half-size video presentation rounds the packed width down to even, so a
source width of 2 mod 4 no longer writes a pair whose second pixel comes
from the next row.

* fix(zz9000): reapply stream gain after a stop and play

Stopping playback destroys the SDL stream, but the cached gain survived,
so the next stream started at unity gain and pump_audio() never applied
the session's gain to it. Opening a stream now invalidates the cache.

Also cover a FLAC stream fed in one EOF-marked write draining through a
PCM ring a quarter of its decoded size.

* fix(zz9000): keep the media audio clock on its first decoded timestamp

Acknowledging PCM rebuilt the audio PTS from zero, so streams whose
audio starts at a nonzero timestamp jumped backward on the first read.
Like the card, the clock is now the first decoded audio timestamp plus
the acknowledged duration, and status page 1 reports that origin.

* fix(zz9000): finish media and Vorbis streams only when they are complete

A media session reported DONE as soon as FFmpeg finished, while decoded
PCM could still be queued on the host waiting for ring space; a client
that closes on DONE lost that tail. DONE is now held back with the same
BUSY audio-backpressure reply the MPEG-1 path uses until the queue is
empty.

An Ogg Vorbis stream cut at a page boundary flushed and ended normally.
Like the firmware, the stream must now reach its EOS page; EOF before it,
a packet cut by EOS, or another complete page after EOS fails with
IO_ERROR, and other trailing bytes are ignored.

* fix(zz9000): fail media on decode errors and parse large FLAC feeds

The media worker treated any avcodec_receive_frame() or av_read_frame()
error like EAGAIN/EOF, so corrupt data could end as DONE. Only EAGAIN
and AVERROR_EOF now end a drain or the read loop; other errors fail the
session with IO_ERROR.

FLAC rejected any queued input over 128 KiB, so a valid feed larger than
that failed. The parser already takes 4 KiB at a time; retained input
is now bounded by the session's input capacity plus one partial frame
or Ogg page, as FEED only hands over new input once the previous feed
is decoded.

* fix(zz9000): judge Vorbis EOF only after parsing can continue

With a single EOF-marked feed whose pages decode to more PCM than the
ring holds, PCM backpressure stopped parsing before the EOS page and the
EOF check then failed a valid stream. The check now waits until the
parser is no longer held back, like the FLAC path.

* fix(zz9000): accept the next feed when only a partial page is buffered

has_pending() reported any retained input as pending work, so a feed
that ended inside an Ogg page or FLAC header made FEED refuse every
later feed and the stream stalled. Pending now means decoded PCM waiting
for the ring or decoding stopped by output backpressure; bytes that need
more input no longer block the feed that would complete them.

* fix(ci): build Windows ARM64 without FFmpeg and use an even WebP animation

vcpkg's FFmpeg port fails to configure for arm64-mingw-dynamic, so the
manifest skips it there, as it already does for mpg123; that build keeps
libwebp and leaves the FFmpeg codecs unadvertised.

FFmpeg 6.1 (Ubuntu 24.04) encodes the 2x3 animated WebP test fixture
with a 2x2 canvas, so the fixture is now 2x2 on every FFmpeg version.

The shared SDK test compile helper moves to tests/lib/ so run_tests.sh
no longer runs it as a test.

* fix(zz9000): select Matroska PCM and MPEG audio tracks like the card

The track scan only accepted DVD LPCM and MP2. Matroska stores LPCM as
A_PCM/INT/LIT, which FFmpeg reports as PCM_S16LE, and the card's
Matroska and Program Stream demuxers accept MPEG audio of any layer.
Audio tracks are now matched per container: MP1/MP2/MP3 for MPEG audio,
DVD LPCM in Program Streams, and 16-bit 48 kHz mono or stereo
little-endian PCM in Matroska.

* fix(zz9000): reject FLAC streams shorter than STREAMINFO declares

A FLAC file cut on a frame boundary drained and flushed normally. Like
the card's step_finish(), a nonzero STREAMINFO total-sample count must
now match the decoded samples at EOF, otherwise the stream fails with
IO_ERROR.

* fix(zz9000): check Ogg pages the way the card's page layer does

A Vorbis stream with a lost page still decoded to a short, successful
result. The page parser now applies the card's libogg and next_page()
checks: the page CRC, consecutive sequence numbers, a single BOS, a
continuation flag that matches the packet in progress, and another
stream's pages (a new BOS is unsupported, anything else an error).

* fix(zz9000): admit decoded PCM frames larger than the audio queue

A Matroska PCM block can decode to more than the worker's 512 KiB audio
queue; the worker then waited forever for room it could never get. A
frame is now admitted whenever the queue is empty, so an oversized block
drains through the guest ring like any other.

* fix(zz9000): decode a WebP image once per session

Tile output repeats the EOF-marked feed for every band, and each one
decoded the whole WebP again, up to thousands of times for a large image
with a small tile buffer. Like the JPEG/PNG path, a still is decoded
once and later feeds reuse its pixels; an animation is likewise set up
only on the first EOF feed.

* fix(zz9000): count published Vorbis PCM in bytes for granule trimming

consume_pcm() counted whole frames and dropped the remainder, so with a
ring or read size that is not a frame multiple the published count drifted
low and the EOS trim kept extra samples. Published PCM is now counted in
bytes.

* fix(zz9000): bound the converted console row by the framebuffer row

For BGRA framebuffers served as RGB565 the requested bytes-per-row was
only bounded below, so a request could size the host shadow and snapshot
at up to 65535 bytes per row regardless of the framebuffer. The
converted row may no longer be wider than the 32-bit source row.

* fix(zz9000): switch media PCM format only after the old PCM is retired

When a stream's audio changed rate or channel count, the next chunk
overwrote the session format while PCM in the old format was still in
the guest ring, so acknowledgements were checked and the clock computed
against the wrong frame size and rate. A new format now waits until all
earlier PCM is acknowledged, then the clock restarts from that chunk's
timestamp.

* fix(zz9000): downmix multichannel AC-3 to stereo like the card

Any decoded audio with more than two channels failed the session, so an
ordinary 5.1 AC-3 VOB could not play. The card decodes AC-3 with liba52
fixed to A52_STEREO output; the worker now downmixes AC-3 to stereo too.
Opus, Vorbis and the other codecs still accept only mono or stereo, as
the card's WebM and Matroska backends do.

* fix(zz9000): share one 64 MiB budget across media-input allocations

Each card-only media allocation was limited to 64 MiB on its own, so
filling every buffer slot could make the host allocate about 1 GiB.
Like the card's MEDIA_INPUT pool class, all media-input buffers now
share 64 MiB; an allocation beyond it returns NO_MEMORY.

events.title: Sample the village walk in runs at cruise pace and widen the side-on search
events.message:
Sample the village walk in runs at cruise pace and widen the side-on search

The walk probe stopped after one frame: the walker it took had just left
its door with its smoothed speed still easing up (walk share 1), and one
frame later it reached its route pace at walk share 0.06. The walker is
now one at its cruise pace (within 10 %), heading straight at its
waypoint with at least 3 m of that leg left, the slowest such cruiser.
A turn still adds its step to the walk speed and tips a brisk walker
into the jog band for a few frames, so the walk is sampled in runs of
consecutive walk-gait frames: a dip ends the run, a walker that stops
walking is replaced by the next that qualifies, and stances and slips
are measured within a run only. The detail names runs, walkers and gaps.

The side-on camera search found no spot at the kneeling task walker: an
unnamed cylinder blocked the hips on every one of the 18 spots. It now
tries finer angle steps (0, 0.15, 0.3, 0.45 rad either way) and five
distances, and a red names each refused spot's reason (pushed off, or
the blocking mesh with its geometry and position).

events.title: lift32: rep movs into itself repeats the source, as the CPU does (#102)
events.message:
lift32: rep movs into itself repeats the source, as the CPU does (#102)

A rep movs copies one element at a time, so when the destination starts
inside what is still to be read, the copy reads its own output: rep movsd
from p to p+12 repeats p's 12 bytes along the buffer. The lifter emitted
memmove, which copies as if through a temporary. Red Alert 2 starts a
Tesla bolt's three strands that way, and memmove left the second and
third holding stale stack: lines ran off the top of the screen on every
shot (redalert2-recomp#10).

recomp_rep_movs walks element by element in that one case and keeps
memmove for every other. difftest: forward and backward overlap cases.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: run64tass: give 64tass paths of 260+ characters with the \\?\ prefix on Windows (#118)
events.message:
run64tass: give 64tass paths of 260+ characters with the \\?\ prefix on Windows (#118)

64tass on Windows cannot open a path of MAX_PATH (260) characters or more:
"fatal error: can't open file '<...>.tas'", and the rebuild proof called every
such listing "diverged" (a GMod2 project at a 155-character root: 0 of 64
byte-identical). Measured: the source, -o and -l paths all need the prefix;
259 characters work, 260 fail.

run64tass now passes each of the three through longPathArg(): on win32 and
only at 260+ characters it becomes path.toNamespacedPath(path); shorter paths
and other platforms are unchanged. New test:
scripts/e2e-issue118-64tass-long-path.mjs.

events.title: assemble-source, fingerprint: split path lists on path.delimiter; 64tass.exe on Windows (#113)
events.message:
assemble-source, fingerprint: split path lists on path.delimiter; 64tass.exe on Windows (#113)

resolveFromPath split PATH on ":" and looked for "64tass" only, so on Windows
(";" separator, "64tass.exe") a 64tass on PATH was never found and the rebuild
proof skipped unless C64RE_64TASS_BIN was set. loadLibraries split
C64RE_FINGERPRINT_LIBS on ":" too, which breaks every "C:\..." entry.

Both now split on path.delimiter (":" off Windows, unchanged there); on win32
the PATH lookup asks for "<name>.exe" (execFile runs no .cmd/.bat without a
shell). New test: scripts/e2e-issue113-path-list-delimiter.mjs.

events.title: pipeline: toPosixRelative takes path.relative, so Windows manifests stay relative
events.message:
pipeline: toPosixRelative takes path.relative, so Windows manifests stay relative

toPosixRelative stripped a `${base}/` prefix. On Windows the base ends in
"\", the prefix never matched, and the CRT, boot-payload and menu-export
manifests kept absolute paths ("C:/..."). disasm_menu then ran
join(workspaceRoot, file.file) and opened a doubled path (ENOENT).

Now the path is computed with path.relative; a target outside the base
keeps its full path, as before. New check scripts/e2e-pipeline-posix-relative.mjs
(RED 3/3 on Windows before, GREEN 6/0 after); e2e-one-store-writer goes
from 60/3 to 63/0 on Windows.

events.title: loader-lens: a BLOCK_READ2 visit is taken only with most of the data block (#77)
events.message:
loader-lens: a BLOCK_READ2 visit is taken only with most of the data block (#77)

TRX64 counts every GCR byte latched after the data sync as data, so a loader
that hunts for the next header sync and rejects the data block after its
block id leaves records with dataBytes 1-2. `taken: dataBytes > 0` counted
those passes as reads: on the IM II capture 905 of 1282 taken records were
d1/d2, crediting three payloads the run never loaded and producing 5 false
"read past" FAILs (criteria 2b and 4).

A visit of a sector with a header is now taken only with dataBytes >= 163
(TAKEN_MIN_DATA_BYTES, more than half of the 325-byte GCR data block). Every
real read on the capture is d324/d326. Sector 0xff (no header, no block
length) keeps dataBytes > 0.

Tests: e2e-loader-lens and e2e-validate-extraction build the read-set from
BLOCK_READ2 events with d1/d2 passes; RED on master, GREEN here.

events.title: lores sliced: stop dropping a seed colour; retune OCS d5 sliced dither
events.message:
lores sliced: stop dropping a seed colour; retune OCS d5 sliced dither

Regression from 5e451589 (2026-05-06). encode_copper's seed fill put
lock_color0 black at slot 0, then copied the quantizer output into
slots 1..N in order. When the quantizer picks black, two_pass_quantize
retries at K = num_colors and the result contains that black. The
in-order fill put a second black at slot 1 and dropped the last
colour. On DIV2K 0041 that colour was the near-white of the wall
highlights: S2 56 -> 27. Before 5e451589, finalize_palette removed the
black from the quantizer output.

New palette_locks::fill_unlocked_slots fills the unlocked slots and
skips quantizer entries that bit-match a locked slot, the same rule
assemble_locked_palette uses. copper.cpp (lores/AGA sliced) and the
EHB strips seed in strips.cpp had the same in-order fill; both now
use the helper.

The OCS lores d5 sliced dither default (1.0 / 0.10) was swept when
the mean was 35.6. On a 34-image DIV2K tuning set, disjoint from the
21 verification images, 0.72 / 0.35 scores 53.40 against 51.06 for
1.0 / 0.10 (plain lores d5: 51.48).

21 DIV2K images, in-process S2 means:
  plain 55.39, sliced 50.47 -> 56.89.
EHB sliced is unchanged (0779 / 0041 / 0091 = 55.97 / 63.34 / 58.39).

events.message:
grm-dos9.13: drop partly known states that contradict an overlay's wrap-invariant residence

grm-dos9.12 dropped a flow into an overlay only when the state was fully known
and named another occupant. A partly known state whose known bits contradict
the overlay still clamped. It is now tested against residenceInvariant: the
mode bits (never wrap) plus the bank bits canonicalBank keeps -- obtained by

events.title: tls: a chain sent out of order is checked in order
events.message:
tls: a chain sent out of order is checked in order

Some servers send their certificates in another order than each one's
issuer next - www.gutenberg.org: leaf, root, the intermediate's issuer,
the intermediate - which TLS 1.2 forbids and browsers forgive; BearSSL's
validator took them as sent and stopped at the first mismatch (55,
DN_MISMATCH). xdefer_order puts them in order first, by their names
(cert_names), from the leaf up; what isn't on that path follows, as
sent. Nothing is trusted that wasn't: the validator still checks every
signature and name, and only certificates on the checked path are
learned. The T425's work ahead follows the same order (on the TT: three
signatures ahead, all used). tests/test_xdefer.c.

feeds: RSS and Atom as pages; F, the page's feed

html/feed.c turns RSS 0.9x/1.0/2.0 and Atom into HTML as it streams,
item by item: the title as a link, date, author, picture, text (the full
one over a summary; XHTML content's markup kept, plain text's line
breaks) and enclosures. Its own small XML tokenizer: the HTML one would
take <link> for a void element and CDATA for a comment. Other XML shows
as its source. tests/test_feed.c, and fuzz_feed in make check.

pages are walled off or need JavaScript keep one - Stack Exchange

events.title: grm-u7cy: realrom-test.sh solo-reruns a batched FAIL up to 3 times; FLAKY verdict
events.message:
grm-u7cy: realrom-test.sh solo-reruns a batched FAIL up to 3 times; FLAKY verdict

A batched row whose dump differed from its golden got ONE solo diagnostic
rerun, and a pass labelled it BATCH-DEPENDENT. grm-pwuh's deadly_towers
was flaky solo (FAIL/FAIL/PASS), passed its one sample, and was triaged
for a day as a cross-program leak.

Now up to GRM_REALROM_SOLO_RERUNS (default 3, validated) solo reruns,
stopping at the first pass/fail disagreement:
  all pass  -> BATCH-DEPENDENT (solo passes N/N)
  mixed     -> FLAKY (nondeterministic even solo, not a batch leak)
  all fail  -> genuine diff, + NONDETERMINISTIC if the solo dumps differ
               from each other or from the batched dump
Each rerun gets its own .soloN log/dump/diff. FLAKY and NONDETERMINISTIC
evict the batched candidate from the cache, as BATCH-DEPENDENT did.

Verified: a golden corrupted on purpose, smb+contra batched -> smb
"genuine diff: solo passes 0/3", no NONDETERMINISTIC note (deterministic
row); GRM_REALROM_SOLO_RERUNS=0 exits 2. The BATCH-DEPENDENT and FLAKY
branches need a genuinely nondeterministic row and were reviewed, not run.
Docs: usage text, .claude/rules/realrom-tier.md, realrom/README.md;
bd memory realrom-batching updated. No analysis change.

events.title: EHB sliced: stop half-brite twin capturing idle base slots
events.message:
EHB sliced: stop half-brite twin capturing idle base slots

find_best_swap_ehb offered the doubled half-brite centroid for any slot
with a non-empty k+32 cluster, even when the base half k served no
pixels in the window. A slot idle on a stretch of rows (DIV2K 0041: the
#EEE highlight base, slot 31) was walked EEE->DEE->AFF->8EF->8FF to
serve the teal half-brite cluster. Swap candidates come only from
cluster centroids, and the later highlight pixels fall into the #DDD
wall cluster, so white was never proposed again: the wall wisp and drum
glint clipped to #DDD with no brighter entry for the dither to reach.

Only re-aim a slot via its twin when the base half still holds >= 0.5
weighted px (the same emptiness bar as kStealEmptyThreshold), matching
the indexed planner, which never moves an empty slot.

ehb --sliced S2 (in-process), 19 DIV2K images: 0041 42.96 -> 59.24
(plain EHB 59.84); mean 56.40 -> 57.16; the other 18 move -0.10 mean.

events.title: fix(loader): enter an erased-header cart at $802000, not $800000 (#979)
events.message:
fix(loader): enter an erased-header cart at $802000, not $800000 (#979)

Phase Zero (2000) (PD) differs from the signed, verified [a1] dump in
660 bytes: the encrypted boot block and the $400-$40B universal header
are erased to $FF.  In HLE, cart+$404 = $FFFFFFFF is not a valid
vector, so the loader fell back to $800000 -- $FFFF, a line-F trap --
and the 68K ping-ponged between it and the HLE RTE stub from frame 1
(black screen for the whole run).  The program is at $802000, the
address [a1]'s vector names.

An erased vector ($FFFFFFFF) with a 68K entry at $802000 now enters
there.  Any other invalid vector keeps the $800000 fallback (raw code
at the cart base, the case the existing comment describes).

HLE frames 300 and 600 are pixel-identical to the [a1] HLE reference.
Loader census, 699-file corpus: Phase Zero (PD) (3 copies) moves, and
so does the Developer CD BIOS image when loaded directly as content
(also an erased $404, entry $802000 = MOVEA.L #,A7): it now enters at
$802000 like the retail CD BIOS row.  The CD boot path stages BIOS
images through external_cd_bios, not this loader, so CD boots are
unaffected.  Real-BIOS mode is unchanged (it ignores jaguarRunAddress);
the BIOS reject there is authentic (no boot block).

Refs #974

events.title: fix(debug): give gdbdisasm.h the MSVC < 2015 snprintf shim (buildbot msvc05/10) (#982)
events.message:
fix(debug): give gdbdisasm.h the MSVC < 2015 snprintf shim (buildbot msvc05/10) (#982)

gdbdisasm.h calls snprintf in 13 places. MSVC 2005 and 2010 have no
snprintf, so libretro-common's compat/msvc.h maps it to
c99_snprintf_retro__. gdbtarget.c includes that shim before the header.
vjdebug.c (the app debug interface) does not, so it referenced a
snprintf symbol the old CRT does not have. Since v3.9.0 that has failed
the GitLab buildbot's msvc05-i686, msvc10-i686 and msvc10-x64 jobs at
link time.

The shim now comes from the header that needs it, guarded by
_MSC_VER, so no future includer can miss it.

Preprocessing every Makefile.common TU as MSVC 2010 (-D_MSC_VER=1600
-D_WIN32) found vjdebug.c to be the only one with bare snprintf calls.
After this change it has none.

Fixes #981

events.title: feat(zztop): check GitHub for newer firmware and install it
events.message:
feat(zztop): check GitHub for newer firmware and install it

The Firmware page gains Check online, a Board chooser and Download and
install. ZZTop asks the GitHub API for the latest non-prerelease
zz9000-firmware release, compares it with the running firmware and
downloads zz9000-firmware-<tag>-<variant>.zip over AmiSSL. The ZIP is
streamed through a local-header reader that inflates BOOT.bin to T:,
checks its CRC-32, size and Zynq boot header, then installs it with the
existing FWUP path (BOOT.bak kept).

- Board is preselected from the bitstream's field-diagnostic variant
  word and the C28 capture ID (firmware 2.8+); an image for the other
  Zorro bus is refused, any other build change asks first.
- The installed patch level comes from the new firmware patch register
  (ZZ_FW_CAP_FW_VERSION_PATCH, 0xC2); older firmware falls back to the
  tag ZZTop last installed (ENVARC:ZZTopFirmware), else "may be newer".
- Status shows 2.8.1-style versions when the card reports a patch.
- HTTPS client: bsdsocket + AmiSSL 5, TLS 1.2+, certificate and host
  name verification, redirects, chunked bodies, non-blocking with
  Esc/close cancel. DOS volume requesters are off while it runs:
  AmiSSL falls back to AmiTCP:Libs/usergroup.library and would
  otherwise stop ZZTop on stacks without that assign.
- Inflation uses vendored miniz 3.1.2 tinfl (MIT). The toolchain
  libz.a corrupts the real v2.8.1 BOOT.bin on m68k, and GCC 6.5's bbb
  peephole pass miscompiles tinfl, so common/miniz/build-m68k.sh
  builds it with -fbbb=-.

Tests: common/tests/fw_release_test.c (tags, version comparison,
variant detection, JSON, URLs, HTTP heads, chunked decoding, ZIP
extraction at every split, corruption and rejection paths) and
fw_release_m68k.sh, which runs the production extractor under vamos in
CI and fails without -fbbb=-.

feat(site): per-page share cards and a favicon set from the app icon (#985)

* feat(site): per-page share cards and a favicon set from the app icon

Every page shared one og:image, the Cybermorph true-color comparison,
which reads as a small low-contrast strip in a link preview; the site had
no favicon at all.

- scripts/make_share_cards.py (Pillow + rsvg-convert) composes two
  1200x630 cards: home.png, eight game captures from site/assets/home/
  over the icon and wordmark, and app.png, zoomed crops of the desktop app
  captures (library, Rayman under the Lottes CRT shader, palette debugger,
  light theme). It refuses to write a card that is not exactly 1200x630 or
  is 1 MB or more. It also renders favicon.svg/.ico, icon-192/512.png and
  an opaque full-bleed apple-touch-icon from
  app/packaging/icons/virtualjaguar.svg. Outputs are committed; the
  stdlib-only site build only copies them.
- build_site.py: SHARE_DEFAULT plus a per-page SHARE_IMAGES map replace
  the global SHARE_IMAGE; each page gets its own og:image, twitter:image,
  alt, type, width and height (read from the PNG), and the home JSON-LD
  image follows. Every page head links the favicon set; favicon.ico is
  also copied to the output root.
- check_site.py: twitter:image must equal og:image, the width/height tags
  must match the PNG, the card must be under 1 MB, and every page must
  carry rel=icon and rel=apple-touch-icon links.

Closes #984

events.title: Multibyte Macros: Simplify handling of addressing modes
events.message:
Multibyte Macros: Simplify handling of addressing modes

The macros like add16 handled addressing modes with a big "if"
statement branching on whether particular macro parameters were
registers or not, with separate code generation paths for each. This
made maintenance difficult and support was inconsistent across macros.

The code generation already used helpers that would handle
working on the Nth byte of a value differently depending on whether
it was immediate or absolute. So this change:

* Extends the helpers to handle indexed modes.

* Has the main macros squash their arguments, so if called with e.g.
  two args "lsr16 foo, x" convert that into "lsr16 {foo,x}" and let
  the helpers do the dirty work.

No binary changes.

carries the new one. Stored tags/boundary attrs are renamed once on graph open
(meta.slot_ids), contract.json and the standing ledger on read.

runtime-trace, knowledge-import, signatures, signature-resolve, cartridge, document,

through a writer), idempotent; callers' old ids are read through canonicalProducer.

reason); e2e:legacy-names proves both migrations and the old-input acceptance.

events.title: Complete the data that the code reads past its declared bounds
events.message:
Complete the data that the code reads past its declared bounds

AddressSanitizer runs of the port's stage scenarios showed reads and writes
past declarations that are only contiguous in the original's layout:
- g_weatherSymbolPositions (0x52718c) holds the weather map symbol
  positions of all eight countries (0xb0 bytes); only the first country was
  declared, so the others read the strings after it.
- The four driver group records at 0x52ebc0 and the tables after them
  (0x52f0e0..0x52f2a7) are one RallyDriverGroupTable: the network setup
  packet copies the pairing tables, 0x52f0fc, 0x52f290 and 0x52f294 as
  offsets from the records. Its read/write functions now use the fields.
- g_loadedSplitTimes has the twelve entries the stage HUD reads; the last
  two are never written and stay zero, as in the original's free space.
- Race_StorePlayerRouteAndClearSlots documents that the original writes
  past its two-entry arrays for computer cars.

Bytes unchanged: 2923 exact, 0 data issues (the full weather table
compared against the original).

events.title: tickDelta reads frameCnt once; entity trims; seam and test switches
events.message:
tickDelta reads frameCnt once; entity trims; seam and test switches

- tickDelta read frameCnt twice; an IRQ between the reads put a tick into
  lastMv but never dtv. ~1 frame in 8 on level 9's spin, so motion ran
  slower at HIGHER fps (turn -4.7% at 21 fps, -1.7% at 9). Now exact.
- obOrder: survivors go into a sorted list as the keys are made, instead
  of a repeated minimum over every entity (-1,090/frame, 8 sentries).
- svTick writes sprite pointers only when the spark frame or ink changes;
  osFlush -> svWr rewrites them every rendered frame (-1,130/frame).
- SEAMEVERY=n (panel line every n cells) and SEAMGAP=1 (no line one cell
  from a corner): opt-in, default build byte-identical.
- Test switches: SVFREEZE (sentries still, no sparks: level 9 builds can
  be compared), PADX (PADIN's inner count), OPENALL (every level 9 door
  open; restarts are known to misbehave).

regress: renders the same as 87965f2. fps suite: clean except level 2's
walk bump, present since level 8 shipped.

events.title: fix(input): keep Host Only cursor hotspot stable during slow movement (#2457)
events.message:
fix(input): keep Host Only cursor hotspot stable during slow movement (#2457)

* fix(input): keep Host Only cursor hotspot stable during slow movement

The guest moves its pointer sprite a frame or two after it receives a new
position, so while the pointer moves the pointer-to-sprite displacement
includes the distance covered during that lag. Steady slow movement keeps
that biased value constant, and the tracker confirmed it as the hotspot for
the rest of the session.

Only learn from settled samples, where pointer and sprite have not changed
for three samples. An axis is confirmed when a second resting position along
it gives the same displacement.

Fixes #2452

* fix(input): count settled cursor samples per frame

createwindowscursor() can run more than once per frame: a P96 shape change
calls it directly and again through setupcursor(), and window events rebuild
the native cursor too. Repeats within one frame gave the guest no time to
move its sprite but still counted toward a settled position. Pass
vsync_counter and only count unchanged samples from distinct frames.

events.title: grm-pwuh: read post-switch jump tables from the switched-in bank (BankContext, gib.2 stand-in)
events.message:
grm-pwuh: read post-switch jump tables from the switched-in bank (BankContext, gib.2 stand-in)

deadly_towers was FLAKY, not batch-dependent: it also failed solo most runs. Its bus-conflict-safe
BNROM trampolines (fc27/fc3c/fc51 in every bank) switch banks and THEN read their jump table, so at
runtime the table comes from the switched-in bank. Ghidra read it from each copy's own bank. In
B2's copy that gave 59 garbage targets whose decodes raced real flow, so FUN_PRG_ALL_B2__fc3f's body,
and the helper model findHelpers builds from it, varied run to run (fd42 bank 3 vs 0).

- BankContext (new): the extension-side stand-in for gib.2's context-aware address resolution
  (docs/rfc-banked-memory.md). It is usable at any analysis priority. stateBefore() simulates the
  straight-line run locally: residence seed (clampToResidence), then the board's mechanisms via
  BankDataflowEngine.applyDirectSwitch. resolve() maps an operand to the occupant the state selects.
  switchedInCopyReadsTableIn() corroborates from raw bytes (PseudoDisassembler, pure indexed loads
  by p-code), so the answer does not depend on analysis order. The cache holds values weakly: the
  configured strategies keep MemoryBlocks, which would otherwise pin each Program in a batched JVM.
- CrossBankTable (new, pure): model fitting (word-LE or planar lo/hi, +k) that must reproduce
  EVERY decompiler target from the bytes it read, plus the valid-prefix rule (at most one leading
  junk slot, then up to the first target outside the switched window).
- JumpTableBoundAnalyzer: when the table resolves to another bank, re-read it there, keep the
  valid prefix, require corroboration (the switched-in bank's own copy reads an overlapping table,
  with one stride of slack below), and ALWAYS pin by references. An override cannot carry
  cross-space targets (decompiler-no-cross-space-branch). The pin also stops stock switch analysis
  laying down the garbage. Any decline leaves the pre-change path untouched.

deadly_towers: B1/B2/B3 copies pin 18/26/95-entry tables in the right bank. The bank-0 copies'
"$8000 tables" are code in every bank, so they decline. Byte-identical across 4 solo runs and the
batched run. Re-blessed (owner rulings 2026-10-15): bank comments are unchanged from the old
golden, symbols drop 636 -> 350 (garbage case labels gone), and the code reached across banks goes
up. The one new warning (ad41) is real code flowing into RAM.

Gates: build-and-test.sh check SUITE OK (79/79); realrom-test.sh check nes 34 PASS + deadly_towers
(re-blessed); no other row moved.

events.title: fix(gui): make FPS adj. usable and remove the inert Refresh slider (#2456)
events.message:
fix(gui): make FPS adj. usable and remove the inert Refresh slider (#2456)

* fix(gui): make FPS adj. usable and remove the inert Refresh slider

The FPS adj. row indexed changed_prefs.cr[] with cr_selected, which defaults to -1, so its checkbox and slider read and wrote memory outside the chipset refresh array. The checkbox was also clipped out of its table column. The row now edits the PAL or NTSC entry of the selected video standard and follows the WinUAE dialog: locking marks the entry in use, unlocking restores 50/60 Hz, the slider covers 1-99 Hz and the value can be typed in.

Frameskip (gfx_framerate) has no visible effect with the WinUAE 6 core, where Denise draws and the host presents every frame; WinUAE 6.0.3 behaves the same. Remove the Display panel Refresh slider and the default_frameskip global setting that only set it to 2.

* fix(gui): reset an invalid FPS adj. rate to the edited standard's rate

The fallback used currprefs.ntscmode, which still holds the running standard until pending settings are applied, so switching PAL to NTSC and typing an invalid rate locked NTSC at 50 Hz. Derive it from the entry being edited, and treat typed rates below 1 Hz (including 0 and negatives) as invalid too.

events.title: fix(debug): give gdbdisasm.h the MSVC < 2015 snprintf shim (buildbot msvc05/10)
events.message:
fix(debug): give gdbdisasm.h the MSVC < 2015 snprintf shim (buildbot msvc05/10)

gdbdisasm.h calls snprintf in 13 places. MSVC 2005 and 2010 have no
snprintf, so libretro-common's compat/msvc.h maps it to
c99_snprintf_retro__. gdbtarget.c includes that shim before the header.
vjdebug.c (the app debug interface) does not, so it referenced a
snprintf symbol the old CRT does not have. Since v3.9.0 that has failed
the GitLab buildbot's msvc05-i686, msvc10-i686 and msvc10-x64 jobs at
link time.

The shim now comes from the header that needs it, guarded by
_MSC_VER, so no future includer can miss it.

Preprocessing every Makefile.common TU as MSVC 2010 (-D_MSC_VER=1600
-D_WIN32) found vjdebug.c to be the only one with bare snprintf calls.
After this change it has none.

Fixes #981

  reserve, foehit, skeep, bmax, guns.

Μετά, ό,τι έκανε ακόμη το παιχνίδι, και οι επιλογές του χρήστη:

events.title: fix(loader): place BJL RAM images and $802000-based images where they were linked (#978)
events.message:
fix(loader): place BJL RAM images and $802000-based images where they were linked (#978)

* fix(loader): read GEMDOS/DRI 601A executables and JAGR type 2 with their own layouts

Mandelbrot Demo (PD) is a plain GEMDOS/DRI executable: 601A, text $EBE,
symbols $2CD8, a zero relocation long, and no "JAG" at $1C.  It was
parsed as JST_WTFOMGBBQ, whose load address is the little-endian long at
$1C -- here the first instruction, $46FC2700, read as $0027FC46 -- so
the program was copied outside main RAM and the 68K parked in the
ILLEGAL guard at $1000 from frame 1.  A 601A file whose sizes add up to
the file is now JST_DRI: text+data go to the base the raw-binary scorer
infers, else the BJL upload address $4000, and a GEMDOS relocation
table, if present, is applied against that base.  Files that are not
self-consistent keep the old reading.

Jaguar Server INTRO / INTROMOD are JAGR type 2 ($0002 at $20): load
$22, length $26, code at $2A, entered at the load address.  The loader
assumed type 3 (run $2A, code $2E), so it took the first code long
$23FC03D0 as the run address and dropped four code bytes.

Loader census over the 699-file private corpus: only these rows move
(Mandelbrot x3 copies -> $4000; INTRO/INTROMOD x3 copies -> $4FF6).
HLE frames: the Mandelbrot set and the Jaguar/cube/ATARI intro render,
matching the triage's hand-wrapped loads.

Refs #971

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(loader): place BJL RAM images and $802000-based images where they were linked

Issue #972 (raw-binary round 2):
- Hubble Fade, Hubble Nebula and Drumpad2 are headerless BJL programs
  with one absolute reference or none in their first 2 KiB, so the raw
  scorer (bar of 8) could not place them and they fell through to the
  sub-1 MiB cartridge fallback: HLE ran from cart+$404 / $800000 and the
  boot ROM rejected them in BIOS mode.  A sub-1 MiB image with no $400
  marker that opens with a 68K instruction and has no encrypted boot
  block (byte 0 $F6-$FE) now loads as a RAM program at $4000.
- Painter (bin) is the payload of the JAGR Painter, linked at $10000.
  $10000 is a new, last candidate.  Containment gave $4000 a 14-13 edge
  through one LEA $4000,A0 (a RAM buffer below the image); a JMP abs.L
  that lands on an abs.L instruction the scorer decoded now counts as
  entry evidence (its JMP $10012 hits the LEA $1FFFFC,A7 at offset $12
  under $10000 only).  JSRs onto decoded instructions are not counted:
  over the corpus that matched only by coincidence.

Issue #973 (offset 0 = $802000):
- BadCode4 (Metal)/(Modified) "(rom)" open with a stub that reads its
  own header through cart addresses ($802054/$802048/$80204C) and copies
  the (bin) build to $4000.  Two such abs.L loads in the first $40 bytes
  -> JST_ALPINE, whatever the size.
- Rayman Demo is exactly 2 MiB with no $400 universal header; its
  startup JSRs to $802xxx.  An exact-MiB image without the marker whose
  raw-scorer verdict is $802000 -> JST_ALPINE.  Only Rayman Demo and
  Phase Zero (PD) lack the marker among exact-MiB files in the corpus,
  and Phase Zero is all $FF up front (no verdict), so it stays a cart.

Loader census, 699-file private corpus: the only rows that move are
those titles (all copies).  HLE frames match the triage's hand-fixed
loads (Hubble photographs, Painter title menu, Rayman gameplay, Bad Ball
2001 title); Drumpad2 goes from 0 to 154,968 non-silent samples after one
button press (black screen is authentic, like Drumpad).  These titles no
longer run the boot ROM in BIOS mode (RAM programs / Alpine images).

BadCode4 (Metal) (bin) [a1] stays unresolved by design: it is the (bin)
build with its first $1A0 bytes (big-endian mode, stack, video timing
init) cut and a different 176-byte prologue; its JSR targets line up
with subroutine starts only at base $41A0, and loaded there it waits
forever for a VBL counter.  An incomplete dump, not a loader bug.

Refs #972, #973

events.title: test(matrix): score a black run whose 68K is stuck in an exception loop as a crash (#980)
events.message:
test(matrix): score a black run whose 68K is stuck in an exception loop as a crash (#980)

* test(matrix): score a black run whose 68K is stuck in an exception loop as a crash

The cart matrix called a run GAME_CODE when the final 68K PC was in
RAM, cart space or the boot ROM.  Two crash states pass that test and
were published as "Runs; video undetermined headlessly":

  - parked in the loader's ILLEGAL guard ($1000: BRA.S *, vector 4),
    e.g. Mandelbrot Demo, Painter (bin), Gorf 2000, the Jaguar Server
    examples;
  - an RTE ping-pong between one faulting PC and the HLE RTE stub at
    $404, e.g. Rayman Demo, Phase Zero (PD), Hubble Nebula.

The probe now reads the pcQueue ring and the RAM vector table every
frame and reports trap_frames (consecutive frames, up to the last, in
which every ring PC is inside an RTE / BRA.S * handler that one of
vectors 2-11 names, or is one single other PC), trap_pc (the faulting
PC; for a parked guard, the PC saved in the exception frame) and
trap_handler.  cart_classify.sh turns 30+ such frames into
"? (trap_loop)" when the run also never put a picture up.  With video
the row stays GAME_CODE and the notes say the 68K is parked: BJL demos
(DEMO1, DEMO1B, DEMO1C, Ladybug) end their 68K main on purpose and let
the GPU/OP run the demo.  A legitimate idle loop is not caught: Jaguar
Server JAGOS's 14-PC wait loop reads trap_frames=0.  The classifier's
final-PC extraction is now anchored to the field so trap_pc= cannot
match it.

matrix_diff reads GAME_CODE -> "? (trap_loop)" as backward (rank 1);
the baseline refresh that lands with this records those rows.

Refs #975

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(matrix): refresh the cart matrix baseline for ? (trap_loop)

Full cart sweep on the corpus host (155 titles, both modes, FAST
blitter, develop + the classifier change).  Against the previous
baseline, matrix_diff reports 29 cells GAME_CODE -> "? (trap_loop)":
the 18 HLE rows the matrix triage found crashed in frame 1-60 and the
BIOS cells of the 11 RAM-loaded ones (the boot ROM is not used there,
so they mirror HLE).  These are the scoring being corrected, not a
regression: every one had 0 lit frames and a 68K parked in the $1000
ILLEGAL guard or ping-ponging with the HLE RTE stub.  Each is ticketed:

  #971  Mandelbrot Demo, Jaguar Server INTRO / INTROMOD
  #972  Painter (bin), Hubble Nebula (HLE)
  #973  Rayman Demo x2, BadCode4 (Metal)/(Modified) (rom)
  #974  Phase Zero (PD) (HLE)
  #975  authentic, no loader fix possible: Jaguar Server 50HZ / 60HZ /
        KEYB (helpers that need the resident server), Gorf 2000 (a
        stale-A0 address error in the game's own startup), BadCode4
        (Metal) (bin) [a1] (an incomplete build), Assassin (for BJL),
        FFYL [a2], Kasumi Ninja [a1] (bad / altered dumps)

Seven GPU/OP-driven BJL demos (DEMO1 x2, DEMO1B x2, DEMO1C, Ladybug
x2) keep GAME_CODE with video; their notes now say the 68K is parked.
Every other row is unchanged apart from the build stamp.  The legend
gains the new stage.

Refs #975

events.title: gui: Drop the TextLength() calls placed before Text()
events.message:
gui: Drop the TextLength() calls placed before Text()

AfA_OS 4.8, which AmiKit uses, patches Text() and tests the count in d0
as a 32-bit value, skipping the call when it looks negative. Text()
takes a 16-bit count, and the ROM ignores the upper half of d0. Release
0.7.0 was built with macro-style inlines that loaded the count into a
16-bit register variable, so d0 often kept $FFFF in its upper half and
AfA drew nothing (#29). The TextLength() calls only helped because the
ROM routine returns with ext.l d0, which cleared the upper half for the
following Text().

The current NDK inlines pass the count as a zero-extended ULONG, so
every Text() call loads d0 as a full long and the extra calls do
nothing. Remove them and describe the real requirement in the file
header.

events.title: Let a standing-down head session carry its card answer to the owner
events.message:
Let a standing-down head session carry its card answer to the owner

The decision-card guard recognised a user prompt only by promptSource
"typed", but this CLI writes human prompts as promptSource "sdk" with
origin.kind "human", so every seeded session entry held a null
userMessage. vdzk-answer also read only CLAUDE_SESSION_ID (the harness
exports CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID) and, with the head session's entry
missing from the shared seed, could not identify the message at all.

Accept origin.kind "human" as the typed channel, read the harness's
session id, and fall back to the session's own transcript by exact id
when the guard seed has no message for it. The due-redeem path then
removes the answered card without any step in another session.

events.message:
build(sdk): pin the SDK at firmware master for the ZZPlay window fit

The installer still built ZZPlay from 6f9c9915 (ZZPlay 0.6). That version opens a video larger than the Workbench at its full size, Intuition clamps the window to the screen, and the resize handler then refits it to the video aspect on every IDCMP_NEWSIZE. The fit rounds one side down each time, so a 720p or 1080p window on a 1280x720 Workbench shrank by a pixel per frame until it reached an exact 16:9 size, moving the overlay and dropping frames on the way.

Firmware master opens the window already fitted to the screen and leaves a fitted window alone (f9a52a79, 91d08efa), along with the other ZZPlay and SDK changes since 0.6.

events.title: daemon: name each mounted medium by sha256 — state, trace header, media records (909)
events.message:
daemon: name each mounted medium by sha256 — state, trace header, media records (909)

C64RE files what a trace saw under the cartridge it ran on, and had only
the file name the runtime reported. The daemon now names every medium by
its hash.

- session/state: media.cart gains sha256, hwType (CRT header $16),
  mapperType, banks, crtName; media.disk and each drives[].disk gain
  sha256. A cartridge's hash is over the .crt bytes as mounted; a disk's
  over the file as the mount read it (media_identity.rs, cached per image,
  so a state poll does not rehash).
- .c64retrace header: a versioned `media` object {v:1, cart, drives:{unit}}
  at trace start. The older mediaSha/mediaName (drive 8 as written, the
  run descriptor's `media`) now also reach the header, where the readers
  already looked for them.
- Inside a trace: a MARK (0x01) record `media/1 <slot> in|out sha256=…`
  at the cycle a medium changed, and `media/1 power off` when the machine
  is switched off. A cartridge change is a power cycle, so a capture ends
  there and never spans it; the next capture names the new cartridge.
  Every reader already skips a MARK by its length, so old readers are
  unaffected. FrameSink gains write_mark (label cut at 200 bytes, the TS
  cap).
- traceindex: a trace_media table (run_id, cycle, slot, action, sha256,
  format, source_name, hw_type, mapper_type, banks, crt_name): `start`
  rows from the header, `in`/`out`/`power-off` from the records. Media
  records do not land in trace_mark. Stale "no schema change" and "TRX64
  writes no MARK" comments corrected.

Test: tests/media_identity_909.rs (real binary): a disk swap inside one
capture, a cartridge swap ending one, the next capture naming the new
cart, all hashes checked. Acceptance on Yeti Mountain EF → GMod2 copies:
both sha256 equal shasum, the swap cycle on the out and power-off rows.

events.title: input: drop stale live marks so scripted input never pins warp
events.message:
input: drop stale live marks so scripted input never pins warp

A live key or button mark outlived a release that did not come from the
operator's hand -- release_amiga_rawkey_if_held on the debugger
hand-back, release_mouse_buttons on a capture release, a reset clearing
the host keys -- and was only masked by the machine's held state. A
later scripted or control-protocol press of the same key or button made
the mark count again and paced that scripted input to real time under
warp.

Any host-keyboard transition now clears the key's mark (a live one sets
it again afterwards), the forced releases and resets clear theirs, and
each pass drops marks the machine no longer backs before deciding the
yield.
events.author: LinuxJedi

events.title: feat(mp): WITH-LOCK-HELD and WITH-RECURSIVE-LOCK-HELD take :TIMEOUT
events.message:
feat(mp): WITH-LOCK-HELD and WITH-RECURSIVE-LOCK-HELD take :TIMEOUT

(mp:with-lock-held (lock :timeout secs) body...) acquires with the
timeout MP:ACQUIRE-LOCK already understood (seconds, NIL = forever) and,
when it elapses first, skips the body and returns NIL -- the shape of
sb-thread:with-mutex and of bordeaux-threads' with-lock-held :timeout.
Without :timeout the expansion is unchanged.  with-recursive-lock-held
forwards the keyword.

The bordeaux-threads maintainer approved the AmiLisp backend (PR #137)
but asked that the timed lock path be fixed in the implementation rather
than hand-rolled in the library; the backend's %with-lock is now a
one-line delegation to this macro.  The macro lives in boot.lisp's
(in-package :mp) block, so its expansion uses only IF / LET /
UNWIND-PROTECT, which a source boot can read before the CL macros
boot.lisp defines are external.

Tests: tests/test_threads.c (free lock, timeout elapsed against a held
lock skips the body, timed wait sees the release, the timeout form is
evaluated once with NIL meaning forever, recursive nesting),
tests/amiga/run-tests.lisp, and a forced-compaction case in
tests/test_gc_stress_regression.sh.  docs/mp.md and the README's MP
section updated.

events.title: Adapt to existing project layouts via targets, [layout] and [[targets]]
events.message:
Adapt to existing project layouts via targets, [layout] and [[targets]]

A target is one thing being disassembled: a binary and its load
address, a driver, and the .asm/.json it writes. A target's files now
resolve in three layers, each overriding the last key by key: the
versions/ convention (unchanged, and the only layer a project without
the new sections uses), [layout] path templates, and explicit
[[targets]] entries with paths relative to the project root.

- The leading TARGET argument is optional when the project has one
  target or sets [project] default_target; otherwise omitting it fails
  with the list of targets.
- Explicit targets read load/exec addresses from a .inf sidecar. The
  new parser accepts the DFS and extended ADFS/stardot variants and
  reports unparseable files with a hint to set load_address.
- disassemble also sets FANTASM_TARGET, FANTASM_IMAGES, FANTASM_ASM and
  FANTASM_JSON, and honours a per-target driver_cwd.
- verify's assembler is configurable in [verify] (command, cwd and the
  output file to compare), defaulting to the existing beebasm call; a
  missing output is now a clean error. verify --all iterates targets.
- lint's driver argument defaults to the target's driver; a missing
  metadata file is fine and a malformed one is a clean error.
- project init writes [binary] rather than [rom], and --layout explicit
  adopts an existing project by writing a [[targets]] entry and
  nothing else. project add --binary appends one; project list shows
  each target's source and load address.
- Help text uses binary/target wording where commands aren't
  ROM-specific, and a new docs page covers disassembling disc-loaded
  programs, single-file and as one target per file.

Targets with more than one image are rejected for now.

events.title: input: pace host mouse motion and let warp yield to held input
events.message:
input: pace host mouse motion and let warp yield to held input

Two input problems reported on a fast Linux/X11 machine.

Fast mouse motion lost track of the pointer. X11 hands winit the
mouse's raw, unaccelerated device counts, and each host delta went into
the 8-bit JOYxDAT counters in one piece. Software takes the difference
of two reads of those counters, normally once a frame from the vertical
blank, so 128 counts or more between reads aliases into motion the
other way: a high-DPI mouse moved briskly sent the pointer backwards. A
real Amiga mouse never turns its encoders that fast. Live host motion
now reaches the counters at most 63 counts per axis per emulated frame
(half the wrap limit, since a delivery can land on either side of a
read), with one more frame's worth carried and the rest dropped so the
pointer stops when the hand does. Netplay already sampled with a clamp
of its own; scripted --mouse-after motion is unchanged.

Under warp, keys repeated and double-clicks failed. Warp runs the
guest's clock flat out, so a 100 ms key tap was held for seconds of
emulated time (input.device repeated it) and two clicks landed too far
apart for the double-click window. While a host key or a button on the
guest's mouse is held, and for 0.75 s after the last release, the
window now engages Emulator::set_warp_input_yield, which keeps the
pacer's sleep in force underneath warp. Warp stays engaged and paced()
still reports it, so the toggle, menus and control protocol are
unaffected. Scheduled and control-protocol input never engages it, so
text pasted as keystrokes keeps its warp speed. The emulated timeline is
the same either way.

project.title: ZZ9000 — native AmigaOS driver suite
project.display_title: ZZ9000 — native AmigaOS driver suite
project.status: active; ZZTop is rebuilt for a 640x256 GadTools window and the network driver has bounded asynchronous RX/TX paths
project.notes: Independent continuation of MNT’s ZZ9000 Amiga-side driver suite, with RTG, network/audio/USB/SD and native control utilities. Network device.c implements native SANA-II Amiga driver dispatch and hardware access; rtg/mntgfx-gcc.c implements graphics-card integration. README identifies the original MNT source and independent fork status, with firmware and ARM-side logic in separate repositories. Top-level build invokes pinned Amiga toolchain workflows; net/Makefile sets68020 and includes host-side test targets elsewhere in the suite. A reviewed code-fix commit explicitly credits Codex review; attribution is limited to review assistance. project.title: WinUAE
project.display_title: WinUAE — Amiga emulator & debugger
project.status: active; optional loopback GDB server plus current display-filter and RTG correctness fixes
project.notes: Actively maintained Windows Amiga emulator and a key compatibility/debugging tool for Amiga reverse engineering and retro development. Tracked as adjacent tooling rather than as a source-reconstruction target. Current main adds an opt-in, unauthenticated loopback GDB remote server shared by Windows and Unix builds. It exposes 18 m68k integer registers, physical RAM/ROM access, stepping, PC breakpoints and bounded data watchpoints; subsequent commits add standard vCont range stepping and complete RAM/ROM XML memory maps. It is disabled by default, single-client and local-only, and its memory addresses are physical rather than guest-MMU translations. Evidence: https://github.com/tonioni/WinUAE/commit/bdb195ec7bbea8ca43c37d30976e0f8ffd51d7b1 https://github.com/tonioni/WinUAE/commit/d7dc9b0ef7e19b016f36a18ad494d1f48e40aeda https://github.com/tonioni/WinUAE/commit/5afd2b2111e4340bad2c017c7082586b46c35b4d Subsequent mainline changes bound GDB range-watch values to supported memwatch widths and preserve debugger-requested resets at restart. Display work makes filter border blanking optional, adds its GUI control, corrects 15-bit low-resolution PCem/86Box RTG output and follows with an NTSC drawing fix. These are narrow debugger/display corrections; no compatibility-wide claim or tracker-side build is made. Evidence: https://github.com/tonioni/WinUAE/commit/342d5030ef7f4ea6a5be82647576072a25050d43 https://github.com/tonioni/WinUAE/commit/dacbc08d5620b4b8660cb8d6d6c4f5d5ba06ec4f https://github.com/tonioni/WinUAE/commit/2ab1c5acdfc3f94d287a943a71a57e698772fcd6 https://github.com/tonioni/WinUAE/commit/9c56300a6482f538071188ae49d7f57adfa8814b

project.notes: Swift macOS C64 emulator with shared Emu6502 core, C64 chip/1541 models, debugger and Metal/AVFoundation application. The same root also contains a secondary, earlier-stage NES emulator. Generic machine emulator/debugger tooling. Named games and compatibility media are tests, not game reconstructions; the secondary NES core does not imply mature NES compatibility. README explicitly says it boots to BASIC and links packaged v0.3.0, supporting runnable=true only as an upstream-reported partial emulator. Xcode and SwiftPM build instructions were inspected but not executed. Many games/demos still fail; true-drive/protected-media, analogue SID and flux behavior remain incomplete. No downloaded release or game was executed; compilable/playable/byte_exact stay null. Work in progress: README says many games/demos do not yet run correctly, true-drive compatibility needs validation, and analogue SID/flux behavior remains approximate. ROMs/commercial media are not supplied. No build, packaged release execution or compatibility testing was performed. Do not promote referenced games as game reconstructions. Root LICENSE is MIT. Copyrighted ROMs and commercial media are not supplied; the application imports user-provided copies.   Reviewed on 2026-10-05; no independent build, execution or byte comparison was performed. Evidence: https://github.com/peercom/swift64/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/peercom/swift64/blob/main/Sources/C64Core/C64.swift https://github.com/peercom/swift64/blob/main/Sources/Emu6502/CPU6502.swift https://github.com/peercom/swift64/blob/main/Package.swift https://github.com/peercom/swift64/blob/main/Swift64.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj https://github.com/peercom/swift64/blob/main/LICENSE Latest upstream commit: https://github.com/peercom/swift64/commit/030be2250cc44beb86aa1aa8015d696f4916bbab The v0.4.2 universal macOS release explicitly contains Apple Silicon and Intel binaries and requires macOS 14+. Upstream reports 768 release regressions with 757 passes and 11 opt-in slow-drive skips; 49/50 bounded VIC programs pass, including 45 exact image comparisons, while Blackmail FLI retains 5,558 differing pixels. The packaged app reached BASIC READY on Apple Silicon; Intel is build-verified only. Broader game/demo and chip-revision compatibility remains open. No tracker-side package run occurred. Evidence: https://github.com/peercom/swift64/releases/tag/v0.4.2 https://github.com/peercom/swift64/commit/112adfa283882a6effacc68a2e3901c0343074d6
