events.title: OMTI: real REQUEST SENSE, FORMAT to end of drive, more opcodes
events.message:
OMTI: real REQUEST SENSE, FORMAT to end of drive, more opcodes

HDNDF.Z80 formats the whole drive with one FORMAT (0x04) at 0/0/0 and
reads 4 sense bytes after an error. We wrote a single sector for 0x04
and returned no sense data.

- REQUEST SENSE returns the error code (bit 7 = address valid) and the
  address of the failed command. Codes are those of the S1410A manual.
- FORMAT (0x04) writes the pattern from the addressed sector to the end
  of the disk, FORMAT TRACK / BAD TRACK (0x06, 0x07) over one track,
  both bounded to the drive so the image cannot grow.
- Answer 0x05, 0x09, 0x10 and the diagnostics 0xe0, 0xe3, 0xe4, which
  used to fail as unknown commands.
- The sector buffer now survives the end of a command, so READ SECTOR
  BUFFER returns what was loaded. READ zero-fills before reading, so
  short reads are unchanged.

Sense data is not part of the save file.
events.author: Egbert-Azure

events.title: grm-w9ev.5: time out hung headless runs, killing only this run's processes
events.message:
grm-w9ev.5: time out hung headless runs, killing only this run's processes

Every analyzeHeadless invocation, batched or single, now runs under
run_headless_timed. The limit is GRM_HEADLESS_TIMEOUT_BASE (120s) plus
GRM_HEADLESS_TIMEOUT_PER_PROGRAM (10s) per program, about 20x the largest
batch. GRM_HEADLESS_TIMEOUT=S sets a flat limit and 0 turns it off. A
timed-out batch falls back to single runs, and a timed-out single run FAILs
that fixture while the gate continues. The banner prints the setting.

The kill: lib/kill-headless.ps1 matches only java.exe/cmd.exe whose command
line contains the run's own project dir. That dir is under the per-run
mktemp WORK, so it matches nothing else. Each match is killed by PID with no
tree walk; the script never matches itself and refuses a short needle.
An earlier draft used 'taskkill /T' on the child's winpid. /T selects
children by stale ParentProcessId, which can reach unrelated processes, and
that draft is suspected of killing the agent session that ran it.
GRM_HEADLESS_KILL_DRYRUN=1 prints the would-be kills.

Verified with a temporary 90s sleep in banktest2 and a 30s limit. The dry run
listed only that run's cmd.exe+java.exe. The real kill removed exactly those
PIDs (20364/2668, then 15428/14932), and two unrelated JVMs and the agent
session survived. The batch fell back, banktest2 timed out alone and FAILed,
and the other three matched their goldens, in 84s. Full gate at defaults:
SUITE OK in 182s with 0 TIMEOUT and 0 fallbacks. Per-fixture results are
identical to the previous size-30 run (79 fixtures, 840 CRITERION).
docs/testing.md now says the log splits on the IMPORTING line, not FIXTURE.

events.title: Smooth display off in games that play MSX-Music (FmUsed)
events.message:
Smooth display off in games that play MSX-Music (FmUsed)

With smooth display a late frame costs a whole Amiga frame (the commit
lands at the next VBlank and DbPre waits for it), and games whose music
driver runs on the MSX VBlank slowed audibly on PiStorm (Lilly's Saga,
Bombaman; confirmed: perfect with smooth display off). The first OPLL data
write (port 7Dh) sets FmUsed until Power ON/Reset; DbPre then stops the
double buffer and SprWaitSw no longer waits. Games without FM keep it.

events.title: Βήμα 135: ο έμπορος δέχεται και πουλά νομίσματα — δέκα ανά πάτημα, αμέσως, όπως στο Planetbase
events.message:
Βήμα 135: ο έμπορος δέχεται και πουλά νομίσματα — δέκα ανά πάτημα, αμέσως, όπως στο Planetbase

Το βήμα 134 έδωσε στην αποικία νομίσματα χωρίς να έχει πού να τα ξοδέψει. Ο
παίκτης διάλεξε: ο έμπορος τα δέχεται ΚΑΙ τα πουλά (αξία 1, με το κέρδος του,
όπως στο Planetbase), δέκα ανά πάτημα, και αμέσως μετά τα δικά του αγαθά στη
σειρά των βελών.

- Το απόθεμα 0 (νερό, δεν ανταλλάσσεται) ήταν άδειο στο TR_NET, tr_value,
  tr_lot: εκεί τα νομίσματα, σε δεκάδες (αξία 10, μία ανά πάτημα). Η δεκάδα
  του εμπόρου 14-17 ανάλογα με το κέρδος του.
- src/ship.asm: τα bits 6-7 του πρώτου byte του φορτίου (ελεύθερα) δίνουν 0,
  50, 100 ή 150 νομίσματα· EC_MCOIN = EC_X + 11 (τράπεζα 6, στο σώσιμο). Η
  ακολουθία των συμβάντων ίδια.
- src/lines.asm: «<COINS  > SHIP 150 GIVE 120 HAVE 123», χωρίς «@ αξία». ΠΑΝΩ
  ως όσα φέρνει και ως 999, ΚΑΤΩ ως όσα έχεις και ως 990. Στη συμφωνία
  αλλάζουν χέρια αμέσως, χωρίς φορτία. Διαβάζονται μία φορά στο tr_open: όσο
  είναι εδώ ο έμπορος άλλο πλοίο δεν πληρώνει. (Η πρώτη εκδοχή τα διάβαζε σε
  κάθε πλήκτρο μέσα στη σχεδίαση, και το asc_b1 έβγαζε την τράπεζα 7 των
  ονομάτων: το C του COINS ερχόταν από την 1.)
- tr_sum σε έναν βρόχο στα 14 αποθέματα: το πάρσιμο περνούσε τις θέσεις του
  φορτίου, και μια κενή θέση (απόθεμα 0) θα μετρούσε τα νομίσματα ξανά. Ίδιο
  ζύγι, κοντύτερος κώδικας. Το tr_deal μηδενίζει το net των νομισμάτων πριν
  γράψει τις ποσότητες του φορτίου, για τον ίδιο λόγο.
- tools/econ.py: η ίδια προσγείωση και συμφωνία· COIN_MAX και MER_COIN στο
  src/const.asm. «COINS» στο t_f_names (τράπεζα 7, 8 bytes).
- Κόστος: προσγείωση εμπόρου 1.252 -> 1.265 us, η γραμμή ίδια (838 / 4.499).
  Τράπεζα 0 128 bytes (458 -> 340, 148 κάτω από το #3E00· η πρώτη εκδοχή
  201), b6code 12 (233 -> 221).
- Η εκκίνηση από το μενού 370 -> 400 frames, όχι από πιο αργό κώδικα: ο
  κώδικας στο &0100 πέρασε από 30 σε 31 τομείς (παράδοση στο frame 365 από
  361), η στιγμή του τυχαίου μετακινήθηκε, και το test_disc πήρε άλλον κόσμο.
  Η γεννήτρια στον πλανήτη 3: seed 294A 259 frames, FE35 (βήμα 134) 227. Το
  134 γεμισμένο στο ίδιο μέγεθος πήρε το 0122, 220 frames, και ξεκίνησε σε
  360. Ταβάνι 450.
- Τα άλλα κόστη ίδια· test_oibuild 6-8 us φθηνότερο, από τη διάταξη.
- Τεστ: test_trade νέα σκηνή ΝΟΜΙΣΜΑΤΑ (το 999, νομίσματα για αγαθά, αγαθά
  για νομίσματα με κενή τέταρτη θέση), ο περίπατος της γραμμής και από τα
  νομίσματα (342 πλήκτρα), 4 νέα αρνητικά, 3 μετακινημένα· test_sim τρεις
  προσγειώσεις (0, 50, 150) και ένα αρνητικό· test_carry ένα ΔΕΞΙΑ ακόμη.
- DESIGN.md: νέα υποενότητα στο §6.11, ο πίνακας και το «δεν ανταλλάσσονται»
  του βήματος 93, §4.2, §10.1, §13, §15 — και διόρθωση: το βήμα 134 έγραψε 63
  και 280 bytes για τον κώδικα της τράπεζας 2 και το b6code, ενώ άφησε 29 και
  233.

events.title: disasm: follow a pointer walk out of the image into the project's other files (#83)
events.message:
disasm: follow a pointer walk out of the image into the project's other files (#83)

A pair handed to a routine that is resident in ANOTHER file of the project is a pointer or not
by what that routine does with it. disasm now writes a catalog of the project's other PRGs that
have analysed code (code segments and `jmp` jump tables; src/project-knowledge/callee-catalog.ts)
and the renderer (--callee-catalog) walks into the file whose code covers a jsr/jmp target, its
instructions decoded on demand, with the same rules: stops at a store to either cell, rts
returns, (low),y / (low,x) / jmp ($00low) is a pointer, KERNAL ROM calls are stepped over.
Files resident at the same address must agree; if they do not, the bytes stay literal and the
zp-pair comment says "callee $XXXX ambiguous: N residents". No catalog / no file with code there
is unknown flow: literal. The label still has to exist in this listing.

The walk is now recursive with per-path state so real engines are readable: a routine that
borrows the caller's cells and puts them back (lda cell/pha ... pla/sta cell, or parked in the
operand of a later lda #imm) no longer ends the path, and a call below the two-level bound is
stepped over when everything it can reach is shown to leave both cells alone.

Real projects (93 listings, 6 projects): the 7 pairs handed to a loader/printer in another image
(Neuromancer chunk_4300 x5, disk 04, LN1 lut00) keep their label halves; the LN1 lut01 pair built
across a call stays literal; byte-identical rebuild 93/93.

e2e:zp-pointer-halves: k-q added (callee in another file, plain reads, ambiguous residents,
agreeing residents, save/restore, nested transparent calls, patch-operand save).

events.message:
fix(filesys): apply the .uaem metadata toggle while emulation runs (#2444)

The "Create .uaem metadata files" checkbox only changed changed_prefs. Nothing copied filesys_custom_uaefsdb into currprefs on resume or reset, so the running emulation kept writing .uaem sidecars until it was restarted, and reopening the GUI showed the box ticked again.

Copy the flag in check_prefs_changed_gfx, next to filesys_limit. Every sidecar read and write checks it per call, so changing it live is safe.

"Disable UAEFSDB" changes filename translation for mounted volumes, so it is not applied live. Its checkbox is now disabled while emulation is running.

events.title: disasm: a label half needs a dereference of THIS setup's pointer, not of the cell somewhere (#83)
events.message:
disasm: a label half needs a dereference of THIS setup's pointer, not of the cell somewhere (#83)

applyZpPointerSetupOverrides accepted a constant pair when its low zero-page cell was
dereferenced anywhere in the listing. In an engine with a shared pointer pool
((ptr_a),y 82 times) every pair passed, including rectangle coordinates handed to a
routine that reads the cells as plain operands.

The rule is now flow: zpPointerDereferencedAfter walks from the setup stores - fall-through,
both branch arms, jmp abs, jsr callees two levels deep (rts returns), and, when the setup
routine itself returns, behind its callers - and stops a path at a store to either cell.
Only a (zp),y / (zp,x) / jmp ($00xx) on the pair's low cell on such a path makes the
immediates label halves. Unknown flow (indirect jump, jsr to an address outside the image
or into undecoded bytes) proves nothing: the bytes stay literal. KERNAL/BASIC ROM calls the
platform names are stepped over.

Also: the two halves of a pair must come from one straight-line setup (no call or branch
between the stores) - the high half of one setup and the low half of the next were paired
across a jsr on a real listing - and the zp-pointer SEMANTICS comment now says zp-pair
("no pointer use reached") when no path dereferences the pair.

e2e:zp-pointer-halves: cases e-j added (shared pool, callee deref, overwrite, cross-setup
pairing, outside-image callee, setup helper whose caller derefs).

events.title: slots: one answer to 'does this file carry a load address' (#82)
events.message:
slots: one answer to 'does this file carry a load address' (#82)

The store never recorded a headed flag, so each reader guessed from kind and the
writers disagreed: register_payloads_from_manifest wrote kind prg + format raw for
a headerless block (rooms, towers, save areas lost 2 bytes each), the disk import
wrote a payload extent two bytes past a PRG's body, and a PRG-typed record file
with no load address was registered as a headed PRG by its extension.

artifact-header.ts is the one helper (kind + format). S12, the byte door's
registered-kind, the machine report and the payload workflow use it. Writers say
it unambiguously now: manifest and register_payload write kind raw for headerless
sources; the disk import registers the file by the extractor's own format and its
extent is the body. project_inventory_sync re-labels old prg+raw payload sources
once and re-imports manifests (which repairs old extents).

e2e-payload-body-size now registers through the real writers over stdio
(register_payloads_from_manifest, register_payload, inventory sync) plus the disk
manifest import, with a contract scope; denominators asserted to the byte.

events.title: wasabid 0.8b1: encryption is optional
events.message:
wasabid 0.8b1: encryption is optional

Not everyone has AmiSSL. The daemon reads each connection's first byte:
TLS when asked for, plain from this machine, when TLS cannot be had
here (said at startup and in discovery), or when started with 'plain';
otherwise an ERR saying encryption is required. The client encrypts
whenever it has keys, goes plain with a warning to an Amiga without
TLS - but never to an address it once reached encrypted (tls-hosts,
like SSH's known hosts; `wasabi keys forget HOST`). --plain is allowed
for any command. 252 tests pass.

events.title: ISSUE-77 recorded (ttcompatopen's uninitialised state), and the bootinfo size skew noted
events.message:
ISSUE-77 recorded (ttcompatopen's uninitialised state), and the bootinfo size skew noted

The driver line found and measured a rare boot-time ttcompat panic. The
mechanism is checked here: the 3B2-shaped ttcompatopen clears only
bytes 4..31 of its 0x44-byte state, while ttcompat_ioctl_ack trusts
t_state, t_iocid and t_ioccmd at 56..64. Later USL trees bzero the
state. The fix is to arrive from them as an opt-in pass.

boot-path-map: the loader's struct bootinfo is 0x778 bytes and config
copies 0x76c, so kernel +0x66c holds the loader's data fields and
reserved[] lines up at +0x678 on both sides.

events.title: rename: the Lisp-level names follow -- AMILISP package, AMILISP_* env, AMILISP port
events.message:
rename: the Lisp-level names follow -- AMILISP package, AMILISP_* env, AMILISP port

The second half of the AmiLisp rename: what a Lisp program sees.  The
implementation package is AMILISP (amilisp::...), its reference
docs/amilisp.md; the environment variables are AMILISP_* (AMILISP_HOME,
AMILISP_GC_STRESS, AMILISP_FASL_CACHE_DIR, ...); the default ARexx port
is AMILISP; the FASL cache lives under S:amilisp/faslcache/ on AmigaOS and
~/.cache/common-lisp/amilisp-<version>-fasl<n>/ on the host; the
Quicklisp helper package is amilisp-ql.  The bundled boot.fasl/clos.fasl
are regenerated (the package name is inside them).

The old names stay as aliases so existing code and environments keep
working, never as the primary spelling: CLAMIGA is a nickname of the
AMILISP package (clamiga::x reads as the same symbol); *features* has
:amilisp and :amicl next to :clamiga and :cl-amiga (the library forks
say #+clamiga); platform_getenv (string_utils.c, now the one lookup
every env read goes through) reads an unset or empty AMILISP_X under its
old CLAMIGA_X name; the REPL prompt's package-less fallback says AMILISP.

tests/test_reader.c pins the nickname and the four features,
tests/test_userinit.sh the env-var fallback, the Amiga suite both;
CLAUDE.md's Naming section and the README's name paragraph say which
spelling is current and which is the alias.

Clamacs follows in its own commit (pin bumped): amilisp:: references,
AMILISP_* variables, the AMILISP port first in its port list, and
*amilisp-heap* / *amilisp-options* with the *clamiga-* names kept as
symbol macros.

events.title: Default CD32 yellow to cancel and add ToolType and CLI overrides
events.message:
Default CD32 yellow to cancel and add ToolType and CLI overrides

Change the built-in CD32 pad default so the yellow button is CANCEL
instead of NONE. CANCEL is the ESC key: in the shop it returns to the
hangar, in the hangar it acts as the physical ESC key and in game it
opens the "Abort Mission ?" confirmation. The other defaults are
unchanged: red = FIRE, blue = SPECIAL_SELECT, green = MEGA_BOMB,
reverse / forward = NONE, play = PAUSE, and cd32 still defaults to OFF.
New amiga.cfg files and the one-time volumes-only migration therefore
write "cd32_yellow = CANCEL".

Explicit per-user values are preserved: an existing amiga.cfg without a
cd32_yellow key gets the new CANCEL default, an explicit
"cd32_yellow = NONE" still leaves the button disabled, and no existing
NONE is migrated to CANCEL automatically. The yellow button is not
hardcoded to ESC - the action mapping (FIRE / SPECIAL_SELECT / MEGA_BOMB
/ PAUSE / CANCEL / NONE), the working pause, BUY/SELL, the shop filters
and the held-button blocking are unchanged.

Add a CD32=ON|OFF startup parameter:
- icon ToolType CD32=ON / CD32=OFF and CLI -cd32=ON|OFF or CD32=ON|OFF;
- recognized case-insensitively; tooltypes in parentheses (e.g.
  (CD32=ON)) stay inactive through the existing FindToolType mechanism;
- implemented with the existing CLI parsing and
  RAP_ParseWorkbenchToolTypes (icon.library / FindToolType).

Precedence (the parameter is parsed before AmigaCfg_Load, so it is kept
as a separate tri-state session override, not as the persisted value):
- a valid startup setting wins over the cd32 value in amiga.cfg;
- without one the amiga.cfg value (and its OFF default) applies;
- CD32=OFF selects the shared 1/2/3-button joystick handling, it does not
  disable the joystick; a final disabled joystick state still blocks
  lowlevel.library, the gameport configuration and the potgo button-3
  line, and CD32=ON can never re-enable input disabled that way;
- an invalid value is ignored: it never clears an earlier valid selection
  and never enables the pad by accident;
- the GAMECTLR -> JOYSTK fallback is unchanged.

The override is never persisted: it is resolved after the cfg load and
before the gameport is configured, and Load/Save/create only ever write
the stored amiga_cfg_cd32 value. AmigaCfg_Load() is now called
unconditionally, also with NOJOY / JOYSTICK=OFF, because the file also
holds the audio volumes and runs the one-time migration; only the
library/port/potgo setup stays gated behind the disabled-joystick state.
A single startup log line reports the source of the mode, the effective
value and the resulting port mode (no per-frame logging).

Documentation: README.md, README_AMIGA.md, README_AMIGA_PL.md,
CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased], docs/amiga.cfg.example, docs/porting-analysis.md,
raptor.readme and the source comments / cfg generator were updated to
describe YELLOW=CANCEL as the default, the shop -> hangar / hangar -> ESC
/ in-game "Abort Mission ?" behaviour, PLAY=PAUSE, the ToolType/CLI
override and its precedence and non-persistence, and that an old
amiga.cfg with an explicit cd32_yellow = NONE must be changed to CANCEL
(or the line removed) to use the new default. The obsolete claim that
CANCEL has no default assignment was removed. There is no versioned icon
(.info) or icon generator in the repository; the docs therefore only
describe the CD32=ON ToolType to enter in the existing icon.

Tests: the amiga.cfg host test (bash tests/run_amiga_cfg_test.sh, which
exercises the real production AmigaCfg_Load/Save/ResolveCd32/
SetCd32Override code, not a copy of the implementation) was extended and
passes: a missing cd32_yellow key defaults to CANCEL, an explicit NONE is
kept, custom assignments and Options saves are preserved, the
volumes-only migration creates CANCEL, override ON with cfg OFF and
override OFF with cfg ON both resolve correctly, no override / invalid
values keep the previous selection, the override is not persisted by
Load/Save/create, and a disabled joystick stays disabled in the port
setup. The Workbench ToolType path and the lowlevel/potgo port
configuration are analysed and built but not exercised by the host test.

Builds (all successful, before this commit):
- bash build_amiga.sh            -> raptor          (68060 + FPU)
- bash build_amiga_nofpu.sh      -> raptor_nofpu    (no FPU instructions)
- bash build_amiga_030.sh        -> raptor_030      (no FPU, no 68040/68060-only instructions)
- bash build_amiga_030_fpu.sh    -> raptor_030_fpu  (68030 + external FPU)
No new compiler warnings are introduced by this change. No real-hardware
or AmigaOS testing was performed for this change.

events.title: disasm: an immediate is a label half only when its pointer is dereferenced (#83)
events.message:
disasm: an immediate is a label half only when its pointer is dereferenced (#83)

The zero-page pointer guess turned two immediates into #<label / #>label whenever
they were stored to adjacent cells and their combined value hit a label, so a
constant that merely equalled a label's low byte became a label half: the
listing rebuilt byte-identical but was no longer relocatable. The pair must
also be dereferenced as (zp),y or (zp,x) somewhere in the listing; a lone half
or an undereferenced pair stays the literal. Annotation overrides still win.
Hermetic e2e (real setup, undereferenced constants, lone half) wired into
package.json and the gate workflow.

events.title: slots: S12 counts a payload's body, not a PRG header on everything (#82)
events.message:
slots: S12 counts a payload's body, not a PRG header on everything (#82)

The denominator subtracted 2 bytes from every file without an address range,
so each raw .bin/extract lost two bytes and read as partly uncovered. Only a
headed PRG gives up its load address; raw and extract count every byte, and a
recorded range still wins. One helper (payloadBodySize) serves both the file
and the stored-in-file payload path. New hermetic e2e with one PRG + two raw
payloads, wired into package.json and the gate workflow.

slots: S11 no longer claims a run settles free RAM (#80)

A canary run proves "not written during that run", never "unused":
read-only data survives it. Free RAM is established by reading the
listing (no reader, no writer); the run is the second witness. Reword
the S11 fills/because, slot_record's method text and refusal, the slot
state detail, the free-zp candidate text and the agent doctrine. Slot
state logic is unchanged.

project.status: v0.10 published; current main adds non-AUTOINIT disk libraries and opt-in UAE/Emu68 guest debug ports
project.notes: Wine-style host runtime for classic AmigaOS m68k command-line tools: interprets guest instructions (optional m68k-crate trace JIT) and reimplements OS library calls in Rust. No Kickstart ROM is needed for normal use. It is generic development/analysis tooling, not a native reconstruction of a specific game; graphics, custom chips, Workbench GUI and games are explicitly out of scope. Linux/macOS build and guest execution are corroborated by current CI logs; published Windows x86-64 binaries compile but Windows/Wine runtime remains unverified. Interpreter/JIT parity covers six fixtures; comparison with vamos includes three documented known divergences, so it is not universal compatibility proof. The math-library shims now return comparison/test results in both D0 and 68k condition codes, matching the documented ROM calling behavior needed by SAS/C's scmieee.lib; before the fix, SAS/C double comparisons appeared equal and exp() overflow checks returned HUGE_VAL. Evidence: https://github.com/sidick/volamos/commit/de321627fd5f1c16ca6cc76020222d7f3c18d564 exec.library SetFunction now installs executable guest JMP entries, returns a synthesized callable stub for the previous host-backed handler, supports hook chaining and restoration, and is covered by an end-to-end guest test. The patch is deliberately limited to one guest invocation and does not emulate AmigaOS-wide persistent hooks. Evidence: https://github.com/sidick/volamos/commit/018fd8f047d27fa3f85948b1595f44acf3f6f596 v0.10 incorporates non-AUTOINIT disk-library loading and the MakeLibrary/AddLibrary/InitStruct/MakeFunctions exec paths. Current main also adds opt-in CLI handling for UAE's formatted debug port at $BFFF00 and Emu68's byte debug port at $DEADBEEF, routing guest diagnostics to stderr without claiming broader GUI/custom-chip emulation. Evidence: https://github.com/sidick/volamos/releases/tag/v0.10 https://github.com/sidick/volamos/commit/2ee28f5f2759a9ea5096ba7f0068c4ec4cf94011 https://github.com/sidick/volamos/commit/359f762476c061b3b487cdcaf1dc86acdc786dd9 https://github.com/sidick/volamos/commit/fcec136d6f7f416b89af11d6bb76f6c89c96a8f5

project.title: sdltrs-MultiHDC
project.display_title: sdltrs-MultiHDC — TRS-80 hard-disk archaeology emulator
project.status: active; OMTI/Xebec save-state and media-bound validation hardened
project.notes: TRS-80/TCS Genie IIIs emulator derived from SDL2TRS/xtrs with independently implemented OMTI, WD1000/1010 and Xebec S1410 hard-disk paths. Primary documentation records live Z80-driver disassembly, recovered controller behavior, verified CP/M/GDOS boots and a zbx DAP bridge. Current controller work rejects out-of-range OMTI/Xebec save-state fields before fixed-buffer use, rebuilds the Xebec format pattern locally, rejects invalid OMTI sector sizes and prevents FORMAT commands beyond the last cylinder from extending an HDV image. These are bounded controller correctness/safety changes, not broader boot-compatibility proof. Evidence: https://github.com/Egbert-Azure/sdltrs-MultiHDC/commit/7c3afc7522d5602bbc009d7fa94bc6a6094536b6 https://github.com/Egbert-Azure/sdltrs-MultiHDC/commit/04cb5608ff82ed03c288d1c8eda0904e34a92287 https://github.com/Egbert-Azure/sdltrs-MultiHDC/commit/d2dc33e437d38a0a81cc682c8e730fbc2aac68df

project.status: active; M14.17 completes a deterministic reconstruction pipeline, while the upstream 2.0.0 publication gate remains open
project.notes: General-purpose TypeScript C64 reverse-engineering toolkit controlling stock VICE and integrating disk/BASIC/static-analysis/assembly/equivalence workflows. package.json now declares 2.0.0 and publishable CLI/MCP/host bins, while the primary roadmap explicitly leaves npm trusted-publisher setup, the v2.0.0 tag and verification of the published package open. C64RT_TRACE adds per-process JSONL field traces for host requests, VICE lifecycle, MCP calls, native tool runs and stderr without exposing the trace to the agent. Node.js 24+, VICE 3.9+ and user-supplied ROMs remain prerequisites; no host CPU/RAM minimum or independent execution is established. Evidence: https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/blob/main/package.json https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/11987768d056 https://github.com/henols/c64-re-tools/commit/5ceac29bb61b Current M14 work now generates byte-identical ACME source from an unpacked image or PRG, curated knowledge and Ghidra instructions; an optional loader is run in VICE and checked at the recovered entry state. The documented ten-stage workflow adds explicit acceptance criteria, exit checks, deliverables and coverage reporting. Release comparison can attach first-access/runtime-change evidence to differing bytes, single-release separation reports unpack/access/reachability provenance, and platform symbols can be exported as an ACME include. These are upstream live-tool checks rather than an independent tracker run, and they do not close the separate npm publication gate. project.status: active; firmware plus ffemu host-side UI/UX development emulator
project.notes: Open firmware for Gotek hardware exposes USB disk images as a floppy drive to Amiga and Atari ST hosts. Official documentation lists ADF and ST support. This is drive emulation rather than a title reconstruction; compatibility with protection/extended formats varies and should not be inferred from ordinary ADF/ST support. Firmware is built for explicit ARM Cortex-M3 and Cortex-M4 Gotek-class microcontrollers; these are firmware output CPUs, not properties of the ADF/ST/HFE inputs. The new ffemu subtool compiles FlashFloppy's own UI, display, FatFS and image-handler code for Windows or Linux and runs it against emulated Gotek controls, flash state, USB media and display hardware in a terminal. Current support includes Shugart and Apple II firmware variants, OLED/HD44780/7-segment displays, scripted testing and FF.CFG/FLASH.DMP configuration workflows; the documentation explicitly says floppy-interface data flow is not emulated. Its README explicitly credits Claude assistance. Evidence: https://github.com/keirf/flashfloppy/commit/ef97d8db661c30c6bab4af894f857005d1ea1c32 https://github.com/keirf/flashfloppy/blob/master/ffemu/README.md https://github.com/keirf/flashfloppy/commit/884a6748c51197bc86033b19fd59165b2aa37309

project.title: Copperline
project.display_title: Copperline — Amiga emulator & reverse debugger
project.status: active
project.notes: Cycle-driven Amiga emulator with reverse stepping and source debugging. Native screenshot capture preserves original pixels before presentation effects, and memory-write output follows WinUAE conventions. WASM board plugins can now opt into manifest-scoped persistent-resource writes; upstream tests cover capability denial, bounds, reset/cache coherence and host-file write-through. Current main preserves AGA Alice's hard $D8 bitplane-fetch stop, weaves both chipset fields into full-height native interlaced screenshots and persists menu-only settings without discarding launcher-less keys. A second change adds CYL.SIDE display plus WinUAE/FS-UAE floppy sample-set playback while serializing mechanism events so save states, run-ahead and netplay checksums do not depend on installed host sounds. These are targeted fidelity/tooling improvements rather than universal compatibility proof. Evidence: https://github.com/CopperlineHQ/Copperline/commit/9e8359ea6cce6fc5e5028d1f4e31b960b53f7da6 https://github.com/CopperlineHQ/Copperline/commit/c3220bc325d68f85a5730b50627ef419879b19a2

project.notes: Substantial JetPac-inspired Amiga game in high-level HAS syntax; reviewed gameplay applies joystick thrust/gravity, wrapping, tile collisions and landing state, with m68k asset assembly. Authored JetPac-inspired native Amiga game. jetpac.has supplies high-level HAS gameplay for thrust, gravity, wrapping, collision and landing; Makefile transpiles HAS to m68k assembly and also compiles star.c with VBCC. HAS, assembly and C describe the maintained implementation, not a recovered original JetPac language. Astronaut Jet Pac is a newly authored JetPac-inspired game using HAS. Reviewed material does not identify a particular original executable being reconstructed; source_cpu is not applicable. The Makefile’s CPU setting belongs to emitted Amiga output. Makefile defaults CPU to 68000 and passes it to hasc, VASM and vbccm68k, then VLINK emits Amiga hunk executables. Record m68000 for the default output. A help-string CPU=68020 override is not treated as an independently validated variant. Makefile runs Python hasc.cli from sibling highamigaassembler (Lark dependency), VASM, VLINK, VBCC, external library directory and asset assembly; default CPU=68000. Not a plain standalone assembly build. The default HAS compilation also links separately assembled asset/library objects and VBCC-generated star.c assembly; optional 68020 help text is not build verification. project.title: ASE — Atari ST-family system emulator
project.display_title: ASE — Atari ST-family system emulator
project.status: current source marks v1.13 with hard-drive game-library and joystick-port configuration; Linux remains described as untested
project.notes: Primary README describes a C# Atari ST-family emulator using Moira, partly derived from the author's 1990s emulator and Hatari. Substantial machine implementation and .NET project are present. README supplies Moira wrapper build and dotnet publish commands. Generic system emulation, not a game-specific CPU wrapper. Linux support is described as expected but untested by the author; no local build or compatibility validation. README supplies Moira build and dotnet publish instructions, says ready-to-use releases exist, and reports Windows/macOS execution. True flags reflect upstream evidence, not an independent build. Linux remains untested upstream. No independent compilation, execution or benchmarking was performed during this catalogue review. Evidence: https://github.com/thebitculture/ase/blob/main/README.MD https://github.com/thebitculture/ase/blob/main/ASE/ASE.csproj https://github.com/thebitculture/ase/blob/main/ASE/CPU.cs https://github.com/thebitculture/ase/blob/main/ASE/Memory.cs https://github.com/thebitculture/ase/commit/4a60df85090ad3485c5bd6dec73b26ab8664d42a The v1.13 source commit adds hard-drive-adapted games to the library and configurable Atari joystick ports, separating port state and mouse/joystick button-line behavior in the IKBD path. The repository's previously documented Windows/macOS execution and untested-Linux boundary remain; this pass did not observe or execute a new release asset. Evidence: https://github.com/thebitculture/ase/commit/cac0f6093cdc32fdcd747a325860b7e8c69c6aa4 https://github.com/thebitculture/ase/blob/cac0f6093cdc32fdcd747a325860b7e8c69c6aa4/README.MD

project.title: StarCraft — AmiSC 68K
project.display_title: StarCraft — AmiSC 68K

runtime_profiles.name: Native AmigaOS build
runtime_profiles.notes: README states 68020 minimum with no FPU, AGA or RTG graphics, and enough memory for about 20 MB of sprite graphics plus sound samples. That working-set description is not treated as an exact total-RAM minimum; 68060 is recommended for AGA and a fast 68040 for RTG. v0.8.2 recommends 320x240 on slower machines, and Shell launches require the documented 2 MB stack that the icon already supplies.

evidence.excerpt: AmigaOS 3.0 or later; 68020 minimum, no FPU required; AGA chipset, or a graphics card (RTG / Picasso96).

project.status: alpha; v0.8.2 published with 320x240 original-menu path and campaign fixes
project.notes: Native Amiga 68k StarCraft port that reads the user's original MPQ-derived game data and supports playable skirmishes. The repository currently publishes binaries/documentation but not the port source, so implementation provenance cannot be audited from source. v0.8.2 adds an original-menu path that keeps menus, campaign screens, briefings and the in-game menu at 320x240, with one-time smoothed conversion to menu-lores.pack, plus bounded Terran mission/UI fixes. The README says the icon supplies a 2 MB stack and recommends 320x240 on slower machines; these details refine usage guidance without turning the approximate graphics/sample working set into an exact RAM minimum. The repository still publishes binaries/documentation rather than auditable port source. Evidence: https://github.com/angree/AmiSC/releases/tag/v0.8.2 https://github.com/angree/AmiSC/commit/1fdee2e0aa306af94d56473117fd1a144dda6355 https://github.com/angree/AmiSC/blob/1fdee2e0aa306af94d56473117fd1a144dda6355/README.md

events.message:
Βήμα 133: διπλό βιοπλαστικό και 137 στο φορτίο — το εργοστάσιο πλαστικού χτίζεται σε κάθε κόσμο

Το τρίτο εύρημα του βήματος 131: τα 107 βιοπλαστικά της αρχής πήγαιναν σε
θόλους και διαδρόμους, και το εργοστάσιο που θα έφτιαχνε κι άλλα δεν
χτιζόταν ποτέ. Ο παίκτης διάλεξε και τους δύο μοχλούς.

- tools/econ.py: το mach_bioplastic κάνει 2 βιοπλαστικά από 2 άμυλα (ως
  τώρα 1), όπως το μέταλλο στο 125. Οχι MF_ADDS: δουλεύει και με γεμάτη
  αποθήκη. Κανένα byte κώδικα, κανένα us.
- src/newgame.asm: 137 βιοπλαστικά στο φορτίο (107). Οχι περισσότερα:
  χωρίς το νερό το φορτίο είναι 498 και το αμπάρι χωρά 500 — από 140 το
  παιχνίδι θα ξεκινούσε με STORAGE FULL. Το test_newgame το ελέγχει πια.
- tools/play.py: ο παίκτης-σενάριο εξόπλιζε μηχανές μόνο με 4
  βιοπλαστικά, ενώ μια μηχανή κοστίζει 2· το εργοστάσιο έμενε άδειο.

  Κάθε αποικία παίρνει πια το πρώτο πλοίο αποίκων και σταματά στους δέκα:

events.title: SCSI ticked only when it has work; docs for --idle-count, ND-5000 status and verification
events.message:
SCSI ticked only when it has work; docs for --idle-count, ND-5000 status and verification

- device_scsi.c: the controller is no longer ticked after every instruction.
  It is ticked while the chip or a disc has a timer running, or while it is
  Active and the chip has raised an interrupt or a DMA data request. Every
  IOX and every reset requests a tick. The --trace output of a SCSI boot
  (60 million instructions) and of an SMD boot with SCSI configured (100
  million) is identical before and after. 300 million instructions, SMD boot:
  25.1 s -> 22.3 s. SINTRAN leaves the Active bit set while the bus is idle,
  so Active alone is not work.
- --idle-count / [runtime] idle_count in the option list, the config design
  document and the two sample INI files.
- ND5000-X4-PLAN.md: 12-OCT progress entry, open question 2 answered.
- VERIFICATION.md: the four-users-at-once ND-5000 test and the trace
  comparison for device tick changes.

events.message:
Βήμα 132: πλατό 8 και ανάμειξη ως το 16 σε κάθε πλανήτη — ο πάγος έχει χώρο γύρω από το σκάφος

Ο παίκτης-σενάριο του βήματος 131 βρήκε αποικίες στον πάγο που δεν χωρούσαν
τέταρτο θόλο και πέθαιναν από πείνα. Ο παίκτης διάλεξε πλατό 8 και ανάμειξη
ως το 16 (ως τώρα 5 και 10) για όλους τους πλανήτες.

- tools/worldgen_ref.py: R_PLATEAU 8, R_BLEND 16, GEN_VERSION 3. Ο Z80
  διαβάζει τις ίδιες σταθερές από το tools/mkgentables.py (πίνακας βαρών 9
  bytes αντί για 6)· στο src/worldgen.asm άλλαξαν μόνο τρία σχόλια. Byte
  προς byte ίδιος με την αναφορά, 268 frames αντί για 265 (5,35 s).
- Θέσεις 4x4 δεμένες με το σκάφος, 48 κόσμοι ανά πλανήτη (ελάχ./διάμεσος):
  πάγος 6/14 -> 20/28, έρημος 20/30 -> 40/50, θύελλα 12/25 -> 26/44,
  φεγγάρι 30/52 -> 45/66. Κανένας κόσμος κάτω από 12 (ως τώρα 15 στους 48
  του πάγου).
- Οι φλέβες: η ανάμειξη απλώνει τις πλαγιές, και ο βράχος γύρω από την
  κορυφογραμμή πλαταίνει. Η κοντινότερη θέση σε φλέβα: η έρημος κερδίζει,
  θύελλα και φεγγάρι χάνουν λίγο (κανένα ως το 30: 8 -> 12 και 5 -> 9 στα
  48). Από το βήμα 123 το ορυχείο δουλεύει και αλλού, με μισή απόδοση.
- Ο κώδικας του παιχνιδιού δεν άλλαξε ούτε byte· άλλαξαν 400 tiles του
  κόσμου κοντά στην αποικία, και μαζί έξι σκηνές δοκιμών:
  το colony.sna στρώνει τη δική του φλέβα (στήλη βράχου x = -13 δίπλα στην
  κορυφογραμμή, COLONY_VEIN στο tools/balance.py)· το test_meteor ψάχνει
  σπόρο με πτώση δίπλα σε tile μισού πλάτους· το test_install ζητά τον
  δεύτερο θόλο νοτιοδυτικά και ελέγχει ότι τελειώνει με το πρώτο στήσιμο·

events.title: manxmail: writing mail - new, reply, reply to all, forward - and sending it
events.message:
manxmail: writing mail - new, reply, reply to all, forward - and sending it

A message is written in $EDITOR as headers and plain text (a reply quotes
what it answers, laid out at 72 columns from the page engine, and
carries In-Reply-To and References), shown before it goes, then sent
over SMTP: mail/smtp.c, TLS from the start (465), AUTH PLAIN or LOGIN,
dot-stuffed. mail/compose.c puts it together: names and subjects outside
ASCII as RFC 2047 words, the text quoted-printable unless it is 7-bit,
long headers folded. What isn't sent stays in ~/.manx/draft and is
offered next time; a reply marks its message \Answered; mail_sent files
a copy by IMAP APPEND for servers that don't (Gmail does).

Decoded header words have their control characters blanked, so a
subject can't carry a line break into a reply's headers. The fuzzer now
runs SMTP replies, typed addresses and texts too, and checks every built
message for headers it didn't mean, bare CR or LF and long lines (it
found a lone CR going out bare in 7-bit text).

Keys: c changes folder and g gets new mail (were g and r); m, r, a, f.

events.title: manxmail: mail over IMAP on a terminal, each message through the page engine
events.message:
manxmail: mail over IMAP on a terminal, each message through the page engine

A program of its own, so the browser stays small. mail/imap.c is an
IMAP4rev1 client (TLS, validated before anything is sent; plain only to
this machine), AUTHENTICATE PLAIN or LOGIN, responses parsed into values
with literals; mail/mime.c does base64, quoted-printable, RFC 2047
headers, modified UTF-7 folder names and BODYSTRUCTURE's parts.

The list is newest first, fifty at a time; a message's HTML or plain
text goes through the HTML engine and layout (plain text with its URLs
as links), nothing it links to fetched. Links open in manx, attachments
save, folders from LIST. A connection the server dropped is made again
and the command tried once more. OAuth2-only servers (Outlook) are named
as such.

tests/mailserver.py is a fake IMAP server; tests/fuzz_mail.c runs a
server's mutated transcripts through it all under ASan/UBSan (in make
check).

events.title: Keep a reset requested at the debugger's restart stop
events.message:
Keep a reset requested at the debugger's restart stop

After a reset, m68k_go() enters the debugger before it clears
SPCFLAG_MODE_CHANGE and runs the CPU. A reset requested from that stop,
such as a second remote checkpoint restore, sets quit_program; the next
hsync raises MODE_CHANGE for it before m68k_go() clears the flag. The CPU
then runs with the reset pending and never returns to process it.

Keep MODE_CHANGE while a reset is already pending, so that m68k_run()
returns for it.

events.title: daemon: a closed stderr no longer aborts the process
events.message:
daemon: a closed stderr no longer aborts the process

eprintln! panics when the write fails. With stderr a pipe whose reader
has gone (EPIPE), the first log line panicked, the panic hook logged
the same way and panicked again, and the process aborted (SIGABRT),
losing any unflushed trace. A launcher that dies takes the daemon down.

trx64_core::elog! writes the line and drops the error. The daemon, the
core, the session and the indexer thread use it (or the same pattern)
wherever they log at run time. Test: tests/stderr_closed.rs starts the
real binary with its stderr reader closed, makes it log, and checks it
is still running (fails without the fix).

events.title: rename: the product and the executable are AmiLisp / amilisp
events.message:
rename: the product and the executable are AmiLisp / amilisp

CL-Amiga, said out loud "Clamiga", becomes AmiLisp wherever a person
reads or types the name: the binary (build/host/amilisp,
build/cross/amilisp, build/morphos/amilisp, release bin/*/amilisp), the
bare-boot heap image amilisp.img, the install layout <prefix>/lib/amilisp/,
the user init file ~/.amilisprc / S:.amilisprc, the banner, $VER cookie
and LISP-IMPLEMENTATION-TYPE, the Workbench icons (AmiLisp, AmiLisp-FPU,
AmiLisp-MOS, amilisp.guide), the FS-UAE volume AmiLisp:, the manual
amilisp.guide, include/amilisp.h, the examples and tools, the GitHub URL
(github.com/mdbergmann/amilisp), and the prose of README, docs and specs.
The Aminet package keeps its name (dev/lang/clamiga.lha), so the next
upload is still an update of the existing entry.

The Lisp-level identifiers deliberately keep the old name, because user
code and the library forks depend on them: the CLAMIGA package, the
:clamiga / :cl-amiga features, the CLAMIGA_* environment variables, the
ARexx port name, the S:cl-amiga/faslcache/ root, docs/clamiga.md.
*features* gains :amilisp and :amicl next to those two.

The pre-rename file names stay accepted, so an existing installation
keeps working after swapping the binary: image discovery tries
amilisp.img then clamiga.img at every location, the init file
.amilisprc then .clamigarc (then S:clamiga.lisp), the library search
../lib/amilisp/ then ../lib/clamiga/.  CLAUDE.md records the naming
policy; tests/test_image.sh, test_userinit.sh, test_lib_search_cwd.sh,
test_userinit_paths.c and test_reader.c pin the fallbacks and the
feature set.

The Clamacs pin moves to its own rename commit (8e9b57d6), which starts
amilisp (probing PROGDIR:amilisp, then PROGDIR:clamiga).

events.title: spec 907: read-set buckets per (half-track, sector) credited to the block the head is in
events.message:
spec 907: read-set buckets per (half-track, sector) credited to the block the head is in

The old lane asked sector_under_head, which scans FORWARD to the next header, and
credited the bytes to the sector being left, so every read landed on the wrong
sector. Rotation now caches the block list of the current half-track (invalidated
by a generation counter on write, attach, detach and snapshot restore) and answers
which header the head last passed and whether it is in that sector's data part.
Buckets split header and data bytes, carry the C64 clock, survive re-arming and
are flushed on disarm.

cdb/dcb index, lun and phase from the save file unchecked and then used
them against fixed-size buffers. Reject out-of-range values and reset
the controller instead.

Xebec's fillbuf was a constant that nothing loaded; build the default
pattern in xebec_format(). The save file layout is unchanged.

OMTI keeps fillbuf (the pattern survives a READ, unlike the real
single-buffer controller); document that at the declaration and in
omti.md.

README: note on keeping one file per controller.

events.title: tpoff: tpsig run from the T425's own memory, so any desktop can have it
events.message:
tpoff: tpsig run from the T425's own memory, so any desktop can have it

On the ATW800/2 the T425's memory from 0x80000000 is the card's past
2 MB, which a desktop at 32 bits a pixel shows: tpsig's code and stack
landed on the screen and X's drawing on tpsig, so xmanx left the T425
alone there (and the first visits lost its ~2x on certificate checks).

tp/tpreloc.py assembles a 51-byte first stage, booted ahead of tpsig.btl
as it is: it reads the bootable's own first stage from the link to
0x80200070, sets the workspace and registers as a boot from a link would,
and jumps there. The INMOS bootstrap and C runtime place themselves with
ldpi (no ldmemstartval anywhere), so the rest loads next to it; the
runtime's memory top is MostNeg + IBOARDSIZE, now answered #300000.
tpsig thus lives in 0x80200070-0x80300000, which only the T425 sees, and
that is what is wiped after.

On Hatari's T425 core with the ATW800/2's own hello.btl (same toolset):
relocated, 0 bytes written in 0x80001000-0x801fffff (23636 above);
as built, 19674 bytes there. Not yet run on the real card (the TT is
off the network): if the boot or the ping fails, tpoff falls back to
the 68030 as before.

xmanx's _ATW_FRAMEBUFFER check (tpoff_forbid) goes: nothing of tpsig's
is in the card's shown memory any more.

events.title: pictures: srcset, <picture> and data-src - the smallest that will do
events.message: pictures: srcset, and data-src - the smallest that will do Manx fetched an 's src, which on today's sites is often the largest version (or, on lazy-loading pages, a 1x1 stand-in). On the 68030 a picture costs seconds a megapixel to decode. Now: - srcset (and data-srcset): the smallest candidate at least as wide as it's shown (the pane, or width=), else the widest; with densities, the lowest; never WebP or AVIF (doc_srcset_pick, the HTML spec's parsing). The choice is made as the page is read and only it is kept (whole lists took 165 KB of a big page's 1.2 MB); where no pictures are shown (a terminal, uparse: doc.img_w 0) srcset and data-src aren't kept at all, so the text layouts are unchanged. - : the first whose type= this can show and whose media= holds (css_media_matches, the sheets' media query reader). - data-src where src is a stand-in (a short data: URL, blank/spacer/ pixel/transparent/placeholder files). Tests: srcset choices (test_html); fuzz_html reads half its pages with pictures shown. On a test page xmanx fetched s640.png of 320/640/1280w, the 's wide.png past a WebP and a narrow-only source, and a lazy page's data-src - nothing else. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5

events.title: xmanx: grid cells as their own boxes - bands, backgrounds, borders; <font color>
events.message:
xmanx: grid cells as their own boxes - bands, backgrounds, borders; <font color>

In fonts a grid's rows were lines shared by all its cells: a tall picture
in one cell made that line tall in every column, opening gaps in the
rest (atari.org's sidebars and news beside its pictures). Now, with
metrics, a grid goes out as bands (layout.c compose_bands): each cell's
lines keep their own heights, one under the other; a band runs from
where some cell's line starts to where the next one does; each cell's
line goes in the band it starts in at its own baseline (lspan.asc) and
reaches down into the bands below where it is taller (lheight.over,
page.max_over). Rows are as tall as their tallest cell, the others'
text at the top, middle (as browsers, unless valign= says) or bottom;
cellspacing/cellpadding (browsers' 2 and 1) between and around.

Backgrounds and borders are boxes under the text (page.boxes): the
table's bgcolor/border/bordercolor, the cells' bgcolor or style=
background, a row's bgcolor for its cells; a table inside a cell brings
its boxes along. A one-column table with such a look is a grid too (its
box drawn). Text on a dark box keeps its colour as given (SA_ONDARK ->
CA_ONDARK: not darkened for white). <font color=> sets the text colour,
under the sheet's. css_attr_color reads HTML colour attributes.

Drawing (manx.c): boxes first (scr_rect, new; a no-op on a terminal),
then lines above the view whose tall content reaches into it, then the
view; each span at its own baseline; a click finds a link reaching down
from a band above (layout_tops: the lines' tops, worked out once).
xscreen keeps boxes like images: painted first in each band, diffed
each against each, moved with a scroll.

The terminal's layout is unchanged (108 corpus layouts identical).
Tests: bands beside a tall picture, valign middle, boxes and SA_ONDARK;
fuzz_html checks images against their own baselines and boxes' bounds
(make check, and 3 x 15000 iterations, clean).

events.title: wasabid 0.6b1: TLS on every network connection
events.message:
wasabid 0.6b1: TLS on every network connection

- tls.c (from AmiClaude's AmiSSL 5 recipe): TLS 1.3 server, client
  certificates required, both signed by the user's own Wasabi CA;
  ChaCha20 and X25519 preferred; dates not checked.
- No plain fallback. Loopback (FS-UAE, SSH tunnels) may skip TLS, told
  apart by the first byte; WASABI_TLS=always encrypts there too.
- If TLS cannot start the daemon keeps running, refuses network
  clients, says why in its discovery answer and retries every 30 s.
- wasabi keys init|amiga|drive|show (Ed25519, via openssl); --plain
  only to update a pre-0.6 daemon; the update probe is TLS whenever a
  network is in between.
- NAS deploy copies the client half of the keys.
- Mock speaks TLS; 246 tests pass.

Level 9 sentries on the full engine; level 8 ships; seam-edge glyphs

A checkpoint of everything since a7797f3.

Level 9 (WIP; WIP=1 compiles it in, LAB=1 builds it alone to build/lab9.d64):

  the third range of the shared variant list (SV_V0) after the angel's, and entities

  ship as IAR1 at OVLBASE. lvlArtT/artCur swap the two sets per level during the fall.
- svLiftT becomes one byte a rung (svCtrT). faceIdT/remLoT and runPlaneT/runFaceT are
  declared "within" rather than page-aligned.

Also: level 8 ships (hub black hole -> 8 -> ending); SEDGE seam-edge glyphs, eight codes
dropped from the shipped charset plan by tools/dropcodes.mjs; the fps suite covers level 8.

- Default game: regress.sh renders the same as 9c01164; the fps suite matches.

Opt-in, CLI-only. Guest stores to 0xBFFF00/+4/+8 push arguments, print a
format string, or switch to a va_list-style argument block; text goes to
stderr. Stores are intercepted in the AddressBus impl before any bounds
or sanitizer check, so the port works at any --ram; the JIT is forced
off, the 12 bytes are reserved out of the guest heap, and nested runs
inherit the flag.

events.title: debug: limit range watch values to the memwatch widths
events.message:
debug: limit range watch values to the memwatch widths

memwatch compares values at the width of the watch, computing the mask
from its size. For a range longer than 4 bytes that mask is zero, so a
value condition on such a range matched every access. Accept value
conditions only for ranges of 1, 2 or 4 bytes.

Also document that instruction fetches are only seen when the CPU
emulation fetches through the memory banks, as for console watchpoints.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: fix(whdbooter): prefer SHA1 matches and refresh outdated game database (#2441)
events.message:
fix(whdbooter): prefer SHA1 matches and refresh outdated game database (#2441)

* fix(whdbooter): prefer SHA1 matches and refresh outdated game database

- Entry lookup (JSON and XML): an exact SHA1 match wins; without one,
  use the last entry with the same filename. Before, the first entry
  matching filename or SHA1 won, so an earlier entry with the same
  filename could shadow the exact archive.
- On startup, replace the user's whdload_db.json with the bundled copy
  when the bundled 'generated' timestamp is newer, keeping a .bak and
  restoring it if the copy fails. Seeding only copied missing files, so
  upgrading Amiberry never updated an existing database.
- Seed candidates include the executable directory, where Windows
  installs whdboot.
- Help text: the update button downloads the JSON database from
  amiberry-game-db.

* fix(whdbooter): stage the bundled database before replacing the user copy

Copy the bundled whdload_db.json to whdload_db.json.new and check its
size first. Only then back up the user's database; if the backup fails,
keep the user's file and drop the staged copy. If the final rename
fails, restore the backup. A failed or partial copy can no longer
leave a truncated or missing database.

events.title: Keep blitter register writes after BBUSY drops out of the finishing blit
events.message:
Keep blitter register writes after BBUSY drops out of the finishing blit

BBUSY drops with the sequencer's last body cycle, two cycles before the
terminal D flush writes the final word. With 020+ chip-bus timing a CPU
polling DMACONR can land its next register write inside that window, and
a BLTCON0 write there was still treated as a mid-blit write: it disabled
the pending D output and the final word was lost. For a one-word,
one-row blit that word is the whole output, so graphics.library's
per-plane BltBitMap loop on a fast A4000 dropped entire bitplanes of
small copies (p96cts ClipBlit-disjoint on native PAL, issue #573). Only
a write while BBUSY is set now reaches the running blit.

The end-of-blit register write-back had the same window: it ran at
completion and overwrote values software had already written for its
next blit (BLTCDAT, the BLTBDAT B-old reset, and after a line blit the
whole BLTCON0/BLTCON1). The blit now publishes its register state once,
when BBUSY drops; the terminal cycles only retire the queued D word.
The released flag is a serde-default field, so older states still load.

events.title: ffemu: Add emulator of firmware user interface for terminal
events.message:
ffemu: Add emulator of firmware user interface for terminal

ffemu builds the firmware's own user interface code for the host and runs it in a terminal:
main.c, the display driver, FatFS and the image handlers are compiled as they are, against
models of the few peripherals they need. Nothing is connected to the floppy interface.

The screen is in the colors of Turbo Vision. The OLED display, an SSD1306 or an SH1106 of 32 or
64 rows, is drawn as Braille dots, half blocks or ASCII, in a color of the settings; in ASCII,
the whole screen is. Beside it, the FF.CFG that the firmware reads; below, the Controls window
pictures the USB port, the buttons, the encoder and the beeper, lighting up what is in use, the
Status window shows the device and the paths, and the Flash mem window the configuration in
flash, option by option; the firmware's console fills the rest, and also goes to a log file.
The keyboard stands in for the buttons and the rotary encoder; Space latches buttons, for long
and combined presses. Dialogs ask before quitting, choose the display fitted, and edit the
configuration in flash.

The USB drive is a FAT32 volume synthesized from a host directory, with the short names, long
names and attributes that copying the files to a real drive would give them: as Windows does
when built for Cygwin, in the OEM code page of the system, and as Linux vfat does otherwise.
It can also be read from an image file of a whole drive, or from a disk itself, such as a real
USB flash drive. What the firmware writes to it goes to a temporary file, never to the host
files, the image or the disk, and lasts until the drive is removed.
A power cycle re-executes the program, carrying over the flash and the drive. The settings are
kept in ~/.config/ffemu/ffemurc, written with the defaults on the first run and updated on a
change from the keyboard; its [Flash mem] section mirrors the flash memory, as hex and as
FF.CFG options, so that the flash lasts across runs as on the device.

A crash or a fatal signal restores the terminal. Where the host sleeps only in steps of
milliseconds, as a virtual machine on a Windows host may, the firmware's time is kept by
spinning. Commands on standard input drive it without a terminal, for testing, and can save
the drive as the firmware sees it.

It builds on Linux and on MSYS2, where the result also runs in Git Bash. ffemu/README.md has
the details.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Keep latched buttons through power cycle, reset all with Ctrl+Home
events.message:
ffemu: Keep latched buttons through power cycle, reset all with Ctrl+Home

Home power-cycles the device alone, as the firmware's own resets do, and
now keeps latch mode and the buttons it holds down, as fingers stay on
real buttons, so that a function the firmware checks at power-on can be
reached by latching the buttons and pressing Home. Until now a power
cycle released them.

Ctrl+Home, new, resets ffemu and the device together, as starting ffemu
again with the same arguments would: the host computer's signals are
back at their defaults, latching is off, and the firmware's writes to
the USB drive are dropped; only the terminal's modes go along. It undoes
in one press what Home keeps, such as signals left active. The script
command is "key relaunch".

The Controls window lists Home as "Power-cycle device" and the new key
below it, each hint one space after its key instead of in a column.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Change display-type in FF.CFG too when display change needs it
events.message:
ffemu: Change display-type in FF.CFG too when display change needs it

FF.CFG on the drive overrides flash on every boot, so the change of
display-type that fitting another display offered lasted one boot when
the file set it too: the device restarted twice and ended with the
mismatch. The dialog now says what the file sets; on a drive made from a
directory or a mounted disk the line is rewritten along with flash, the
old file kept as .BAK, and for an image, which cannot be written, the
dialog warns that the file will override the change.
