The flash stubs log "CFG:" and "Flash v%u %u bytes", as the firmware's
flash_cfg.c does since its lines were shortened for flash size.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Bump version to 1.4
events.message:
ffemu: Bump version to 1.4

Release 1.4: factory defaults marked in the Flash mem dialog, the Console
kept through the firmware's own resets, one question for every option
FF.CFG would override, the 8x16 font made from the 6x13 one as a choice
in the Display type dialog, the LCD's unlit dots shown faintly in half
blocks, and fixes to the dialogs' colors, hotkeys and notes.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Show errors in bright magenta, fit display frame to its title
events.message:
ffemu: Show errors in bright magenta, fit display frame to its title

Error messages were red, the message boxes white on red, and the note
"display type mismatch" in the display's frame dark red, which the frame
cut short when the title outgrew the pixels, as the LED display's does:
the title then showed in the frame's gray with its end missing. Errors
are bright magenta now, the boxes on bright magenta paper, and the frame
widens to its title.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Fix slow display on OS whose coarse sleeps were missed at start
events.message:
ffemu: Fix slow display on OS whose coarse sleeps were missed at start

ffemu spins instead of sleeping where the OS sleeps only in coarse steps, as a virtual
machine may, since each of the firmware's waits would otherwise last a whole step. Whether it
does was decided once, at the start, by the shortest of five sleeps of 100 us; on an Ubuntu VM
on Windows, whose steps are 6 to 15 ms, one of them now and then returns early, and then the
display, waiting for each I2C transfer, ran at a quarter of its speed: a long file name
scrolled slowly. Now eight sleeps in a row that take over 2 ms also switch to spinning.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Disable display-type suffix boxes while display type is not OLED
events.message:
ffemu: Disable display-type suffix boxes while display type is not OLED

The suffixes exist only after oled-128xNN in the firmware's encoding of
display-type, where bit 0 means narrower only while the OLED bit is set.
With auto chosen, a ticked suffix was dropped without a word when the
value was composed, so OK changed nothing and the box came back
unticked. The boxes are now dimmed while the display type is not an OLED
one, and Tab, Shift+Tab, the arrows and their hotkey pass them by; their
ticks are kept, and apply again once an OLED type is chosen.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Add Unpack FLASH.DMP to ffemurc button to Flash mem dialog
events.message:
ffemu: Add Unpack FLASH.DMP to ffemurc button to Flash mem dialog

FLASH.DMP is the settings area of a Gotek's flash memory, its 2 KB of
configuration slots, which the firmware writes beside FF.CFG at the
first insertion of a drive after "Save FLASH.DMP" in its main menu. The
new button, under the two that write FF.CFG, takes the slot from it
that the firmware would take, found as flash_cfg.c finds it, and puts
its settings into the emulated flash, and so into ffemurc as hex and
options, as OK puts the dialog's: they set the dialog up, its edits
dropped, FF.CFG on the drive is checked for options that it would undo,
every option of the dump counting, and the device is power-cycled. A
dump with no such slot leaves flash with no settings, so that the
factory defaults apply.

The button asks first, in a box over the dialog with OK and Cancel: the
file it unpacks, by its folder on the drive and the drive's path, the
[Flash mem] section of ffemurc by that file's path, and that the
dialog's edits are dropped and the device restarts; in dark red, if
FF.CFG on the drive sets some of the dump's options otherwise, that it
will then override them after restart. A path too long for the box is
shortened at its left with "...".

The button is disabled, with no tab stop, in light gray on dark gray,
while the drive holds no FLASH.DMP, which is looked for again whenever
the drive has been written.

The firmware takes the area it dumps from flash_ff_cfg_area(), which
ffemu stubbed as blank flash; this commit builds the area from the
emulated flash instead, its settings in the first slot as the firmware
writes one.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Add Save all and Save diff-from-flash to FF.CFG buttons to Flash mem dialog
events.message:
ffemu: Add Save all and Save diff-from-flash to FF.CFG buttons to Flash mem dialog

Two more buttons write FF.CFG on the USB drive as the dialog shows the
options, edits included: every option, or only those whose value differs
from what flash holds, which is all the firmware needs, since it keeps
the flash value of an option the file does not name. Nothing else moves:
the dialog stays open, flash changes only on OK, and the firmware reads
the file when the drive is next inserted or the device restarts; the
bottom line says what was written. The file is generated afresh from the
firmware's own examples/FF.CFG, built into the program by mk_text.py, so
that each option stands below the comments that explain it and its
values; a value that FF.CFG cannot give is noted in a comment instead.
The previous file is kept as FF.CFG.BAK, in place of an older .BAK. The
file goes where the firmware looks for it: into the folder FF if the
drive has one, else into the root. A drive made from a directory is
written in that directory, a real drive where the system has it mounted,
by its drive letter on Windows or its mount point on Linux; an image
file is not written, and the dialog says so, as it does for a disk that
is not mounted.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Say in Flash mem dialog that only options ffemu supports are offered
events.message:
ffemu: Say in Flash mem dialog that only options ffemu supports are offered

The dialog's explanation becomes one paragraph, wrapped at blanks to the
dialog's width, and ends by saying that only the options ffemu supports
are offered; the columns start below it, however many lines it takes.
The wrapping comes out of the message box into a helper both use.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Take USB drive attached when run without argument
events.message:
ffemu: Take USB drive attached when run without argument

Without an argument ffemu takes the USB drive attached, if there is just one. The current
directory, the default before, was of little use: a directory worth running against is given
by name anyway. If there are more drives, ffemu lists them and stops, each on a line that ends
with what to give instead, such as "Generic Flash Disk, 1.9 GB, J: is /dev/sdf1"; if there is
none, it says so and asks for a directory, an image or a disk.

A drive is given as its first partition, the one that FatFS would take, which starts with the
FAT volume as a drive without a partition table does: Windows lets anyone read a volume on
removable media, but only an administrator the physical drive. When reading a whole disk is
denied on Windows, ffemu suggests its partition too.

usbdisk.c takes the disks from /proc/partitions, which Cygwin provides too, with the drive
letters of their partitions, and leaves out the empty ones, such as card reader slots. Linux
tells which are on USB in /sys/block, with vendor and model, and the mount point comes from
/proc/mounts; Windows tells it in the storage descriptor of \\.\PhysicalDriveN, with vendor
and product, which it gives without administrator rights. Reading the disk itself still needs
them, or sudo on Linux.

This is the last change of release 1.2, so the version becomes 1.2.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Show IMAGE_A.CFG in Status
events.message:
ffemu: Show IMAGE_A.CFG in Status

A line of Status shows the firmware's IMAGE_A.CFG, where it keeps the
image selected, as the firmware sees it now, its own writes included:
the name in cyan, the text in yellow, a line end as a bright magenta
\r or \n, and a green > in the frame when the line is cut short. The
file is read through the emulated volume, with the overlay of the
firmware's writes, whenever the drive has been written since; "none"
while there is no drive or no such file.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Keep README and scripts within 80 columns
events.message:
ffemu: Keep README and scripts within 80 columns

The README had a line per paragraph and per list item, many of them far
wider than the 80 columns the project keeps; it is wrapped at 79 now,
code blocks, headings and the words themselves unchanged. One docstring
line of mk_text.py went past 80 as well.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Bump version to 1.3+
events.message:
ffemu: Bump version to 1.3+

The commits from here on change what ffemu shows, so the binaries no
longer behave as the 1.3 release does.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Shorten Esc delay to 25 ms, keeping 200 ms over ssh
events.message:
ffemu: Shorten Esc delay to 25 ms, keeping 200 ms over ssh

Esc took 200 ms to act, the time ncurses was told to wait for the rest
of a key sequence that starts with that byte. A terminal writes a
sequence whole, so htop's 25 ms is enough there and is what ffemu sets
now. An ssh session delivers a sequence in pieces now and then, and
25 ms turned an arrow key into a stray Esc, so ffemu keeps 200 ms when
SSH_TTY says it runs in one; the environment variable ESCDELAY, if set,
overrides either.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Shorten path in Flash mem dialog's note at its left to fit
events.message:
ffemu: Shorten path in Flash mem dialog's note at its left to fit

The note of what Save did names the file written, and a path longer than
the dialog's last row was cut at the frame: the row showed the start of
the path and nothing of the note. ff_cfg_write() now marks the path in
its message, and the row shortens the marked part at its left with "..."
to leave room for the rest; the green '>' at the frame stays only for a
text too long all the same. The log drops the marks, and the note's
buffer now holds a whole path.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Ask about every option FF.CFG would override, without listing them
events.message:
ffemu: Ask about every option FF.CFG would override, without listing them

When OK changed options that FF.CFG on the drive sets otherwise, which
the firmware puts back on the next boot, the question listed at most
four of them, and Yes changed only those four in FF.CFG: a fifth was
undone silently. The dialog now says that FF.CFG will override some of
the new values after restart, and Yes changes every one of them, in a
single pass that keeps the original file as .BAK; before, each option
rewrote the file in turn, so .BAK held all but the last change.

The file is also taken as the firmware takes it: the last line for an
option counts, and every such line is rewritten; a value differs when
it parses to another setting, not when its text does. The display
change's question about display-type in FF.CFG uses the same test.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Keep LCD character ROM choice enabled whatever display is chosen
events.message:
ffemu: Keep LCD character ROM choice enabled whatever display is chosen

The ROMs in the Display type dialog were dimmed and skipped by Tab unless
an LCD was chosen, although lcd-rom applies whatever the display, and
since disabled controls became light gray on dark gray, the dimmed rows
had the dark gray only behind their text, the rest staying cyan. The
ROMs are now always enabled, and Tab goes over every control.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Keep showing FF.CFG, dimmed, while USB drive is out
events.message:
ffemu: Keep showing FF.CFG, dimmed, while USB drive is out

The FF.CFG window went blank as soon as the drive was ejected. It now keeps showing the file in
its colors made dark, as are the scroll marks and the key legends, with the frame, the path and
the scroll bar in dark gray: for a drive made from a directory, the file as it is on the host
now, so that an edit there shows what the next insertion will give the firmware; for an image
or a disk, the FF.CFG last read from it.

Every Del, even with the drive already out, looks for the FF.CFG of a directory again and reads
it again, so that a new file shows, and an edit that changes neither the size nor the time.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Note in README that it was written with help of Claude
events.message:
ffemu: Note in README that it was written with help of Claude

The note ends the README's first section, which is about ffemu as a
whole, so it speaks of the program, not of the README alone.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Draw Display type dialog's radio buttons as Flash mem dialog does
events.message:
ffemu: Draw Display type dialog's radio buttons as Flash mem dialog does

The Display type dialog drew its list by hand, "(*)" and bold for the
choice, while the Flash mem dialog has the Turbo Vision cluster, the
bullet on cyan with the current row highlighted. radio_row() draws such a
row for any dialog now.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Show help inside Flash mem dialog, explaining item under cursor
events.message:
ffemu: Show help inside Flash mem dialog, explaining item under cursor

The help of the control in focus was on the screen's bottom line, where
it went unnoticed. It is now on the dialog's last row, above the bottom
frame, in dark blue on the dialog's gray; a text too long for the row is
cut at the frame, which a bright green mark replaces, as in the panes.

A radio button or check box explains itself: the row shows the text of
the item under the cursor, from a table keyed by option and item, and
falls back to the control's own text. The texts are rewritten to say
what the dialog does not show already: units and ranges of the fields,
and what each value does.

The note of a Save goes to the same row, in green, until the next key;
before, it was never cleared and could outlive the dialog. While a
dialog is open, the bottom line lists its keys, Enter OK, Esc Cancel and
the navigation keys, and it is drawn after the dialog, whose shadow
darkened it in a short window. The suffix check boxes are labeled
"display-type suffix".
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Emulate 7-segment LED display, 3 digits on TM1651 or 2 on 74HC164
events.message:
ffemu: Emulate 7-segment LED display, 3 digits on TM1651 or 2 on 74HC164

The display dialog gains the two LED displays. led_7seg.c models them on
the two GPIO lines, PB6 and PB7 on this board, whose levels hw.c now
takes from port B's configuration and output registers: the TM1651's
two-wire protocol with its ACK, which the firmware's probe relies on,
and the shift registers' 16-bit frames, read once CLK has rested. The
digits are drawn as pixels in the three renderings, from fonts in
led_7seg_font.h, one per rendering, each row a string of segment
numbers; the unlit segments are faint where the terminal has 16 colors.
"dump" prints the digits as text and in the ASCII shape. The firmware
finds an LED display only when display-type is auto, so fitting one
offers to set that, and the frame says "display type mismatch" when
flash says otherwise.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Add check box for 8x16 font made from 6x13 one to Display type dialog
events.message:
ffemu: Add check box for 8x16 font made from 6x13 one to Display type dialog

The firmware built with oled_font_8x16_synth=y, as its STM32F105 logfile
and debug builds are by default, draws the 8x16 font from the 6x13 one.
ffemu defines the display driver's OLED_FONT_8x16_SYNTH as a variable,
emu_oled_synth_8x16, so that the one program has both ways: the check
box "Made from 6x13, bold" under "OLED 8x16 font" in the Display type
dialog switches it at once, with no restart, and ffemurc keeps it as
oled-8x16 = font | synth.

The check box is always enabled, whatever the display chosen, as the
ROMs are, and Tab goes over it.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Emulate host computer's signals on floppy interface
events.message:
ffemu: Emulate host computer's signals on floppy interface

The keyboard stands in for the host computer's signals that select the drive and move its
head, so that the track display can be watched as a computer would drive it. Two new rows of
the Controls window show the kind of controller on the other side of the cable, Step/Dir or
Apple2, and its signals, each lit in dark yellow while active as on the schematics, whatever
its voltage, with the keys that change them below:

- Shugart: [ toggles drive select, ] motor on, - the step direction, + sends a step pulse and
  \ toggles side select. Selected and stepping inward are the defaults.
- Apple2: [ toggles drive enable, + and - move the four stepper phases to their next or
  previous state in the cycle that a computer goes through, single phases and pairs between
  them, and \ releases them all, keeping their state, which is shown after the phases, for the
  next press to go on from. Enabled is the default.

= also works as +, and / as \, which the Russian layout types with that key, as it types the
keys of [ and ]. The signals survive a power cycle, as the computer's would. The Status window
shows the cylinder and the side as the firmware sees them, and as Floppy the image mounted;
Controls, Status and Flash mem are four rows taller for it. The script command key takes the
actions by name, and status prints the signals and the drive.

The firmware's handling of the signals is in src/floppy.c, floppy_generic.c and
gotek/floppy.c, which ffemu now builds itself, so that the signals from the keyboard reach it
as pin levels and the firmware decides what they do, the motor and its delay included: no
steps unless selected, none beyond max-cyl, the side only for a double-sided image.

hw.c models what that code uses: port B as well as port A as inputs, the signals of the host
computer on their pins (active low, but the Apple2 stepper phases active high), EXTI per line
as AFIO routes it, so that the floppy lines and the rotary encoder coexist, its pending
register cleared by writing ones, and TIM2 capturing the end of each STEP pulse. The timers and
DMA channels of the read and write data are mere registers: no data flows.

The Apple2 build compiles src/floppy.c, as it does gotek/board.c, at the logfile level, which
puts the stepper phases where the release has them. ffemu renames floppy_handle(),
floppy_insert() and floppy_cancel() when building it, and stubs.c wraps them: the loop that runs
while an image is mounted idles for a millisecond each time round, and the name of the image
mounted is kept for the Status window.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Redesign keys and buttons: red keys, round buttons, lit when pressed
events.message:
ffemu: Redesign keys and buttons: red keys, round buttons, lit when pressed

Keys were yellow, the color of values too. They are red now, as hotkeys are in Turbo Vision:
bright red, and dark red where their window is dimmed, in the Controls window, in the paging
hints of window frames, and in the dialogs.

The buttons are drawn round, as on the Gotek: < and > in parentheses, as Ent already was for
the knob, with the keys in bright red on the window's blue. The arrows above and below the
knob stand right of its middle, where its rim moves: up when it is turned anticlockwise, down
when clockwise.

The key names of the Controls window, Ins, Del and Home, the keys under the FDD signals, and
the paging keys in the frames of the Flash mem and FF.CFG windows light up for the hold time
when pressed, so that a press shows even where it changes nothing else on the screen. The keys
typed in place of others, = for + and / for \, light up the key shown; Ctrl+PgUp lights Ctrl
as well.

A key or button in use is dark red on bright yellow: a pressed button, a turned knob, a key lit
by its press, the latch key while its mode lasts, a button held in latch mode. A button at
rest in latch mode is dark red on light gray, as before. The USB port, lit for a moment when
the firmware reads or writes the drive, is dark yellow instead of bright yellow, less glaring
for an indicator that flickers, and "Ejected" is dark gray instead of red, as an idle state.

In the Status window, the lines of the drive and of the USB drive show their values and states
in green and their words and punctuation in gray: "Cyl 2, side 0, selected", "2 files, 0 dirs".

The focused window keeps its double-line frame when its color pair is the bright twin of the
focus pair, where the frame fell back to a single line.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Add build for Apple2 firmware
events.message:
ffemu: Add build for Apple2 firmware

make -C ffemu TARGET=apple2 builds ffemu-apple2, which runs the firmware of the Apple2 target:
it lists only HFE images. TARGET defaults to shugart, which builds ffemu as before. Each program
has a build directory of its own and keeps its settings, flash mirror and log in directories
named after it, so that both can run at once.

The Apple2 debug build moves two stepper phases onto the rotary encoder pins and turns off
the KC30 header, since the UART takes the release's phase pins. ffemu compiles gotek/board.c
alone at the logfile level, which keeps the pins of the release; the level is tested in the
headers only for ASSERT() and prototypes, so one file may differ from the rest. ffemu takes the
console output itself, as before.

The target is shown in the usage, in the status script command and, in bright green, in the
Status window; the top line has the program's name.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Mark factory defaults in Flash mem dialog with =
events.message:
ffemu: Mark factory defaults in Flash mem dialog with =

Each radio button that the firmware's defaults choose, and each check
box that they check, has a dark gray "=" in the leftmost column of its
cyan field, black where the terminal has only 8 colors; the paragraph
at the top of the dialog says so, its "options supported by ffemu"
shortened to "options used by ffemu" to keep it to two lines. The
defaults are the values the firmware has when its flash holds no
settings, taken from its own table, so the marks follow the firmware.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Rename Firmware console pane to Console
events.message:
ffemu: Rename Firmware console pane to Console

The pane shows ffemu's own lines, those starting with "ffemu:", among
the firmware's console output, so it is the Console now.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Bump version to 1.3
events.message:
ffemu: Bump version to 1.3

Release 1.3: the character LCD and the 7-segment LED displays, writing
FF.CFG from the Flash mem dialog, IMAGE_A.CFG in Status, and the help
row in the dialog.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Check FF.CFG on OK of Flash mem dialog for options it would undo
events.message:
ffemu: Check FF.CFG on OK of Flash mem dialog for options it would undo

FF.CFG on the drive overrides flash on every boot, so a change made in
the dialog and confirmed with OK lasted one boot when the file set the
option too: the device restarted twice and the change was gone. OK now
lists the options it changes that FF.CFG sets to another value; on a
drive made from a directory or a mounted disk it offers to change them in
the file as well, and for an image, which cannot be written, it warns
that the file will restore them and asks whether to write flash anyway.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Fix hang of firmware in handler waiting on I2C bus
events.message:
ffemu: Fix hang of firmware in handler waiting on I2C bus

The display could stop for good, with one CPU core at 100%: on Windows a live session showed
the firmware's thread in i2c_stop(), which the SH1106 code calls from the I2C event handler,
spinning on the STOP bit until the I2C model clears it. Two things kept it from ever being
cleared.

A tick that came in the middle of the firmware thread's own update of the models ran the
interrupt handlers right there. The handler then spun with the models' lock held by the update
it interrupted, so no later update could run. On Linux the firmware recovered after the 200 ms
timeout of its display DMA, logging "I2C: Error (0000)"; on Windows it did not. Handlers now
never run in the middle of an update; every update is followed by a run of them anyway.

Even so, a handler that waits on a peripheral was released only by a nested tick, and Cygwin
defers a signal to a thread that spins inside a handler until the thread calls into Cygwin,
which a register poll never does. The I2C bus and its DMA now also run on a thread of their
own every 100 us, as the hardware runs beside the CPU; the models change the bits of the
registers that the firmware also writes atomically. The one-shot timer and GPIO stay on the
firmware's thread, since the timer's end clearing its enable bit would race the firmware
setting the next deadline.

A test build without nested ticks hung at the first display update before, and ran on with
this change.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Show LCD's unlit dots faintly in half blocks, white ink on any blue
events.message:
ffemu: Show LCD's unlit dots faintly in half blocks, white ink on any blue

A real character LCD shows the dots of its characters faintly even where
they are not lit. In the half block rendering, on a terminal of 16 colors
or more and with the backlight on, the dots of each character that are
not lit are now drawn in the panel's color of the other brightness, the
gaps between the characters keeping the panel's own color;
hd44780_pixels() gives the dots for that. The characters are bright white
on a bright blue panel too, not only on the dark blue one, as such
modules are made.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Fix dialog colors and Flash mem dialog's Tab order
events.message:
ffemu: Fix dialog colors and Flash mem dialog's Tab order

The note that says what a Save button wrote was bright green on the
dialog's light gray, hard to read; it is dark green now. The help that
the note replaces on that row keeps its color, and the mark of a cut
line stays bright green.

A button's text is bright white while the button has the focus. OK is
light cyan while the focus is on no button, since Enter presses it
then, and black otherwise, as the other buttons are. The Display type
dialog drew OK bright white while the focus was on its radio buttons,
as if OK had it.

The hotkey letters in the dialogs are dark red instead of bright red,
on the light gray and on the cyan alike.

Tab went to OK and Cancel before the two FF.CFG buttons of the Flash
mem dialog, which stand above them; it now takes the buttons in the
order they are seen.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Keep Console through firmware's own resets, marked by separator
events.message:
ffemu: Keep Console through firmware's own resets, marked by separator

A reset that the firmware does by itself, as after a factory reset or a
change of display options in FF.CFG, re-executed ffemu as a power cycle
does, and so began the console anew, the old one moved to console.bak.
It is no power cycle, which only ffemu itself does: now console.log goes
on, the new process takes its tail back into the Console pane, and a
green "======= Firmware reset =======" marks where the reset was.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: gotek/floppy: Provide C fallbacks for ARM-only code
events.message:
gotek/floppy: Provide C fallbacks for ARM-only code

The SELA interrupt enters through a speculative stub in ARM assembly, which also defines
gpio_out_active and gpiob_setreset, and which update_SELA_irq() patches to tail-call the Amiga
HD-ID handler; dma_rd_set_active() writes through a bitband alias; and a few pointers are cast
to uint32_t. None of this builds for a 64-bit host. When not compiling for ARM, the stub is a
C function that calls the handler chosen by a flag, which update_SELA_irq() sets, the bitband
store is an atomic update of the word, and the casts go through uintptr_t, so that the floppy
interface can be built for a host, as ffemu does.

The ARM build is unaffected: all firmware binaries are byte-identical.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Emulate HD44780 character LCD on I2C backpack, CYR and A00 ROMs
events.message:
ffemu: Emulate HD44780 character LCD on I2C backpack, CYR and A00 ROMs

The display dialog gains LCDs of 16x2, 20x2, 20x4 and 40x2 characters,
the sizes of display-type lcd-CCxRR. hd44780.c models the controller
behind a PCF8574 port expander at I2C address 0x27: it decodes the 4-bit
protocol that the firmware clocks through the expander's pins, and keeps
the display RAM, the display shift and the backlight. The I2C bus routes
a transaction to the LCD or the OLED controller by its address. The LCD
is drawn dark on its lit panel in the display color, white on the dark
blue one, dimmed while the backlight is off, with the same margins in
every rendering.

The glyphs come from one of two character ROMs, each a header with the
labeled glyphs and the Unicode character of each code: lcd_font_cyr.h,
the default, page 0 of MELT's modules, whose codes the other Cyrillic
modules share, and lcd_font_a00.h, the HD44780's A00 of most other
modules. The ROM is chosen in the display dialog, whose last row names
the header of the ROM in focus, and kept as lcd-rom in ffemurc. The
ASCII rendering prints the characters, as "dump" does in UTF-8, and a
white square for a code that stands for none. Fitting an LCD offers the
display-type to match, the firmware driving an LCD as 16x2 with auto,
and the Flash mem dialog offers the lcd-CCxRR types.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Show FLASH.DMP in Status and firmware's in Console, warn of drive's own
events.message:
ffemu: Show FLASH.DMP in Status and firmware's in Console, warn of drive's own

The firmware writes FLASH.DMP into ffemu's store of its writes, never
onto the drive's medium, and ffemu now says so. Status has a line for
FLASH.DMP under the USB drive's lines, as the firmware sees the drive:
"virtual from fw" while the drive holds a FLASH.DMP whose data the
firmware wrote, as the store tells, so across power cycles too, with
"masks drive's" if the medium holds one of its own; "exists on drive"
for the medium's own alone; "absent", all in dark gray, for none; and
the name alone, in dark gray, while the drive is out. The IMAGE_A.CFG
line follows suit: all in dark gray when absent, and the name alone
while the drive is out, where it said "absent" though the medium may
well hold the file. The Console logs the firmware's write, with whether
flash held settings for the dump's first slot, and the Unpack button's
question names the firmware's dump as what it unpacks.

As soon as "Save FLASH.DMP" is chosen in the firmware's main menu, a
message box warns if the drive's medium, or the last drive's while it
is out, holds a FLASH.DMP of its own: the Unpack button will load the
firmware's dump, not that file. For that, ffemu's build makes the
firmware's flag of a pending dump, static in main.c, global with
objcopy, and the medium is read without the firmware's writes, which
for a drive made from a directory means its sectors as built from the
files.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Write FF.CFG beside image file, after asking, for drive from image
events.message:
ffemu: Write FF.CFG beside image file, after asking, for drive from image

The two Save buttons of the Flash mem dialog refused a drive made from
an image file, which ffemu never writes. They now ask first, in a box
like the Unpack button's: the file goes beside the image, named as the
image with ".FF.CFG" appended, and the firmware will not see it; if one
is there already, it is kept as .BAK. The box and the Unpack question
share a helper that lays such a question out, its paths shortened at
the left with "..." where the window is too narrow.

The options in FF.CFG are still changed only in the drive's own file,
which a drive from an image does not have.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Add show-filename-ext to Flash mem dialog
events.message:
ffemu: Add show-filename-ext to Flash mem dialog

The option is read and written in the settings file's flash mirror by
name, and the dialog offers its three values as radio buttons under the
OLED font, with the hotkey h; the help row explains each value.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: ffemu: Exit when terminal goes away without hangup signal
events.message:
ffemu: Exit when terminal goes away without hangup signal

When the terminal closes, the hangup signal may reach only the process
that the terminal runs: a shell that started ffemu, under tmux on MSYS2
for one. ffemu then outlived it, and since reads of the terminal fail
at once, the TUI thread's wait for a key no longer waited, so it redrew
for ever, a whole core busy.

The TUI thread now takes three waits in a row that end at once with no
key, while poll() reads the terminal as ready, as the terminal's end,
and raises the hangup signal itself, which ends ffemu as the real one
does.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

enclosure, a card reader or anything else that presents a USB mass
storage volume does as well. So the messages, the comments and the
README now say USB drive, the term the firmware's own messages use.

events.title: img, dsk: Fix data CRC when read starts within sector's data
events.message:
img, dsk: Fix data CRC when read starts within sector's data

When a track is read from mid-track, as after every seek, and the start
falls within a sector's data, calc_start_pos() regenerates the data from
its first chunk with the CRC seeded with 0xffff instead of the CRC of
the data mark before it. That sector then carries a wrong CRC in the
first revolution. No host can read the sector then, having missed its
marks, so the error is harmless.

Nonetheless we can easily do better when the read starts within the
first 1kB chunk of a sector's data. So let's do so.

A start within a data CRC field, or beyond the first chunk of a larger
sector, still gives that sector a wrong CRC in the first revolution.
The same is also true if a DSK sector's data mark is abnormal. However
the incorrect CRC is "safe" in all cases as the ID and Data marks
are not emitted on this first (partial) revolution.

Based on an original patch from Mike Shevchenko.

events.title: Enhance 68020 code generation efficiency and alignment
events.message:
Enhance 68020 code generation efficiency and alignment

- Implemented support for long branches (`BRA.L`/`Bcc.L`) and improved branch size selection based on displacement.
- Updated handling of arbitrary strides in indexed addressing to use `mulu.l` for non-{1,2,4,8} strides on 68020, avoiding 16-bit truncation.
- Added alignment directives for `long` and `ptr` data labels, ensuring 4-byte alignment with `cnop 0,4` where necessary.
- Updated documentation to reflect changes in emitted code efficiency and alignment strategies.
- Added tests to validate new behaviors for branch sizing, data alignment, and stride handling across both 68000 and 68020 targets.

events.title: 0.2b2: convert filenames between Amiga Latin-1 and server UTF-8
events.message:
0.2b2: convert filenames between Amiga Latin-1 and server UTF-8

AmigaDOS names are ISO-8859-1 while Linux, TrueNAS and Synology store
names as UTF-8, so accented names came out as mojibake on one side and
were unreachable from the other. Convert at the wire boundary only:

- pk_name() encodes outgoing names (LOOKUP, CREATE, MKDIR, REMOVE,
  RMDIR, RENAME) as UTF-8; the buffer holds 2*NAME_MAX_AMIGA+1 bytes.
- nfs_readdir() decodes entries to Latin-1 into DirEnt.name; the
  NAME_MAX_AMIGA check now happens after decoding. Code points outside
  Latin-1 become '?' so the entry stays listable; truncated or invalid
  sequences pass through byte-wise.
- New Startup option CHARSET=UTF8 (default) | RAW (old byte-for-byte
  behaviour, for Latin-1 servers or names written by 0.1).
- lower() folds the Latin-1 letters 0xC0..0xDE (except 0xD7) like
  utility.library ToLower(), so the case-insensitive fallback lookup
  also matches accented names.

Also: Makefile finds m68k-amigaos-gcc on PATH, in ~/opt/amiga/bin or in
the ApolloCrossDev tree (override with CC=); `make check` runs a native
unit test that extracts the converter block from nfs-handler.c so it
cannot drift from the real code; doc/readme/NFS0 updated; the stray
tests/__pycache__ file is removed and ignored.

Tested by the author on WinUAE (bsdsocket emulation) against TrueNAS
SCALE NFSv3, and on the A1200 (Emu68 lwIP) against Linux nfsd: list,
read, create, mkdir, rename and delete with accented names both ways;
case-insensitive lookups match accented letters.

Taken from Renaud's branch charset-latin1-utf8 (03acf73) with these
changes: version 0.2b2 on top of 0.2b1; the Makefile's toolchain search
only runs when CC is make's built-in default (CC ?= never fired, as
make predefines CC=cc); BUILD-FR.txt left out, the doc covers it;
HISTORY credits him.

docs(gc): Immix against classic on the real hardware — the Vampire and the MorphOS box

Both machines ran both binaries of the trimmed tree (c569c96d) through
trunk/gc-phase0.lisp, trunk/gc-mark-bench.lisp and the Amiga suite:

- Vampire (68080): mutator 1,229 -> 379 us/step bare, 1,041 -> 384
  loaded; the churn cycle flat at 2.4-2.8 s against 8.2-9.6 s once
  classic leaves the bump front; the idle editor pause 80 against 120 ms;
  the mark alone 96 against 64 ms on 2.1 MB (the +50 % of the 68020).

  mark-loop pass on hardware.  Suite without the AHI file 5,181 of 5,188
  under Immix, 5,180 under classic, the same non-passes (deployment and
  machine) plus the audio flake.  The AHI playback checks froze the

- MorphOS (first Immix run on that box): 38.0 -> 7.5 us/step bare,

  the same 4,625 of 4,629 under either collector.

events.title: gc: gc_backend.h, the backend seam, with GC= build knob and test tagging (seam step 5)
events.message:
gc: gc_backend.h, the backend seam, with GC= build knob and test tagging (seam step 5)

The heap core (mem.c) and the shared facilities (gc_trace.c,
gc_compact.c, gc_jitscan.c, gc_verify.c) now know the collector only
through src/core/gc_backend.h; gc_classic.c is the one file that
implements it.  mem.h selects CL_GC_CLASSIC / CL_GC_IMMIX (exclusive;
classic when neither is defined, so the cross and MorphOS makefiles are
untouched) and makes CL_GENGC a mode of classic.

The interface as landed, where it differs from the spec's table:
gcb_arena_alloc/free (gen mode needs write-watched pages), gcb_init /
gcb_shutdown (self-resetting side tables), gcb_alloc_fast
(CL_ALWAYS_INLINE: the cursor SHAPE is the backend's, so the front/chunk
cuts moved into the header next to the chunk refill that shares them),
gcb_alloc_slow, gcb_collect(why) for cl_gc / cl_gc_reclaim_young (now
backend-neutral wrappers in mem.c, with gc_stop_world_timed), the two
image-adoption phases, gcb_before_image_save, three compactor hooks
(gcb_compact_begin / _fallback(outcome) / _done) that take the gen-mode
blocks and the classic policy counter out of gc_compact.c, and
gcb_stats_report.  GCB_ON_MARK is called in gc_mark_obj (the gen survivor
note) and GCB_ON_ALLOC_FINALIZABLE in cl_alloc; GCB_HDR_* are defined but
the raw CL_HDR_* sites, the grep lint and the iterator's GCB_WALK_CLIP
land with the backend that needs them (Part 2) -- gc_walk_next gains no
token here.

gc_classic.c owns alloc_from_bump, the free-list probe, the chunk refill,
gcb_alloc_slow and gc_sweeps_since_compact; gc_compact_pending and
gc_last_compact_cycle are the compactor's own (gc_compact.c).
cl_gengc_enabled() is declared unconditionally (0 without CL_GENGC), which
also un-breaks the CL_NO_GENGC build of test_mem and
test_alloc_freelist_perf; cl_gc_if_stale stays public under CL_GC_CLASSIC
for test_gc_threaded's dedup tests.

Makefile: GC ?= classic; GC_DEF in CFLAGS_HOST and CFLAGS_TEST, GC_SRC
picks the backend file, GC=immix builds into build/host-immix (the
two-binary host A/B, like FPU=1) and stops at the header's #error until
gc_immix.c exists.  Tagged #ifdef CL_GC_CLASSIC (trivial pass otherwise):
test_gc_fwd_bitmap, test_gc_hdr_index, test_alloc_sweep_escape,
test_gc_root_dedup, test_alloc_freelist_perf, test_gc_cursor.

Gates on this tree: make test 419/419; test-gc-stress and test-memleak
rc 0; CL_NO_GENGC+CL_NO_TLAB make test 417 with only the two config
artefacts (docs-symbols misses %GENGC-STATS, cross_wide_knob inherits the
BUILDDIR override); DEBUG_GC+DEBUG_GC_STRESS C unit tests all green except
test_gc_threaded's error_unwind_restores_gc_roots_nested BADMARK abort,
which the step-4 baseline reproduces byte-identically (pre-existing, noted
separately); bench-opt vs step 4 interleaved min-of-3: total 873 -> 873,

fast path still inline (same four calls as before); FS-UAE fresh
5321/5322 (audio flake) + restored 5274/5274.

events.title: gc: the Immix per-visit trims — validation out of the precise drain, the mark set by a flip
events.message:
gc: the Immix per-visit trims — validation out of the precise drain, the mark set by a flip

Two of the items the Immix visit still did over classic's leave the loop;
the third was measured and stays.

Validation is a compile-time constant of the drain.  The run-time flag
gc_mark_validating and the context word are gone: gc_mark_drain is
instantiated twice from one always-inline body — gc_mark_drain for the
precise trace and the generational minor, gc_mark_drain_validating for
the two phases that can push garbage (after the conservative JIT scan,
and the overflow rescan; each preceded by GCB_VALIDATE_BEGIN, which
resets the object-start cursor).  gc_mark_children takes the flag as a
parameter — a register test per slot of a non-cons object — so the
per-type walk, most of the trace's text, exists once; the cons, which
the drains scan inline, has the constant.  Under classic the two drains
are the same code.  On the 68020 the flag was worth 6 %: the register it
needed was one the drain did not have (the disassembly showed the arena
size, the sense and the line map spilled around it).

The mark is set by flipping the bit (Immix GCB_HDR_SET_MARK_C): the visit
calls it only for an object GCB_HDR_MARKED_C just found unmarked, whose
bit therefore equals the sense — one instruction, no second constant to
hold across the loop.  Another 1.5 %.

The live byte count stays.  An experiment binary that derived it from the
line map at sweep time measured the per-object add at 32 ms of 2,572 per
cycle (1.2 %), and the line-level number is not the same quantity: it
reports every live line in full (2,319 KB for 2,167 KB of objects) — the
very figure the compaction policy subtracts from the hole total to see
line-level fragmentation, so with the two equal that test could never
fire.  trunk/gc-mark-bench.lisp gained *mark-bench-units* (a fixed live
set regardless of what the binary under test reports) for that run.

FS-UAE 68020 cycle-exact, trunk/gc-mark-bench.lisp, 2.1 MB live, mark
per cycle: Immix 2,768 -> 2,612 (validation) -> 2,572 ms (flip);
classic 1,656 (1,648 before; noise).  m68k text: Immix +28 bytes,
classic +396.  docs/gc-phase0-results.md "The Immix per-visit trims",
spec "The per-visit trims".

Gates: make test (classic + GC=immix), make test-gc-stress (both),
make test-memleak (both), FS-UAE 040 test-amiga.

gc: backend-seam + Immix spec, Phase 0 measurements, ext:%heap-stats

specs/gc-backend-immix.md proposes splitting mem.c behind a compile-time
GC backend interface (classic+gen stay one backend) and an Immix-style
mark-region collector for the m68k/MorphOS builds: exact line marks, a
mark-bit sense flip instead of a clearing walk, dead-spanner clipping on
the arena walk, the sliding compactor kept as the rare defrag/image path.

Phase 0 (the spec's measurement gate) is done: trunk/gc-phase0.lisp
profiles a classic collection cycle from the runtime's own counters, and
docs/gc-phase0-results.md records Vampire, FS-UAE 68040, FS-UAE 68020 and
host.  Under churn the sweep is 40-60% of the pause and free-list
allocation makes the mutator 2-4x slower than bump allocation; on a dense
idle heap the pause is 85% mark (4.1 s with Clamacs resident on a 68020);
the first collection after a FASL load is a FreeVec storm from dead
loader bytecodes.

(ext:%heap-stats) is the allocator-side counterpart of %gc-time-stats:
arena size, bump, live, consed, free-list probe steps, TLAB refills and
the free-list shape (cl_heap_free_list_stats).  Covered by
test_runtime_forms.sh; README and docs/package-symbols.txt updated.

events.title: gc: one allocation cursor behind cl_alloc, gcb_alloc_slow as the refill (seam step 4)
events.message:
gc: one allocation cursor behind cl_alloc, gcb_alloc_slow as the refill (seam step 4)

Unification C of specs/gc-backend-immix.md.  cl_alloc is now the cursor
cut and nothing else: cursor_cut_front / cursor_cut_chunk (CL_ALWAYS_INLINE,
new in platform.h) cut the regime's cursor lock-free, and gcb_alloc_slow
(mem.c, CL_NOINLINE — the classic backend's half of the seam until step 5
moves it behind gc_backend.h) refills the chunk and cuts, or allocates
directly under the unchanged classic policy, and owns the accounting.

The classic backend's two cursors, chosen by `multi`: single-threaded the
LIVE bump front [cl_heap.bump, arena_size) — a cut is the bump allocation,
exact for every reader with nothing to flush; multi-threaded the chunk of
the former TLAB, now alloc_cur/alloc_lim/alloc_consed in CL_Thread on
every build (CL_TLAB carves them; without it multi-threaded allocation
takes the locked slow path as before).  gc_tlab_reset_all ->
gc_cursor_drop_all (unconditional, also in cl_mem_adopt_image_begin),
cl_tlab_retire -> cl_cursor_retire.  A chunk left over after the thread
count drops to one is never cut again and is dropped by the next
collection or slow-path entry.

Measured and rejected on the way: a per-thread SNAPSHOT of the front with
a kind flag (the spec's literal "cursor = the remaining bump region")
costs +2 ms on alloc.cons-churn and alloc.mixed-churn on the host (the
thread-pointer load plus the dependent cursor loads) and needs a kind
check on every cut to survive thread-count transitions; the live front
has neither.  The m68k -Os build was CALLING alloc_from_bump on every
cons; the front cut is inline now.

tests/test_gc_cursor.c (7): front == bump after every cut with exact
accounting; the arena tail absorbed so the front lands on arena_size;
sweep / compaction / retire / image adoption leave the front consistent;
both regime transitions with a registered newborn (the leftover chunk
never cut, a walkable hole throughout, its accounting flushed by the
next collection and by the slow path); chunk accounting flushed by a
collection.

Gates: make test, test-gc-stress, test-memleak rc 0; CL_NO_GENGC+CL_NO_TLAB
and DEBUG_GC+DEBUG_GC_STRESS configs green; bench-opt vs step 3
interleaved min-of-3: every row within +-1 ms (total 897 -> 894);
m68k .text 804440 -> 804820 (+380 B); FS-UAE fresh 5283/5284 (the known
audio flake) + restored image 5274/5274, identical to step 3.

events.title: gc: the Immix-style mark-region backend on the seam (make host GC=immix)
events.message:
gc: the Immix-style mark-region backend on the seam (make host GC=immix)

Part 2 of specs/gc-backend-immix.md.  src/core/gc_immix.c implements
gc_backend.h: one byte per 128-byte line, stamped by the trace
(GCB_ON_MARK, exact) and zeroed by an O(lines) sweep; allocation claims
the next run of available lines as the thread's chunk cursor and cuts
lock-free; the mark bit's sense flips per cycle (gc_hdr_xor) so nothing
in a cycle is proportional to dead space.  The shared compactor stays the
rare defragmentation and the image-save path.

Three deviations from the spec text, recorded there under "As landed":
no block table or hole-start flag (the line map is the only allocator
state), the header chain is kept exact at the claim (the dead block
before a hole is truncated, the one straddling its end is split) instead
of clipped in every walk, and dead blocks carry CL_TYPE_DEAD so the
conservative JIT scan and the finalizers can refuse them.  The scan now
runs after the precise trace with object-start validation on every push,
since a corpse sharing a line with a live object reads unmarked on every
other cycle.

Shared code: GCB_HDR_* replaces every raw mark-bit access outside the
collector (tests/test_gc_mark_macros.sh is the lint), GCB_MAKE_HDR gives
newborns the current sense, the compactor's sub-header gaps are tagged
dead, %GENGC-STATS / %GC-MINOR exist on every build.  Classic m68k .text
+168 bytes, cl_alloc untouched.

make test-gc-stress GC=immix adds a mixed regime
(CLAMIGA_GC_STRESS_IMMIX=8: seven line-sweep cycles per compaction) that
sees a bug class classic gc-stress cannot: a value held unprotected
across an allocating call after it was allocated never moves on a dense
heap, but the cycles scatter fresh objects into holes and the next
compaction moves them.  Its first run found two, fixed here with
regression coverage in that regime: (setf gethash) returned its value
unrooted across the bucket-vector rehash, and %ffi-stub-info passed its
plist in the same argument list as a keyword intern (tests/gc_arg_order.pl
now also matches *intern* / *_keyword helpers).

Tests: tests/test_gc_immix.c (claims and cuts, cycle and hole reuse,
spanner truncation, straddler split, hole selection, large runs, sense
flip, finalization once, list across compaction and adoption, re-init,
fragmentation-forced compaction, storage error);
scan_traces_a_corpse_without_marking_interiors in test_jit_gc_scan.c;
classic-only tests tagged CL_GC_CLASSIC.

events.title: test(gc_threaded): re-run package + symbol init after every heap re-init
events.message:
test(gc_threaded): re-run package + symbol init after every heap re-init

Under a DEBUG_GC (+DEBUG_GC_STRESS) unit-test build the file aborted
deterministically in error_unwind_restores_gc_roots_nested:

  [GC-BADMARK] gc_mark_push(0x00004a70): implausible object start
    (type=0 size=0 bump=0x00010218)
    parent @0x00010208 type=9 size=16      (a CONDITION)

Not a collector bug.  The file re-inits the heap mid-process at 18 sites
(cl_mem_shutdown + cl_mem_init) without re-running cl_package_init /
cl_symbol_init, so the arena the packages and boot symbols lived in is
freed while the SYM_* / KW_* globals keep their old offsets.  The first
cl_error after that stores SYM_SIMPLE_ERROR (== 0x4a70, confirmed in lldb)
as the condition's type_name; the condition is rooted through the thread's
last_condition slot, and the next mark walks the stale offset into zeroed
arena.  Only DEBUG_GC's plausibility guard sees it — release and gc-stress
builds silently OR a mark bit into whatever spans that offset and pass.

reinit_heap(size) now does shutdown + init + package init + symbol init and
replaces every re-init pair (reinit_classic/reinit_default included), the
contract main() and tests/test_gc_immix.c already follow.
shared_tables_reset_on_heap_reinit keeps its raw cl_mem_init — its asserts
are about what cl_mem_init itself clears — and re-runs the two inits right
after them.

Verified: DEBUG_GC+DEBUG_GC_STRESS 3x 24/24, classic 24/24, immix 22/22,
make test green.

gc: split mem.c into heap core + collector translation units (seam step 1)

Phase 1, step 1 of specs/gc-backend-immix.md: the mechanical split.
mem.c (6,913 lines) becomes

  mem.c          arena, cl_alloc fast path, TLAB, constructors, root
                 stacks, registered roots, init/shutdown, stats
  gc_trace.c     mark stack, gc_mark_obj, root enumeration (value form),
                 overflow re-scan, srcloc hooks, dead-object finalizers
  gc_classic.c   gc_sweep, cl_gc + stop-the-world wrappers, the whole
                 CL_GENGC section
  gc_compact.c   forwarding bitmap/page table, slot-form root walk,
                 slide, rehash, cl_gc_compact
  gc_jitscan.c   conservative JIT native-stack scan, block-start index
  gc_verify.c    DEBUG_GC verifiers, root audit, ext:%heap-verify
  gc_internal.h  the formerly-static state and entry points the files
                 share, plus the GC_WALK_OBJ_CHILDREN X-macro

Pure move: every function body is byte-identical to the one-file
mem.c (checked by script); the only edits are `static` dropped from
the symbols that now cross a file boundary and the forward
declarations gc_internal.h makes redundant.  alloc_from_bump /
alloc_from_free_list stay in mem.c beside their only callers so the

events.title: gc: one root walk in slot-visitor form (seam step 2)
events.message:
gc: one root walk in slot-visitor form (seam step 2)

The roots were enumerated twice: gc_mark_thread_roots + the shared half
of gc_mark (value form, gc_mark_obj(x)) and gc_update_thread_roots +
gc_update_shared_roots + gc_update_registered_roots (slot form, *slot =
gc_forward(*slot)), kept in step by comments saying "mirror of the mark
phase".  Now gc_trace.c enumerates the root slots once —
gc_visit_thread_roots / gc_visit_registered_roots / gc_visit_shared_roots
— and gc_mark instantiates the walk with "mark the value", the compactor
with "forward in place".  A slot the walk skips is neither kept alive nor
rewritten; one it visits is both.  The module-side holders (compiler
chain, VM extra args, FASL readers/writers/MLF) became visit walkers
too; their mark twins are gone.

Two places where the twins differed are settled on the forwarding side:
the compiler env chain is walked once per compiler (the marker used to
re-walk every ancestor env per descendant), and readtable slots are
visited unconditionally (both visitors ignore NIL).

The registered-root dedup no longer keeps its own list of "independently
forwarded" ranges — it runs the thread + shared walks once more with a
probe visitor that flags every registered address they visit, so the
alias set IS the walk and cannot drift from it; root_slot_independently_
forwarded (the audit and the no-memory fallback) probes the same way.
That also covers a CL_GC_PROTECT of a thread scalar or a table global,
which the range list never did: tests/test_gc_roots.c protects
CT->pending_tag and compacts, and on the step-1 tree the slot came back
as an unrelated object.  The rest of that file pins the contract: every
root slot once, the stale words (nlx mv_values, pre_call_mv_values,
pending_mv_values beyond the count) never, no address visited twice.

Gates: make test, test-gc-stress, test-memleak; DEBUG_GC+DEBUG_GC_STRESS
and CL_NO_GENGC+CL_NO_TLAB builds; m68k cross (.text 806004 -> 804268);
bench-opt neutral (min of 3, interleaved vs step 1, every row within
2 ms); FS-UAE test-amiga 5283/5284 (the audio flake) + restored
5274/5274.

events.title: gc: Immix on the m68k builds, the GC= knob in Makefile.cross/Makefile.mos, and the default decided (Phase 3)
events.message:
gc: Immix on the m68k builds, the GC= knob in Makefile.cross/Makefile.mos, and the default decided (Phase 3)

Phase 3 of specs/gc-backend-immix.md.  `GC=immix|classic` now selects
the collector in Makefile.cross and Makefile.mos the way it does in the
host Makefile, and the m68k cross build defaults to Immix: `build/cross/`
is the Immix binary, `GC=classic` builds to `build/cross-classic/`
(composing with FPU=1/WIDE=1 as cross-fpu-classic etc.).  The object-dir
suffix names the NON-default backend so make-binary-release.sh and every
helper that knows build/cross keep working; make does not track CFLAGS,
so switching a default needs one `make -f Makefile.cross clean`.  The
MorphOS default stays classic (GC=immix -> build/morphos-immix/) until a
native run — the box was off.

The numbers behind the default (docs/gc-phase0-results.md "Phase 3",
both binaries built the same afternoon, measured with the new
verify/realamiga/run-gc-phase0.sh BINDIR [CONFIG], which runs
trunk/gc-phase0.lisp bare and with Clamacs loaded in FS-UAE through the
boot-override hook):

  FS-UAE 68040: churn mutator 936 -> 293 us/step bare, 1503 -> 346 with
  the editor loaded (3.1x / 4.3x); per-cycle wall flat at 1.5-2.3 s
  against 5.7-8.8 s in classic's free-list phase; sweep 0-20 ms per
  cycle against 120-140; mark unchanged on a quiet heap.
  FS-UAE 68020 (cycle-exact): 30.6 -> 9.4 ms/step bare, 26.3 -> 11.4
  loaded; cycles 63-74 s flat against 83 s once and 168-323 s
  thereafter; sweep 0.2 s against 4.8 s.
  The mark is 10-30 % slower under Immix on the 020 (the per-object line
  stamp) — the mark-loop pass stays the next lever for the idle-editor
  pause, which Immix leaves where it was.  The sliding compactor is 4-5x
  slower on an Immix heap (it walks every un-coalesced corpse); the
  policy asked for none in any churn run.  Binary +3.4 KB.

Gates under Immix on the 68040 config are identical to classic (both
binaries rebuilt from this tree): fresh 5284/5285 (the one failure is
the FS-UAE audio flake), restored 5275/5275, every image / executable /
stack / Workbench leg.  test-amiga-lowend cannot finish
inside its 30-minute hard timeout for either backend; the Immix run was
at 2712 passes and no failure when the watchdog ended it.

One multi-threading bug in the Immix backend, found by
test_mt_dispatch_addmethod_race under `make test GC=immix` (crashes and
"CDR: argument is not of type LIST" in two runs of six, never under
classic): a claim walks the header chain on the LIVE heap — under
alloc_mutex, but a hole's neighbour can be another thread's chunk, whose
owner rewrites its headers lock-free on every cut — and cl_alloc zeroed
the whole block, header word included, before storing the object's
header.  A claim walking through a peer's chunk could read a zero header
or, on a weakly-ordered host, the new object header followed by the
stale bytes where the remainder header had not landed yet, follow a
garbage size, and truncate a header inside the peer's live objects.
Fix: alloc_zero keeps the header word (the slot always holds a header
that covers the block), and the Immix gcb_cursor_cut orders the
remainder-header store before the object-header store with a barrier
when threads are live (a compiler barrier on the single-core m68k).
tests/test_gc_threaded.c claims_vs_concurrent_cuts fails every run
without either half of the fix and passes with it.

ROOM now ends with the collector's own lines (gcb_stats_report takes a
writer so WITH-OUTPUT-TO-STRING captures them): the free list's shape
and probe count for classic, the line map, holes claimed, cycles and
policy compactions for Immix; trunk/gc-phase0.lisp prints them after
each section.  tests/test_cross_wide_knob.sh covers the GC knob and
clears MAKEFLAGS and the knob variables for its dry-run sub-make (`make
test GC=immix` hands them to every sub-make, and the test is about
Makefile.cross's own defaults).

Gates on this tree: make test + test-memleak + test-gc-stress, classic
and GC=immix, all green; FS-UAE 68040 test-amiga for both backends with
the rebuilt binaries, counts above.

Open: the Vampire and the MorphOS box have not run Immix; the Clamacs
typing-latency spike was not taken; the first 68020 loaded-churn
measurement wedged in its third cycle (the shape of the known FS-UAE
wedge) and the re-run with the same binary finished — its numbers are
the recorded ones.

events.title: gc: one arena iterator for every header-chain walk (seam step 3)
events.message:
gc: one arena iterator for every header-chain walk (seam step 3)

Phase 1 Unification B of specs/gc-backend-immix.md.  The eighteen
hand-written `while (ptr < end) { size = CL_HDR_SIZE(ptr); if (!size)
break; ...; ptr += size; }` loops across the collector, image.c and the
shutdown path now step through one iterator:

    GcWalk w; uint32_t off, size; uint8_t type;
    gc_walk_begin(&w);
    while (gc_walk_next(&w, &off, &size, &type)) ...

mem.h: GcWalk / gc_walk_begin / gc_walk_next / gc_walk_seek /
gc_walk_complete, static inline — the passes it serves are the O(arena)
loops and the m68k build has no LTO; the struct's address never escapes
to an out-of-line call, so the cursor stays in registers like the old
ptr/end locals (m68k gc_sweep shrinks by 8 bytes).  The cursor advances
before the body sees a block, so a body may rewrite the header it was
handed; the sweep re-seeks past the block it coalesced.

A header the walk cannot step over ends it with gc_walk_complete() false.
A release build truncates the pass as before; DEBUG_GC / DEBUG_GC_STRESS
builds also reject an unaligned size, a block crossing the walk end and
an impossible type tag, and gc_walk_broken (mem.c) names the header and
aborts instead of letting the pass sweep or slide garbage.  The image
relink walk keeps its own alignment/type check with image_fatal and
reports an incomplete walk the same way.

Converted: forwarding, reference update, slide, rehash, the gen-mode
mark clear and the DEBUG_GC hash-chain audit (gc_compact.c); the sweep
(gc_classic.c); the mark-overflow rescan (gc_trace.c); the post-mark and
post-sweep verifiers (gc_verify.c); the JIT scan's no-index fallback and
its index cross-check (gc_jitscan.c); the image adopter's two
normalisations and the shutdown off-heap release (mem.c); the save
preconditions, bytecode census, blob writer and relink walk (image.c).
Deliberately left raw: cl_gc_verify_heap's pass 1 (it is the chain check
and must report, not abort), cl_gc_audit_hdr_index, the gen-mode
page-bounded walks from the crossing map, and the sweep's inner coalesce.

tests/test_gc_walk.c: contiguity from CL_ALIGN to the bump front with
every block's header, free blocks and a bare sub-header gap as blocks,
the dense chain after a compaction, seek, and the broken-header stop
(release builds only; the debug builds abort there by design).

Gates: make test, test-gc-stress, test-memleak; DEBUG_GC+DEBUG_GC_STRESS
build smoke; CL_NO_GENGC+CL_NO_TLAB build with test_gc_walk 6/6,
test_gc_compact 18/18, test_gc_hdr_index 5/5, test_gc_roots 9/9; m68k
.text 804268 -> 804440 (+172 B); bench-opt vs step 2 interleaved min of
3 within 3 ms on every row; FS-UAE test-amiga 5283/5284 (the known
audio flake) + restored image 5274/5274.

events.title: gc: the mark-loop pass — mark at the visit, leaf skip, inline visit, per-walk context
events.message:
gc: the mark-loop pass — mark at the visit, leaf skip, inline visit, per-walk context

The "next lever" Phase 0 and Phase 3 both ended at: on a quiet heap the
pause is the mark, and neither the free list nor Immix's line sweep
touches it.  The 68020 disassembly of the Phase 3 binary (-Os) showed
why the mark was slow: every slot of the per-type walk was a CALL into
the push helper with four tag tests before it, and every popped object a
second call into the walk — about 110 instructions per cons, the ~55 us
per object Phase 0 measured.  The line stamp was a minor part.

The trace (src/core/gc_trace.c, shared by every backend), restructured:

- An object is marked when a reference to it is VISITED, not when it is
  popped.  gc_mark_visit (always inline) filters the immediates with one
  test, loads the header, skips a marked object, sets the mark, runs the
  backend hook, and queues the object only if its type has children
  (GC_TYPE_HAS_CHILDREN, a bit set over the type tag: strings, floats,
  bignums, bit/byte vectors, random states, foreign pointers never enter
  the stack).  gc_mark_drain pops with no check at all, walks the cons
  inline and every other type through gc_mark_children.
- The overflow protocol keeps its shape: an object the full stack cannot
  take is marked-but-unscanned (before: unmarked and dropped) and the
  full-arena re-scan, which scans every marked object, reaches its
  children.  gc_mark_obj stays the root entry; gc_mark_drain is the one
  drain (gc_mark and the generational minor in gc_classic.c).
- GcMarkCtx (gc_internal.h, GCB_MARK_CTX_* / GCB_*_C in gc_backend.h):
  the arena base and size, the stack, its top and capacity, and the
  backend's words — for Immix the mark sense, the epoch, the line map,
  the live byte count and the validation flag, all constant for the
  trace — are loaded once per drain or children walk and kept in locals.
  The queue's slow path (grow or drop) works on the globals so the
  context never has its address taken and the compiler scalarises it;
  on the 68020 that is a register instead of an absolute-address load
  for every operand of the visit.
- Immix: im_stamp_lines stamps a one-line object with a single store.

trunk/gc-mark-bench.lisp is the measurement (a synthetic live set, five
explicit collections, the mark phase per cycle); run-gc-phase0.sh takes
SCRIPT= to run any such file in FS-UAE.  Cycle-exact 68020, 2.1 MB live,
mark per cycle: classic 5,444 -> 1,648 ms (3.3x), Immix 7,624 -> 2,768 ms
(2.75x; the steps were 4,080 after the trace, 3,720 after the stamp,
2,768 after the context).  Host, 32 MB live: classic 11.3 -> 6.6 ms,
Immix 13.2 -> 8.5 ms (the context is invisible at -O3).  m68k text
+6 KB classic / +12 KB Immix.  docs/gc-phase0-results.md "Mark-loop
pass" and the spec's "As landed — the mark-loop pass" have the tables.

tests/test_gc_markstack.c pins the two new invariants: a wide vector of
strings grows the mark stack by nothing (fails on the old trace), and
under a capped stack the strings held by the dropped conses survive a
sweep and a compaction.

Gates on the final tree: make test and make test GC=immix, test-gc-stress
on both backends, test-memleak on both; FS-UAE 68040 test-amiga fresh
5284/5285 (the audio flake), restored 5275/5275, all image/exe/WB legs.

events.title: fix: steady stick mouse speed and better Android audio defaults (#2440)
events.message:
fix: steady stick mouse speed and better Android audio defaults (#2440)

* fix(input): keep the stick mouse moving and honour its speed setting

The analog mouse map fed setmousestate() from SDL axis events. SDL only
reports axis changes, so a held stick stopped the pointer and its speed
followed the controller's report rate; "Analog joy-mouse speed" had no
effect. The left stick is now mapped to the port 0 mouse axes and goes
through the core analog joy-mouse path, so the speed slider and joy-mouse
dead zone apply and a held stick keeps moving. Libretro keeps its own
per-frame routing.

Amiberry's default analog joy-mouse speed is now 25 (WinUAE uses 100,
which is too fast for the stick mouse).

Also:
- combine all joystick hats into the D-pad so centering one hat no longer
  releases directions held on another
- clarify which GUI setting controls which pointer
- repair tests/test_osk_input.py, broken since the libretro OSK change,
  and drop the source-text mouse map check

* fix(android): let SDL3 use AAudio for audio output

The OpenSL ES driver was forced while the Android port used SDL2, whose
AAudio backend had latency and noise bugs. SDL3 fixed those, and AAudio is
available on every Android version we support (minSdk 29). SDL3 now picks
AAudio in low-latency mode and falls back to OpenSL ES only if AAudio
fails to start.

* feat(android): add an analog mouse speed slider to the launcher

Android users can now set the stick mouse speed from the Input tab, next
to "Left Analog Stick as Mouse", without opening the in-emulator GUI. It
writes input.joymouse_speed_analog using the same steps as the emulator's
"Analog joy-mouse speed" slider (5-150, default 25).

* fix(android): default to 48 kHz and a larger sound buffer

Android mixes at 48 kHz, so 44.1 kHz output is resampled and loses
AAudio's low-latency path. The old 3072 buffer gave ~17 ms chunks and only
35-52 ms of queued audio, which Android scheduling stalls can drain.

On Android only, the defaults are now 48000 Hz and sound_max_buff 8192
(~43 ms chunks). Desktop defaults are unchanged so slower hosts such as
the Raspberry Pi 4 do not pay for the extra samples.

The launcher's Sound tab gets a Sound buffer setting that writes
sound_max_buff on every launch. Launcher configs that never stored the
key get 8192 even when amiberry.conf still holds the old 3072 default;
configs that already store a value keep it.

* fix(android): keep the analog mouse speed with the other controller settings

The speed was dropped wherever the launcher carries controller settings
across a rebuild: switching Amiga model, QuickStart and WHDLoad snapshots,
the remembered-controls fallback for configs without the key, and the
launch overrides. Each of those now carries it next to the mouse map
flags, and launch passes it explicitly so a backing config's stored
speed cannot override the slider.

* fix(android): keep valid sound buffer and mouse speed values from configs

The launcher snapped both settings to its own UI steps, so importing a
config silently rewrote values the emulator accepts: sound_max_buff=0
(the in-emulator "Min") became 1024, and a speed set by the mouse speed
hotkeys (2, for example) became 5. Constraints now only replace invalid
values (negative buffers, non-positive speeds). The Sound Buffer
dropdown gains "Min", and the speed slider shows the nearest step for
an off-step value without changing it.

* fix(input): stop a 100% joy-mouse dead zone from dividing by zero

With input.joymouse_deadzone at 100, the analog mouse, lightpen and paddle
branches subtracted the dead zone from the full range and divided by the
result, which is zero. A full-deflection stick on a Mouse Map or Mouse
mode port crashed x86 builds with SIGFPE. A dead zone covering the whole
range now leaves those inputs neutral.

* fix(input): step the mouse speed hotkeys from any current speed

The analog mouse speed hotkeys looked the current speed up in their step
table {2, 5, 10, 20, 40}. A speed outside the table, such as the new
default of 25, was not found, so "down" jumped to 40 and "up" fell to 2.
The hotkeys now move to the next lower or higher step from whatever the
current speed is, and still wrap at either end.

This also drops the file-scope globals the old code used (int i,
mousespeed, num_elements). inputdevice_devicechange() had been using
that global i as its loop counter, and now declares its own.

The remote watch commands match exact 1, 2 or 4 byte accesses, or ranges
of DMA accesses, and none of them watch instruction fetches. Console
watchpoints can do both through the existing memwatch nodes.

to 64 KiB and matches any overlapping access like a console watchpoint.

"range":true; they share removal and the access log with watch add.

events.message:
M14.1: removals hold against analyzers, and four smaller contract fixes (D36)

- A user or LLM removal (remove-symbol, unclassify, unreference) writes a
  suppression that blocks the place for every analyzer; imports skip it and
  count it as suppressed. A write at the place or a revert lifts it.
  `suppressions` lists them; at/history/revision show them. Schema v2.
- c64_memmap says truncated and next when it cuts at maxRanges; the
  unpacker reads on from next instead of splitting windows.
- remove on c64_breakpoint/c64_watchpoint returns {removed: true, id}.
- A scenario autostart returns only when the program runs, so a type step
  right after it reaches the program (live test reproduced the lost key).
- analyze lists up to --max-listed (default 50) with counts and a pointer.
- Host protocol version 3.

project.title: Castle Excellent NES source reconstruction
project.display_title: Castle Excellent / Castlequest NES source reconstruction
project.status: Source reviewed; independent build and runtime untested
project.notes: Identity: README and revision manifest identify Castle Excellent (Japan/HSP-05) and Castlequest (USA) as supported profiles of one CNROM reconstruction. Both exact ROM identities and separate private asset paths are specified. Source 2.0 is described as released and 2.1 as an active compatible candidate in README, while the pinned head commit says it completes 2.1; no release/tag status is inferred from that wording. Classification: The project reconstructs address-ordered semantic 6502/ca65 source from reference-ROM analysis and adds level, graphics and sound authoring tools. The documented pipeline uses Ghidra/GhidraNes static facts, pointer/control-flow evidence and FCEUX code/data logs to separate code from typed data, then rebuilds iNES images. The editors and two revision profiles remain one game reconstruction. Source CPU: The pipeline explicitly analyzes 6502 instructions from the original CNROM PRG; the shared source entrypoint selects .setcpu 6502. NES cartridge/header/mapper evidence establishes the original platform while preserving the directly evidenced ISA label. Target CPU: ca65/ld65 regenerate native 6502 iNES images with one fixed 32 KiB PRG and four switchable 8 KiB CHR banks. Windows x64/PowerShell is the documented release host, and Python/Java operate the research/build pipeline; none are substituted for the console target CPU. Build: README requires Python 3, GNU Make and legally obtained reference ROMs; pinned ca65/ld65 binaries are included, while Ghidra/GhidraNes and the automation emulator are bootstrapped/verified separately. Original ROMs, extracted CHR/data and outputs are ignored, so a public clone cannot produce the complete game without private inputs. Documentation claims byte-identical builds and detailed static/runtime gates, but this pass ran none. Original game rights remain with their owners; the source does not grant a blanket license over them, and no project-wide license was found. The separately credited room extractor is explicitly not bundled because its licensing was unclear. Limitations: No compilation, reference-ROM acquisition, emulator scenario, gameplay or byte identity check was performed. All build flags remain null despite upstream claims. Runtime profiles: The inspected configuration specifies mapper 3/CNROM, fixed PRG and banked CHR image layout and documentation describes FCEUX scenarios. Cartridge ROM capacities and tested emulator/Windows host setup are not console RAM or minimum-host requirements, so no minimum runtime profile is encoded. AI: The pinned latest commit explicitly names Codex in its Co-Authored-By trailer. This supports usage=true and the tool label Codex only; the OpenAI email domain is not treated as a separate tool, and no model/version is inferred. File naming or elaborate manifests are not the attribution basis. Relationships: The provenance document credits wizzard2010/cex room analysis as research evidence rather than imported code and distinguishes machado2/castle for MSX as a different game/platform used only for conceptual comparison. Those linked roots were screened locally and left unreviewed in this bounded lane. Castle Excellent and Castlequest share PRG source and remain one record; no existing title/subject alias was found. Evidence: https://github.com/oranguthang/castle_excellent_src/blob/72e08e0346712fdfdbfd6f02ed996d138bf0a321/README.md https://github.com/oranguthang/castle_excellent_src/blob/72e08e0346712fdfdbfd6f02ed996d138bf0a321/config/revision_profiles.json https://github.com/oranguthang/castle_excellent_src/commit/72e08e0346712fdfdbfd6f02ed996d138bf0a321 https://github.com/oranguthang/castle_excellent_src/blob/72e08e0346712fdfdbfd6f02ed996d138bf0a321/docs/disassembly_pipeline.md https://github.com/oranguthang/castle_excellent_src/blob/72e08e0346712fdfdbfd6f02ed996d138bf0a321/docs/verification.md https://github.com/oranguthang/castle_excellent_src/blob/72e08e0346712fdfdbfd6f02ed996d138bf0a321/src/main.asm https://github.com/oranguthang/castle_excellent_src/blob/72e08e0346712fdfdbfd6f02ed996d138bf0a321/config/linker/cnrom.cfg https://github.com/oranguthang/castle_excellent_src/blob/72e08e0346712fdfdbfd6f02ed996d138bf0a321/docs/provenance.md

* Support non-AUTOINIT disk libraries and MakeLibrary/AddLibrary/InitStruct/MakeFunctions

OpenLibrary can now load an NT_LIBRARY Resident without RTF_AUTOINIT by
calling rt_Init directly (as InitResident does), recovering a self-added
library by name if init returns NULL. Adds guest-callable MakeLibrary,
MakeFunctions, InitStruct (full initializers.i interpreter, also applied
to AUTOINIT tables) and AddLibrary, and makes close/expunge safe for
libraries that own their base.

events.title: Address review: snapshot compatibility, weave scan match, write retry
events.message:
Address review: snapshot compatibility, weave scan match, write retry

The render snapshot's hard-stop flag now holds only the BEAMCON0 half of
the rule, but 1.0 states recorded `harddis` as the whole rule, true on
every AGA machine. Store the new meaning under its own serde-default key
so an old state leaves `harddis` unread instead of restoring an A1200
frame with the $D8 stop lifted.

Weave two native fields only when they share the vertical scan too: the
same row-0 beam line, and rows and frame length within the one line a
long field adds, so a video-standard or programmable-scan change between
them starts a new picture.

Advance the menu write-through baseline only after the saved default was
written, so a failed write is retried by the next change rather than
counted as saved.

events.title: Address the Copilot review findings on PR #773
events.message:
Address the Copilot review findings on PR #773

Bound sample-set decoding before it allocates: a member must declare
1-192 kHz and run at most 60 s, checked from the WAV header. The 64 MiB
file cap alone did not bound the resampled output, which grows as the
declared rate shrinks (a small file claiming 1 Hz would resample to
trillions of samples).

List a set in the launcher by any of its member files, not only its
click, so a motor-only set (which loads fine) can be picked.

Carry each peer's drive sample sets onto the machine desktop netplay
stages from the session bundle, alongside the audio sink. The bundle
never holds a set, so host, guests and spectators all fell back to the
synthesized sounds for the session.

Document [audio] floppy_sounds as the switch for all drive sounds: off
silences them even with a floppy_sounds_set.

events.title: Ship ShowTasks and WatchTasks from third_party/shelltools
events.message:
Ship ShowTasks and WatchTasks from third_party/shelltools

third_party/shelltools (github.com/tinic/shelltools) is a submodule.
src/tools builds it as an ExternalProject with the pinned toolchain
file: shelltools' own CMakeLists keeps its flags and -Werror, MinSizeRel
as in its presets, and SHELLTOOLS_CPU follows AMINETXDUO_CPU (68020-60
for fat, 68000 otherwise).  SHELLTOOLS_VERSION_SUFFIX=" AmiNetXDuo
<version>" puts the name in each $VER: tag, which make-dist's marker
check and the installer's P_is_ours read.  The install step copies the
two binaries into src/tools and strips them one at a time, because the
pinned m68k-amigaos-strip segfaults when it gets two hunk files at once.

make-dist ships both in C/ and C/fat through CMDS; the installer's C/
and C/fat copies, backup loop and uninstall record already cover them.
The CLI inventory gets policy entries for both, and matrix.py reads a
ReadArgs template without the (CONST_STRPTR) cast.  The guide documents
both commands; the ReadMe and the installer's command help name them;
run-workbench.sh runs ShowTasks after the install and reports its rc.

The submodule pin is the head of tinic/shelltools#2 until it merges.
