events.title: port: keep the tick below the disk handlers; 2 ms Forbid budget
events.message:
port: keep the tick below the disk handlers; 2 ms Forbid budget

The ThreadX tick task ran at Exec priority 20, equal to input.device, and
a tick service could hold Forbid() for up to 16 ms of catch-up.

- TX_AMIGA_TIMER_PRIORITY 20 -> 9: above console.device, trackdisk.device
  and IDE drivers (5-6), below the filesystem handlers and disk drivers
  (10+) and input.device (20).
- TX_AMIGA_TIMER_BUDGET_MS 16 -> 2: the first tick of a service always
  runs, the rest of the backlog carries over; TX_AMIGA_TIMER_MAX_CATCHUP
  is unchanged.
- TCP: handler and session processes stay at 5, now named
  AMI_EXEC_TCP_PRIORITY.
- src/thread_priorities.h documents the Exec ladder and asserts it at
  compile time.

events.title: Add CYL.SIDE track display and WinUAE-format floppy sound sets
events.message:
Add CYL.SIDE track display and WinUAE-format floppy sound sets

Track display: [display] track_display = "cylinder" shows the status
bar's floppy counter as cylinder and side (track 81 reads 40.1) with a
lit decimal point, so the first figure moves with every head step and
the last digit is the /SIDE line the guest selected. Switchable live
from Video Settings -> Track Display and from the launcher's Display
page; "track" stays the default.

Floppy sound sets: [audio] floppy_sounds_set plays a WinUAE/FS-UAE
drive sample set (drive_{click,spin,spinnd,startup,snatch}_NAME.wav)
instead of the synthesized sounds. A bare name is looked up in the new
"Floppy Sounds" host-data folder; a path names one of the set's files
or its folder plus the name. Playback follows WinUAE's driveclick
player so sets sound as they do there: 0x6FF0-marked clicks per
cylinder, half of each slice played, snatch on the first spin-up after
an insert, start-up from a standstill, click and motor averaged per
drive and across drives. A missing set warns and falls back to the
synthesized sounds. The launcher's Audio page lists installed sets, and
the UAE config importer maps floppyNsound/floppyNsoundext and FS-UAE's
floppy_drive_N_sounds.

The floppy controller now reports each audible step with its drive and
landing cylinder, plus disk inserts and ejects. These pending events
are serialized (the old step counter's key is retired, so older states
still load): a state captured between an insert or step and the next
floppy tick must replay it. Which set a drive plays is host
configuration (serde-skipped, adopted across restores); what it plays
is a pure function of a serialized per-drive mechanism record that
evolves identically with or without a set, and the synthesizer keeps
running for every drive (muted in the mix for a sampled one). So save
states, run-ahead and netplay checksums do not depend on which sets are
installed.
events.author: LinuxJedi

events.title: Apply the DDF hard-stop rule per BPLCON0 in the renderer
events.message:
Apply the DDF hard-stop rule per BPLCON0 in the renderer

The bus now lifts the $D8 stop for SHRES/UHRES from the BPLCON0 the
sequencer sees, but the render snapshot carried one hard-stop flag for
the whole frame, so a frame whose resolution changed after the wrap
could derive a different fetch width on the two sides. Put the rule in
agnus::ddf_hard_stop_lifted, record only its frame-stable BEAMCON0 half
in the snapshot, and let each control segment apply the BPLCON0 half
from its own register; bus call sites that decide a fetch under an
explicit BPLCON0 use it too.

The retained laced field now copies captured rows into its existing
plane buffers instead of reallocating them each frame, and drops the
in-progress events of the frame that followed it, which a render of the
field when it was current never saw.
events.author: LinuxJedi

events.title: Weave both fields into native screenshots of laced screens
events.message:
Weave both fields into native screenshots of laced screens

A native (1:1) capture rendered only the current field, so a 640x512
hi-res interlaced screen saved as a 640x256 squashed image through
Cmd+Option+S, --native-screenshots and capture.screenshot native.

At each frame wrap the bus now retains the outgoing field when it was
laced, with private copies of its chip-RAM and captured-row snapshots
reused from frame to frame, so the capture side keeps reclaiming its own
buffers. render_native weaves that field with the current one when they
are the long and short halves of one picture on the same scan, long
field on the even rows, and crops to the union of both playfields.
Progressive frames drop the history, and resets and state loads clear it.

Add weave unit and laced-bus capture regressions and update the user and
control-protocol documentation.
events.author: LinuxJedi

events.title: Keep the hardwired $D8 DDF stop on AGA Alice
events.message:
Keep the hardwired $D8 DDF stop on AGA Alice

Alice was treated as if BEAMCON0.HARDDIS were always set, relaxing the
bitplane fetch stop from $D8 to $E0 on every AGA machine. A lo-res window
with DDFSTOP past $D8 then fetched one word per line more than on ECS, so
displays whose modulo assumes the clamped count sheared diagonally (the
Pacmania WHDLoad install on an A1200, DDFSTRT $28 / DDFSTOP $E0).

Alice keeps the stop exactly as an ECS Agnus does. Either relaxes it only
while BEAMCON0 selects HARDDIS or VARBEAMEN, or BPLCON0 selects SHRES or
UHRES, matching WinUAE's check_harddis rule (vAmiga's sequencer also
raises RHW at $D8 on AGA); OCS keeps it unconditionally.

Add the ddfprobe-agahwstop golden probe and unit regressions for the AGA
stop and each relaxing control, and document the rule in the timing model.
events.author: LinuxJedi

events.title: Keep launcher-less keys and remember menu settings across restarts
events.message:
Keep launcher-less keys and remember menu settings across restarts

The configuration screen rebuilt its config from its own fields on Run
and Save, dropping every key it has no row for: rewind and its budget
and interval, autofire, ports 3/4, clipboard sharing, screen centring,
recording clip settings, PCMCIA, ZZ9000, debug, RTC/battmem and serial
phonebook/session. A launcher-started machine and the saved default lost
them, even when written by hand. They are now carried from the config
the screen opened on, and dropped only where an edit made there leaves
the machine unable to take them (ports 3/4 without the adapter, RTC keys
with the clock off, a 68060-only key on another CPU, a PCMCIA card where
there is no slot or a host disk fills it).

Settings changed from the menu, a hotkey or the status bar were
session-only. They are now folded into the session's config, so the
configuration screen shows and saves them, and written through to the
saved default as they change: controller ports, joystick mode, autofire,
mouse sensitivity, rewind, run ahead, warp limit, floppy speed,
clipboard sharing and the video and audio settings. Only keys changed in
the session are written, through a temp file and rename, and a default
that does not parse is left alone. Settings that come from a config,
save state, the window or the host's run-ahead fallback are re-taken as
the baseline instead. Sessions started from --config, ./copperline.toml
or --factory, and headless captures, never write it.

The configuration screen no longer opens on factory settings without a
word when the config it is given fails validation: it shows the reason,
so Save default does not silently replace a default that needed one fix.

events.title: ConfigureNetInterface: the reference template; ALIASADDR/DELETEADDR
events.message:
ConfigureNetInterface: the reference template; ALIASADDR/DELETEADDR

Reference: INTERFACE/A,QUIET/S,ADDRESS/K,NETMASK/K,BROADCASTADDR/K,
DESTINATION=DESTINATIONADDR/K,METRIC/K/N,MTU/K/N,ALIASADDR/K,
DELETEADDR/K,ONLINE/S,OFFLINE/S,UP/S,DOWN/S,DEBUG/K,COMPLETE/K,
CONFIGURE/K,LEASE/K,RELEASE=RELEASEADDRESS/S,ID/K,TIMEOUT/K/N,
DHCPUNICAST/K

Ten of these failed ReadArgs, so a Roadshow multi-step script applied
nothing. The template is now the reference's, our keywords after it.

Alias addresses. NetX Duo holds one IPv4 address per NX_INTERFACE and
accepts, answers ARP for and replies from only that one, so an alias is
an NX_INTERFACE of its own in a free slot, named "<interface>:<slot>",
at a priority below every interface:
- sana2: ami_sana2_alias_driver_entry sends through the interface's
  AmiSana2If and makes no device call; ami_sana2_rx_deliver() hands an
  IPv4 datagram or ARP message addressed to an alias to the alias's
  NX_INTERFACE (one test of alias_count when there are none).
- netstack: netstack_interface_alias_add/_delete; an interface's
  aliases are detached before it is.
- bsdsocket: IFC_AddAliasAddress / IFC_DeleteAliasAddress in
  ConfigureInterfaceTagList(), as Roadshow defines them ("a.b.c.d" or
  "a.b.c.d/bits"; the interface's netmask by default). ENOSPC with no
  free slot, EEXIST for an address in use, EADDRNOTAVAIL for no such
  alias. NETSTATUS_IF_ALIAS marks an alias row; its counters stay with
  the interface's row.
A micro build (one slot) has no room for an alias and says so.

The other keywords do what the interface file's keyword does:
- DEBUG, LEASE, DHCPUNICAST, METRIC, DESTINATION: accepted, no effect
  (config_parse.c IF_INERT); YES/NO ones are checked.
- BROADCASTADDR: refused when it disagrees with ADDRESS/NETMASK.
- ID: offered as the host name (NETCTRL_HOSTNAME_SET); a stronger
  source keeping the name is not an error.
- COMPLETE=YES: IFC_Complete. Static routes already follow the
  interfaces, so there is nothing to reread.
- ADDRESS=DHCP, NETMASK=DHCP: CONFIGURE=DHCP.
- CONFIGURE=AUTO/FASTAUTO: RFC 3927 link-local, through the new
  NETCTRL_INTERFACE_AUTOIP (netstack_interface_autoip_start).
- TIMEOUT without DHCP is accepted; below 10 it is raised to 10.
- ONLINE that fails returns 5, as the reference documents.

events.title: Sort folder entries by base name, then extension
events.message:
Sort folder entries by base name, then extension

Folder entries were sorted by their whole names, so the dot of an
extension competed with the letters of longer names: "GAME 2.DSK" and
"GAME-B.DSK" sorted before "GAME.DSK", since space and hyphen come
before the dot. Names are now compared up to the dots of their
extensions first, and the extensions decide only between equal base
names, so that images of the same name with different extensions sort
together. A folder's name has no extension and is compared whole.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: display: Show image's file extension after its name, per show-filename-ext
events.message:
display: Show image's file extension after its name, per show-filename-ext

Images that differ only in their extension, such as a disk kept as .dsk
and as .hfe, show the same name on the LCD/OLED, and the type on the
status row is hidden by the track info once the image is mounted. The
new FF.CFG option show-filename-ext puts the extension after the name on
the name row, where it scrolls with it: "yes" always, "auto" only when
another image of the folder has the same name with another extension,
"no" never, which is the default and the behavior so far.

For "auto", the slot's image is compared with its two neighbors in the
sorted list in memory, since images of the same name sort together. In
a folder that is not sorted, "auto" acts as "yes", which costs no
directory pass. In the HxC modes, whose slots come from HXCSDFE.CFG,
"auto" works as "no", and "yes" works as expected.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

Διάλεξε: έτοιμοι κόσμοι στον δίσκο, ο κόσμος μένει ίδιος όσο κινείται η

- Το μενού είναι αρχείο: MENU.BIN (src/menu.asm, τα δεδομένα από το

events.title: Main Menu: Add "Save FLASH.DMP", dumping Flash config area at next mount
events.message:
Main Menu: Add "Save FLASH.DMP", dumping Flash config area at next mount

The option asks for a dump at the next mount of a drive, since none is
mounted while the main menu runs: the Flash area that holds the
configuration slots, FLASH_PAGE_SIZE bytes, goes to FLASH.DMP in the
folder of FF.CFG, overwriting an older file of that name, before FF.CFG
is read and can change Flash. So the dump shows what a Gotek has kept in
Flash, the slots no longer in use included. Before this, reading the
settings stored in flash needed a debugger connected to the MCU, or its
built-in ROM bootloader.

It costs 132 bytes of the flash memory in the STM32F105 shugart build.
events.author: mike-shevchenko

events.title: NetMeter: clock steps, startup input through the key path
events.message:
NetMeter: clock steps, startup input through the key path

nm_sample's interval came from two DateStamps cast to ULONG, so a clock
set back between samples (SNTP) read as about 49 days and froze the
session average for good.  nm_interval_ms gives 0 for a clock that went
back or jumped more than NM_INTERVAL_MAX (30 s) forward, and that
interval counts neither bytes nor time.

The console's input is read through nm_tui_keys (netmeter_tui.c), so
what the display does with a run of bytes -- quit, reset, pause, a
bounds reply, a resize -- is host-tested; after SetMode() anything
already readable is taken as keys before the first frame, and the
bounds wait is a quarter of a second.

A q typed ahead with the command still holds NetMeter until one more
key is pressed in the guest: not resolved by this change.

Host checks: typed-ahead q, Esc and other text before and with the
bounds reply, the bounds alone, reset/pause/resize, Ctrl-C; intervals
across a minute and midnight, clocks set back a second and a day,
forward past 30 s, an hour and years.

events.title: AddNetInterface: TIMEOUT 60, Workbench project icons, PRI order
events.message:
AddNetInterface: TIMEOUT 60, Workbench project icons, PRI order

Reference: INTERFACE/M,QUIET/S,TIMEOUT/K/N; "a default timeout value of
60 seconds", "cannot be shorter than ten seconds"; "create an icon for
your interface configuration file (it must be a project icon) and put
'AddNetInterface' into its default tool ... If things should go wrong,
you will see an error requester"; "tool types such as PRI=5 or
PRIORITY=5 ... Higher priority entries will appear before lower".

- TIMEOUT defaults to 60; 10 stays the floor. A DHCP server slower
  than 10 s no longer returns WARN before the lease arrives.
- Started from Workbench, every project in the WBStartup is an
  interface file (NameFromLock + name). Its icon's QUIET and TIMEOUT
  tool types are the arguments. Output goes to T:AddNetInterface.log
  (NIL: without T:), shown in an EasyRequest when the run did not
  succeed and QUIET was not given, then deleted.
- PRI/PRIORITY in each file's icon sorts the interfaces, highest
  first, then by name, from the Shell as well. A bare name's icon is
  looked for in DEVS:NetInterfaces, then SYS:Storage/NetInterfaces.
- ReadArgs results are copied by the pattern expansion already, so
  FreeArgs() now follows it and the later exits lose their copies.

SYS:Storage/NetInterfaces was already searched (config_list.c).

events.title: NetMeter: average carry, quit during the first bounds, frozen span
events.message:
NetMeter: average carry, quit during the first bounds, frozen span

nm_average checked the high word before multiplying, but the low
word's carry could still overflow the high product (hi 0x418937, lo
0xFFFFFFFF, ms 0xFFFFFFFF wrapped to 703); that addition is now
checked and saturates.

A q, Esc or Ctrl-C read while asking the console for its size was
consumed and ignored; nm_con_first_bounds now returns it and NetMeter
leaves at once, through the same console restore.

The session span is nm_span_add in netmeter_fmt.c: an interval that
would take the time past 0xFFFFFFFF ms counts neither its bytes nor its
time, so the average stays where it was, as the comment says.

Host checks: the carry case, the span's intervals, its carry and the
freeze.

events.title: ping, traceroute: the AmigaDOS Command Reference options
events.message:
ping, traceroute: the AmigaDOS Command Reference options

traceroute reference: -d=DEBUG/S,-m=MAXTTL/K/N,-n=NUMERIC/S,-p=PORT/K/N,
-q=QUERIES/K/N,-r=DONTROUTE/S,-s=SOURCE/K,-t=TOS/K/N,-v=VERBOSE/S,
-w=WAIT/K/N,HOST/A,PACKETSIZE/N
ping reference: -c=COUNT/K/N,-d=DEBUG/S,-i=INTERVAL/K/N,-l=LOAD/K/N,
-n=NUMERICONLY/S=NUMERIC/S,-q=QUIET/S,-R=RECORDROUTE/S,DONTROUTE/S,
-s=SIZE/K/N,-v=VERBOSE/S,BELL/S,HOST/A

traceroute: PACKETSIZE is positional (`traceroute host 100`); -d is
accepted and inert; -p and -s are accepted with a one-line warning (ICMP
probes; the route picks the source); -r refuses a host that is not on an
interface's subnet.

ping: -v lists every inbound ICMP message that is not an echo request or
reply; DONTROUTE refuses an off-link host as traceroute -r does; -d is
inert; -R warns (no IP options on a raw socket). DONTROUTE is IPv4 only
and warns for IPv6.

tool_on_link() in tool_diag.c is the shared DONTROUTE check:
bsdsocket.library has no SO_DONTROUTE.

events.title: NetMeter: the console average from byte deltas over measured time
events.message:
NetMeter: the console average from byte deltas over measured time

The session average added each sample's rate as if it were a second's
bytes while the time added the real interval, so a late sample
understated it; nm_average also cut the time to whole seconds.  Each
sample now keeps its byte deltas and whether they span an interval;
the console adds those deltas to a hi/lo count and that interval to
the time (saturating at 49.7 days), and nm_average divides
(hi:lo) * 1000 by the milliseconds exactly with 32-bit arithmetic
only, 0xFFFFFFFF when the quotient does not fit.

Host checks: unequal intervals, a fractional second, rounding down,
8 GiB, 16 GiB over an hour, 1 TiB over 49.7 days, the largest exact
average and both saturations.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: arp: the AmigaDOS Command Reference template
events.message:
arp: the AmigaDOS Command Reference template

Reference: -a=ALL/S,-d=DELETE/S,-s=SET/S,HOSTNAME,ADDRESS,TEMP/S,
PUB=PUBLISH/S,PRO=PROXY/S,-f=FILE/K,-n=NONAMES/S=NUMBERS/S

Every reference example failed on ours (`ARP ALL`, `ARP SET Oberon
00:30:ab:0e:d5:ee TEMP`, `ARP DELETE Oberon`, `arp -a`). The template
is now the reference's, with UNIT, STATS and QUIET after it; -n is
written -n=NONAMES=NUMBERS/S, since the reference's spelling puts
NUMBERS among the modifiers where ReadArgs never matches it.

- HOSTNAME is a name or a number; names go through the running
  stack's resolver (hosts, then DNS). ADDRESS is the hardware address.
- SET HOSTNAME ADDRESS [TEMP]: TEMP makes a dynamic entry
  (NETCTRL_F_TEMPORARY -> nx_arp_dynamic_entry_set); an older library
  ignores the flag and makes it permanent.
- FILE: one `<host> <ether_addr> [TEMP] [PUB]` per line; every line is
  tried, the worst rc returned.
- PUB/PROXY are refused (rc 10): the stack has no proxy ARP.
- -n is accepted; the listing is numeric already.
- Our old `arp <ip> SET <mac>` form is gone; the two harness lines that
  used it are updated.

events.title: NetMeter: a console mode when started from a Shell
events.message:
NetMeter: a console mode when started from a Shell

Started from a Shell whose output is a console window, NetMeter draws a
full-window display in that window, refreshed in place once a second:
per interface the link, addresses, device, RX and TX rate with a bar,
peak and session average, totals, packets, errors and drops, and a
history graph (receive above the middle line, send below).  From
Workbench, or with output that is not interactive (Run >NIL: NetMeter),
it opens the existing window; the ReadArgs template is unchanged.

The frame is console.device control sequences only (no curses): cursor
off, wrap and scroll off, the resize raw event and the window bounds
request, pens 0-3 so a 4-colour Workbench is enough.  One Write() per
frame.  Q, Esc or Ctrl-C quit and restore the console; R resets peaks,
averages and the graph; Space pauses the display.

netmeter_tui.c holds the frame and the input parser with no AmigaOS
calls; test_netmeter_fmt covers 80x25, 40x12, 20x4 and two-interface
frames through a model of console.device, the enter/leave sequences,
the bounds and resize reports and the new formatting helpers.

events.message:
debug: route remote guest input through shared input handlers

Add bounded raw key, mouse and joystick input with remote held-state
tracking, delivered through the shared input handlers. Schedule complete,
validated input sequences on emulated frame boundaries from the shared
input frame callback, keep input frozen during debugger stops, and

events.title: debug: add frame-start checkpoint save and restore
events.message:
debug: add frame-start checkpoint save and restore

State files are only valid at the start of a frame. A checkpoint save
therefore arms a one-shot break at line 0 using the existing cycle
breakpoint, raises the normal STATE_SAVE request there so vsync_do()
writes the file in the same hsync, and stops at the next instruction.
Any earlier stop cancels the request and the command fails. Unwritable
paths are rejected before resuming, since a failing save would be
retried every frame.

Defer restore replies until the normal CPU reset path completes. Retain
the GDB connection and stop at the restored CPU boundary while leaving
ordinary reset disconnection unchanged.

Clear remote debugger ownership before memory remapping and omit remote
watchpoints from saved console state. Reject incompatible devices, busy
filesystems and active input recording before starting a checkpoint.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: debug: add remote DMA watchpoints and watch predicates
events.message:
debug: add remote DMA watchpoints and watch predicates

Allocate remote DMA watchpoints independently of console and standard
GDB CPU entries. Validate source masks and ranges, and report the
triggering source and custom register in stop replies.

Add exact-width watchpoint predicates that reuse the existing memwatch
value masks and change detection, marked through a new memwatch_node
remote field so they match one complete bus access. Capture access
values, previous RAM values and source details from all remote entries
in a 64-entry ring with eviction counts. Log-only entries continue
checking later watchpoints without setting a stale stop reason.

events.title: Fix saved-game session serialization and reject invalid images
events.message:
Fix saved-game session serialization and reject invalid images

The decompiled .rcs writer assumed separately declared, overlapping globals
formed one disk record. Store the original 0x7f4-byte image in one typed object
and use typed profile, driver, setup, stage and unlock fields when saving and
restoring it. Validate the image before listing or applying it, preserve save
names during overwrite, and report file-write failures.

Add a differential regression against the original executable for 1-4 players,
all difficulties, stage boundaries, overwrite, write failures and malformed
sessions. Keep the original disk offsets under compile-time layout checks.

Validation: MSVC6 SP3 default build, full reccmp/relocated-byte audit and global
data comparison (0 issues), all 136 differential harnesses and the 108-case
saved-session regression. The full audit records 2920 exact functions and
444 non-exact functions, versus 2927/437 before the behavior fix. Perfect match
is 56.01%; fuzzy match is 94.41%. Matching regressions are intentional here:
validation and one-object storage change the instruction stream.

events.title: Patch chd onto ruzstd 0.9.1 for RUSTSEC-2026-0344
events.message:
Patch chd onto ruzstd 0.9.1 for RUSTSEC-2026-0344

ruzstd before 0.9.1 never bounds a block's decompressed size, so a
crafted zstd hunk in a CHD image under 128 KB can allocate gigabytes and
abort the process. cargo-deny now fails all four dependency-policy jobs
on it. chd 0.3.4, the latest release, requires ruzstd 0.8, and upstream
master does too, so no lockfile update can reach the fix.

Patch chd to the CopperlineHQ/chd-rs fork at the chd-v0.3.4 release
plus only the ruzstd bump (a0170de), in the root and in each standalone
workspace (player, web, libretro, fuzz), since [patch] applies only at a
workspace root, and allow the fork in deny.toml. Each lockfile changes
only chd's source and ruzstd 0.8.3 -> 0.9.1. The FrameDecoder API chd
uses is unchanged in 0.9, and ruzstd 0.9.1's rust-version (1.87) is
below Copperline's MSRV. The same bump is proposed upstream in
SnowflakePowered/chd-rs#23; drop the patch once a chd release carries it.

Verified by re-encoding a CD32 image with chdman -c cdzs: every hunk
passes its CRC and decodes identically under ruzstd 0.8.3 and 0.9.1,
tests/chd_cd.rs passes on both the original and the zstd image, and a
headless CD32 boot from either renders a byte-identical screenshot.

events.title: feat(android): offer RTG modes shaped like the device screen (#2436)
events.message:
feat(android): offer RTG modes shaped like the device screen (#2436)

* feat(android): offer RTG modes shaped like the device screen

None of the virtual RTG table entries has the shape of a phone or a tablet,
so an RTG screen shown full screen is always either stretched or left with
bars down the sides. Add heights of 480, 600, 800 and 1024, each as wide as
the device's own screen, so they fill it exactly with no aspect correction:
a 3200x2136 tablet gets 720x480, 896x600, 1200x800 and 1536x1024.

Widths are rounded to a multiple of 16, which Picasso96 wants, and shapes
narrower than 640 are dropped, since Picasso96 widens such a bitmap instead
and the screen then scrolls. The screen size comes from the desktop display
mode; either orientation gives the landscape shapes.

The builder is a pure helper in android_rtg_modes.h next to the table one,
covered by android_rtg_modes_test.cpp; addresolutions() emits both lists
through the same dedup path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(android): take the RTG screen shape from the cached display bounds

addresolutions() runs on the extended-trap thread, and SDL3 allows
SDL_GetDesktopDisplayMode() on the main thread only. Use the primary
display's bounds that enumeratedisplays() cached in Displays[] on the
main thread instead; they are in points, but only the shape matters.

Name the limit that leaves out shapes more than twice as tall as the
screen, say why, and cover it with an 854x480 case.

events.title: grm-w9ev.5: batch synthetic fixtures into shared analyzeHeadless runs
events.message:
grm-w9ev.5: batch synthetic fixtures into shared analyzeHeadless runs

About 70% of each fixture's ~4.7s was JVM/Ghidra startup (measured: bare
import 3.3s; 5 fixtures in one invocation 7.6s vs 23.5s separately).
run_one now queues plain imports and flush_batch imports the queue with one
analyzeHeadless and several -import args. Each fixture is then finished by the
same finish_fixture the unbatched path uses (carve, criteria, verdict, cache,
bless or golden diff), so the two paths cannot drift.

The queue flushes, in order, before any non-batchable call (pre/post-scripts,
GRM_KEY_INPUTS, GRM_NO_CACHE), a bless cache hit, run_reject, run_census, or
a step that reads a fixture's log. It also flushes on a loader/options change,
a repeated basename, the size cap, and at end of run. The three fork-summary
log checks move after nescopytest (same chunk) so their fixtures can batch.
The batch log is split per fixture on Ghidra's IMPORTING line, which keeps
each program's analysis output with it. VerifyBankTest prints a FIXTURE marker
to validate each slice; it reaches no golden. A batch that exits non-zero,
or a fixture missing its section, re-runs individually, so a failure is still
attributed to its fixture.

Batch size: GRM_BATCH_SIZE_DEFAULT=10 (a tunable starting point), overridden
by GRM_BATCH_SIZE, then --batch-size N (also accepted by build-and-test.sh).
1 or GRM_BATCH=0 means unbatched, and 0 or a non-integer is a usage error.
The banner prints the effective setting, and every flush logs
'BATCH n=<k> flush=<reason>' for the planned reorder.

Gate: build-and-test.sh check SUITE OK in 230s (was ~6.5 min), 840 CRITERION
lines, 28 batches, 0 fallbacks. Filtered criterion/verdict/golden output is
identical across unbatched, size 10, size 20 and GRM_BATCH=0 runs. A
deliberate criterion failure inside a batch failed and refused only that
fixture, and a deliberate throw exercised the fallback.

events.title: fix: pin operand size of instructions that forward-reference a label (#48)
events.message:
fix: pin operand size of instructions that forward-reference a label (#48)

When a mnemonic has both a zero-page and an absolute form, the
assembler can only choose between them once it knows the operand's
value. For a label defined later in the listing it must guess on its
first pass, and a wrong guess can settle into a self-consistent but
wrong layout, silently:

- 64tass assumes an undefined symbol is 16-bit, so "lda data_00ff"
  with the label defined later at &FF reassembled as "lda $0100";
- beebasm substitutes the instruction's own address, so an absolute
  instruction running in zero page that references a later label just
  above &100 reassembled to the zero-page form. Elsewhere beebasm's
  wrong guess is caught, but only as a second-pass error.

The renderer now records the labels each operand names and pins the
operand size when one of them is defined later in the listing and the
assembler's first-pass guess (the new forward_reference_assumes_zero_page
hook: beebasm "pc < &100", default False) disagrees with the encoded
size. Pinning goes through force_abs_instruction / force_zp_instruction:
64tass uses "@w" / "@b"; beebasm, which has no size-forcing syntax,
emits the instruction as data with the instruction in a comment.

Ordinary code is unaffected: beebasm output for every fixture ROM is
byte-identical, and the 64tass listings gain "@b" on just three
instructions, each a store into a self-modifying JMP in relocated
zero-page code.
events.author: rob-smallshire

events.title: fix(tom): stop scanline renderers writing past the host framebuffer
events.message:
fix(tom): stop scanline renderers writing past the host framebuffer

TOMExecHalfline maps a halfline to a framebuffer row. For interlaced video
(even VP) that is ((halfline - top) / 2) * 2 + field, while the window clamp
(MAX_VISIBLE_HEIGHT) only bounds halflines / 2. With a wild VP/VDB/VDE the row
reached ~1023 against a 512-row host buffer, so whichever renderer VMODE
selected (24bpp, 16bpp, CRY, RGB, mix, Nx) stored past the end of videoBuffer.
Skip and do not count a row the buffer cannot hold.

Also clamp the left border fill (startPos_disp) to the row width in all six
renderers: `width -= startPos_disp` is uint16_t, so HDB1 past the row width
wrapped width to ~65k and ran the pixel loop off the row (and off
tomHiresScratch[1024] in the Nx path).

Found by test_frontend_ext part 3 (garbage cart boot ROM), which segfaulted
every Linux CI job and tripped ASan. One compare per scanline plus one per
renderer call; no per-pixel cost and no change for valid register states.

Closes #944

events.title: Fix 68020 DIVS.L/DIVU.L overflow and signed 64-bit division
events.message:
Fix 68020 DIVS.L/DIVU.L overflow and signed 64-bit division

DIVS.L of $80000000 by -1 in the 32-bit form used a native i32
division, which panics ("attempt to divide with overflow") and takes
the emulator down. A program feeding edge cases to the Toolbox
fixed-point routines hit this on a Mac II with System 4.1.

While there:
- the 64-bit signed form zero-extended the divisor, so a negative
  divisor gave a wrong quotient;
- overflow was only tested on the 64-bit forms, and accepted any
  quotient whose high long was 0 or $FFFFFFFF: an unsigned quotient
  above 32 bits, or a signed one outside the i32 range, went through.

Do signed divisions in 64 bits with a sign-extended divisor, checked
for i64::MIN / -1, and report overflow (V set, operands unchanged)
whenever the quotient doesn't fit in 32 bits.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>

events.title: fix: define labels named by emitted expressions (#47)
events.message:
fix: define labels named by emitted expressions (#47)

An optional label only gets a "name = &xxxx" definition when the
listing references it. Expressions can reference a label by name (a
Sym) rather than by address: the acorn_mos environment registers the
high byte of each MOS vector as "<name>+1" (so &021F renders as
"fscv + 1"), and a driver may write d.expr(addr, "ptr+1"). Rendering a
Sym never counted as a use, so "lda fscv + 1,x" was emitted without a
definition of fscv and the assembler rejected the listing.

Rendering a Sym that names a registered label now records a use of
that label, through the same mechanism as an operand that resolves to
it by address, so its definition is emitted. Unrelated optional labels
stay undefined, and a name dasmos does not know is left to the driver.

The renderer constructor now initialises per-render state, so the
public render_expression helper also works on a renderer that has not
rendered anything yet.
events.author: rob-smallshire

events.title: fix: keep absolute encoding for zero-page operands on reassembly (#46)
events.message:
fix: keep absolute encoding for zero-page operands on reassembly (#46)

An instruction can be encoded with absolute addressing even though its
operand is below &100 (8D 85 00 is STA &0085). beebasm and 64tass both
choose the shortest encoding a mnemonic offers, so rendering it as
"sta data_0085" reassembled to the two-byte zero-page form and shifted
every later address, breaking the byte-exact round trip.

The renderer now detects exactly the case an assembler would shrink:
an ABSOLUTE / ABSOLUTE_X / ABSOLUTE_Y encoding whose operand is below
&100 and whose mnemonic has the matching zero-page mode, taken from
the CPU's opcode table (so LDA abs,Y stays as-is, LDX abs,Y does not).
Such instructions go through the existing force_abs_instruction seam,
which was defined but never called:

- 64tass implements it with its operand-size prefix: sta @w data_0085;
- beebasm has no syntax to force absolute addressing, so the default
  emits the instruction as data with the instruction kept visible:
  equb &8d : equw data_0085 ; sta data_0085 (absolute)

Genuine zero-page encodings and operands at or above &100 render
unchanged; existing golden listings are byte-identical.

events.title: sandbox sessions: runtime_sandbox_start/end/list, session-id routing, parity table, long calls
events.message:
sandbox sessions: runtime_sandbox_start/end/list, session-id routing, parity table, long calls

A sandbox session is the one-shot private daemon kept across calls, started for a stated purpose with a budget. A call whose session_id is sb-... is routed to that sandbox's daemon ahead of the active backend; src/runtime/sandbox-parity.ts holds a verdict per runtime tool (works / ui-only), and the ui-only tools get a session_id in their schema and refuse a sandbox id by name. Owner-private ids (record under the state dir, owner pid), budget/idle/owner-gone ends with a trace finished and the outcome in the step log, long runs and the finalize answer a job id past a grace window, the C64U trace refusal names runtime_sandbox_start and a store file is read by an emulator reader while the device is selected.

Fixes found on the way: the keeper now relays the daemon's stderr (a daemon whose stderr pipe lost its reader aborts on its next log line, with its trace unflushed); runtime_rip_range on a live machine sent a read shape the emulator refuses.

events.title: grm-w9ev.3: share JUnit transaction, program and scanner-double scaffolding
events.message:
grm-w9ev.3: share JUnit transaction, program and scanner-double scaffolding

Removes about 1,090 duplicated lines from 66 test files without changing
what any test checks.

- AbstractBundledLanguageTest: inTx / inTxGet / inTxCommitOnSuccess replace
  112 hand-written start/try/finally/endTransaction blocks.
  MosConstantReferenceAnalyzerTest keeps its commit-only-on-success semantics.
  Blocks that assign outer locals, return, or use the tx id are left as they were.
- New AbstractProgramTest holds the builder/program fields and the addr, put,
  instructionAt, setWritable and makeWritable helpers. 41 classes dropped their
  private copies.
- New StoredValueScannerTestSupport: one NO_HOOKS, assertBank (mask 0x07) and
  assertUnresolved, as static imports. The 0x0F and 0xFF assertBank variants
  stay local.
- One hex(long) on the base replaces five address-string copies. Every copy
  fed only ProgramBuilder's parser, so 0x%x vs 0x%04x never mattered.
  Spc700DisCorpusTest keeps its 16-bit mask at the call sites.

Gate: check unit, 1388 tests, 0 failures (unchanged).

project.title: ZZ9000 — native AmigaOS driver suite
project.display_title: ZZ9000 — native AmigaOS driver suite
project.status: active; current main bounds firmware-update stalls and validates configuration grammar against documentation
project.notes: Independent continuation of MNT’s ZZ9000 Amiga-side driver suite, with RTG, network/audio/USB/SD and native control utilities. Network device.c implements native SANA-II Amiga driver dispatch and hardware access; rtg/mntgfx-gcc.c implements graphics-card integration. README identifies the original MNT source and independent fork status, with firmware and ARM-side logic in separate repositories. Top-level build invokes pinned Amiga toolchain workflows; net/Makefile sets68020 and includes host-side test targets elsewhere in the suite. A reviewed code-fix commit explicitly credits Codex review; attribution is limited to review assistance. Requires ZZ9000 ZorroII/III hardware; ZZ9000AX audio and Picasso96/USB/network dependencies vary by component. Matched firmware/bitstream/SDK versions matter, especially ZorroII memory-layout negotiation; driver source alone does not provide a complete setup. The board’s ARM coprocessors are not the CPU executing the Amiga-side network driver; retain separate roles. No independent hardware/runtime/test execution; original MNT lineage is one family, not an extra project count. Maintained Amiga-side hardware driver source, not a reconstruction of a historical original binary. No source CPU is inferred from the modern hardware family. net/Makefile explicitly defaults to CPU=68020 and soft float. This records the inspected native network-driver target; other suite components can vary. The board ARM/FPGA firmware lives elsewhere and is not the Amiga driver CPU. Amiga-side m68k toolchain; inspected network component default 68020 and soft float. Board FPGA/ARM firmware separate from host driver CPU. Requires ZZ9000 ZorroII/III hardware; ZZ9000AX audio and Picasso96/USB/network dependencies vary by component. Matched firmware/bitstream/SDK versions matter, especially ZorroII memory-layout negotiation; driver source alone does not provide a complete setup. The board’s ARM coprocessors are not the CPU executing the Amiga-side network driver; retain separate roles. No independent hardware/runtime/test execution; original MNT lineage is one family, not an extra project count. No complete independently verified hardware matrix is asserted. GPL-3.0-or-later for driver tree with retained MNT/contributor and third-party notices; external payload licenses remain separate. Multiple sampled commits explicitly credit Codex review. Commit 6944da9 fixes a concrete ZZDiag control-flow problem identified in that review; no broad claim that all driver code is AI-generated. Role: code review. No broad AI-generated-code claim. Snapshot: 701ee6e9bf96f19e302d874b166e22e06952e0b6. Repository creation is not a verified RE start date. Evidence: https://github.com/BlitterStudio/zz9000-drivers/blob/master/README.md https://github.com/BlitterStudio/zz9000-drivers/blob/master/net/device.c https://github.com/BlitterStudio/zz9000-drivers/blob/master/rtg/mntgfx-gcc.c https://github.com/BlitterStudio/zz9000-drivers/blob/master/Makefile https://github.com/BlitterStudio/zz9000-drivers/blob/master/net/Makefile https://github.com/BlitterStudio/zz9000-drivers/blob/master/LICENSE https://github.com/BlitterStudio/zz9000-drivers Current main avoids a potentially indefinite Amiga-bus read when the firmware-update status mirror is frozen, and expands configuration-key tooling to compare the documented grammar with the parser, sample and editor. These are source/test-backed robustness changes, not independent hardware execution. project.title: prog8
project.display_title: Prog8 — 6502 and 68000 development language
project.status: active; distributed compiler available while the m68k backend remains experimental and adopts word-packed argument slots
project.notes: Structured low-level language/compiler for 6502-family computers and 68000, with experimental Amiga 500/1200 targets; README says the m68k targets are not yet production-ready. The current README documents official runnable compiler distributions, source builds and explicit 65xx/m68k output targets. IR format 8 now uses word-packed byte/bool/word argument slots and four-byte long/pointer/float slots across the experimental Amiga 500, Amiga 1200 and QEMU m68k targets. This does not promote the m68k targets to production-ready or establish target-machine RAM minima. Evidence: https://github.com/irmen/prog8/blob/master/README.md https://github.com/irmen/prog8/commit/0b902f06b55356b76b0c0f5fee5e207a87c33dfc

project.title: m68k-tools
project.display_title: m68k-tools — 68000 assembly analysis & language tooling
project.status: active; register-liveness diagnostics and conservative save/restore auto-fixes under development
project.notes: Motorola 68000 assembly tooling used across retro-development workflows: parser, formatter, cycle counter, static-analysis/lint libraries and language servers with CLI, VS Code and web front ends. Tracked as adjacent m68k development/analysis infrastructure rather than a platform-specific reconstruction project. Current source preserves saved registers as possibly live when routine analysis encounters unknown code and distinguishes unknown availability from definitely unavailable values. A subsequent safe multi-edit fix trims an unnecessary register from matching save/restore sites, while leaving word-sized saves manual because of sign-extension semantics. Evidence: https://github.com/grahambates/m68k-tools/commit/03d58430ca99f1ca8a415af63f0a784f03aad11a https://github.com/grahambates/m68k-tools/commit/5170da4d67258ee9caf3641d84db11d081078f14

project.title: ghidra-retro-machines
project.display_title: Ghidra Retro Machines — bank-aware loaders and retro CPU languages
project.status: Active; analysis-order-independent jump-table overrides and deterministic unpinned NES corpus analysis
project.notes: Ghidra extension for banked C64/C128/PET PRG and NES iNES analysis, with SPC700 and 65C816 language variants. The current NES pass bounds split low/high pointer tables by the next section gap: Dodge shrinks from 64 to 26 entries, River City Ransom from 64 to 27 and Mega Man 2 from 255 to 15. Upstream reports build-and-test SUITE OK and 29 NES baseline passes plus the three corrected fixtures. Existing 65C816 oracle-defect guards and language limitations remain; these gates show bounded analysis improvements, not universal correctness. The reviewed commit explicitly credits Claude Opus 5.5. Evidence: https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/6556e84ff267a0c96e7c89c5dbe2d3c3777d2aad The next analyzer pass extends RAM save-slot proofs across admitted cross-function jumps and narrowly recognized save-helper calls, while preserving conservative abandon rules and declining unresolved overlay-bank cases. Upstream reports 33 NES tests passing; the separate Dragon Power symbol-output flap remains documented. Evidence: https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/3f983b0189e67e2f8337804e0c2beb46c5483d44 The latest bank-analysis passes persist provenance for analyzer-created overlay references so later rounds retract stale targets without deleting user-owned references, and remove fall-through code only when a conditional branch is provably taken and no flow, entry point, function or user label preserves the old path. Upstream reports deterministic NES corpus updates and passing synthetic/JUnit gates; these are bounded analyzer-correctness receipts, not universal decompilation correctness. Evidence: https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/475eeadd4fb50ad045bd8e01dd428243279bfe2d https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/1251af61b1d65c8849bc90795d186ee274938db4 The newest passes write jump-table overrides once a containing function exists, eliminating first-reference analysis-order sensitivity, then remove the default single-thread pin while retaining GRM_THREAD_PIN=1 as a diagnostic. Upstream reports byte-identical results across all 34 NES fixtures at 12, 4 and 2 threads plus passing synthetic gates; this is bounded corpus determinism rather than universal analysis correctness. The reviewed commits explicitly credit Claude Opus 5.5. Evidence: https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/2a15e0df8abeeccc0842b212a00e1d08d2316e41 https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/48c66e952687ddaa24979626263f9b24dbd6b11d

project.display_title: Geargrafx — PC Engine emulator and MCP debugger
project.status: active; post-1.8.2 development head improves CD pregap, WAV chunk and relative CUE media handling
project.notes: Identity: Geargrafx remains the PC Engine/TurboGrafx-16/SuperGrafx/CD-ROM²/LD-ROM² emulator with integrated debugger and MCP server. Classification: The libretro CD-media validation change is emulator runtime maintenance and preserves the development-tool classification. Source CPU: The in-tree core and debugger continue to identify the emulated HuC6280 architecture; the media-loading change introduces no CPU change. Target CPU: This host-run emulator/debugger has no reconstructed retro output CPU. Published host artifact architectures remain runtime variants, not guest or port targets. Build: The 1.8.3 development head detects a zipped CUE in libretro, rejects the unsupported CD-ROM form with a specific user-facing message, and recommends CHD rather than reporting generic corruption. Earlier post-1.8.2 deterministic, CD-audio and input fixes remain current. No build or media load was reproduced locally. Limitations: The latest published release remains 1.8.2, so the 1.8.3-head diagnostic is not described as released. Runtime profiles: README still publishes x64 and arm64 packages but states no minimum CPU generation or RAM. The new media diagnostic supplies no additional hardware requirement. AI: Existing GitHub Copilot attribution remains supported by explicit co-author metadata; workflow model settings are not treated as additional development contribution evidence. Relationships: The repository remains an independent target in the Gear emulator/debugger family; no new separately titled project appeared in the reviewed diff. Evidence: https://github.com/drhelius/Geargrafx/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/drhelius/Geargrafx/commit/b1ca0bff1a11d524c0ba934779725c3abf93dd02 https://github.com/drhelius/Geargrafx/commit/4d174c29a0cbe112ecf186f5712504b6df21b641 https://github.com/drhelius/Geargrafx/releases/tag/1.8.2 https://github.com/drhelius/Geargrafx/commit/c0092458428c https://github.com/drhelius/Geargrafx Later development-head fixes play stored audio pregaps between audio tracks, locate WAV format chunks by bounded RIFF traversal rather than assuming a fixed 44-byte header, and resolve bare relative image paths next to the CUE file. These are source-level media-correctness fixes after 1.8.2, not a new release or a local playback result. Evidence: https://github.com/drhelius/Geargrafx/commit/cb3ed1465b774ebc4de927d7bcb8a97cf1024c03 https://github.com/drhelius/Geargrafx/commit/dabb5cf88780aac0ad9181efbc447440758ec4b1 https://github.com/drhelius/Geargrafx/commit/efb31097898d36d2319ce210a7d5304de0282f1e

project.notes: Clean-room Dungeon Master-family engine using authenticated original media. project.status: v8.4.0 published; current development adds an optional GDB remote server and MacPorts packaging
project.notes: General-purpose UAE/WinUAE-derived Amiga machine emulator. v8.4.0 publishes Windows ARM64/x86-64, macOS universal and Linux ARM64/x86-64 assets, establishing upstream compilable and runnable variants without establishing minimum hardware. The release adds ZZ9000 AHI/SANA-II/SDK/MHI/MPEGA/image/ZZPlay support, optional external MiniGL and dma-buf paths, relative media paths, cartridge and .A1000 ROM handling, runtime GL fallback, Raspberry Pi 4 drawing improvements, ARM64 JIT fixes, FreeBSD amd64/aarch64 CI and broad networking/display/input/libretro/Android corrections. m68k remains the guest CPU; ARM/x86/RISC-V/LoongArch are host families, not guest minima. External Kickstart ROMs and game media remain outside the GPL source grant. No independent execution or equivalence test was performed. Evidence: https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/releases/tag/v8.4.0 https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/blob/master/README.md Post-v8.4.0 development fixes apply RetroArch auto-loaded save states only after the emulated CPU loop is active, correct CIA-B time-of-day increments in fast and programmed-sync paths, preserve open-file keys across host renames, honor cache-inhibited pages in 68030/68040/68060 fast-cache paths and restore USE_PPC=OFF linking. These are source-level fixes on current main, not a new published release or independently executed verification. Evidence: https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/71ac39e07d339d9d8e296e15db79642e6ab5619a https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/3b5e647578e667adff3a88ef9557e2f3702b8ebe https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/bdc870008140cff3dbbb4379df94aa92d7322e27 Current main ports WinUAE's optional loopback GDB remote server, disabled by default and unavailable with the threaded CPU, with m68k registers, physical RAM/ROM, stepping, breakpoints, watchpoints and memory-map support. A separate MacPorts integration covers Apple Silicon and x86 hosts and explicitly credits ChatGPT for substantial assistance; this extends the AI record without implying whole-project generation. Evidence: https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/4faddbe399757a663fb3f2e8dc4be678eda96d4d https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/831f13e71ee6e872d6d3570f2c23068493d0dd15

runtime_profiles.name: Q8 accelerated-emulation qualification
runtime_profiles.notes: Upstream recommends Q8 only above 20 MHz. v1.8.0 reports Turbo6510 64 MHz measurements on public PAL cube scenes: Mode 2 precise/hybrid 23.70/25.05 FPS, Mode 5 27.00/27.45 FPS, and distant-cube Mode 7 standard/fast/fast+LOD 3.10/6.95/11.50 FPS. These are scene-specific emulator measurements, not minima, general guarantees or physical-hardware qualification. The v1.10.2 stable qualification additionally reports Mode 4 stock/turbo results of 0.649958/30.186113 FPS with defaults and 0.749952/38.484510 FPS with arithmetic, camera and visibility experiments; Mode 7 defaults report 0.044442/3.091013 FPS and arithmetic+UV 0.061107/3.703647 FPS. These remain emulator measurements, not physical-hardware or minimum-machine claims.

project.status: v1.10.2 stable source SDK released; optional Q8 experiments remain emulator-qualified and physical hardware remains untested
project.notes: Source SDK for eight C64 graphics modes: polygon rendering and a distinct Mode 8 2.5D DDA bitmap renderer. PowerShell/Python scene builders emit 6510/6502 assembly for 64tass. v1.8.0 adds opt-in gradual Mode 7 texture LOD, optional Q8 hybrid line rasterization for Modes 1/2/5 and safe presentation for Modes 1–7; legacy geometry, standard texture quality, precise raster and LOD-off remain defaults. Upstream reports all 22 public tests passing and bounded Turbo6510 64 MHz scene measurements, while explicitly stating that real hardware has not been tested. Code/data remain PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. Codex usage guides document downstream SDK use, not development-AI authorship of the engine. v1.9.0 adds an explicit experimental Normalized16 build and bounded signed-16 geometry generators while preserving the Q8 defaults unless the optional hook is selected. Native benchmark and qualification tooling are included; this does not change the recorded physical-hardware limitation. Evidence: https://github.com/Librologica/3Dvibe64/commit/562f3c314314abce8de7c30786843c2435b00e94 https://github.com/Librologica/3Dvibe64/commit/6ea4d7cf99513d9714407ea938aed06b8d55d4bc v1.10.2 promotes the qualified development line to a stable source SDK without changing default runtime options. Its optional Q8 arithmetic, UV, camera-table and visibility experiments remain disabled by default; upstream reports PAL-emulated Mode 4 and Mode 7 measurements, complete source/package regeneration gates and Windows/VICE qualification, while explicitly leaving Linux and physical hardware untested. Evidence: https://github.com/Librologica/3Dvibe64/releases/tag/v1.10.2

events.title: grm-w9ev.2: dispatch VerifyBankTest checks by exact fixture name
events.message:
grm-w9ev.2: dispatch VerifyBankTest checks by exact fixture name

run() was a 383-line chain of name.contains() blocks. 14 fixture names matched
more than one block, and only source order kept them right. An unrecognized
name fell through to the C64 checkBanktest() default and printed nonsense
criteria instead of failing (bd memory fixture-dispatch-two-sided).

registerChecks() now maps each of the 100 fixture names to its check, as
'focused' (no dump) or 'dumped' (dump, game identity and async entry points,
then the check). C64 banktest is an explicit entry, registering a name twice
throws, and an unregistered name fails as DISPATCH:unregistered-fixture with
SUITE FAIL. The map is rebuilt on every run() so that a script instance reused
across programs (grm-w9ev.5's batching) cannot trip the duplicate guard.

Gate: build-and-test.sh check SUITE OK with 840 CRITERION lines. Filtered
criterion/suite/dump output is identical before and after (1081 lines).

events.title: fix(app): BIOS selector rows get unique labels and ImGui IDs (#932)
events.message:
fix(app): BIOS selector rows get unique labels and ImGui IDs (#932)

The BIOS combo labelled each row with the file name, title and CRC, so one
dump in two folders (or a library folder that holds the system folder) gave
rows with identical text. Identical text is an identical ImGui ID, so a click
on the second copy selected the first one's path. Rows are now built by
bios::picksFor (testable without a GPU): one row per file on disk, a repeated
label gets its folder appended, and every row is drawn inside a PushID of its
path. A stored choice is matched by file identity, not by string. The cheat
set picker had the same shape (a set can be both a match and a similar name)
and gets a PushID per list.

events.title: listings name the I/O registers, also over $D000-$DFFF; memoryMap says where the window is RAM (#74)
events.message:
listings name the I/O registers, also over $D000-$DFFF; memoryMap says where the window is RAM (#74)

An absolute operand in the I/O window renders as the register's name (vic_ctrl1, sid_volume,
cia1_icr, color_ram+$28, a mirror as register+offset), defined in an equate block of exactly the
names used, in KickAssembler and 64tass, whether or not the image covers the address. The cause of
the raw hex: findOperandExpression answered every $D000-$DFFF target with the bare address before
any label was consulted, and annotatedOperandName refuses addresses the listing holds.

- platform store v3: platform_node.io_name + platform_io_window (mirror periods); graph_find returns
  the name, the book's heading and label, and notes a mirror
- cartridge window by type (cartridge-io): ef_bank/ef_ctrl, gmod2_ctrl, magicdesk_bank, ocean_bank,
  megabyter_bank/mode, else cart_io_deXX
- the equate door takes platform proposals and holds them to the identifier / mnemonic / length /
  collision rules; the project's own name for an address wins
- precedence: human label > memoryMap (RAM/charrom, per routine or whole listing) > register name
- memoryMap in annotations: loader, write_annotations, merge_annotations (memoryMap:<range>)
- e2e:908 in package.json and gates.yml; e2e-cartridge-bank-listing follows the names

events.title: sandbox: a CIA2 port-A re-push is not a RAM store in ramWrittenRuns
events.message:
sandbox: a CIA2 port-A re-push is not a RAM store in ramWrittenRuns

The $DD00 re-push after a store that changes the port-A output is reported
as a bus write at the same cycle as the store, with no on_io_store. It
counted as a surplus bus write, so $DD00 showed up in ramWrittenRuns.
Two CPU stores never share a cycle, so a Write at the previous record's
clk takes that record back out. Counters saturate.

events.title: grm-w9ev.4: write mknesbanktest's hand-encoded builders through _Asm
events.message:
grm-w9ev.4: write mknesbanktest's hand-encoded builders through _Asm

17 make_prg_* builders hand-encoded their code as raw bytes, which is how
grm-kdgv's dead fork arm hid: an instruction-order mistake is invisible in
bytes. Their code now goes through _Asm as mnemonics, and branches use forward
labels (fwd/bind) instead of literal offsets. Data (bank tables, markers,
vectors, RTS stubs at overlay targets) stays as bytes. _Asm gains the opcodes
these builders need, an org() cursor and forward labels.

Gate: all 26 generated images are byte-identical, and main()'s self-check
asserts pass unchanged. No Ghidra gate is needed: identical bytes mean
identical goldens.

events.title: VIA: add common 6522 core
events.message:
VIA: add common 6522 core

The VIA is currently implemented three times (via.rs, macii/via2.rs and
portable/via.rs), each a copy of the register file, timers and
interrupt logic with different port bit assignments.

Add ViaCommon, which implements the machine-independent part.

To "specialize" it, a machine wraps it and describes its wiring through
the ViaWiring trait:

  - The bit assignments of the port and interrupt registers
  - Behaviour adjustement flags:
    - Whether register B accesses clear the CB1/CB2 flags
    - Whether Timer 1 drives PB7.

The adjustments are to map differences between the current emulation and
teal HW behavior (which we might adjust later) and will be used onwards
to also handle potential differenes between VIA implementations (discrete
6522's vs some hacked up variants Apple put in custom chips).

Nothing uses it yet, only unit tests for now.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: MacII: generate the 60.15 Hz interrupt from timer 1 of VIA2
events.message:
MacII: generate the 60.15 Hz interrupt from timer 1 of VIA2

On the Mac II, the "VBlank" interrupt on CA1 of VIA1 is the square wave
that timer 1 of VIA2 outputs on PB7, which the ROM sets up for
60.15 Hz. Wire PB7 of VIA2 to CA1 of VIA1 rather than generating a
60 Hz interrupt in the bus.

The counter in the bus remains for pacing the emulation to the host.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: Portable: update the effective speed
events.message:
Portable: update the effective speed

The effective speed of the emulation is measured by the RTC each time a
second passes, which was never signalled on the Portable. Do so when
the Power Manager counts a second.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: VIA: make the interrupt flag register private
events.message:
VIA: make the interrupt flag register private

All interrupt sources now toggle their interrupts through the common
core accessors, so nothing outside of it needs to modify the interrupt
flags register directly anymore. Make the register private and add a
getter for reading it.

The unit tests of the wrappers use set_irq() to set flags.

No change in behaviour.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: Portable: stop polling ADB devices on the ADB off command
events.message:
Portable: stop polling ADB devices on the ADB off command

On the real PwMgr, Command $21 makes the firmware clear its ADB state,
including the flag that enables the polling of ADB devices, along with
the pending ADB interrupt.

The current model only clears the interrupt.

The ROM sends this command early during startup. When the system is
restarted, which on the Portable is a jump to the ROM without anything
being reset, the model keeps polling the ADB devices. If one of
them had data, such as movement of the trackball, the Power Manager
interrupts the ROM before it had set up its ADB handling, making it
crash.

Clear the ADB state and stop the polling on this command. Polling
resumes once the host initializes ADB again.

This fixes occasional crashes on reboot on the Portable.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: VIA: add accessors for the port pin levels
events.message:
VIA: add accessors for the port pin levels

The current model doesn't distinguish the port latch (register) and the
value on the pins. They can differ based on DDR bits and timer 1 output
potential overlay on top of PB7.

This adds pa() and pb() accessors, which return the levels of the port
pins (not the latch): The output register for pins configured as outputs,
the externally driven level for inputs.

The Timer 1 output is now overlaid on PB7 in pb() rather than written
into the output register, so the value written by the CPU is preserved
and comes back when the output is disabled in the ACR. As on the real
chip, the timer drives PB7 regardless of the data direction register.

Use pb() for the 60.15 Hz tick on the MacII.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: VIA: use the common VIA core for VIA1
events.message:
VIA: use the common VIA core for VIA1

Turn the VIA of the compact Macs (also VIA1 of the Mac II family) into
a wrapper around the common 6522 core. The wrapper keeps what is
specific to that VIA: the keyboard/ADB shifter, the RTC, the one second
interrupt and the SCC write request and ADB interrupt inputs.

No change in behaviour. Registers A, B and their data direction
registers still start out as 0xFF, which a real 6522 does not do.

The layout of the serialized state changes for everything.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: MacII: keep VIA2 at a constant speed when overclocking
events.message:
MacII: keep VIA2 at a constant speed when overclocking

VIA2 was ticked once every 20 bus cycles, which made its timers run
faster when the bus frequency is raised by overclocking. Convert the
bus cycles to VIA cycles the way VIA1 does, so both run at the same
speed regardless of the bus frequency.

No change at the default speed. The layout of the serialized state
changes.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: VIA: register A via port 15 does not clear CA1/CA2 flags
events.message:
VIA: register A via port 15 does not clear CA1/CA2 flags

On a 6522, only an access to register A with handshake (register 1)
clears the CA1 and CA2 interrupt flags. The register without handshake
(register 15) leaves them alone.

The Mac only ever uses the latter (vBufA), so a port A access must not
dismiss a pending VBlank or one-second interrupt on VIA1, or a
slot/SCSI DRQ interrupt on VIA2, potentially causing us to miss interrupts.

All three VIA implementations cleared the flags on both registers.

Test booted a 128, Plus, II and Portable with this change.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: VIA: add the interrupt output and shift completion to the common core
events.message:
VIA: add the interrupt output and shift completion to the common core

Add irq(), which returns the state of the interrupt request output, and
use it in the buses rather than having them combine the interrupt flag
and enable registers.

Add shift_sr(), which completes the shift of a byte through the shift
register and sets its interrupt flag, and use it for the keyboard and
ADB transceiver. As on a real 6522, the register keeps its value when
shifting out, which makes the copy of the outgoing byte redundant.

For now the delay of the shift stays with the VIA of the compact Macs,
although it is the keyboard or the ADB transceiver that clocks the
register so eventually we should probably move it there.

No change in behaviour intended. The layout of the serialized state
changes.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: testrunner: load the display ROM from the file
events.message:
testrunner: load the display ROM from the file

The path given with --display-rom was passed on as the ROM contents,
so the Mac II models ran without a working display card.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: Portable: only hold back ADB device polling until ADB is initialized
events.message:
Portable: only hold back ADB device polling until ADB is initialized

The Power Manager model held back all of its interrupts until the host
had sent a first ADB command with the init flag. The real one has no
such gate: it only refrains from polling the ADB devices until the host
has enabled that.

Apply the gate to the polling of the ADB devices for service requests
only. Interrupts for ADB commands sent by the host before that are no
longer held back.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: MacII: drive the ASC interrupt through VIA2 CB1
events.message:
MacII: drive the ASC interrupt through VIA2 CB1

Feed the level of the interrupt output of the ASC to CB1 of VIA2
rather than setting the interrupt flag for as long as the ASC requests
an interrupt.

As on hardware, the flag is now only set on the falling edge of the
interrupt output. It is no longer set again if it gets cleared while
the ASC still requests an interrupt, which happens until the FIFO
status register is read.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: MacII: drive the SCSI IRQ and DRQ through VIA2 CB2/CA2
events.message:
MacII: drive the SCSI IRQ and DRQ through VIA2 CB2/CA2

Feed the level of the IRQ and DRQ outputs of the SCSI controller to
CB2 and CA2 of VIA2, rather than copying them to the interrupt flags.
Both are active high and directly connected to the VIA.

As on hardware, the flags are now set on the edge selected through the
PCR and stay set until cleared, rather than following the level of the
lines. With the PCR value set by the ROM (negative edge), that is when
the controller releases the line.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: VIA: remove the T1_PB7_OUTPUT wiring option
events.message:
VIA: remove the T1_PB7_OUTPUT wiring option

No machine sets it, the Timer 1 output is always available on PB7
when ACR enables it.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: VIA: honour independent interrupt mode for CA2/CB2
events.message:
VIA: honour independent interrupt mode for CA2/CB2

When CA2 or CB2 is configured through the PCR as an independent
interrupt input, an access to register A (with handshake) or
register B no longer clears the corresponding interrupt flag. Only a
write to the IFR does. The CA1/CB1 flags are unaffected.

The PCR was stored but ignored, so the flags were always cleared.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: VIA: fix the period of Timer 1 in free-running mode
events.message:
VIA: fix the period of Timer 1 in free-running mode

On a 6522, Timer 1 reloads from the latch in the cycle after it ran
out, which makes its period in free-running mode N + 2 cycles for a
latch value of N. It was N + 1.

The ROM of the Mac accounts for this when it uses timers in free running
mode such as when generating the pseudo-VBL on the MacII.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: VIA: drive the VBlank, 60 Hz and one second interrupts through CA1/CA2
events.message:
VIA: drive the VBlank, 60 Hz and one second interrupts through CA1/CA2

Use set_line() with a pulse for the interrupt sources that are single
events: the VBlank interrupt of the compact Macs, the 60 Hz interrupt
of the Mac II and Portable (CA1) and the one second interrupt (CA2),
rather than setting the interrupt flags directly.

The only change in behaviour is that the one second interrupt flag is
no longer set if the PCR configures CA2 as an output, but that shouldn't
be the case anyways.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: MacII: fix the levels of the VIA1 port A inputs
events.message:
MacII: fix the levels of the VIA1 port A inputs

On a real MacII, PA0-PA2 go to the burn-in connector (internal diagnostics)
and are pulled up, they are not model identifiers.

Remove the model field and read all three as high.

The model is identified by PA6 and PB3 of VIA2, which do not change.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: MacII: drive the slot interrupt through VIA2 CA1
events.message:
MacII: drive the slot interrupt through VIA2 CA1

Feed the combined level of the slot interrupt lines to CA1 of VIA2
rather than setting the interrupt flag for as long as a slot requests
an interrupt.

As on hardware, the flag is now only set on the falling edge of
/SLOTIRQ: a slot that requests an interrupt while another one is
still pending no longer sets it again. The slot interrupt handler in
ROM deals with this by looping until all slot interrupts are gone.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: Portable: use the common VIA core
events.message:
Portable: use the common VIA core

The Portable Via becomes a wrapper around ViaCommon which defines the
port and interrupt bit assignments and keeps the one-second counter.
ViaCommon gains a reset() for it.

This follows the behaviour of the 6522 where the previous
implementation differed:

 - Accesses to register B now clear the CB1 (power manager) and CB2
   (SCSI) interrupt flags, the latter unless CB2 is in independent
   interrupt mode. The bus updates the power manager flag from the
   power manager's interrupt line on every bus access, so this is not
   expected to be visible.
 - Timer 1 now drives PB7 when enabled through the ACR.
 - The shift register is implemented. Accesses used to be reported as
   unimplemented and read as open bus.

Savestates containing a Portable are not compatible.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: MacII: use the common VIA core for VIA2
events.message:
MacII: use the common VIA core for VIA2

Via2 becomes a thin wrapper around ViaCommon which only defines the
port and interrupt bit assignments.

This follows the behaviour of the 6522 where the previous
implementation differed:

 - Timer 1 now drives PB7 when enabled through the ACR. The ROM
   configures VIA2 Timer 1 as a free-running square wave on PB7
   (v2VBL), so the PB7 output bit now toggles. Nothing in the bus
   uses it yet.
 - The shift register can be read back. It used to always read as
   zero and log a warning on writes.

The debugger shows the shift register instead of the unused shifter
input/output/timer values.

Savestates containing a Mac II family machine are not compatible.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: VIA: add control line inputs setters to the common core
events.message:
VIA: add control line inputs setters to the common core

Add set_line() to drive the CA1, CA2, CB1 and CB2 inputs rather than
having the bus set the interrupt flags directly.

As on a real 6522, the inputs are strictly edge sensitive: the interrupt
flag of a line is set on the active edge selected through the PCR.

Nothing uses this yet, no change in behaviour.

The layout of the serialized state changes.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: Portable: drive the Power Manager interrupt through VIA CB1
events.message:
Portable: drive the Power Manager interrupt through VIA CB1

Feed the level of the Power Manager interrupt to CB1 of the VIA rather
than copying it to the interrupt flag.

The Power Manager is not modeled accurately enough for an edge
sensitive input: it can request another interrupt while a command is
still in progress, in which case the handshake of that command on
register B clears the interrupt flag and no further edge follows.

On the real device, I believe the firmware will not request an
interrupt until it's idle after processing a command.

To avoid losing interrupts, we add a workaround: another edge
is generated for as long as the Power Manager requests an interrupt,
via checking IFR and re-sending pulses.

This is to be removed once we fix the Power Manager model to only
requests an interrupt when it is idle.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: MacII: run the VIAs at 783.36 kHz
events.message:
MacII: run the VIAs at 783.36 kHz

The VIA clock of the Mac II is the 15.6672 MHz master clock divided by
20. As the bus runs at a nominal 16 MHz, ticking the VIAs once every 20
bus cycles made them run at 800 kHz, about 2% too fast. This affected
the timers and the one second interrupt, which is counted in VIA
cycles.

Tick the VIAs at the right fraction of the bus frequency.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: VIA: start VIA1 from the real power-up state
events.message:
VIA: start VIA1 from the real power-up state

VIA1 started with all pins as outputs driven high, so that the overlay
and the other signals read by the bus had the right level before the ROM
set the data direction registers. A real 6522 comes out of reset with all
pins as inputs and the output registers cleared.

Start from that state and have the Mac II family read the output pins of
port A as high while they are still inputs, as the compact models
already do. The model identification inputs are unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>

events.title: Portable: fix the Power Manager interrupt behaviour
events.message:
Portable: fix the Power Manager interrupt behaviour

Make the Power Manager drive its interrupt line (/PMINT, to CB1 of the
VIA) the way the firmware of the real one does:

 - The line is pulsed rather than held for as long as an interrupt is
   pending.
 - It is only pulsed when the Power Manager is idle, never while a
   command is in progress.
 - This is done on the 60 Hz tick and after an ADB command from the
   host has completed, and repeated on every tick for as long as the
   interrupt remains pending.
 - ADB devices are polled for service requests on the 60 Hz tick.
 - The "Power Manager has been reset" flag is reported but does not
   cause an interrupt.

The repeated pulse is what keeps an interrupt from getting lost when
the VIA clears the CB1 interrupt flag on an access to register B, so
the workaround in the bus is no longer needed.

The Power Manager now also generates the one second signal (to CA2 of
the VIA), every 60 ticks, rather than the VIA generating it and the
Power Manager reading it back from the interrupt flag, matching real
hardware more accurately.

A side effect (but matches the hardware) is that an interrupt for an
input from an ADB device is now raised at the next 60 Hz tick rather
than immediately.

The layout of the serialized state changes.

Signed-off-by: Benjamin Herrenschmidt <benh@kernel.crashing.org>
events.author: ozbenh

events.title: VIA: read port outputs through the pin accessors
events.message:
VIA: read port outputs through the pin accessors

The buses and the VIA wrappers looked at the output registers directly,
which ignores the data direction registers. Use pa() and pb() instead
and make the output and data direction registers private.

A pin configured as input now reads as the level driven from the
outside, so the explicit data direction tests for the sound enable and
the AMU select go away.

events.title: Merge latest updates (#2439)
events.message:
Merge latest updates (#2439)

* Merge latest updates

* fix(a2024): reject frames whose source origin precedes the captured buffer

src->xoffset now follows frame_internal_pixel_start_cnt, so programmed
horizontal blanking can push it past the fixed A2024 beam positions.
The ID sample and the panel origin then go negative and the panel loop
reads before bufmem. Skip such frames, as is already done for ystart.

* fix(graffiti): reject frames whose destination origin precedes the buffer

Graffiti places dstbuf at (xstart << RES_MAX) - src->xoffset. Now that
xoffset follows frame_internal_pixel_start_cnt, programmed horizontal
blanking can make that negative and the render loop writes before the
row. Reject the frame, as A2024 does.

* fix(genlock): scale the image origin by the source pixel width

src->xoffset is in superhires pixels while the genlock loop counts
source pixels. Dividing the delta by 2 is only right at hires, so with
extreme overscan the image shifted at lores and superhires. Divide by
xchange instead.

events.title: loader lens: follow downward runs and stack-buffered copies, page 1 is a buffer (Spec 907 D1)
events.message:
loader lens: follow downward runs and stack-buffered copies, page 1 is a buffer (Spec 907 D1)

Runs grow both ways and are reported at their lowest address, bytes in address
order. A run wholly in page 1 that a transfer filled is a buffer, never a
landing. A write that is a 1:1 (constant-XOR) copy out of transfer-written page-1
bytes, within 16 cycles of the read, is a landing with the buffer as its source
window; relocations and depackers read no transfer-written bytes or are not 1:1
and stay dropped. Tests: stack buffer + downward copy, relocator and
depacker negatives, unfollowed buffer, downward direct landing.
