events.title: fix(app): make the Retina font density path testable (--pixel-density, density log)
events.message:
fix(app): make the Retina font density path testable (--pixel-density, density log)

Maintainer report: System UI / custom text looks soft with uneven letter spacing on a
Retina MacBook.  Dear ImGui 1.92 bakes glyphs at the viewport's FramebufferScale
(io.DisplayFramebufferScale, which the SDL3 backend sets from SDL_GetWindowDisplayScale,
and the per-viewport platform handler); the app never overrides FontGlobalScale,
RasterizerDensity or PixelSnapH for the vector faces, and FontScaleDpi is the content
scale (display scale / pixel density = 1.0 on a Retina Mac).  With density 2 forced
through both paths, FreeType (hinted, the default) and stb_truetype both render crisp,
evenly spaced text, so that path is correct and the soft rendering on the maintainer's
Mac is NOT explained by the font code.

What this adds so it can be pinned down on the real display:
- --pixel-density N (dev): lays the UI out in points on an N-times-larger window and
  reports N pixels per point through io and the platform handler, so a headless or 1x
  host renders what a Retina display does (implies --low-dpi).
- --verbose logs once, inside a frame: SDL pixel density, SDL display scale, io and main
  viewport framebuffer scale, UI scale, and the density the current font is baked at.
  A Retina Mac must show 2.00 for the last one; a 1.00 there is the bug.
- the UI-scale arithmetic moved out of initImGui into ui_scale.h with a unit test
  (fonts_unit): Retina 2/2 = 1, 4K Windows 2/1 = 2, preference clamp, nonsense guard.

events.title: fix(#72): an I/O store is not a RAM byte in sandbox_6502_run's image
events.message:
fix(#72): an I/O store is not a RAM byte in sandbox_6502_run's image

With I/O banked in, a store to $D000-$DFFF went to a chip but the harvest laid its value over
the RAM bytes, so output_path carried VIC values as game bytes. The RAM image now comes from
the runtime's ramHex / ramWrittenRuns (TRX64 branch feat/sandbox-raw-ram-harvest): the runs,
memory windows, output_path and sandbox_depack hold what RAM holds; the answer names the I/O
addresses and splits them into 'inside the written runs' (RAM byte kept) and 'not in the
image' (stored only in I/O). A runtime without those fields cuts the I/O-stored addresses out
of the runs and says so in a WARNING.

events.title: Real floppy: peak shift compensation in the data separator (#15)
events.message:
Real floppy: peak shift compensation in the data separator (#15)

Magnetic pulses close together push each other apart: on the R6 drive an
interval followed by a short one reads 80..110 ns too short, an 8 us
interval between two 4 us ones up to 900 ns. fdc_dsep.vhd now decides an
interval only when the next one has arrived, after subtracting the
learned mean deviation of its (previous, this, next) pattern (27 running
means, gain 1/32). Offline on the MEGA65 captures this doubles the
margin of the weakest sector (track 68 side 0 sector 10: 68 -> 188 ns,
it now decodes in both revolutions). Replays through WF1772IP: both
MEGA65 captures and the four Greaseweazle tracks read 60/60 sectors.

A per-angle learned speed profile was tried as well (the wobble repeats
every revolution) and did not change the margins: not used.

events.title: fix(paths): keep the ROM folder in relative ROM paths (#2438)
events.message:
fix(paths): keep the ROM folder in relative ROM paths (#2438)

* fix(paths): keep the ROM folder in relative ROM paths

With relative paths on and a ROM path spelled like resolved host paths (the portable default on Windows), kickstart_rom_file and cart_file were first shortened to a name relative to the ROM path, then made base-relative against the working directory. That saved ./amiga-os-310-cd32.rom or a bare cart.rom instead of ./roms/... The base-relative form is now taken from the full path before falling back to the ROM-path-relative name.

Empty paths also stay empty in fullpath(), as in WinUAE. On Windows _fullpath() turned an unset rtc_file or flash_file into the working directory, which was saved as rtc_file=./.

Fixes #2432

* fix(paths): keep unset ROM-type paths empty on Linux

An empty flash_file or rtc_file went through the ROM search-path lookup, which joined the search folder with the empty name. On Linux zfile_exists() accepts that folder, so the unset file was saved as ./ROMs/.

events.title: Real floppy: data separator in front of WF1772IP, menu item (#15)
events.message:
Real floppy: data separator in front of WF1772IP, menu item (#15)

The R6 internal drive's speed hunts by +-8 % about 30 times per second
(flux capture: 74 ns per bit cell wobble against 11 ns on a PC drive).
WF1772IP's data separator then misreads 6/8 us intervals and sectors fail
their CRC at random. fdc_dsep.vhd decodes each interval (2/3/4 cells of a
tracked cell length, gain 1/16, glitches < 1.5 cells dropped), queues the
decisions in a 512 entry FIFO and plays them back at the nominal 2 us
cell (+-1/4096 per entry around half full): the controller gets an even
data rate, latency ~1.3 ms.

Replay (run_flux_replay.sh, DSEP=1): the MEGA65 capture of Jim Power
track 3 side 1 reads 10/10 sectors (without: sector 7 fails like on the
hardware); the four Greaseweazle captured tracks still read 40/40.

New menu item "Floppy data separator" (System settings, line 41, on by
default; off = the raw drive signal, e.g. for copy protections that rely
on the WD1772's own behaviour). OPTM_SIZE 104 (new stcfg needed),
C_MENU_* from 41 on shifted, top files main_osm_control_m(53).

FLUX=dump in probe4.tcl reads the capture in one scan (each scan loses
the byte it has loaded last); flux2scp.py accepts that format.

events.title: Neowilderness: lock the read-only files of the volume, rank journeys after a walk
events.message:
Neowilderness: lock the read-only files of the volume, rank journeys after a walk

POM2 report of 13 October 2026: after a Sierra journey, NEOWILD.DAT's EOF in
the volume directory went from $00BC47 to $003F47 (block 2 byte $41) and the
next boot stopped on DISK ERROR $4C. ProDOS 8 rewrites a file's directory
entry from its FCB at CLOSE when the file has the write right and the FCB
is marked modified; a NEOWILD.DAT FCB with that EOF reproduces the image
byte for byte. tools/build_disk.py now locks every file but NEOWILD.HOF
(access $01), so ProDOS can never rewrite their entries. The stray write
itself was not reproduced (a2shot, POM2 with the user's profile).

The end module read the region and journey kind in MAP+32/MAP+33, which the
wild food scan rewrites at every walk: a scenario journey became "FREE
JOURNEY: NOT RANKED". It now reads region_number and a resident
journey_kind written by the loader.

tests/test_hof_volume.py: volume rights, a stray FCB at the loader's CLOSE,
a real journey then a whole-volume comparison after ejection, and a guard
against any store of the game into ProDOS's memory (new a2shot step
storewatch). docs/HOF.md section 10.

events.title: feat(app): CPU debugger window for the 68000, GPU and DSP (#833)
events.message:
feat(app): CPU debugger window for the 68000, GPU and DSP (#833)

One window with three tabs: registers (68K D/A/PC/SR with decoded flags and
USP/SSP; GPU/DSP both register banks side by side with the active one marked,
PC, FLAGS Z/C/N/IMASK/REGPAGE, G_CTRL/D_CTRL), editable while halted through
set_reg; a disassembly view (68K via the vendored Musashi over peek, GPU/DSP via
disasm_risc) with follow-PC, wheel scrolling by instruction, go-to, click-the-
margin breakpoints, run to here / set PC here, a breakpoint list with enable and
remove; Break, Continue, Step, Step over (68K JSR/BSR/TRAP run to the next
instruction through a temporary breakpoint; the RISCs have no call so it is a
step) and Run to cursor.  Step on another tab resumes and halts at that
processor's next instruction.  The window opens and selects the halted
processor's tab on a break or breakpoint, and draws inside App::haltedFrame().

Logic (no ImGui) is cpu_view.{h,cpp}, unit-tested against the mock and end to end
on yarc with the real core; registered through one DebugSession::addProvider.
The core's cur_bank is only REGPAGE, so the window derives the active bank
(IMASK forces bank 0) itself.

events.title: tests/cli: supervisor deadline is elapsed time, not loop turns
events.message:
tests/cli: supervisor deadline is elapsed time, not loop turns

The CLI crash supervisor counted Delay(2) turns against seconds*50.
A child at the same priority that never waits only yields at the end
of its time slice, so each turn took ~6 ticks and the 120 s profiler
budget became ~360 s; the 300 s stall guard in amiberry-run.sh then
reaped the guest before any TIMEOUT line was written.

Budgets (case deadline and the shutdown grace) now compare E-clock
deltas from timer.device, which is monotonic, so an sntp case that
steps the system clock cannot shift them. The supervisor runs one
priority above its children (passed explicitly via NP_Priority) so a
busy-looping child cannot delay the deadline check. Budget values,
journal rows and the TIMEOUT contract are unchanged.

events.title: grm-x51h: keep a decided branch's dead fall-through when pointer data names it
events.message:
grm-x51h: keep a decided branch's dead fall-through when pointer data names it

The tmnt multi-entry chains (b786 LDA #$10 / BNE .., b78a LDA #$11 / ..) are
entries of the JumpEngine table at b57c (b579 JSR $C702; $B5A2 is its 19th
word), which InlineJumpTableDispatchAnalyzer always recognized and laid as
pointers. It only SCHEDULES a function at each target, though, and
DecidedBranchAnalyzer (BLOCK_ANALYSIS) runs on the freshly disassembled
targets first: an entry that linear disassembly reached as the fall-through
of the previous entry's always-taken BNE had only a DATA ref from its
pointer, which the clear guard did not count, so it was cleared.

deadCodeStart now also keeps the fall-through when a reference to it comes
from defined pointer data. The branch's fall-through override is still set.

check nes: 27 pass + 7 rows re-blessed, count lines only, every count UP
(no bank comment, warning, note or sample line changed): tmnt instrs
14930->15099 (its pre-grm-kdgv value), zelda 12868->12957, cv3
19345->19416, contra 2785->2798, tmnt3 4489->4514, lwings 7445->7473,
smb2 6522->6524. blmaster's ebf4 palette table stays cleared. Synthetic
gate SUITE OK. Residual losses no table names: follow-up bead.

events.title: Installer: reject over-long SCRIPT/APPNAME/LOGFILE, bound the title
events.message:
Installer: reject over-long SCRIPT/APPNAME/LOGFILE, bound the title

Rebuilt private Installer 2.17 with AmigaPorts v16.2-rc16.

- A script path longer than the 80-byte window title overflowed it on the
  first busy-pointer update and rebooted the guest (104- and 2048-character
  SCRIPT cases). The title is now built with a bounded append; a path that
  does not fit is shown as its file part.
- APPNAME and LOGFILE were copied into 40- and 128-byte buffers without a
  length check; a 2 KB value overwrote the globals that follow them, so no
  window opened and the process never reached its input loop.
- SCRIPT over 255 (the DOS 2.x BSTR limit), APPNAME over 39 and LOGFILE
  over 127 characters now print a message and return 10, from a Shell or
  a tooltype. Bad arguments also return 10 instead of 0.

events.title: Reduce empty TX reaping and isolate capture frame
events.message:
Reduce empty TX reaping and isolate capture frame

Keep the lock-free reap check inline and outline the existing batch detach. Preserve the under-Disable recheck and cover a competing reaper draining the queue before the lock.

Move transmit capture behind a SANA-local noinline helper so LTO does not reserve BPF buffers on every launch. Existing Emu68 emission on the Pi confirms the empty-reap slice falls from 24 to 9-10 ARM instructions (excluding JIT exits), and launch local space falls from 96 bytes to zero. No hardware throughput claim.

events.title: Real floppy: raw flux capture through JTAG (#15)
events.message:
Real floppy: raw flux capture through JTAG (#15)

flux_capture.vhd records 128 KB of the internal drive's flux (interval
bytes in 62 ns units, 00 at each index, about 3 revolutions) while the
core or the probe drives the drive. USER4 command C3: 01 arms, 02 streams
the buffer (one scan: probe4.tcl FLUX=arm / FLUX=dump); the snapshot is
now 336 bits with the capture status. tools/flux2scp.py writes an SCP
file for scp_mfm.py and run_flux_replay.sh.

Result (Jim Power disk, track 3 side 1, R6 drive): the MEGA65 drive's
flux has a much wider timing spread than the Greaseweazle drive's (speed
wobble 74 vs 11 ns per cell, 652 vs 1 intervals near the 6/8 us
boundary). Replayed into WF1772IP it fails on sector 7 exactly like the
hardware, while a simple software PLL decodes all sectors: the data
separator is the place to improve.

R6 build: WNS +0.277, WHS +0.036, block RAM 95.5 tiles (+32).

events.title: feat(app): cheat scanner for the debug tools (WP3)
events.message:
feat(app): cheat scanner for the debug tools (WP3)

A Cheat-Engine / RetroArch style memory search over the 2 MB main RAM.

- cheat_scan.{h,cpp}: pure engine. 8/16/32-bit big-endian values, signed or
  unsigned, aligned or not, optional address window. Modes: unknown initial
  value, ==, !=, >, < value, in range, changed, unchanged, increased,
  decreased, increased/decreased by N (modular at the width, so a wrapping
  counter is still found). The candidate set is a bitset over the RAM and is
  always kept in full; results() pages through it. Each pass keeps the
  candidate set and the previous-values snapshot, so undo restores both
  (16 passes deep).
- scanner_actions.{h,cpp}: poke a result, or keep it as a cheat through
  CheatManager::addUser(memoryCheatToCode(...)). Refused when the debug tools
  are off, when the cheat manager is hardcore-blocked (addUser itself would
  store it), or outside the 2 MB RAM.
- scanner_ui.{h,cpp}: the window. Start/Next scan, Undo, New search, mode and
  value inputs, a clipped results table (first 1000 shown) refreshing at 10 Hz,
  double-click a value to poke it, "Add as cheat" popup. Greyed with the reason
  when the session is disabled; closed and cleared on a forced close.
- Tests: debug_scan_unit (every mode x width x sign x alignment against a
  brute-force reference, narrowing, undo, window, and the cheat code replayed
  through the core's cheat_parse_one / cheat_list_apply), debug_scan_e2e
  (yarc.j64 on the real core: find a counter by Changed / Increased /
  Increased-by narrowing, hold it with a cheat, control and hardcore arms),
  debug_scan_ui_smoke (the window drawn headlessly through every state).

events.title: grm-uioc: drop the analysis thread pin by default; GRM_THREAD_PIN=1 keeps it as a diagnostic
events.message:
grm-uioc: drop the analysis thread pin by default; GRM_THREAD_PIN=1 keeps it as a diagnostic

The runners (lib/common.sh grm_apply_settings_base) and ghidra-mcp serve.sh now use Ghidra's
default analysis thread pool. GRM_THREAD_PIN=1 restores -Dcpu.core.override=1 for one
invocation; both candidate-cache keys now default the term to 0, so a pinned diagnostic run
never serves a dump to a normal bless.

Basis, measured 2026-10-13 after grm-kon2 on a 12-core machine: check nes was 34/34 with
byte-identical dumps across a pinned run, two unpinned 12-thread runs, and unpinned runs at
cpu.core.override=4 and =2. The synthetic gate was SUITE OK unpinned. The pin no longer changed
wall clock (pinned 480s, unpinned 470-478s). Every pinned/unpinned split found along the way was
an analysis-order race in our own analyzers (grm-4nr, grm-eyn, grm-v60.1, grm-kon2) that the pin
only made rarer, so a row that moves with thread count is now a bug to fix rather than a reason
to pin. No golden changes.

docs/testing.md's section is rewritten around the new default, keeping the grm-nems history;
docs/ghidra-mcp.md follows serve.sh.

events.message:
feat(app): BIOS choice, boot and import

The desktop app can now choose the exact boot ROM / CD BIOS file the core runs,
boot a BIOS on its own and import a BIOS file.

Root causes (maintainer report: BIOS import/scanning and booting the BIOS for CD
is broken; Auto does not allow booting a local file):
- biosUse() compared names and folders case-sensitively while classifyBios() does
  not, so JAGCD.BIN / ATARI - JAGUAR CD/ were labelled 'rename it' on volumes
  where the core finds them.
- A BIOS dropped on the window was run as a cartridge; the only BIOS action was a
  copy under a fixed name, which a cart boot ROM ignores unless Cart BIOS Type =
  Custom and BIOS (Cartridges) = Real.
- CD Boot Mode / BIOS options were reachable only through the generic Core options
  tab, which is empty before a load and hides the CD options while a cartridge
  runs (update_option_visibility); no-content boot could only enter the CD BIOS.

Adds bios.h/.cpp and bios_ui.cpp (Settings > BIOS, the top of the BIOS & system
tab, tile menu: Use / Boot / Copy), CoreHost support for the new private calls,
config keys bios.cart / bios.cd, drop and dialog import into system/bios/, File >
Boot BIOS, and --boot-bios / --cart-bios / --cd-bios / --expect-bios (headless

events.title: Code Health: Detangle event loops in desk accessories
events.message:
Code Health: Detangle event loops in desk accessories

Many desk accessories were implemented with the event loop written to
dispatch to specific handlers via JMP, thus requiring that the
handlers return to the event loop with another JMP. While valid, this
made them difficult to read and maintain.

Switch to having the event loop consistent call (i.e. JSR), so that
the handlers can just RTS. When exiting the DA, the handler pops the
return address off the stack.

Some DAs were already implemented this way, but often in fairly
convoluted way. Use the structured control flow macros to improve
readability and consistency.

events.title: grm-kon2: write the jump-table override for switches first pinned by references only
events.message:
grm-kon2: write the jump-table override for switches first pinned by references only

JumpTableBoundAnalyzer bounds a switch with an override when a real function contains it, and
pins it by COMPUTED_JUMP references when none does. Stock switch analysis never revisits a site
that has computed references, so a switch every pass reached before its function existed kept
the pin and never got its override (or its switch/case_N labels). Whether some pass reached it
after its function existed was timing: dragonpower a546 (in the NMI handler's flow) came out at
152 or 168 symbols, shenlong 97 or 113, and the analysis thread pin only shifted the odds.

JumpTableOverrideRelocatorAnalyzer already runs when a function is created; it now also collects
any switch in the new body that carries our bound comment and no override anywhere, and runs the
bound analyzer's own decompile-and-bound (extracted as boundFunctions) on that function, so both
orders end with the override. Rebuilding the override from the pinned references was rejected:
references are a set, so case order and duplicate targets would be lost and the labels would
differ from the in-order path's. The bound EOL comment is no longer re-appended when a later
pass bounds the same table to the same result.

Real-ROM: 10 rows re-blessed, symbol lines only, every new line an override switch/case label;
no ref, instruction, bank comment, warning or note moved anywhere. dragonpower and shenlong now
match their existing goldens. check nes pinned + two unpinned runs: 34/34 byte-identical.
build-and-test.sh check: SUITE OK.

Adds tools/banktest/SiteStateProbe.java (owner, EOL comment and outgoing refs at given sites),
which told the two paths apart.

events.title: debug: expose Exec tasks and existing execution controls
events.message:
debug: expose Exec tasks and existing execution controls

Read bounded Exec task lists and expose saved stack bounds without
inventing register contexts for suspended tasks. Exec can retain
ThisTask after placing it on a wait queue; include that task once while
still rejecting repeated queue entries and cycles. Task names may point
into Kickstart ROM.

Return instruction history from the existing ring and opt into recording
only on request. Allocate remote conditions in the debugger breakpoint
table and reuse its comparisons and step-over trace mode. Keep ownership
separate from console entries and send the stop reply after monitor
execution resumes the CPU.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: debug: add WinUAE monitor commands for remote clients
events.message:
debug: add WinUAE monitor commands for remote clients

Route GDB qRcmd requests to a WinUAE monitor that extends the plain
target in gdb_monitor.cpp. Each command family has its own handler, and
replies are hex-encoded text, usually JSON.

Start with disassembly through the existing debugger, PNG screenshots
through a new screenshot_save() backend function, capability discovery,
the debugger memory map as JSON, write-range checks against physical RAM
banks and a live execution status query. Allow the capability and status
queries while the guest runs; other commands require a stopped CPU.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: debug: capture CPU exceptions for remote diagnosis
events.message:
debug: capture CPU exceptions for remote diagnosis

Add an independent remote exception mask and capture the selected
vector, instruction address and registers at the existing exception
hook, before frame creation. Stop at the next CPU debugger boundary and
report a meaningful GDB signal with the vector and fault PC.

Read fault address, transfer direction, size and function code before
frame creation can overwrite them, decode MMU transfer fields from the
model-specific status word and retain that raw word. Keep this metadata
separate from the frame-building flags so ordinary exception behavior
remains unchanged, and leave console exception masks untouched.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: debug: stop at AmigaDOS program entries and report segments
events.message:
debug: stop at AmigaDOS program entries and report segments

Add a remote one-shot entry breakpoint selected by process address or
case-insensitive process and CLI command names, and report the loaded
segment list of the current or a selected process as JSON.

Inspect guest process structures through bounded RAM and ROM reads that
never touch I/O. Reject cycles, invalid BPTRs and overflowing allocation
headers before returning a result, and keep host symbol parsing outside
the emulator. Report the matched process in the stop reply and keep
remote ownership separate from console breakpoints.

events.title: Fix the CLI-matrix timeouts: httpd page requester, profspin SCALE, quoted path
events.message:
Fix the CLI-matrix timeouts: httpd page requester, profspin SCALE, quoted path

httpd -T/-C/-F looked for its page at AmiNetXDuo:Terminal/... with
requesters on, so a machine without the assign stopped at "Please insert
volume AmiNetXDuo" before the listener opened. The built-in places are
now probed with pr_WindowPtr -1; a page named by PAGE/CONSOLEPAGE/FILEPAGE
keeps the normal requester.

profspin took SCALE as a ULONG, so SCALE -1 became four billion turns of
a kernel loop that does not check Ctrl-C. SCALE is now 0 to
0xFFFFFFFF / reps[0]; anything else is refused with RETURN_ERROR.

The matrix's quoted value named a volume the guest does not have, and
DOS put up "Please insert volume" for it, which is the AmigaDOS answer
to a typed path. The value now starts with RAM:, so the escaped quote,
'/', ':' and '=' still reach every parser without a requester.

events.title: fix(tools): check CFG keys against the firmware configuration guide
events.message:
fix(tools): check CFG keys against the firmware configuration guide

The firmware docs rewrite moved the ZZ9000.CFG option tables from
README.md into docs/configuration.md and writes the per-scene audio
keys as grammar rows (audio_scene<N>_lpf, `_eq01`, `_eq23` ...,
`_nm1` through `_nm8`), so check-cfg-keys reported every audio key as
missing and failed the Host checks job. Read the guide, expand its
grammar rows, compare it against every parser key (it documents the
legacy trio too), and take profile values from the accepted-values
column only. A new tooling test checks that keys dropped from a grammar
row are still reported.
events.author: midwan

events.title: fix(fwup): time out instead of reading the register after a stalled mirror
events.message:
fix(fwup): time out instead of reading the register after a stalled mirror

When the firmware advertises the status mirror and it does not advance
within the poll budget, the command is still running or the card is
wedged. Reading REG_ZZ_FWUP_STATUS then would hold the Amiga's bus until
the ARM answers, the hang the mirror path exists to avoid. Report
FWUP_STATUS_BUSY ("timed out waiting for firmware") instead. Nothing else
writes the mirror in the boot ROM window, so the fallback had no other
use.
events.author: midwan

events.title: fix(fwup): poll the firmware's status mirror instead of the register
events.message:
fix(fwup): poll the firmware's status mirror instead of the register

A FWUP status register read waits for the ARM main loop, so polling it
while the firmware runs a FatFs call holds the Amiga's Zorro cycle for
the whole SD write. When the firmware advertises the status mirror
(capability bit 11, the boot ROM window's last longword at 0x7FFC),
note it before each command and poll it for a new sequence, yielding
with Delay(1) after a spin budget; the first valid word after ROM
padding counts as new. Fall back to the register if the mirror never
moves. Older firmware keeps the register path.
events.author: midwan

events.title: Βήμα 128: μενού πλανήτη στην αρχή — τυχαίος ή ένας από τους τέσσερις
events.message:
Βήμα 128: μενού πλανήτη στην αρχή — τυχαίος ή ένας από τους τέσσερις

Ο παίκτης ζήτησε μενού στην αρχή του παιχνιδιού για τον τύπο του πλανήτη, και
διάλεξε: τέσσερις πλανήτες και τυχαίος, πριν από τη φόρτωση, βελάκια ή
χειριστήριο και FIRE/ENTER, μία γραμμή περιγραφής ο καθένας.

- src/boot.asm: μετά τον τίτλο, πριν διαβαστεί αρχείο, το CHOOSE A WORLD και
  πέντε γραμμές. KM TEST KEY για βελάκια, χειριστήριο 0, RETURN, μικρό ENTER,
  SPACE και τα δύο FIRE· μετράει μόνο ό,τι πατήθηκε τώρα, οπότε ένα RETURN
  κρατημένο από το RUN δεν διαλέγει μόνο του. Η επιλογή αναποδογυρίζεται με
  XOR #F0 κατευθείαν στην οθόνη (το firmware ήθελε 0,6 s ανά κίνηση), με την
  πάνω ROM σβηστή για λίγο. Ο φορτωτής 1.228 -> 1.677 bytes.
- src/gen.asm: η επιλογή έρχεται στο A. Για διαλεγμένο πλανήτη τα δύο κάτω bits
  του L γίνονται τέτοια ώστε (H ^ L) & 3 να είναι ο πλανήτης: το seed λέει
  ακόμη όλο τον κόσμο, και τίποτα μετά (σώσιμο, N, δοκιμές) δεν αλλάζει. Το
  μηδέν γίνεται H = #AC (κρατά τον πλανήτη 0)· +11 bytes.
- Οι περιγραφές είναι μετρημένες σε 24 κόσμους ανά πλανήτη (νερό, γη για
  χτίσιμο, φλέβες), όχι του πίνακα του §5.7.
- tests/menuread.py: η οθόνη του μενού διαβάζεται με τη γραμματοσειρά της ROM.
- tests/test_disc.py: το μενού, οι κινήσεις με βελάκια και χειριστήριο, το
  κρατημένο RETURN (αρνητικό), κάθε επιλογή ως το worldinfo, δύο τυχαίοι
  διαφορετικοί, ο κώδικας του seed σε 150 περιπτώσεις με τρία αρνητικά, η
  εκκίνηση από την επιλογή (420 frames, ταβάνι 450). Το αρνητικό χωρίς την
  επιστροφή στο track 0 ξαναχτίστηκε: ο μεγαλύτερος φορτωτής τελειώνει στο
  track 1 και το AMSDOS κινούσε την κεφαλή μόνο του· τώρα το byte του AMSDOS
  γίνεται 0, όπως με φορτωτή ενός track.
- tests/test_save.py: διαλέγει τον τυχαίο σε κάθε εκκίνηση.
- DESIGN: §5.7, §13.2, §13.3, οι πίνακες του §13, §15.

events.message:
feat(app): fall back to the site's Jaguar CD artwork when libretro-thumbnails misses

libretro-thumbnails has no Jaguar CD repository (libretro-thumbnails#141). For a
disc, after libretro-thumbnails has no art for a type, ask the project site mirror
(jaguar.provenance-emu.com/thumbnails/Atari - Jaguar CD/...). Upstream is always
first, so its art wins once it exists. Each source has its own cache folder and miss
markers: mirror art is cached under thumbnails/Atari - Jaguar CD/ and never shadows
an upstream copy fetched later; the mirror's misses expire after 7 days (upstream's
stay at 30). A transient upstream failure does not fall through to the mirror, and
carts never use it. Config key library.art_mirror (empty = off); downloads-off still
disables everything.

events.title: feat(app): optional local code signing and notarization
events.message:
feat(app): optional local code signing and notarization

app/packaging/local-package.sh [--sign] [--notarize] packages a normal build on a
developer machine and signs it with a certificate found locally:

- macOS: VJ_SIGN_IDENTITY, else the newest-expiring valid "Developer ID Application"
  identity (chosen by SHA-1 so renewed duplicates are unambiguous), else "Apple
  Development", else ad hoc. --notarize uses VJ_NOTARY_PROFILE (notarytool keychain
  profile) or APPLE_NOTARY_KEY_ID/ISSUER_ID/KEY_PATH, then staples and runs spctl.
- Windows (Git Bash): VJ_SIGN_PFX(+_PASSWORD), else VJ_SIGN_CERT_SHA1, else signtool
  /a, else unsigned; signs exe, dlls and the installer when Inno Setup is present.
- Settings come from the environment, then a gitignored repo-root .env (only VJ_*/
  APPLE_* keys, nothing evaluated, op:// references resolved with `op` if installed).
- -DVJ_APP_SIGN_DEV_BUILD=ON signs the dev executable after each macOS build.

codesign.sh's notarize step also accepts a keychain profile or a .p8 path; CI's
base64 secret path is unchanged. package.sh gets an env-guarded signing hook.

Refs #839

events.message:
Audio capture: channel levels, PSG writes and two WAV files to compare (MCP, GUI, command line)

  - MCP - audio capture for finding sound bugs: emu_audio_capture_start writes into a folder, in
  emulated time, every change of the output level of the sound channels (speaker and PSG channels,
  events.csv), every write to the PSG with its decoding (psg_writes.csv), the sound rendered exactly
  in emulated time (reference.wav) and the sound of the emulator's audio output path, i.e. what the
  user hears (sdl.wav, same format for a direct comparison); capture.json describes the capture.
  emu_audio_capture_stop and emu_audio_capture_status. See mcp-server/tools-overview.md.

  - Audio capture in the GUI and on the command line: Tools -> Audio Capture -> Record Audio Capture
  (Alt+Q) records into a new folder in its own output folder (default audio_captures next to the
  emulator) what the sound hardware does - changes of the channel levels, PSG writes, the exact
  sound and the sound you hear (two WAV files to compare); AUDIO with the captured time is shown in
  the top left corner of the picture, a notification reports the folder. Settings... sets the output
  folder and selects the files to write. --audio-capture <folder> starts it right after startup,
  --audio-capture-frames <count> stops it after the given number of frames (with --headless the
  emulator then exits). See audio-capture.md.

  - Docs: audio-capture.md, command line options in README, hotkeys, MCP tools overview.

  Thanks to Jan Rysavy for the idea.

events.title: FM output: Paula-driven 4-block ring (AUD3 interrupt); smooth display starts from a snapshot
events.message:
FM output: Paula-driven 4-block ring (AUD3 interrupt); smooth display starts from a snapshot

From a review of the FM regression on the PiStorm preset:
- The 2-half buffer picked its half by VBlank parity and assumed N
  samples last exactly one frame. At 60 Hz the frame is 263 lines of
  227/228 clocks, not 262 x 227, so playback drifted into the half being
  written (crackle in waves); FMXFrame also ran either side of the NTSC
  VBlank and late frames wrote a half twice.
- Now a ring of 4 blocks: the AUD3 interrupt (level 4, FMXAud) queues the
  next written block when Paula takes one, or repeats the one playing if
  the emulation is late. FMXFrame writes the next free block and sets N
  from the ring's fill (nominal -2/0/+2), so the emulation's frame rate and
  Paula's clock agree on average at any display rate. Pitch is unchanged
  (step per sample). The OS level 4 vector is saved and restored (exit,
  Workbench mode). Counters FMXUnder/FMXOver (FMXCNT test builds).
- Smooth display: the first frame becomes snapshot 0 at once, so the live
  templates (with the back buffer's plane pointers) are never shown (Space
  Manbow's title logo over the first game frame on BigMig).

events.title: feat(app): identify .chd and .cdi discs; match non-Redump rips by name
events.message:
feat(app): identify .chd and .cdi discs; match non-Redump rips by name

The library skipped .chd and .cdi ("nothing cheap to hash") and name-matched
only on an exact file stem, so most disc rips showed no title.

- .chd: CRC32 of track 1 rebuilt the way the core reads it (2352 of each
  2448-byte frame, audio put back in .bin byte order, virtual pregap left
  out, tracks padded to 4 frames); CHDs the core refuses (several audio
  tracks, no CHSE) are not hashed.
- .cdi: best-effort track 1 CRC from the descriptor layout.
- A disc whose checksum is not in the dat falls back to a normalized name
  match of the file name, then the folder name (case, punctuation, region and
  Track/Disc tags ignored; exact title first, then a unique longer title,
  never a guess between two games).
- Tiles say how a disc was identified in the tooltip.
- Scan cache v2: old caches re-hash only disc images that had no checksum.

Verified against synthetic uncompressed CHD/CDI images; real Redump CHDs are
still to be checked.

Refs #838

events.title: fix(fwup): time out instead of reading the register after a stalled mirror
events.message:
fix(fwup): time out instead of reading the register after a stalled mirror

When the firmware advertises the status mirror and it does not advance
within the poll budget, the command is still running or the card is
wedged. Reading REG_ZZ_FWUP_STATUS then would hold the Amiga's bus until
the ARM answers, the hang the mirror path exists to avoid. Report
FWUP_STATUS_BUSY ("timed out waiting for firmware") instead. Nothing else
writes the mirror in the boot ROM window, so the fallback had no other
use.
events.author: midwan

events.title: feat(debug): merge WinUAE optional GDB remote server (#2434)
events.message:
feat(debug): merge WinUAE optional GDB remote server (#2434)

* feat(debug): add optional GDB remote server

Port of WinUAE c7334f41 (tonioni/WinUAE#532). The server is off by
default and is enabled with debugging_features=gdbserver and gdb_port
(default 2345). It listens on 127.0.0.1 for one client and drives the
existing debugger: registers, physical memory, single step, PC
breakpoints, CPU data watchpoints, range stepping and the memory map.

The event-pump poll goes into Amiberry's handle_events(). The sources are
added to the CMake and libretro builds, the packet parser test runs from
tests/test_gdb_protocol.sh, and docs/gdb-debugging.md describes usage.

* fix(debug): report GDB FPU registers as unavailable

GDB's m68k register set also lists fp0-fp7, fpcontrol, fpstatus and
fpiaddr. The server answered p packets for them with E01, so
"info registers" stopped with 'Could not fetch register "fpcontrol"'.
Reply with x digits instead, which GDB shows as <unavailable>.

* fix(debug): give unavailable GDB FPU registers their full width

fp0-fp7 are 12-byte registers in GDB's m68k description, so answer p for
them with 24 x digits; fpcontrol, fpstatus and fpiaddr keep 8.

* fix(debug): pause PPC on GDB stops and map the UAE boot ROM

The remote stop path returned before uae_ppc_pause(1), so a running PPC
CPU kept changing guest memory while GDB had the machine stopped. Pause
it around gdb_server_stop(), as the console debugger does.

The memory map listed only ABFLAG_ROM and ABFLAG_RAM banks. rtarea is
ABFLAG_ROMIN, so GDB refused to read the UAE boot ROM that read_memory()
already allows. Report ROMIN banks as rom.

* fix(debug): reject GDB watchpoints beyond the 24-bit address space

With 24-bit addressing the memwatch mapper only restores the first 256
banks, so a watchpoint at or above 0x01000000 left a stale wrapper in
mem_banks after removal. The CPU never generates such addresses there
anyway; refuse them.

* fix(debug): serialize GDB server access with the threaded CPU

With cpu_threaded, debug() and gdb_server_stop() can run on the CPU
thread while the main thread keeps calling gdb_server_poll() from
handle_events(), so both threads used the session, pending output and
socket at once. Guard all server state with a mutex, skip main-thread
polls while a stop is in progress so the stopped thread runs every
command, and make gdb_server_connected() an atomic flag.

* fix(debug): keep debugger reads from tripping watchpoints; reject 24-bit-unreachable breakpoints

debug() read the opcode at PC (and, for some trace modes, task data)
with get_*_debug() before inside_debugger was set, so a read or access
watchpoint covering that memory triggered on the debugger's own read
and reported a spurious watchpoint stop on the next resume. Suppress
memwatch for the trace-check block and restore the previous state.

With 24-bit addressing debug() compares PC breakpoints against the
masked PC, so a remote breakpoint at or above 0x01000000 was accepted
but could never trigger. Refuse it on insert.

* fix(debug): disable the GDB server with the threaded CPU

With cpu_threaded, debug() runs on either the CPU or the main thread
while the other keeps executing. Remote breakpoint, watchpoint and
detach handling then change debugger tables and remap or free memory
banks under a running thread, and a disconnect seen by the main thread
called detach() while the CPU thread was running.

Do not listen in that mode and log why. Every GDB call now stays on the
main thread again, so the mutex added in d8f0b42b9 is no longer needed
and gdb_server.cpp returns to the upstream version plus this check.

From an independent review of BigMig-only symptoms (blink, glyphs):

  rebuilt was the one on screen until the next frame start (stale or
  half-written line routines: palette events skipped for a frame).

The grid takes the four left rows (24 cells: the 21 verbs and up to three

descriptions: the message, word by word, and on the last row the stock row

print in the result column.

Tests read the idle loop from build/wildmenu.bin (common.idle_bytes) and
answer the start menu with key 1 for the Sierra; test_menu_bar covers the

commands. Everything in make test passes but the uncommitted night-terrain

events.title: httpd: size the href escape for three-byte UTF-8, refuse what does not fit
events.message:
httpd: size the href escape for three-byte UTF-8, refuse what does not fit

httpd_escape was x6, two bytes of UTF-8 per local byte; ISO-8859-2 and
other codesets map bytes to U+0800 and up, three bytes and nine escaped
characters.  It is x9 now (+1110 bytes of BSS), the exact worst case of
the longest href httpd builds.

A href that still cannot be built (the joined path longer than its
buffer) used to come back as "/", a URL to another resource.  It is
NULL now: listing and PROPFIND entries are skipped as too large, the
lock and multistatus answers fail as any other overflow does, and the
drawer redirect is 414.

Host test: httppath_escapes escapes the longest href of three-byte
characters into the x9 size and refuses it at x6.

events.title: Neowilderness: the four 80-column rows as a command surface (lot 8, step 2)
events.message:
Neowilderness: the four 80-column rows as a command surface (lot 8, step 2)

Rows 20-22, columns 0-37 hold the grid of verbs (contextual ones first:
EXIT, ENTER, IGNORE SCARE ATTACK), six proportional cells per row, scrolled
by row with ^/V marks in the separator column; RETURN or UP opens it, the
arrows move, RETURN opens a verb's list (durations, directions, admissible
items in cells of 12, ounces) and composes the keyboard's text in inbuf;
menu_noun carries the item chosen (COTTN SOCKS is not a vocabulary word).
DOWN on the empty line shows STATUS; typed commands stay accepted; a
command from the grid leaves it open. Columns 40-78 hold the last message,
placed word by word on three rows, and the stock row (FOOD, WATER, HERE)
when the third row is free; row 23 shows the command as the parser reads
it, without a cursor, then the key hints. The load report prints its rows
in the result column.

Memory (docs/MEMORY.md section 11): src/menu.s is resident at $BA00-$BDFF
(the former ProDOS I/O buffer: the loader reads with its own at $AB00);
the grid, lists and tables sleep in the HGR rows 176-191 of both banks
(never shown in mixed mode nor drawn) and are copied to $B000-$B5FF at
every prompt; the message routines moved to WILDGAME, the hints to
RESIDENT, nine temporaries to zero page $F0. Volume 250/280 blocks.

Start menu: the Sierra Nevada first, keyed 1, chosen by RETURN alone
(tools/genmenu.py MENU_ORDER, menu_regions/menu_rows tables; the H screen
follows the same order; tests translate region numbers in menu_keys); a
blank line under the title of the loading page. Also carries the earlier
uncommitted lighter loading page and one-line scenario menu.

Tests: tests/test_menu_bar.py (grid, lists, composition equal to the typed
commands, contexts, ESC, numeric prompt) added to make test; the tests
read the result column through common.result_rows.

events.title: textconv: a UTF-8 system codeset is identity everywhere
events.message:
textconv: a UTF-8 system codeset is identity everywhere

txt_codeset_open() said TXT_CS_UTF8 but returned the ISO-8859-1 set,
and httpd dropped the flag, so on a UTF-8 system a disk name "B C3 BC"
went out as B%C3%83%C2%BC and B%C3%BC came in as "B FC"; /shell and the
clipboard had the same wrong mapping.

The codeset now carries it: txt_codeset.utf8.  With it, UTF-8 in is
validated and passes byte for byte (a name, a paste, a /shell
keystroke), malformed UTF-8 is still '?' or 400, and local bytes go out
as they are.  The clipboard and /shell copies of the codeset carry the
field.  ssh already turned conversion off on the flag.

Host tests: text_codeset, httppath_escapes and console_clipboard_text
cover a UTF-8 system codeset (B C3 BC <-> B%C3%BC, ä€ paste, C3 28).

events.title: Per-PC profiler: executions, T-states and WAIT per instruction address (MCP and GUI)
events.message:
Per-PC profiler: executions, T-states and WAIT per instruction address (MCP and GUI)

  - Debugger - the CPU Profiler window has a new Per PC tab: for every instruction address it counts
  executions, T-states (including wait states) and WAIT states, also in code that is jumped to
  rather than called. Columns can be sorted, a range of addresses can be shown, a left click opens
  the address in the Disassembly; the status line splits the time into instructions, waiting in HALT
  and the rest (mainly interrupt acknowledge). Export CSV writes all addresses. See
  debugger/profiler.md.

  - MCP - per-PC profiler for finding where a program spends its time: emu_profiler_pc_start,
  emu_profiler_pc_stop, emu_profiler_pc_reset, emu_profiler_pc_get (busiest addresses with the
  nearest symbol, sorted by T-states, executions, WAIT or address, optional address range) and
  emu_profiler_pc_export (CSV). Time outside instructions is reported separately (halt_idle,
  other_tstates). With the profiler off the emulation is not slowed down. See
  mcp-server/tools-overview.md.

  - Docs: per-PC profiler in debugger/profiler.md (section 10) and the MCP tools overview.

  Thanks to Jan Rysavy for the idea.

events.title: codesets.library: build with stack arguments, as upstream does
events.message:
codesets.library: build with stack arguments, as upstream does

The tree compiles with -mregparm=3; upstream's code passes arguments on
the stack in two places: libinit.c's stackswap_call asm (it reads its
three arguments from the stack and pushes LibInit's argument) and the
qsort()/bsearch() callbacks.  The first OpenLibrary(), which ramlib runs
through stackswap_call because its stack is under 64K, swapped to a
garbage stack and hung the machine (ramlib's tc_SPLower/tc_SPUpper read
0).  -mregparm=0 for this target; the 14 -Wcallconv-mismatch warnings
the build printed are gone.

Seen with ssh under Amiberry: the guest hung right after ssh opened
codesets.library.  With this build ssh opens it, maps the text and
types back UTF-8.

project.status: active; optional loopback GDB server with range stepping and memory-map reporting
project.notes: Actively maintained Windows Amiga emulator and a key compatibility/debugging tool for Amiga reverse engineering and retro development. Tracked as adjacent tooling rather than as a source-reconstruction target. Current main adds an opt-in, unauthenticated loopback GDB remote server shared by Windows and Unix builds. It exposes 18 m68k integer registers, physical RAM/ROM access, stepping, PC breakpoints and bounded data watchpoints; subsequent commits add standard vCont range stepping and complete RAM/ROM XML memory maps. It is disabled by default, single-client and local-only, and its memory addresses are physical rather than guest-MMU translations. project.title: MegaST — Atari ST/STE MiSTery-derived FPGA core for MEGA65
project.display_title: MegaST — Atari ST/STE MiSTery-derived FPGA core for MEGA65

runtime_profiles.name: MegaST v1.0 on MEGA65 R6
runtime_profiles.notes: Primary README reports stable real-hardware R6 operation with floppy/hard-disk images, TOS 1.04, named games and additional tester-reported TOS/game configurations. Requires an SD card, tos.img and user media. No 45GS02 requirement or guest ST-RAM size is treated as a host CPU/RAM minimum.

runtime_profiles.name: MegaST v1.0 on MEGA65 R3/R3A
runtime_profiles.notes: The dedicated R3/R3A core keeps 512 KiB of guest ST RAM in FPGA block RAM because HyperRAM is too slow for cycle-exact timing. Upstream reports R3A operation including hard-disk images. Viking and STEroids modes are unavailable. The 512 KiB value is guest configuration, not host minimum RAM.

source_language: Atari ST/STE/Mega STE hardware and ROM behavior
types: generic FPGA system recreation, substantive platform port
project.status: v1.0 stable; upstream-tested on MEGA65 R6 and R3A; R4/R5 untested
project.notes: Ports the tracked MiSTer AtariST/MiSTery core to MEGA65 with MiSTer2MEGA65. Its machine wrapper, SDRAM/ACSI controller, native keyboard, TOS loader, RTC, video scaling and virtual-drive integration establish a distinct target port rather than a mirror. Version 1.0 is the first stable release. Primary documentation reports real R6 operation, tester-reported R3A hard-disk support, TOS 1.62 and named games; R4/R5 and several optional devices remain untested. The R3/R3A core keeps 512 KiB of guest ST RAM in FPGA block RAM because HyperRAM is too slow for cycle-exact timing; that is not a host RAM minimum. Releases through 0.4.10 could damage hard-disk images when writing. v1.0 restores remembered media, centres additional HDMI modes and ships distinct R3/R3A, R4, R5 and R6 core files. TOS and user media are required; EmuTOS ships in release archives, while proprietary Atari TOS remains separate. AUTHORS identifies the FX68K cycle-accurate 68000 CPU. The output is an FPGA bitstream/framework integration, not a program targeting the MEGA65’s default 45GS02 CPU, so no target CPU is inferred. GPL v3 aggregate includes upstream GPL v2-or-later and FX68K GPL v3 components. before.name: MEGA65 R6 (upstream-tested beta)
before.notes: README explicitly reports 0.4.7 beta tested on a real R6. Requires the board’s SDRAM, SD card, tos.img and user media. R4/R5 projects are advertised but explicitly untested; R3/R3A are unsupported. No 45GS02 requirement or guest ST-RAM size is used as a host CPU/RAM minimum.

after.name: MegaST v1.0 on MEGA65 R6
after.notes: Primary README reports stable real-hardware R6 operation with floppy/hard-disk images, TOS 1.04, named games and additional tester-reported TOS/game configurations. Requires an SD card, tos.img and user media. No 45GS02 requirement or guest ST-RAM size is treated as a host CPU/RAM minimum.

after.name: MegaST v1.0 on MEGA65 R3/R3A
after.notes: The dedicated R3/R3A core keeps 512 KiB of guest ST RAM in FPGA block RAM because HyperRAM is too slow for cycle-exact timing. Upstream reports R3A operation including hard-disk images. Viking and STEroids modes are unavailable. The 512 KiB value is guest configuration, not host minimum RAM.

change_details.after: v1.0 stable; upstream-tested on MEGA65 R6 and R3A; R4/R5 untested

project.title: Lanthorn — interactive-fiction disk and format interpreter
project.display_title: Lanthorn — interactive-fiction disk and format interpreter
project.status: v0.9.5; runnable multi-format interactive-fiction and disk-image interpreter
project.notes: Runnable Rust terminal interpreter for Z-machine, Glulx and Scott Adams formats, with loaders for original ADF, ST, D64, DSK and other disk images, automapping and artwork rendering. v0.9.3 moves new installations to platform-standard data folders, adds a migration command and Glulx border defaults, and bounds runaway stories plus damaged media/image/audio handling. This is historical story/media format implementation, not a claim of recovered game source. v0.9.5 adds game-probed automap exits and non-cardinal room placement, Scott Adams autocomplete, and single-pass/lazy media reads that reduce a documented 354 MiB CD launch from repeated full-image reads to about 27 MiB. It also corrects narrower-window save restoration, multi-command mapping and platform data-folder migration. The following unreleased compass styling is not promoted into the release status. Evidence: https://github.com/sharkusk/lanthorn/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md https://github.com/sharkusk/lanthorn/releases/tag/v0.9.5

project.title: ghidra-retro-machines
project.display_title: Ghidra Retro Machines — bank-aware loaders and retro CPU languages
project.status: Active; deterministic overlay-reference cleanup and decided-branch dead-code analysis
project.notes: Ghidra extension for banked C64/C128/PET PRG and NES iNES analysis, with SPC700 and 65C816 language variants. The current NES pass bounds split low/high pointer tables by the next section gap: Dodge shrinks from 64 to 26 entries, River City Ransom from 64 to 27 and Mega Man 2 from 255 to 15. Upstream reports build-and-test SUITE OK and 29 NES baseline passes plus the three corrected fixtures. Existing 65C816 oracle-defect guards and language limitations remain; these gates show bounded analysis improvements, not universal correctness. The reviewed commit explicitly credits Claude Opus 5.5. Evidence: https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/6556e84ff267a0c96e7c89c5dbe2d3c3777d2aad The next analyzer pass extends RAM save-slot proofs across admitted cross-function jumps and narrowly recognized save-helper calls, while preserving conservative abandon rules and declining unresolved overlay-bank cases. Upstream reports 33 NES tests passing; the separate Dragon Power symbol-output flap remains documented. Evidence: https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/3f983b0189e67e2f8337804e0c2beb46c5483d44 The latest bank-analysis passes persist provenance for analyzer-created overlay references so later rounds retract stale targets without deleting user-owned references, and remove fall-through code only when a conditional branch is provably taken and no flow, entry point, function or user label preserves the old path. Upstream reports deterministic NES corpus updates and passing synthetic/JUnit gates; these are bounded analyzer-correctness receipts, not universal decompilation correctness. Evidence: https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/475eeadd4fb50ad045bd8e01dd428243279bfe2d https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/1251af61b1d65c8849bc90795d186ee274938db4

Evidence: https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/d3b50c77c364455674d783c6bf4d4755777dbc44 https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/ec51d5c1b2f58b51b235fc2145abb384d55b597c https://github.com/yeager/firestaff/commit/da1e85756e618dd321ec42257cb31afbb2b341d1 v3.0.376 receipts now cover DM1 Amiga 2.0 resume, the published Linux x86-64 AppImage under QEMU on an ARM64 VM, and the DM2 FM Towns selected-hero HUD icon sourced from authenticated interface data. They do not establish native x86-64 hardware, physical input, aura/panel completion or full visual parity. The release also publishes Android and iOS arm64 artifacts; publication alone is not runtime verification. project.status: v8.4.0 published; current development fixes libretro saves, CIA timing and MMU cache handling
project.notes: General-purpose UAE/WinUAE-derived Amiga machine emulator. v8.4.0 publishes Windows ARM64/x86-64, macOS universal and Linux ARM64/x86-64 assets, establishing upstream compilable and runnable variants without establishing minimum hardware. The release adds ZZ9000 AHI/SANA-II/SDK/MHI/MPEGA/image/ZZPlay support, optional external MiniGL and dma-buf paths, relative media paths, cartridge and .A1000 ROM handling, runtime GL fallback, Raspberry Pi 4 drawing improvements, ARM64 JIT fixes, FreeBSD amd64/aarch64 CI and broad networking/display/input/libretro/Android corrections. m68k remains the guest CPU; ARM/x86/RISC-V/LoongArch are host families, not guest minima. External Kickstart ROMs and game media remain outside the GPL source grant. No independent execution or equivalence test was performed. Evidence: https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/releases/tag/v8.4.0 https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/blob/master/README.md Post-v8.4.0 development fixes apply RetroArch auto-loaded save states only after the emulated CPU loop is active, correct CIA-B time-of-day increments in fast and programmed-sync paths, preserve open-file keys across host renames, honor cache-inhibited pages in 68030/68040/68060 fast-cache paths and restore USE_PPC=OFF linking. These are source-level fixes on current main, not a new published release or independently executed verification. Evidence: https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/71ac39e07d339d9d8e296e15db79642e6ab5619a https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/3b5e647578e667adff3a88ef9557e2f3702b8ebe https://github.com/BlitterStudio/amiberry/commit/bdc870008140cff3dbbb4379df94aa92d7322e27

events.title: Wall overlays: unique blocks are no longer shared with other walls (#66)
events.message:
Wall overlays: unique blocks are no longer shared with other walls (#66)

Walls with overlays are loaded as unique blocks (Duplicate_or_load_block)
because the overlays are drawn into the wall graphics. If the wall graphics
were still in memory and unused (e.g. from the last visit of the map), the
cached block itself was claimed as the unique block, but it could still be
found by its file and subfile number until the overlays were drawn. The
unique walls are sorted first in the batch (bit 15), so a wall without
overlays but with the same graphics then shared this block with
Reallocate_memory and showed the overlays of the other wall (e.g. riddle
mouths on all walls of Newlake, wrong windows and pillars in Illien).
As the painted block is removed when it is freed, this alternated between
wrong and correct overlays every time the map was entered.

The unique block (the claimed cached block or the copy) is now invalidated
at once, so no other load can find and share it.

events.title: Βήμα 127: όσες μηχανές τρώνε μέταλλο αφήνουν 30, και ο παίκτης-σενάριο μετρά τον αέρα
events.message:
Βήμα 127: όσες μηχανές τρώνε μέταλλο αφήνουν 30, και ο παίκτης-σενάριο μετρά τον αέρα

Ο χρήστης ζήτησε να διορθωθούν τα ανοιχτά. Μια SPARES με μέταλλο να φάει το
έτρωγε όλο, και η αποικία δεν μπορούσε να χτίσει τίποτα· διάλεξε απόθεμα:
όσες τρώνε μέταλλο σταματούν όταν πέσει κάτω από 30, όσο κοστίζει ένα
ορυχείο. Οχι όριο ανά προϊόν, ούτε διακόπτη ανά μηχανή.

- Ποιες: WEAPONS, CHIPS, ROBOTS, SPARES — όλες έχουν το μέταλλο πρώτη είσοδο,
  και το tools/econ.py το ελέγχει (assert): ο Z80 κοιτάζει μόνο την πρώτη.
  Σταματημένη ούτε τρώει ούτε ζητά ρεύμα. Το χτίσιμο, ο εξοπλισμός και το
  εμπόριο δεν περιορίζονται.
- Πότε: το st_check, στην αρχή κάθε κύκλου ροής, όπου κάθε μηχανή τρέχει μία
  φορά ανά κύκλο, γράφει το ec_keep (src/stock.asm, δίπλα στο ec_full).
- Χωρίς κόστος με μέταλλο: το ec_setfull, που ήδη ξαναγράφει την τρίτη κλήση
  εισόδου, ξαναγράφει και την πρώτη (erm_c1): erm_in ή erm_ink (cp S_METAL ·
  jp nz,erm_in · scf · ret). Με το απόθεμα ενεργό οι άλλες πληρώνουν 5 us, οι
  τέσσερις σταματούν: στην αποικία του test_sim οι βαριές επισκέψεις της θέσης
  11 7.090 και 12.160 us, χωρίς 8.390 και 12.520 — φθηνότερο. Οχι το bit 7
  της ποσότητας στη συνταγή (μηδέν us): μέσα σε έναν κύκλο το μέταλλο μπορεί
  να ανέβει πάνω από 128 και η SPARES θα έτρωγε 129 με τη μία.
- Το wheel_reset σβήνει το ec_keep· το LOAD_STATE του simtest το παίρνει από
  την αναφορά.

Μετρημένο με το σχέδιο spares (12 κόσμοι, 30 sol): τα ανταλλακτικά ως 12-14
αντί για 26-38, εργαστήρια 6 -> 11, ορυχεία 7 -> 10, ζωντανές 0 -> 5, πείνα
65 -> 12 θάνατοι — και αέρας 7 -> 43: το σχέδιο ξοδεύει το μέταλλο ως το
τελευταίο σε θόλους πριν από τον δεύτερο ηλιακό, και οι νύχτες παίρνουν το
οξυγόνο (BEEF 3: ρεύμα 18 με ζήτηση 22).

Ο ΠΑΙΚΤΗΣ-ΣΕΝΑΡΙΟ (tools/play.py, ship_ok): ένα πλοίο μόνο όταν το οξυγόνο
που βγαίνει — το χαμηλότερο του τελευταίου sol — φτάνει για όλους και τους
τέσσερις, και τα γεύματα φτάνουν πέντε sol και δεν πέφτουν. Ως τότε μετρούσε
θόλους οξυγόνου: στο ACE1 3 πέθαναν 33. Σχέδιο long, 40 sol: 9/12 ζωντανές,
18 θάνατοι αντί για 135, όλοι από πείνα στους τρεις κόσμους χωρίς θερμοκήπια·
τέσσερις αποικίες φτάνουν τους 10 και κρατιούνται εκεί, με την τροφή να πέφτει
(το βιοπλαστικό τελειώνει πριν από τα δεύτερα θερμοκήπια).

Δοκιμές. test_sim: νέος έλεγχος «μέταλλο» — κύκλος ροής με 29, 30, 200 και
ολόκληρο σάρωμα της παραγωγής στον ίδιο Z80, ίδια bytes με την αναφορά· με 29
καμία από τις τέσσερις δεν φτιάχνει τίποτα και το μέταλλο δεν πέφτει, με 30
και 200 φτιάχνουν· από το ec_keep σε 200 σβήνει· το κόστος των βαριών
επισκέψεων (ταβάνι 12.170)· τέσσερα αρνητικά (όλες περνούν, η πρώτη κλήση
μένει, όρια 31 και 29)· ο τροχός: το wheel_reset σβήνει το ec_keep, με
αρνητικό. Η αρμάθα μεταφέρει το ec_keep όπως το ec_full.
Χρόνοι: ο κύκλος ροής +35-40 us (test_sim 8.670 -> 8.710, 9.050 -> 9.090·
test_drill 1.660 -> 1.695, 4.076 -> 4.111, 2.037 -> 2.072, το ανέβασμα 2.530
-> 2.565)· το game_new +19 us (το wheel_reset)· test_reach ΒΗΜΑ +10 us (η
φάση του ρολογιού του HUD)· -1 us σε πολλές μετρήσεις ρουτινών που δεν
άλλαξαν (ήχος, κρούσεις, σχεδίαση, τοποθέτηση): η μέτρηση, όχι ο κώδικάς τους,
που είναι ίδιος· test_disc 550 -> 570 frames (άλλος κόσμος).
Τα ταβάνια ανέβηκαν όσο τα μετρημένα.
Μνήμη: τράπεζα 0 +26 (494 ελεύθερα), b6code +18 (1.011). DESIGN: §6.5 (νέα
υποενότητα), §10.1 (νέα υποενότητα για τον παίκτη), §13, §15, §4.2.

events.title: Neowilderness: complete constellations, night turns that scroll, new band layout, parallel-branch integration
events.message:
Neowilderness: complete constellations, night turns that scroll, new band layout, parallel-branch integration

Stars (docs/STARS.md section 14): the catalogue is built by figures, 42
complete constellations (262 stars, to V 4.95) replace the 44 faintest lone
stars, still 282 stars; the selection class is figure membership (class 0 is
drawn in every night mood, a full list drops fillers first; 16-bit index
compare in st_append); the magnitude is in the pixel (3 rows for the first
magnitude through a second entry, 2 tinted rows below V 3.0, 1 grey row
above); the projection above 45 degrees shares sin(alt) evenly so the
Big Dipper and Cassiopeia stay in the view at culmination; the dark night
sky is dark blue so the ridge shows; turn_view scrolls in the dark night
instead of redrawing the whole view (a 22.5-degree turn now costs 0.9-1.3 s
at night, like the day).

Survival band: HEALTH alone on the upper left, the alert or hint below it;
the clock and the journey day (DAY 1 on the crash day) on the upper right,
the worse of hunger and thirst below; the right panel starts 4 pixels after

fix(app): BIOS files in library folders are recognized in any case and can be copied where the core reads them

The library already classified BIOS files found under user folders, but two
things kept them from being useful: a name match was case-sensitive (JAGCD.BIN
fell through to Cartridges as a playable game), and the core only reads BIOS
files from its system folder under fixed names, so a BIOS found elsewhere was
only ever labelled 'Not read here'. Names now match ignoring case, and a BIOS
tile the core would read from the system folder offers Copy, which writes it
there under the name the core searches for (never over an existing file).

events.title: Screenshots, MZ-800 hardware scroll fixes, MCP VRAM and I:R state
events.message:
Screenshots, MZ-800 hardware scroll fixes, MCP VRAM and I:R state

  - New feature: screenshots (Tools -> Screenshot) on all platforms. Save Screenshot (Alt+F) saves a
  PNG of the picture shown in the window into the output folder (default: screenshots next to the
  emulator) with a name made of the platform and time, Save Screenshot As... asks for the file name.
  In Settings... you choose the area (whole frame with border, or the picture without the border),
  the scale (native computer dots - 320x200 or 640x200 picture - or 1x to 4x with the aspect ratio
  of the window, 2x = window at 100 %) and the output folder; the settings are saved in the
  configuration. See screenshots.md.

  - MCP - emu_screenshot_save_to_file has new optional parameters area (full frame or the picture
  without the border), scale (framebuffer pixels as before, native dots of the computer - 320x200 or
  640x200 picture - or 1 to 4 times with the aspect ratio of the emulator window) and crop (a
  cut-out of the native image). See mcp-server/headless-mode.md.

  - CHANGE: MCP - emu_set_register with IR now writes the complete I:R pair (previously only bits
  0-6 of R, I unchanged) and emu_set_cpu_flags writes all 8 bits of R including bit 7, the same as
  the LD R,A instruction. A saved CPU state can thus be restored exactly. Editing R in the CPU
  window of the debugger still keeps bit 7.

  - MCP - emulator://periph/gdg on the MZ-800 also returns the VRAM access registers (vramctrl:
  write format WF with the write mode and planes, read format RF with search mode and planes, VBANK)
  and the hardware scroll registers (hwscroll: SOF, SSA, SEA, SW in the units written to the ports,
  and whether the scroll is active).

  - BUGFIX: MZ-800 hardware scroll - a change of a scroll register (SOF, SW, SSA, SEA) in the middle
  of a picture line was applied also to the part of the line the beam had already drawn. The drawn
  part now keeps the previous scroll position.

  - BUGFIX: Debugger - the I/O ports window showed the hardware scroll registers SOF, SW, SSA and
  SEA of the MZ-800 shifted (e.g. 28h after writing A5h to SOF). It now shows the values the program
  wrote.

  - Internal fixes: a queued timer event of a removed timer could read freed memory or fire another
  timer; debugger windows are not drawn before the debugger is initialized; indexed images with a
  row padding were converted to textures shifted.

  - Docs: MCP document emulator://docs/screenshot_workflow, screenshots.md, and the MCP tools
  overview now lists every tool.

  Thanks to Jan Rysavy, whose fork (github.com/janrysavy/mz800emu) pointed out several of these
  problems and ideas.

events.title: fix(app): Settings shows when the Netplay window (or --option) pins a core option
events.message:
fix(app): Settings shows when the Netplay window (or --option) pins a core option

Root cause: CoreHost::optionValue()/GET_VARIABLE give a session override
(overrideOption) precedence over the saved value. Since the Netplay window
(#888) the app pins virtualjaguar_netlink (link mode) and, when joining or
hosting, virtualjaguar_netlink_host / _port with such overrides for as long
as a session is configured. drawOption() still let the user pick a value:
setOptionValue() saved it, but the combo kept displaying (and the core kept
reading) the override, so network settings looked dead while every other
category worked. (Same for --option.)

The overrides must stay -- they are what makes the Netplay window work and
they are deliberately never saved -- so the row now says so: CoreHost gains
optionOverridden(key), and drawOption() greys the combo and adds a one-line
note to Disconnect in the Netplay menu. A pick made after Disconnect shows
and persists as before.

Test: vj_network_options_test (ctest network_options) drives the real core
for every option in the "network" category: picks must show immediately and
across frames, must not re-push the definitions (the UI iterates them), and
with a Netplay session active the mode/host/port rows must report
optionOverridden (before the fix: 37 failures); after Disconnect every pick
shows.

Refs #833
Refs #888

events.title: Βήμα 126: ο δεύτερος και ο τρίτος εργάτης του ορυχείου έρχονται μετά τις μηχανές
events.message:
Βήμα 126: ο δεύτερος και ο τρίτος εργάτης του ορυχείου έρχονται μετά τις μηχανές

Ο χρήστης ζήτησε να διορθωθούν οι χειριστές που έλειπαν, και διάλεξε: ο
πρώτος εργάτης κάθε ορυχείου κρατά τη θέση του, ο δεύτερος και ο τρίτος
έρχονται μετά από κάθε μηχανή.

Μετρημένο πρώτα: ο tools/play.py κατέγραφε τι κάνει κάθε άποικος σε κάθε
δείγμα (12 κόσμοι, σχέδιο long, sol 3-40). Το Operate του εργοστασίου έμενε
αδιάθετο στο 75% των δειγμάτων· οι εργάτες περνούσαν 27% στο ορυχείο και 7%
στο εργοστάσιο. Ολες οι Drill είχαν 4, πάνω από το Operate του εργοστασίου
(3): με έξι αποίκους δύο έσκαβαν και η METAL περίμενε με το μετάλλευμα να
μαζεύεται.

- dr_post (src/drill.asm): DRILL_PRIO (4) χωρίς κανέναν στο ορυχείο,
  DRILL_LOW (2) με κάποιον — κάτω από κάθε room_prio. Γράφει την τιμή στο
  job_prio πριν δημοσιεύσει (το jp_have τη διαβάζει από εκεί), και το
  ST_DLOW (bit 4 του ST_OPS) μπαίνει μαζί με το bit 7 μόνο όταν η εργασία
  μπήκε (το C του st_post).
- Η άφιξη (ja_oper) σβήνει και το ST_DLOW· στο D_OPS ενός θόλου το bit 4
  δεν φτάνει ποτέ.
- Ορυχείο που άδειασε με τη Drill του χαμηλά (ο μόνος γύρισε για αέρα ή
  πέθανε): το ST_OPS & #93 του σαρώματος είναι #90, και το hl_pile, που
  καλείται αμέσως μετά με τον ίδιο A, καλεί το dr_raise (b6code): ένα
  πέρασμα του πίνακα, η Drill πίσω στο 4. Χωρίς εργασία σβήνει και το bit 7,
  που αλλιώς θα έλεγε ψέματα. Στο hl_pile και όχι στο σάρωμα: εκεί έβγαζε το
  «jr z,ef_extr» της διανομής 5 bytes εκτός εμβέλειας.

Μετρημένο μετά, στο build του 126: το εργοστάσιο αδιάθετο 69% (75%), το
εργαστήριο 10% (23%), οι εργάτες 16% στο ορυχείο και 15% στο εργοστάσιο,
τέσσερις αποικίες ξεπερνούν τους έξι (τρεις στο 125). Ο δεύτερος εργάτης
φεύγει από το ορυχείο αλλά πάει πρώτα στο εργαστήριο, στα θερμοκήπια (4) και
στο κυλικείο (5): το εργοστάσιο είναι το 3, η βιομηχανία μετά την τροφή. Το
εργοστάσιο στο 5 μετρήθηκε κι αυτό (20% αδιάθετο, έξι αποικίες ως 19-30):
ανοιχτή επιλογή στο §15.

Δοκιμές. test_drill: η ροή θέλει Drill στο 4, 2, 2 και ST_OPS 80 91 92· νέα
σκηνή ΧΑΜΗΛΑ — το άδειο ορυχείο πίσω στο 4 (90 -> 80), χωρίς εργασία και τα
δύο bits (90 -> 00), όσα έχουν κάποιον μένουν στο 2, όλα απέναντι στο
flow_cycle· η άφιξη με κλήση του jb_arrive (91 -> 02)· το κόστος του
ανεβάσματος με τη Drill στην τελευταία θέση· έξι αρνητικά ακόμη, και το
μοτίβο του «χωρίς το bit 7». test_haul: η πρόζα της ροής με τις χαμηλές
Drill, και δύο μοτίβα (and #93, η αρχή του hl_pile). tools/econ.py:
post_drill με προτεραιότητα, raise_drill, η άφιξη σβήνει το ST_DLOW.
Χρόνοι: test_drill ο πρώτος κύκλος με τρία ορυχεία 4.026 -> 4.076 (δύο
δημοσιεύσεις, ~20 us η καθεμιά), οι επόμενοι 2.022 -> 2.037 (5 us ανά
ορυχείο), το ανέβασμα 2.530· test_sim ο κύκλος ροής 8.630 -> 8.670, 9.000 ->
9.050. test_disc 570 -> 550 frames (άλλος κόσμος στον δίσκο), test_save 30 ->
31 bytes (άλλη προσομοίωση). Τα ταβάνια ανέβηκαν όσο τα μετρημένα.
Μνήμη: τράπεζα 0 +7 (520 ελεύθερα), page2 +16 (74), b6code +40 (1.029).
DESIGN: §6.7 (νέα υποενότητα, ο πίνακας εργασιών), §13, §15 (νέα γραμμή: η
βιομηχανία περιμένει την τροφή), §4.2.

events.title: fix: merge WinUAE filesys rename and MMU cache-inhibit fixes, fix USE_PPC=OFF build (#2433)
events.message:
fix: merge WinUAE filesys rename and MMU cache-inhibit fixes, fix USE_PPC=OFF build (#2433)

* fix(filesys): move open file keys to the renamed object

Port of WinUAE 4f23db65. ACTION_RENAME_OBJECT freed the old a_inode while
files still open on it for reading kept keys pointing at it. On Unix hosts
the host rename succeeds with the file open, so the next ACTION_READ used
freed memory. Point every key of the old object at the new one before
freeing it and keep the new object from being recycled.

* fix(build): compile PPC sources only when USE_PPC is on

src/ppc/ppc.cpp was always compiled and calls ppc_interrupt(), which
cpuboard.cpp only defines under WITH_PPC, so -DUSE_PPC=OFF failed to link.

* fix(mmu): honor cache-inhibited pages in fast-cache paths

Port of WinUAE 4b274948 (tonioni/WinUAE#529).

68040/68060: write hits in mmu_put_* and mmu_put_user_* took the cache
state from the read fast-cache entry in the same slot, which can belong
to a different page, so writes to a cache-inhibited page could run as
copyback.

68030: mmu030_get_atc_generic() and mmu030_put_atc_generic() did not set
mmu030_cache_state from the ATC entry, so the data cache miss path
ignored page-level cache inhibit.

events.title: Add Neowilderness: Apple IIe 128K ProDOS DHGR port of Wilderness
events.message:
Add Neowilderness: Apple IIe 128K ProDOS DHGR port of Wilderness

Separate port of the Wilderness reimplementation for the Apple IIe
enhanced 128 KB and IIc, on a single 140 KB ProDOS floppy
(dist/NEOWILDERNESS.po):

- ProDOS 8 boot (NEOWILD.SYSTEM), common trunk NEOWILD.DAT and six
  region packs; every module resident in auxiliary RAM, zero disk
  reads during play; simulation state byte-identical to the HGR
  reference.
- DHGR 16-colour landscape with ten time-of-day moods, native compass
  and survival panels, 80-column message rows, TOPO sheet generated in
  RAM, MAP in 80 columns, 282-star night sky with the Moon rule.
- Six original regions (headers, 27 sprites and encounter rules probed
  on the original), start menu, four-species fauna, per-region
  palettes and texts, named interruption causes, score and hall of
  fame, credits on the loading page.
- Tools, Python references, benches (dhgr.mk, stars.mk, hof.mk),
  ~70 emulator tests (make test), docs and a five-direction TODO.
- dev/tools/a2test.py: Session() gains an iie option.

events.title: grm-kdgv: drop and clear the dead fall-through of a provably-taken conditional branch
events.message:
grm-kdgv: drop and clear the dead fall-through of a provably-taken conditional branch

DecidedBranchAnalyzer (6502/6510, beside BranchAlwaysPairAnalyzer at
BLOCK_ANALYSIS.before()): for a branch StoredValueScanner.knownBranchOutcome
decides TAKEN, set a fall-through override of none, then clear the code reached
only from the old fall-through (ClearFlowAndRepairCmd), unless a flow reference,
entry point, function or user label sits there. blmaster ebf2 LDA #0 / BEQ no
longer runs its body into the $EBF4 palette table.

Owner ruling: clearing is a reachability statement. The multi-entry
LDA #n / BNE common chains (tmnt b786.. via the word table at $B5A2, kicarus
a217/a21e/a225) were decoded only by the impossible fall-through and are
cleared; reaching them through their tables is grm-x51h.

HelperArgumentRecovery.prologueOutcome steps along such a branch over the
cleared gap, so ultimaav FUN_f34b (LDA #$0E / BNE / [LDA #$0F] / LDX #5 ...)
keeps its 'NO INBOUND ARGUMENT' proof.

Fixtures: make_prg_fork/make_prg_forkhome did LDA $10 / LDX #imm / BEQ, so LDX
decided the branch and one 'runtime' arm was dead; LDX now comes first.
Goldens: nesforktest/nesforkhometest IDENTITY only; real-ROM contra cv3 ff1
kicarus lwings megaman3 rcransom smb2 smb3 tmnt tmnt3 zelda re-blessed, count
and sample-ref lines only, every count down, no comment/warning/note moved.

events.title: Fix invalid color and list item index handling
events.message:
Fix invalid color and list item index handling

Guard palette clicks against out-of-range color indices and fix selected/checked item cleanup when removing list entries to avoid stale indices, incorrect state transitions, and invalid UI updates.

Geändert wurde `C64Studio/Controls/ColorPalette/ColorPaletteRaster.cs`, Methode `HandleMouseOnColorChooser`. Die ursprünglichen Zeilen 122/123 setzten den Palettenindex ungeprüft und benutzten ihn sofort als Listenindex (`_SelectedColor = (byte)( colorIndexX * _NumColorsPerColumn + colorIndexY );` und `_LastSelectedEntry = _ColorIndices[_SelectedColor];`). An ihre Stelle treten jetzt eine Zwischenvariable und eine Grenzprüfung: Der Index wird zuerst in `int` berechnet und vor jeder Verwendung gegen `0` und `_ColorIndices.Count` geprüft; liegt er außerhalb, wird der Klick verworfen (`return`) — `_SelectedColor`, `_LastSelectedEntry`, `Redraw()` und `RaiseColorSelectedEvent()` bleiben dann unberührt. Erst danach werden `_SelectedColor` (jetzt gefahrlos auf `byte` gekürzt, weil der Wert vorher als gültig nachgewiesen ist) und `_LastSelectedEntry` gesetzt; die Raise-Kette sieht damit nur noch einen Index aus `0..Count-1`. Das ist der kleinste Eingriff an der belegten Stelle: keine Signatur, keine neue Öffentlichkeit, keine Änderung an der Zellzuordnung selbst (`x * R + y` bleibt wie in `Redraw()`), keine Collection-Mutation, kein Platzhalter, keine Testanpassung und keine zweite Datei.

Die Ursachenrichtung habe ich beim Lesen bestätigt: Zeile 119/120 schneiden bei der Division ab, Zeilen 109–112 prüfen nur gegen `panelCharColors.ClientSize`, nicht gegen die Eintragszahl, und die Zellteilung in Zeile 34 (`R = ceil(Count/NPL)`) kann den Randstreifen oberhalb der letzten echten Zeile nicht abbilden. Bewußt **nicht** gemacht habe ich zwei Dinge: Erstens habe ich `_SelectedColor` nicht vor der Validierung gekürzt — die alte `(byte)`-Kürzung hätte einen zu großen Index still auf einen zufälligen, formal gültigen Wert umbrechen können, so daß die Prüfung ins Leere gelaufen wäre. Zweitens klemme ich den Index nicht wie der Setter in `ColorPaletteBase.cs` (Zeilen 74–77) auf `0`, sondern verwerfe den Klick: Der Setter hat einen Aufrufer, der einen gültigen Index erwartet, der Mauspfad hat einen Klick auf eine leere Zelle — eine Klemmung auf `0` würde dort eine Farbe auswählen, die der Nutzer nicht angeklickt hat (stille Fehlauswahl). Die Divisoren in Zeile 119/120 habe ich nicht zusätzlich abgesichert, weil ein Nulldivisor nicht belegt ist: Bei `_NumColorsPerLine = 0` oder `_NumColorsPerColumn = 0` würde bereits der Konstruktor in Zeile 34 werfen, so daß der Handler nie erreicht wird; alles Weitere wäre ein Eingriff über den Befund hinaus.

Zum Belegstand, offen benannt: Die Ereignisverdrahtung der beiden Handler und die tatsächliche Client-Höhe zur Laufzeit liegen außerhalb des zitierten Codes — die Fenstermetrik (Fixed3D-Rahmen gegen `ClientSize`) habe ich nicht gemessen. Die Grenze `_ColorIndices.Count` ist an dieser Stelle aber in jedem Fall die richtige Schranke: Sie gilt unabhängig davon, welche Client-Höhe der Rahmen liefert, und die Invariante, die der Setter derselben Klasse bereits durchsetzt, wird damit auch im Mauspfad eingehalten.

Automap and magic map: ignore walls the labdata doesn't have (#99)

The airship maps (435-437) use wall byte 114 (wall 14) for their border,
but their labdata 33 only has 9 walls. The 3D view and the location status
check this, but Automap_ModInit and Insert_3D_in_minimap read the wall data

Complete Source Reconstruction 3.0

Since the 2.0 tag the Level, Graphics and Sound studios, the level
playtest and the YM2612 preview have left the repository: Flicky opens

this tree: the inherited 2.0 gate, then the Retrolarium audit, in which
every revision opens in the kit and builds back to its ROM byte for
byte.

Every revision still builds byte for byte, and the evidence of the
earlier releases carries over unchanged. A shifting source, an extended
version, MAME scenarios and CI are outside this release; they are the
3.x plan.

events.title: fix(disk): a disc from a .zip is written back as a DSK beside the archive, never into it (#107)
events.message:
fix(disk): a disc from a .zip is written back as a DSK beside the archive, never into it (#107)

* fix(disk): a disc from a .zip is written back as a DSK beside the arc…

…hive, never into it

flush_dirty_media_unit() wrote a disc's unsaved writes to the file the disc
was read from. For a disc loaded out of a .zip that file is the archive: it
was truncated and filled with the raw DSK image, which destroyed its other
entries and left a DSK under a .zip name.

The bridge now also remembers which entry of the file the disc is
(media_entry, handed over with the bytes by file_load and read by
read_media_file when the machine is built). A disc with an entry is written
to <entry name>.dsk in the archive's directory and the archive is not
opened for writing at all. A file already there is not overwritten: the
first free of NAME.dsk, NAME-2.dsk, NAME-3.dsk ... is taken. When the file
cannot be created the disc stays marked altered and the failure is logged.

The new file goes on the Recent list. When the disc stays in the drive (a
machine rebuild, which reads the drive's file again) the drive is pointed at
it: CPC.driveA/B.file, the bridge's media_path, and media_note() +
media_changed(), so the rebuilt machine does not read the unwritten disc
back out of the archive. beads-lels

* docs(disk): where a zipped disc's writes go (beads-lels)
