events.title: fix(pacing): a stop shorter than 250 ms is not repaid as a burst of unpaced frames (beads-drzi) (#105)
events.message:
fix(pacing): a stop shorter than 250 ms is not repaid as a burst of unpaced frames (beads-drzi) (#105)

* fix(pacing): a stop shorter than 250 ms is not repaid as a burst of u…

…npaced frames (beads-drzi)

The 50 Hz pacer is drift-corrected: a frame that arrives past its deadline
is released at once and the ones after it too, until the grid is caught up.
Only a deadline more than a quarter second old was dropped. A stopped
machine does not call the pacer, so a pause, a breakpoint stop or the end
of a step that lasted less than that left a stale deadline behind, and the
machine ran the frames it "owed" unpaced when it was run again: 62 frames
in the 1.08 s after a stop of about 140 ms, on macOS.

That is the 54 frames a second the MSVC UI-free job measured, twice, for
the machine "alone" in test_polling_every_chip_changes_nothing: the window
opens right after a paused machine was read out over some twenty text IPC
connections and run again. The burst is over in a few milliseconds on a
fast host and still going when the window opens on a slow one.

The frame runner now tells the pacer when it finds the machine in an
announced stop (FramePacer::stopped()), and the next frame that arrives
past its deadline restarts the grid there. A pause lease alone is not such
a stop: the frames it holds up are still made up, so a client that writes
all the time does not slow the machine down, and a stop that ends before
the deadline releases nothing early.

Tests: FramePacer.AStopIsNotCaughtUp and
AStopThatEndsBeforeTheDeadlineKeepsTheGrid; test_a_stop_is_not_caught_up
in test_kcpc.py (fails on master: 62 frames where 56 are allowed). The
polling test compares the watched rate with min(alone, 50). A text IPC
connection the core drops now reports the core's exit code and the end of
its stderr, for the ConnectionResetError on `load rom/system.cpr` the same
job showed once.

events.title: grm-if81: retract overlay references an earlier analysis round placed and this one no longer derives
events.message:
grm-if81: retract overlay references an earlier analysis round placed and this one no longer derives

retargetReferences was additive across rounds: nesintrawintest's round one resolves 8008/800b
to bank 1 before the overlay callee exists, round two to bank 2, and both sets of overlay
references stayed. This is the reference twin of grm-3mg0 (comments) and grm-mej.26 (bookmarks).

OverlayRefProvenance keeps a user-property record, per instruction, of the overlay references
retargetReferences CREATED. Each round settles every retargeted instruction: recorded references
it did not place are deleted, and where that leaves an operand with no reference into base space
or its overlays, a base-space reference is restored (references are the flow graph; grm-bfb may
have retired the stock one). An end-of-round sweep does the same for instructions that left the
tracked flow. A reference found already present (TransferMaterializer's, a user's) is only
confirmed, never adopted, so it is never retracted. A settled round writes nothing.

Synthetic: nesintrawintest loses its 2 stale PRG_LO_B1 refs (new criterion W5); nesskiptest
loses c009 -> PRG_LO_B2::8010 (round one's pre-FixSkipInstructions bank). JUnit: five
BaseReferenceRetirementProgramTest cases (retract, restore-on-home, unowned survives,
write-free, sweep) + OverlayRefProvenanceTest.

events.title: fix(cartridge): a cartridge loaded into a running machine is the one the board reads (#106)
events.message:
fix(cartridge): a cartridge loaded into a running machine is the one the board reads (#106)

* fix(cartridge): a cartridge loaded into a running machine is the one …

…the board reads

The board holds the cartridge image by a raw pointer. cpr_load() freed
that image before it had read the new file, and only emulator_init() told
the board about the new one: the File menu, the Recent list, a dropped
file and the text IPC `load x.cpr` left the board reading released
memory. The text IPC did it with the Z80 thread running and without a
reset. A file that was refused left no image at all, and left
CPC.cartridge.file naming it, so the next rebuild exited the emulator.

- cpr_load() parses into an image of its own and makes it the cartridge
  only when the file is whole: a refused file changes nothing.
- cpc_cartridge_insert() is the one way a cartridge goes into a built
  machine: pause lease, load, re-attach to the board, reset. All four
  paths call it. cpc_cartridge_swap() is the load and re-attach alone,
  for a caller that holds the machine itself.

   τις συνταγές και το γράφει το pack.py (MF_ADDS, bit 2 των σημαιών)· σήμερα
   μόνο το VITROMEAT. Οι μετατροπές συνεχίζουν και αδειάζουν την αποθήκη· οι
   κήποι και το σκάψιμο σταματούν ακόμη. 9 από 12 ζωντανές· οι τρεις που
   πεθαίνουν είναι κόσμοι όπου ο παίκτης δεν βρήκε θέση για θερμοκήπια, και
   πεθαίνουν το ίδιο με τον παλιό κανόνα.
   Το erm_inf: ld a,(ix+9) · and MF_ADDS · ret z · scf, 2 bytes και 1-3 us
   ανά μηχανή, μόνο με γεμάτη αποθήκη. Με χώρο η παραγωγή είναι ίδια (12.520,
   13.130, 8.390 us)· γεμάτη 11.550 και 6.830 (10.400 και 4.900 στο 122, γιατί
   τώρα τρέχουν οι μετατροπές), πάντα κάτω από αυτήν με χώρο.

2. Από το 121 καμία θύελλα δεν ερχόταν. Ενα r2 κάτω από 32 έχει πίσω του μόνο
   μικρούς αριθμούς (ο Galois με το XOR βάζει το bit 15, άρα μια τιμή κάτω από
   #8000 έχει έναν προκάτοχο, τον εαυτό της ολισθημένο): οκτώ βήματα πριν,
   το r3 τρεις περιστροφές νωρίτερα έχει τα επτά χαμηλά bits μηδέν και r1
   ζυγό — ζαριά βλάβης, μέσα στο FAULT_GAP. Η ησυχία την έκοβε κάθε φορά.
   Μετρημένο στην αναφορά με 20 ζωντανούς, 12 σπόρους, 40 sol: 0,131
   καταστροφές το sol, καμία θύελλα, διάμεσο κενό 8 sol. Η έκλαμψη (r3 < 64)
   έχανε έτσι τις 51 από τις 63 τιμές της.
   Τώρα θύελλα r2 >= #FFE0 και έκλαμψη r3 >= #FFC0, με τους στόχους από τα έξι
   χαμηλά bits (οι ίδιοι 64)· 0,252 το sol, 45 % θύελλες, διάμεσο κενό 3,1 sol.
   Θύελλα και βλάβη ποτέ στην ίδια ζαριά· 7 από τις 32 θύελλες του Galois
   πέφτουν σε 64 περιστροφές από ζαριά βλάβης, όσο δίνει η τύχη.

Τι δεν άλλαξε: η απόδοση της μηχανής METAL. Με 6 αποίκους καμία αποικία δεν
μεγαλώνει σε 40 sol: το METAL περιμένει χειριστή, και οι τέσσερις που
μπορούν δουλεύουν και αλλού (στη φλέβα το μετάλλευμα φτάνει τα 140 με το
μέταλλο κάτω από 25). Με METAL x2 (--tweak iron=2) τρεις από τις δώδεκα
φτάνουν τους 18-20 ως το sol 40. Το DESIGN το προτείνει, ο χρήστης διαλέγει.

tools/play.py: τα σχέδια store και long (θόλος Storage όταν πλησιάζει η
χωρητικότητα, πλοία όσο χωρά το οξυγόνο, δεύτερα και τρίτα δωμάτια ως τους
15), το δωρεάν πρώτο ορυχείο, μισό ορυχείο δίπλα στα κτίρια όταν δεν βρει
φλέβα, η χωρητικότητα, η σημαία και τα ορυχεία σε κάθε δείγμα, --json, και
--tweak iron=N.

Δοκιμές. test_sim, αποθήκη: γεμάτη, το σύνολο δεν ανεβαίνει, κανένα από
άμυλο, λαχανικά, φαρμακευτικά, κρέας δεν ανεβαίνει, και τα αγαθά κινούνται
(14 λιγότερα σε ένα σάρωμα)· τα αρνητικά «το VITROMEAT δεν σταματά» και
«σταματούν όλες, και το οξυγόνο». Ησυχία: οι ζαριές στα νέα όρια· η περίπτωση
«θύελλα και βλάβη στην ίδια ζαριά» δεν υπάρχει πια, και στη θέση της ο έλεγχος
και των 65.535 θέσεων του Galois (καμία κοινή ζαριά, 7 από 32 θύελλες κοντά σε
βλάβη· με το r2 < 32 όλες οι 31). Η έκλαμψη με r3 & 63. test_meteor: οι 16
τιμές της βροχής απέναντι στις νέες ζαριές.
test_power: η στάθμη του ρεύματος και το νερό διαβάζονται πια την ίδια
στιγμή. Το A.snap ανάμεσά τους τρέχει το μηχάνημα ως το vsync και τρία καρέ·
με τη φάση του 124 (δύο καρέ αργότερα) ο κύκλος ροής έπεσε εκεί, και ένα
διάστημα έδειξε στάθμη 2 με το νερό του επόμενου κύκλου, που είχε στάθμη 1
και άντλησε (158 -> 168). Ιχνηλατημένο καρέ προς καρέ στο 123 και στο 124·
περνά και στα δύο, και με τις αντλίες αφημένες να δουλεύουν στο πεσμένο
φορτίο (jr nz του ef_setp κομμένο) πιάνει το λάθος.
Χρόνοι: μόνο η εκκίνηση του test_disc, 540 -> 570 frames (ταβάνι 600). Ο
κόσμος του δίσκου είναι άλλος: το seed βγαίνει από τον R, που αλλάζει με κάθε
byte που αντιγράφει ο φορτωτής (F535 -> F151), και η γεννήτρια κρατά όσο ο
κόσμος — 590 στο 121, 550 στο 122, 540 στο 123. Η παραγωγή με χώρο ίδια· με
γεμάτη αποθήκη μετρημένη χωριστά (πάνω).
Μνήμη: τράπεζα 0 +14 (527 ελεύθερα, 335 κάτω από το πάτωμα). DESIGN: §6.5
(νέα υποενότητα, και ο κανόνας του 122 διορθωμένος), §6.10 (νέα υποενότητα,
ο πίνακας των ρυθμών, το 121), §10.1 (η μέτρηση, νέα υποενότητα), §4.2,
§13 (και η γραμμή του test_power), §15 (νέα γραμμή: η αποικία των έξι δεν
μεγαλώνει)· ένα νούμερο του 123 (το commit δομής 887, όχι 892) και τρεις
σύνδεσμοι που έδειχναν σε παλιούς τίτλους.

events.title: Symbolic pointers from the gameplay-hacks branch
events.message:
Symbolic pointers from the gameplay-hacks branch

The hack branch made the PRG relocatable without changing the reference
bytes; this brings that part to main, without any hack:

- the audio track table and the stream loop pointers are .addr entries
  naming the music streams;
- the NMI task handler tables name their upload routines byte by byte;
- the object sprite handler table is an .addr list annotated per runtime
  type;
- the 90 LDX/LDY frame pointers in the sprite selectors address
  ObjectSpriteFrameRecords, now a label in the metasprite data;
- the player and object collision flag tables list each cell's halves.

PrgStart, PrgBaseAddress and PrgTileTablesAddress let the PRG tail pad up
to the fixed tile tables at $FF30 instead of with literal $FF bytes, and
RELOCATION_TEST_SHIFT inserts up to $48 bytes at the start of PRG to try
a moved layout: the tile tables stay put and the vectors follow.

All of it is source replacements in the source layout, so make
disassemble reproduces it. Both revisions still build byte for byte;
lint, format-check, the reconstruction audit, the disassembly check,
the debugger symbols, the studio check and the 610 tests pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: Βήμα 123: ορυχείο παντού — μισό χωρίς φλέβα, και το πρώτο δωρεάν
events.message:
Βήμα 123: ορυχείο παντού — μισό χωρίς φλέβα, και το πρώτο δωρεάν

Ο χρήστης ζήτησε το μέταλλο να μην τελειώνει ποτέ για πάντα, και διάλεξε:
ορυχείο σε οποιοδήποτε έδαφος χτίζεται, με τη μισή απόδοση μακριά από φλέβα,
και δωρεάν όταν η αποικία δεν έχει άλλο (έτοιμο ή εργοτάξιο)· η μηχανή METAL
χρειάζεται ακόμη.

- Το bd_res δεν αρνείται πια το ορυχείο χωρίς φλέβα: κρατά την απάντηση στο
  bd_half, και η σειρά 4 του πίνακα λέει NO VEIN  HALF ORE (στη θέση του
  NEEDS AN ORE VEIN). Η αντλία θέλει ακόμη νερό· το ποιο από τα δύο το λέει ο
  E που κρατά ήδη το υλικό (ld a,e · rra, 2 us). Οταν αλλάζει το bd_half
  σβήνει η υπογραφή των σειρών 3-4, αντί για ένα byte ακόμη σε αυτήν που θα
  πλήρωνε κάθε βήμα κέρσορα.
- Μισή απόδοση, προς τα πάνω: 1/2/2 μετάλλευμα με 1/2/3 στη δουλειά, αντί
  για 2/3/4. Το bit 2 του ST_OPS (ST_HALF)· το hl_pile το κοιτάζει, 8 us σε
  κάθε ορυχείο που σκάβει, μία φορά ανά κύκλο ροής.
- Δωρεάν: το bd_mprice ψάχνει στις 32 δομές για ορυχείο έτοιμο ή εργοτάξιο
  (μια άδεια εγγραφή κρατά το είδος της: μετρά και η κατάσταση) και κάνει
  την τιμή 0 αν δεν βρει. Τρέχει στον κατάλογο και μετά από κάθε τοποθέτηση,
  γιατί η διεπαφή μένει στο PLACE. Το bit 3 (ST_FREE) σημαδεύει το δωρεάν: η
  κατεδάφισή του δεν επιστρέφει τίποτα — αλλιώς ένα δωρεάν εργοτάξιο,
  βαλμένο και γκρεμισμένο, θα έδινε 30 μέταλλο κάθε φορά.
- Τα bd_mprice και bd_mflags ζουν στο src/mine.asm, μόνο στο παιχνίδι: στο
  terrain.asm το tests/uitest.asm περνούσε το #3F00 των ανιχνεύσεων. Εκεί
  είναι ένα ret, και το ορυχείο πληρώνει όπως ως το 122.
- Η βοήθεια: MINE «ORE, BEST ON A VEIN».

Δοκιμές. test_terrain: το bd_half από τυχαία αρχή, η υπογραφή που σβήνει
μόνο όταν αλλάζει, τρία αρνητικά ακόμη. test_place: bd_select δωρεάν χωρίς
άλλο ορυχείο (όχι από άδεια εγγραφή), το commit με ST_HALF και ST_FREE και
την τιμή του επόμενου, ο χρόνος ενός commit ορυχείου (1.530 us, μόνο στο
FIRE), τέσσερα αρνητικά. test_reach: το bd_half στο ui_validate. test_map:
στο παιχνίδι που τρέχει, NO VEIN  HALF ORE χωρίς φλέβα, το πρώτο ορυχείο
χωρίς μέταλλο με ST_FREE, το δεύτερο 30 με ST_HALF. test_demolish: τα δύο
εργοτάξια γκρεμισμένα, πίσω 30 και 0, και ένα αρνητικό. test_haul: τρία
ορυχεία εκτός φλέβας στον κύκλο, και ένα αρνητικό. test_drill: η αλυσίδα
δέχεται και δεύτερο εργάτη (το δωρεάν ορυχείο δεν θέλει Supply, και οι
εργάτες είναι ελεύθεροι νωρίτερα)· ο μετρητής ακολουθεί τους ανθρώπους.
test_bar: το νέο κείμενο βοήθειας. tools/balance.py: το B.build κρίνει
την τοποθέτηση από τις εγγραφές, όχι από το μέταλλο.
Χρόνοι: ο έλεγχος ορυχείου σε φλέβα 1.424 -> 1.437 us, χωρίς φλέβα 1.050
(θέση πια, ως τότε άρνηση στα 1.021), η αντλία χωρίς νερό 818 -> 821, το
commit δομής 887 -> 927 και του θόλου 1.494 -> 1.514 (το bd_mprice που
ξαναμετρά την τιμή, και στη δομή το bd_mflags)· ο πρώτος κύκλος ροής του test_drill με τρία ορυχεία
4.008 -> 4.026, του test_sim 8.610 -> 8.630.
Η κατεδάφιση: +0,2-0,3 ms στον γύρο του FIRE (test_demolish, test_leftover,
test_unlink), η 35η γραμμή της επικάλυψης που αντιγράφεται. Στο test_unlink ο
S1 του ΑΓΚΥΡΑ 84,4 -> 95,2 ms (ταβάνι 150): η ίδια δουλειά, μοιρασμένη αλλιώς
στους δύο πρώτους γύρους (84,4+33,5 = 117,9, 95,2+22,6 = 117,8)· χωρίς τις
φωτογραφίες της δοκιμής 84,8 -> 85,0. test_drill: το πρώτο ορυχείο δωρεάν,
χτίζεται σε 100 frames αντί 150. test_haul: η σκηνή έχει πια τρία ορυχεία
εκτός φλέβας (άλλος σωρός). test_disc: 550 -> 540 frames, δείγμα ανά 10.
test_save 31 -> 30 bytes, test_split μόνο στα αρνητικά, test_reach -3 us: η
φάση του main.sna.
Μνήμη: τράπεζα 0 +111 (541 ελεύθερα), page2 +9 (90), η επικάλυψη της
κατεδάφισης +19 (35η γραμμή, 5 bytes ως το τέλος του log), κείμενα +4 (86).
Η έκδοση σωσίματος μένει 9. DESIGN §6.5 (νέα υποενότητα), §6.8, §9.3, §4.2,
§11, §13, §15.

events.title: debug: support standard GDB range stepping
events.message:
debug: support standard GDB range stepping

Handle vCont range requests with bounded address and thread parsing.
Use the existing trace checks to stop when execution leaves the range,
while preserving breakpoints and manual interrupts. Clear range state
at every stop and execute one instruction for an empty range.

The CPU debugger asks the target whether to stop through a new hook
and lets it finalize the stop reply.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: debug: add optional loopback GDB server
events.message:
debug: add optional loopback GDB server

Expose CPU registers, physical memory, execution control, PC breakpoints
and CPU data watchpoints through a GDB remote server on 127.0.0.1. Keep
it disabled by default and use the existing debugger to stop at CPU
instruction boundaries.

Separate packet parsing from the portable socket transport and keep the
target in gdb_target.cpp. The debugger exports small execution-control
helpers instead of its trace state, and all guest operations run on the
emulation thread. Validate writes before changing state, apply SR before
A7, and refresh caches after RAM writes. Track remote breakpoint and
watchpoint ownership so disconnect preserves console entries.

Add the gdbserver debugging feature and gdb_port option, integrate the
Windows and Unix builds, and add a protocol unit test.

Adapt the existing debugger memory map to the standard GDB

omit the map when the debugger's region table is truncated, so clients
never treat an incomplete map as authoritative.

events.title: Βήμα 122: η αποθήκη έχει χωρητικότητα, και όταν γεμίσει οι μηχανές σταματούν
events.message:
Βήμα 122: η αποθήκη έχει χωρητικότητα, και όταν γεμίσει οι μηχανές σταματούν

Ο χρήστης ζήτησε χωρητικότητα αποθηκών και όριο στην παραγωγή· διάλεξε μία
χωρητικότητα για όλα τα αγαθά μαζί, όπως στο Planetbase, και κανένα άλλο
όριο: μια μηχανή σταματά μόνο όταν η αποθήκη γεμίσει.

- Χωράνε 500 (το αμπάρι του σκάφους· το φορτίο της αρχής είναι 468 χωρίς το
  νερό) και 100 / 300 / 600 κάθε θόλος Storage κατά μέγεθος, ως οκτώ: 500 ως
  5.300. Μετράνε όλα τα αγαθά εκτός από το νερό. Το ταβάνι των 600 ανά
  απόθεμα (EC_CAP) μένει.
- Γεμάτη όταν το σύνολο φτάσει τη χωρητικότητα: σταματούν οι μηχανές που
  βγάζουν απόθεμα (πριν φάνε τις εισόδους τους και πριν ζητήσουν ρεύμα), οι
  κήποι, και το σκάψιμο των ορυχείων. Οχι το οξυγόνο, τα κρεβάτια, οι αντλίες,
  οι μεταφορές, ο έμπορος, οι πληρωμές. Το HUD λέει STORAGE FULL, κάτω από το
  SANDSTORM.
- Το st_check (src/needs.asm, b6code) μετρά μία φορά ανά κύκλο ροής, πριν
  σκάψουν τα ορυχεία. Κανείς στο θερμό μονοπάτι δεν διαβάζει τη σημαία: το
  ec_setfull (τράπεζα 0) ξαναγράφει την τρίτη κλήση εισόδου του ec_run_mach
  (erm_in ή erm_inf) και το «or a» του κήπου («xor a»). Η πρώτη μορφή, με
  έλεγχο σε κάθε μηχανή και το άθροισμα στην αρχή του σαρώματος της
  παραγωγής, πρόσθετε 530 us στο βαρύτερο frame της θέσης 11 (13.130 ->
  13.660)· τώρα η παραγωγή είναι ακριβώς όση στο 121 (12.520 / 13.130 /
  8.390 us), και με γεμάτη αποθήκη λιγότερη (10.400 / 4.900). Ο κύκλος ροής
  8.360 -> 8.610 us (+54 κάθε θόλος Storage ακόμη, 8.990 με οκτώ), μία φορά
  ανά 64 περιστροφές. Το wheel_reset καθαρίζει την αποθήκη (νέο παιχνίδι ή
  φόρτωση)· η σημαία δεν σώζεται, η έκδοση μένει 9.
- Η αποικία του populate (tests/test_sim.py) κουβαλούσε 2.380 αγαθά και θα
  ήταν πάντα γεμάτη: τώρα 630 απέναντι σε 800.

Τι δεν περιορίζει: κάθε μηχανή εκτός από το VITROMEAT κάνει δύο ή
περισσότερα σε ένα, άρα η μετατροπή ελευθερώνει χώρο, και ένα SPARES με
μέταλλο το τρώει όλο, όπως είδε ο παίκτης-σενάριο στο 120. Θα μετρηθεί στο 124.

Δοκιμές. test_sim: η αποθήκη — έξι κύκλοι ροής στα όρια (ένα λιγότερο,
ακριβώς, 700 πάνω, χωρίς θόλο Storage, θόλος L ένα λιγότερο και ακριβώς),
καθένας με ένα ολόκληρο σάρωμα της παραγωγής στον ίδιο Z80, και ένας από
γεμάτη σε «ένα λιγότερο»· ταβάνια στον κύκλο ροής· έξι αρνητικά (νερό αντί
για τροφή, μηχανές και κήποι που δεν σταματούν, ec_setfull που αφήνει την
τρίτη κλήση, ορυχεία που σκάβουν, θόλος M 200). Ο τροχός: το wheel_reset
αφήνει την αποθήκη να χωρά, με αρνητικό. test_hud: STORAGE FULL, και κάτω από
θύελλα. Το LOAD_STATE της σκαλωσιάς βάζει και τον κώδικα της σημαίας.
Δύο ακόμη δοκιμές άλλαξαν. test_drill: ο κύκλος ροής της σκηνής της (χωρίς
θόλο Storage) +180 us, όσο κοστίζει η μέτρηση — 1.480 -> 1.660, 3.807 ->
4.008, 1.842 -> 2.022, ταβάνια 1.668, 4.016, 2.030. test_alertname: έβαζε 500
τρόφιμα και 500 μέταλλο και βιοπλαστικό, πάνω από τα 600 της αποικίας
δοκιμών, και η γραμμή έλεγε STORAGE FULL· τώρα 100 τρόφιμα (ένα γεύμα ανά
άποικο) και 100 + 100 μετά την πληρωμή. Με 100 τρόφιμα η μπάρα είναι κόκκινη,
+27 us: τα ταβάνια του HUD είναι το 121 με 100 τρόφιμα (9.170, 9.390,
11.346)· το 122 μετρά 9.163, 9.373, 11.329.
Χρόνοι απέναντι στο 121, σουίτα σε πέντε αντίγραφα, 76/76: οι παραπάνω, η
νέα γραμμή του κύκλου ροής στο test_sim, το test_newgame +24 us (το
ec_setfull στο wheel_reset), το test_reach +3 us στο βήμα κέρσορα, το HUD του
test_trade -17 us, το test_disc 590 -> 550 frames (ο τυχαίος κόσμος), και
±0,2 ms στις κατεδαφίσεις.
Μνήμη: τράπεζα 0 +60 (652 ελεύθερα), b6code +137 (1.069), κείμενα +13 (90).

events.title: ZZTop 3: rebuild as a single-window ReAction control panel
events.message:
ZZTop 3: rebuild as a single-window ReAction control panel

The GadTools ZZTop grew from the MNT diagnostics tool into seven nested
modal windows with three different save verbs. Replace it with one
resizable ReAction window: a page list (Status, Display, Audio, System,
Firmware; Capture, Scenes and Diagnostics in advanced mode), a status
line, and one global Save / Revert.

Structure: board.c (registers, health), settings.c (ZZ9000.CFG model with
per-field dirty tracking), video.c + align.c (live capture calibration),
audio.c (firmware audio control plane), app.c (cross-model Save, Revert,
Quit), ui.c (framework), page_*.c (presentation only).

Behaviour changes and fixes:
- Save re-reads the card file and applies only edited fields, so keys
  written meanwhile survive and untouched absent keys stay absent.
- The firmware audio Save rewrites non-audio keys from its cold-boot
  parse and silently reverted settings saved earlier in the same boot.
  Every audio save is now bracketed by a guard that restores them; the
  guard fails closed and survives a slow firmware save or failed repair.
- Live edits (scanlines, phase, crop, capture window, audio) are tracked
  from submission, Save refuses unconfirmed values, and Revert/Discard
  restore the state ZZTop opened with.
- Firmware install/restore controls are disabled during a transfer.
- Requester text is word-wrapped; temperature range can be reset.

events.title: Ship codesets.library: built from third_party/libcodesets, installed on 3.0+
events.message:
Ship codesets.library: built from third_party/libcodesets, installed on 3.0+

third_party/libcodesets (LGPL-2.1) is pinned at 34442b75 (6.22) and built
unmodified by src/codesets/ at the tree's CPU (-m68000 in the shipping
build), regparm 0, no LTO.  cs_libc.c supplies stricmp/strnicmp (clib2's,
which upstream builds against), and atoi/strtol/__locale_ctype_ptr/NewList
so nothing pulls newlib's locale, stdio or exit into a library with no
crt0, or an amiga.lib object check-pcrel-exact cannot read.

The archive carries Codesets/codesets.library, COPYING and SOURCE (the
pinned commit URLs).  The Installer puts the library in LIBS: on 3.0 and
up only when none there is as new; a replaced copy goes to Backup, and
the uninstall record removes ours when unchanged before Backup's Restore
puts the old one back.  The licence and SOURCE go to the AmiNetXDuo
drawer.  The upstream Charsets tables (108 KB) are not shipped.

events.title: ssh: convert console text to the local codeset; OSC sets the window title
events.message:
ssh: convert console text to the local codeset; OSC sets the window title

Between consoles (stdin and stdout both interactive) the server's UTF-8
is converted to the local codeset and keystrokes back to UTF-8:
codesets.library v6 when it opens (system codeset or CHARSET=, look-alike
text for the rest), ISO-8859-1 and '?' otherwise.  0x80-0x9F never reach
the console.  When stdout is a console, OSC sequences are stripped and
OSC 0/2 set the window title, restored at exit.  Redirected data passes
unchanged.

The pure part is clients/dropbear/sshcs.c, tested on the host as
ssh_console_text.  codesets 6.22 frees a caller CSA_Dest when
CSA_MapForeignChars expands a character, so the library allocates the
result and CodesetsFreeA() returns it.

events.title: software: Show the graphics system with its version
events.message:
software: Show the graphics system with its version

The graphics-system field named the system only, and a PrismRTG system
came out as plain AmigaOS: PrismRTG has no rtg.library or CyberGraphX
preferences drawer, so identify.library found nothing it knew. Update
identify.library to recognize PrismRTG by the "prism" semaphore its
daemon publishes (IDGOS_PRISMRTG).

identify.library only names the system, so take the version from the
system itself:

- PrismRTG: from interface version 7 the semaphore carries the release
  ("1.1b6") and the board name (lainejones/PrismRTG#12).
- Picasso96: the installer records the release ("3.6.3") in
  Picasso96/Version, which boot copies from ENVARC: to ENV:. Without
  it, the rtg.library version is shown and labelled as such.
- CyberGraphX: the cgxsystem.library or cybergraphics.library version,
  labelled as such, since there is no release number to read.

IDGOS_PICASSO is the original Picasso software and is now called
"Picasso" rather than "Picasso96".

events.title: Βήμα 121: οι καταστροφές περιμένουν τους είκοσι αποίκους, και έρχονται αραιά
events.message:
Βήμα 121: οι καταστροφές περιμένουν τους είκοσι αποίκους, και έρχονται αραιά

Ο χρήστης ζήτησε καταστροφές τυχαίες και αραιές, και καμία πριν από τους 20
αποίκους· τις βλάβες τις είπε φθορά, όχι καταστροφή.

- Θύελλα, έκλαμψη και βροχή μετεωριτών μόνο με 20 ζωντανούς (DIS_POP), ποτέ
  μέσα σε δύο sol από την προηγούμενη, ποτέ μέσα σε 64 περιστροφές από
  οποιοδήποτε γεγονός.
- Βλάβες από την αρχή (1/256 όπως πριν), ποτέ μέσα σε 64 περιστροφές από
  άλλο γεγονός.
- Οταν επιτρέπεται: θύελλα 1/2048 (r2 < 32), έκλαμψη 1/4096 (r3 < 64 και μία
  περιστροφή στις τέσσερις του ρολογιού), βροχή 1/4096 όπως ήταν: μία
  καταστροφή κάθε ~3,4 sol, οι μισές θύελλες.

Δύο χρονοσφραγίδες [sol, frame] (EC_LDIS, EC_LEV) στα έξι από τα 28 bytes του
node_occ που αφήνουν οι πράκτορες 100-127: στην τράπεζα 6, μέσα στο μπλοκ
που σώζεται, με την ίδια έκδοση σωσίματος. Τις ρωτούν τα ev_may/ev_since
(src/meteor.asm, στο b6code) μόνο όταν πέσει μια ζαριά, οπότε η θέση 15
κοστίζει όσο πριν (450-460 µs). Η πρώτη μορφή, με μετρητές, κόστιζε 35 µs σε
κάθε περιστροφή και περνούσε το ταβάνι της μάχης· και στην τράπεζα 0 οι
ρουτίνες έπαιρναν 144 bytes αντί για 46. Η έκλαμψη παίρνει τα δύο νέα bits
από το ρολόι: το r3 < 64 ορίζει ήδη όλο το r1, και με r3 < 16 οι στόχοι της
ήταν μόνο οι θόλοι 37-52 — το βρήκε η test_sim.

Δοκιμές. test_sim: calm_branches, δεκαπέντε ζαριές στα όρια (19 και 20
ζωντανοί, ακριβώς δύο sol και μία περιστροφή νωρίτερα, ακριβώς 64
περιστροφές και μία νωρίτερα, θύελλα και βλάβη στην ίδια ζαριά, βλάβη με
τρεις), 9.000 περιστροφές με 20 ζωντανούς ίδιες byte προς byte με κενά
καταστροφών ≥ δύο sol, τέσσερα αρνητικά· το παράθυρο κινδύνων με βλάβη από
στημένο σπόρο, όχι από τύχη· οι ζαριές θύελλας και έκλαμψης στους νέους
κανόνες. test_impact: ζωντανοί, sol και χρονοσφραγίδες στις 400 σκηνές από
δική τους γεννήτρια, η «ησυχία» νέο είδος κλήσης (193 µs), η αρχή μιας
βροχής 6.657 -> 6.835 µs (ταβάνι 7.041). test_meteor: μια σημείωση.
Χρόνοι απέναντι στο 120: όλα ίδια εκτός από το test_impact (η αρχή της
βροχής, και το νέο είδος) και το test_disc, 560 -> 590 frames: άλλος κόσμος
(σπόρος από τον R, CC74 -> DF4F) — το ταβάνι των 600 εξαρτάται από τον τυχαίο
κόσμο κάθε build (550, 560, 590 στα τρία τελευταία). Στο test_sim το
παράθυρο κινδύνων είναι πια ο στημένος σπόρος: 3 βλάβες, και θύελλα μόνο η
αρχική των 20 περιστροφών.
Μνήμη: τράπεζα 0 +46 (712 ελεύθερα), b6code +107 (1.206).
DESIGN §4.2, §6.10 (νέα υποενότητα), §11, §13, §15.

events.title: fix(fwup): poll the firmware's status mirror instead of the register
events.message:
fix(fwup): poll the firmware's status mirror instead of the register

A FWUP status register read waits for the ARM main loop, so polling it
while the firmware runs a FatFs call holds the Amiga's Zorro cycle for
the whole SD write. When the firmware advertises the status mirror
(capability bit 11, the boot ROM window's last longword at 0x7FFC),
note it before each command and poll it for a new sequence, yielding
with Delay(1) after a spin budget; the first valid word after ROM
padding counts as new. Fall back to the register if the mirror never
moves. Older firmware keeps the register path.
events.author: midwan

events.title: MMU 68030: set mmu030_cache_state from ATC entry in generic get/put paths
events.message:
MMU 68030: set mmu030_cache_state from ATC entry in generic get/put paths

mmu030_get_atc_generic and mmu030_put_atc_generic called
mmu030_add_data_read/write_cache without first setting mmu030_cache_state
from the ATC entry's cache_inhibit bit, so the fast-cache entry recorded a
stale cache state and page-level CI was ignored for those accesses.
events.author: stefanskotte

events.title: MMU 68040/68060: use write fast-cache entry's cache state on write hits
events.message:
MMU 68040/68060: use write fast-cache entry's cache state on write hits

mmu_put_long/word/byte and the _user_ variants took mmu_cache_state from
atc_data_cache_read[idx2] when the WRITE fast-cache entry hit. The read
entry in that slot can belong to a different page (slots alias every
MMUFASTCACHE_ENTRIES pages), so writes to a cache-inhibited page could run
as copyback. With the 68060 whole-line push this corrupts data in CI-mapped
hardware/shared memory (seen with an A2386SX bridgeboard window at $200000
aliasing fast RAM at $C00000).

Use atc_data_cache_write[idx2].cache_state instead.
events.author: stefanskotte

events.title: filesys: move open file keys to the renamed object
events.message:
filesys: move open file keys to the renamed object

ACTION_RENAME_OBJECT frees the old a_inode after a successful rename.
Files still open on it for reading keep valid host handles, since a
Unix rename does not invalidate them, but their keys still pointed at
the freed a_inode, so the next ACTION_READ used freed memory. On
Windows the rename of an open file fails and the relock path moves the
keys; on macOS it corrupted the heap and crashed the emulator later in
unrelated code (seen when starting IBrowse a second time).

Point every key of the old object at the new one before freeing it
and keep the new object from being recycled.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: bsdsock_unix: allocate at least an int for socket options
events.message:
bsdsock_unix: allocate at least an int for socket options

host_setsockopt() and host_getsockopt() allocate the option length the
Amiga side passes, but mapsockoptvalue() and mapsockoptreturn() always
store or load an int, so an option length below 4 overflowed the host
heap buffer.

events.title: fix(libretro): apply save states loaded before the core boots (#2430)
events.message:
fix(libretro): apply save states loaded before the core boots (#2430)

* fix(libretro): build after linear_display_vpos rename

The WinUAE 6100b17 merge renamed linear_display_vpos to linear_vpos_start in src/osdep/writelog.cpp but not in the libretro copy of write_log_get_ts(), so the core no longer compiled.

* fix(libretro): apply states loaded before the core boots

RetroArch's auto-load unserializes before the first retro_run(). The core's first yield then comes from a frame presented inside custom_reset() in m68k_go()'s reset handling, and queuing the restore there set quit_program after the loop had checked it while m68k_reset2() cleared SPCFLAG_BRK. The restore never ran and IHF_QUIT_PROGRAM froze the boot screen.

Only hand a pending state to the emulator while m68k_go() is running the CPU (m68k_run() or its halt loop); otherwise keep it pending and retry on the next retro_run().

Fixes #2429

events.title: display: Make 8x16 font from 6x13 one in STM32F105 logfile and debug builds
events.message:
display: Make 8x16 font from 6x13 one in STM32F105 logfile and debug builds

To save the flash size for the logfile and debug builds for
STM32F105/AT32F415 (the most flash-hungry build types), a makefile
option oled_font_8x16_synth is introduced which defines a C macro
OLED_FONT_8x16_SYNTH=1 for those builds - this option generates the
8x16 font glyphs at runtime as a bold (shifted-by-1) version of 6x13,
instead of placing the 8x16 font in the flash memory.

It saves around 1.5 KB of flash.

The C macro is tested at runtime, so that the translation units can be
used in the builds which need to trigger this option in runtime, e.g.
for testing.

never negative there, so using `%u` everywhere makes the linker store

events.title: Βήμα 120: ένας παίκτης-σενάριο από την άδεια αρχή — και η ισορροπία που βρήκε
events.message:
Βήμα 120: ένας παίκτης-σενάριο από την άδεια αρχή — και η ισορροπία που βρήκε

tools/play.py παίζει το main.sna όπως το βλέπει ο παίκτης, με τα πλήκτρα του:
κατάλογος, θέση που δέχεται ο κανόνας του reach.py, FIRE, εξοπλισμός υποδοχή-
υποδοχή, C και FIRE για πλοίο, στο x4 για 20 sol. Ενα σχέδιο είναι λίστα
σταδίων· κάθε 1/8 του sol δείγμα (αποθέματα, ρεύμα, εργοτάξια, εργασίες, οι
ανάγκες του καθενός), οι θάνατοι με την αιτία τους, βλάβες, χτυπήματα,
θύελλες, πλοία. --make φτιάχνει snapshot για κάθε seed και πλανήτη με το
G_worldinfo του δίσκου· --tweak πειράζει φορτίο ή ζαριά για τα πειράματα.

Στο βήμα 119 καμία αποικία δεν έφτασε το sol 14, σε δώδεκα κόσμους και έξι
σχέδια. Βρήκε τρία λάθη και τέσσερα στενά:

- Μια ανάγκη χωρίς το δωμάτιό της πάγωνε την αποικία: χωρίς κοιτώνα, και οι
  τέσσερις στο κυλικείο με T_NEED από το sol 2· χωρίς ιατρείο ένας
  τραυματίας δεν ξαναέτρωγε. Τώρα περνά στην επόμενη ανάγκη (G_room_n, χωρίς
  ψάξιμο), και ένα δωμάτιο χωρίς δρόμο είναι «χορτάτος» (nd_far). Το
  δωμάτιο στον B αντί για το nd_room το πληρώνει: ο χειρότερος γύρος της
  θέσης αναγκών 4.550 -> 4.490 µs, χορτάτοι 3.010 -> 2.970, νυσταγμένοι
  χωρίς κοιτώνα 3.707 -> 3.017· πιο αργό μόνο «έξω, απρόσιτοι, διψασμένοι»,
  +44 µs μέσο (ο χορτάτος δρόμος όπου το 119 γύριζε). Και το seek της αναφοράς.
- Ενας θόλος που σφραγιζόταν άφηνε τους χτίστες του ΕΞΩ πάνω σε έτοιμο
  airlock: η στολή τους έστελνε στο airlock που ήδη πατούσαν, και καμία
  άφιξη δεν τους έβαζε μέσα. Ο μηχανικός πέθανε έτσι στο sol 4,27. Το
  lko_one ρωτά πια το en_in.
- Το EC_RND ξεκινούσε πάντα από #ACE1: κάθε δίσκος είχε τη βλάβη του θόλου
  0 στο sol 4,44 και τη βροχή μετεωριτών στο 10,5. Τώρα από το G_worldinfo·
  το main.sna και οι δοκιμές βρίσκουν μηδέν και κρατούν το #ACE1.

Τα στενά, και οι επιλογές του χρήστη: τα 4 ανταλλακτικά τελείωναν ως το sol
4 και το OXYGEN χωρίς ανταλλακτικό ήταν όλοι -> 12, και η βλάβη 1/128 ->
1/256 (και το bit 0 του r1, που δεν είναι μέρος του r3)· τα 40 τρόφιμα δεν
έφταναν ως να σταθεί η αλυσίδα -> 100· τέσσερις άποικοι έδιναν τρεις
χειριστές για έξι θέσεις -> πλήρωμα έξι, δύο εργάτες ακόμη, και η βάση του
ταβανιού είναι το πλήρωμα (POP_BASE 6). Η αποικία δοκιμών κρατά τους
τέσσερις της, τα 40 και τα 4.

Με αυτά, το σχέδιο χωρίς εργοστάσιο ανταλλακτικών σε δώδεκα κόσμους: έξι με
6/6 στο sol 20, δύο με 4/6 (πείνα από το 19,2, ο πλανήτης του νερού), και οι
τέσσερις του seed 1048 νεκροί ή με έναν ζωντανό από το 19,2: ο παίκτης δεν
βρήκε θέση για ορυχείο, και τα 12 ανταλλακτικά τελείωσαν ως το sol 16. Στο
§15: το μέταλλο μπορεί να τελειώσει για πάντα, η παραγωγή δεν έχει όριο, οι
καταστροφές έρχονται σε ριπές, και το §6.5 υπόσχεται αποθήκες, φωτισμό και
διαρροές.

tests/test_noroom.py: χωρίς κοιτώνα, χωρίς ιατρείο, απρόσιτο, με όλα, ίδια
bytes με την αναφορά, πέντε ταβάνια κόστους, και στο παιχνίδι το άνοιγμα
του play.py ως το sol 2,4· πέντε αρνητικά. test_outside: ένας νέος θόλος
δίπλα στο airlock της αποικίας δοκιμών, οι χτίστες του στο airlock ΜΕΣΑ.
test_newgame: έξι, 100, 12, ταβάνι 6, ο σπόρος από τα σκουπίδια του
G_worldinfo· δύο αρνητικά ακόμη. test_sim: η βλάβη που κόβει το r1 και το
αρνητικό της, παράθυρο κινδύνων 8x. test_game, test_crew: έξι και 54.
test_save, test_disc: 100 τρόφιμα και έξι άποικοι στην αρχή, POP 6 στο HUD,
και το nd_room που έφυγε από όσα γράφει ο τροχός. test_figure: η ΑΡΧΗ με
έξι, οι ζυγές θέσεις κάτω από το σκάφος και οι μονές από πάνω.

Χρόνοι απέναντι στο 119, ο καθένας με το πείραμά του σε αντίγραφα:
- game_new +2,5 ms: οι δύο άποικοι (με τέσσερις 247.774 µs, όσο το 119).
- test_figure: δύο φιγούρες ακόμη στη λίστα του main.sna, ~11 µs ανά
  εγγραφή σε κάθε σάρωση· fg_erase/fg_paint +12..36 µs, και η χρέωσή τους
  ανεβαίνει μαζί. Το ΤΑΒΑΝΙ «σβήνει και ζωγραφίζει, ελεύθερο έδαφος» 2.266 ->
  2.344 µs από 2.400: 56 µs περιθώριο.
- test_unlink, ΑΓΚΥΡΑ στο main.sna: οι χειρότεροι γύροι 89,7 -> 108,2 και
  105,3 -> 84,3 ms (ταβάνι 150)· με πλήρωμα τεσσάρων ξανά 89,8 και 105,3.
  Ούτε το needs, ούτε το door, ούτε το econ τους κουνούν.
- test_leftover +0,1 ms: το en_in του lko_one (ΕΡΓΟΤΑΞΙΟ) και το πλήρωμα
  (ΣΚΑΦΟΣ).
- test_reach, ΒΗΜΑ +13 / -6 µs: ο δειγματολήπτης ανά 20 µs σε έξι βήματα·
  με τον κώδικα αρχής του 119 30.653 / 19.783, ούτε 119 ούτε 120.
- test_disc 550 -> 560 frames: άλλος κόσμος (ο σπόρος από τον R, 9A32 ->
  CC74), δείγμα ανά 10 frames.
- test_trade ίδιο· το 9.253 του tdiff ήταν παλιότερο log του 119.
Μνήμη: τράπεζα 0 +6 (758 ελεύθερα), τράπεζα 2 +31 (99), b6code +14 (1.313).

events.title: grm-mej.25 follow-up: slot writer census propagates X/Y forward through the callee closure
events.message:
grm-mej.25 follow-up: slot writer census propagates X/Y forward through the callee closure

1d809f6 made the census sensitive to the TOP-LEVEL crossed call's index registers via a
RegisterEnv entry stop. That never reached cv3: ebdd's crossed call is JSR ec04, and the
add helper e899 (STA $00,X / INC $01,X) is called NESTED inside ec04, from three sites
(ec2b, ec54, ec6e) behind loop joins no backward straight-line walk crosses. Found by
querying the kept cv3 project through pyghidra-mcp.

calleeClosureCensus now carries an IndexRegs state (X/Y each a constant or unknown) per
address, seeded with the call site's values: LDX/LDY #imm, INX/DEX/INY/DEY on a constant
update it, any other writer (by mnemonic or Ghidra result objects) makes it unknown, a
callee is entered with the caller's registers, and the fall-through after a call keeps a
register only when calleePreserves proves it. States merge at joins (disagreement ->
unknown) and a weakened address is re-visited, so every store is classified under every
value that reaches it. This subsumes the entry-stop env and its re-entry guard (a loop
back into the entry now merges to unknown by itself); both are removed. An index the
propagation does not know still falls back to state-free constantIndex/loopIndexRange.

JUnit: CrossCallSaveSlotProgramTest section 12 gains the nested ec04 shape (LDX #0, loop
calling the helper behind a join -> resolves), a loop stepping X (-> declines) and a
non-preserving call before the helper (-> declines); 64/64 pass.
build-and-test.sh check: green, no golden moved. check nes: 33 pass + cv3 (intended,
re-blessed): ebdd WARNING -> partly known bank comment via FUN_e2e6 (bank_5115 bits
0,3,5,6 = 0, merged over the ebd5/ebe0 save-helper arms' $21 read-backs);
warnings 16 -> 15, bankComments 170 -> 171. No flap drew.

events.title: CheckNetDevice: report the PC Card in the slot
events.message:
CheckNetDevice: report the PC Card in the slot

turo: "checknetdevice should at least show the pcmcia card id,
irregardless... important for debugging."

A PC CARD SLOT section now follows the probe report, and is printed
also when the driver has not run: card present or "No card", the
owner, CISTPL_MANFID, the CISTPL_VERS_1 strings, CISTPL_FUNCID, the
first CISTPL_FUNCE and the archive's driver for that identity, for any
card, network or not.  Without card.resource it says there is no slot.

The card.resource code moves out of InstallNetProbe into
netprobe_pcmcia.c and both tools use it.  Card detect is read first,
so an empty slot is never owned.  A free slot is owned IFAVAILABLE,
read with CopyTuple() and released; a slot another driver owns is read
from attribute memory with the bounded CIS walk.  No reset, COR or
Gayle write, and no driver is loaded or opened for it.

The report text is built in netprobe_card.c so test_netprobe_card
checks it against the 3C589 fixture (now with VERS_1), a CompactFlash
disk, an empty slot, no card.resource and an over-long VERS_1.

The driver mapping names only anxnet.device rows and xircomce2.device;
the Prism2 tables are untouched.

perf(dsp): run the timing models in their own DSPExec loop

"Model off unchanged" is the S1 gate, and the slice-latched checks of
6fea9dc still measured ~3.4% on jagniccc with both options off.  Restore
develop's DSPExec loop and opcode handlers verbatim and choose the path
once per call: DSPExec() is now a two-way dispatch to out-of-line loops.
DSPExecUntimed() is develop's DSPExec() body unchanged (only made static
and noinline) and runs whenever virtualjaguar_gpu_pipeline_timing and
virtualjaguar_dram_timing are both off.  DSPExecTimed() is a copy of
that loop (minus the #569 idle probe, which both options already
disable) carrying the model hooks -- DSPPipeCheckUse before dispatch, a
load/store memory hook and timed jump/jr variants via
dsp_executeOpcodeT(), and DSPTimedCharge for the deduction.  The untimed
path no longer tests either option per instruction, per load/store or
per taken jump.  Timed results are unchanged.

events.title: grm-mej.25: slot writer census carries the call site's constant index registers into the callee
events.message:
grm-mej.25: slot writer census carries the call site's constant index registers into the callee

calleeClosureCensus was state-free, so a zero-page indexed store in a callee with an
unknown index counted as "may write any zp slot". cv3's ec27 LDX #$00 / JSR e899 enters a
16-bit add helper (CLC / ADC $00,X / STA $00,X / BCC / INC $01,X / RTS) that under X=0
writes only $00/$01, yet the census called the closure DIRTY for $22.

callCensus now evaluates X and Y at the call (constantRegisterValue, state-free) and runs
the census under a RegisterEnv entry-stopped at the callee entry, so constantIndex and
loopIndexRange adopt the caller's value when their walk reaches the entry unchanged -- the
same context-sensitive argument the helper-argument env already rests on. The memo key
(CensusKey) gains entry X/Y. Guard: a closure with any edge back into its own entry
(branch, jump, call or fall-through) answers null under an env and is re-run state-free,
since on that path the register no longer holds the caller's value.

JUnit: CrossCallSaveSlotProgramTest section 12 (the e899 shape under X=0 / X=$D3 / X=$D2
via INC / unknown X, a callee looping back into its entry, the memo key).
build-and-test.sh check: all green, no golden moved. check nes: 33 pass + dragonpower 152
symbol flap; cv3 byte-identical (ebdd/ebd5 still warn -- see grm-mej.19).

events.title: Fix rows that never redraw after being cleared
events.message:
Fix rows that never redraw after being cleared

term_ui_draw skips blank rows on mono before copying them to the
shadow buffer, so a cleared row kept its old text in the shadow. When
the same text came back (a server greeting after Reconnect, `clear`
followed by the same output), the shadow check called the row unchanged
and it was never drawn until the next full redraw. Copy the row to the
shadow before the blank-row skip.

That stale shadow had been hiding a second bug: do_reconnect draws
without saving the cursor state, so the update event for the dismissed
alert loaded stale state and left an XOR cursor block in the top-left
corner. Save the state after the redraw, as the disconnect path does.

events.title: fix(dsp): keep the DSP out of the VJ_DRAM_SCALE stress multiplier
events.message:
fix(dsp): keep the DSP out of the VJ_DRAM_SCALE stress multiplier

Maintainer decision on #892.  VJ_DRAM_SCALE (busArbiter.contention_scale)
is the #406 liveness-sweep knob for the GPU/68K/OP/refresh charges; S1
let it multiply the DSP's new bus cost too, and at scales >= 10 that
starved Doom's MiniLoop on the dspfinished handshake ($F1B034 polled
~1,600-1,700 times per field) so dram_scale_sweep.sh fell below its
liveness floor.  The DSP now always pays its real 1x bus cost; the knob
scales exactly what it scaled before S1.  No effect at the default
scale of 1.

Refs #313

events.title: grm-mej.26: retract bookmarks an earlier analysis round left at sites this round did not bookmark
events.message:
grm-mej.26: retract bookmarks an earlier analysis round left at sites this round did not bookmark

A switch site whose outcome improves between rounds (WARN in round 1, clean in round 2)
kept its round-1 WARNING forever: the clean exit writes a comment and no bookmark, and
setBookmarkClearingOther only swaps WARNING<->NOTE when a new bookmark is written.

BankAnnotationAdapter.retractStaleBookmarks is the bookmark twin of
BankCommentProvenance.sweep: after Phase 3 (the last writer of the analyzer's category),
every WARNING/NOTE in this analyzer's category at an address not bookmarked this round is
removed, and the addresses are logged. Phase 3 now records its violation sites in
alreadyWarned so the set is the round's complete bookmark record. Mode-lock bookmarks keep
their own self-clearing category.

Synthetic: nesmmc3mirrortest loses its stale 'BOOKMARK Warning e2dc' (the one-line diff;
golden edited by hand to exactly that reviewed line). MM9 now asserts no WARNING at e2dc.
build-and-test.sh check: only that row differed. check nes on this build: 32 pass +
shenlong 97 / dragonpower 152 symbol flap (shenlong PASS on --only rerun); no warning or

project.notes: Takeda Toshiya’s MS-DOS Player family, represented by cracyc’s maintained vt branch, runs original DOS command-line utilities directly against Windows files and console services. The official site and maintained fork are one counted project family. readme.txt explicitly targets 16-bit DOS command-line utilities and demonstrates msdos lcc sample.c followed by msdos sample.exe. msdos.cpp identifies Takeda as author, loads MZ/ZM EXEs with relocation and otherwise uses the COM entry at 0x100. The selected maintained source root is cracyc/msdos-player, default branch vt. Its README credits imported fixes from the cracyc fork; the official Takeda distribution is lineage/context, not a second project. Root and record ID are absent from the fresh 1702-project baseline at ac4ea751fcdb273322cfdac18cd679b83f03a90f and the prior dedup index. Inspected vt tip: b3ebaa8452be478afec604361db32e9451eb43e2. Emulator/development tooling with CPU execution plus DOS/BIOS service translation. The INT 21h dispatch sends 3Dh/3Fh/40h/4Bh to host-backed open/read/write/execute handling. The direct console workflow does not boot a DOS disk image, but this is not a CPU-only layer: text-mode hardware scaffolding, memory services and optional driver/VDD support exist. README excludes Win16, graphics/sound hardware and gaming as the project’s goal; protected-mode capabilities vary by CPU build. Original COM/MZ DOS binaries are x86 guests. README lists separate 8086, 80286, 80386, 80486, Pentium4, NEC V30 and IA32 emulation variants, including protected-mode capabilities and an optional V30 8080 mode. Canonical source_cpu=x86 describes the principal DOS guest ISA without mistaking the emulated model labels for host CPU requirements or claiming full PC compatibility. README explicitly distinguishes _x86 binaries for 32/64-bit Windows and _x64 binaries for 64-bit Windows; msdos.vcxproj independently contains Win32 and x64 output configurations. These support host target_cpu x86 and x86-64. The i86/i286/i386 suffixes and HAS_I286 macro select the emulated guest core, not the native output ISA. No native Linux or macOS support is established by these Windows/MinGW recipes. Source includes Visual C++ projects and build batch routes, plus MinGW Makefile.mingw. Current CI is configured on windows-latest for i86, V30, i286, i386 and i486 variants; it is configuration evidence rather than an observed successful run. The older simple Makefile selects an i586-mingw32msvc cross compiler and Windows libraries, so it does not establish a native Unix build. README’s packaged-binary count says 12 but lists 14 variants; record variant names rather than repeating that count. All four build flags remain null; no candidate compilation, guest execution, emulation, gameplay or byte comparison was performed. Two host-output profiles retain explicit _x86 versus _x64 Windows requirements from the README. No Windows version or numerical host RAM minimum is established from the reviewed pinned material. The emulated 1/16/32 MB memory configuration is guest memory, not host RAM. Direct commands use host paths; original COMMAND.COM is needed for batch execution. VDD support is limited to selected 32-bit process builds with companion ntvdm.exe and is not available in x64 process builds. For MS-DOS Player, review of 30 latest available default-branch commit metadata/messages (requested 30), the complete non-truncated 957-entry tree, and selected documentation, implementation/build and license sources found no affirmative development-AI attribution. ai.usage remains null and ai.tools empty. This bounded search is not proof of non-use; agent/config filenames, provider/bot emails, gameplay AI and project age are not evidence. Older history beyond this 30-commit window was not exhausted. One family combines Takeda’s MS-DOS Player and the cracyc maintained fork; GitHub fork=false is hosting metadata and does not negate the documented lineage. README licenses source under GPL v2 and credits MAME CPU cores, Neko Project 21/W, DOSBox/DOSBox-X, DOSVAXJ3 and ReactOS-derived portions; component notices need preservation. Guest DOS compilers, commands, libraries and COMMAND.COM retain separate rights and must be supplied lawfully. This is neither Microsoft’s original NTVDM nor davidly/ntvdm. project.display_title: Ghidra Retro Machines — bank-aware loaders and retro CPU languages
project.status: Active; save-slot proofs now cross function jumps and bounded save-helper calls
project.notes: Ghidra extension for banked C64/C128/PET PRG and NES iNES analysis, with SPC700 and 65C816 language variants. The current NES pass bounds split low/high pointer tables by the next section gap: Dodge shrinks from 64 to 26 entries, River City Ransom from 64 to 27 and Mega Man 2 from 255 to 15. Upstream reports build-and-test SUITE OK and 29 NES baseline passes plus the three corrected fixtures. Existing 65C816 oracle-defect guards and language limitations remain; these gates show bounded analysis improvements, not universal correctness. The reviewed commit explicitly credits Claude Opus 5.5. Evidence: https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/6556e84ff267a0c96e7c89c5dbe2d3c3777d2aad The next analyzer pass extends RAM save-slot proofs across admitted cross-function jumps and narrowly recognized save-helper calls, while preserving conservative abandon rules and declining unresolved overlay-bank cases. Upstream reports 33 NES tests passing; the separate Dragon Power symbol-output flap remains documented. Evidence: https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/3f983b0189e67e2f8337804e0c2beb46c5483d44

project.title: Downland — native C reconstruction and console ports
project.display_title: Downland — native C reconstruction and console ports
project.status: Active alpha native reconstruction; CD-i port in progress; upstream-playable ports remain close rather than exact
project.notes: Native C/C++ game logic derived from Downland_RE, with a separate game_8bit implementation and platform layers. player.c implements physics, hazards, pickups, doors and game flow rather than interpreting original 6809 instructions. The research repository is a predecessor, not a second C port. Reconstruction of Downland graphics, physics, hazards, climbing, pickups, room timers, and repeated-game difficulty. Shared normal and 8-bit C game implementations with native platform layers. Windows graphics filters and numerous console/handheld targets documented upstream. game/player.c contains native player-death, sprite, pickup, door, and game-loop logic rather than a 6809 interpreter. Repository has distinct game_8bit implementation and platform-specific source/build trees. SG-1000 Makefile links SDCC, SGlib, PSGlib, and crt0_sg. Based on the author's Downland_RE research; this C runtime is meaningful separate implementation. Original Downland v1.1 ROM supplies resources and is required; console asset pipelines extract and convert those resources. Inspected SG-1000 README and Makefile: requires devkitSMS, SDCC, DLExporter, convertToC.bat, and adjusted local SDK path; output uses .sms extension for banked SG-1000 ROMs. Windows Visual Studio projects and other target makefiles are present. No target built or tested in this review. README explicitly labels this Alpha, documents controls/game completion behavior and says it is close rather than fully accurate; alpha prereleases and the SG-1000 author emulator-test report support upstream-reported runnable/playable=true. The source/recipes do not prove a current reproducible build on all targets, so compilable remains null. ROM assets and local SDK/exporter prerequisites are required. Downland_RE claims about recreating an original ROM are not transferred into this different native C port; byte_exact stays null. Original Downland v1.1 ROM is mandatory, either loaded by the runtime or extracted for console assets. SG-1000 uses banked ROM and was tested only in an emulator upstream; a physical cartridge needs banking and .sms is used to enable banking in emulators. Playdate requires its real console or SDK simulator; no CPU/RAM minimum beyond these target identities is documented. Build flags and heap/stack allocations are not converted into minimum hardware profiles. README explicitly calls this Alpha and says close rather than 100% accurate to original. SG-1000 author has tested only in an emulator; a physical cartridge needs banking. This caveat must accompany SG-1000 support. Latest GitHub releases are 2025 alpha prereleases; source is newer, with September 2026 rendering changes. Playdate and experimental slow ESP32 CYD are also claimed, but those names are new to baseline and flagged separately. MIT for reconstruction code. Original ROM/resource rights are separate, and users must supply the ROM. No explicit AI-assistance declaration found in the README, selected source/build files, and reviewed recent commits. This is a bounded observation, not proof of human-only authorship. Downland_RE is credited as basis. No baseline Downland title/root found; do not count future discovery of RE documentation as a second native C port. Playdate is a distinct supported machine established by its dedicated README, Playdate SDK 2.7.5 device/simulator workflow, CMake armgcc branch and pd_api.h C platform layer. It is added as a new canonical platform label. The Playdate README/CMake use Downland.pdx, while its separate Makefile still says HelloWorld.pdx; current build consistency is unverified. ESP32 Cheap Yellow Display is retained in notes as the exact ESP32-2432S028 board: Arduino/Visual Micro, TFT_eSPI and XPT2046_Touchscreen, v1.1 ROM on SD, experimental below-half-speed full-screen blitting, rudimentary touch controls and empty sound functions. No ESP32 platform alias or ISA is invented. The earlier folder-only CD-i signal was not promoted; current active source changes now establish it as an in-progress target. SG-1000 requires devkitSMS, SDCC, SGlib/PSGlib, DLExporter, convertToC.bat and adjusted local SDK paths. No independent compilation, installation, tests, execution, playtest or original-program binary comparison was performed. Positive build/runtime flags are limited to the explicit upstream claims described above; unknown facts stay null. project.status: active; bridge v1.21 and end-to-end MCP/Amiga live-test path
project.notes: Host/target bridge over serial to a real or FS-UAE Amiga, with memory/register inspection, breakpoints, remote execution, a web dashboard and MCP tools. The optional patched FS-UAE enables a separate emulator-level debugger; ordinary FS-UAE still supports the serial bridge. Docker is used for the 68k cross compiler. The environment now includes a reproducible AmigaOS 4.1 PPC/newlib build of Mesa 7.8.2 OSMesa for fixed-function software rendering, an on-guest self-test, an opt-in ES1370 QEMU audio route, and updated examples pins for three PPC ports. Upstream reports the OSMesa self-test passes in the QEMU guest; this was not independently reproduced. Evidence: https://github.com/geekychris/amiga_mcp/commit/1195f1277048a803c7e11ab0f0ebe292c357a28d https://github.com/geekychris/amiga_mcp/commit/9242be4af0 Bridge v1.21 now signals the task owning the registered reply port before falling back to a name lookup, preventing an older same-named task from consuming STOP. A new live-test script exercises the same MCP path used by clients through sysinfo, file transfer with CRC, launch, variable read/write, screenshot and STOP on classic 68k or AmigaOS 4 targets. This is executable test infrastructure and commit-level evidence, not an independently observed passing run. Evidence: https://github.com/geekychris/amiga_mcp/commit/73ce765b8b32fe968518da2d205897754062199b https://github.com/geekychris/amiga_mcp/commit/c605e4a12e2ac374da9ece533570cd1107a634de

events.message:
perf(app): reuse the shader chain's output when the emulated frame has not changed

The chain ran once per UI frame, so a display faster than the core (or a
paused game) re-ran every pass for the same picture, and fed duplicate frames
to history/feedback textures. Output is now keyed on the emulated frame, source
and output size, aspect and fps; params and preset changes invalidate it.

events.title: perf(risc): run the idle-loop fast-forward under any RISC clock scale
events.message:
perf(risc): run the idle-loop fast-forward under any RISC clock scale

riscClockScalePct != 100 switched virtualjaguar_risc_idle_skip off in
DSPExec/GPUExec (and was reported as a suppressor by libretro.c). It was a
precaution from the #569 design, not a found hazard: SCALE_RISC_CYCLES is
applied where the budget is handed out (JaguarExecuteNew), and the probe
measures cost/opcost from live budget deltas, so the skip already works in
the scaled domain. The one scale-dependent per-instruction term
(gpu_stall_scale_accum) only moves on a nonzero gpu_bus_stall, which is
structurally 0 in an admitted loop body.

Drop the gate, the IDLE_SUP_CLOCK suppressor/sublabel/log text, and the
user-facing 'overclock switches idle-skip off' claims. Add
test/tools/idle_skip_scale_ab (skip on vs off per-frame state digest at
0.5x/1.5x/2x, wired into make test, --require-fires so it cannot pass
vacuously) and repoint test_option_explain cases 3/5/9 at dram_timing.

Refs #569 #378

events.title: grm-mej.24: slot writer census treats a call into a realized overlay as a known bank
events.message:
grm-mej.24: slot writer census treats a call into a realized overlay as a known bank

StoredValueScanner.entersUnknownBank called every banked target outside the
caller's own block DIRTY, including a realized overlay, which holds one bank
image by construction. cv3's trampoline far calls are retargeted into overlays
(e67c JSR -> W8000_M2_B8::b1fb), so the save-slot census abandoned before it
looked at a single instruction. An overlay target is now walked. Base-space
banked targets entered from another block (a window's home bytes, cv3's $C000
window) still abandon.

JUnit: CrossCallSaveSlotProgramTest section 11 (overlay far call restores;
base-window call, slot-writing overlay callee, and overlay -> base-window call
decline; intra-overlay + fixed-bank flow restores). The two positive tests fail
without the rule.

Synthetic: nesmmc3mirrortest re-blessed, one line. e2dc LDA $59 / JSR H now
carries the slot's r7=3 over JSR $A000 -> WA000_B2::a000; MM9 updated to match.
Its round-1 Warning bookmark is stale and is not retracted (grm-mej.26).
check nes: 33 pass + shenlong 97 flap (PASS on rerun); cv3 byte-identical.

events.title: docs(timing): S2 result -- traffic census, read-derived grant-latency function, NO-GO
events.message:
docs(timing): S2 result -- traffic census, read-derived grant-latency function, NO-GO

Doom's critical (GPU) chain gains 0.31/0.46/0.68 field per flip from the
latency function x measured traffic (every bound < 1.0); injected into the
emulator it moves the present rate +0.01..+0.05 (stock) / +0.16..+0.46
(all timing options).  The function is assembled from JTRM rev 8 and the
ARB.NET state machine (not simulated: no Verilator rig or jag_sim checkout
on any host) and is written up as gpu-timing-spec.md section 15.  Also
corrects plan premises H-A (94% of GPU external traffic is spin polls),
H-B (68K work is 0.31 field/flip) and H-C (DSP traffic is large but its
chain has 1.25 fields of slack), and records the 6% 68K slice-overshoot.

events.message:
perf(dsp): keep the untimed DSP path a single table lookup

The first cut read vjs.gpuPipelineTiming and busArbiter.enabled in
every load/store body and tested dsp_bus_stall after every instruction,
which cost ~6.7% on jagniccc with both options off (release build,
A/B/B/A on the Studio).  Latch the timing mode once per DSPExec slice
into one byte (the #532 pattern), branch on a local in the exec loop,
and move the timed accounting into out-of-line helpers, so the default
path is the legacy dsp_opcode_cycles[] deduction plus one predictable
branch.  Behaviour is unchanged in every mode.

Also records the DSP's netlist-identity provenance in jtrm-errata B2.

events.title: feat(app): Netplay window for the core's link-cable networking (#833)
events.message:
feat(app): Netplay window for the core's link-cable networking (#833)

A friendly front end on the core's existing Network Link (TCP host/client,
JagLink / Voice Modem) -- not rollback netplay (#864).

- Netplay window + menu: host a game (port, this machine's LAN addresses),
  join (LAN-discovered hosts + typed address), device choice, disconnect,
  live status and link stats, a plain latency note, and the titles that use
  the link.
- Settings go through the core options. Mode/host/port are session overrides
  (never saved, so relaunching does not start listening); the address uses the
  core's vj_netlink.txt route (the host option is an enumeration), an out-of-list
  port uses VJ_NETLINK_PORT. Changing host/port while linked bounces the mode
  through "disabled" because the core only re-opens on a mode change.
- Status and stats: CoreHost::onLog taps the core's [NETLINK] lines (link
  UP/DOWN, "link stats"); discovered hosts are read back from the host option's
  value list the core re-pushes with SET_CORE_OPTIONS_V2.
- CLI twin (--netplay host|join|join-discovered|browse|loopback, --netplay-*)
  and ctest: parsers, the real core in-process, two app processes on localhost,
  a no-partner control, and a discovery test that skips where broadcast fails.

Refs #833

test(timing): S2 per-halfline bus-traffic census (TEST_EXPORTS only)

Counts every bus master's external traffic per halfline, independent of
the dram_timing option (whose charge sites are gated, which is how an
earlier census read zero GPU external accesses with timing off): 68K bus
cycles and clocks split work/spin by PC window, GPU external transactions
split by the gpu_busy windows, DSP 16-bit transactions, the OP occupancy
rule ungated plus RELEASE-bit counts, blitter B_CMD/BUSHI counts and
(BENCH_PROFILE) phrase traffic.  Nothing charges emulated time.  Compiled
only under VJ_TRACE; release objects unchanged.

test/tools/bus_census_probe drives it and dumps per-halfline CSV plus
hot-PC lists for spin-window verification.

events.title: feat(dsp): pipeline scoreboard + external-bus timing model (#313)
events.message:
feat(dsp): pipeline scoreboard + external-bus timing model (#313)

Mirror the GPU pipeline/gateway model (virtualjaguar_gpu_pipeline_timing)
onto the DSP, under the same option, and give the DSP the external-access
charge hook it never had (bus_arbiter.h's documented asymmetry, campaign
hypothesis H-C).

The DSP is "a variant of the GPU" with the same pipe-lining (JTRM v8
p.97), and the netlists agree at gate level: jag_sim jerry/SBOARD.NET and
EXECON.NET are byte-identical to the tom/ files, DSP_MEM.NET's local
arbitration matches GPU_MEM.NET, and DSP_GATE.NET is the GPU gateway
minus the phrase path.  The GPU's netlist/Verilator-pinned rules (R2 RAW,
R3 flags, R5 local load, R9 external load L=7+D, R15 divide, R16 MOVEI,
R6/R7 indexed, R12/R13 jump refill, the section-14 write-back port
conflict) therefore carry over by netlist identity.  DSP differences:

- local space is $F18000-$F1FFFF (DSP_MEM.NET), so GPU RAM is external;
- external memory sits behind JERRY's 16-bit interface (JTRM v8 p.97,
  pin note p.124): a long transfer is two word cycles (JMEM.NET), priced
  by the new bus_arbiter_dsp_access() as word + 1-clock pause + page-hit
  word for DRAM, two full cycles for ROM/I/O;
- indexed-store data is not score-boarded (TOM/JERRY bug 2, v8 p.134),
  consistent with the existing dsp_div_store_fixups data effect.

Inferred, not simulated (no JERRY Verilator rig): the JERRY<->TOM bus
handshake is costed as the GPU's idle-bus grant (2), and the split
pause as 1 clock.

With the model on, every DSP opcode's base cost is 1 (R1) instead of the
legacy dsp_opcode_cycles[] table, whose load/div/mmult entries are the
hand-tuned stand-ins the rules now replace.  Bus waits are wall time and
are rescaled under risc_clock_scale (bus_arbiter.h contract); interlocks
are core time.  With dram_timing on and the model off, DSP external
accesses pay the same immediate self-cost the GPU does.  Both options
off: the DSP path is unchanged.

Model state is transient (one transfer + one divide), zeroed on reset,
interrupt dispatch and option toggle -- the GPU model's convention.

feat(tools): install.sh/install.ps1 install and update the core, the app, or both

install.sh gains --what core|app|both (and --core/--app/--both), --app-dest,
--app-format, --force, --allow-unsigned and the VJ_INSTALL_BASE_URL /
VJ_INSTALL_RETROARCH / VJ_INSTALL_NO_TTY overrides.  The app is the macOS zip
or DMG (/Applications, else ~/Applications), the Linux AppImage
(~/.local/bin + .desktop) or the .deb via apt/dpkg, picked from the userland,
not the kernel.  Updates are detected from the machine (Info.plist, dpkg, the
AppImage path) with an install receipt as a hash cache for nightlies.  Every
download, core included, is checked against SHA256SUMS.txt; a channel with no
app build says so instead of erroring.  Unattended runs stay core-only unless
this script installed the app.  Gatekeeper protections are never stripped
silently.  Also: --auto-update off no longer reinstalls first, and --help works
under zsh.

install.ps1 is the Windows twin (5.1 and 7, irm | iex friendly): core into the
cores folder discovered from retroarch.cfg / registry with the word size read
from the retroarch.exe PE header, app as the portable zip (+ Start-menu
shortcut) or the silent setup.exe, -DryRun, -Force, SHA-256 verification.

test/installer/ holds hermetic suites for both over a fake file:// release
tree; .github/workflows/installer.yml runs them (plus shellcheck and

events.message:
grm-mej.22/.23: save-slot proof walks cross-function jumps and resolves through save helpers

Pieces 1 and 2 of grm-mej.19 (cv3's e67f LDA $22 shared epilogue, whose
save happens inside callee FUN_e2e0).

- grm-mej.22: solveSlot enumerates predecessors with the 4-arg
  closedWorldPredecessors (admitCrossFunctionJumps), as grm-mej.21's
  cross-block search does. The function-entry and call-reference
  abandons still apply at every node.
- grm-mej.23: a crossed call whose census is DIRTY is still a usable
  source when its callee is a SAVE HELPER (saveHelperStore): a straight
  fall-through line from the entry, with no flow, call, mechanism write
  or other slot writer, reaches one plain store to the slot, and the
  closure after that store passes the census. The call ends the path as
  that store. saveHelperArms resolves the store once per call under
  stateAt(call), not the store's merged state, and adopts only when
  EVERY arm is a RESTORED_BANK read-back of one cell, read on that line.
  SlotCarrier.storedVia names the call; the note wording names it.

check nes: 33 pass + dragonpower 168/152 symbol flap (A/B --repeat 4:
this build produced HEAD's exact dump hash too). cv3 is unchanged, as
expected: its far calls land in overlays, which entersUnknownBank still

events.title: bridge: STOP signals the registered client's own task (v1.21)
events.message:
bridge: STOP signals the registered client's own task (v1.21)

STOP looked the client up with FindTask(name). Another task can carry the
same name, for instance an earlier run of the same program that is still
loaded (bridge clients rename their task to the client name), so the signal
could go to that task and the registered client never saw it, while devbench
still reported success. Signal the task that owns the client's reply port
instead, and fall back to the name lookup only when there is none.

feat(app): controller remapping incl. the 12-key Jaguar keypad (#837)

Profiles (keyboard, every gamepad, one controller model) with per-game
overrides keyed by cartridge CRC, SDL3 gamepad auto-detection plus an
optional gamecontrollerdb.txt, "press a button to bind" capture, and a

events.title: feat(app): per-game cheat browser fed by the libretro cheat database
events.message:
feat(app): per-game cheat browser fed by the libretro cheat database

Cheats window (Emulation > Cheats...): the .cht set for the running game
is matched by name against the core's own title identity (or the file
name), its cheats toggle on and off, manual hex codes can be added, and
the choices persist per game under <data>/cheats/games/<key>.ini, keyed
by the cartridge CRC32.  Everything is re-sent to the core after each
load and state restore (the core drops its list on every unload).

The Jaguar database is RetroArch memory-style (decimal address/value,
width in memory_search_size): converted to the core's hex ADDR:VALUE
codes with the value little-endian in memory, ~10% already carry a
code and pass through unchanged, anything else is shown unsupported
with the reason.  cheatN_enable is ignored so nothing is on by itself.

The data is not vendored (CC BY-SA 4.0): -DVJ_APP_FETCH_CHEATS=ON
downloads the 41 Jaguar files at configure time, pinned by commit and
per-file SHA-256; a folder of .cht files can also be set in the window
or with --cheats-dir.

Refs #835

events.title: Keep the branch identity through the gate cache, run reduction and HEAD fallback
events.message:
Keep the branch identity through the gate cache, run reduction and HEAD fallback

Second review round on the ci/gate fold found three false-green paths:
- A sha's cached green now records the branch it was judged for; the
  same sha judged under another branch (main moved on, a feature ref now
  owns it) is asked again, and the observer's cache write records its
  branch too.
- A target whose own branch carries a red gate is judged by its own
  branch's runs, so another branch's newer run on the same sha cannot
  supersede that red. Without such a gate, main included, nothing changes.
- The HEAD fallback target carries the checked-out branch beside the bare
  ref HEAD, and the durable wait keeps it, so its gate is folded in.

Records the review verdict that raised them.

events.title: Keep a freed batch lock out of the window a person is typing into
events.message:
Keep a freed batch lock out of the window a person is typing into

The Stop guard's atomic acquire took a freed lock for any live session, so
the interactive window the user was chatting in became the batch owner
unasked. A turn end now needs an invitation before it acquires: a lock held
here, the window's own claim, or a transcript that shows no human prompt
(launcher workers and other unattended sessions acquire exactly as before;
an unreadable transcript keeps the never-ownerless path). An interactive,
uninvited window instead says the batch is free and how the user takes it.
A turn end that does take the lock leads its hook output with its own
ownership-change line. The guard-preflight prediction mirrors the rule.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Judge a soft branch CI run by its ci/gate commit status

A feat/** push runs every CI step with continue-on-error, so a red gate
concludes success and only the ci/gate (branch) commit status says
failure. The CI-status guard read run conclusions alone and reported such
a branch green, and the CI-terminal handoff passed that green on.

The guard now reads the commit statuses beside the runs and folds a
failing ci/gate status into the run it names (matched by target_url,
newest status per run). main posts no such status and is unchanged.

events.title: fix(core): fill BIOS-mode power-on RAM with $FF, not zero (#856 follow-up)
events.message:
fix(core): fill BIOS-mode power-on RAM with $FF, not zero (#856 follow-up)

#868 zero-filled power-on RAM in both boot modes to fix Fight For Your
Life under the real boot ROM.  The release PR's JaguarDemos full suite
(#875) then failed three size-coded BootIntros, which always run under
the boot ROM.  Of the three, only JaGol really changed: it seeds its Game
of Life from power-on RAM, so all-zero RAM leaves an almost empty board.
algorip renders identically under every fill (the probe's 4x4 pixel grid
misses its pattern) and solidWaves draws nothing under any fill; their
old PASS came from random RAM shown before the intro drew.

Fight For Your Life needs only the long at $F9A90 to be benign, and zero
and $FFFFFFFF both are.  So BIOS mode now fills with $FF bytes: still a
uniform fill (not the per-word PRNG that broke #856), not blank like
real RAM isn't.  HLE keeps its zero fill.

Studio check, fill variants x {JaGol, algorip, solidWaves, noisewaves,
test_ffyl_856}: zero 0/0/0/2.1%, FFYL PASS; PRNG 92.7/92.7/92.6/2.1%,
FFYL FAIL; $FF 93.3/93.3/93.3/2.1%, FFYL PASS.

Refs #856

events.title: fix(jaggd): zero GD_DirRead's record on a bad handle, refuse SD paths with no card root
events.message:
fix(jaggd): zero GD_DirRead's record on a bad handle, refuse SD paths with no card root

Two findings from the release PR review (#875):

- GD_DirRead copied its 278-byte stack record into emulated RAM on every
  call, but JGDFSDirRead fills it only on success or end of directory.  A
  stale or bogus handle leaked host stack bytes to the ROM (which can then
  write them to the SD folder).  The record is now zeroed first.
- jgdfs_host_path() joined "" + "/" + rel when no card root was set, so a
  savestate's handles could reopen an absolute host path on restore
  (JGDFSStateLoad does not go through jgdfs_root_ready).  It now refuses to
  build any path while the card is off or has no root.

test_jaggd_fs: a state whose saved path reaches the card through the host
root must not reopen with the root cleared (fails before, passes after).

Refs #783

events.title: grm-5dgx: realize one overlay per image for windows that ignore low bank bits
events.message:
grm-5dgx: realize one overlay per image for windows that ignore low bank bits

MMC1 modes 0/1 (prg_bank >> 1) and MMC5's shifted windows (modes 0-2) realized
one overlay per FIELD value, so 2k and 2k+1 got byte-identical twins
(cv3: W8000_M2_B1..B31, 32 blocks for 16 images).

- DescriptorExpressions.decodedMask: bits whose flip changes the maps: value,
  derived by evaluation and shared by loader and analyzer; canonical(v) =
  v & decodedMask, and home = the image of the initial value.
- NesRomLoader realizes only canonical values; names are unchanged.
- bankUniverse re-expands canonical values to every valid field value, so
  impossibleBank, canonicalBank and BankMirrors see the same sets as before.
- Every bank-to-overlay-name step canonicalizes (resolveComputedBank /
  resolveModeBank incl. override and home tests; BankMirrors.readWindowImage).
- clampToResidence pins only decoded bits; window resolution judges a bank
  known on decoded bits.
- DecodedMaskTest pins the masks and that only MMC1/MMC5 shipped windows are
  non-injective; nesmmc5test pins no-twin and odd-value -> canonical overlay.

Goldens: 11 synthetic and 16 real-ROM rows lose twin BLOCK lines only; no
ref/instr/comment/warning count moved. build-and-test.sh check OK;
realrom-test.sh check nes 34/34.

Restart a stale chat watcher through a request file with a bounded drain

Second review round on the code-changed restart:
- The restart request is a file naming the target pid

  responder gets SIGTERM, after RESPONDER_KILL_GRACE_MS SIGKILL, and the
  watcher exits regardless.
- A request that could not be delivered is logged as a failure, never

events.message:
Make the stale-watcher restart drain its responder and prove identity

Review fixes for the code-changed restart:
- The launcher sends a restart request (SIGUSR2) instead of SIGTERM; the
  watcher then admits no new responder and exits only once its running
  responder has, so a responder spawned after the claim read is not killed.
- A restart needs positive identity (watcher command line or a matching
  start time); the lenient liveness branch only prevents a second start.
- An unreadable fingerprinted file yields no fingerprint; the check is
  deferred and logged instead of restarting.
- The watcher's fingerprint is read by its first import
  (chat-watcher-fingerprint.mjs), before its startup awaits; the launcher
  reads the current one through the same module.

the GError hasn't been set.

The GError parameter was added in tracker-3.1, but there's no easy
way to determine the tracker version (aside from the ABI version).
Hence, if we're using ABI version 3L, the GError will be set, but
for all older versions, we'll only return `true` to prevent the
segfault from happening.

tracker-mini.c: New variable rp_tracker_is_3L, which is set to true if
ABI version 3L (localsearch) is in use, and false otherwise.
