Retired StewBC/c64m is recorded as a duplicate alias; Apple II/shared components are included in this root without multiplying the project count. Compatibility-test games/demos are not reconstructed-game records. README/product documentation explicitly reports booting/running guest software and testing on Windows/Linux/macOS, supporting author-reported runnable=true. Root build requires CMake 3.24+, SDL2 and Python; README says C99 while CMake requires C11. Build and CTest were not run. Some C64 tests skip without local assets, and known test failures are documented. c64m lacks complete G64 write/format/copy support and exact pin/open-bus timing; byte_exact remains null. Canonical current home replaces retired StewBC/c64m; count the monorepo once. C64 documentation lists remaining drive/media and timing-accuracy gaps; some tests require unavailable local assets and skip when absent. AI disclosure applies specifically to c64m, not automatically every Apple II/shared component. No build/tests or gameplay were run. Root LICENSE uses the Unlicense with vendored/external font/library exceptions. Product documentation says C64 ROMs ship in roms and Apple II ROMs are embedded; do not infer that the source license relicenses those historical ROMs. StewBC/c64m is explicitly frozen; StewBC/machines brings together a2m, c64m and am65. Current and predecessor roots were checked against all catalogue files and are absent. c64m is described as almost entirely written with coding agents; explicitly names Codex, Claude Code and Grok, with CPU/assembler/external-code qualifications. This disclosure covers c64m specifically, with CPU/assembler/external-code qualifications; it does not establish that every a2m/shared component was AI-written. Reviewed on 2026-10-05; no independent build, execution or byte comparison was performed. project.status: v6.4.2 plus protocol-v0 binary debugger frontend under active development
project.notes: CPC/Plus and GX4000 emulator with sub-cycle hardware models, flux-image decoding, an integrated debugger and TCP/headless automation. Beyond v6.4.2, the new protocol-v0 binary frontend on port 6545 implements HELLO/PING/MACHINE_INFO, register and memory reads/writes, PAUSE/RUN/RESET/STEP control, run-state queries and subscribed pushed events. Its design includes a 4096-entry lock-free event ring and controller lease; reviewed commits add server skeleton, reads, writes/control and run/events in successive tested slices. These are upstream implementation receipts, not an independent run by the tracker. No minimum host CPU/RAM was stated. project.status: Active; NES suite passes 29 baseline cases plus three corrected planar-split fixtures
project.notes: Ghidra extension for banked C64/C128/PET PRG and NES iNES analysis, with SPC700 and 65C816 language variants. The current NES pass bounds split low/high pointer tables by the next section gap: Dodge shrinks from 64 to 26 entries, River City Ransom from 64 to 27 and Mega Man 2 from 255 to 15. Upstream reports build-and-test SUITE OK and 29 NES baseline passes plus the three corrected fixtures. Existing 65C816 oracle-defect guards and language limitations remain; these gates show bounded analysis improvements, not universal correctness. The reviewed commit explicitly credits Claude Opus 5.5. Evidence: https://github.com/CBongo/ghidra-retro-machines/commit/6556e84ff267a0c96e7c89c5dbe2d3c3777d2aad

events.title: Project metadata updated
events.message: notes: Ghidra extension configures banked memory maps, ROMs, hardware registers and symbols for C64/C128/PET PRG and NES iNES analysis, and bundles explicit SPC700 and 65C816 language variants for SNES code. The SPC700 language is decode-capable with p-code still under rewrite; the 65C816 language is disassembly-oriented while its p-code is verified against exhaustive vectors. Current NES work resolves proven constant-pointer indirect jumps and bounds table-after-code jump tables by their switch window; Mega Man and Life Force rows were re-blessed, while Contra, Final Fantasy and TMNT changes remain held for owner review. Its exhaustive 65C816 vector baseline now reports 500 PASS, 8 N/A and 4 FAIL rows after isolating one named SBC (dp,X) test-vector oracle defect. The exception is guarded by tripwires that fail if the case starts passing or disappears, so it cannot mask wider regressions. Build and real-ROM gates therefore demonstrate bounded progress rather than universal correctness claims. → Ghidra extension for banked C64/C128/PET PRG and NES iNES analysis, with SPC700 and 65C816 language variants. project.title: Dethrace
project.display_title: Carmageddon — incremental DOS executable reconstruction
project.status: Active function-by-function reconstruction; new graphics and view routines reach 100% reccmp matches
project.notes: Buildable native Carmageddon reimplementation that replaces original DOS executable assembly with C function by function. Historical Watcom symbols exist but do not match released-code positions. Current CI builds and tests Windows x86/x64, Linux x64/arm64 and macOS x86_64/arm64 variants; no minimum host hardware is documented. The latest reviewed commits report exact reccmp matches for GetGraphicsOptions, ChangingView and drpixelmapcopy, demonstrating incremental function parity rather than whole-program completeness or playable parity. project.title: Amigo
project.display_title: Amigo — Amiga emulator for iPhone, iPad and Apple Silicon
project.status: v0.7.8 live on the App Store; v0.7.9 handed to TestFlight
project.notes: Native Apple-platform WinUAE adaptation with SwiftUI interface, ROM/disk import and classic-Amiga configurations. README documents ARM64 iOS builds; source CPU remains the emulated 68k family. The latest handoff identifies v0.7.9 on TestFlight, while v0.7.8 remains the evidenced live App Store release. A primary performance record for Amigo 0.7.8 on an M4 iPad Pro uses an Amiga Imager OS 3.2.3/Kickstart 47.115 guest configured as 68060+FPU without MMU, RTG 1280x720 and 256 MiB Z3 RAM. Four amibench runs (one discarded) vary by at most 0.8%, and the document reports 14.66 M integer ops/s, 1043.5 MiB/s copy, 2112.8 MiB/s set and 748.5 MiB/s read; guest 68060 selection is within roughly 5% of 68040 on the same device. This is a measured configuration, not a host or guest minimum. No independent install/runtime test was run. Evidence: https://github.com/thomas-luebker/Amigo/commit/760ae33879b42c4e33fb732dbc82f463c6f596a0 https://github.com/thomas-luebker/Amigo/commit/9067cf3e980612f115a288b6e0bc68e29091c71e https://github.com/thomas-luebker/Amigo/commit/c7c3678db457c710aff7e705d04dfcd80f95fd63

events.title: Stack-ours: per-file, per-run backups; Novice notice; pretend netdb
events.message:
Stack-ours: per-file, per-run backups; Novice notice; pretend netdb

P_backup decides file by file (it does not name AmiNetXDuo) instead of by
the library, so another stack's configuration kept under our library is
still backed up when it is set up again later.  Each run that keeps
anything gets a drawer of its own, Backup/1, Backup/2, ..., the first
number not taken, and never writes into an existing one.  AmigaDOS Copy
CLONE keeps protection bits, date and comment; a copy that does not arrive
stops the installation before the file it was for is touched.

The kept-configuration notice for another stack is drawn at Novice through
(user), as its pages are; 2.17's (message) has no (all).  A pretend run
writes no netdb files.  The ReadMe's manual removal restores from Backup
and keeps it until last.

Harness: Backup/<n> paths; -f roadshow-keepredo (ROADSHOW_KEEP_REDO) keeps
the configuration on run 1 and sets it up again on run 2, whose backup must
hold it; ROADSHOW_PRETEND runs without netdb files present.

events.title: grm-mej.20: refresh partial bank comments across rounds; $21-style shadows behind a bypass entry
events.message:
grm-mej.20: refresh partial bank comments across rounds; $21-style shadows behind a bypass entry

Root cause of the e722 blocker was not dataflow: BankCommentProvenance.removeSegment split the
comment on its "; " join, but every partial-state bank comment contains "; " itself
("[known: ...; assumed from initial: ...]"). The recorded text never matched as one segment,
plan() took the human-edit fail-safe, and round 1's comment stuck for good. A temp probe showed
the CallEffect at e722 correct in every round (rounds 2-3: bank_5115 bits 2,4 unknown -- the join
of bank 0 via a8ad and bank 20 via W8000_M2_B20::b146). removeSegment now finds the segment by
its boundaries.

BankMirrors' write-through walk now crosses a CALL entry into a helper's middle (cv3's IRQ
JSR $e2e8 lands on the latch store past STA $21, the grm-p9y bypass), but only while the walk
has read no cell below that entry: Dragon Ball Z Datach's JSR $cc28 lands on LDA $59 / STA $8008,
and its callers do LDA #$08 / STA $59 / JSR $cc0b -- an argument cell. Without that guard $59
went WRITE_THROUGH and 6 false 'requires prg_bank known on entry' warnings appeared.

Re-blessed (reviewed):
- cv3: warnings 21->17, notes 11->13; e141/e24a RESTORED via shadow $21; e6d1 bank_5115=0;
  e722 bank_5115 bits 2,4 unknown; e2dc's unretractable stale bank comment retracted.
- ultimaav: f1f1/f522 RESTORED via shadow $5e (FUN_f331 STA $5e, bypass entry f333).
- tmnt3 (3) / megaman2 (11): bank comments lose stale round-1 bits (r7.2; mirroring).

events.title: grm-d59c: bound PLANAR split lo/hi jump tables by the gap between their halves
events.message:
grm-d59c: bound PLANAR split lo/hi jump tables by the gap between their halves

dodge 8251 dispatches through low bytes at 8254 and high bytes at 826e (AND #$3F -> 64 cases,
26 real). The two byte LOADs overlap past their ends and reach JumpTableBoundAnalyzer as ONE
size-1 load table of 64 + 0x1a = 90 bytes; 90 divides by nothing, so Shape.of declined and no
rule ran -- hence no [JumpTableBound] comment at the switch.

JumpTableBound.planarGap reads the gap off the merged extent (num - caseCount, claimed only in
2 <= gap < caseCount: gap 1 is grm-yjiq's overlapping 2-byte table, >= caseCount is a shape
Shape.of already reads); bound() then re-runs the lowest-target rule over the first gap cases
as the two byte tables they are, so the cut covers both halves and only ever shrinks.
The analyzer accepts a planar cut only when every kept target == byte(lo+i) | byte(lo+gap+i)<<8
read from the image. Bound comment notes "planar lo/hi tables N apart".

Corpus survey (temp post-script over check nes): three sites, all decoded from the pinned ROMs.
- dodge 8251: 64 -> 26; junk-code warnings fea5/fea9/fead gone (warnings 24 -> 21).
- rcransom W8000_M0_B10::82b3: 64 -> 27 (same Technos engine); +201 overlay instrs, +48 refs.
- megaman2 92e4: 255 -> 15 (LDA $9470,Y / LDA $947f,Y / JMP ($0008)); switch/case labels.
build-and-test.sh check: SUITE OK. check nes: 29 pass + those 3 + dragonpower/shenlong flap.

events.title: feat(kcpc): run control and pushed events: SUBSCRIBE, PAUSE/RUN/RESET/STEP (beads-3o1.4) (#96)
events.message:
feat(kcpc): run control and pushed events: SUBSCRIBE, PAUSE/RUN/RESET/STEP (beads-3o1.4) (#96)

* feat(kcpc): run control and pushed events: SUBSCRIBE, PAUSE/RUN/RESET…

…/STEP (beads-3o1.4)

Slice 4 of docs/protocol/kcpc-binary-v1.md. A client subscribes and is
pushed EVT_STOPPED, EVT_RESUMED, EVT_RESET, EVT_FRAME, EVT_OVERRUN,
EVT_SHUTDOWN and EVT_CONTROL_CHANGED; the controller gets PAUSE, RUN, RESET
and STEP (in, frames), anyone RUN_STATE. Sets CAP_RUN_CONTROL and
CAP_EVENTS.

The run state is announced by the core, not sampled by the server.
cpc_pause(), an applied resume and the last pause lease letting go compare
the state that now holds with the one last announced and call one observer
when they differ. A lease that pauses a running machine and runs it again
is never announced, so reads and writes do not make the run state flicker,
and a pause from the text IPC or the GUI is pushed like a client's own.

A stop is announced when it has happened: a pause from another thread
leaves the frame in flight to finish, and the runner announces it when it
parks, so the event's frame and pc are the ones a read then finds.

RUN goes through the new cpc_run(), which is not dropped while another
actor holds a pause lease (the defect of beads-pja3): the machine runs when
the last holder lets go.

Events travel through a fixed 4096-entry lock-free ring to a fan-out
thread. The ring takes several producers, not the one the design named:
pauses are settled on the thread that pauses. A client past its event cap
has its events dropped and counted, and is told with EVT_OVERRUN. An event
a request caused is sent after the response to that request.

No request waits for emulated time: a frame step arms the existing frame
counter and its end is an event.

* fix(ci): count coverage atomically, so threaded tests cannot produce …

…negative hits

The Coverage Report job failed on master and on this branch with gcovr's
'Got negative hit value in gcov line' for src/kcpc/kcpc_gate.gcda. gcov's
counters are plain increments; the KCPC gate and server tests run reader,
runner and fan-out threads through the same lines, and a lost or torn
update makes gcov compute a negative branch count. -fprofile-update=atomic
makes GCC update the counters atomically.

events.title: feat(kcpc): control role and machine writes: CONTROL, REGS_SET, MEM_WRITE (beads-3o1.3) (#95)
events.message:
feat(kcpc): control role and machine writes: CONTROL, REGS_SET, MEM_WRITE (beads-3o1.3) (#95)

* feat(kcpc): control role and machine writes: CONTROL, REGS_SET, MEM_W…

…RITE (beads-3o1.3)

Slice 3 of the KCPC binary protocol.

Roles. At most one client is the controller. HELLO with role 1 gets
control when it is free and never takes it away; CONTROL acquires and
releases it, and with the force flag always succeeds: the newest request
wins and the previous controller stays connected as an observer. An
observer's REGS_SET and MEM_WRITE answer NOT_CONTROLLER before their
payload is looked at. Control is free the moment its holder disconnects,
and a controller that sends no frame for 30 s is closed with the new
status IDLE_TIMEOUT. The role comes with CAP_MACHINE_WRITE, which the
server now announces.

Writes. Both run on the controller's reader thread under a CpcPauseLease,
while that lease is the only one held (change_alone()), and end with
restore_run_state(): a running machine keeps running, a paused one stays
paused. Alone, because a machine rebuild runs under a lease of its own
and reallocates the RAM a MEM_WRITE would be writing to.

REGS_SET sets the fields its mask selects through the new
subcycle_bridge_write_regs(), which subcycle_bridge_regs_to_machine() now
also goes through, so the rules of the text IPC and DevTools hold: the
instruction in flight is neither dropped nor replayed, and at a breakpoint
a new PC drops the fetched instruction while the PC that is shown is no
edit. HALT cannot be set (BAD_PAYLOAD); nothing in the core can set it.

MEM_WRITE writes CPU_RAM and PHYS_RAM, all of the bytes or none. The CPU
view, the ROM spaces and ASIC_PAGE are refused.

REGS_GET reported the Z80's own PC at a breakpoint, one past the address
the text IPC and the debugger show (0x0039 for a breakpoint on 0x0038).
It now reports the breakpoint's address, so a block read there can be
written back unchanged.

* fix(kcpc): a lease holder that is not alone lets go before it tries a…

…gain

A write and a read that had fallen back to a pause lease each waited to
be the only lease holder while holding their own lease, so each kept the
other from being alone until one gave up after 250 ms: the write answered
BUSY. Seen on the Linux and MSVC UI-free CI jobs and reproduced locally
on the efficiency cores (test_readers_and_a_writer_at_once, 1 run in 3).

Both now go through alone_under_lease(): take a lease, try once, and when
another lease is held drop this one, wait 200 us and take a new one,
within the same 250 ms. 6 of 6 runs pass where 1 of 3 failed.

The document also records that a controller writing back to back slows
other clients' reads (beads-df1x).

* fix(kcpc): a write lets a frame boundary pass when reads are waiting

Every write pauses the machine between two frames, and reads of a running
machine are taken at a frame boundary. A controller that sent its next
write as soon as the last was answered left the runner no frame at all:
on the Linux and MSVC CI hosts three clients reading beside it got 15
reads through in 1.5 s, each by the gate's 250 ms fallback, under a pause
lease.

The gate now counts the reads that have been asked for and not yet taken
(Gate::waiting()), and a write that finds some on a running machine waits
for one frame boundary first, at most 50 ms. With nobody reading, and on a
paused machine, a write waits for nothing.

Locally, three readers beside a writer: 153 to 253 reads in 1.5 s (was 71
to 177, down to 15 on CI), 22 to 40 writes (was thousands).

events.title: feat(map): scan each room's exits in the shadow the first time you are in it (SQ-1773)
events.message:
feat(map): scan each room's exits in the shadow the first time you are in it (SQ-1773)

On arrival (or in a still-unscanned room) a silent copy of the game is asked
look, then n s e w ne nw se sw u d in out plus the story's ship words, each from
a fresh restore; every landing is replayed once to confirm. A landing on a room
the map holds is recorded as a verified passage (probed, never tried); a
landing on an unseen room records only the direction (Room::scan_exits) so the
map never reveals, names or creates it; the rest become Room::scan_walls, the
only directions a later visit asks again. For a scanned room MapGraph::untried
is the real exits not yet walked, shown as the new MatrixCell::Exit (») with
selector map.matrix.cell:exit. The scan is the lowest-priority shadow user,
chunked in four-word questions, queued and capped. Setting scan_exits (default
on), independent of return_probe.

events.title: fix(gpu): long stores force alignment in every addressing form (#866)
events.message:
fix(gpu): long stores force alignment in every addressing form (#866)

`store (r15+rn)` was the only GPU long load/store form that did not drop
A1:A0 for GPU local RAM: GPU_CORRECT_ALIGNMENT_STORE was never defined.
Ruiner Pinball's GPU kernel patches four movei immediates in GPU RAM with
long load/store pairs at word-aligned addresses; the store form landed at
$F03A3A/$F03A56 instead of the long-aligned slot, `jump (r8)` at $F03A4A
went to $F09850, and the GPU escaped into DSP RAM at frame 56.

Hardware basis: MiSTer Jaguar_MiSTer rtl/jaguar_common/gpu_mem.v line 299,
`ram_addr[11:2] = ... dataddr[11:2]`, feeds gpu_ram.v (rama = ram_addr).
Every GPU data access (all load/store forms share the one dataddr mux in
ins_exec.v ~1010) addresses local RAM by bits 11:2 only, so A1:A0 are
dropped regardless of opcode. The JTRM (v8 p.55 etc.) only says the
address "must be long-word aligned" (errata B11), so this rests on the
netlist-derived RTL. The DSP instantiates the same module (JERRY=1) and
dsp.c already masks every form. External (main RAM) long stores are not
changed here: gpu_addr[1:0] passes through to the bus and the existing
storep comment explicitly leaves them for separate evidence.

Test: test_gpu_ops now stores through all five long forms to a
word-aligned GPU RAM address; before the change (r15+rn) wrote
1111CAFE/BABE2222 across two longs, after it lands at the aligned long.

Refs #866

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: JoeMatt

events.title: net_tcp: Reset connections that receive data after close()
events.message:
net_tcp: Reset connections that receive data after close()

After close(), a socket in FIN-WAIT kept accepting data that nothing
could read. Once the receive window had filled, the peer could never
deliver its FIN, so the socket and both of its buffers were never freed.

Reset the connection when data arrives for a socket that has been
closed, and when close() is called with unread data, as RFC 9293 3.6.1
recommends. Also reset a closed socket that is still waiting for the
peer to finish closing after 2*MSL, so that a peer which goes away
cannot hold it forever.

events.title: fix(file): break raw-binary base ties on I/O descriptor tables (#866)
events.message:
fix(file): break raw-binary base ties on I/O descriptor tables (#866)

Native Demo (bin) is a headerless raw binary linked at $5000 (its .jag
twin's JAGR header says load=run=$5000). Every one of its 15 absolute
references also fits a $4000 window and it has no JSR/JMP entry-point
hits, so InferRawBinaryLoadAddress's containment tie went to $4000 and
the image ran 4 KiB low: GPU runaway at frame 1, gpu_pc_escape,
video_stall, black video in both boot modes.

What separates the bases is that its startup LEAs descriptor tables
({dest, size, src}) whose first long is the Jaguar I/O destination of a
GPU/DSP upload ($F03000, $F1B000). Under $5000 three LEA targets start
with such a long; under $4000 none do. Exact containment ties now go to
the base with more of these hits; with no hits the historical winner
stands.

Scorer A/B over the 141 resolvable cart-matrix images: only Native Demo
(bin) changes base. After: GAME_CODE "video, silent" in HLE and BIOS,
same as the .jag version. Ruiner Pinball (the other #866 title) is a
separate GPU store-alignment issue and is not addressed here.

Refs #866

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: JoeMatt

events.title: perf(netlink): stop the frame-slot margin from re-overrunning every two seconds (#860)
events.message:
perf(netlink): stop the frame-slot margin from re-overrunning every two seconds (#860)

JLinkFrameTick widens the wait margin by 1 ms when a frame that waited ran
past its vsync, then decays it by 0.5 ms after 60 clean frames.  When the
frontend's post-hook cost really exceeds the 3 ms margin the decay walks the
margin straight back into the failure, so a vsync is dropped about every
2 s for as long as the link is up.  Simulator, Doom 2P, 3 ms of frontend cost
after the frame-end hook: 0.5 missed vsyncs/s (30/min) on both a 3 ms/way and
a Wi-Fi link, identical on the pre-change and the idle-wait builds.

A late frame now also raises a floor (failed extra + one decay step, at most
4 ms) under the decay, which relaxes by one step per minute of clean frames,
so the margin settles just above what the frontend needs and re-probes once a
minute at worst.  A late frame whose emulation cost was more than 1 ms over its
EWMA (a scene change or level load, not the margin) does not raise the floor,
so those still recover within seconds as before.  Same simulator profile after:
0.0 missed vsyncs/s, tic rate unchanged (20.0 tics/s at 3 ms/way, 15.3 on the
Wi-Fi link).  With no late frames the code path is identical to before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: JoeMatt

events.title: perf(netlink): wait for unprompted link bytes, add on-device hop diagnostic (#860)
events.message:
perf(netlink): wait for unprompted link bytes, add on-device hop diagnostic (#860)

A Doom link tic is 12 one-way single-byte hops (6 pairs, ping-pong).  Two
parts of the old behaviour made the tic rate depend on the vsync phase
between the two devices, collapsing to 5 tics/s at bad phases even on a
fast link: JLinkAwaitReply only engaged after we transmitted, so a side that
only ANSWERS spun on ASISTAT with no wait, finished its frame in ~2 ms and
sat in the frontend while the partner's byte arrived; every such hop then
cost a whole video frame.

uart.c now counts consecutive ASISTAT reads with nothing to send or receive
and, past 24 in a frame, calls JLinkAwaitIdle(), which blocks like the reply
wait (same frame budget and timeout) so the byte is seen the moment it
arrives.  A silent partner backs off exponentially (1..32 frames without idle
waits); any received byte resets it.  Real transports on the JagLink device
only (not loopback, not the voice modem).

Simulator, Doom 2P, tics/s averaged over 4 vsync phases, before -> after
(emu 2 ms, 5 us poll_receive):
  2 ms one-way 27.5 -> 27.5   2.5 ms 19.8 -> 26.0   3 ms 16.3 -> 20.8
  4 ms 7.5 -> 19.2   Wi-Fi A (2 ms+3 jitter+2% spikes) 8.9 -> 16.0
  Wi-Fi B (3 ms+8 jitter+3% spikes) 5.4 -> 9.0   3 ms with emu 6 ms 10 -> 15

Also: a once-per-5-s INFO log line while a link carries traffic (hops/s, mean
hop time, wait per hop, slipped-hop share, timeouts, budget cuts, emulation
cost, idle-wait hits) so the numbers can be read from the RetroArch log on
iOS; netlink_sim gains --btrace/--log/--loss-pct/--rto-ms/--udp-rto-ms/
--corrupt and the clock patch gains a byte-event hook; netlink_btrace_report.py
breaks hop time down by cause and analyses the Doom tic structure.

events.title: fix(blitter): charge only the 68000 for WMCJ's blits so gameplay stops tearing
events.message:
fix(blitter): charge only the 68000 for WMCJ's blits so gameplay stops tearing

White Men Can't Jump flickered heavily in gameplay at default settings, and
almost not at all with the 68K at 3x and the RISC chips at 2x.

Mechanism: the game triple-buffers. Each field it clears a back buffer at
about halfline 67, the GPU draws it with about 40 blits, and the 68000's VI
handler swaps the OP object pointer at halfline 507. The titledb row from
#827 enables blitter bus timing, and that model also made the GPU wait out
every one of its own blits at the worst-case cost (a DRAM row change on
every access). With that wait the draw started late (median halfline 244)
and in 86 of 125 fields was still running at the swap. The OP then showed
half-built frames: horizontal tears, and sprites missing for a field.

Disabling only the GPU-side charge produces output identical to having
blitter timing off entirely (median start at halfline 67, draw finished by
halfline 200, no spill past the swap). The intro logo fix still holds: boot
frames 0-300 hash identically and the logo is 43.8% lit. That fix needs
only the 68000 to be frozen during its own fade copies (JTRM v8 p.8 and
p.69).

The change adds blitter_timing value "m68k" ("68000 only"). GPU accesses
neither wait nor close the busy window, and GPU-kicked blits do not open
one. "enabled" keeps its old meaning, so no other title changes by default.
The WMCJ titledb row now selects "m68k".

Flicker metric over the attract-demo match, two saved start points of 600
frames each (frames where a third of the picture reverts to its state two
frames earlier / single-tear spliced frames):
  stock row (enabled)   68/12  95/15
  fixed row (m68k)      21/2   23/4
  m68k 3x + RISC 2x     12/2   16/1

Test: test/tools/fb_flicker_probe gates frames 1250-1850 from boot (limits
54 big, 6 splice; fixed 40/2). A control run with blitter_timing=enabled
must exceed the limits (68/12). test_titledb pins the row value.

Closes #736

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: JoeMatt

events.title: fix(gpu): instructions behind a G_FLAGS store use the pre-store register bank (#865)
events.message:
fix(gpu): instructions behind a G_FLAGS store use the pre-store register bank (#865)

GPUWriteLong's G_FLAGS case switched the register bank and dispatched
interrupts inside the store itself, with no retire window. JTRM v8 p.59
(GPU flags register): "writing a value to the flag bits and making use of
those flag bits in the following instruction will not work properly due to
pipe-lining effects" -- at least one other instruction must lie between.
Software Reference v2.4 p.46 says two (four for an indexed STORE); Hardware
Bugs & Warnings p.3 #11 says two NOPs after a STORE to G_FLAGS or D_FLAGS
and names the register bank explicitly. This ports the DSP model (d220aa2,
#853/#862) to the GPU.

GPU-specific findings (JTRM v8 pp.38-39, 58-59):
- Bit layout matches the DSP: IMASK bit 3 (writing 1 has no effect),
  INT_ENA0-4 bits 4-8, INT_CLR0-4 bits 9-13, REGPAGE bit 14 (overridden by
  IMASK, which forces bank 0). No INT_ENA5/INT_CLR5 on the GPU.
- p.39: "Jump instructions are always atomic with the instruction which
  succeeds them", and of the example ISR epilogue `jump (r28); store
  r29,(r30)` (G_FLAGS restore in the delay slot) "Interrupts are re-enabled
  on the instruction after the jump". So the jump ordering the DSP had to
  infer is manual text on the GPU.
- Unlike the DSP (#744), GPU interrupts are dispatched synchronously from
  GPUSetIRQLine and at GPUExec slice entry; there was no in-loop re-check.

Change (src/tom/gpu.c):
- GPU_FLAGS_RETIRE_DELAY = 2 (store + one instruction). A GPU-issued
  G_FLAGS store sets gpuFlagsRetireDelay and, if it cleared IMASK,
  gpuFlagsIRQPending; it no longer repoints gpu_reg/gpu_alternate_reg nor
  calls GPUHandleIRQs. The INT_CLR latch clear stays immediate.
- GPUExec counts the delay down after each instruction (ahead of the idle
  probe and the SINGLE_STEP break); at zero GPUFlagsRetire() commits the
  bank (GPUUpdateRegisterBanks) and, if pending, runs the interrupt check
  the store used to make. Only hot-path cost: one predictable branch.
- GPUHandleIRQs holds off while a window with a pending IMASK clear is open
  (covers event-callback asserts and the slice-entry call); a dispatch
  retires any open window.
- jump/jr commit the bank before the inline delay slot (no dispatch there,
  p.39) and, AFTER applying the branch target, retire and re-check
  interrupts -- so `jump (Rret); store G_FLAGS` still pushes target-2 and
  the target sees the new bank; `store G_FLAGS; jump (Rn)` reads Rn from
  the old bank.
- Host (68K/DSP/blitter) writes switch immediately; they also honour a
  re-check a pending GPU store still owes.
- Savestate: GPU chunk's existing active_bank byte carries the remaining
  delay in bits 1-2 and the pending re-check in bit 3 (v17 extended in
  place, src/core/state.h). Old states hold 0/1 = no window.
- Idle-loop probe theorem comments updated (no window can be live in an
  admitted body: no stores admitted, and the taken jr retires any window).
- gpu_pipeline_timing: unchanged; the deferred commit uses the same
  GPUUpdateRegisterBanks path the store used.
- Window length and indexed-store latency as on the DSP (errata B10).

Tests (test/test_gpu_ops.c, CI, no ROM), mirroring test_dsp_unit 17-21:
store REGPAGE then movei / move (old bank, then new); store; jump (target
from old bank, delay slot new bank); jump; store in slot (target new bank);
savestate inside the window (both the in-flight and the owed switch
survive a load); plus IMASK-clear hold-off (the instruction behind the
store runs masked, pushed address $F03102) and the p.39 ISR epilogue
regression guard (pushed target-2). Against the 470a507 core: 5 FAIL
(movei, move, store;jump, savestate, hold-off); with this change 66/66
PASS. Perturbing the savestate load to drop the delay makes the savestate
test fail, so it checks the window, not just the live bank.

events.title: NetWireless: older prism2, prism2 joins, drawer installs
events.message:
NetWireless: older prism2, prism2 joins, drawer installs

- prism2.device before 2.9 answers S2_ONEVENT with the online bit alone
  and CONNECT/DISCONNECT only on a change, and its signal whenever it is
  online.  Such an answer is now "association not known": STATUS says
  the driver does not tell, the window and ENV:WiFi say "Online", and
  nothing counts as connected from the signal alone.
- Whether the signal answer can be trusted comes from the driver: every
  driver but prism2.device (no longer from a past reading), so a missed
  reassociation on anxwifipi.device is found by the next reading.
- A join on prism2.device 2.9 waits for LINKUP (associated and keyed), so
  a wrong key never says "Connected."; an older prism2 counts a join only
  on a new access point.
- Interface files are read where the stack reads them
  (ami_cfg_resolve(): AmiNetXDuo:Devs on a self-contained installation),
  the search takes up to 64 files from a temporary list instead of 24 in
  the resident commodity's BSS, and the wifipi file is read once.

events.title: NetWireless: fixes from review of the prism2 support
events.message:
NetWireless: fixes from review of the prism2 support

- nw_dev_link() asks S2_ONEVENT with ONLINE|OFFLINE as well, which every
  driver answers at once, and never aborts it: either driver may already
  have taken the request off its queue when the lock is busy, and the
  abort then hung (anxwifipi.device) or replied twice (prism2.device).
- The commodity takes answers a driver gives at once before it reads
  the link, so an unassociated prism2 card is "Not connected" from the
  first picture.
- A unit whose signal answer says "not associated" (anxwifipi.device)
  is asked for both CONNECT and DISCONNECT again, and its signal answer
  is not overridden by an event state: a missed transition is found by
  the next reading.  Only a driver that answers whenever online gets the
  change-only mask.
- nw_dev_find() keeps nothing of a rejected interface file (its UNIT
  leaked into the next), and searches in name order.
- A join on a driver that names no network counts once the link went
  down or the access point changed, not because the card is still on
  the old one.
- The stub's prism2 mode takes LINKUP/LINKDOWN, lays out
  GETNETWORKINFO as prism2 does, and changes access point on a join.
  The harness adds: the commodity started on an unassociated card,
  explicit INTERFACE and DEVICE/UNIT winning over the search, a JOIN on
  prism2, and the fallback when no interface names a Wi-Fi driver:
  52 checks.

events.title: NetWireless: find a prism2.device Wi-Fi with nothing named
events.message:
NetWireless: find a prism2.device Wi-Fi with nothing named

With no DEVICE and no INTERFACE, both programs now take the first file
in DEVS:NetInterfaces whose DEVICE is a Wi-Fi driver they know
(anxwifipi.device, wifipi.device, prism2.device), wifipi first, and
anxwifipi.device only when there is none: a PC Card machine no longer
lands on the Pi driver.

prism2.device (Neil Cafferkey, Aminet driver/net/prism2v2, read from its
Source/request.c and unit.c) differs from anxwifipi.device in three
ways the tools now handle:
- S2_GETSIGNALQUALITY answers whenever the unit is online, associated
  or not.  NetWirelessPrefs asks S2_ONEVENT {CONNECT|DISCONNECT}, which
  prism2 answers at once from its state, and aborts it on a driver that
  waits instead (nw_dev_link()).
- S2_ONEVENT answers every requested bit that is true at once.  The
  commodity now asks only for the change from what it knows (DISCONNECT
  when associated, CONNECT when not, both when unknown), so it cannot
  spin on such a driver; association comes from the events.
- S2_GETNETWORKINFO gives the BSSID and no SSID: STATUS prints the
  access point alone, and a join counts any association.
Scans (GETNETWORKS, same tag layout, InfoElements with a length word)
need nothing new.

run-netwireless.sh brings the stub unit up a second time as
prism2.device with prism2's semantics: found from DEVS:NetInterfaces/
wifi0 with no argument, online-not-associated reported as not
connected, the commodity's event requests do not spin (0 in 3 s), and
nothing is polled while not associated: 48 checks.

events.title: fix(pause): lease holders let go through one call that says what they mean (beads-mk1w) (#94)
events.message:
fix(pause): lease holders let go through one call that says what they mean (beads-mk1w) (#94)

* fix(pause): lease holders let go through one call that says what they…

… mean (beads-mk1w)

About twenty CpcPauseLease holders released and resumed by hand
(release(); if (!was_paused) cpc_resume();) or let the lease fall out of
scope. With a second actor that resumed over a breakpoint or frame-step
stop that landed while the lease waited out a frame, left an instant in
which the machine was paused with no lease held (a real stop, to
cpc_stopped()), and did nothing at all while another lease was held.

Every holder now ends with restore_run_state(), release_stopped() (steps,
reset --no-resume, a machine that failed to build) or release_running()
(reset, the start of a frame step). release() is private. The chain's run
state is the single source for the last holder's resume, so the last
request stands: a stop after a release_running() stays stopped, and a
release_running() takes effect when the last holder lets go.

A KCPC read that falls back to a lease goes through read_alone(): it runs
only while its lease is the only one and holds the pause mutex meanwhile,
so it cannot copy RAM a machine rebuild is reallocating.

events.title: NetWireless: fixes from the #234 review
events.message:
NetWireless: fixes from the #234 review

- nw_iface_device() wrote a second DEVICE line after the first, past
  the buffer (nw.device[128] in NetWireless); it writes from the start
  again, so the last DEVICE wins.  Host test with two DEVICE lines and a
  canary behind the buffer.
- An S2_ONEVENT refusal other than IOERR_NOCMD/S2ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED is
  asked again on the next timer tick, never at once, so a driver that
  refuses every request cannot spin.
- Bars move with 3 dB of hysteresis (nw_bars_held(), host-tested), so a
  level at a threshold does not re-add the AppIcon every INTERVAL.
- A refused AddAppIconA()/AddAppMenuItemA() (a start before LoadWB) is
  tried again each tick until Workbench takes it; the unit is not read
  for that.
- A bare DEVICE name is opened from DEVS:Networks/ again when DEVS: has
  none and no resident driver of that name refused.
- The band follows from the channel when the driver leaves it out.

NetWireless is 8,832 bytes on disk, 11,152 bytes in RAM beside its
stack; 39 checks in run-netwireless.sh.

events.title: ND-5000: real CPU time in PROCESS-STATUS, and the preempting kick
events.message:
ND-5000: real CPU time in PROCESS-STATUS, and the preempting kick

X5PRO, the "current process" cell of each CPU's mailbox block, is now
written as the MICRO-5800-B30 microprogram writes it (PRNOWR, 025416):
the process number while the CPU executes a process, -1 when it does
not. nd100x only ever wrote -1, so SINTRAN's 20 ms clock routine never
added time to any process and PROCESS-STATUS showed 0.0 s.

A correct X5PRO also makes SINTRAN send kick 1 (ACT52) when a message
outranks the process a CPU is executing. mfbus_preempt_for_kick does
what the microprogram's ACTIVATE does: stop the process between two
instructions, save its registers to its context block, put its message
back in the queue (N5STA 2 -> 1) and let the kick walk the queue. When
the walk reaches that message the process resumes from the saved
registers and the message's answer is not applied a second time.

external/nd500x moves to 5a3f84b, which stops the servicer writing 1
into the high half of 500TU (the false "21 min 50.7 s").

Measured under SINTRAN III VSX/500 L, four LEDs on four CPUs: CPU times
grow with use; with the console running CPU-STAT on CPU 1 while keys
were typed into the LED there, SINTRAN preempted the LED process seven
times and it resumed seven times. ctest is 89 of 89.

events.title: feat(kcpc): machine reads through a frame-boundary gate: REGS_GET, MEM_INFO, MEM_READ (beads-3o1.2) (#93)
events.message:
feat(kcpc): machine reads through a frame-boundary gate: REGS_GET, MEM_INFO, MEM_READ (beads-3o1.2) (#93)

* feat(kcpc): machine reads through a frame-boundary gate: REGS_GET, ME…

…M_INFO, MEM_READ (beads-3o1.2)

Slice 2 of the KCPC binary protocol (docs/protocol/kcpc-binary-v1.md).

The machine gate (src/kcpc/kcpc_gate.{h,cpp}) is how a socket thread reads
the machine without pausing it. A reader queues a read job; the frame runner
runs it at the next frame boundary from kcpc_service_frame(), called once
from the shared frame epilogue. On a stopped machine the reader runs the job
itself under cpc_read_while_stopped(). A read that got neither within 250 ms
falls back to a pause lease. Each job has an atomic state
(queued -> claimed -> done) and runs exactly once.

- REGS_GET, MEM_INFO and MEM_READ for the spaces CPU, CPU_RAM, PHYS_RAM,
  ROM_LOWER and ROM_UPPER; HELLO announces CAP_MACHINE_READ and CAP_MEM_ROM.
  MACHINE_INFO moved onto the gate too, so it no longer pauses the machine.
- The stamp's frame count is the gate's own 64-bit counter.
- The memory Device gained bulk reads (mem_peek_cpu_range, mem_peek_ram_range,
  mem_lower_rom, mem_upper_rom): a 64 KiB view is four memcpys, about 1 us,
  where the per-byte peek took 116 us.
- cpc_read_while_stopped(): a stopped machine is read under the pause mutex,
  not under a lease. cpc_resume() does nothing while any lease is held, and
  three clients polling a paused machine through leases got 3 of 60 `run`
  commands refused (ERR 409 pause-lease-held). Now none.
- The gate reads the atomic g_emu_paused on the path of a running machine,
  never cpc_stopped(): the runner holds the pause mutex for the whole of
  every machine frame, and a reader waited about 15 ms for it per read.

The document is corrected where it was wrong: the fallback is 250 ms, not
100 ms (a paced frame's 19 ms sleep was measured at up to 107 ms on a loaded
host, and 14 of 301 reads then paused a healthy machine for nothing); a read
is never split over frame boundaries, so "a 4 MiB dump takes four frames"
is gone; the stopped-read path and the status precedence are described.

Measured, interleaved, -H, limit_speed=0, 15000 frames x 6 rounds (median
FPS): master 2443, this branch with no client 2454, with one client reading
64 KiB at every frame 2460, with three such clients 2359. GUI build: 2427,
2413, 2400, 2260. Paced, both builds: 49-50 FPS with or without clients.

* test(kcpc): leave room for a slow client in the running-reads frame b…

…ound (beads-3o1.2)

Link __lisa_init into SEG1; RAM= for run-los-tool.sh

__lisa_init copies the data segment's initial image out of SEG1. Linked
into another segment, the copy needs three segments in memory at once,
and on a 1 MB Lisa the Office System could not always make room: a
program with more than one code segment hung before main, on "Just a
moment, please...". lisalink.py now always puts it first in SEG1.

emu/run-los-tool.sh takes RAM=1024 to boot a 1 MB Lisa (the default
stays 2048), as granny-smith's web build and most real Lisas have.

  online/offline bit from the last event, so nothing that happens while

  only IOERR_NOCMD and S2ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED mean the unit has no events.

  roam to another network.
- "Wi-Fi..." in the Tools menu works with icons selected.
- NetWirelessPrefs is started on the commodity's DEVICE and UNIT.
- The program's icon is freed once its ToolTypes are read; QUIET=NO is
  honoured; a negative INTERVAL is 1.

events.title: Servicer: stop writing in front of the message on an inline buffer copy
events.message:
Servicer: stop writing in front of the message on an inline buffer copy

ndbus_servicer_write_inline_buffer set bit 0 of the word 16 bytes before
the message, taking it for MIFLAG bit WSMC. MIFLAG is a field of
SINTRAN's CPU datafield in ND-100 memory. In the message the same
displacement, 177770B, is 500TU, the process's CPU time used, a double
word in 20 ms units.

Measured under SINTRAN III VSX/500 L with write watches on the cell: the
ND-100 only ever wrote 0 there, the servicer wrote 0x0001 before every
MON 504B copy, and PROCESS-STATUS showed "21 min 50.7 s" (0x00010000
units) for every process that had printed anything. Without the write
the ND-100 still takes the inline arm, CPU-STAT and LED print normally
on four CPUs, and the cell stays 0.

The two unit checks that demanded the bit now check that the cell is
left alone. ctest is 44 of 44.

NetWireless: the Wi-Fi commodity and its AppIcon

The resident half of the Wi-Fi tool, status only (PR plan items 9 and
10 together: the AppIcon is the commodity's display):

- AppIcon: 0-4 bars by signal, bar outlines when not associated, dotted
  outlines when the unit is offline, crossed out with no unit, a "!"
  when it does not answer; the label is the SSID.  The 32x16 two-plane
  picture is drawn by netwireless_sig.c into chip memory.  A changed
  picture is a new AppIcon; from Workbench 3.9 on PropagatePosition
  keeps the place it was dragged to.  The planned render hook was tried
  on Workbench 3.2 and dropped: Workbench keeps its own copy of the
  picture, a hook returning TRUE draws that stale copy over ours, and
  returning FALSE leaves the label undrawn.  do_Type is WBAPPICON; with
  WBTOOL Workbench 3.2 drew no label.
- "Wi-Fi..." in the Tools menu, the CX_POPKEY hotkey (ctrl alt w),
  Exchange Show/Hide/Enable/Disable/Remove, CX_POPUP: all open
  NetWirelessPrefs, which brings its window forward if it is open.
- ENV:WiFi ("Home 3/4", "Not connected", "Off", "No Wi-Fi unit"),
  written only when it changes; %e WiFi in a Workbench 3.2 title bar.
- One S2_ONEVENT waits for CONNECT/DISCONNECT/OFFLINE (ONLINE when
  offline); GETSIGNALQUALITY every INTERVAL (5) seconds only while
  associated; nothing is polled otherwise.
- ToolTypes and Shell arguments: CX_PRIORITY, CX_POPKEY, CX_POPUP,
  DEVICE, UNIT, INTERFACE, INTERVAL, APPICON, APPMENU, ENVVAR, QUIET.
  commodities.library, workbench.library and icon.library are each
  optional (Kickstart 2.04).

Size: 7,936 bytes on disk (target 8 KB).  To get there the device core
opens DEVICE as given (a relative name in DEVS:; the default is
Networks/anxwifipi.device) instead of retrying a bare name.

run-netwireless.sh runs the commodity against the stub unit: ENV:WiFi
follows CONNECT, DISCONNECT, OFFLINE and ONLINE at once; the signal is
read once a second at INTERVAL=1 while associated and not at all for
4 s while not; 37 checks.  The stub now keeps S2_ONEVENT's mask.
run-wbgrab.sh -s netwireless shows the AppIcon beside the window, and
-V 32 boots Workbench 3.2 on its own Kickstart.

events.title: grm-dos9.5: keep bank state out of base-space bytes the flowing bank does not map
events.message:
grm-dos9.5: keep bank state out of base-space bytes the flowing bank does not map

Base space holds each banked window's HOME occupant only. The dataflow fed a
base-space flow target whatever state arrived, even when that state fully
pinned the window to another bank or mode -- so home-bank bytes were analyzed
as if bank n were mapped, and their refs were retargeted into phantom
overlays (nesmodetest's BRK -> c010 refs; 640 base->own-overlay refs across
11 real ROMs, every one from source bytes that differ from the overlay's).

BankDataflowEngine.mapsElsewhere drops such a flow, fall-through, or fallback
seed, mirroring retargetForState's rule for retiring the base reference:
knowledge only (no placement override), same-window flows exempt
(duplicated routines), and the state is kept when no overlay is realized
for the occupant (gmap-suppressed modes: drmario/tetris) or when the overlay
byte is the same file byte. Pass 1 now gets a BankResolution, so boards
without helpers are covered too.

Re-blessed nesmodetest, nesmmc5test and 11 real-ROM rows (blmaster contra
cv3 lwings megaman megaman2 rcransom smb3 tmnt tmnt3 ultimaav).
build-and-test.sh check OK; realrom-test.sh check nes 34/34.

events.title: initial commit
events.message:
initial commit

# PETSCII Panic — Devlog

A lawn-defense game in C64 BASIC V2, drawn entirely in PETSCII

https://m0nde.itch.io/petscii-panic

---

## 2026-10-11 -- I asked myself, if this is even possible and whether I could do it.

Can a Plants-vs-Zombies game run in C64 BASIC? C64 BASIC is slow, and is is real-time with lots of things moving at once. But zombies are slow, the board is a playfield is a fixed 9×5 grid, and everything stays in their own cells. That makes it much more doable than a pure action game.

### Core

- **Round-robin lanes.** Each pass of the main loop updates one lane: zombies, pea, firing. When the board gets busy the whole game slows down evenly.
- **Tick-based movement** Zombies move one column every few lane visits, not on a timer, so difficulty stays consistent no matter how much the loop is under load.
- **Sorted lists of zombies** Each lane keeps its zombies ordered front to back, and they queue instead of overtaking. A pea always hits zombie 0, so hit detection is a single comparison, with no searching or PEEKing.
- **One pea per lane.** Instead of tracking dozens of projectiles, each lane has one pea in flight, and its damage equals the number of peashooters in the lane. Stacking shooters still matters, and the game never has more than five moving shots.
- **Stock PETSCII only.** No custom charset means the full ~38K for BASIC and no charset loading at boot. Everything is built from block, line and circle characters plus color RAM.
- **Speed housekeeping.** The most used loop sits at the lowest line numbers, because GOTO/GOSUB search from the top. The variables that are the most used are created first, because C64 BASIC finds variables in the order they were created.

### The cast of characters in PETSCII approximation

| | Look | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Peashooter | `●─` / `│` | fires down its lane |
| Sunflower | `○○` / `││` | more sun per payout |
| Wall-nut | solid brown block | blocks enemies by being bitten |
| Cherry bomb | `╱╲` / `●●` | instant 3×3 clear |
| Zombie | `○` / `π` | basic, conehead, buckethead by color |
| Lawnmower | `┌█` / `└█` | one per lane, single use |

### Controls

Joystick in port 2 or keyboard. On the title screen, fire picks joystick and space picks keyboard. Keyboard uses W/A/S/D to move and SPACE to plant. Keys 1–4 choose a seed in either mode.

### Changes after play testing

- Peas originally flew on their own row below the plants and looked like they passed under the zombies. This didn't make sense. This was changed to travel along the head row, straight out of the peashooter's mouth. They are only drawn on empty cells and only erased if they're still a pea, so they pass "behind" plants without wiping them. This was much easier to accommodate than having to redraw screen elements.
- **Too easy with too much sun.** Initally, with five sunflowers the bank could hit 4,600+. The sun interval had to be slowed and zombies had to be made tougher.
- **Difficulty levels added.** Throttling sun and changing zombie speed led to Easy, Normal and Hard difficulty levels, chosen with the joystick or A/D after picking controls:

  | | Easy | Normal | Hard |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Sun interval | fast | medium | slow |
  | Basic / Cone / Bucket HP | 10 / 25 / 65 | 15 / 35 / 80 | 20 / 40 / 85 |
  | Wall-nut HP | 35 | 30 | 20 |
  | Cherry bomb cost | 150 | 175 | 200 |
  | Waves | standard | standard | bigger, more armor |

  Peashooters and sunflowers have 5 HP on every difficulty.

### HUD

The top row is now a dashboard:

```
SUN  125 ████░░░░ +75   NORMAL  WAVE 2/6
```

- **Sun meter.** Eight blocks fill in yellow as the next payout approaches, so you can see when sun is coming. It costs one comparison per sweep and one color POKE per block.
- **Payout label.** Shows what the next drop is worth, and updates when a sunflower is planted or eaten.
- **Seed bar colors.** White means ready, dark gray means recharging, red means not enough sun.
- **Message row.** Wave announcements on the left, the selected seed's name in the middle, and **RECHARGING** or **NEED 50 MORE** on the right.
- **Plant health.** The row below shows the health of the plant under the cursor (e.g. `WALL-NUT 18/20 HP`), ticking down live as it gets bitten.
- **Wave heads.** The bottom row shows one head per zombie in the wave, in spawn order. Heads waiting to spawn are drawn in dark shades (dark gray, brown, blue). They light up (light gray, orange, light blue) when the zombie hits the lawn, and disappear when it dies. To make this work, each wave's zombie types are now rolled when the wave starts instead of at spawn time, with the same odds as before.

### The lawnmower

The mower started as a single red block placeholder. This became a 2×2 character block: a gray handle made from box corners (`┌` `└`) and a red reversed space body. Because it's two rows tall, it has to drive over the plants rather than under them. Each step saves the four cells underneath, draws the mower, then restores the old position. The first version erased before drawing and caused a lot of flicker. Drawing the new position first and then restoring the old one keeps the mower on screen the whole time.

### Some specs

- About 225 lines of C64 BASIC V2, every line under 80 characters so it can be typed in, numbered in steps of 10.
- No machine code. All drawing is POKEs to screen and color RAM, using only PRINTs for the HUD text.
- SID sounds: a triangle "pop" for pea hits, sawtooth for planting and errors, noise for chomps, explosions and the mower.

### Next

- Playtest balance across all three difficulties.
- More zombie and plant variety.
- Custom character set mode

events.title: Cut the per-instruction cost of the ND-5000 doorbell poll and the wall-clock RTC
events.message:
Cut the per-instruction cost of the ND-5000 doorbell poll and the wall-clock RTC

Measured with perf on the ND-100 thread, four ND-5000s started and idle:

- mfbus_service_nd5000_mailboxes took 19.5%. It called four levels deep
  per station per ND-100 instruction to learn that no doorbell was rung,
  and cleared the scan flag with a locked operation every time. The tick
  now reads each started station's X5ACT word directly and calls the
  servicer only when it is zero, and clears the scan flag only when it
  is set. Now 3.9%.
- rtc_tick took 8.7%, most of it reading the host clock on every
  instruction. The clock is now read once per batch of up to 64 ticks;
  the batch is sized from the measured tick rate and falls to zero when
  ticks come slowly, so a slow or debugged machine keeps its 50 Hz.
  Now 2.5%.

The thread's own load barely moves (about 70% to 65% of a core): it is
set by the idle rule in private_cpu_tick, so the saving shows up as more
ND-100 instructions per second.

events.title: The game's names, profile and tables for Retrolarium

config/names.json keeps the game's own names (characters, enemies,
items, places) in English and the lists that carry them; Retrolarium
Studio and Kit read them when a project opens and keep none of them. Its
guard list names what Retrolarium's repositories must never contain.

accept the new configs.

until now: the revisions with their hashes and, for each resource, where

events.title: Put files onto a disk, and never save over the one that was opened
events.message:
Put files onto a disk, and never save over the one that was opened

F-031, on D-018's terms. Dragging a file out of a disk worked; dragging one
in said "not a disk image", because the window opened it as one — nothing in
ADE could put a file on a disk.

The filesystem layer places a directory or a file with all of a filesystem's
bookkeeping: allocation from the rootblock outward, the hash chain kept in
block order, the bitmap, the parent's and the volume's datestamps, and on
DOS\4/DOS\5 the parent's directory cache, grown a block at a time. Every
block is planned before any is written, so a refusal leaves the image as it
was. The layer above keeps an edit only if the health report finds nothing
new on the result — a write ADE's own report objects to is ADE's bug — and
refuses a disk whose bitmap already marks live blocks free.

Edits live in memory. A save is always a Save As to a new file, never over
the original nor any existing file the session did not make, and is atomic:
a temporary file beside it, then a rename. Undo and redo are whole-disk
snapshots.

`ade mkdir` and `ade put` take a required --output; the C ABI gains
ade_edit_* and ade_image_save*, with ADE_REFUSED and a reason; the window
copies files and folders dropped onto a disk or a folder, keeps a drop on
empty space as "open", and has an Edit menu, Save / Save as, an "unsaved
changes" marker and a question before closing over them.

Across the corpus a directory and a file went onto all 3,023 images ADE will
edit with no new finding on any, and ADFlib extracted the file byte for byte
from 3,013 — the other ten it cannot read at all. Five deliberate breakages
in the writer are each caught by the tests; the first, a wrong hash
function, got through until the tests used accented names, read the slot
directly and asked ADFlib for files by name, because every reader that walks
a directory visits every slot.

Logged, not fixed: BUG-011 (accented paths cannot be looked up), BUG-012
(three commands ignore --format=json), IMP-012 (ade check cannot see a wrong
hash slot), IMP-013 (cargo doc collision), IMP-014 (a drop is many undo
steps).

events.title: feat(kcpc): binary frontend server skeleton on port 6545 (beads-3o1.1) (#92)
events.message:
feat(kcpc): binary frontend server skeleton on port 6545 (beads-3o1.1) (#92)

* feat(kcpc): binary frontend server skeleton on port 6545 (beads-3o1.1)

Slice 1 of docs/protocol/kcpc-binary-v1.md: a second, binary server for
out-of-process frontends, next to the text IPC.

- src/net_socket: non-blocking loopback sockets with timeouts, the one
  place with #ifdef _WIN32 for this server. No SDL.
- src/kcpc/kcpc_proto.h: opcodes, status codes, capability bits and a
  bounds-checked little-endian field reader/writer.
- src/kcpc/kcpc_server: acceptor thread, a reader and a writer thread per
  client, 8 clients, port probing 6545..6554 on 127.0.0.1, stop() that joins
  every thread. HELLO, PING, MACHINE_INFO and the unsolicited ERROR.
- src/kcpc/kcpc_host: the seam to the emulator; MACHINE_INFO is read under a
  CpcPauseLease.
- Startup manifest version 3 with ports.binary; [ipc] binary_port_enabled
  (default 1) turns the port off.
- test/integrated/kcpc: a stdlib-only Python client and an e2e suite, run
  from make e2e_test (-H and GUI loop) and from the UI-free CI steps on
  Linux, macOS and MSVC.

Two bugs in the pause lease surfaced as soon as two clients could hold one
at a time, and are fixed here:

- Overlapping leases lost the resume. The second holder found CPC.paused
  set by the first one's lease, took it for "was paused" and left it so,
  while the first holder's resume was refused because a lease was still
  held. Four clients reading MACHINE_INFO stopped the machine for good.
  Every holder of a chain now gets the run state from before the first
  lease, restore_run_state() lets go and resumes in one critical section,
  and a real stop that arrives while a lease is held is not resumed over.
- The text IPC's `step frame` took any pause for the machine having been
  stopped under it, so a lease abandoned the step after a few frames and
  left the machine running. It asks the new cpc_stopped() instead.

The design document is brought in line with what the slice implements.

* fix(telnet): two Windows instances no longer share one telnet port (b…

…eads-3o1.1)

On Windows SO_REUSEADDR lets a second process bind a port that is already
being listened on, so the telnet console's port scan never moved on: a second
emulator reported the same ports.telnet as the first. The text IPC had
already been moved to SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE for this; the telnet console had
not. Caught by test_second_instance_gets_its_own_port on the MSVC UI-free
job, which asserts that all six ports of two cores differ.

* fix(m4): two Windows instances no longer share one M4 HTTP port (bead…

…s-3o1.1)

Same cause as the telnet console: SO_REUSEADDR on Windows lets a second
process bind a port that is already being listened on, so the scan from the
configured port never moved on. SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE makes bind() fail on a
port in use, as the text IPC and net_socket.cpp already do.

events.title: ND-5000: up to four CPUs on one MFbus, each on its own octobus station
events.message:
ND-5000: up to four CPUs on one MFbus, each on its own octobus station

The machine configuration accepts 1 to 4 ND-5000 CPUs and rejects more.
mfbus_bridge.c keeps one slot per octobus station, each with its own
runner thread, and the mailbox servicer hands a message to the CPU that
the message names.

- A message for a CPU that is executing another process stays WAITING
  and is served once that CPU stops.
- WEXT from an ND-5000 reaches the octobus through the bridge, which is
  how the swapper kicks another CPU.
- TSET and TSETP on the ND-100 side take the same lock as the ND-5000
  TSET, so a semaphore in the shared pool has one owner.

external/nd500x moves to 39e78bc, which holds the nd500x half of this
and the WEXT, REXT, CLINIT and CLREAD instructions.

tests/test_mfbus_bridge.c and tests/test_machine_config.c cover the new
paths; ctest is 89 of 89. docs/ND5000-MULTI-CPU.md describes the design,
the measurements under SINTRAN and what is still open.
events.author: Ronny Hansen

events.title: Run up to four ND-5000 CPUs on one shared pool; add WEXT, REXT, CLINIT, CLREAD
events.message:
Run up to four ND-5000 CPUs on one shared pool; add WEXT, REXT, CLINIT, CLREAD

Several ND-5000 CPUs can now execute at the same time against the same
MPM-5 pool:

- TSET is one locked read-modify-write for every CPU and for the ND-100
  side, so two CPUs cannot both take a free semaphore.
- A write to a page a translation walk has read flags every attached CPU
  to flush its translation cache at the top of its next instruction.
- Pool accessors use relaxed atomic loads and stores, so ordinary memory
  references stay unlocked but are defined behaviour across threads.

New instructions, ND-05.009.4 sections 16.28, 16.29, 15.17 and 15.18:

- WEXT (FFEC-FFEF) sends a word to external device 0, the octobus ACCP,
  through hooks set with nd500_set_ext_device_hooks. K is set when the
  device is not 0 or the word is refused.
- REXT (FFE8-FFEB) answers "nothing read": register 0, K set.
- CLINIT (FF1E) and CLREAD (FF1F) give each CPU a microsecond clock taken
  from the host's monotonic clock.

SINTRAN's swapper executes WEXT and CLREAD only when a second CPU is
configured, which is why they were missing until now.

test/test_wext_clock.c runs the four instructions through
nd500_cpu_step(); ctest is 44 of 44.

events.title: grm-mej.18: cv3 $8000 far-call trampolines restore via an ALIAS identity byte
events.message:
grm-mej.18: cv3 $8000 far-call trampolines restore via an ALIAS identity byte

Castlevania III saves the live bank with LDA $8000 / PHA, switches, calls far,
then PLA / JMP e2e6 re-commits it. Two things kept $8000 from being a mirror:

- MMC5 declares every PRG window mode-dependent, and deriveBankMirrors scanned
  only mode-invariant windows. It now also scans the windows of the layout
  mode a verified pass-1 mode lock (grm-dos9.6) pins, recording the window's
  bank field as before.
- The byte is $80|bank: bit 7 is the untracked ROM-select bit, and the field's
  low bit is ignored by the 16K window. New ALIAS IdentifyingEncoding: the
  byte, cut to the field width, names a realized bank whose window image is
  byte-identical, so committing it back re-selects the live bank. It yields no
  value (byteFor refuses); a read-back is RESTORED only with membership PROVEN
  or HINTED. Only agreement identity cannot explain counts toward the
  4-distinct-image floor, so MMC2's "identity except the top bank" stays
  refused (grm-km4f: identity draws no exemption).

Consumers: a call-site read-back of an alias cell is kept when the helper
commits the cell's field (encodedIdentifyingCell); restoreDetail words it;
trampoline field scoping and restoreAliasesLiveBank treat it like biased.

cv3: warnings 31->21, notes 1->11 (e5bc e5e9 e7d9 e7e9 e9b0 ff3d ff87 ffa7
ffb7 ffc7), all PROVEN by tracked state, no game hint. nesmmc3idtest gains
bank_id_9ff0 -- correct: under its mode-0 lock W8000 shows the same $1FF0
identity byte through R6; ID8 updated to allow it.

Split out: grm-mej.19 (e681/ebdd, $22 saved inside callee e2e0) and
grm-mej.20 (e6d1/e722 save $21, which derivation fails to call a shadow;
e63e pushes on two joined paths).

Gates: build-and-test.sh check OK; realrom-test.sh check nes = 31 pass + cv3
(intended, blessed) + dragonpower/shenlong symbol flap, both PASS on rerun.

events.message:
Install WirelessManager with the Pi Wi-Fi and start it before DHCP

The archive carries WirelessManager 1.5, vendored unmodified from Aminet
driver/net/prism2v2 (archive sha256 25b400ef..., member 196780 bytes),
with its wpa_supplicant BSD notice beside it.  dist/make-dist.sh packs

tools/fetch-wirelessmanager.sh re-checks the vendored copy against Aminet.

With the Pi Wi-Fi selected, the Installer copies it to C: unless C: has
one, installs the licence into the AmiNetXDuo drawer, asks for the SSID
and passphrase and writes ENVARC:Sys/Wireless.prefs unless a
Wireless.prefs exists.  When wifipi is the interface S:Network-Startup
starts, that file runs WirelessManager first (guarded by the prefs,
reused through Status COMMAND=, 32 KB stack via Run +) and gives the
interface AddNetInterface TIMEOUT=30.  A Wi-Fi defined but not started
gets the same lines commented.  Wired-only installs are unchanged.

run-workbench.sh -w join|keep and two run-all.sh rows cover the answers,
preservation across a reconfigure, a planted prefs file and
C:WirelessManager, the absence of all of it on wired installs, and a boot
of the written startup with a stand-in supplicant (install/test/wm-stub.c).

events.title: Open in Amigo: take images handed over by Amiga Imager
events.message:
Open in Amigo: take images handed over by Amiga Imager

Amiga Imager (de.amiga-imager.ipad) clones a built image into the shared
App Group group.de.amiga-imager/AmigoInbox/<id>/ with a machine.json and
opens amigo://import?id=<id>. SDL owns the app/scene delegates and turns
the URL into a drop event the core ignores, so the URL is only the wake-up:
the inbox is checked when the overlay is up and on every didBecomeActive.

The offer: Boot (saves the current setup as "Before Amiga Imager image",
applies the image's CPU/RAM/RTG/network, mounts it as the only drive, one
restart via ConfigStore.bootHandedOverImage), Add to Hard Drives, Not Now.
The image is moved into HardDrives (same volume: a rename, stays sparse).
The CPU must travel with the image: emulator images carry only the chosen
CPU's library and stop at "CPU library is missing" on the other one.

Also: MediaImport.uniqueDestination factored out of receive() for reuse.
Contract: AmigaImagerPad docs/AMIGO-HANDOFF.md.

recompiler's m68k target) now runs the m68k-elf GNU as already shipped in

events.title: fix(core): zero-fill power-on RAM in BIOS mode too (#856)
events.message:
fix(core): zero-fill power-on RAM in BIOS mode too (#856)

Fight For Your Life (1996) trapped under the real boot ROM: it sizes a
byte fill from RAM $F9A90, which nothing ever writes. BIOS mode filled
power-on RAM with a per-word xorshift PRNG, so the read returned
$1B90172F. The fill overran from $F9F58 to $FA5C7, destroying the GPU
parameter block at $FA260 (written by the 68K at frame 685). The GPU
kernel read a garbage loop count at $F030B0, its output pointer swept RAM,
and its store at $F031CE put $022F0057 at $1D8870. The 68K copy loop at
$81A7B8 then took an address error into the boot ROM's $E005DC pad (frame
1032). HLE zero-fills and never hit it.

Bisected by RAM swap to the single longword $F9A90: zeroing only it fixes
the run, and $FFFFFFFF is benign too; only the PRNG word breaks it.
MEMCON1/2, 4 MB banking, the #851 mirror and GPU/DSP boot state are
exonerated.

DRAM power-on contents are undefined (MiSTer does not clear main SDRAM),
but real parts come up in near-uniform runs, not independent random words,
and the per-word fill was an upstream VJ modelling choice. The old
comment's premise that the BIOS clears most of RAM is also false:
frame-610 dumps show $3D000-$FE000 untouched. So both modes now start
from the same zeroed RAM (RAM[0..7] and any RAM-loaded image are still
preserved), as the maintainer chose.

Test: test_ffyl_856 runs the good dump (CRC $B14C4753, checked; the [a1]
bad dump is an authentic BIOS reject) under the boot ROM for 1400 frames.
It requires the handoff and fails if the 68K parks on $E005DC. develop
fails it at frame 1032 (handoff 611); with the fix it passes, ending in
game code at $8037DA.

Closes #856

events.title: Fix ByteBuffer.Append byte[] grow path using capacity instead of used bytes
events.message:
Fix ByteBuffer.Append byte[] grow path using capacity instead of used bytes

When the buffer had slack (capacity > used bytes, e.g. after Resize or
Reserve), the grow path of Append(byte[], StartIndex, NumBytes) reserved
capacity + NumBytes, appended the new data at offset capacity instead of
usedBytes and set usedBytes to the full capacity — stale slack bytes
became part of the data and the appended bytes ended up behind a gap.

Now reserve only usedBytes + NumBytes, copy just the used bytes, append
at the usedBytes offset and increment usedBytes accordingly.

events.title: SNES boot ROM: the console's port timing, so uploads run on its schedule
events.message:
SNES boot ROM: the console's port timing, so uploads run on its schedule

romdev's SPC700 boot ROM now samples ports 0-3 and answers on port 0 on the
same SPC700 cycles as the console's boot ROM, matched from outside only: an
emulator's S-CPU side wrote the ports at every cycle offset and the cycles of
each sample and echo were measured (byte loop: port 0 every 11 cycles, echo 10
after, 25 a byte, 31 at the index wrap; first byte of a block: a 7-cycle wait;
kicks echoed 31 cycles after the byte loop sees them, 30 after the $CC loop;
ports 2-3 and 0-1 read as word pairs; entry 12 cycles after the echo). Still 64
bytes with the reset vector; same handover state.

4000 randomized upload scripts (single bytes, 256+ byte blocks, several blocks,
start right after the kick, restarts through $FFC0, out-of-protocol port 0
values) give identical port traces, ARAM and handover registers on both boot
ROMs in the recompiler's snes9x SMP; a 65816 cart logging the H/V counters at
3708 echoes matches the console boot ROM's log on the snes9x and bsnes cores.

The snes9x reference values the slower loop had changed are back to their
original values (S-DSP ARAM, word access, SPC7110 counts, APU speedup counts
and samples). snes9x and bsnes rebuilt; binary manifest updated. The 0.150.0
changelog no longer lists a boot timing change.

events.title: PS1 decomp tools: build psx-assets, psx-disk and psx-str without the game's names
events.message:
PS1 decomp tools: build psx-assets, psx-disk and psx-str without the game's names

The upstream tools compile in the game's stage, boss and character names,
its short title (module, package and crate names, project file paths, env
var names, messages) and the disc's volume identifiers. romdev now builds
them from a rewritten copy of the pinned source instead of the tree itself:

- scripts/src/decomp-go-wasip1/gen-source.mjs copies the two Go modules to
  build/ as psxdecomp/psx-assets and psxdecomp/psx-disk, renames the game
  package, and turns every string naming the project into a run-time value
  from projectid.go, which reads the project's own tools/<name>-assets/go.mod
  in the working directory. It also carries the WASI changes the -overlay
  did, drops the stage/boss/character tables (romdev_names.go derives kinds
  from overlay codes and reads the console-port lists from config/saturn/),
  and makes `make` copy the volume identifiers from the original image
  (romdev_pvd.go). Every rewrite checks the exact source shape and the
  build fails if the name is left in code or in a built binary.
- scripts/src/psx-str/gen-source.mjs copies the string encoder crate as
  psx_str: neutral messages, and the define and temp file name its `cc`
  wrapper uses are derived from the project's tools/<name>_str directory.

Verified on a real project tree at the pinned commit, old binaries against
new: extract-assets output identical; build-assets identical apart from
layers.h declaration order, which the unmodified build also varies run to
run; objdiff-gen units and category ids identical for us, pspeu and hd;
psx-disk make images byte-identical; psx-str process output identical on
40 project sources. Derived overlay kinds and ids match the upstream table
for all 191 overlays, and the console-port lists match. Go tests: 12
packages pass. psx-str unit tests pass as WASM. Name scan: psx-assets 125
stage/boss/character hits and about 1429 short-title hits before, 0 after;
psx-disk 221 before, 0 after; psx-str 5 before, 0 after.

events.title: docs(protocol): design the KCPC binary frontend protocol v1 (beads-3o1) (#91)
events.message:
docs(protocol): design the KCPC binary frontend protocol v1 (beads-3o1) (#91)

docs(protocol): design the KCPC binary frontend protocol v1 (beads-3o1)

Phase 3 of the headless-core epic (beads-cv2). Decision D1 put the frontend
protocol on its own binary port, 6545, next to the unchanged text IPC.

docs/protocol/kcpc-binary-v1.md is the contract: 16-byte little-endian
framing with request ids, HELLO version and capability negotiation, the error
model, the threading model (changes under CpcPauseLease, reads at the frame
boundary, hits through the bridge probe hook), one controller plus observers,
event subscription, bulk memory with six address spaces, the opcode table
with payload layouts, the startup-manifest port line and the loopback-only
security position. It ends with the eight PR-sized slices the implementation
lands in and the exit test of the phase.

No code changes.

docs(protocol): apply the user's decisions to the KCPC design (beads-…

…3o1)

Four answers from 2026-10-11:

- Takeover: CONTROL acquire gains a force flag and the newest request wins.
  The previous controller is demoted to observer, its held keys are
  released, and EVT_CONTROL_CHANGED (now with previous and reason) tells
  every client. No client has a special role.
- The port is on by default; [ipc] binary_port_enabled=0 turns it off.
- Media, snapshots and configuration join phase 3 as a ninth slice:
  MEDIA_INSERT/EJECT/INFO, TAPE_CONTROL, SNAPSHOT_SAVE/LOAD (SNA),
  CONFIG_GET/SET/APPLY, in the ranges that were reserved, behind three new
  capability bits.
- The protocol stays at major 0, same checkout only, until phase 5 has
  shipped. Slice 8 runs the exit test and finishes the docs without
  freezing; the freeze to major 1 comes after phase 5.

events.title: Βήμα 109: τα εργοτάξια των δομών έχουν ρίγες — και ο μετεωρίτης φαίνεται
events.message:
Βήμα 109: τα εργοτάξια των δομών έχουν ρίγες — και ο μετεωρίτης φαίνεται

Ως τώρα μια δομή που χτιζόταν φαινόταν ίδια με χτισμένη. Μόνο ο θόλος
ζωγραφιζόταν άδειος. Ενας καινούργιος ηλιακός έμοιαζε έτοιμος από την
τοποθέτηση, και μια πίστα που χτύπησε μετεωρίτης έμενε ίδια ως να ξαναχτιστεί
(§15). Ο παίκτης διάλεξε το σήμα «περιμένει» των μηχανών (βήμα 100): κίτρινες
και μαύρες ρίγες στο κέντρο της δομής, ως να χτιστεί.

Τι άλλαξε:
- st_mark (src/figure.asm, τράπεζα 2): η ουρά του ob_struct. Μια δομή που δεν
  είναι DS_ACTIVE παίρνει το σήμα 2x6, αδιαφανές, ένα byte αριστερά και τρεις
  γραμμές πάνω από το κέντρο. Περνά από το ob_mark, που το μοιράζεται πια με
  τις μηχανές. Ετσι το ζωγραφίζει κάθε δρόμος που ζωγραφίζει τη δομή.
- st_built (src/meteor.asm): στη θέση του DK_BUILT του ja_build. Βάζει το
  DK_BUILT, και για δομή ένα DK_TILE στο tile του κέντρου. Το dh_tile
  ξαναζωγραφίζει τα 3x3 γύρω του, και οι ρίγες πέφτουν πάντα μέσα.
- st_redraw: το ίδιο DK_TILE από το mth_struct, όταν ο μετεωρίτης κάνει μια δομή
  πάλι εργοτάξιο.
- Το dh_tile σηκώνει πια το φάντασμα (dt_ghost_rect), όπως το dh_crow. Ο
  κέρσορας μένει πάνω στη δομή μετά την τοποθέτηση. Χωρίς αυτό το αρχείο του
  φαντάσματος κρατούσε το εργοτάξιο, και το ui_hide έγραφε πίσω 8 bytes από τις
  ρίγες. Το ίδιο λάθος το είχε από το βήμα 38 ένας κρατήρας κάτω από το
  πλαίσιο του κέρσορα: στο binary του 108 το ui_hide έγραφε πίσω 9 bytes από
  το έδαφος που είχε αντικαταστήσει.
- Το dh_occ_a δεν το καλούσε κανείς από το βήμα 106: έφυγε, και η μάσκα του
  and έγινε σταθερή.

Μετρημένα σε us:
- ob_struct εργοταξίου ηλιακού: 14.250 -> 15.438, για τις ρίγες.
- ob_struct της χτισμένης πίστας: 11.182 -> 11.197.
- Το DK_TILE της ολοκλήρωσης: 23.032, ή 34.636 με το φάντασμα από πάνω.
- test_reveal, ο χειρότερος γύρος:
  - ολοκλήρωση του ηλιακού 31 -> 49 ms (όριο 100);
  - τοποθέτηση 97 -> 98 ms.
- test_meteor, η βροχή: 44 -> 46 ms (όριο 120).
- test_impact, μια κρούση σε κτίριο: 5.176 -> 5.262 (όριο 5.270, από το 76).
- test_suit, κρούση σε airlock με τρεις μέσα: 6.952 -> 7.070 (όριο 7.100).
- test_figure, σβήσιμο φιγούρας πάνω σε εργοτάξιο: 3.274-3.370 -> 3.570-3.748.
  Οι ρίγες στήνονται και κόβονται έξω από το κελί. Η χρέωση είναι 18.096.
- test_reach: το βήμα κέρσορα 19.796 -> 19.786 και 31.863 -> 31.860. Οι γύροι
  της τοποθέτησης +1-2 ms, για τις ρίγες στην εμφάνιση.
Η λίστα χρεώνει κάθε DK_TILE 11.000, όσο ένας κρατήρας. Το κέντρο μιας δομής
κοστίζει το διπλό, μία φορά ανά κτίριο, και ο πίνακας έμεινε ίδιος.

Μνήμη:
- 68 bytes στην τράπεζα 2. Μένουν 3.
- Η τράπεζα 0 κέρδισε 2 στο τέλος της: 221, 29 κάτω από το όριο των δοκιμών.
  Ο κώδικας πριν από το #2C00 μεγάλωσε 7, και τα πήραν τα κενά των align.
Το format του save δεν άλλαξε.

Δοκιμές:
- test_reveal, ο ηλιακός:
  - Ρίγες κάτω από το κόκκινο φάντασμα μετά την τοποθέτηση, και καμία μετά την
    ολοκλήρωση.
  - Νέο Game.under: η οθόνη χωρίς φάντασμα, μια πλήρης σχεδίαση χωρίς αυτό, και
    με αυτό ξανά.
  - Τρία αρνητικά: χωρίς st_mark, χωρίς το DK_TILE του st_built, χωρίς το
    dt_ghost_rect του dh_tile.
- test_reveal, κρατήρας κάτω από τη γωνία του κέρσορα: η οθόνη κάτω από το
  φάντασμα είναι η πλήρης σχεδίαση. Αρνητικό: χωρίς το dt_ghost_rect, 9 bytes
  λάθος, όπως στο 108.
- test_meteor: η πίστα που χτύπησε έχει ρίγες στην οθόνη και στην πλήρη
  σχεδίαση. Αρνητικό: χωρίς το st_redraw λείπουν (10 bytes).
- test_impact: το μοντέλο της μνήμης ξέρει πια το DK_TILE μιας χτισμένης δομής
  που χτύπησε (όχι του σκάφους). Τα έξι αρνητικά πιάνονται ακόμη.

DESIGN:
- §6.9: «Sites you can see, at milestone 109», και το βήμα 4.
- §6.10.
- §15: «A struck structure looks untouched», λυμένο.
- §13: building, meteor showers, impact.
- §4.2.

got the -m68000 ssh from C/.  build-release.sh now builds the Dropbear
client a second time with AMIGA_CLIENT_ARCH=-m68020-60 (still -O2 and

stays on the MULU.W half) into build/ssh-fat.

  refuses an archive whose C/ has one of the three and C/fat does not.

- amiga-client.sh: a -m68020-60 client links the libm060 multilib.
  libm020's newlib and libgcc are -m68020 and carry 64-bit MULU.L
  (vfprintf: 36 of them in dbclient); libm060 is soft-float 020 code
  without them.
- dropbear/build.sh: a non-ANY -m68020-60 build takes the MULW X25519
  half, not MULU.L (the *68020* arm matched it first).
- Installer: comments only; C/fat is copied with (all) over C: at every
  level, and a full reinstall copies C/ back over it.
- run-workbench.sh: ssh, scp and scp-runner in C: asserted by name
  against the selected drawer (sha256), and not the fat build after a
