events.title: fix(map): replay a chained command line piece by piece instead of filing it under its first direction (SQ-1772)
events.message:
fix(map): replay a chained command line piece by piece instead of filing it under its first direction (SQ-1772)

`go north then east` from West of House mapped one passage north straight
to Behind House: parse_direction read only the first word, so the line was
filed under it and landed on the final room. A chained line (cut at then,
and, '.', ',' outside quotes) is now not a move in any one direction; it
lands as a provisional ? stub and app::chain_probe replays the pieces in
the shadow from the pre-turn snapshot, recording each room change (rooms
passed through included; a directionless piece goes through the SQ-1771
relocation search from the state just before it) only if the shadow ends
in the room the live game did. A game that reads only the first command
(Scott) is mapped as that one command via a first-piece-only retry.
Separator findings per game are in the chain_probe module docs.

events.title: fix(android): launcher, touch and TV fixes from Play Store testing (#2413)
events.message:
fix(android): launcher, touch and TV fixes from Play Store testing (#2413)

* fix(android): touch input, rotation and on-screen keyboard access

- Latch on-screen joystick fire and d-pad releases to the next emulated
  frame so short taps reach the game.
- Android windows have no frame: stop subtracting a stale desktop frame
  delta on rotation (fixes "Height (-272) must be at least 128").
- Clear ImGui hover after a touch release so tooltips do not stick, and
  restore the touch position on press so repeated taps on one spot work.
- Remove hard-coded mid-sentence line breaks from the GUI help texts.
- Add amiberry.vkbd_touch_button: the KB button on the on-screen joystick
  can be hidden while the gamepad toggle keeps the keyboard reachable.
  A gamepad connected at startup on Android no longer disables the
  on-screen keyboard, only the on-screen joystick.

* fix(android): launcher fixes from Play Store testing

- Keep the Quick Start launch mode in the ViewModel's SavedStateHandle and
  only run WHDLoad auto-config in WHDLoad mode, so Disk/CD selections
  survive rotation and returning from emulation.
- Complete the static brand colour schemes and sync system-bar icon
  appearance with the in-app theme.
- TV: let D-pad Up/Down leave dropdown fields, keep focus on the launch
  mode button when it is selected, refocus content after dismissing the
  Welcome card, and draw focus rings on navigation items and buttons.
- Reserve bottom padding so the Start button no longer covers controls.
- Label joystick ports 1 and 2 as in the emulator GUI.
- Write amiberry.scaling_method instead of the unknown bare key.
- Separate the on-screen keyboard button from the gamepad toggle: the
  toggle is always configurable and vkbd_enabled is derived from both.

* fix(android): advance the on-screen joystick latch once per frame

inputdevice_read_msg() drains the event queue by calling handle_msgpump(true) repeatedly in one vblank, so a release deferred by the first call became due in the next one before emulation resumed. Key the latch clock on vsync_counter.

* fix(android): migrate the remembered on-screen keyboard switch

last_on_screen_keyboard held the keyboard master switch. Read it once as the new last_on_screen_keyboard_button value, and turn a legacy off into a disabled gamepad toggle too, so upgrading does not re-enable a keyboard the user had switched off.

* Update agp to latest version

* docs(android): describe the separate KB button and gamepad toggle

* clean up old notes

events.title: Fix mirror tap and protocol guards
events.message:
Fix mirror tap and protocol guards

Mirror play no longer routes the cable through monitor_a; it uses a count-only observer to avoid desyncing the other PC when only one side has the debugger open. This keeps the tap from altering the link timing while still counting traffic.

The patch also hardens netplay/lobby validation against malformed JSON, bad version numbers, and oversized frames, and fixes client shutdown semantics so close/connection races do not leave dead sockets or stale state. Added regression tests for mirror debugging, malformed hello packets, and protocol checks.

events.title: Βήμα 108: οι θόλοι ζωγραφίζουν μόνο ό,τι έχουν — το σκρολάρισμα στη βάση ένα πέμπτο φθηνότερο
events.message:
Βήμα 108: οι θόλοι ζωγραφίζουν μόνο ό,τι έχουν — το σκρολάρισμα στη βάση ένα πέμπτο φθηνότερο

Το §15 έγραφε από το βήμα 43 «1,6-5,0 frames ανά tile μέσα στη βάση».
Μετρημένο στην αποικία των 12 θόλων του test_scroll, το PC ανά 4 us:
- πλήρης σχεδίαση 642 ms: 184 το bmf_run (καθρεφτισμένα με μάσκα), 71 το
  bml_run, ~100 ο βρόχος γύρω τους·
- ένα βήμα βόρεια 93 ms, 29 το bmf_run·
- ένα βήμα δυτικά 91 ms: η στήλη των 4 bytes κόβει 192 γραμμές θόλου M, και
  κάθε γραμμή πλήρωνε ~100 us βρόχου για 4 bytes.

Τα περισσότερα bytes ενός κελύφους δεν αλλάζουν τίποτα: ένα ζεύγος (#FF, 0)
αφήνει την οθόνη όπως ήταν. Είναι το 40% ενός θόλου (έξω από τον κύκλο, και
οι οκτώ πρώτες γραμμές) και το 75% ενός δακτυλίου (και το εσωτερικό του, που
ο θόλος το καλύπτει). Στην πλήρη σχεδίαση: 3.362 από τα 5.888 καθρεφτισμένα
bytes, 107 ms.

Τι άλλαξε:
- build/span_tables.asm (tools/pack.py, από το assets/sprites.bin):
  ανά οκτώ γραμμές πηγής το διάστημα που έχει κάτι, (a << 4) | n. 36 bytes·
  η γεννήτρια αρνείται διάστημα που αφήνει έξω κάτι που φαίνεται.
- src/span.asm: ο βρόχος του ob_blit τρέχει σε κομμάτια, ένα ανά ομάδα· ανάμεσα
  στα κομμάτια το διάστημα κόβεται στο clip, η πηγή μετακινείται, το DE από
  το scr_addr, και μια άδεια ομάδα δεν ζωγραφίζει.
- ob_blit: πηγή, πυρήνας, πλήθος και βήμα μέσα στις εντολές του βρόχου, το
  d += 8 μόνο του. 83 -> 51 us η γραμμή έξω από τον πυρήνα, για κάθε sprite.
- Μόνο το ob_quads μπαίνει στο ob_bspan με πίνακα· όλοι οι άλλοι στο ob_blit,
  που τον σβήνει.

Μετρημένα σε us (test_scroll, με ταβάνια):
- πλήρης σχεδίαση 642.284 -> 498.940 (μόνο ο βρόχος: 607.440)
- βήμα βόρεια 93.328 -> 72.700, δυτικά 90.604 -> 72.540
- ανατολικά 14.412 -> 14.220, νότια 24.448 -> 23.480
Σε frames, μέσος όρος πέντε βημάτων: 1,2-4,0 μέσα στη βάση (1,6-5,0).
Στο παιχνίδι, με την αποικία δοκιμών, ο χειρότερος γύρος ενός βήματος πάνω
από τους θόλους 126-136 -> 104-125 ms προς τα πάνω, 127-139 -> 103-105 δεξιά.

Στη σουίτα οι χειρότεροι γύροι έπεσαν: test_link M -> M 96 -> 70 ms,
test_demolish ο θόλος 125 -> 105, test_reach ο θόλος M 91 -> 78. Ενας
ανέβηκε από φάση: ο ευθύς διάδρομος του test_reveal 83 -> 114 ms, γιατί το
ρολόι του HUD και 22 ms δουλειάς που έρχονταν τέσσερις γύρους μετά πέφτουν
πια στον γύρο του FIRE· η δουλειά μετά το FIRE 141,5 -> 135,5 ms. Το βήμα
κέρσορα του test_reach 31.666 -> 31.863 us (ηλιακός 19.693 -> 19.796):
εκεί δεν καλείται το ob_blit, και το προφίλ βάζει τη διαφορά στη διακοπή
(+150 us) και στο πού πέφτουν τα δείγματα.

Μνήμη: το span.asm είναι 264 bytes της τράπεζας 0, και ob_blit με ob_shell
άλλα 59. Τα πλήρωσαν:
- η οθόνη βοήθειας, τρίτο κομμάτι στις τρύπες του DIST μετά την κατεδάφιση
  και το σώσιμο (src/help_ov.asm, 211 bytes, στο GH_BUF). Στην τράπεζα 0
  μένει το hp_show: σβήνει τον κέρσορα, αντιγράφει, καλεί, και μετά
  ξαναζωγραφίζει. Η βοήθεια 374.640 -> 376.360 us στο πλήκτρο της.
- το src/install.asm στην τράπεζα 2, 68 bytes.
Μένουν 219 στην τράπεζα 0 (27 κάτω από το όριο των δοκιμών) και 71 στην
τράπεζα 2. Το OV_LOAD κρατά 1.939 από 2.048. Το zz_page2_end έχει πια assert
στο #C000: το πρώτο σχέδιο έφτανε 125 bytes μέσα στην οθόνη, και μόνο το
tools/mkdsk.py θα το έλεγε.

Δοκιμές:
- tests/test_span.py, νέα: 144 τεταρτημόρια (τρία μεγέθη, δακτύλιος και
  θόλος, τέσσερις προσανατολισμοί, μέσα και έξω από το κάδρο, όλο το κάδρο,
  στήλη, σειρά ή ό,τι να 'ναι) με και χωρίς διαστήματα, και 40 άλλα sprites,
  απέναντι σε μοντέλο. Πέντε αρνητικά, κι ένα που φαίνεται μόνο στον χρόνο:
  μια άδεια ομάδα που ζωγραφίζει γράφει μόνο (#FF, 0). Βρήκε το λάθος του
  πρώτου σχεδίου (ld (hl),h αντί για 0) στην πρώτη του περίπτωση.
- test_scroll: ταβάνια σε us, και αρνητικό χωρίς τα διαστήματα.
- test_disc: και το τρίτο κομμάτι στις τρύπες. test_bar: το αρνητικό της
  βοήθειας πειράζει τις τρύπες, όχι το GH_BUF. test_install: το mc_arrive
  στο page2.
- tests/uitest.asm: το span.asm και το objindex.asm στη δική του περιοχή της
  τράπεζας 2· στην επίπεδη θα περνούσαν το #3F00.

DESIGN: §8.4 («Only what a shell covers, at milestone 108»), §8.2, §9.3,
§4.2, §13 (νέα γραμμή για το test_span, και του test_scroll, του test_disc,
του test_bar), §15 (το σκρολάρισμα, η μνήμη, τα κομμάτια στις τρύπες).

events.title: grm-dos9.2: resolve calls into multi-entry helpers sharing one store tail
events.message:
grm-dos9.2: resolve calls into multi-entry helpers sharing one store tail

A call into a helper whose later entries converge on one store (cv3
e2e0 -> e2e6 -> e2e8 STA $5115; e2da -> e2dc STA $5116, also a BNE
target) left the mini-inline scan stopped at the first entry-join,
because the grm-k90 licence crosses only ONE join. RegisterEnv gains
entryPathJoins: every join on the call's straight-line fall-through
path from its entry to the helper's last site, excluding any join the
call itself can re-enter (a loop head -- smb3 FUN_ffad's select loop,
which a first cut licensed and rendered select=5 where the loop ends
on 0).

cv3 re-blessed: warnings 61 -> 31, bankComments 144 -> 169,
instrs.inOverlay 19539 -> 19717. Values checked against the ROM bytes.
check nes otherwise clean (dragonpower symbol flap). Residue filed as
grm-dos9.11 and grm-mej.18.

events.message:
toolchain: 16.2.7, GCC on AmigaPorts amiga16.2 1d4ca5d4, no patches

GCC moves to AmigaPorts amiga16.2 1d4ca5d4 ("allow an incoming
single-register SP parameter"), mirrored as tinic/gcc amiga16.2-16.2.7.
It carries AmigaPorts/gcc #82, #83 and #84 merged, so no local patch
remains: the 16.2.6 visibility fix (42ba31a2, fb3ead73) is upstream
with identical patch ids.  binutils, newlib, libnix and the NDK are as
in 16.2.6, and the allocator objects are byte-identical, so the
allocator map is unchanged.

Same commit, default/fat/minimal/micro: all 162 shipped images are
byte-identical to 16.2.6.  No a5/sp, visibility or callconv diagnostic
in any build log.

#84 passes a char or short __asm register argument in its declared
mode, so the caller no longer widens it; callees still extend it.
Under vamos, a garbage-carrying hand-written caller and mixed
16.2.5/16.2.6/16.2.7 callers and callees pass every check.

- build-toolchain.sh: the GCC pin.
- fetch-toolchain.sh, package-toolchain-mirror.sh, setup-amiga cache
  key: asset series 16.2.7 and its two sha256 values.
- Mirror notes and 16.2.7 release notes.

project.notes: Identity: Primary README continues to identify the original Japanese Touhou 4 and its MAIN.EXE, OP.EXE, MAINE.EXE and ZUN.COM reconstructions. Classification: The repository remains a PC-98 source reconstruction with a separate unfinished native x64 port; the new work expands bounded native recovery rather than changing that classification. Source CPU: Maintained source and existing primary documentation continue to establish 16-bit x86 PC-98 executables; the new instruction-vector work does not change the source architecture. Target CPU: The project still produces 16-bit x86 DOS targets and maintains a Linux/Windows x64 native port. No additional architecture is introduced by the reviewed commits. Build: The latest verified snapshot reports 71 GNU CTests, seven optimized UBSan contracts, agreement across 184,908 original-instruction vectors including 514 DIV faults, and eight startup/four-demo routes retaining 129 prior outputs at 15,988 selected-state boundaries. These are bounded upstream receipts, not whole-picture, physical-timing or whole-file byte-exact acceptance. Limitations: No build or replay was run locally; boss/death/process coverage, full pictures, physical timing and Windows input/audio remain open. Next check: Re-attest the combined startup/motion and newer renderer producer, then extend paired coverage to boss combat, death/respawn and complete process transitions. Runtime profiles: The refreshed startup/motion handoff still states no safe minimum physical PC-98 CPU/RAM configuration or minimum x64 host configuration. Measured cadence and instruction-vector counts are verification data, not hardware minima. AI: The reviewed primary commit subjects explicitly identify gpt-6.1-sol; the project records AI use without converting a commit label into a broader authorship percentage. Relationships: ReC98 remains a pinned source-routing and migration input while this repository maintains its own standalone product source and native-port verification history. Evidence: https://github.com/N0zoM1z0/th04/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/N0zoM1z0/th04/commit/5e04432eb943c8155c7525cbe93f6211a5ca7414 https://github.com/N0zoM1z0/th04/commit/637273d4da8c24b1e6b7af4f49e860039d14e738 https://github.com/N0zoM1z0/th04/commit/7c982075eb517870e7658198904d0b8dbc823454

events.message: notes: Reconstructs the original Japanese PC-98 Touhou 4 executables MAIN.EXE, OP.EXE, MAINE.EXE and ZUN.COM from maintained source. The primary handoff reports accepted authored-function counts of OP 93/93, MAIN 493/495, MAINE 72/72 and ZUN 3/3, while explicitly separating function acceptance from whole-file exactness. The repository builds a standalone DOS game and maintains a separate unfinished Linux/Windows x64 port. ReC98 is a pinned source-routing and migration input, but product source no longer includes masters.lib or ReC98 product includes. Current upstream evidence reports original/reconstructed DOS agreement across four bundled demos for consumed input, score, RNG, nine complete actor/effect pools and 22 state blocks. runtime_profiles.notes: Upstream's successful package lane compiles and checks a PRG, exercises SIDScore, starts bundled VICE with visible frames, runs a BASIC POKE through Electron input, and verifies power-off/restart. No minimum Apple Silicon generation, macOS version or RAM is stated.

project.status: active development; macOS Apple Silicon packaged compiler, SIDScore, VICE and Electron path verified upstream
project.notes: Identity: Commodore Commander remains the Eclipse Theia/Electron IDE integrating Kick Assembler, VICE debugging, graphics tools and SIDScore. Classification: The new packaged-product tests strengthen the directly relevant development-environment classification; they do not turn the tool into a reconstructed game or imply equal support for every machine profile. Source CPU: Existing primary documentation still explicitly supports NMOS 6502 disassembly and C64 6510 debugging. The package-test changes do not expand the demonstrated guest instruction-analysis set. Target CPU: The packaged-product documentation explicitly identifies the tested macOS Apple Silicon output. ARM64 records that evidenced host-output architecture; it is not a minimum Apple Silicon generation and does not convert guest 6502/6510 CPUs into host targets. Build: A successful upstream nightly package run now covers all package jobs, while the Apple Silicon path compiles a Kick Assembler program and checks its PRG bytes, exercises SIDScore/SRAP/MIDI, launches bundled VICE and Electron, verifies visible Machine pixels and a BASIC border-color POKE, then powers off and restarts. Compilable and runnable are upstream-verified, not locally reproduced. Limitations: The documented full UI product path currently applies to macOS Apple Silicon; Windows/Linux UI and external VICE remain separate development-test lanes. Signing is ad hoc and notarisation remains manual. Next check: Verify equivalent packaged UI paths on Windows/Linux and retain the distinction between embedded and external VICE coverage. Runtime profiles: The Apple Silicon package is an explicitly exercised runnable variant. No minimum Apple Silicon generation, macOS release or RAM is stated, so the profile records only the verified architecture and path. AI: The reviewed README, packaging change and release-priority documentation contain no explicit development-AI attribution. Agent configuration and automation alone are not proof; usage remains unknown. Relationships: The IDE continues to integrate Theia, VICE, Kick Assembler and independently maintained SIDScore. The reviewed changes bundle and test those dependencies but do not establish a new separately titled project. Evidence: https://github.com/turesheim/commodore-commander/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/turesheim/commodore-commander/commit/f2f645989b5cd5b60133d9404b75d17afa173db8 https://github.com/turesheim/commodore-commander/blob/main/packages/debug-adapter/src/vice-debug-adapter.ts https://github.com/turesheim/commodore-commander/actions/runs/38157335163 https://github.com/turesheim/commodore-commander/actions/runs/38157582224 https://github.com/turesheim/commodore-commander/commit/5b9bf467a0a9117dc392aa764366a1c7fb8af43a https://github.com/turesheim/SIDScore

project.status: active; 1.8.3 development head clarifies unsupported zipped CD media while retaining post-1.8.2 runtime fixes
project.notes: Identity: Geargrafx remains the PC Engine/TurboGrafx-16/SuperGrafx/CD-ROM²/LD-ROM² emulator with integrated debugger and MCP server. Classification: The libretro CD-media validation change is emulator runtime maintenance and preserves the development-tool classification. Source CPU: The in-tree core and debugger continue to identify the emulated HuC6280 architecture; the media-loading change introduces no CPU change. Target CPU: This host-run emulator/debugger has no reconstructed retro output CPU. Published host artifact architectures remain runtime variants, not guest or port targets. Build: The 1.8.3 development head detects a zipped CUE in libretro, rejects the unsupported CD-ROM form with a specific user-facing message, and recommends CHD rather than reporting generic corruption. Earlier post-1.8.2 deterministic, CD-audio and input fixes remain current. No build or media load was reproduced locally. Limitations: The latest published release remains 1.8.2, so the 1.8.3-head diagnostic is not described as released. Runtime profiles: README still publishes x64 and arm64 packages but states no minimum CPU generation or RAM. The new media diagnostic supplies no additional hardware requirement. events.title: Fix JSON tree leak, CTC/speaker write timing and z80_step overflow
events.message:
Fix JSON tree leak, CTC/speaker write timing and z80_step overflow

  - BUGFIX: Debugger - every save of JSON metadata leaked the whole JSON tree: trace recordings
  (each chunk rewrites its metadata), breakpoints, bookmarks, watches, breakpoint variables and the
  Memory Heatmap. The memory use of a long trace recording kept growing with its length.

  - BUGFIX: CTC 8253 and speaker - the time of a write to the CTC (including the CTC0 gate) and of a
  speaker change was taken as if the already executed part of the instruction had passed twice,
  e.g. 14 CPU cycles after the start of LD (HL),A, which takes 7. CTC0 thus started counting a few
  CLK0 periods late and speaker edges were timestamped late by the same amount. The measured load
  behaviour of the CTC on a real MZ-800 is unchanged.

  - BUGFIX: CPU - z80_step() computed the instruction length from the 32-bit cycle counter through
  signed int, which overflows (undefined behaviour in C) when the counter crosses 2^31. Ordinary
  builds returned the right value; the difference is now computed unsigned. New test
  cpu_z80_step_cycles.

  Thanks to Jan Rysavy, whose fork (github.com/janrysavy/mz800emu) pointed out all three problems;
  the leak turned out to be in 11 places, not only in the trace metadata.
events.author: michalhucik

events.title: tests: accept FUSE-T exit after successful unmount
events.message:
tests: accept FUSE-T exit after successful unmount

Allow the SIGPIPE exit observed with FUSE-T on macOS after the unmount
command succeeds. Keep waiting for process exit without forcing it, and
verify persisted file contents and lock release by remounting each
partition while its peer remains usable.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: disk: keep whole-image locks where range locks are unavailable
events.message:
disk: keep whole-image locks where range locks are unavailable

PartitionFileLock only implements byte-range locks on Windows, macOS
and 64-bit Linux. Elsewhere, such as 32-bit Linux and the BSDs, every
RDB session failed with "session-owned partition locks unavailable on
this platform", including single read-only mounts that worked with the
whole-image lock.

Select range locks only where amitools supports them. Other platforms
keep the exclusive whole-image lock, while handler I/O stays bounded to
the selected partition.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: disk: report truncated partitions as truncated images
events.message:
disk: report truncated partitions as truncated images

The partition bounds check rejected a partition that starts past the
end of the image as "Invalid partition bounds or overlap with RDB
metadata". That made the truncated-image diagnostic in HandlerBridge
unreachable and pointed users at the RDB instead of the short file.

Drop the image-size condition: _check_range already rejects I/O past
the image, and MBR containers keep their own size check. Report bad
geometry and overlap with RDB metadata separately, naming the
partition.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: cli: report a busy image as IMAGE_IN_USE
events.message:
cli: report a busy image as IMAGE_IN_USE

A lock conflict with another session surfaced as "Error initializing
handler: cannot exclusively lock disk image ...: [Errno 13] Permission
denied" on Windows, and as HANDLER_ERROR in JSON. The handler never
started and the image is busy, not inaccessible, which users who
mounted by double-click have no terminal to discover.

Classify lock failures on image files in BlockDeviceBackend: EACCES
from msvcrt, EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK from flock and fcntl, and Windows lock
violations from the partition range locks raise ImageInUseError, naming
the image or partition. Failures to open the image itself, such as a
read-only image opened for writing, keep their original error.
Physical disks are left alone: AmiFUSE and vamos sessions already
exclude each other there with a named mutex, so a failure on the
device itself comes from another program, and amitools' message says
so. The CLI reports IMAGE_IN_USE in JSON and a plain "Error:" line in
text mode; mount and format show the same message.

Fixes #86
events.author: reinauer

events.title: docs: describe the amitools-amifuse 0.8.0.post10 floor
events.message:
docs: describe the amitools-amifuse 0.8.0.post10 floor

post10 ships Win32Disk and the partition range locks, so the README and
TESTING notes about the post8 floor and needing a source checkout for
physical disks are stale. The image_access fallback for a missing
amitools.util.Win32Disk can no longer trigger, since driver_runtime
already imports it unconditionally; import it directly instead.

Also document that a session without --partition uses the first
partition, which sessions count as whole-image sessions, and that
platforms without byte-range locks keep whole-image locking.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: disk: allow concurrent mounts of independent partitions
events.message:
disk: allow concurrent mounts of independent partitions

Select the RDB partition under the shared image guard and reserve its
absolute byte range before starting the handler. Include the MBR offset
when locking embedded RDBs and reject metadata or container overlaps.

Bound handler reads and writes to the selected partition and image size
so another session cannot be reached and truncated files cannot grow.
Keep whole-image locking for ADFs, ISOs and physical disks.

Require the amitools release with the shared partition locks.
Cover independent sessions, failed opens, partition bounds and
persistent writes through concurrent PFS3, FFS and SFS handlers and
FUSE mounts.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: mount: report partition lock refusals without a traceback
events.message:
mount: report partition lock refusals without a traceback

With concurrent partition sessions, a refused combination is expected
behaviour, but mount_fuse let the OSError from the partition lock (or a
ValueError for an invalid partition) escape as a Python traceback. The
file commands already printed a one-line error.

Translate both into "Cannot mount <image>: <reason>", keeping the
original exception in debug mode.

events.title: Fix second-start crash (Landscape key), version display, and Exit+reopen on Android
events.message:
Fix second-start crash (Landscape key), version display, and Exit+reopen on Android

- Destroy the viewer when the game view is disposed so a stale viewer no
  longer stays registered in the game manager. On the next start it would
  receive game events and access the disposed render view's layers, throwing
  'The given key Landscape was not present in the dictionary' (sporadic on
  the second start, e.g. after closing via the Exit button).
- Set the version on Freeserf.Core so Global.VERSION shows the app version
  on Android (the entry assembly is missing there, so it fell back to the
  core assembly's default 1.0.0).
- Guard Window_Load against a second OnRun while the first game view is
  still rendering (its Reset() cleared the running view's atlases -> black
  screen).
- Keep a local view reference in OnRun so the old OnRun's Reset/Dispose
  cannot touch the new view after an activity recreation.
- FinishAndRemoveTask + kill the process on Exit so the next start is a
  clean one instead of hitting the activity-recreation race.

events.title: net: keep the device until its asynchronous sends have retired
events.message:
net: keep the device until its asynchronous sends have retired

db_Tx survives close/reopen, but DevExpunge() freed the device base with
sends still outstanding, and the next DevInit() reset the slot state
(inuse = 0, next = 0) and only sampled the completed count. If frames
were still in DMA across an expunge and reload (TX paused by flow
control, say), the new instance copied into the same TX-window slots
while the GEM could still be reading them, and counted the old
completions against its new submissions.

DevExpunge() now drains first: it reclaims from ETH_TX_STATUS until
nothing is outstanding, bounded like the slot wait, and refuses the
expunge (LIBF_DELEXP) if sends are still in flight. The firmware's
stall watchdog retires a stuck send, so a later expunge succeeds.

tx_test covers the drain: still outstanding after the read budget,
then drained once the card retires.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: net: read the RX header serial first only on firmware 2.8+
events.message:
net: read the RX header serial first only on firmware 2.8+

The serial-first header read takes serial 0 for an empty slot. Only
firmware 2.8+ (0x0208) skips serials 0 and 1 on the u16 wrap; 2.1/2.2
and earlier hand serial 0 to the frame after 0xffff. On Zorro II with
that firmware the frame read as empty, the WAIT path never acked it,
and reception stalled at the first serial wrap.

zznet_rx_serial_first() gates the split read on FW_VERSION >= 0x0208.
Older firmware keeps the longword read, size first on Zorro II, and
with it the torn-header race this read was added for.

Host tests: on FW_LEGACY and FW_21 the Zorro II read delivers 0xffff,
0, 1 across the wrap, where serial first delivers one frame and
stalls; on FW_28 it is serial first and crosses the 0xffff -> 2 wrap.

events.title: net: bound the frame_proc drain at priority 10
events.message:
net: bound the frame_proc drain at priority 10

frame_proc only sleeps once the RX backlog is empty. At priority 10, a
flood faster than the 68k drains keeps the backlog full, the loop never
sleeps, and every task below 10 starves, including a stack task that
has to repost CMD_READs.

Count DROP and DELIVER decisions per wakeup. After 64 frames without
sleeping, frame_proc drops to priority 0 for the next 64, where Exec
preempts it for tasks above 0 and time-slices it with priority-0 tasks,
then returns to 10. It is back at 10 whenever it sleeps.

64 is half the 128-slot firmware backlog and more frames than a TCP
receive window keeps in flight, so the TCP receive case measured for
priority 10 never yields; only a sustained flood does.

The budget logic is zznet_rx_drain_reset()/zznet_rx_drain_frame() in
rx.c. Host tests cover a flood that never empties the backlog and a
burst within the budget.

events.title: fix(clonezilla): restore uncompressed and logical-partition images correctly
events.message:
fix(clonezilla): restore uncompressed and logical-partition images correctly

A Clonezilla savedisk of an Ubuntu install (sda1 + extended sda2 holding
sda5/sda6 swap, partclone .uncomp) could neither be inspected nor restored.

- Partclone streams: pick the decompressor by magic (uncompressed, zstd,
  gzip/pigz, bzip2, xz, lz4); only zstd was understood before.
- Restore wrote every partition after the first at the wrong offset:
  patch_hidden_sectors_for leaves the writer at the boot sector, and the
  next gap fill seeks relatively. Re-seek to the absolute position.
- Rebuild the EBR chain and the MBR extended entry. Clonezilla saves only
  the first EBR; the old code also wrote it one sector early.
- Reserve EBR sectors in the layout so logicals keep their original LBAs.
- sfdisk MBR types are bare hex: "type=83" is 0x83, not decimal 83.
- Recreate swap with the UUID/label from swappt-<dev>.info, as Clonezilla
  does, so an fstab swap-by-UUID entry doesn't stall boot.
- Accept a folder that holds exactly one Clonezilla image directory.

Verified: restored image's table matches sda-pt.sf, both ext4 volumes pass
e2fsck -f, swap keeps its UUID, and the disk boots to login in QEMU.

events.title: Βήμα 107: ένα βήμα κέρσορα δίπλα στην αποικία, ένα τέταρτο φθηνότερο
events.message:
Βήμα 107: ένα βήμα κέρσορα δίπλα στην αποικία, ένα τέταρτο φθηνότερο

Το §15 είχε από το βήμα 85 «ένα βήμα κέρσορα κοντά σε κτίσματα κοστίζει
7-15 ms περισσότερα». Μετρημένο τώρα ολόκληρο στο παιχνίδι: ο γύρος του
βρόχου που κουνά τον κέρσορα, το PC ανά 20 us, χωρίς την αναμονή του vsync.
- Θόλος S στο PLACE δίπλα στην αποικία: 43,8 ms δουλειάς. ~17 ήταν ο
  πίνακας: το κόστος των διαδρόμων αλλάζει σχεδόν σε κάθε βήμα, η υπογραφή
  μαζί του, και τα 80 κελιά των σειρών 3-4 ξαναγράφονταν για δύο ψηφία.
  ~13 το φάντασμα.
- Ηλιακός: 23,0 ms. ~9 το φάντασμα, ~7,5 ο έλεγχος του γείτονα (τα Γ).

Τι άλλαξε:
- hud_s34: οι σειρές 3-4 έχουν δική τους κρυφή μνήμη, 80 bytes. Το
  hud_inval τη σβήνει. Το hud_to βρίσκει τη στήλη με το hud_tb, και η
  βοήθεια ζωγραφίζει χωρίς, όπως πριν (hud_sp = 0).
- Ενας δείκτης ανά κελί, όχι δύο: η οθόνη είναι hud_sp + hud_dd. Ενα κελί
  που δεν άλλαξε προχωρά μόνο το hud_sp. Το ζεστό τικ του HUD: 11.981 ->
  9.984 us.
- Οι στήλες του φαντάσματος (ghw_col, gs_col) κάνουν μόνες τους το d += 8,
  με call c,scr_nlw μόνο στην αλλαγή σειράς χαρακτήρων, και djnz.
- gh_rect: χωρίς τα δύο ob_clip όταν το ορθογώνιο είναι όλο μέσα στο clip
  (ghr_in).
- al_emit: τα δύο αποτυπώματα γραμμένα μέσα στις εντολές του (al_rsync στην
  αρχή κάθε Γ). Ενα tile έξω και από τα δύο ~22 us αντί για ~54.
- al_cbk: το tile_addr και το bd_ok μέσα.

Ενα βήμα, δουλειά: θόλος S 43.798 -> 31.666 us, ηλιακός 22.992 -> 19.693.
ui_validate του ηλιακού με μονοπάτι 7.500 -> 6.045. Με το joystick
κρατημένο ένα δευτερόλεπτο, ο θόλος S κάνει 15/21 βήματα (αριστερά/δεξιά)
αντί για 12/19 και ο ηλιακός 19/23 αντί για 17/21.

Δύο χειρότεροι γύροι ανέβηκαν από φάση, όχι από δουλειά: οι γύροι πριν
από το FIRE είναι πιο σύντομοι, και το ρολόι του HUD (ανά 16 γύρους) και
οι θέσεις του τροχού πέφτουν αλλού.
- test_link, M -> M διαγώνιος: 74 -> 96 ms. Το ρολόι του HUD πέφτει πια
  στον γύρο του FIRE, πριν πέντε γύρους μετά. Η δουλειά μετά το FIRE (PC
  ανά 100 us, χωρίς το vsync) 231 -> 204 ms, το τικ του HUD 28,4 -> 17,0.
- test_reveal, ο θόλος L: 104 -> 112 ms. 3,5 ms περισσότερη αναμονή του
  vsync και μια θέση του jb_arrive (1,6 ms) στον γύρο του FIRE. Η σχεδίαση
  ίδια ως 0,5 ms, όλη η τοποθέτηση 762 -> 732 ms δουλειάς.

Μνήμη: 192 bytes της τράπεζας 0 (80 η κρυφή μνήμη), μένουν 287, τα 95 κάτω
από το όριο των δοκιμών. 75 της τράπεζας 2, μένουν 139.

Δοκιμές:
- test_reach, ΣΚΙΑ: στο παιχνίδι, βήματα σε όλες τις κατευθύνσεις ως να
  σκρολάρει η κάμερα, άλμα κάμερας, άλλο αντικείμενο, ESC. Μετά από το
  καθένα οι σειρές 0-4 = η σχεδίασή τους από το μηδέν, με μαύρες λωρίδες,
  κενές κρυφές μνήμες και άκυρη υπογραφή από τη δοκιμή, όχι από το
  hud_inval.
- test_reach, ΒΗΜΑ: ταβάνια 33.000 / 20.800 us. Το ui_validate του ηλιακού
  ως 6.400.
- Πέντε νέα αρνητικά στο test_reach, τέσσερα στο test_ghost. Το πρώτο
  ghr_in σύγκρινε με το κάδρο αντί για το clip, και το μοντέλο του
  test_ghost το έπιασε.
- Το παλιό αρνητικό «όλο το σκέλος ξαναζωγραφίζεται» δεν πιανόταν πια: ο
  πίνακας κοστίζει λιγότερο και στο FIRE, και το airlock έβγαινε 199 ms
  κάτω από το όριο των 200. Η σκηνή του airlock έχει πια δικό της ταβάνι,
  170 (μετρημένο 135, 144 στο βήμα 106).

Το al_rsync καλείται και στο al_s4, αν και οι δύο καλούντες του σήμερα δεν
το χρειάζονται. Το alc_pth έρχεται αμέσως μετά από ένα al_w4 με τα ίδια
αποτυπώματα. Το lk_draw με το al_cbr αγγίζει μόνο ελεύθερο έδαφος, που ένα
αποτύπωμα δεν είναι ποτέ. Είναι άμυνα, 3 bytes, και κανένα αρνητικό δεν
μπορεί να το δείξει.

DESIGN: §9.3 («A cursor step near the colony, at milestone 107»), §9.2, §13
(νέα γραμμή για το test_reach, και του test_ghost), §15, §4.2.

events.title: clock: Accept years past 1999 from the OKI and Ricoh RTCs
events.message:
clock: Accept years past 1999 from the OKI and Ricoh RTCs

The Clock page shows no date on machines whose clock was set by
AmigaOS after 1999.

battclock.resource stores the year as years since 1900, so from 2000
on the 4-bit tens counter holds 10-15. from_bcd() rejected any digit
above 9, so the date could not be read.

Decode the year as battclock does, taking 78-159 as 1978-2059. Keep
treating two-digit years below 78, as other software writes them,
as 2000-2077.

events.title: cli: reject incomplete reads and stage extracted files
events.message:
cli: reject incomplete reads and stage extracted files

Require hash and read to consume the advertised file size before
reporting success. Include expected and actual byte counts on failure.

Stage regular-file output in a private directory beside the destination
and replace it only after the complete read and file close succeed.
Remove staged output on failure, including read-only files on Windows.

Refuse unwritable destinations, retain existing permission bits and
follow output symlinks. Use normal file creation to apply the umask to
new output. Keep stdout and special-file destinations as streams.

Fixes #62
events.author: reinauer

events.title: read: name the output directory when staging fails
events.message:
read: name the output directory when staging fails

Atomic replacement needs to create an entry in the output directory,
which plain open(..., "wb") did not. Errors from creating the staged
file named a temporary .amifuse-* path the user never asked for: an
existing writable output in a directory that denies new entries, a
mistyped --out directory, or a read-only filesystem.

Keep the atomic path, but name the directory instead. A permission
error says the directory is not writable; other errors give their
cause, e.g. "No such file or directory".
events.author: reinauer

events.title: read: stage extracted output beside the destination
events.message:
read: stage extracted output beside the destination

Since Python 3.12.4, TemporaryDirectory creates its directory with an
owner-only DACL on Windows. The staged file inherited it and os.replace
moved it with the file, so `amifuse read --out` produced files that
other local users could not read, even in directories granting them
access.

Stage a plain .amifuse-*.tmp file beside the destination instead. It
is created exactly like the output: with the umask on POSIX and with
the directory's inherited ACL on Windows. Partial data is as private
as the finished output, matching plain open(..., "wb"). Make a staged
file writable again before removing it, so a copied read-only mode
does not block cleanup on Windows.

(macrecomp #6: a relative Move, the title's FONT resources, glyphs in

A match runs to 15 (opponent a5-0xca6, you a5-0xca8) and Ctrl+O (Game >
New Opponent) goes back to the bar (macrecomp #7: MenuKey from the

The loader gains --stroke (a mouse glide in one argument; a match of

events.title: lift32: the x87 compares leave EFLAGS alone
events.message:
lift32: the x87 compares leave EFLAGS alone

fcom, fucom, fcomp, fucomp, fcompp, fucompp and ftst write the x87
condition codes and nothing else, but lift32 also set its flag state from
them, so a jcc after one read the float compare. MSVC schedules integer
tests in front of x87 compares, and Bully's camera update
(0x00509E84: test ecx, ecx; fld; fucom st(1); fnstsw ax; fstp st(1); je)
branched on the floats instead of on ecx and passed a null pointer to its
blend: the first crash after frame 1.

The compares now set only _fpu_cmp, which fnstsw turns into the status
word and sahf or test ah turns into flags, as before. The 'fcom' flag
state and its jcc mapping are gone; nothing else produced it. fcomi and
friends (#79) still write EFLAGS.

difftest: 5 new cases (fucom, the join-point path, fcompp, ftst); all 5
fail without this change, and 314/314 match with it.

events.title: Βήμα 106: ένα βήμα αποίκου έξω, άλλο ένα τρίτο φθηνότερο — και η φλέβα χρεώνεται
events.message:
Βήμα 106: ένα βήμα αποίκου έξω, άλλο ένα τρίτο φθηνότερο — και η φλέβα χρεώνεται

Το §15 έλεγε 4 ms για ένα βήμα έξω και έδειχνε τι έμενε: η φιγούρα στο νέο
κελί, το fg_want, οι σαρώσεις. Ενα προφίλ (το PC ανά us) έδειξε ότι το
μεγαλύτερο μέρος ήταν γενικός κώδικας για ένα κελί που είναι πάντα όλο μέσα
στο κάδρο:
- τα έξι ob_clip του dhv_clip και του ob_fig: ~600 us;
- το παράθυρο του fg_draw, δύο φορές: ~200 us;
- η φιγούρα μέσα από το κόψιμο του ob_fig: ~300 us παραπάνω;
- τα 3x3 της κατοχής μέσα από vr_clip και dh_occ_a: ~370 us;
- ο βρόχος του πολλαπλασιασμού στο fg_want: ~220 us.

Τώρα το σβήσιμο και το ζωγράφισμα ξέρουν ότι κρατούν κελί (src/figure.asm):
- fg_cclip: το clip είναι το κελί, κατευθείαν.
- Τα 3x3 διαβάζονται από τον κόσμο: μία διεύθυνση, +128 η σειρά. Ενα tile
  έξω από το κάδρο μετρά κι αυτό.
- fge_free: σε ελεύθερο έδαφος το tile (fg_tile) και οι φιγούρες, χωρίς τον
  βρόχο των tiles και χωρίς το πέρασμα αντικειμένων. Δίπλα σε κτίσμα, το
  dhv_rect_us μετά το clip (dhv_rect_c).
- fg_cell: οι φιγούρες του κελιού με cpir στη στήλη των ux, κατευθείαν στο
  obfs_lp, με τη σειρά της λίστας, και μία χρέωση για όλα.
- fg_want: ο πολλαπλασιασμός ξεδιπλωμένος, οι πίνακες χωρίς ob_addu. Το
  πληρώνει κάθε περιπατητής έξω σε κάθε βήμα, στο κάδρο ή όχι.
- inc l αντί inc hl στους βρόχους φιγούρας και tile (σελίδα / όριο 64,
  assert).

Ενα βήμα: 3.810 -> 2.294 us σε ελεύθερο έδαφος, 4.244 -> 3.056 δίπλα σε
κτίσμα, 686 -> 586 όταν δεν αλλάζει τίποτα. Οι χρεώσεις κατέβηκαν μαζί:
DK_AGENT 1.200, FG_ERASE_US 1.100, FG_PAINT_US 500, 300 ανά φιγούρα στο
κελί. Ενα βήμα σε ελεύθερο έδαφος χρεώνεται ~3.200 αντί για ~4.300.

Βρέθηκε στον δρόμο: τα μέρη χρεώνονταν λιγότερο από όσο κόστιζαν. Στο βήμα
105, μετρημένο μόνο του σε κάθε κελί, το σβήσιμο σε ελεύθερο έδαφος ήταν
1.564-1.900 us για χρέωση 1.296, σε φλέβα ως 3.360 (το ob_put της φλέβας,
~1.700, δεν το χρέωνε κανείς), δίπλα σε κτίσμα ως 2.208 για 1.696. Το σύνολο
του βήματος το κάλυπτε το περιθώριο του DK_AGENT, γι' αυτό το παλιό ΚΟΣΤΟΣ
περνούσε. Τώρα κάθε μέρος είναι κάτω από τη δική του χρέωση, και η φλέβα
γράφεται κατευθείαν (~280 us) με δική της χρέωση (FG_VEIN_US 300).

Δύο χειρότεροι γύροι άλλαξαν, όχι η δουλειά. test_unlink, ο ηλιακός S1:
89,1 -> 101,8 ms (ταβάνι 150). Οι τρεις πρώτοι γύροι 89/30/71 -> 102/36/53,
και η δουλειά μετά το FIRE (PC ανά 100 us, χωρίς το vsync) 439,1 -> 437,6
ms. Το airlock A1 99,4 -> 96,2, με 30 ms λιγότερη δουλειά στους ίδιους 11
γύρους. test_reveal 119 -> 118.

241 bytes της τράπεζας 2, μένουν 214.

test_figure:
- ΣΤΟΙΒΕΣ: λίστα της δοκιμής (fg_build -> jp ob_touch), δύο φιγούρες στο
  ένα κελί στα τρία. Σβήσιμο πάνω σε σκουπίδια, και κελί χωρίς φιγούρες
  και ζωγράφισμα: κάθε φορά η πλήρης σχεδίαση.
- ΜΕΡΗ: σβήσιμο και ζωγράφισμα μόνα τους σε κάθε κελί δύο καμερών, το
  καθένα κάτω από τη χρέωσή του.
- Ταβάνια στο ΚΟΣΤΟΣ: 2.400 / 3.150 / 620 / 780.
- Εννέα νέα αρνητικά.

DESIGN: §8.5 («The cell's own way, at milestone 106»), §13 (γραμμή για το
test_figure), §15 (το βήμα έξω, η μνήμη, και η γραμμή για το δεύτερο byte
κλείνει: δεν συμβαίνει ποτέ), §4.2.

The RMW reset recogniser read the target byte only when it lay inside the
instruction's own encoding. Every MMC1 PRG window is 16K or 32K and

events.title: native32: hold a guest image's range from process start
events.message:
native32: hold a guest image's range from process start

A 32-bit process places its first thread stack (the /STACK reserve),
heaps and locale files bottom-up before main() runs. With the 16 MB
/STACK the native32 hosts use, the stack alone is 0x00400000-0x01400000,
which is where a guest exe is based. The loader's fallback then commits
the image into the stack's own reservation: KotOR's 4.4 MB image sits
under its main thread's stack today, and Bully's 29 MB one runs past the
stack's top and cannot be mapped at all.

native32_hold_image(path, base) starts the host again suspended,
reserves [base, base + SizeOfImage) in it before its loader runs, and
waits for it in a kill-on-close job; the child maps into the reservation
(the loader already commits into one). A host links a small /STACK and
runs the lifted code on a thread with a large one.

events.title: Βήμα 105: ένα βήμα αποίκου έξω, ένα πέμπτο φθηνότερο — και η φλέβα μένει
events.message:
Βήμα 105: ένα βήμα αποίκου έξω, ένα πέμπτο φθηνότερο — και η φλέβα μένει

Το §15 είχε από το βήμα 89 την τιμή ενός βήματος έξω: ~5 ms, και είκοσι
περιπατητές στο κάδρο ένα τρίτο της μηχανής. Ο φθηνότερος δρόμος περίμενε
bytes, και το βήμα 103 τα έδωσε.

Το σβήσιμο του παλιού κελιού έστρωνε το έδαφος με το γενικό ob_put: όλο το
tile, κομμένο στο 2x8, ~1 ms για 16 bytes. Τώρα για το σβήσιμο το call του
ob_put στο dhv_rect_us γράφεται για λίγο στο fg_tile (fge_go), που γράφει τα
16 bytes κατευθείαν:
- το κελί είναι όλο μέσα στο κάδρο, άρα το clip είναι το κελί·
- αρχίζει σε σειρά χαρακτήρων, άρα κάθε γραμμή είναι +#800·
- η διεύθυνσή του είναι ζυγή (cam_p πολλαπλάσιο του 4), άρα τα δύο bytes
  δεν χωρίζονται ποτέ σε δύο σελίδες·
- μέσα στο tile είναι ένα τέταρτο του, +32 / +2.
Το άδειασμα θέσης και η μηχανή που βγαίνει δεν πληρώνουν τίποτα.

Ενα βήμα: 4.836 -> 3.810 us σε ελεύθερο έδαφος, 5.270 -> 4.244 δίπλα σε
κτίσμα. Οι χρεώσεις κατέβηκαν κατά το ίδιο 1.000 (FG_ERASE_US 1.200,
FG_ERASE_NEAR 1.600), άρα η λίστα αλλαγών χωρά περισσότερα βήματα σε κάθε
καρέ. 86 bytes της τράπεζας 2, μένουν 455.

Βρέθηκε στον δρόμο: η φλέβα χανόταν κάτω από όποιον περπατούσε. Το
tile_one ζωγραφίζει το βουνό με το bit πόρου και τη φλέβα από πάνω, αλλά το
σβήσιμο ζωγράφιζε μόνο το tile. Στο seed της δοκιμής 18 από τα 36 κελιά
εννέα φλεβών έχαναν pixels. Το fg_tile βάζει τη φλέβα με τη μάσκα της.

test_figure, ΚΕΛΙ: 457 κελιά σε οκτώ κάμερες (ελεύθερο έδαφος, δίπλα και
πάνω σε κτίσμα, φλέβες), σκουπίδια και σβήσιμο: κάθε φορά η πλήρης
σχεδίαση. Μετά ένα άδειασμα θέσης εκτός σειράς χαρακτήρων. Τέσσερα
αρνητικά: πάντα το πάνω αριστερό τέταρτο, χωρίς τη φλέβα, το call που δεν
ξαναγράφεται, χωρίς το fg_tile (το ΚΟΣΤΟΣ).

DESIGN: §8.5 («A cheaper erase, at milestone 105»), §13 (γραμμή για το
test_figure), §15, §4.2.

σε εργοτάξιο. Από το βήμα 38 το mt_hit σταματά μία μηχανή του, και η γραμμή
έκανε λάθος από το βήμα 90.

Η άλλη ήταν αληθινή. Οποιος ταξίδευε στον σωλήνα από θόλο προς ένα airlock
τη στιγμή που ο μετεωρίτης το έκανε εργοτάξιο έφτανε εκεί με το F_INDOORS,
και ανέπνεε τον αέρα της αποικίας. Τώρα το lk_air_out τον βγάζει έξω τη
στιγμή της κρούσης, με γεμάτη στολή, και φαίνεται στο έδαφος. Ενα δεύτερο
πέρασμα των 128 βρίσκει όσους η ακμή τους καταλήγει στο airlock
(node_adj[node * 8 + edge]). Η άφιξη, που τρέχει σε κάθε βήμα του τροχού, δεν
άλλαξε.

Το lk_each βρίσκει τον κόμβο με cpir και προσπερνά νεκρούς και άδειες θέσεις
χωρίς push/pop: 1.194 -> 811 us για κόμβο χωρίς κανέναν, 6.154 -> 3.163 για
τον θόλο 0. Μια κρούση σε έτοιμο airlock κοστίζει 6.952 us αντί για 6.025.
Δεν είχε μετρηθεί ποτέ: το test_impact δεν χτυπά ποτέ έτοιμο airlock. Τώρα
έχει ταβάνι 7.100 στο test_suit. Ο κώδικας είναι 57 bytes στην τράπεζα 2 και
μένουν 541. Το σώσιμο δεν άλλαξε (SV_VER 8).

test_suit:
- ΣΩΛΗΝΑΣ: στο παιχνίδι, με αληθινή βροχή στοχευμένη στο airlock, ένας στον
  σωλήνα προς κάθε μεριά.
- ΤΥΧΑΙΑ: 400 κλήσεις του lk_air_out = η αναφορά (tools/entity.py, air_out,
  που παίρνει πια και τον γράφο).
- ΚΟΣΤΟΣ.
- Τέσσερα αρνητικά.

Το αρνητικό «lk_out μόνο για τον χτίστη» του test_supply ψάχνει πια το
ld bc,N_AGENT του νέου lk_each.

events.title: Fix Android bugs: game speed, audio re-init, pause sound loop, loading screen, focus ring
events.message:
Fix Android bugs: game speed, audio re-init, pause sound loop, loading screen, focus ring

- Cap the Android game loop at 50 FPS (the game's design rate). The game
  update runs inside the render loop and the swap did not block on vsync,
  so the game ran much too fast on Android.
- Reset BASS state in FreeBass() (Initialized, soundFont, soundFontProcs) so
  a later EnsureBass() performs a clean re-initialization after the app was
  closed; start the BASS output device after init.
- Do not play sounds while the game is paused: the tick counter is frozen and
  some sound triggers restarted the same sound every frame (fast loop).
- Reset all static state in OnCreate when the activity is recreated (EGL
  context loss) and show an error dialog instead of an endless loading screen
  when initialization fails.
- Disable the system focus ring on the native data import dialog buttons.

events.message:
grm-dos9.9: explicit mode sets outvote shifter resets in the prg_mode lock

Owner ruling: a game runs in one layout mode because its ROM organization
depends on it, so an explicit mode write trumps the mode a hardware reset
forces as a side effect. SwitchOutcome gains an implicit flag, set by the
MMC1 reset forms; a helper call is implicit when every site of its helper
is. The lock census and its verification drop implicit writes whenever an
explicit one exists. The analyzer log names the outvoted resets.

rcproam now locks prg_mode 0 (resets ff85/ffea outvoted); re-blessed with
one new "assumed to stay 0" note at the f8ce tail call. Its initial_state
hint stays: it fixes the load-time base layout, which the lock cannot.

Gates: build-and-test.sh check SUITE OK; realrom-test.sh check nes 32 pass
+ rcproam (intended, blessed) + the known dragonpower 152 symbol flap.

window is 3+5 dots wider than the picture: EDGEL/EDGER), stored in a 4.0 block
after the prefs credits; key-script 'option mask 1'. Off by default; off is
pixel-identical to before.

events.message:
Βήμα 103: μνήμη — 247 bytes στην τράπεζα 0, 597 στην τράπεζα 2

Ενα βήμα μόνο για μνήμη, χωρίς καμία αλλαγή συμπεριφοράς.

Τράπεζα 0: μπήκαν τα μπαλώματα που είχαν μείνει στην άκρη από το βήμα 101
(και τα δύο επίπεδα), με τις αλλαγές τριών βημάτων ενωμένες με το χέρι. Ο
κώδικας τελειώνει στο #3CE1 αντί για #3DD8: 479 bytes ως τη σκαλωσιά των
δοκιμών (ήταν 232). Τα πλήκτρα διαβάζονται από τα bits του act_hit, και τα
in_hit/in_held μένουν μόνο στις δοκιμές· το rt_node μπήκε μέσα στο rt_slice·
το is_init μέσα στο start· κοινές ουρές, πίνακες σε μία σελίδα, σημαίες
αντί για συγκρίσεις.

Τράπεζα 2: το save.asm και το fdc.asm (633 bytes) είναι δεύτερο κομμάτι
στις τρύπες του DIST, μετά την κατεδάφιση. Τρέχουν από το GH_BUF + 512,
μετά την κεφαλίδα του σωσίματος, και τα φέρνουν σε κάθε S και L τα sv_save
και sv_load, που μένουν στην τράπεζα 2. Το φόρτωμα δείχνει τον κέρσορα αφού
γυρίσει ο κώδικας. Ο κώδικας της τράπεζας 2 έχει 598 ελεύθερα (ήταν 1). Το
OV_LOAD κατέβηκε στο #6800 για να χωρέσουν και οι δύο εικόνες.

Κόστος: τίποτα που τρέχει σε κάθε frame δεν έγινε πιο αργό. Η περιστροφή
του τροχού είναι 28.954 us όπως πριν. Το HUD κάθε τικ πήγε 12.979 -> 11.981
us, το routing 2,84 -> 2,64 s στα 128 κόμβους, και το x2 τρέχει πια 2,00x.
Πιο αργά, μόνο στο πάτημα ενός πλήκτρου: η μπάρα +40 us και η βοήθεια +180.

Δοκιμές: το test_save σώζει με rst 0 σε όλη τη θέση του κώδικα, και ένα
τελευταίο αρνητικό, χωρίς την αντιγραφή, δεν σώζει. Το test_disc διαβάζει
και τα δύο κομμάτια από τις τρύπες μετά από εκκίνηση από τον δίσκο. Το look
του test_unlink κρατά και τις οκτώ τράπεζες, γιατί η πλήρης σχεδίαση
ξαναγράφει και τα αρχεία του renderer. Η σουίτα: 70/70.

events.title: install/test: fat installer scenarios; exact 060 wording
events.message:
install/test: fat installer scenarios; exact 060 wording

The previous commit said nothing traps on a 68060.  The exact statement:
at -m68020-60 the compiler emits no 060-unimplemented instruction; the
hand-written 64-bit MULU.L/DIVU.L in crypto68k and ami_udivdi3.c remains
and is selected at run time only on a non-060, as in full.  The
toolchain comment and docs/RESEARCH.md 88 now say that.

run-workbench.sh gains the scenarios the fat default needs:

  -P fail|broken   InstallNetProbe exits RETURN_FAIL, or is not a
                   program; the default must stay the full stack
  -x fat-full      fat installed, then a reinstall choosing full
  -x full-fat      the reverse
  -p fat on an A600  fat is refused on a 68000, the stack page is asked
                   again, and full is picked there (config-only)

Whenever fat is involved, every installed library and C: command (with
the SYS:Prefs/NetPrefs and SYS:Utilities/NetMeter copies) must be the
selected drawer's by sha256; drivers were already compared against
Devs/Networks or Devs/Networks/fat.  run-all.sh carries the five as
FAT_68000, FAT_FULL, FULL_FAT, PROBE_FAIL and PROBE_BROKEN.

events.title: lift16: a divide faults on overflow too, with cs:ip at the divide
events.message:
lift16: a divide faults on overflow too, with cs:ip at the divide

x86 raises INT 0 for a zero divisor and also when the quotient does not
fit its destination. lift16 checked only for zero: an overflowing
quotient was truncated in C, and idiv of INT64_MIN by -1 killed the host
process outright.

It also called DIV0_FN with nothing that said where the fault was. A
game that installs its own INT 0 handler reads the faulting instruction
through the return address the CPU pushed -- Microsoft Space Simulator's
looks for a 66h prefix to choose between 16 and 32 bits, saturates the
quotient and steps over the instruction. Before the call, cpu->cs:ip is
now set to the divide, so a runtime can push that frame.

test_lift16_div.py lifts div/idiv at 8, 16 and 32 bits and checks 36
cases (ordinary, zero divisor, overflow) against Python's reference,
including that every fault reports cs:ip. Needs a C compiler only.

events.title: lift16: a push-call can jump with retf to a target it pushed
events.message:
lift16: a push-call can jump with retf to a target it pushed

The same hand-built call, for a target only known at run time:

    push cs / push label / push 0 / push seg / push off / retf

The retf pops the target, the routine's near ret pops the 0 into the
segment's lone retf, and that returns to label. Treated as a return, the
code after the label never ran -- Microsoft Space Simulator's SMDL
interpreter calls a model's code this way and restores its own state
after the label, so without it the interpreter carried on with the
callee's FS:SI and a stack two bytes short.

push_calls may now name a retf: the lifter pops the target and dispatches
to it, and the frame cleanup and the goto to the label are as before.

events.title: lift16: return when a callee unwinds the guest stack past this frame (opt-in)
events.message:
lift16: return when a callee unwinds the guest stack past this frame (opt-in)

Hand-written assembly often leaves deep nesting by resetting SP: save it
on the way in (mov [saved], sp) and, from anywhere below, mov sp, [saved]
followed by ret. On the CPU that single ret leaves every frame in
between. Lifted, every guest frame is a C frame, and the ret leaves only
the innermost; the callers resume with a guest stack that no longer
holds what they pushed, read garbage return values and locals, and in
time jump somewhere absurd.

With Lifter.unwind_sp set, each lifted function notes SP and SS at entry
(SP then points at its own return address) and checks after every call:
if SP is above that on the same stack, its frame has been unwound, and
it returns at once, which repeats up the C stack to the frame the guest
actually returned to. A call that balances the stack never trips it.

Microsoft Space Simulator's SMDL model interpreter saves SP at entry and
its opcode handlers abort with mov sp,[7E60] / ret; without this the game
stopped with its own "Bad SMDL Opcode" error and dispatched to 0800:0800.

Default off: one compare per call site, and nothing changes without it.

Fixes found running the Finland stage on a 64-bit build of OpenCMR2:
- SceneNode names cameraDistance (0x16c), the transparent draw sort key;
  Game_CompareTransparentDrawEntries reads SceneNode fields (stays exact).
  pParent, dirty and pObject reads go through the fields (car wheel textures,
  challenge scene, node value thresholds).
- Car::pSceneRoot / pBodyNode instead of Car + 0x71c / 0x720.
- StageTiming_GetStartTableField244 returns FixAngles *; CarDamage_
  RebuildPartBounds and CarDamage_BuildPartVertexBuffer take SceneNode * and
  CarPartSet *.
- Race_ResolveStageTexturesAndPalettes keeps the 48 time-of-day records as
  BYTE * and reads colour[k] (it read a dword at colour + 5; still exact).
- The race render callbacks (RallyData_GrowEntry*, ShrinkEntry*,
  UpdateUnavailableEntryText, DrawViewEndFrameOverlay,
  NotifyAdjacentMenuKeyValue, UpdateViewFrameAndDebugOverlay,
  InRaceMenu_AdvanceScreenEntries) take the CallbackStateMachine * and read
  count / records[].bits.state.
- The engine sound archives are GenericFile[2] (walked 12 bytes apart).
- Mesh readers: Graphics_SetRecordField2C takes Mesh *, the ground reference
  mesh is a Mesh *, body light textures read pTriangles->textureIndex.
- Draw queues are sorted with sizeof(element), not 4.
- The four wheel-slot thresholds 0x590c44..0x590c53 are one int[4] (the code
  reads them as an array); the slot loop scales its pointer-table offset by
  sizeof(PartState *) / sizeof(int), 1 on Win32. StageObject_
  RebuildCarLightMeshes' biased vertex walk is scaled the same way.

FrontendText_LoadRegionLanguages goes back to 81.76%: it had become exact in
b21ecaa only through a register tie that any new member or type visible in
GameInfo.cpp flips (SceneNode::cameraDistance here). Differential suite: 129
harnesses pass; data comparison clean.

events.title: 64-bit: stage mesh records typed (Mesh LOD fields, Sector as 0x88 bytes), option archives read as GenericFile (2925 exact preserved)
events.message:
64-bit: stage mesh records typed (Mesh LOD fields, Sector as 0x88 bytes), option archives read as GenericFile (2925 exact preserved)

The stage mesh file holds scene nodes, meshes, stage objects, sectors and
collision records that the loader relocates in place; a 64-bit build has to
copy them to native structures, which needs every access to go through the
fields:
- Mesh names its tail: field_0x108 (shadow colour bytes), lodIndex (0x112),
  lodCount (0x113, 1 in every stage file), field_0x114. Mesh_Clone, the
  scene shadow meshes, Sector_FreeMeshPartLists and the LOD uploads use the
  fields instead of byte offsets; the shadow tail clear runs from
  offsetof(Mesh, pCollisionRecords) to sizeof(Mesh) (0x10c..0x120 on Win32).
- Sector::pMesh is a Mesh *: SectorModel was a second view of the same
  record whose lodIndex sits elsewhere once pointers grow. Sector gains its
  last 0xc bytes, so sizeof(Sector) is the 0x88 of the file record, and is
  documented as ON-DISK.
- The scene lighting pass reads Sector::pObjects by name.
- Graphics_LoadTextureRecordList takes its record list and name table as
  pointers, not ints.
- OptionMenu_ReleaseTextures read the archive buffers as ints (truncating
  them on 64-bit); it reads them through GenericFile *. Declaring the three
  archives as GenericFile flips two tie-sensitive functions of GameInfo.cpp,
  so they stay int[4] (commented).

Differential suite: 129 harnesses pass.

events.title: lift16: bt/bts/btr/btc with a register offset into memory address a bit string
events.message:
lift16: bt/bts/btr/btc with a register offset into memory address a bit string

With a memory destination and a register bit offset, the offset is
signed and is not reduced modulo the operand width: `bt word [x], ax`
with ax = 37 tests bit 5 of the word at x+4. lift16 masked the offset
to the word and tested the word at x, so every bit past the first
operand read the wrong one. Immediate offsets are reduced, and keep the
old path.

Microsoft Space Simulator keeps its key-down map as a bit string and
tests it with bt [map], ax. difftest16 over its main code segment:

    before  bt word ds:[0x8418], ax   CF=0 want 1  (and two fs: forms)
    after   3 distinct testable instructions, 24 pairs: all agree

events.title: lift16: rcl and rcr on a dword keep the carry bit
events.message:
lift16: rcl and rcr on a dword keep the carry bit

Rotate-through-carry works on the operand and CF together: w+1 bits.
lift16 built that in a uint32_t, which is right for bytes and words and
wrong for dwords -- the carry, bit 32, fell off the top, and the 33-bit
mask overflowed. `rcr eax, 1` came out as garbage.

Microsoft Space Simulator's software floating point shifts 64-bit
mantissas right with `shr edx,1 / rcr eax,1`; with the bad rotate its
Kepler solver never converged and the game hung at its logo.

The working value is now uint64_t for every width. difftest16 over the
game's maths segment, before and after:

    before  12 instructions disagree (rcr eax/ebx/edx, 1 among them)
    after    3 instructions disagree, none of them rotates:
             two reads of CS (a per-function constant by design) and a
             32-bit address past 64 KB, which real mode would fault on

difftest16 also stops comparing OF after shld/shrd, which the manual
defines only for a count of 1, as it already did for the other shifts.

events.title: lift32: loope/loopne test ZF, not CF
events.message:
lift32: loope/loopne test ZF, not CF

Both were lifted as `--ecx != 0 && _cf == 0`. loope continues while ZF is
set and loopne while it is clear; neither reads the carry. The condition
now comes from _make_condition('je'/'jne'), the same flag-setter-aware
expression a jcc gets, and is evaluated before ecx counts down, since a
setter's captured operands can name ecx.

Found on Streets of SimCity: its texture-span loop ends `inc edi; loopne`.
ZF is never set there, so the loop is a plain count, but the lift tested
the carry an earlier `shr` left, ended spans early, and the next span was
drawn through a corrupt destination (a write fault at 0x004B7CBE, the
first frame of a mission). tools/lift/test_loopcc.py checks the lifted
line for both forms and for a plain loop.

events.title: toolchain: 16.2.6 notes, the narrow __asm argument ABI
events.message:
toolchain: 16.2.6 notes, the narrow __asm argument ABI

16.2.6 widens a char or short argument bound to a register with __asm
at the caller; 16.2.5 (bebbo 41bef684) did not.  The callee side is
unchanged: both compilers still extend the value themselves (andi.l
#255, ext.l), so mixed objects need no rebuild.  Measured under vamos
with 16.2.5 and 16.2.6 callers and callees and a hand-written caller
that leaves garbage above the byte or word: 120 checks per binary, at
-Os/-O2, -m68000/-m68020, with and without -mregparm=3, zero failures.
A non-extending control callee is caught.

The only narrow register parameters in the tree that ship are four
RawDoFmt character callbacks (loghook.c, ami_diag.c, crashguard.c and
the debug-only tls_resume.c); each tests and stores d0 as a byte.

events.title: revm lock step bug fix in cpumock for late IRQ accepts
events.message:
revm lock step bug fix in cpumock for late IRQ accepts

In enter_interrupt's late-edge branch (skew < 0: Main's pending rose after
Twin's accept boundary), Twin was stepped a full -skew Phi2 "to bring it
level". The count is measured from the boundary and ignores that
twin_resolve_accept_kind had already advanced Twin into the accept
sequence (state 0x0d, ~2 Phi2 short of the vector-target opcode fetch).
With skew = -8, Twin was carried through the fetch into the handler body,
so the thunk's entry JoinAtPc(vector) could never meet it and failed with
"Twin left this IRQ/NMI nest" (Paradroid original2 frame 1363, the only
late accept in four plays).

The leveling loop now stops as soon as Twin leaves the IRQ/NMI accept
sequence, parking it at the fetch exactly where every skew >= 0 accept
leaves it; the handler-entry join's align_after_arrival closes any
residue. Main never takes values from Twin; no compare is relaxed.

Verified: Paradroid original2 bound 1362 -> 1395; original1/3/4 bounds,
frontiers and no-twin smokes byte-identical. FranticFreddie (FranticOrg)
stage3 original1-3 + no-twin1 and all eight stage4 gates (incl.
--main-blank) give identical logs before/after. ./rework selftest passes.

events.title: decode16/lift16: bsf and bsr
events.message:
decode16/lift16: bsf and bsr

0F BC / 0F BD decoded as 'db 0xF', so a walk stopped at the first bit
scan and everything after it became a run-time dispatch miss. Microsoft
Space Simulator normalises its fixed-point values with bsr (23 sites, in
all three code segments), and with the walk cut short there its maths
routines ended in jumps to unlifted code -- each one another nested C
frame, until the host stack overflowed.

decode16 decodes both, 16- and 32-bit. lift16 scans for the lowest or
highest set bit; a zero source sets ZF and leaves the destination alone,
which is what every 386 and later does (the manual says undefined). The
other flags are undefined and are left as they were.

difftest16 now treats CF, OF, SF, AF and PF as undefined after a bit
scan, as the manual does, and compares ZF and the destination:

    7 distinct testable instructions

events.title: drm: unpack Microsoft EXEPACK DOS executables
events.message:
drm: unpack Microsoft EXEPACK DOS executables

LINK /EXEPACK run-length encodes the load module and puts a small
unpacker segment at the entry point, so the disassembler sees only the
unpacker. pcrecomp had LZEXE (unlzexe.py) but nothing for EXEPACK, which
turns up wherever a DOS program went through Microsoft's linker.

unexepack.py decodes the format directly, nothing is run: the header at
the unpacker's CS:0000 (both the 16-byte and the later 18-byte layout
with skip_len), the fill/copy command stream read backwards from the end
of the module, and the relocation table that follows the unpacker's
"Packed file is corrupt" message. The output is a plain MZ with the
original entry, stack and relocations.

test_unexepack.py builds a packed file with its own encoder (runs,
literals, an uncompressed prefix, 0xFF padding, relocations in two
frames) and checks both header layouts, so it needs no game files.

events.title: lift16: a jmp after push cs / push label is a call that returns to label
events.message:
lift16: a jmp after push cs / push label is a call that returns to label

Hand-written real-mode assembly that calls a near routine in another
segment cannot use a near call, so it builds the frame itself:

    push cs / push label / push 0 / jmp far seg:routine

The routine's near ret pops the 0 and lands on seg:0000, a lone retf,
which pops label:cs. Without the 0 it is a far call to a routine that
ends in retf; with a near jmp and no push cs, a near call.

lift16 had no way to see these as calls: the jmp was a tail jump, the
function ended there, and the label was only ever reached as a runtime
dispatch of the pushed return address -- from inside the callee's retf,
nesting another C frame per call.

A driver now names each such jmp in Lifter.push_calls ({jmp address:
(label, address of the push of the label, bytes pushed after it)}). The
label push becomes the 0xFFFF sentinel every lifted call pushes, the jmp
becomes a C call, and whatever of the hand-built frame the callee left
(the label and CS, when its ret stopped at the trampoline) is popped as
the trampoline's retf would, before a goto to the label.

Default off: with push_calls empty nothing changes.

half (MULU.W addmul, the dispatched MULU.L ones) instead of forcing the

its 060-safe paths.  n68k_iocopy.S keeps its movem copy unless the
build is 68060-only.  The 68020+ checks for sibling calls and for

events.title: Restore the storage last, and check card size and writability first
events.message:
Restore the storage last, and check card size and writability first

From the third review of PR #225 (Greptile, CodeRabbit). A restore
replaced the flash and the PC Card contents before the rest of the file
was checked, so a restore that failed later had already overwritten
the user's storage:

- The flash and the card contents now come last in the file (version
  13), after everything else was loaded and checked. The card images
  come before the flash, because only writing them can fail.
- The size of each card's contents is part of the identity, so a card
  of the same kind but another size is refused before anything changes.
  A read-only ATA image is refused up front if its contents would change.
- ATA cards write the image first and copy the contents into memory
  only then; a write error fails the load. Unchanged contents are not
  written again (linear cards too).
- The note that a card will be replaced is printed only when the file
  is actually loaded.

Tested with a 2 MB linear card: a wrong card size is refused before
loading; a file that fails late leaves card, image and flash as they
were and resets; a valid restore replaces the card byte in memory and
image; round trip identical; fast start works.

events.title: win32hle: MFC/GDI surface for SimCity 2000 bring-up on Linux
events.message:
win32hle: MFC/GDI surface for SimCity 2000 bring-up on Linux

Driven by the permissive loop against a lifted SIMCITY.EXE (Win95, MFC MDI +
GDI). It now runs its CRT, MFC AfxWinInit, window-class registration, the
install-registration check, the 256-colour video warning (it takes its
truecolour path since the host reports 32bpp), and into data/palette loading.

user32: the WH_CBT hook (SetWindowsHookExA / CallNextHookEx /
UnhookWindowsHookEx), fired with HCBT_CREATEWND before WM_NCCREATE so MFC
subclasses each window as it is created (how CWnd attaches to an HWND); plus
RegisterWindowMessageA and SetMessageQueue.

module: an EXE's own resources are now found. The main image is registered
before it is mapped (hle_set_module_path runs first), so its resource directory

iso_peek: read the Joliet tree when the disc has one

The walker read only the primary ISO9660 tree, whose names are 8.3 and
upper case. A disc mastered with Joliet keeps its real names only in the
supplementary tree, so a game that opens selectCar.bmp or BMP\steer\comp+30.bmp
found SELECT~1.BMP and nothing at all for names ISO9660 cannot spell
(36 of Streets of SimCity's 978 game files).

walk() now looks through the volume descriptors after the primary one for a
Joliet SVD (type 2, UCS-2 escape %/@, %/C or %/E) and walks its root
instead, decoding names as UTF-16BE. Discs without one are read as before.

events.title: lift32: packed integer SSE2 on xmm, and no xmm form lifted as MMX
events.message:
lift32: packed integer SSE2 on xmm, and no xmm form lifted as MMX

lift_sse returned None for an xmm instruction it did not know, and lift32
then tried its MMX forms, which share the mnemonics. psrlq, psllq and
pcmpeqd with an xmm operand lifted as `mmx_psrlq(0 /* unknown reg */)`: a
wrong value, and not counted as UNIMPLEMENTED, so a lift reported nothing.

A static VC++ 2005 CRT carries the SSE2 math library (pow, exp, log, sin,
cos and friends), which it selects whenever CPUID reports SSE2. Those
routines use the lane shifts, pextrw/pinsrw, pmovmskb and cvtdq2pd.

- The lane shifts psrl/psll/psra w/d/q, with an immediate, xmm or memory
  count; a count at or past the lane width saturates as the CPU does.
- pcmpeq/pcmpgt b/w/d, pmaxsw/pminsw, pextrw, pinsrw (register or m16),
  pmovmskb, cvtdq2pd.
- Any other instruction with an xmm operand lifts as a counted
  UNIMPLEMENTED line and never reaches the MMX code.
- difftest: 50 new cases (25 forms on float and integer data, saturating
  counts included). 49 of them fail without this change; 359/359 match
  Unicorn with it.

events.title: grm-dos9.7: MMC1 rows form the prg_mode lock; say why when none forms
events.message:
grm-dos9.7: MMC1 rows form the prg_mode lock; say why when none forms

The phase-A census counted every direct site whose mechanism owns the
layout-mode field. On MMC1 that is every link of a shift chain: writes 1-4
deposit nothing (NO_DEPOSIT echoes), and inside a control-register helper
the chain's first write and its commit are HELPER_ARGUMENT -- the caller's
value, already judged once per call site. Each read as an unresolved mode
write, so no MMC1 row ever locked. Both kinds are now skipped.

The census also reports WHY no lock formed (no writes / unresolved sites
with their stop reason / disagreement / partial coverage), logged next to
the existing "locked to" line.

Locks now form on blmaster, kicarus and zelda (prg_mode 3). blmaster's
fixed_after_init: [prg_mode] hint is removed: its golden is byte-identical
without it. zelda re-blessed (instrs.inOverlay 11428 -> 12958, refs
2567 -> 2889). drmario/rcproam genuinely disagree (shifter reset 3, then
control writes 0) and keep their hints -> grm-dos9.9.

Gates: build-and-test check green; check nes 32 pass + zelda (blessed)
+ dragonpower 152 (known symbol flap).

events.title: grm-dos9.3: bank comments show the layout-mode field when it is known
events.message:
grm-dos9.3: bank comments show the layout-mode field when it is known

A bank comment echoed only its own mechanism's bits, so on MMC5 (where $5100
and $5116 are separate mechanisms) cv3's e03d rendered prg_mode 'assumed from
initial' although the dataflow knew it was 2. The layout-mode field decides
which window a bank feeds, so it is now always echoed: helper calls widen the
echo window to the mode field; direct switches add the in-state's known mode
via BankAnnotationAdapter.withLayoutMode. Both only alongside knowledge the
site itself has, so an undeterminable write keeps its WARNING.

Wording-only re-bless: cv3, rtk2, nesmodetest, nesmmc5test, nesmmc5wraptest.
nesmodetest F4:c002/8042 criteria updated; the old 8042 comment said
'prg_mode=0?' inside the mode-1 overlay, which was wrong. No count moved.
New JUnit LayoutModeEchoTest.

events.title: SNES boot ROM: echo each byte sooner (33 SPC700 cycles a byte, was 42)
events.message:
SNES boot ROM: echo each byte sooner (33 SPC700 cycles a byte, was 42)

The upload loop keeps the new port 0 value as the last echo as soon as it
sees a change, then echoes the index before storing the byte, so the S-CPU
can send the next byte while the boot ROM stores this one. An 8 KB upload
from a tight S-CPU loop takes 16 frames instead of 19 (Nintendo's boot ROM,
measured the same way from outside: 12). Same size, same handover state.
snes9x and bsnes rebuilt; the unit test values read from snes9x are re-read
from the rebuilt core (the same procedure reproduces the previous values on
the previous core); binary manifest updated.

events.message:
Βήμα 101: η κατεδάφιση

Ο παίκτης γκρεμίζει θόλους και δομές, τελειωμένα ή εργοτάξια, ποτέ το
σκάφος: M, D (DEMOLISH), FIRE. Οι διάδρομοι ενός θόλου φεύγουν μαζί του.
Πίσω τα μισά υλικά (του κτιρίου, των διαδρόμων, των μηχανών), όλα από
εργοτάξιο. Οσοι είναι μέσα πάνε στο κοντινότερο airlock ή στο σκάφος με
γεμάτη στολή· οι εργασίες του κόμβου σβήνουν. Κόκκινο στο σκάφος, στο κενό,
και στην πίστα ή σε αποθήκη όσο έρχεται ή κάθεται πλοίο.

- Ο κώδικας (891 bytes) ζει στις στήλες 96-127 του DIST, που δεν τις διαβάζει
  κανείς (το rt_flush γράφει πια 96), και τρέχει από το GH_BUF με το φάντασμα
  κρυμμένο (ov_install, ov_run). Η σειρά 0 είναι δύο χειριστές της λίστας
  αλλαγών που τρέχουν επί τόπου.
- Η κατοχή του κόσμου ξαναγράφεται σε ορθογώνια (το αποτύπωμα και κάθε

  έδωσε τους πέντε χαρακτήρες μετά το z για το σύμβολο και τα κείμενα.

Build scripts: keep build-machine paths out of shipped toolchain binaries

Every recipe whose output shipped a builder path now produces a path-free
artifact by construction, instead of the path being edited out afterwards.

- gcc/binutils WASM tools (arm, m68k, mips-elf, sh-elf): one
  -ffile-prefix-map for the whole build tree (sources, build dirs and the
  gmp/mpfr/mpc/isl deps), --prefix=/romdev for the baked default search
  dirs, and the builder path rewritten out of gcc/configargs.h.
- mips-linux-gnu binutils: --prefix=/romdev (ld SEARCH_DIRs).
- Native stage 1 (arm, mips, sh): libgcc keeps -g -O2 with the tree mapped
  to /romdev; arm newlib is built -O2 with __FILE__ mapped, as the shipped
  libc.a was.
- mips cc1 is compiled at -O2 from gcc/ (gcc/'s own Makefile drops the
  -O2; an -O0 cc1 aborted on real input with the 64KB default stack).
- arm: the re-link reruns each tool's make link step (emcc cannot take the
  JS launcher of a finished link as input) and gives the tools an 8MB
  stack (cc1 is -O0 there). Output also copied into romdev-platform-gba.
- m68k: stage 2 fetches its own gcc/binutils sources, builds cc1 the way
  the arm recipe does and re-links all five tools.
- Rust decomp tools: RUSTFLAGS --remap-path-prefix for the cargo registry
  (/crates) and the build dir (/src).
- flycast: pinned to the commit the shipped core was built from
  (cores.flycast), core changes the WASM dynarec needs as a patch,
  -ffile-prefix-map, no /tmp, output copied into romdev-core-flycast.
- cc65: honours JOBS. Its libs only needed a rebuild with the existing
  reproducible-debug-info patch.

events.title: grm-dos9.6: lock the layout mode when every reset-reached write agrees
events.message:
grm-dos9.6: lock the layout mode when every reset-reached write agrees

Owner idea: most games set the PRG mode once at reset, or on every control
write but always to the same value. After the reset-side fixpoint converges,
a census of mode writes locks the field to V when there is at least one write,
all resolved and agreeing. Async entries and unreached-function fallback seeds
then carry V. After the full fixpoint every write is re-checked: a KNOWN
contradiction rejects the lock, the run is redone without it, and the analyzer
raises a WARNING per contradicting site (owner: a wrong lock must be reported).
A later write whose mode bits do not resolve keeps the lock (owner ruling):
it deposits V on those bits and gets a NOTE 'assumed to stay V here'.
The locked value is published as the 'Detected PRG mode' program property,
erased when no lock holds.

Locks on cv3 (2), smb2 (0), megaman3 (0), tmnt3 (1); none rejected.
Re-blessed smb2, megaman3, tmnt3, nesmodetest, nesmmc5test (the latter two:
more grm-dos9.5 phantom refs). New JUnit ModeLockProgramTest (9 tests).

events.title: SNES: romdev's own SPC700 boot ROM; chip data ROMs and boot ROMs are user-supplied
events.message:
SNES: romdev's own SPC700 boot ROM; chip data ROMs and boot ROMs are user-supplied

The SPC700 boot ROM (IPL) in the snes9x core, the bsnes core and every
recompiled SNES cart is romdev's own: scripts/spc700-ipl/ipl.asm (MIT), a
clean-room reimplementation of the documented upload protocol ($AA/$BB ready
signature, $CC kick, index echo, new block on any other port 0 value, jump
when port 1 is zero), assembled with asar into romdev_iplrom.h. Handover
state: A = X = Y = 0, SP = $EF, PSW = $02, $01-$EF cleared, $00-$01 the
entry address. 62 bytes of code plus the $FFFE reset vector to $FFC0.
install-ipl.mjs rewrites the upstream array in the fetched trees at build
time; snes9x-apu.mjs takes the bytes from romdev_iplrom.h.

The DSP-1, DSP-3 and ST010 data ROM tables snes9x embeds (and the DSP-1
sine table copied from the data ROM) are emptied before snes9x code is built
(recompile-gen/snes9x-chips/hle-data.mjs) and filled from the user's data
ROM (glue/romdev_hledata.h, shared by the core and the chip units):
- the snes9x core reads dsp1b.data.rom / dsp1b.rom, dsp3.data.rom /
  dsp3.rom, st010.data.rom / st010.rom from its system directory and refuses
  the cart with the file and its size named when it is missing or not the
  data ROM the emulation was written against (snes9x-romdev-hle-data.patch,
  patches/snes9x/romdev_hledata.cpp);
- a recompiled cart is built with the same file (options.firmware,
  hle-data.js) and is refused without it; the verifier hands the file to
  the reference;
- LibretroHost includes a core's "romdev:" error log lines in the load
  refusal.

bsnes is built with its DSP-1 data ROM, ST010 tables, Cx4 data ROM and Super
Game Boy boot ROMs emptied (patches/bsnes/strip-firmware.mjs);
bsnes-romdev-firmware.patch drops the DSP-1 and ST010 high-level emulation
(the chips run from the user's firmware or the cart is refused with the
file named), runs the Cx4 with its high-level emulation when cx4.data.rom
is absent, and reads sgb_boot.bin / sgb2_boot.bin from the system directory.

Unit test values read from snes9x (ARAM and audio hashes, per-frame sample
counts) are re-read from the rebuilt core: the boot ROM's own instruction
timing moves when an uploaded program starts. The same procedure reproduces
every old value against the previous core. The DSP-1, DSP-3 and ST010
chip tests run with ROMDEV_SNES_FIRMWARE set to a directory holding the
data ROMs. NOTICE, package READMEs, the bsnes NOTICE, BUILD_MAP and the
recompiler NOTICE describe the new state; binary manifest updated for the
rebuilt snes9x and bsnes cores.

events.title: grm-dos9.4: seed only real entries; power-on state is a fallback, not a rival
events.message:
grm-dos9.4: seed only real entries; power-on state is a fallback, not a rival

Every function entry used to be seeded with the board's power-on state marked
fully known, and that seed merged against the state callers carried in -- so
any field a caller had moved off its power-on value (cv3 prg_mode 2, MMC1
mirroring, MMC3 r6/r7) was lost in every callee. Now only external and async
entries are seeded up front; when the worklist runs dry, unreached function
entries with no calling instruction are seeded (lowest address if all have
callers), repeating until every entry has state.

Re-blessed after review: 19 real-ROM rows (blmaster 0->566 overlay instrs,
rcransom 6404->11587, tmnt3 3425->4365, ...) and nesmodetest, nesmmc3mirrortest,
nesmmc3idtest, nesmmc5test. nesmodetest's new BRK->c010 refs are phantom,
tracked as grm-dos9.5. New JUnit CallerStateReachesCalleeProgramTest.
check OK; check nes 33 pass + known shenlong flap, reproduced twice.
