events.title: asm: a short call behind code that has grown stays short
events.message:
asm: a short call behind code that has grown stays short

In a pass in which code further up has grown, a branch has moved, while a
label further down still has its address of the previous pass. The
distance to such a label was measured from where the branch stands now,
so it came out too small by the growth:

- a BSR.S whose target lay exactly that far ahead seemed to call the very
  next instruction and was widened for good, with the warning "does not
  reach its target" - in the same module or in a later one
- a branch without a size, its label that near, seemed to go backward:
  it was short for one pass and long again in the next, which made the
  code behind it grow once more

Code grows when a short branch does not reach, and also when an address
turns out to need a long word because its constant is defined further
down - so the warning could come without any branch being too far. The
code produced was correct, two bytes longer for every such call.

The distance to a label further down is now measured from where the
branch stood in the previous pass: the distance the two really had
there. For that the assembler notes where every branch stands, and the
passes only end when no branch has moved either. A value knows whether it
names a label the pass has not reached yet, and a branch to such a label
is forward whatever the addresses say. Should a short branch still not
fit when the code is written, that is an error now, not silently wrong
code.

tests/regress/ShortCall (two modules) has the cases; 1.2.2 gives six
warnings there instead of three and widens three of the four short
calls. The reference test over the MDS projects is unchanged (ok=65, the
9 known differences). Of 337 programs built with 1.2.2 and with this,
336 are byte for byte the same; one loses the single call that had been
widened without need, and nothing else in it changes.

events.title: Fix palette serialization offset
events.message:
Fix palette serialization offset

Correct palette serialization to use the active palette offset when reading RGB values.
This fixes incorrect colors when exporting partial or offset-based palettes. The
generated output now reads from ColorValues[StartIndex + i] in both the sorted and
unsorted serialization paths, ensuring the byte stream matches the selected palette
range and preserves the correct red, green, and blue component order.

To be or not to be.

events.title: Βήμα 98: τα αγαθά του εμπόρου κουβαλιούνται
events.message:
Βήμα 98: τα αγαθά του εμπόρου κουβαλιούνται

- Ο παίκτης, μετά το 97: τα αγαθά του εμπόρου κουβαλιούνται, όπως στο
  Planetbase. Οπως τα εργοτάξια: όσα δίνεις φεύγουν στο FIRE, όσα παίρνεις
  μπαίνουν όταν φτάσει κάθε φορτίο σε αποθήκη ή στο σκάφος. Ο έμπορος
  περιμένει ώσπου να κουβαληθούν όλα (το μισό sol μόνο χωρίς συμφωνία), και
  κουβαλά οποιοσδήποτε: κάθε άποικος και τα ρομπότ μεταφοράς (#5F).
- tr_deal (src/lines.asm): τα φορτία που οφείλονται στον έμπορο, ως δέκα
  μονάδες, στρογγυλεμένα ανά αγαθό, στο EC_MARKUP· όσα πήρες στις ποσότητες
  του EC_CARGO· EC_SHKIND = SK_DEALT, EC_SHETA #FFFF· δύο J_TRADE στην πίστα
  (trd_post). Καμία συμφωνία με τον πίνακα γεμάτο ή χωρίς πίστα. Ιδια bytes
  με το 93: SV_VER μένει 8.
- src/carry.asm (tr_arrive, από το sp_arrive): στην αποθήκη ένα φορτίο του
  στα αποθέματα και ένα για εκείνον, στην πίστα ό,τι φέρνει μένει και το
  επόμενο από το πλοίο του — κάθε ταξίδι και προς τις δύο μεριές. Στο τέλος
  οι ανοιχτές άδειες J_TRADE σβήνουν, και αν δεν μένει καμία ο έμπορος φεύγει.
- ΤΟ ΦΟΡΤΙΟ ΕΙΝΑΙ ΤΗΣ ΕΡΓΑΣΙΑΣ (J_SITE), όχι του πράκτορα: στο spare χανόταν σε
  κάθε διάλειμμα για ανάγκη. Το jb_reap αφήνει τη J_TRADE όπως τη Haul.
- Η πρώτη αλυσίδα στο παιχνίδι που τρέχει βρήκε το EC_PADNODE 255 (το πέρασμα
  δωματίων ξαναβρίσκει την πίστα): χωρίς πίστα, ένας μετεωρίτης, ο μεταφορέας
  περιμένει όπου είναι αντί για τον κόμβο 255.
- Μνήμη: 239 bytes της τράπεζας 0, που είχε 32. Μίκρυνε η διεπαφή χωρίς
  αλλαγή συμπεριφοράς: ui/bar/fit -304, lines/help -109, act/info -78 στην
  τράπεζα 2. Τράπεζα 0 206 κάτω από το πάτωμα, τράπεζα 2 74 (4). LOOK 984 ->
  845 us, PLACE 1.036 -> 894· η μπάρα σε πλήκτρο 8.620 -> 8.800· όλη η
  περιστροφή 28.954, ίδια.
- Δοκιμές: tests/test_carry.py (15 σκηνές της θέσης 13, πίστα χτισμένη και
  δύο μεταφορείς στο παιχνίδι, 3 κόστη, 12 αρνητικά)· test_trade η συμφωνία
  (6 νέα αρνητικά)· test_sim η μεταφορά byte προς byte με την αναφορά, με και
  χωρίς αποθήκη (2 αρνητικά). 66 δοκιμές, όλες OK.

events.title: 実装: GET@・PUT@（l4-graphics 第6版、l4-s9x）
events.message:
実装: GET@・PUT@（l4-graphics 第6版、l4-s9x）

l4-graphics 第6版第12節・共通部とl4-program 第14.16版4.10.8を根拠に独立実装。
既存のar_elemの番地計算と型別の連続バイト領域を使い、LE16bitの幅・高さ、行ごとのB/R/G、MSB左、バイト詰め、未使用上位バイトの保持を実装した。
GETの逆順と第2点STEP、PUTのPSET/PRESET/OR/AND/XORと既定XOR、白黒アクティブページ・明示色、容量・はみ出し・誤り・LPを扱う。
bank2のgx_*速い入口とgx_addrを使用。VRAM選択中はレジスタと画面だけに触れ、DI→選択→読み書き→OUT 5F→EIとしてVSYNCとの競合を防ぐ。
bank0の語表にGET/PUTを加え、POINT照合語を既存固定入口間の空きへ移して収めた。

再開後の検証（正式な検証1〜4は各1回、最大2系統）:
- GET/PUT: 88/88一致、88腕×2走の全関門通過。
- DIM: 143/143一致、143腕×2走の全関門通過。GET値の4腕が全て一致。
- LINE: 68/68一致。CIRCLE: 45/45一致。
- PAINT: 57/67一致、67腕×2走の全関門通過。既知の10差を維持（check rc=1）。
  差はws-10a/b/c/d/e、ws-2c、ws-6c、ws-8a/e/f。全10件を読んだ。
- s9t GFX: 83腕×2走の判定・群判定・gateは自作HEADとの差0。両ROMの全関門通過。
- 速度（同じGET/PUT全腕測定の100回ループ、各2走同値、追加測定なし）:
  GET 1785、PUT 2091、空ループ37フレーム、誤り0件。
  空ループ差引GET1748、PUT2054。仕様にある公式291/403（空9）より遅い。
- verify_l1, l3_main, conform_l4, ext_bank, vsync_regcheck, memmap, memdyn,
  deffn, deftype, line, gfx, circle, paint, getput, check_cleanroom: 各rc=0。
- array_impl初回: rc=1。既存8腕は全てOK、新規の@明記腕だけが打鍵失敗で停止。
  フロントエンドは@を打鍵できず、HEAD指定でもROM走行前にrc=1を再現。
  frontend/main.cはHEADと同一。HEAD既存array_implには追加@腕がない。
  追加腕を測定と同じ@省略形へ修正、行組立の迂回は撤回。
  修正後のarray_implは未検証。「検証1回」の指定のため再実行可否を質問し、回答待ち。
  全16検査rc=0という条件はまだ満たしていない。@明記の動的検証も未実施。
- 自己検査ログのNG表記13行を全件確認。array_implのTraceback以外は意図した陰性対照。
  l3_main/conform_l4のNG表記は前回記録と同一。前回memmapの別名不整合はMM_GP_*正典登録で解消。
- check_cleanroomは閲覧禁止のdocs/notes/・tmp/をgit ls-filesの内容検査対象から除外した制限付き実行。
  禁止資料の内容検査は未実施であり、全追跡ファイルの無制限検査とは扱わない。

器具の修正理由（自作ROMの結果に合わせた期待値生成・照合条件の緩和なし）:
- l4_dim_measure.py: HEADは152腕を生成するが採用期待値は143腕で、集合完全一致のcheckがHEADでも成立しなかった。
  第14.16版4.10.10で保留された長い次元48/64/96/120/127/128/254/255/256の9腕だけを通常の採用集合から除く。
  数値・ERR・総誤り・終了印・較正・固定腕集合・2走一致の判定コードと採用期待値は維持。
- l4_getput_measure.py: selftestが未実装ERR2を固定していたため、正しい実装の観測を拒否していた。
  前回の「自作ROMの成功値を直接assertする」変更を取り除き、固定済みexpected_l4_getput.tsvで10腕の全項目をcheckする形へ修正。
  成功100回に加え、仕様ERR2のGET第1点STEPを100回×2走する独立したエラー計数対照を維持。
  数値・較正・2走不一致・期待値破損・VRAM故障注入の陰性対照を維持。
  arms・事前仮説・valid・calibrated・comparable・check・採用期待値は変更しない。
- l4_getput_selftest.sh: 固定期待値を利用する自己検査へ説明を更新。
- l4_array_impl_selftest.py: 非0の未使用上位バイト保持と既定XOR2回の自作専用腕を追加。
  @打鍵不能という器具制約のため省略形を使う。未対応文字拒否やDIM器具の@禁止関門は緩めない。

配置・残り容量:
- GETPUT本体935B、bank2 0x6B43〜0x6EE9、0x7000手前278B。
- bank0末尾65B、bank1末尾93B、bank2末尾23B、bank3末尾27B（追加使用なし）。
- main末尾126B、追加使用0B。測定ROM用116B以上を保持。
- 自作HEAD a8fbcd978b63d3f56e9914a461fdd34c296635b5 とmain・bank1・bank3は完全一致。
  bank2はGETPUT領域と文分岐0x7399〜0x73A0の8B以外が完全一致。0x79D7不変。

自作判断:
- @省略／明記を字句上受理する（公式の@字句測定は未実施、今回の動的検証も省略形）。
- 未DIMの添字省略はERR5、幅／高さ0はERR5。失敗GETは容量確認前に配列を書き換えない。
- 明示色は1プレーンとして復号し、カラーは下位3bit、白黒は非0を使用する。
  観測されたPSET,5,2とPSET,8,0以外の組合せは自作判断。
- x=7,w=9の余りビットは先頭有効バイトから生成する。
  別の模様・高さへの一般化は自作判断であり、確定した公式仕様としない。
- LINE作業域をGET/PUTと排他的に再利用し、配列容量は物理再利用枠ではなく生きた論理領域で確認する。

CarDamage_BuildRelativeVelocityHull byte-exact (50.0% -> exact); 64-bit: stage object pointers typed

CarDamage_BuildRelativeVelocityHull written as an index loop is exact,
and the exact form fixes a behaviour bug: the original raises vertices
4/5 by field_0x770[1] and 6/7 by field_0x770[0]; the decompiled code had

Pointers that travelled as int are typed: the AI working state passed to
AI_SelectWallCollisionResponse (int *, indexed like its other readers),
the car in the car-light, submesh, damage-rebuild and steering-blend
functions (Car *), the sky/ground/cloud node getters (SceneNode **) and
their users in StageObjects.cpp and TrackCollision.cpp (fields instead
of +0x98/+0xc/+4), the scene node of the moving objects
(StageObjectEntry0x128::pObject, in both copies of the struct), the
replay lane records (BYTE *), the reference matrix of the car-mount
dispatch (FixMatrix *) and Glow_Add's two unused vector arguments.
Unused arguments that receive different pointer types are void *.

Pointer loops compared as (int)p < (int)&end are written as index
loops where MSVC6 generates the same code (moving objects, glow
records, menu sounds, the five replay slot walks, object value reset);

events.message:
Scene_FreeShadowCasters byte-exact (50.2% -> exact); 64-bit: shadow casters and texture stages typed

The shadow caster table holds ShadowCaster * and the cylinder cache
Mesh *; Scene_FreeShadowCasters walks both by index and re-reads the
entry on every access, which is the original form (signed loop compare,
partCount reloaded). ShadowPart names the light basis at 0x0 and the
emitted face/vertex counts, and Scene_EmitProjectedShadowMesh (exact)
takes a ShadowPart * with fields instead of byte offsets. Table loops in
Scene_InitLighting, the type 2 object release and Scene_RestoreLights
use indices with identical code.

CGraphics::ApplyTextureStageChange and ConfigureTextureStageBlendMode
take Texture *, as does the cached stage texture; the 22 callers lose
their (int) casts. The null-texture branch passes D3DTA_DIFFUSE where
the decompiler had reused the null register (same code).

2923 byte-exact (+1), no function loses score; suite 116/116.
x64 pointer/integer casts: 816 -> 733.

Game_DrawSceneViewport takes the root and camera as SceneNode * and the
view rectangle as void *; Game_PrepareScene and
Sector_CullGridAroundViewNode take the same rectangle, and Particle_DrawAll
the camera. The scene-root globals and their getters

are SceneNode *, and wheel parents are read through pParent.
Sector_BuildC3DModelScene returns the relocated SceneNode * and takes its
parent and archive; OptionPreview_LoadStageGeometryRecord uses buffers,
nodes and the GenericFile record with their own types.

the two readers that indexed the triangle as int[].

symbol count; the new MeshTriangle field flipped it, and dropping the
unused SavedGames_ReleaseRecords prototype from FrontendScreens.cpp
restores it. Details in docs/structure-recovery/64bit-scene-roots.md.

project.title: volamos
project.display_title: volamos — AmigaOS CLI compatibility runtime

runtime_profiles.name: Linux x86-64 command-line runtime
runtime_profiles.notes: Current CI builds the release executable on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and executes vamos comparison and interpreter/JIT fixtures. No minimum RAM or Linux release is established.

runtime_profiles.name: Apple Silicon command-line runtime
runtime_profiles.notes: Current CI log identifies aarch64-apple-darwin and passes unit/end-to-end guest fixture execution. No minimum RAM or macOS release is established.

project.status: active
project.notes: Wine-style host runtime for classic AmigaOS m68k command-line tools: interprets guest instructions (optional m68k-crate trace JIT) and reimplements OS library calls in Rust. No Kickstart ROM is needed for normal use. It is generic development/analysis tooling, not a native reconstruction of a specific game; graphics, custom chips, Workbench GUI and games are explicitly out of scope. Linux/macOS build and guest execution are corroborated by current CI logs; published Windows x86-64 binaries compile but Windows/Wine runtime remains unverified. Interpreter/JIT parity covers six fixtures; comparison with vamos includes three documented known divergences, so it is not universal compatibility proof. The math-library shims now return comparison/test results in both D0 and 68k condition codes, matching the documented ROM calling behavior needed by SAS/C's scmieee.lib; before the fix, SAS/C double comparisons appeared equal and exp() overflow checks returned HUGE_VAL. Evidence: https://github.com/sidick/volamos/commit/de321627fd5f1c16ca6cc76020222d7f3c18d564 exec.library SetFunction now installs executable guest JMP entries, returns a synthesized callable stub for the previous host-backed handler, supports hook chaining and restoration, and is covered by an end-to-end guest test. The patch is deliberately limited to one guest invocation and does not emulate AmigaOS-wide persistent hooks. Evidence: https://github.com/sidick/volamos/commit/018fd8f047d27fa3f85948b1595f44acf3f6f596

project.status: Native game collection with bootable outputs and upstream tests; independently unbuilt
project.notes: Identity: The creator’s repository contains eight native Apple II games, including original Arkabreakout/ChromaBreak and ports of POM1 games. Reviewed concrete Arkabreakout gameplay assembly, Snake C implementation, ChromaBreak bootstrap/build, and Chess documentation. This is one repository-level collection record, not eight inflated entries. Classification: Native Apple II source collection and ports. Arkabreakout assembles a standalone BRUN binary and DOS 3.3 disk; ChromaBreak builds a ProDOS system file. The bundled a2run/a2shot emulator code serves tests and is not embedded in the games. LOGO, demos and generic dev tooling are incidental to this game-scoped record. Source CPU: The README and Snake header identify POM1 Apple-1/GEN2 versions as predecessors, and Chess documents reused POM1 rules code. Those predecessor files were not independently inspected, so no source CPU is inferred from the target assembly or Apple-1 label. Target CPU: Arkabreakout’s game.s explicitly specifies NMOS 6502 and contains native gameplay assembly. ChromaBreak’s Makefile passes --cpu 65c02; boot.s starts with a 6502 CPU probe and then selects .setcpu "65C02", rejecting an NMOS IIe. These establish separate 6502 and 65C02 outputs, not a single machine minimum. Build: The reviewed game Makefiles invoke ca65/ld65 or cl65 and construct bootable DOS 3.3/ProDOS disks. The README claims deterministic rebuilds and emulator-based tests, but those claims were not independently reproduced; byte_exact remains null. Limitations: Static primary-source review only. No candidate code, build, emulator, gameplay, hardware test or byte comparison was executed; all independent build flags remain null. Runtime profiles: Upstream describes II+ 48 KB/DOS 3.3 for Arkabreakout/classic ports and enhanced IIe or IIc 128 KB/ProDOS for ChromaBreak, with keyboard/paddle or AppleMouse controls. The bootstrap explicitly rejects NMOS machines for ChromaBreak. These are source/author requirements, not independently verified runnable minima. Limitations: Profiles preserve directly observed requirements/author claims only; no independent runtime hardware validation was performed. AI: The latest commit explicitly includes Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>; the same named tool is present in the inspected recent commit sample. This is development-AI evidence, separate from the chess opponent AI. Relationships: The README and source headers explicitly derive the classic games from VERHILLE Arnaud’s POM1 work. Chess credits cc65-Chess for board/piece art and its Apple II port, but identifies its engine as POM1 rules code; this is not another copy of the already catalogued cc65-chess-stewbc-native. GPL-3.0 code, Skinner Microban levels, CC-BY-3.0 sprites and separate Apple ROM/DOS rights are disclosed. No blanket original-authorship or permissive-license claim is made. Normalized roots were screened programmatically against prior-roots.json before file review; current catalogue titles/subjects were checked for aliases. This is bounded lineage review, not proof of complete originality. The root README states Apple II+ 48 KB or //c with mouse or joystick; this is an upstream requirement, not an independent run. project.display_title: lxa — Linux Amiga executable runtime
project.status: v0.11.45; upstream reference corpus reports 2 platinum, 25 gold and 9 silver applications
project.notes: Runs AmigaOS 68000 binaries through CPU emulation and Linux-backed system-library reimplementations. Recent AmigaOS 3.1 probes corrected full-D0 BOOL/LONG returns and assign-root ParentDir behavior, while the roadmap reached v0.11.25 phases for BCPL and FPU programs; broad compatibility remains ongoing. Version 0.11.32 closes the Phase 238 corpus sweep: all 36 tracked applications now open windows comparable to the AmigaOS 3.1 reference, while remaining behavioral differences stay assigned to later phases. The same change fixes preserved-register ABI behavior, volume names and the harness Workbench backdrop. Evidence: https://github.com/gooofy/lxa/commit/d7cc3ddb29be6356109c034db97fcfc3b233ee12 The v0.11.34–0.11.45 pass completes a 9,943-program Fred Fish comparison against AmigaOS 3.1 with 13 remaining lxa-only crashes, then advances the 36-app corpus to 2 platinum, 25 gold and 9 silver. Compatibility fixes include fast-RAM vectors, misc.resource, foreign-vector register handling, condition codes, Workbench screen semantics and clean 32-bit BOOL returns; these are upstream reference results, not independent validation. Evidence: https://github.com/gooofy/lxa/commit/03c1d12f8af19276a4755f0b3edd6085559d18b2 https://github.com/gooofy/lxa/commit/331b8a012448c947be3696381012296b5663567c

project.title: Oscar64: C/C++ cross-compiler for 6502 systems
project.display_title: Oscar64: C/C++ cross-compiler for 6502 systems
project.status: Partial source audit; no independent build, runtime, hardware or byte-identity verification
project.notes: README describes a C99/C++ cross-compiler for 6502-family systems, especially C64, PET and VIC-20, including banked cartridges and disk overlays. CMakeLists.txt defines a C++17 executable from the compiler directory; inspected oscar64.cpp drives the compiler and disk-image tooling. Directory contains parser, optimizer, linker, assembler, disassembler, native and bytecode generators. Modern-host cross-compiler and runtime/toolchain, not a reconstruction of an older binary. Windows, macOS and Linux describe compiler hosts; C64, PET and VIC-20 describe generated-code targets. Host architecture is not inferred from C++. README performance and language-support claims are upstream assertions, not independently measured. Only explicitly documented core target labels are proposed, not every possible 6502 target. Source inspection only. No compilation, execution, gameplay, hardware test or byte comparison was performed. Build: CMake 3.15+ with C++17, or repository make/Visual Studio project. Host-specific dependencies and runtime include installation are declared; no host or target build tested. No candidate build, execution, gameplay, hardware test or byte comparison was performed. Supplied binaries, recipes and upstream success claims do not independently establish compilable/runnable/playable or byte-identical output. Architecture: README explicitly says the compiler targets the classic 6502 family. target_cpu=6502 describes generated code, never the CPU running the compiler. Host CPU and minimum hardware are unspecified. Rights: Repository license evidence: GPL-3.0. GPLv3 text inspected. Samples/runtime may require their own finer-grained interpretation before reuse. Relationships: Repository metadata reports fork=false; no separate mirror counted. Runtime: README documents Windows PC, Mac and Linux compiler hosts and separate C64/PET/VIC-20 code targets. It supplies no explicit host CPU/RAM minimum. Do not represent the cross-compiler itself as running on its generated-code targets; runtime_profiles remains empty. AI evidence: No explicit AI development tool/model declaration found in sampled source/README/build/license content and inspected commit messages. This is not proof that AI was unused. Gameplay AI or historical Lisp terminology is not development-assistance evidence. Inspected 3 returned commits (up to three for ordinary candidates), including author/committer names and full messages; no inference from provider domains. Latest activity uses the inspected default-branch commit date, not repository creation or push time. Primary evidence: https://github.com/drmortalwombat/oscar64/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/drmortalwombat/oscar64/blob/main/CMakeLists.txt https://github.com/drmortalwombat/oscar64/blob/main/LICENSE https://github.com/drmortalwombat/oscar64/blob/main/oscar64/oscar64.cpp https://github.com/drmortalwombat/oscar64/commit/3f4268cdf0792a0b74a75a99dbbe77edaf1c9a06 https://github.com/drmortalwombat/oscar64/commit/3de1bbef4b436b14f6af7290dd6af152028bf125 https://github.com/drmortalwombat/oscar64/commit/07b98fb3e15f044b75a40f55f1fbbd10137acc4c The current compiler pass adds C23 explicit enumeration underlying types, preserves enum width/signedness, corrects unsigned wraparound arithmetic, and fixes integer promotions across parsing, constant folding and code generation with dedicated tests. project.status: active
project.notes: Clean-room Dungeon Master-family engine using authenticated original media. Current primary documentation records bounded startup/runtime coverage for DM1 on DOS, Atari ST, Amiga and FM Towns; CSB on Amiga, Atari ST and FM Towns; and DM2 on DOS, Amiga, FM Towns and Macintosh. The latest receipts correct DM1 Amiga HD and DM2 FM Towns boot assertions and expand the cross-game startup matrix and diagnostics. These remain bounded startup/audio receipts rather than full-game parity. project.title: CPCSyntaxError
project.display_title: CPCSyntaxError — CPC/Plus cycle-level emulator
project.status: active; v0.5.0 media, cheat and peripheral expansion release
project.notes: Emulates CPC 464/6128, Plus and GX4000 with per-model CRTC/Gate Array timing, disc and tape support, a debugger and embedded RASM. Inspected src/core includes Z80, CRTC variants and debugging code. README calls expansion hardware and UI work in progress; SHAKER compatibility is upstream's claim. v0.4.0 adds host-backed M4 TCP/DNS/server and plain-HTTP operations, a folder-backed FAT16 IDE/CF interface for SYMBiFACE II/III, and LambdaSpeak 3 Epson/DECtalk command handling using host voices. The release documents tests with Duke's TCP/telnet examples, SymbOS and LambdaSpeak software; these upstream compatibility claims were not independently reproduced. Evidence: https://github.com/WacKEDmaN/CPCSyntaxError/commit/c909c7f7e465dc54640248cbd91a4d78a1c45656 v0.5.0 adds guided and manual RAM cheats, CDT/TZX tape recording and turbo loading, HFE read/write, IPF read support, image writeback, a 300-rpm real-time floppy model, Multiface II, RS232C endpoints and folder-backed M4 DSK images. The bundled IPF decoder retains its non-commercial licence; upstream compatibility tests were not independently reproduced. Evidence: https://github.com/WacKEDmaN/CPCSyntaxError/commit/35ca66c5bb974eb0b1113e08980ea166cf93362a

runtime_profiles.name: Acorn A3010 ArchieSDK port
runtime_profiles.notes: The README and platform source explicitly target an A3010 with ARM250, 2 MB RAM and RISC OS 3.11. This is author-stated compatibility, not an independently executed minimum.

project.status: cross-platform original homebrew with native Apple II and Acorn A3010 builds; independently unbuilt
project.notes: Identity: Stefan Wessels’ chess game combines a real move generator, legality/attack tests, make/unmake operations and board UI. Oliver Schmidt’s Apple II port has platform C and HGR assembly; the current tree replaces the 2014 engine with a 2026 rewrite. Classification: Original cross-platform homebrew with a native Apple II port. This entry reviews the Apple II output; other ports remain part of the same repository and are not split into duplicate game entries. Chess-opponent search is distinct from development AI. Source CPU: This is newly authored native game code rather than a recovered predecessor executable. No original-binary CPU is assigned from its target machine or the game that inspired it; source_platforms, source_cpu and source_language remain empty. Target CPU: README explicitly describes the Apple II version among the approximately 1 MHz 6502 machines. The inspected Apple II HGR source contains native 6502 instructions and the port file selects cc65 apple2; no 65C02-only or IIgs-native requirement is claimed. Build: Apple II make/port and shared cc65 rules compile C/assembly and package ProDOS images via Cadius. The repository has a measurement/test harness, but its strength, perft and game-count claims were not independently run or adopted as validation. Limitations: No compilation, launch, gameplay, hardware test or original-binary comparison was performed; every independent build flag remains null. Runtime profiles: The reviewed output is the native Apple II HGR board with keyboard controls and a ProDOS image recipe. No exact numeric RAM floor, Apple II model minimum or OS version is established by the sample. AI: README explicitly discloses AI assistance for the 2026 replacement engine, documentation and tests while identifying the 2014 program as hand-written. Recent real implementation/build commits carry Claude coauthor trailers; the upstream model label is not treated as independent version verification. Relationships: The 2014 game, 2026 engine rewrite and Apple II frontend are one project. Root LICENSE is a public-domain dedication. Generic Chess title matches do not identify this code lineage. Normalized root, title/alias and lineage were screened against the 1,798-project f003aa64 catalogue, source/decision files and expanded 2,198-root prior union; no same-code catalogue entry was found. Evidence: https://github.com/stewbc/cc65-chess/blob/401f1a87ca6fb8cb5c3bbb0fede7c8b709828fe5/README.md https://github.com/stewbc/cc65-chess/blob/401f1a87ca6fb8cb5c3bbb0fede7c8b709828fe5/src/engine.c https://github.com/stewbc/cc65-chess/blob/401f1a87ca6fb8cb5c3bbb0fede7c8b709828fe5/src/apple2/hires.s https://github.com/stewbc/cc65-chess/blob/401f1a87ca6fb8cb5c3bbb0fede7c8b709828fe5/src/apple2/platA2.c https://github.com/stewbc/cc65-chess/blob/401f1a87ca6fb8cb5c3bbb0fede7c8b709828fe5/make/ports/apple2.mk https://github.com/stewbc/cc65-chess/blob/401f1a87ca6fb8cb5c3bbb0fede7c8b709828fe5/make/toolchains/cc65.mk https://github.com/stewbc/cc65-chess/blob/401f1a87ca6fb8cb5c3bbb0fede7c8b709828fe5/LICENSE https://github.com/StewBC/cc65-Chess/commit/facf2525ccf542323edba279c7b8da3f9dd4de31 The same original homebrew now has an ArchieSDK port targeting an Acorn A3010 with ARM250, 2 MB RAM and RISC OS 3.11. It builds a RISC OS application/ZIP and has host-side platform tests; this is a new native target, not evidence of reverse-engineering lineage. Evidence: https://github.com/StewBC/cc65-Chess/commit/4de42f63f1eb04830ecd921165e61bfca54a43fd https://github.com/StewBC/cc65-Chess/blob/master/README.md

Target CPU: README explicitly describes the Apple II version among the approximately 1 MHz 6502 machines. runtime_profiles.name: C64RE workbench
runtime_profiles.os: Node.js 22 or newer; TRX64 0.12.9; user-supplied Commodore ROMs
runtime_profiles.notes: No minimum host CPU or RAM is stated.

project.status: active; pins TRX64 0.12.9 and can drive a C64 Ultimate through a shared bridge daemon
project.notes: C64 forensic and semantic-disassembly workbench. The Node.js 22+ application verifies reconstructed assembly with byte diffs and now pins TRX64 0.12.9 with user-supplied ROMs. The current changes use execution breakpoints for reachability claims, prevent duplicate equate definitions in relocated listings, preserve byte-identical rebuilds, and scope negative knowledge claims to their owning evidence coverage. A separately running C64 Ultimate bridge exposes the TRX64 wire protocol to multiple clients; hardware execution remains gated on a successful emulator run of the same bytes. Evidence: https://github.com/Jondalar/C64ReverseEngineeringMCP/commit/669c1346e4ec https://github.com/Jondalar/C64ReverseEngineeringMCP/commit/74fe38185ca5 https://github.com/Jondalar/C64ReverseEngineeringMCP/commit/cbfcadbf92b3 https://github.com/Jondalar/C64ReverseEngineeringMCP/commit/f68fe3d28d92 The current platform pass adds explicit VIC-20 and TED-machine tags, Plus/4 BASIC 3.5 listing/tokenization, VIC-20/TED BASIC-stub recognition and signature-based raw-cartridge placement. Follow-up fixes emit outside-image addresses as equates and place names inside relocated blocks at the defining instruction while preserving every reference. Evidence: https://github.com/Jondalar/C64ReverseEngineeringMCP/commit/38f1292610839c16db44f06a565a0ee4e49693f5 https://github.com/Jondalar/C64ReverseEngineeringMCP/commit/86f2e560ae1608c751018daac2abf2af5c63120e https://github.com/Jondalar/C64ReverseEngineeringMCP/commit/be6a640cbcd7d217562502fdd3b28f7cb613af52

project.display_title: Acorn NFS and ANFS — BBC Micro ROM disassemblies
project.status: active byte-exact ROM reassembly with expanded NFS/ANFS annotation coverage
project.notes: Annotated Acorn Network Filing System and Advanced NFS ROMs across multiple 3.x and 4.x versions. The project documents label/comment cross-references, version comparisons and dasmos/fantasm generation; CI reassembles with BeebAsm and compares each supported ROM byte for byte. README documents an 8 KB NFS and 16 KB ANFS successor. The October 2026 annotation pass comments every instruction across the supported NFS/ANFS versions, models command and pointer tables symbolically, corrects mis-decoded data and now requires Fantasm 1.2.1 for the strengthened comment checks; byte-exact BeebAsm verification remains the project's build claim. Evidence: https://github.com/acornaeology/acorn-nfs/commit/5b58991161d5a5bac86e1e58d235c7bffa0f8e82 https://github.com/acornaeology/acorn-nfs/commit/1a96ee5c81aa287e4d20cd03e03945adba33b8ce

project.title: 3Dvibe64
project.display_title: 3Dvibe64 — Commodore 64 graphics engine SDK

runtime_profiles.name: Q8 accelerated-emulation qualification
runtime_profiles.notes: Upstream recommends Q8 only above 20 MHz. v1.8.0 reports Turbo6510 64 MHz measurements on public PAL cube scenes: Mode 2 precise/hybrid 23.70/25.05 FPS, Mode 5 27.00/27.45 FPS, and distant-cube Mode 7 standard/fast/fast+LOD 3.10/6.95/11.50 FPS. These are scene-specific emulator measurements, not minima, general guarantees or physical-hardware qualification.

project.status: v1.9.0 source SDK released; experimental Normalized16 geometry remains opt-in and physically unverified
project.notes: Source SDK for eight C64 graphics modes: polygon rendering and a distinct Mode 8 2.5D DDA bitmap renderer. PowerShell/Python scene builders emit 6510/6502 assembly for 64tass. v1.8.0 adds opt-in gradual Mode 7 texture LOD, optional Q8 hybrid line rasterization for Modes 1/2/5 and safe presentation for Modes 1–7; legacy geometry, standard texture quality, precise raster and LOD-off remain defaults. Upstream reports all 22 public tests passing and bounded Turbo6510 64 MHz scene measurements, while explicitly stating that real hardware has not been tested. Code/data remain PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. Codex usage guides document downstream SDK use, not development-AI authorship of the engine. v1.9.0 adds an explicit experimental Normalized16 build and bounded signed-16 geometry generators while preserving the Q8 defaults unless the optional hook is selected. Native benchmark and qualification tooling are included; this does not change the recorded physical-hardware limitation. Evidence: https://github.com/Librologica/3Dvibe64/commit/562f3c314314abce8de7c30786843c2435b00e94 https://github.com/Librologica/3Dvibe64/commit/6ea4d7cf99513d9714407ea938aed06b8d55d4bc

events.title: Unlock the platform event queue when NewtonOS reboots
events.message:
Unlock the platform event queue when NewtonOS reboots

"NewtonScript Reboot" sends Reboot() as a platform event. The REX
interrupt handler locks the event queue and unlocks it when NewtonOS
answers the event, but NewtonOS reboots first. mQueueLockCount stayed at
1, and no later event reached NewtonOS: no power button, keyboard or
package installation, and a fast start on quit timed out.

TMainPlatformDriver::Init is called once per boot, before
PowerOnDeviceCheck releases the boot lock. It now resets the queue locks
to their state at launch (no lock, boot lock set). Pending events stay
in the queue and are sent when the boot is complete. No REX change.

events.title: Suspend the PTY, Pipes and BasiliskII serial workers during save and load
events.message:
Suspend the PTY, Pipes and BasiliskII serial workers during save and load

Only the TCP client implemented Suspend() and Resume(). The other worker
threads kept writing emulated memory and DMA registers while the state
was saved, loaded or reset, so RAM could be saved before a byte arrived
and the registers after it.

The DMA mutex and Suspend()/Resume() move from the TCP client to
TBasicSerialPortManager, which holds the DMA registers. Each worker
holds the mutex while it transmits (including the checks of the enable
and countdown registers) and while it writes received bytes to memory.
The reads and their sleeps stay outside, so Suspend() does not wait for
them.

Tested with all four drivers: round trip identical, save, load and quit.
The PTY worker did not start, because /tmp/BBridge.Einstein did not exist.

Found by Greptile in PR #225.

events.title: Deliver platform events again after a Hardware Reset
events.message:
Deliver platform events again after a Hardware Reset

The reset through the state tree locks the platform event queue until
NewtonOS has booted (mQueueBootLock), as at launch. The lock was only
released by the first PowerOnDeviceCheck call per process (a static
counter), so after a Hardware Reset or Brain Wipe no event reached
NewtonOS any more: no power button, no keyboard, no package
installation, and a fast start on quit timed out because the Newton
never fell asleep. Now every PowerOnDeviceCheck releases the lock;
releasing it again does nothing.

events.title: Don't lose state requests while the monitor starts or stops the emulator
events.message:
Don't lose state requests while the monitor starts or stops the emulator

Two windows could lose a Save/Load/Check State or reset request from
the UI; afterwards every request was refused until the next run:

- RunEmulator() had left its loop (breakpoint, stop command) but not
  set mHalted yet. The UI queued the request, and nobody processed it.
  Now mHalted is set under a small mutex that the UI also holds while
  it queues a request, and a request found after halting is processed
  right away. The emulator stays halted.
- RunEmulator() had set mHalted to false but not entered
  TEmulator::Run() yet, which set mRunning = true over the UI's Stop().
  TEmulator now counts Stop() calls, and Run(inStopCount) returns at
  once if a stop came after the caller read the count. Run() without
  an argument behaves as before.

Both cases were reproduced with temporary delays in the two windows:
the request stayed pending before, and is processed now.

Found by CodeRabbit and Greptile in PR #225.

events.title: perf(cd): read CD images by sector, not whole (SQ-1761)
events.message:
perf(cd): read CD images by sector, not whole (SQ-1761)

Opening one game off the 354 MB Masterpieces CD read all of it, copied
308 MB of it out of its sector frames, and did so per launch step. Now a
CD image stays on disk and the volume readers fetch the sectors they are
asked for.

* blorb::source::Source: the readers' byte access is a range request over
  either memory (today's behaviour, borrowed slices) or a window onto a
  Disc read through the same cd::Sectors mapping as the in-memory path.
* blorb::image::open sniffs the first 48 KB by content (Apple-partitioned
  HFS, or cooked ISO 9660) and returns a handle with no bytes; floppies,
  bare Mac volumes and story files are read whole, once, as before.
* Everything that walked every file has a header-only form: story
  detection from the 64-byte header and the catalogued length, per-file
  Volume::files/read_prefix/read_file, story_named, story_count_up_to,
  has_story. read_extents reads a run in one piece. Native-sound reading
  is limited to sound/ paths; the Scott scan, the Amiga-font scan and the
  packed-Apple-volume probe are skipped for a disc read by sector.
* assets lists a CD's files and reads them on demand.

Masterpieces CD, mount + list + extract one game: 354,011,280 bytes read
and ~55 ms in memory, 4,510,704 bytes and ~2 ms by sector (warm local
cache; the saving over a network share is the bytes). A whole launch
sequence reads ~27 MB.

events.title: Check sizes and counts read from a state file
events.message:
Check sizes and counts read from a state file

The CRC catches damaged files. A file edited by hand still has a valid
CRC, so values that become sizes, counts or indices are checked as
well. TStream::CheckLimit() throws when a value is too large;
CheckDataSize() also throws when the data would be larger than the rest
of the stream (TMemoryStream knows what is left), so no allocation can
be larger than the file. The existing catch in LoadState() reports
which value is wrong, and a fast start boots normally.

Limits: card image paths 2048 bytes (longer paths are saved empty),
card state blocks 64 MB + 4 KB (the largest linear card and its CIS),
the ATA FIFO one sector, 65536 platform events of at most 256 bytes,
1024 platform buffers of at most 64 MB, breakpoints 65536, pen sample
positions inside the ring buffer. The RAM size and end are
configuration and must match, so RAM is no longer reallocated.

Found by CodeRabbit and Greptile in PR #225.

events.title: Network play over UDP with ENet, replacing DirectPlay
events.message:
Network play over UDP with ENet, replacing DirectPlay

src/net implements port/net.h (the game's DirectPlay 4 model) over UDP
with ENet 1.3.18 (third_party/enet, MIT):

- the host is the session's server and relays between guests, so only
  it must be reachable (LAN, Tailscale or another VPN, a forwarded port);
- channel 0 reliable and ordered (guaranteed messages, protocol),
  channel 1 unreliable (car states);
- host migration as the game expects: the earliest joined machine
  becomes the host (NET_SYS_HOST) and the others reconnect;
- asynchronous search on the session port (ENet intercept): LAN
  broadcast, [net] peers and the online Tailscale machines;
- a service thread keeps connections up while the game loads;
- every packet is bounds-checked, the host drops machines that speak
  for others' players, and names fit the game's strcpy buffers.

tests/net_session.cpp runs hosts and guests on the loopback (search,
passwords, ordering, migration, host loss, garbage and impostors); it
passes under ThreadSanitizer and AddressSanitizer. docs/NETWORK.md
describes use, design and protocol.

[video] run_in_background keeps the game running without the focus
(default 0, the original's pause). tools/net_local_test.sh starts two
windowed copies with separate user directories to try network play on
one machine.

events.title: Refuse damaged state files before loading anything
events.message:
Refuse damaged state files before loading anything

SaveState() now collects the state in a TMemoryStream and writes it with
a CRC32 at the end. Every write and the close are checked, so a full
disk no longer publishes a cut-off file as complete. LoadState() and
ReadStateCards() read the whole file and check its size and CRC before
they look at the contents. Before, a file cut off inside the flash
section of a debug file overwrote part of the user's flash.

The CRC costs about 8 ms for a fast start file and 24 ms for a debug
file. TMemoryStream is now a TRandomAccessStream with one cursor for
reading and writing, so the round trip check still knows where each
section starts. File version 11.

Found by CodeRabbit and Greptile in PR #225.

events.title: Refuse a state file that was saved with a different screen size
events.message:
Refuse a state file that was saved with a different screen size

TScreenManager::TransferState() loaded the saved screen size and then
copied that many pixels into a buffer allocated for the current size.
After making the screen smaller, the next fast start wrote past the
buffer. The screen size, full screen and landscape mode are
configuration: they are no longer saved, and the screen size is part
of the identity block, so a mismatch boots normally. File version 10.

Found by Greptile in PR #225.

events.title: perf(launch): read a disk image file once per launch (SQ-1762)
events.message:
perf(launch): read a disk image file once per launch (SQ-1762)

Every step of a launch did its own std::fs::read of the image: the story
step, the artwork/sound step, the native-font step (twice), the picker's
scan and the machine-detection fallback. Over a network share the 354 MB
Masterpieces CD made each of those a minute.

blorb::image is now the one door an image file is read through. open()
returns a DiskFile (path, detected format, bytes) from a small cache keyed
on (path, length, mtime), so an image edited between scan and launch is
read afresh; a non-disk file is remembered as a negative with no bytes.
hints, assets, native_font, system_fonts, interpreter and cli-host's
disk_set/storage all go through it.

image_read_once pins the count (12 whole-file reads for the synthetic
launch with the cache off, 1 with it) and scans app/cli-host for an
fs::read feeding a mount or sniff, which a count cannot see.

Completes: SQ-1762

events.title: Amiga port: the text pages
events.message:
Amiga port: the text pages

A port of the demo's own 68000 code, as the web port's textpage.ts, on a
copy of the ST's RAM ($12000-$25B00): the 4 bands, the text-spreader and
the channel analysers, with Enigma going on. What changes is the display:
- the Timer B chain becomes a Copper list rebuilt in the frame it shows
  (the Copper waits for line 45 before reading the rasters);
- the drawing routines compute Amiga addresses; a letter on the last byte
  of a line wraps to the start of the next one, as on the ST;
- the analysers use bitplane 0 only (on the ST, bitplanes 0 and 3, colours
  1 and 8 being equal): the CPU draws a band's first line, the blitter
  copies it down;
- the spreader erases only what it drew 2 VBLs ago, as the ST does.
A VBL takes at most 190 of the frame's 313 lines; the STE colours'
conversion and the lines' offsets are precomputed.

The music's tick records what the analysers read (row read, note or
instrument, effect, volume). compare.py also compares with the web port's
rendered frames: the text pages are identical to them, analysers included,
over the first 6,000 VBLs and around the raster script's first loop.

events.message:
dos: locks are real FileLocks; file system port; DosList at boot - v0.11.47

- A lock is now a BPTR to a struct FileLock in a table the ROM hands the
  host (EMU_CALL_DOS_LOCK_TABLES): fl_Key (the object), fl_Access,
  fl_Task (the file system port) and fl_Volume (a DLT_VOLUME node named
  like NameFromLock()'s volume, the same node the DosList holds) are
  filled in, as on AmigaOS 3.1 (probe dos/lockfields).  Modula-2
  programs read the volume name through fl_Volume: Fish calendarfactory,
  AmigaPunt, Pennywise (CHK) and SafeBoot (bus error) now run

events.title: Implement exec.library's SetFunction (#122)
events.message:
Implement exec.library's SetFunction (#122)

* Implement exec.library's SetFunction

Jump-table patching was previously deliberately out of scope on the
assumption it needed a "call back into guest code" primitive this
runtime didn't have. That assumption doesn't hold for SetFunction:
installing a hook just needs the entry to become a real JMP abs.l to
guest code, which the m68k backend already executes natively, same as
MakeLibrary's own loaded-library vectors.

The "old function" returned for a never-before-patched LVO is a
synthesized stub (a verbatim copy of the entry's previous bytes) rather
than a bare sentinel, so a guest hook chaining through to default
behavior -- the common real-world SetFunction idiom -- works, not just
a bare patch/restore pair.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Ca9VZPFNnpZiis2hWsZcsH

* docs: clarify SetFunction patches don't persist across invocations

Simon pointed out the docs didn't make clear that a SetFunction patch
is purely in-memory for the single guest run that installed it -- no
persistence across separate volamos invocations, and no shared
system-wide library state the way real AmigaOS's one shared
exec.library instance provides. Real SetFunction's classic uses
(Enforcer, SnoopDos, a resident debugger) depend on exactly that
system-wide persistence, which this one-guest-process-per-invocation
runtime has no equivalent of -- so it's only useful for testing a
program's own hooking logic against itself.

The WD1793 with a disc that turns in guest cycles (wd1793.c), the

events.title: ppc: Pass the RunPPC arguments in a0 on WarpOS
events.message:
ppc: Pass the RunPPC arguments in a0 on WarpOS

Since 0.12.0, xSysInfo hangs on startup on CyberStorm PPC and
BlizzardPPC systems running WarpOS, right after detecting the CPU.

warpos_info() bound a0 to the PPCArgs block before calling memset()
on it. A local register variable is only guaranteed at the asm
statement, and GCC never loaded a0 before the RunPPC call. RunPPC
read whatever memset() left in a0 and never returned.

Fill the arguments first and bind a0 and a6 in a separate helper
that does only the library call.

events.title: Identify the printer-server status enquiry (ANFS)
events.message:
Identify the printer-server status enquiry (ANFS)

The eight bytes "PRINT " &01 &00 are the data of the printer-server
status enquiry: the printer name padded to six characters, reason
code 1 (status request) and a reserved zero byte (RISC OS PRM,
"Printer server protocol interface"). *PS and *POLLPS overwrite the
name with the printer type given and broadcast the block on port &9F.

In every ANFS version:
- reverse_ps_name_to_tx becomes build_ps_enquiry. It was described
  as copying the name "in reversed byte order"; the push-then-pop
  copy fills downwards, so the bytes keep their order. Its banner now
  describes the broadcast control block it builds.
- The header template is control &80, port &9F, station and network
  &FF (broadcast), not "port &D1" and a "function-code stub".
- The receive blocks that reinit_ps_slot sets up are open (&7F) on
  the reply port &9E; the comments called these a slot status and a
  "control byte (PS-init pattern)" or a "workspace page".

The *HELP "On" entry in 4.24-4.26 was confirmed in B-Em on 4.25: bare
*HELP lists On, Net and Utils, and *HELP ON does nothing.

Fixes #58

events.title: Rewrite flash driver: two-bank journal with integrity
events.message:
Rewrite flash driver: two-bank journal with integrity

Replace the old append-only flash save with a robust two-bank journal across templates (base/cavegen/platformer/racer). Main changes: dynamic cart-size detection, bank offsets, SAVE_SIZE power-of-two support, CRC16+sequence+commit byte journal layout, never-erase-current-bank policy, BIOS VECT_FLASHWRITE usage, interrupts masked (di/ei) during flash ops, and updated ASM primitives for erase/write. New/changed API: ngpc_flash_ready, ngpc_flash_cart_size, ngpc_flash_load_legacy, ngpc_flash_slots_used, ngpc_flash_erase, and modified ngpc_flash_save/verify/load. Also: ngpc_sys adds a VBlank hook, fixes language/pad/power constants, fixes RGB widening, Makefile Python null-device detection, and autrun uses SAVE_SIZE buffers.

Fish mass-run fixes: VBR in fast RAM, misc.resource, foreign vectors, ILLEGAL, GetCC, math CCR, BltBitMap cost - v0.11.33

All reference-verified with new probes (tests/probes, .ref.out from AmigaOS 3.1):
- exec: the exception vectors live in fast RAM (VBR moved, as on the 68040
  reference); the table at 0 stays filled, user vectors 66..255 point into
  ROM (exec/superstate, exec/vectors).  Fish 60or80 wrote a window title
  at NULL+32 and broke Supervisor()
- exec: misc.resource (AllocMiscResource d0/a1, FreeMiscResource) - Fish
  voice.library (exec/miscres)
- exec: library init, Open/Close/Expunge and device Open/Close/BeginIO/
  AbortIO vectors are called with every register saved (midi.library's
  Manx init, voice.library's Open left A5 changed) (exec/initregs)
- exec: InitSemaphore() keeps D0/D1/A1 (bsh.library) (exec/preserveregs)
- exec: GetCC() uses move ccr (move sr is privileged on 68010+; Fish CanDo
  decks) (exec/getcc)
- an ILLEGAL that is no emulator call takes the illegal-instruction
  exception instead of ending the emulator silently (Fish Scrambler);
  other illegal opcodes no longer reach the emulator-call dispatcher
  (exec/illegal)
- mathffp SPCmp returns the compare's condition codes; IEEESPTst/IEEEDPTst
  set X from the sign (Manx C branches on them: Fish Gwin) (math/cmpccr)
- graphics: a BltBitMap() call costs ~205 us + 4 ns/word emulated time as
  on the reference (graphics/blittime); byte-wise host blit path
  (Fish Marble-Slide was an emulator hang)
- WaitForChar() on a handle that is no host file no longer hands a garbage
  fd to FD_SET (host SIGBUS: Fish Xlisp, AmigaFox, Hextract)
- massrun: lxa time budget from program load, running = the program has
  not returned (as WAIT_EXIT), reference retries on harness errors, names

events.title: BUGFIX: CTC 8253 - a counter loaded the written value depending on when the control word came instead of on the phase of its CLK input. Measured on a real MZ-800, the value is loaded by the first complete CLK pulse after the write: written while CLK is HIGH it loads one pulse later than written while CLK is LOW, the time of the control word does not matter. The CTC2 interrupt (clocked by CTC1) therefore came one CTC1 period earlier or later than on the real computer in some programs. Mode 0 now reads 0000h for a whole CLK period after reaching zero (previously FFFFh at once). Mode 3 reads the counter in steps of 2 like the real chip (previously 1); with an odd N the first half period of the output (HIGH) is the longer one, the tone frequency does not change.

events.title: Detect misplaced and mismatched comments in comments check
events.message:
Detect misplaced and mismatched comments in comments check

Add checks for comments that are well-formed but sit on the wrong
line or describe the wrong value:

- mid_item_comment: inline comments keyed to an address inside an
  instruction or data item (read from the driver script), which the
  disassembler attaches to the covering item.
- copied_comment: comments identical to a parent version's comment at
  the same numeric address while the instruction there differs; the
  parent-to-child address map, when available, says where the parent's
  instruction moved to. --no-parents skips the comparison.
- byte_of_address: lo/hi-byte claims whose address doesn't match the
  immediate operand.
- quoted_string_address: a quoted string placed at an address whose
  bytes say something else.
- char_literal_operand: a character-literal immediate described as an
  offset, byte or address.
- branch_phrasing: branch/loop phrasing on a non-branch, or
  load/push/pull phrasing on a branch.
- code_read_as_data: code referenced only by indexed reads, usually a
  table traced as code after an always-taken branch.

Validated against acorn-nfs history: the pre-fix snapshots yield the
known instances (separator table, lo-byte and string-address comments
carried from 3.60, ~100 mid-item and ~85 copied comments), with a
handful of findings on the current tree.

Fixes #24.

events.title: Name the ANFS URD/CSD/library handle setters for what they do
events.message:
Name the ANFS URD/CSD/library handle setters for what they do

fsreply_3_set_csd does set the CSD: it calls the routine that stores
Y in the CSD handle (&0E03, or &C003 on the Master). That routine and
its two siblings were described as station-table searches ("find
station bit 2/3", "set boot option for a station"). They record the
URD, CSD and library handles: each looks for the channel slot on the
current file server already marked with its role bit (2, 3 or 4),
stores the handle there or allocates a new slot, and sets the slot
status to &26, &2A or &32.

In all ANFS versions:
- find_station_bit2/3 and flip_set_station_boot become
  set_urd_handle, set_csd_handle and set_lib_handle (inner labels
  renamed to match), with new banners and comments.
- fsreply_2_copy_handles, fsreply_3_set_csd and fsreply_5_set_lib
  comments describe the three reply bytes as the URD, CSD and library
  handles, not station, network and boot type.

In 4.21-4.26 the HAZEL bytes &C002-&C004 become hazel_fs_urd_handle,
hazel_fs_csd_handle and hazel_fs_lib_handle (were
hazel_fs_saved_station, _context_copy, _prefix_stn). The FS header
copy that substitutes the URD or library handle for the CSD gets
matching comments, and use_lib_station, which substitutes the URD,
becomes use_urd_in_csd_slot.

Fixes #57

events.title: Parse driver annotations with ast for both py8dis and dasmos
events.message:
Parse driver annotations with ast for both py8dis and dasmos

backfill and lint matched annotation calls with line-anchored regexes
that only recognised the py8dis shapes (bare `comment(0x..., inline=True)`,
`label(`, `subroutine(` with the address on the same line). dasmos
drivers call these as `d.comment(..., align=Align.INLINE)` etc. and
usually split `d.subroutine(` across lines, so backfill proposed
nothing and lint checked zero annotations, passing vacuously.

Add fantasm.api.driver_annotations, which walks the driver's AST for
comment/label/subroutine calls (bare or on any receiver) with literal
addresses, and route parse_annotations, extract_annotations and
subroutine-name extraction through it. Syntax errors in a driver now
surface as a usage error instead of an empty result.

Fixes #23.

events.message:
ndskit: the self-test checks the overlay slots again after loading an image

The self-test loads each vector file's memory images with nds_mem_write,
which does not count as the cartridge's data: a slot's resident overlay
stayed the one the previous file had loaded. With two files for two
overlays of one slot whose first functions open with the same
instruction (a 2009 cartridge's overlays 0 and 1, both at 0x020BB360),
the second file's first function ran the first overlay's code and the
file stopped there (1 function, 17 failures in place of 836 functions
and 0 failures). Loading an image now moves the overlay epoch on, as the
cartridge's data does in the runtime, so the slot is checked again.

Found running the 2009 port's whole self-test in one command (before
this change, with the kit as published, the same 17 failures).

events.title: ndskit: lz, the BIOS's Huffman (4- and 8-bit units)
events.message:
ndskit: lz, the BIOS's Huffman (4- and 8-bit units)

The BIOS's HuffUnComp (SWI 0x13) as the BIOS reads it: the tree's size
byte, the tree from its root (each node's low six bits giving its
children's place, bits 7 and 6 marking a leaf), then the bits in 32-bit
words from their top bit down; 4-bit units fill each byte low nibble
first. decompress, probe and --scan know types 0x24 and 0x28.

Checked on a 2010 cartridge whose own archive wraps its members in the
BIOS's formats: all 406 members of type 0x28 decode to their stated
size within their records, and the 38 SDK G2D files among them carry
their own size fields equal to what came out. No 4-bit stream met yet.

events.title: ndskit: discovery of Thumb switches, halfword tables, long bl, guesses refused
events.message:
ndskit: discovery of Thumb switches, halfword tables, long bl, guesses refused

Forms a Thumb-heavy 2010 cartridge (and its newer SDK ARM7) taught:

* switches through tables of halfword offsets right after the jump:
  CodeWarrior's Thumb switch (adds rB, rI, rI; add rB, pc; ldrh; lsls
  and asrs #16; add pc, rB) and a newer SDK ARM7's (add rB, pc, rI, lsl
  #1; ldrh; add pc, pc, rB), the bound from the compare before, through
  `bls ok; b default` or a long `bl default`;
* a Thumb bl used as a long branch, not a call: its target inside the
  function's own span, or a literal pool after it (past one mov r8, r8).
  It is walked as a b; the emitter writes it as a goto or a tail call
  (the runtime would otherwise stop at "returned to ..., expected ...");
* Thumb's return through a popped low register (pop {r3}; add sp, #k;
  bx r3), and a call through a conditional `movne lr, pc; bxne r12`;
* add pc, pc, rI, lsl #3: a jump into unrolled code, any instruction of
  the run;
* an entry guessed from a pointer, a prologue or a crossing whose
  descent meets data once the rest is known is refused and the
  discovery done again without it: a call or a pointer meant for
  another overlay, at the same address or at another base over it.

Checked by discovery on the five cartridges, both CPUs, overlays
included (the lists before and after diffed): Moon's and Nostalgia's
unchanged, the 2010 one with 366 overlays unchanged in its ARM9 and 23
functions more in its ARM7 (37 halfword switches); the 2008 Thumb one
103, 1 143, 628 and 66 functions more in its program and its three
overlays; the new cartridge 163 switches (118 before), its ARM7 39 (2),
0 conflicts but in its encrypted overlay. Every function no longer
listed is a long bl's target inside its own function or another
overlay's function refused as above. 0 conflicts everywhere else.

events.title: Fix two mis-decodes and a class of misplaced comments; fill 4.21 comments
events.message:
Fix two mis-decodes and a class of misplaced comments; fill 4.21 comments

Mis-decodes:
- ANFS 4.21-4.26: a stray d.entry on the last byte of read_osbyte_table
  (the mode 7 entry, &7C) decoded it as JMP (&4898,X), swallowing the
  TYA / PHA that start cmd_cdir; the description explained this as a
  never-executed jump. Declare the byte as data, drop the bogus label
  and index base, and fix the description.
- NFS 3.40: labels at &8096 and &F086 hid JSR parse_decimal / BEQ in
  the station-number parse, decoding "20 86 F0" as a JSR into the MOS.

Misplaced comments:
- Comments copied by numeric address from the parent version onto
  different code (63 in 4.21 and inherited by 4.24-4.26, 8 in 4.18,
  4 in 3.35D, 2 in 3.65): replaced with the comment of the truly
  corresponding parent instruction, found with fantasm addresses map.
- Inline comments keyed to an address inside an instruction or data
  item, so they attached to the wrong line (3.34B decimal printing,
  leftovers inside strings and word tables): moved or removed.
- fsreply_4_notify_exec in 3.34 and 3.34B was commented for different
  code; describe the load-and-execute sequence (Tube reason 4, start
  execution, also corrected in 3.40-3.65) and rename
  net_handle_validate to exec_at_load_addr.

Coverage: fill 4.21's uncommented instructions from 4.24/4.25 by the
same mapping, and the remainder by hand; 4.21 is now at 100%.

Refs #53

events.title: fix(#63): a bounded runtime_session_run advances when no UI is attached
events.message:
fix(#63): a bounded runtime_session_run advances when no UI is attached

The daemon reported streamPump while no A/V client kept the pump thread
alive, so the capped live run was accepted and never advanced. runCapped
now spots a run that has not moved in 300 ms, pauses, restores the pace and

events.title: fix(#59, #60): a payload counts for the file it is stored in; data segments satisfy an annotate region
events.message:
fix(#59, #60): a payload counts for the file it is stored in; data segments satisfy an annotate region

S12 measured a file only against ranges under its own stem, so a payload's
segments (keyed under the payload's owner) never reached it: 0 %. Payloads
recorded as stored in a counted file now add their ranges (unioned when they
sit at the file's addresses), and a payload is a measurable scope target.
The annotate check took routines and tables only; named data segments
(charset, music_data, sprite, text, bitmap ...) count now.

events.title: ci: publish the site only for tags on a release branch
events.message:
ci: publish the site only for tags on a release branch

Releases are now cut only from the vN maintenance branches, and main is
never released from: the next major version gets its own branch when it is
ready for a beta. The Browser demo and Docs site HTML workflows still
published copperline.dev for any v* tag, so a stray or test tag on main
would have replaced the live browser demo and manual.

Both workflows gain a release-branch job that runs first on a tag push and
checks whether the tagged commit is on an origin/vN branch. Only then does
the publish job run; otherwise it is skipped with a notice and the site is
left alone. The release-asset workflows are unchanged, and a manual
workflow_dispatch run still publishes whatever ref it is run on.

RELEASE.md says nothing is released from main, that the release commit
must reach v1 before its tag, and how to point the site back at one line
when two release branches are live.

events.title: Explain R3 status bit 7 in the type 6 block-write loop
events.message:
Explain R3 status bit 7 in the type 6 block-write loop

On the parasite side, bit 7 of R3 status is the NMI-request flag:
set when R3 holds a byte from the host or when the host has emptied
R3. During a P-to-H block write only the second case arises, so the
loop is waiting for the host to take the previous byte, not for a
host-sent pacing byte. Per the Tube ULA logic in ReTuLaReMake tube.v
(nmi_flag = hp3_dav | ph3_sav) and b-em's tube.c.

Fixes #1

live job. The next command now waits a short time for such answers, and
until one that has begun is whole, before it drops what is left over.

events.title: ci: maintain a v1 branch beside main
events.message:
ci: maintain a v1 branch beside main

Copperline now keeps two long-lived branches: main, the default branch and
the development line for new features and compatibility breaks, and v1,
the 1.x maintenance branch cut after 1.0.0. Fixes land on v1 and reach
main by merging v1 forward.

- Every push-triggered workflow that filtered on main also runs on v1, so
  maintenance commits get the same CI, packaging and lockfile checks. Pull
  request triggers already have no branch filter. Only main keeps saving
  Rust caches; v1 restores the default branch's.
- Dependabot gains a cargo block targeting v1 that opens one grouped PR of
  patch updates and ignores minor and major series. Security updates still
  go to main only, which is how Dependabot works.
- RELEASE.md gains a Branches section: the forward-merge rule and the
  cherry-pick -x exception, what may and may not land on v1, how to resolve
  forward merges (version line, metainfo, formula, golden renders), how to
  release from v1, and that release tags from either branch publish the
  website.
- CONTRIBUTING.md and AGENTS.md say which branch a change should target.

feat(field): a field kit for a dev container, the prerelease channel and version-aware refusals (D33, M13.2)

The field kit in test/field/kit/ runs from a git clone of the release tag
and imports nothing from src/. install.ts installs the package through npx
(@next by default, or a tarball), copies the c64-field-debug skill and the
prompts in, and writes C64RT_TRACE and the host token into
.claude/settings.local.json, whose env Claude Code gives to the MCP server
and every Bash command. bundle.ts packs the run in the container;
report.ts here merges it with the host's trace, measures the clock
difference and writes summary.md. setup.ts is the one-machine route.

A version with a hyphen publishes under the dist-tag next, and install
declares the MCP server from the channel of its own version. Every trace
starts with the running version, and an installed skill's package.json
names it. A handshake refusal names the older side and how to update it.

events.title: docs: correct the Kickstart range and the IPF cell-density limit
events.message:
docs: correct the Kickstart range and the IPF cell-density limit

The README said Copperline supports Kickstart 1.3 through 3.1, while the
getting-started guide said 1.x through 3.2 plus the CDTV and CD32
extended ROMs. The guide is right: the A1000 boots Kickstart 1.1 from
its bootstrap ROM, 1.2 boots, and the copperhf and IDE integration tests
run against Kickstart 3.2. The README now gives the same range.

The IPF section of the configuration guide still said tracks recorded
with a variable cell rate (the Copylock, Speedlock and Brierley density
models) are decoded with uniform 2 us cells. Since the DSKBYTR and IPF
density work, src/ipf.rs models all seven of those profiles and the
drive replays each cell at its mastered rate; only a density model the
decoder does not know falls back to uniform cells, with a warning at
load time. Describe that instead.

events.title: grm-cqwn: follow inline split-pointer dispatches the decompiler declines
events.message:
grm-cqwn: follow inline split-pointer dispatches the decompiler declines

wizwarr's NMI state dispatch (b18c LDX $03 / LDA $b19b,X / STA $66 /
LDA $b19c,X / STA $67 / b198 JMP ($0066)) was never followed: the decompiler
fails it ("Too many branches", then treats the jump as a call) because
JumpBasic::findSmallestNormal refuses a 1-byte switch variable's 256-value
range unless a LOAD is common to every address byte -- and a split pointer
has one LOAD per byte. With no recovered table there was nothing for
JumpTableBound to bound, so grm-fxtp's bank-0 code stayed unreached.

SplitDispatchTableAnalyzer (grm-3er5) now also matches the inline form, where
the four instructions fall straight into the JMP (P), when that JMP carries no
computed reference and no 'switch' label. The table walk gains the
lowest-target stop: a table cannot overlap a handler above it, even one not
yet disassembled (b19b's 19 entries end exactly at entry 15's b1c1).

Eight corpus sites fire; every table was hand-decoded from the ROM bytes.
Re-blessed wizwarr (bankComments 14 -> 59, all fxtp lines back), megaman
and rcransom (newly reached banked handler code; pure additions).

events.title: native32: run a module's original code among lifted ones, and bisect it (#57)
events.message:
native32: run a module's original code among lifted ones, and bisect it (#57)

* native32: run one module's original code among lifted ones

native32_set_native(base) makes a mapped module's code executable again and
sends every call into it from lifted code through the native bridge; its own
calls out still reach lifted code through the callback trampoline. A title
built from several modules can then bisect a lift bug by module: if the
output is right with module X native, the bug is in X's lift. Gunman's
runtime had this as --native; Unreal Tournament's renderer needed it.

Opt-in: nothing changes unless a host calls it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* native32: run chosen functions of a native module lifted

native32_lift_in_native(vas, n) patches each entry with ud2; the trap goes
through the callback trampoline to the lifted body, and lookups of those
addresses find it. With native32_set_native, a lift bug found in one module
can be bisected down to a function: run the module's original code with half
its functions lifted, and halve whichever half shows the bug.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* native32: code in a guest module's data section runs natively

A call into a module outside its code sections is code kept in data, where
old hand-written asm patches its own constants: Unreal Tournament's Fire.dll
runs its procedural-texture loops from .data. No static lift can hold that,
and it was written for this CPU, so it goes through the native bridge and
the section is made executable the first time it is called into.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: native32: guest C++ exceptions for lifted x86-32 code (eh32) (#53)
events.message:
native32: guest C++ exceptions for lifted x86-32 code (eh32) (#53)

* native32: guest C++ exceptions for lifted x86-32 code (eh32)

A guest throw reached the host's _CxxThrowException, whose SEH walk knows
nothing of the guest's frames, so a throw the guest catches one frame up
killed the process. Unreal Tournament's UObject::StaticLoadObject catches its
own 'can't resolve package name' on a normal path; UCC died there before
printing its banner.

x86 MSVC describes its frames on the stack, so the dispatch reads only guest
data: the fs:[0] chain, each C++ frame's FuncInfo (from its handler stub), its
state at record+8 and ebp at record+12. _CxxThrowException is a native32
built-in: it finds the matching catch by type name, runs the unwind funclets
and the catch funclet as guest code, and longjmps into the catching function
at the address the catch returned. The lifter gives every function that
installs a frame with catch blocks a setjmp landing pad (RECOMP_EH_ENTER) and
labels its resume points in the local dispatch (tools/lift/eh32.py,
generate.lift_function_linear eh_resume=). A throw nothing catches still goes
to the real _CxxThrowException.

Opt-in at lift time (a driver passes eh_resume); the runtime built-in is
default, and a title whose lift has no pads behaves as before except that an
uncatchable throw is reported the same way.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Changelog: eh32

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* eh32: compile as part of native32.c

So a host that lists native32.c in its build gets the built-in
_CxxThrowException without adding eh32.c (ra2, gunman and The Movies would
otherwise fail to link).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: name_lift: readable names and a header on every lifted function (#63)
events.message:
name_lift: readable names and a header on every lifted function (#63)

* name_lift: readable names and a header on every lifted function

A lift names every function by its address and leaves its constants as
numbers. tools/lift/name_lift.py rewrites a finished lift in place with what
the binary says about each function: RTTI's classes and vtable slots (COM's
by name), MSVC's deleting destructors and operator delete by their shape,
constructors and destructors by the vtables they store, and debug messages
that name their function. Each function gets a header (strings, Windows
calls, source file, this class, callers), and a constant that is a string's
or a vtable's address gets a comment. Only the lift's own sub_XXXXXXXX
identifiers change, so the dispatch table follows.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* name_lift: name the Windows calls made through the import table

MSVC calls an import as call [__imp_X], which the lift writes as
RECOMP_ICALL(MEM32(slot)): the slot is now named in the line's comment and
in the function's header (calls Windows: ...), from the PE's import table.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: lift32: ordering jccs after or/xor test the result, as after test (#58)
events.message:
lift32: ordering jccs after or/xor test the result, as after test (#58)

or and xor capture their result in both flag slots, so the TEST_* macros
are exact for them, but they fell through to the CMP_* pairing:
`xor eax, [b]; jge` became CMP_GE(r, r), always true. The lifter carried a
note that this was approximate. Unreal Tournament's clipper decides whether
an edge crosses a plane by xor-ing two float sign words and `jge`, never saw
one cross, and drew clipped polygons as stretched shards; bisected to the
function with native32_set_native / native32_lift_in_native.

difftest: four cases, the xor one fails before this change; 206/206.

events.title: disasm32: a data pointer to a padded start inside a body is an entry (#54)
events.message:
disasm32: a data pointer to a padded start inside a body is an entry (#54)

The data scan skips a pointer that lands on an instruction another body
already decoded, as a label. When the body ran past a call that never
returns, through nop padding, into the next function, that skips a real
entry: UT's UWeb.dll has a static constructor named only by its _initterm
table, behind 'call <throw>; nop x12', and loading the DLL faulted on it.
A target that is 16-aligned right after nop/int3 padding is taken as an
entry; interior labels are not padded, so they are unaffected.

events.title: native32: the bridge survives a callee that breaks the C ABI (#59)
events.message:
native32: the bridge survives a callee that breaks the C ABI (#59)

The bridge kept its esp anchor in ebx and its locals behind the compiler's
base register (ebp, or esi under clang-cl), trusting the callee to preserve
both. Windows does; the guest's own hand-written asm, run natively because
no lift can hold it, need not: Unreal Tournament's Fire.dll texture loops
return with ebx and ebp changed, and the bridge then rebuilt esp from
garbage and faulted inside itself, with no report. ebp, esi and ebx are now
saved on the stack and the anchor kept in the thread's TEB
(ArbitraryUserPointer), restored in order so nested bridges unwind.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: sp00nznet

events.title: native32: _ftol, _CI* and _controlfp on the lifted FPU stack (#56)
events.message:
native32: _ftol, _CI* and _controlfp on the lifted FPU stack (#56)

* native32: built-in _ftol and _CI* that work on the lifted FPU stack

msvcrt's _ftol and the _CI intrinsics (_CIpow, _CIfmod, _CIsqrt...) take
their arguments on the x87 stack. native32's bridge passes stack arguments
only, and lifted code keeps its FPU stack in g_st, so a guest that links
msvcrt.dll dynamically ran these natively on whatever the real FPU held:
every float-to-integer cast returned the integer indefinite. Unreal
Tournament's clock (FTime, double * 2^32 to int64) stuck at
0x8000000000000000 and its intro camera barely moved.

They are now native32 built-ins: operands popped from g_st, the result
pushed back or returned in edx:eax. x87crt.c is #included at the end of
native32.c, so hosts that list native32.c in their build need no change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* native32: _controlfp and _control87 reach the lifted control word

Run natively, they set the real FPU's control word, but lifted fistp and
frndint round by g_fpu_cw, which stayed at the default. Unreal sets its
rounding and precision this way at startup; its renderer, lifted, drew
overlapping and stretched polygons, and ran clean with Render.dll's original
code (native32_set_native). The real call still runs (native code uses the
hardware word), then the word it left is copied into g_fpu_cw.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: image_loader: map a section's file data to its page, not its VirtualSize (#51)
events.message:
image_loader: map a section's file data to its page, not its VirtualSize (#51)

Windows maps a section's raw data up to VirtualSize rounded up to the
page; the bytes past VirtualSize in the last page come from the file.
The loader cut the copy at VirtualSize. Tiberian Sun's Game.exe keeps a
patch's code there (0x006C9A10, past .text's 0x006C9A0D), and under
--original it ran as zeroes (`add [eax], al`) and faulted on the
skirmish screen. With the copy to the page, the shipping code reaches a
skirmish under the host as the lift does.
