events.title: win32hle: DirectDraw, DirectSound, Bink, a window manager — Tiberian Sun and Red Alert 2 run natively on Linux (#62)
events.message:
win32hle: DirectDraw, DirectSound, Bink, a window manager — Tiberian Sun and Red Alert 2 run natively on Linux (#62)

* win32hle: WinMain bring-up -- window, threads, WINMM, data paths

Driven by running a lifted Fury3 under the permissive host and implementing
each import it reached on the way through WinMain.

user32: the window-setup and RECT surface a GUI WinMain needs -- FindWindowA
(single-instance), Load Icon/Cursor/Image/Bitmap/Accelerators/Menu (non-NULL
handles; a NULL accelerator table is fatal to some games), GetSystemMetrics,
client/window rect + Adjust*, Begin/EndPaint, MessageBoxA, focus/z-order, and
the *Rect helpers.

winmm (new): multimedia timers, no joystick, and a silent waveOut that retires
every buffer at once so a mixer thread keeps cycling without a sound card;
MCI stubbed.

kernel32_crt: CreateThread runs the lifted start routine on a pthread via
hle_call_guest (each guest thread already gets its own stack + TIB); guest
threads interleave cooperatively, yielding the machine lock in blocking shims
(Sleep now yields, WaitForSingleObject).

kernel32_ext: CreateFileA translates '\' to '/', and GetModuleFileNameA /
GetCurrentDirectoryA return the real image path (hle_set_module_path) so a
title finds its data relative to the exe. HLE_FILETRACE=1 logs opens.

With these a lifted Fury3 runs its whole CRT and WinMain on Linux -- window
creation, its worker thread, timing -- into its own asset loader (which then
wants its .POD data manifest: game packaging, not a runtime gap). 10/10
selftests green under gcc -m32.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* win32hle: DirectDraw, DirectSound, a window manager and the rest of Win32 a DirectDraw game needs on Linux

Driven by Tiberian Sun (tiberiansun-recomp src/linux), which on this boots,
plays its movies and music, runs its menus and the Win32 dialogs behind
them, and plays a skirmish on Linux with no Windows and no Wine.

- ddraw.c: DirectDraw in software; screen.c: the primary in an SDL2 window,
  SDL input as window messages
- dsound.c: DirectSound on SDL2 audio, a software mixer
- user32.c: windows, the queue with WM_PAINT/WM_TIMER, focus and capture,
  dialogs from templates, the standard controls with owner-draw
- gdidc.c: DCs on surfaces, fonts on SDL2_ttf, TextOutA
- module.c, hle_path.c: LoadLibraryA and resources; Windows paths on a
  case-sensitive disk
- kernel32*.c: files on descriptors, find, sized heap, virtual memory, sync
  objects, TLS, locale; ole32.c, advapi32.c, wsock32.c, winmm.c timers
- host_lite.c: the machine lock hands over with the registers saved (a
  nested unlock let another thread's registers into this one's code)
- recomp_types.h: __rdtsc from x86intrin.h off MSVC

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* win32hle: structured storage, IPX over UDP, cross-thread SendMessage, a fair hand-back

- storage.c: StgCreateDocfile/StgOpenStorage, IStorage, IStream,
  OleSaveToStream/OleLoadFromStream on compound files in Windows' format
  (MS-CFB v3, mini stream for small streams); storage_selftest round-trips
  one, and olefile reads it strictly
- wsock32.c: IPX sockets as IPXEmu carries them on UDP (socket number = port,
  the node's first four bytes = the IPv4 address), so a native game and a
  Windows one with IPXEmu share a LAN; HLE_NETTRACE logs datagrams
- user32.c: SendMessage to another thread's window runs on that thread, the
  sender waiting, as on Windows; a mode change resizes a window that covered
  the screen; hle_queue_dump
- host_lite.c: hle_block_end lets a waiting thread take the machine first (a
  polled wait took it straight back and starved a timer callback holding a
  game mutex)
- ddraw.c: the last Release of the DirectDraw object returns 0;
  hle_dd_surface_pixels; screen.c: scalings (sharp, smooth, CRT, nearest,
  integer), blurred bars, F11/F12, a host's 2x picture

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* win32hle: Bink on ffmpeg, and the calls Red Alert 2 adds

bink.c answers binkw32.dll with ffmpeg (HLE_WITH_FFMPEG): a movie opened by
name or from the game's own file handle, frames converted into the game's
surface, the soundtrack through a dsound.c host stream. With MulDiv,
FormatMessageA, OpenEventA, GetLogicalDriveStringsA, GetTempFileNameA,
ChildWindowFromPointEx, GetSysColor, IMM32 no-ops and EnumProtocolsA,
Red Alert 2 and Yuri's Revenge run natively. Invalidating a window without
WS_CLIPCHILDREN now repaints its children, as on Windows.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* win32hle: room for 512 guest COM classes

Yuri's Revenge registers more than 64 class factories (its saved classes
and locomotors), and the ones past 64 were dropped without a word: the Ship
locomotor among them, so the first Soviet mission threw on load. An
overflow now says so.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* win32hle: SIGINT and SIGTERM end the process

SDL turns them into SDL_QUIT, which the host gives the game as a close, and
a game at its main menu closes a dialog and carries on: timeout, kill and
Ctrl+C did not stop it. SDL_HINT_NO_SIGNAL_HANDLERS before each SDL init.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* win32hle: the guest's own cursor where its host says the game does not draw one

LoadCursorA builds a cursor from the guest's resources (RT_GROUP_CURSOR, a
32x32 monochrome RT_CURSOR) and SetCursor records it. screen.c shows it, or
the system arrow, while hle_screen_cursor_hook says so: Red Alert 2's menus
are Win32 dialogs that use the Windows cursor, and had none on Linux. With
no hook the window keeps no cursor, for a game that draws its own.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* win32hle: an overlay for mods; host keys and the window title

hle_set_overlay(base, overlay) lays a folder over the game's: a file under
base is read from overlay when it has one, writes to files under base go to
overlay (a file opened to change in place is copied there first), and
FindFirstFileA lists both, the overlay's first. Directories stay the game's,
so a game that sets its working directory to its own folder keeps it.
kernel32_ext_selftest checks it, relative names included.

screen.c: hle_screen_key_hook lets a host keep a key for itself (a mod
switch), and hle_screen_title names what is playing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: player: restore Framing and Autocrop, and declare the macOS 14.2 floor
events.message:
player: restore Framing and Autocrop, and declare the macOS 14.2 floor

The standalone player writes its menu settings to settings.toml and its
startup layers that file back over the game's manifest. Two settings did
not survive the round trip: the Framing choice (display.overscan) was
written but merge_player_settings never read it back, and Autocrop was
read back but never written. Both now persist like the rest of the
player's Video Settings.

The settings fragment is now built by App::player_prefs, separate from
the file write, so a test can check that every field the player writes
comes back through the merge.

tools/publish declared LSMinimumSystemVersion 11.0 for player bundles,
but the player links the same Core Audio host as the full app, which
strongly imports AudioHardwareCreateProcessTap (macOS 14.2). Declare
14.2 to match packaging/macos/Info.plist.in, so older systems refuse to
open a bundle instead of crashing at launch. The publishing guide says
so and lists the player's Framing and native screenshot button rows.

source_language: Atari hardware and TOS software behavior
project.status: active
project.notes: Core Atari ST/STE/TT/Falcon emulator with a built-in debugger, conditional breakpoints, disassembly, symbol support, CPU/DSP profiling and remote-control facilities. project.status: active
project.notes: Clean-room Dungeon Master-family engine using authenticated original media. Current primary documentation records bounded startup/runtime coverage for DM1 on DOS, Atari ST, Amiga and FM Towns; CSB on Amiga, Atari ST and FM Towns; and DM2 on DOS, Amiga, FM Towns and Macintosh. The latest receipts correct DM1 Amiga HD and DM2 FM Towns boot assertions and expand the cross-game startup matrix and diagnostics. These source-owned handoffs do not establish full campaign, save, display or audio parity; Nexus and Theron's Quest remain explicitly bounded, with authentic level/campaign consumers still incomplete. events.title: Project metadata updated
events.message: notes: Clean-room Dungeon Master-family engine. DM1 PC/DOS 3.4 remains playable/source-locked. v3.0.373 publishes x86-64 and arm64 host packages, verifies the authentic DM1 Amiga 2.0 F0437 title regions, RGB4 palette stages and 18 source-derived zoom steps, and the subsequent 17ce8dc change admits authentic CSB Amiga 3.3 media through the native title/menu/runtime startup path. Those bounded receipts do not establish full Amiga campaign parity. A separate isolated DM1 Amiga 2.0 M12 run still lacks first-Hall validation, while the native macOS DM2 capture reaches New/Resume/Quit without establishing physical-M5 testing, dungeon presentation, audio parity or complete gameplay. Subsequent Theron's Quest work corrects the authenticated HuC6280 bank-$1f initializer call target, aligns the bounded C decoder with the retail final-byte lookahead boundary, and hardens stale transition-queue rejection. execution_paths.name: Native Java/Swing remake
execution_paths.notes: Native Java/Swing source-level reimplementation informed by ReDMCSB C routines and original DAT formats. No guest CPU runtime is identified; successful unit tests are not complete-game playability evidence. GitHub Actions run 37373594209 completed successfully with mvn -B verify at reviewed main SHA 536961e22dbda1fb8f8a08c266ffb83dbd76c7d6, supporting compilable=true from remote CI. README documents actual exploration/controls and tested PC data, supporting upstream-reported runnable output. CI skips real-DAT tests when assets are absent; it does not establish a complete playthrough, so playable stays unknown.

project.status: Substantial Java/Swing implementation through Sprint 27; successful upstream Maven CI, no independent gameplay verification.
project.notes: Substantial Java/Swing source reimplements original Dungeon Master data loading, rendering and gameplay, including a concrete endgame state machine; Maven build and current-head successful CI are verifiable. Requires user-supplied DUNGEON.DAT; original game assets are excluded. GRAPHICS.DAT must be PC version, otherwise placeholder art is used. Atari ST and Amiga dungeon format support is documented but only uncompressed PC data is reported tested. CI skips real-DAT tests when data files are absent; successful synthetic tests do not establish complete gameplay or fidelity. No repository license file was present in the inspected tree; source availability is verified, unrestricted reuse is not. GitHub Actions run 37373594209 completed successfully with mvn -B verify at reviewed main SHA 536961e22dbda1fb8f8a08c266ffb83dbd76c7d6, supporting compilable=true from remote CI. README documents actual exploration/controls and tested PC data, supporting upstream-reported runnable output. CI skips real-DAT tests when assets are absent; it does not establish a complete playthrough, so playable stays unknown. Independent non-fork Java implementation. README and Endgame.java explicitly credit/port ReDMCSB routines; CLAUDE.md and spell commit additionally identify ScummVM as a cross-check. No independent compilation, installation, execution, playtest or original-program binary comparison was performed in this catalogue review. Evidence: https://github.com/kswkev/dungeon-master-claude/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/kswkev/dungeon-master-claude/blob/main/src/main/java/dm/Main.java https://github.com/kswkev/dungeon-master-claude/blob/main/src/main/java/dm/model/Endgame.java https://github.com/kswkev/dungeon-master-claude/blob/main/src/main/java/dm/model/Party.java https://github.com/kswkev/dungeon-master-claude/blob/main/pom.xml https://github.com/kswkev/dungeon-master-claude/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml https://github.com/kswkev/dungeon-master-claude/actions/runs/37373594209 https://github.com/kswkev/dungeon-master-claude/commit/536961e22dbda1fb8f8a08c266ffb83dbd76c7d6 Sprint 27 adds map rendering for wall buttons and traversed illusionary walls, click-selected active champions, a party-direction compass, item transit through opening teleporters/pits, and hidden walls that remain solid until opened. These upstream feature claims do not change the existing unknown complete-playthrough state. Evidence: https://github.com/kswkev/dungeon-master-claude/commit/eb7b199de0d8 https://github.com/kswkev/dungeon-master-claude/commit/5f9e3a49ff4a

runtime_profiles.os: Node.js 22 or newer; TRX64 0.12.9; user-supplied Commodore ROMs
runtime_profiles.notes: No minimum host CPU or RAM is stated.

project.status: active; pins TRX64 0.12.9 and can drive a C64 Ultimate through a shared bridge daemon
project.notes: C64 forensic and semantic-disassembly workbench. The Node.js 22+ application verifies reconstructed assembly with byte diffs and now pins TRX64 0.12.9 with user-supplied ROMs. The current changes use execution breakpoints for reachability claims, prevent duplicate equate definitions in relocated listings, preserve byte-identical rebuilds, and scope negative knowledge claims to their owning evidence coverage. A separately running C64 Ultimate bridge exposes the TRX64 wire protocol to multiple clients; hardware execution remains gated on a successful emulator run of the same bytes. Evidence: https://github.com/Jondalar/C64ReverseEngineeringMCP/commit/669c1346e4ec https://github.com/Jondalar/C64ReverseEngineeringMCP/commit/74fe38185ca5 https://github.com/Jondalar/C64ReverseEngineeringMCP/commit/cbfcadbf92b3 https://github.com/Jondalar/C64ReverseEngineeringMCP/commit/f68fe3d28d92

events.title: feat(jaggd): GameDrive SD-card file API against a host folder (#783)
events.message:
feat(jaggd): GameDrive SD-card file API against a host folder (#783)

The GameDrive's file/dir functions were stubs returning -1, so software
that keeps its data on the SD card (JagOS 'Spot', streamed assets,
screenshots) could not run. Blob functions 9-16, 20-23 and 26 now work
against <save dir>/jaggd-sd (system dir fallback), per the new core
option virtualjaguar_jgd_sd (Read/write default, Read-only, Disabled).

- Call path: each of those blob slots is one backdoor write, $C000 |
  function. The core services the call during that write: it reads the
  68K's d0/d1/a0/a1 and leaves the result in d0 via m68k_set_reg. Safe
  because the 68K's JERRY writes are synchronous and the stub's
  move.w #imm,abs.l never touches d0; only a 68K writer triggers it.
  Paths and buffers move through JaguarRead/WriteByte, bounds-checked.
- src/core/jaggd_fs.c: FatFs semantics, matching RetroHQ's published
  gdbios.h (facts only, none of their files vendored): FA_* open
  dispositions, write/create needs a writable card, short reads succeed,
  FILINFO records big-endian (22/278 bytes). End of directory returns -1
  with a zeroed record. Sandbox: .., drive letters, FAT-invalid chars
  and symlinks refused; components matched case-insensitively.
- Savestate v17 (first bump of the v3.8.0 cycle): trailing "JGF1" chunk
  with card-relative path, access and position per handle. Restore
  reopens with the original access only (never create/truncate/append),
  re-seeks a handle already open on the same file, closes deleted ones.
- Blob grows 208 -> 338 bytes (limit 510).

Tests: test_jgd's probe now drives the file API through the real blob
(size 7 and the read buffer are values only the host can produce;
sandbox escape returns -1); new host test test_jaggd_fs covers every
disposition, read-only cards, sandbox refusals, FILINFO layout,
directories, the handle limit and savestate restore.

events.title: cookies, cache: times held at January 2038 in a 32-bit long
events.message:
cookies, cache: times held at January 2038 in a 32-bit long

On the 68030 a long is 32 bits. Expires dates were clamped at 2100,
which is past 2^31 seconds, and now + Max-Age (cookies) or max-age
(cache) could wrap too: far-future cookies (consent, "remember me")
came out expired and were dropped. Dates after 2037 are now
COOKIE_TIME_MAX, before 1970 the past, and cookie_time_add saturates.

events.title: feat(titledb): key Jaguar CD titles by boot-stub CRC (#747)
events.message:
feat(titledb): key Jaguar CD titles by boot-stub CRC (#747)

CD titles could carry no per-title row: the DB was cartridge-CRC only.
Disc rows now live in their own table, keyed by the CRC32 of the boot
stub CDIntfExtractBootStub() returns. The issue proposed the
sessions/tracks/sectors layout instead; measured across all 53 corpus
images it is neither stable (CDI rips report +150 sectors against the
CUE/CHD of the same pressing in 11 of 12 pairs) nor unique (eight
homebrew discs share 2/6/18044). The stub CRC is identical across CUE,
CHD and CDI for every title whose stub extracts, and separates Vid Grid
from Vid Grid Rev 1. Its limits are documented: seven homebrew discs
share one loader, Songbird re-releases share the original's stub, and
discs with no extractable stub have no key.

- Separate table, so a cart CRC can never match a disc row or the
  reverse; 0 is never a key in either lookup. TitleDBContentCRC() stays
  cartridge-only, so texture dump/replace paths are unchanged for CD.
- The disc is probed (open, extract, close) before the option reads on
  the load path, so a disc row has a cart row's full reach, including
  cd_boot_mode and load-latched options. A disk-control insert re-keys
  and re-reads options before resolving the boot; a failed insert
  restores the previous disc's key.
- Every CD load logs its boot-stub CRC so row authors can read the key
  off the RetroArch log. The table ships empty.

Tests: test_titledb disc-table integrity and namespace isolation;
test_pertitle_db 15/16 (a synthetic disc row on Baldies' key resolves
the real-BIOS strategy; a non-matching key leaves HLE) and 17 (CUE, CHD
and CDI rips of Baldies all log $82B88060); test_disk_control 9/10 (the
same row applies on an insert after a no-content boot; control without
it). Case 15 fails with the probe removed.

events.message:
Hard disk: restored images were ejected at once (#11, #12)

The eject at a firmware restart (#10) used main_reset_m2m_i, but the M2M

events.title: grm-ze06.4: one BitField(lsb, width) replaces FieldSpec/StateField/2x FieldPos positions
events.message:
grm-ze06.4: one BitField(lsb, width) replaces FieldSpec/StateField/2x FieldPos positions

Four records carried a bit-field's position, and two of them spelled mask()
differently: DescriptorSupport.StateField.mask() was the UNPOSITIONED width
mask (callers wrote mask() << lsb), while FieldSpec and both strategies'
private FieldPos records meant the POSITIONED one. BitField has no mask() at
all -- only widthMask() and positionedMask() -- plus extract/place/deposit
(int and long) and MechanismState extract/deposit/forget/valueIfFullyKnown.

- FieldSpec is now (name, BitField pos), with a (name, lsb, width)
  convenience constructor and delegating accessors; it also absorbs
  StateField, so the loader side (DescriptorSupport, NesRomLoader) and the
  analysis side share one named-field record. Its long valueIn overload
  serves the loader's long packed state (MapCompiler caps that at 31 bits, so
  int and long agree bit for bit).
- SelectData/SerialShift: FieldPos deleted; their setFieldFromByte,
  setUnknownField and fieldValueIfFullyKnown copies became BitField.deposit,
  forget and valueIfFullyKnown (each identical bit for bit).
- Inline extract/deposit shifts in BankMirrors.fieldPinnedToVerified,
  BankAnnotationAdapter.impossibleInEveryReachableLayout,
  BankDataflowEngine.clampToResidence, DescriptorSupport (x3), NesRomLoader
  applyMode and both strategies' mirroredByte now go through BitField.
  applyMode's deposit additionally clips the mode to the field width; the
  only shipped mode_mask (MMC3 0x40 >>> 6 into 1-bit prg_mode) always fits.
- BitFieldTest pins both masks and the extract/deposit round trip.

Pure refactor: build-and-test.sh check SUITE OK, no bless; ab-test.sh
--dirty HEAD --all: 32/34 byte-identical; shenlong (97 vs 113) and
dragonpower (168 vs 152) differ only in the documented symbol-count flap,
each side drawing the low state once, in opposite directions.

events.title: M12: performance, corpus and soak (#12)
events.message:
M12: performance, corpus and soak (#12)

* M12: the corpus run

tools/fetch-corpus.sh fetches TOSEC's Oric-1 and Atmos set of 2012-04-23
from the Internet Archive, checked by SHA-1, into out/corpus: 1,061
titles, those in parts as a directory of their files under their own
names, and 221 disc images for M14.

oric-corpus loads each title on the guest harness with CLOAD"", served
as tapeio serves the card, starts a last file that did not autorun, and
counts every undocumented opcode by replaying the field that trapped it,
with the instructions before the first. -N and -B measure two proposed
changes to tapeio: CLOAD's name as it is before NAME.tap, and a tape's
last file one byte short. tools/corpus-run.sh runs the set on the Atmos
and the Oric-1, 48K, and corpus-summary.py writes the report.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* M12: the soak program and its check

tools/soak.bas draws a text page with serial attributes and a hires one,
plays the AY's three channels with noise and an envelope, and prints
"C<count> K<key>" from KEY$ after each page. test_soak types it into the
Atmos 48K as soak.sh will, a line at a time, and requires the count to
rise, H and J to be read, hires to be drawn and the AY written; a
misspelt line, the control, must show no count.

soak.sh and soak-check.py, copied from pico-ace with the Oric's program
and heartbeat: undocumented opcodes zero, AY writes in every heartbeat,
and no park or card change once the program runs. A three-minute trial
on the board passes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* M12: tapes from the archive load as they are

From the corpus run, at the owner's choice: CLOAD's name chooses a file
on the card as it is before NAME.tap, so a title in parts finds its next
part, CLOAD"GAME.TA1" or "GAME2.TAP", as the emulators its tapes were
made for served it; and a tape's last file one byte short loads, the
last address keeping the byte it holds (oric_tape_load_keep), as
Oricutron allows. 83 of TOSEC's 1,061 tapes end one byte short. Titles
that load on one machine or the other: 879 before, 980 now.

test_tape loads a file one byte short on all four machines: kept, the
ROM's own load ends with every byte but the last and the last address
unchanged; not kept, the control, the ROM waits. With the keep planted
out, it fails on all four. oric-corpus now serves as tapeio does.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* M12: the record, and the corpus in the design

design.md: §5.1 the stable undocumented opcodes not implemented, on the
corpus's evidence and the owner's decision; §10.3 the two tape rules;
§3.4 the tape buffer's floor, the archive's largest file; §14 the
workloads at tier 2 against tier 0 and the trap compiled out, on the
Oric-1 16K; §16, §17 and §19 to match. milestones.md: M12's record,
the soak passed on the board, the owner's check of the archive tapes
outstanding.

* M12: the owner's check on a Pico 2 W

Ubuntu's GCC found that a long CLOAD name could cut the message short

events.title: net: build asynchronous frames 2 bytes into their TX slot
events.message:
net: build asynchronous frames 2 bytes into their TX slot

The TX window slots are longword aligned, so the IP header that follows
the 14-byte Ethernet header lands 2 mod 4 and the stack's CopyFromBuff
writes the whole payload to a misaligned Zorro address. Firmware that
reports ETH_RX_META (0xA6) bit 13 accepts ETH_TX bit 14 (OFFSET2): the
frame starts 2 bytes into its slot, putting the IP header on a longword
(zz9000-firmware "shifted TX slots with per-frame checksum consent").

With the asynchronous path and that bit present, every frame is built at
slot+2 and submitted with OFFSET2. Placement alone does not change the
bytes sent. The firmware's checksum-consent bit (ETH_TX bit 13) is never
set: SANA-II has no way for an opener to ask for checksum insertion, so
every frame goes exactly as written. Firmware without bit 13 of
ETH_RX_META keeps the unshifted asynchronous send.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: tinic

events.title: net: send through the four TX window slots asynchronously
events.message:
net: send through the four TX window slots asynchronously

On firmware with the asynchronous send path (ETH_TX bit 15, ETH_TX_STATUS
0x68 bit 15 present; zz9000-firmware "asynchronous transmit with an
in-order completion count"), each CMD_WRITE is copied into the next of
the four 2 KB TX window slots and submitted without holding the Zorro
bus until the GEM has sent. A slot is reused only after the firmware's
in-order retired count has passed it; refused submissions retire in
order too. With all four in flight the writer polls 0x68, bounded, then
fails the write with S2ERR_NO_RESOURCES. Firmware that reads 0 at 0x68
keeps today's synchronous send unchanged.

The slot bookkeeping is tx.c, without Amiga headers; net/tests/tx_test.c
covers firmware without the path, in-order reuse, a full ring after four
slots, refusals behind and without DMA-owned frames, a DMA restart and
the wrap of the 15-bit count. The bounded wait itself is in device.c.

A3000 (68060/50), ZZ9000, iperf TCP send: 1.3 -> 11.7 Mbit/s.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: net: keep _00RomTag in GCC 10+ builds
events.message:
net: keep _00RomTag in GCC 10+ builds

_00RomTag is a static const that nothing references by name, so GCC 10
and later discard it. The device then carries no RTC_MATCHWORD, exec
finds no resident tag when it loads the file, and every OpenDevice()
fails: AmiNetXDuo reports ENXIO, "unit 0 did not open". Mark it used.

Checked with bebbo's m68k-amigaos-gcc: without the attribute the built
ZZ9000Net.device contains no 0x4AFC match word, with it one. The CI
image's compiler happens to keep the tag, so release builds were not

events.title: net: run frame_proc at priority 10
events.message:
net: run frame_proc at priority 10

frame_proc ran at priority 0, so it got the CPU only when every task
above it was idle, and a TCP stack's own tasks sit above it: the card's
RX backlog never emptied and every frame waited for the stack. At 10 it
drains the window as frames arrive.

the 14-byte header once (three longwords and a word) and take the filter
input and the type from that copy.

events.title: net: receive with RX offset 2 when the firmware offers it
events.message:
net: receive with RX offset 2 when the firmware offers it

The payload behind the 14-byte Ethernet header sits 2 mod 4 in the RX
window, so the staging copy out of the window starts misaligned.

Firmware that reports ZZNET_ETH_CONFIG_CAP_RX_OFFSET2 (bit 2 of the
ETH_CONFIG read) can place received frames 2 bytes further into the
slot (the zz9000-firmware RX offset 2 change). The framer asks for that when it starts
(write 0x1000|1) and hands the default layout back when it stops. Each
frame written that way carries ZZNET_RX_LEN_OFFSET2 in its length word;
zznet_rx_next() masks it out of the size and reports it, and the framer
reads that frame 2 bytes later. A frame queued before the switch keeps
its own layout. Firmware without the capability is never asked and never
sets the flag.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: tinic

events.title: net: read the RX header serial first on Zorro II
events.message:
net: read the RX header serial first on Zorro II

The presented slot header (size:16, serial:16) is fetched with one
longword read. On Zorro III that is one bus cycle. Zorro II splits it into
two word cycles, size first, so a frame the firmware publishes between
them reads as the empty slot's size 0 beside the new frame's serial.
zznet_rx_next() then drops it as a torn header and acks it: the frame is
consumed unread and counted as BadData.

On Zorro II, read the serial first, as the publication marker. 0 is an
empty slot and the size is not read; any other serial was published
together with its size. Zorro III keeps the single longword read. The
split read is zznet_rx_header_split() in rx.c, so the host suite covers
it: a frame published between the two word reads is lost size first and
delivered serial first.

Firmware that writes the header with byte stores can still tear a single
serial or size word. zz9000-firmware #148 publishes it with one 32-bit
store.

events.message:
Βήμα 96: οι διάδρομοι στο κέντρο, ενωμένοι με τον δακτύλιο

- Ο παίκτης, σε μια εικόνα του 95: «οι διάδρομοι δεν είναι κεντραρισμένοι·
  να σταματάνε στον εξωτερικό κύκλο, όχι στο εσωτερικό». Και στην πρώτη
  εκδοχή: «να μπαίνουν 1 pixel πιο μέσα». Τα δύο πρώτα ήταν κανόνες της
  τέχνης (assets/SPRITES.md §8, §10): το conn_points έχει την αριστερή στήλη
  μιας κάθετης πόρτας και την πάνω γραμμή μιας οριζόντιας ακριβώς στον άξονα
  του θόλου, άρα ο διάδρομος έπεφτε 1 byte δεξιά ή 4 γραμμές κάτω, και οι
  πόρτες (conn_*) ζωγραφίζονταν πάνω από τον δακτύλιο ως τον εσωτερικό κύκλο.
- Οι αξονικοί πάνε μισό πλάτος πίσω (corr_dir, oc_bend) και είναι στο κέντρο
  ως το pixel. Οι διάδρομοι ζωγραφίζονται πριν από τα κελύφη, και οι πόρτες
  έφυγαν: ob_conns, ob_conn_scan, τα οκτώ sprites (256 bytes).
- Οι αρμοί (src/joint.asm): το βήμα 3 του θόλου, πάνω από το κέλυφος, σε κάθε
  κατεύθυνση με διάδρομο. Το κενό της διαγωνίου (το tile DIAG_K-1 όσο
  φαίνεται), και τα pixels του εξωτερικού περιγράμματος του δακτυλίου που
  ακουμπούν το γκρι του διαδρόμου, γκρι. 2 pixels στον κάθετο, 6 στον
  οριζόντιο, 14/41/5 στη διαγώνιο S/M/L. Εννέα σχέδια με μάσκα στην τράπεζα 5
  (328 bytes) από το tools/pack.py (joint_px, build/joint_tab.asm)· τα νότια
  είναι τα βόρεια με κάθετο καθρέφτισμα, τα ανατολικά δικά τους (το flip_mode0

events.title: grm-wiwv: HelperModel.placement() refuses composed models; window -> BankState.restrictedTo
events.message:
grm-wiwv: HelperModel.placement() refuses composed models; window -> BankState.restrictedTo

Three constructions build a HelperModel with neither a strategy nor an argReg,
all at lsb 0: findHelpers' degraded multi-mechanism union, composeTailCalls'
composed exit effect, and findSecondTierHelpers' wrapper (the wrapped helper's
real effectMask, but lsb still 0). On nes-mmc5 / nes-modetest that lsb would
mis-shift any conversion. placement() now throws IllegalStateException for
such a model. A model with an argReg but no strategy still answers: HAR's
no-strategy fallback is real, and JUnit fixtures exercise it.

The throw found one real caller, introduced by grm-ze06.3 (8d1265f): the

events.title: ndskit: discovery across overlays
events.message:
ndskit: discovery across overlays

Running a 2009 cartridge into its battles met code that one overlay
reaches only through another: the battle's overlay calling the field's
and the menus' (a direct call, a veneer, a vtable whose class inherits
methods held in an overlay of the other slot).

* The recompiler discovers each overlay again with the targets other
  overlays' runs found in its area, their calls and the pointers in
  their data and literal pools; such a foreign target is taken only
  where its descent is clean and it starts as a function would (a
  prologue or a boundary).
* A run with an overlay loaded knows the areas of the overlays it
  cannot see: a table neighbour pointing there counts, a veneer jumping
  there is one.
* A function ends at any unconditional transfer that is not a call (a
  veneer's bx r12), and a literal pool of up to four words after it,
  each word loaded by the code just before, is a boundary; a prologue
  after such a pool is a function.

Checked on four cartridges, both CPUs: 0 conflicts, no function lost or
split (a first, looser prologue rule split Moon's variadic functions and
its movie decoder and was dropped); Moon's ARM9 unchanged, a 2009
cartridge's program 101 functions more, all opening with a prologue. The
cartridge then played through three battles and its prologue in a
window, 20 068 frames, without a stop.

that a shadow skips its own polygon ID is not followed yet.

A fatal stop writes the backup memory too: the player's save is not the
fault's.

Checked on a 2009 cartridge: its pre-battle transition (a capture) and
its dungeon's shadows as the user saw them on melonDS; its first dungeon

events.message:
Angels lunge, the player always runs, and a locked-in per-level benchmark

Angel lunge (ANGSLIDE, builds with an idol): while the idol is carried an
angel slides into its next cell in world space over the last 24 sixtieths
before its 2 s beat, landing exactly when it used to teleport. It owns both
cells for the slide and switches cell halfway. angOne is split into
angPick/anGo so the lunge can decide early and commit on the beat.

Death scene fixes: a watched death now turns to centre the angel
(steer by its projection side at hand speed), no angel moves once the
scene starts, and the marking angel holds the cell it caught you on.

The player always runs (3 cells/s, 127 deg/s). The walk was barely twice
an angel's pace and nothing rewarded it; SHIFT is now free. The scaling
lives in tickDelta, so the benchmark movers move at play speed too.

fpsr.mjs "" suite is the benchmark: for every level, a spin and a shuttle
run (out the clear distance, back, repeat) from the same pose, timed by
the build itself (MOVEAT/MOVEFOR/MOVELEGS, maS) because probe's reads land
~12 ticks late. It exits 1 on a bump or a failed build, so it doubles as
a functionality check. Level 2 and 7 run from poses of the rig's own.

Deleted: the scripted tours (TOURW, ROUTE, RECORD, TOURPOSE, PROFTOUR,
FRAMELOG) and their route compiler, seamprof.mjs, flog.mjs and fpsr's
old level-1 segments. Shipping disks byte-identical across the deletion.

compact.mjs now says when it cannot place a cluster instead of skipping
it silently; pvN and ocos are declared not page-aligned. Tool test disks
go to build/ so the only disk at the top level is lest-c64.d64.

events.title: Βήμα 95: η μεταφορά
events.message:
Βήμα 95: η μεταφορά

- Ως τώρα ο κύκλος ροής έβαζε το μετάλλευμα κάθε ορυχείου κατευθείαν στα
  αποθέματα, και η Haul υπήρχε μόνο στους πίνακες. Τώρα, όπως αποφάσισε ο
  παίκτης: ό,τι σκάβεται μένει στο ορυχείο, σε σωρό ως 30 (το όγδοο byte της
  δομής, ST_OWED). Γεμάτος σωρός σημαίνει ότι το ορυχείο δεν βγάζει τίποτα.
  Με σωρό από 10 και πάνω δημοσιεύεται μία Haul (το bit 6 του ST_OPS). Εργάτες
  και ρομπότ μεταφοράς κουβαλούν 10 τη φορά στην κοντινότερη αποθήκη σε
  λειτουργία, αλλιώς στο σκάφος, με το sp_take της τροφοδοσίας. Στον
  προορισμό +10 μετάλλευμα με το ec_make, άρα μετρά για την Ανεξαρτησία.
- Δύο σκέλη στην ίδια εργασία (src/haul.asm, hl_arrive). Ο σωρός γεμίζει στο
  ίδιο το σάρωμα του κύκλου (hl_pile), με το ρεύμα του τελευταίου
  ισοζυγίου, όπως οι μηχανές της θέσης 11. Η πρώτη εκδοχή ξανάψαχνε τον
  πίνακα μετά το ισοζύγιο: ~400 us με ορυχείο στη θέση 31. Ενα φορτίο που
  έμεινε στη μέση το παραδίδει ο επόμενος, γιατί το μάζεμα δεν γυρίζει το
  J_NODE της Haul. Χωρίς προορισμό που φτάνεται, παραδίδεται στο ορυχείο.
- Δικές μου αποφάσεις: η Haul στην προτεραιότητα 5, πάνω από τη Drill (4).
  Με το 2 του πίνακα, λίγοι εργάτες θα έσκαβαν όλοι και ο σωρός θα
  σταματούσε για πάντα στα 30.
- Χρόνοι: κύκλος ροής χωρίς ορυχεία 1.577 -> 1.472 us, με τρία 1.941 ->
  1.834 (3.841 -> 3.799 ο πρώτος), ίδιος και με τα ορυχεία στις τελευταίες
  θέσεις. Το ld de,STRUCT_REC βγήκε από τις άδειες θέσεις. Θέση 13 με Haul:
  322 us στο ορυχείο και 255 στον προορισμό, πάνω από μια επίσκεψη χωρίς
  εργασία.
- Μνήμη: το πάτωμα των δοκιμών #3D60 -> #3E00 (το παιχνίδι δεν γράφει τίποτα
  ως το #3FC0). Ετσι τα probes πήγαν στο #3E00, τα stubs στο #3F00 και η
  σκαλωσιά του test_loop στο #3F80. Τράπεζα 0 401 -> 256 ελεύθερα (64 κάτω
  από το πάτωμα): haul.asm 127, ο πίνακας εργασιών 20. Τράπεζα 2 9 -> 5
  (st_post). b6code 16 -> 25. SV_VER μένει 8.
- tests/test_haul.py (νέο): οι πίνακες, ένας κύκλος με πέντε ορυχεία και
  εργοτάξιο απέναντι στην αναφορά byte προς byte, έξι αφίξεις στη θέση 13,
  μια ολόκληρη αλυσίδα στο παιχνίδι (εργάτης και ρομπότ μεταφοράς ως το
  σκάφος), δύο κόστη, έντεκα αρνητικά. test_drill: ο σωρός αντί για τα
  αποθέματα, ταβάνια κάτω από το 94, και μια ένατη μέτρηση με τα ορυχεία
  στις θέσεις 29-31. test_sim: οι δομές στον γράφο της αποικίας, άρα τα
  ορυχεία φτάνονται. Αυτό έβγαλε ένα λάθος στην άφιξη ορυχείου της
  αναφοράς (tools/econ.py) που ο Z80 δεν είχε, και ο μετεωρίτης ελέγχεται
  ως να ξαναχτιστεί η δομή. test_loop, test_bar, test_place, test_corridor:
  το νέο πάτωμα.

Modern edition: Zarch-style defence game, new renderer, hazards

Rework everything around the ported flight model, which is unchanged

Game

- Volcanoes: three cones stamped into the terrain that rumble, erupt and
  throw lava bombs.
- Wind turbines: five farms whose streams of air drag the ship along;
  tower, nacelle and blades are solid.
- Quit to title from the pause and game-over screens.

Rendering and feel
- Sun and hemisphere lighting with shadows, dusk sky dome, HDR target
  with MSAA, bloom, grade pass and tone mapping.
- Sea with Gerstner waves, breakers, foam and reflections.
- Cloud layer with moving shadows, plus horizon cloud banks.
- Static chunked terrain, instanced scenery, GPU point-sprite particles.
- Chase camera, ground markers, HUD and overlay screens, keyboard
  alternatives for every mouse button, expanded synthesised audio.

events.title: fix(ifdb): ranged requests ask for identity encoding; gzip replies no longer fake a size
events.message:
fix(ifdb): ranged requests ask for identity encoding; gzip replies no longer fake a size

Ranged requests (size probe, preview, remote zip reads) now send
Accept-Encoding: identity, so Content-Range is the file's real size. A host
that gzips anyway yields no size rather than the compressed one. A preview
that over-delivers keeps its first n bytes, and SearchError::TooLarge carries

events.title: fix(#49): monitor stepping is VICE-conform around IRQ/NMI
events.message:
fix(#49): monitor stepping is VICE-conform around IRQ/NMI

VICE (6510core.c DO_INTERRUPT, monitor.c monitor_check_icount / _interrupt): an interrupt
taken at an instruction boundary ends a step-into right after the 7-cycle entry, on the
handler's first opcode; under step-over/return it is a new level like a JSR, runs through
its RTI and the step ends in the interrupted code. TRX64 folded entry + first opcode into
one step (landing on $FF49) and `n` only ran JSRs through.

- core: two one-shot step gates (step_entry_stop, step_prologue_only), off outside a
  monitor step; the delta ring drops the entry of a boundary-only call that ran nothing.
- daemon: one step_boundary primitive (opcode, then the boundary's interrupt check);
  run_through = VICE level counting (JSR/interrupt up, RTS/RTI down) shared by n, ret,
  API stepOver/stepOut. z, sf/nf, until, sd, API stepInto and debug/step use the gated
  step. The FlowTracker gets the entry as its own step; PORT NOTE corrected (it claimed
  the fold was VICE-faithful). BRK stays an opcode, as in VICE.
- tests: tests/step_interrupt_gate.rs (IRQ + NMI step-into, step-over, breakpoint in the
  handler, ret + flow pop).

- Faster: the mission lists, Open mission, Check and the menu dialogs no

  released over them, so a press can be taken back.

  the end. The Template list turns pages and shows the position. Files starts
  at the mission selected in Open. The Resize confirmation names the objects
  and their cells. The game-disk prompt names the install's disk files.

events.title: ndskit: overlays in the recompiler and the runtime
events.message:
ndskit: overlays in the recompiler and the runtime

The recompiler makes one module per overlay besides the program's: each
overlay discovered with the program loaded, its module holding its own
functions and calling the program's directly (emit learnt names of
another module's entries), the program's module holding every function
of its own that an overlay's run found. An overlay's module lists its
code's ranges with their crc32 and each entry's first instruction.

The runtime looks an address in an overlay's load area up in the module
of the overlay resident there: recognised by its code's crc32 (data the
overlay changes once loaded lies outside the ranges), checked again when
the cartridge has delivered data since, or when a dispatched call's
first instruction is not the module's; a change of hands is reported.
Segments now have a kind (program, copied, overlay). The self-test takes
an overlay (--overlay N): its functions with it loaded and the
program's module active, through the same dispatch.

Checked on a 2009 cartridge with 14 overlays: it boots, plays its title,
starts a new game and walks into its first dungeon, the overlays
changing hands three times; 8 361 frames on, 2 112 bytes of main RAM
differ from melonDS's state, the ITCM and the shared WRAM not at all;
its self-test 100 994 vectors with no failure, 8 773 of them an
overlay's.

events.title: ndskit: discovery of C++'s tiny methods
events.message:
ndskit: discovery of C++'s tiny methods

Three forms that hid small functions reached only through data: C++'s
pointers to member functions, records of the function and one or two
small adjustments, whose neighbour is 8 or 12 bytes away; tables of
tiny methods none of which is known yet, whose candidates with a
boundary and a clean descent now count for each other; and a function
that exactly fills a gap (a few instructions to a return, then known
code or a prologue). A word that is the literal pool of a return also
ends a function. Found running a 2009 cartridge, whose new game called
three of them (an empty callback, two methods returning a type's id).

Checked on four cartridges, both CPUs: 0 conflicts; every function
added is a getter, a setter, an empty callback or the SDK's protection
region setters (Moon's ARM9 6 580 to 6 613, its ARM7 943 to 944).

events.title: ndskit: discovery with an overlay loaded, melonds --overlays
events.message:
ndskit: discovery with an overlay loaded, melonds --overlays

discover --overlay N (or all) reads the program with one of its overlays
loaded as a segment of its own, its static initialisers as seeds. Other
overlays share its addresses, so calls and jumps into it from outside
are entries only where their descent is clean. With {id} in --out, one
list per overlay and the program's own functions with those only the
overlays reach. A trial descent that runs into a literal it loads itself
is refused: an odd pointer to a string had passed for a Thumb function.

melonds --overlays names the overlay each load address holds in a state,
by the share of its bytes found there.

Checked on a 2009 cartridge's 14 overlays (0 conflicts, every reachable
function of Ghidra's found) and a 2008 one's 3; without overlays the
four cartridges' discovery is unchanged but for the false entry.

events.title: Port audio, input, network and movie code; the whole game compiles
events.message:
Port audio, input, network and movie code; the whole game compiles

All 69 game TUs build with Clang for 32-bit Linux. The game links except
for the 144 functions of the platform API (gfx, audio, input, net, movie),
whose backends come next.

- src/port/audio.h: DirectSound's buffer model (play, loop, duplicate,
  volume/pan/frequency, ring buffers) and a built-in MS-ADPCM decoder.
  Sound.cpp ported: samples, slots, the streamed music (WAV reader on Sys,
  ADPCM instead of ACM). 3D buffers are plain buffers: the game never
  places them.
- src/port/input.h: DirectInput's model (DIK key codes, joystick objects
  by data-format offset, axis range/dead zone/saturation, force-feedback
  effects). Input.cpp ported; the DirectInput data formats are gone.
- src/port/net.h: DirectPlay 4's session model with its message layouts.
  The network code in Game.cpp, GameInfo.cpp, FrontendScreens.cpp and
  NetPlayers.cpp ported; no DirectPlay dialogs.
- src/port/movie.h: Bink's playback model for our own decoder; the movie
  loop presents through the renderer.
- Remaining Direct3D call sites, vertex buffer locks, friend functions
  declared at namespace scope, MSVC-only conversions fixed.

runtime_profiles.name: Source and upstream runtime evidence

The bootstrap explicitly rejects NMOS machines for ChromaBreak. These are source/author requirements, not independently verified runnable minima.

project.status: Native game collection with bootable outputs and upstream tests; independently unbuilt
project.notes: Identity: The creator’s repository contains eight native Apple II games, including original Arkabreakout/ChromaBreak and ports of POM1 games. Reviewed concrete Arkabreakout gameplay assembly, Snake C implementation, ChromaBreak bootstrap/build, and Chess documentation. This is one repository-level collection record, not eight inflated entries. Classification: Native Apple II source collection and ports. Arkabreakout assembles a standalone BRUN binary and DOS 3.3 disk; ChromaBreak builds a ProDOS system file. The bundled a2run/a2shot emulator code serves tests and is not embedded in the games. LOGO, demos and generic dev tooling are incidental to this game-scoped record. Source CPU: The README and Snake header identify POM1 Apple-1/GEN2 versions as predecessors, and Chess documents reused POM1 rules code. Those predecessor files were not independently inspected, so no source CPU is inferred from the target assembly or Apple-1 label. project.title: papple2
project.display_title: papple2 — Apple II reverse-engineering emulator/debugger
project.status: active
project.notes: papple2 is a small Apple II reverse-engineering emulator/debugger with a completed rebuilt instrumentation layer and an IPython workbench. Its prompt_toolkit listing editor now edits labels, operand targets and comments in place, follows calls, preserves back/forward breadcrumbs, and offers a routine picker; annotations are persisted in the dossier and refreshed between terminal sessions. Lode Runner's byte-identical XekriRedmane reconstruction remains an external grading oracle, never an analysis input. Evidence: https://github.com/fschuhi/papple2/commit/99c38d0aa3838a095e09713058a598a33bb5b672 https://github.com/fschuhi/papple2/commit/71383884923cf04a022948a464fc370b65db02f3 The disassembler now uses observed execution to name operand bytes inside labeled instructions as label+offset, which supports self-modifying-code analysis without treating arbitrary data as instructions; later editor work suppresses holes from the listing. The repository's current education charter explicitly addresses an AI model as a code/documentation collaborator, so development AI is now affirmative but the specific model family remains unstated. Evidence: https://github.com/fschuhi/papple2/commit/2a67d217687c9ca781f13ad100699a6745b9c099 https://github.com/fschuhi/papple2/commit/defb6a8910d0d9d0f00f944fb436298015eb0d0a

events.title: ndskit: the sound in step with memory, the FIFO's read-ahead
events.message:
ndskit: the sound in step with memory, the FIFO's read-ahead

A channel now reads memory as it stands at the channel's own time. The
sound unit used to catch up only at the ARM7's register accesses and at
each frame's end, reading memory the ARM9 had written since: a stream
refilled right behind the play position came out with samples of its
next lap. It now runs after every quantum of the machine (half a
sample), at no measurable cost, and a run stays the same run.

The samples come through a FIFO as the hardware's do: 32 bytes fetched
as a channel starts, 16 more each time it is down to 16. A feeder told a
block is played while its last 3 samples are still to play overwrites
them at once; the hardware has them by then, and so does the runtime.

events.message:
Begin a sleeve's cap ring at the shoulder joint

Begun above the joint it lay inside the shoulder, and the settle pulled

events.title: assets: refresh the bundled AROS ROM to master 949d6834f8
events.message:
assets: refresh the bundled AROS ROM to master 949d6834f8

Rebuilt from upstream master at 949d6834f8 (2026-10-09) with no local
patch and no unmerged pull request. Free memory at a --run program's
start rises by 35,112 bytes on a 1 MB chip-only A500 (758,624 ->
793,736) and on a 2 MB A1200 (1,793,920 -> 1,829,032), and by 31,968 on
the default 512K chip + 512K slow A500, where all of it is slow RAM.

The build links .rom at 523,156 and .ext at 522,678 bytes of the
524,288-byte banks, leaving 1,132 and 1,610 bytes spare. The main bank
overflowed upstream this cycle and lowlevel.library moved to the ext
bank (55d7530cc1), which also gains ramdrive.device (1bcf9a04ae).

Among the upstream changes that reach the ROM:

- the memory gain: m68k system tasks on measured 2 KiB stacks, a guru
  alert buffer allocated only while an alert is shown, 1 KiB file-handle
  buffers on machines without Fast RAM, RunCommand stacks clamped to the
  8 KiB process default, the bootstrap task's 16 KiB stack freed when it
  exits, and the CD boot shell run inside the boot process.
- cia.resource lays CIABase out like Kickstart and dispatches through
  its iv_Code/iv_Data vectors, so a program that patches a CIA interrupt
  vector in place no longer overwrites the resource's jump table.
- exec keeps the scheduler flags in Kickstart's SysFlags bits and calls
  a SetFunction()ed ExitIntr() or Schedule() and a replaced
  ex_LaunchPoint.
- lowlevel.library reads the first CD32 pad button before the first
  clock pulse and reports native mice; timer.device reloads the full
  E-clock period after a timer migration.
- amigavideo, graphics and intuition: classic sprite streams and live
  pointers, interleaved and caller-owned planar bitmaps, raw custom
  screens and user Copper list sizing; dos.library BCPL packet fixes;
  afs-handler hardening.

The timing-test and bltprobe-pace goldens are re-blessed for the new
boot handoff phase, as on every refresh. Five timing-test rows move by
one E-clock tick and row 31 (beam cck across a DIVU loop in a 6-plane
display, bistable on the handoff phase) returns from $1306 to $12D8;
two bltprobe-pace bars shift by a few pixels. The other 43 probes are
pixel-identical. The DAP hello-one-frame cpuprofile golden is re-blessed
too: the program's functions are unchanged and the capture from the
breakpoint to the next video frame boundary is shorter.

The full unit and integration suites pass. Of the asset-gated --ignored
suite only the hardware- and network-gated tests and the two
pre-existing failures (run_flag_boots_and_runs_a_guest_binary,
mhi_m2_savestate_resume) fail, as under the previous ROM.

The M2, M3 and M4 integration tests measure the --audio-wav capture,

events.title: gemdos: set _bootdev to the GEMDOS HD boot drive once TOS has booted
events.message:
gemdos: set _bootdev to the GEMDOS HD boot drive once TOS has booted

Hatari sets _bootdev (0x446) to the boot drive before TOS starts, but a
cold start of TOS 1.04, 1.06, 1.62, 2.06 or 4.04 clears low RAM,
including it, and TOS then sets _bootdev only from its own boot (a
floppy or a hard-disk driver's boot sector), which a GEMDOS HD boot has
neither of. So it stays 0 and programs that build paths from it look on
drive A. TOS 3.06 leaves the variable alone and EmuTOS sets it itself;
with --fast-boot TOS skips the RAM clear and the pre-boot value
survives.

Write it once more from GemDOS_Boot(), after TOS has initialised and
before the AUTO folder runs; later changes (MiNT, drivers) are left
alone.

Measured with a probe in the AUTO folder and on the desktop, booting
from a GEMDOS HD with fast boot off: _bootdev is 2 in both places on all
of these TOS versions. Dgetdrv() in the AUTO folder still returns 0 on
them; that is TOS's own state.

events.title: ndskit: the sound unit, the audio device, WAV files
events.message:
ndskit: the sound unit, the audio device, WAV files

The runtime is heard. The ARM7's sound unit runs a sample at a time at
the DS's 32 728.5 Hz in virtual time: its 16 channels (PCM8, PCM16,
IMA-ADPCM with the loop's saved state, PSG on 8-13, noise on 14-15), the
start delay, loops and one-shot ends, two capture units, and the mixer in
the hardware's integers (volume and divider, panning, SOUNDCNT's outputs,
the master volume, the bias, the speakers). It is run lazily, at each
access to its registers and at each frame's end, so a channel's busy bit
drops when its samples end and a run is the same with or without a
listener.

A window's run plays it through an SDL3 audio stream, its queue held
near three frames by nudging the playback ratio by at most 0.5%; --wav
writes any run's sound to a file, --mute silences the window. The boot
now leaves the speakers on (POWCNT2 = 1), as melonDS's and the real one
do. The BIOS's sine and volume tables are exact against the BIOS's own:
the sine times 32 767, the volume out of 128 with 128 kept as 127 and
127 as 126.

melonds reads the savestates' sound unit: a state's running channels,
and both units' channels side by side in a comparison, from the ARM7's
registers and the channels' places that a run now writes.

that folder. Ported from netfox-website (53491c8, dd2802a), which runs it in
production on 16.3.8. jest.setup.cjs gets netfox's guard, so the script's
test can run in the node environment.

events.title: Rmk234  postscriptstream and font (#2759)
events.message:
Rmk234  postscriptstream and font (#2759)

This reworks the MCCS mappings of Postscriptstream and makes correlated
changes in postscript's outcharfn. It eliminates the hashtable lookup in
favor of getting the mappings from a block associated with particular
charsets. Also tries to avoid unnecessary calls to FONTCREATE, which
showed up as costly in some spy runs. The external format is now UTF-8,
and the MCCS characters in the mapping tables are coded as characters,
not octal code points. So they are easier to interpret in Medley and
also in external editors.

Also includes some performance improvements to FONT, again to address
issues with FONTCREATE and \FONT.CHECKARGS. This optimizes for the
common case of calling (FONTCREATE X) where X is often already a
fontdescriptor and the call is just against the possibility that it can
be a font class or a fontspec that needs some coercion. This now does a
quick check for that case before it gets into the more elaborate
checking in \FONT.CHECKARGS.

I reworked FONTCOPY so that the property detection is separated from the
font creations, also improved how it deals with color (which we don't
really have, but...). I also slightly changed the interpretation of
NOERROR: this suppresses the font-not-found error, but like FONTCREATE
it will still cause an illegal-arg error if one of the specified
properties is not legitimate. E.g. specifying ... XXSIZE 10 will given
an illegal-arg XXSIZE error.

EDITFONT is a minor order-of-arguments change for compatibility with
FONT.

events.title: Setup front door: setup.sh, doctor.sh, start.sh + SETUP.md
events.message:
Setup front door: setup.sh, doctor.sh, start.sh + SETUP.md

- scripts/doctor.sh [68k|os4|all]: checks every prerequisite (Python,
  devbench, Docker + images, FS-UAE + config + Kickstart + system disk +
  serial port, deploy folder + bridge, QEMU + sam460ex, amitools, OS4
  disks + bridge on the dev disk, OSMesa, ports) through devbench's own
  config loader, with the fix for each problem. Changes nothing.
- scripts/setup.sh [68k|os4|all]: installs what can be installed
  (Homebrew/apt), pulls the toolchains, builds OSMesa and both bridges
  (PPC first, 68k last, clean in between: they share amiga-bridge/src),
  deploys them, then runs the doctor. Re-runnable.
- scripts/start.sh [68k|os4|all|status|stop]: devbench per target on fixed
  ports (OS4 :3000, 68k :3001), emulator started through devbench's API,
  waits for the bridge; ~45 s from cold for both.
- make setup / doctor / start / start-68k / start-os4 / stop / status;
  `make devbench` keeps the old single-devbench start.
- SETUP.md: the one-page guide; README and CLAUDE.md point to it.
- amiga-bridge/src/net_io.c: a clean 68k build failed ("unknown type name
  '_sfdc_vararg'"): define it, guarded, before <proto/socket.h>.

events.title: Harness Workbench backdrop window (LXA_WB_WINDOW=1, as LoadWB's on the reference) for suite-ref and mass runs; ExAll no longer writes past small buffers
events.message:
Harness Workbench backdrop window (LXA_WB_WINDOW=1, as LoadWB's on the reference) for suite-ref and mass runs; ExAll no longer writes past small buffers

Fish ISAM opens its window through GetScreenData(WBENCHSCREEN)->FirstWindow
and crashed without one.  The window is opened by a "Workbench" process
before the program starts, is app=false in tree dumps and not counted by
lxa_get_window_count().  Probe intuition/wbwindow from the reference.
ExAll() zeroed the whole ExAllData for every level, overrunning an
ED_NAME buffer (probe dos/exall showed it once the memory layout moved).

events.message:
wasmcart WebGPU: an event-loop turn between every two stepped frames

Asynchronous results (buffer maps, error scopes) now arrive before the next
frame inside one step burst, as in a browser or native player, so one
frame({op:'step', frames:N}) call matches N one-frame calls. cartwheel's
run-cart had stepped WebGPU carts one frame per call for that (thousands of
calls per gate run); it now takes one call. Freeing released Dawn objects
(the reason for the old every-16-frames turn) only gets more frequent.

events.title: fix(rewind): cut the live transcript back instead of rebuilding it
events.message:
fix(rewind): cut the live transcript back instead of rebuilding it

A rewind rebuilt the transcript from per-command records, so text printed
after a "press any key" pause (a game-driven turn records nothing) and every
style run were lost. AppState now carries a transcript rewrite epoch, bumped
whenever the transcript is shortened, an earlier line shifts, or it is
replaced wholesale. Each TurnRecord stamps the transcript length, epoch, the
prompt line's char count and the clear anchors; resume_from_turn cuts the
real transcript back to that mark when the epoch still matches, trimming the
prompt line the next echo had grown, and otherwise falls back to the old
rebuild. Archive-loaded records carry no mark and rebuild.

macOS/clang). Make it a union with a ULONG, as the board buffer
already is, so it is longword aligned like an opener's buffer.

events.title: DOCS FIX: MCP - the memory banking description (emulator://docs/memory_layout) claimed that IORQ OUT does not change the CG-ROM mapping on the MZ-800; in fact OUT (0E0h) unmaps the CG-ROM too (the VRAM stays) and OUT (0E4h) maps it together with the VRAM in MZ-800 mode and unmaps it together with the CG-RAM in MZ-700 mode. The pair IN A,(0E0h) + OUT (0E0h),A therefore gives RAM at 0000h-1FFFh and the VRAM at the same time. The emulator already behaved this way.

Unify Amiga joystick controls and migrate legacy volume-only configuration

Make cd32=OFF use the shared Amiga 1/2/3-button joystick path by default,
removing the separate joy3 enable switch. Keep CD32 selection through
cd32=ON and use the shared joystick path after a successful JOYSTK

events.title: warnings: widen the gate to 19 flags, portably, on compile and link
events.message:
warnings: widen the gate to 19 flags, portably, on compile and link

warnings: widen the gate to 19 flags, portably, on compile and link

The gate had seven flags.  Eleven more cost nothing -- the tree already passed
them -- and three needed code fixed first; the list is now nineteen, with
-Werror on the compile and on the LTO link.

New flags: -Wformat=2 -Wundef -Wvla -Walloc-zero -Wshift-overflow=2 -Wlogical-op
-Wduplicated-cond -Wfloat-equal -Wdouble-promotion -Wpointer-arith
-Wnested-externs -Wshadow -Wswitch-enum -Wduplicated-branches.

The three that needed fixing, and why they were real:

  * -Wshadow, 19 sites.  A local that shadows a nested local, a global, or a
    BUILT-IN function (index, time, ...).  Renames, behaviour-preserving; the
    one in netstack_dns.c was two hits from a single name.
  * -Wswitch-enum, 6 sites.  The flag wants every enumerator named as a case
    even when there is a default, so the option arms that were "covered" by
    default: now say what they mean.
  * -Wduplicated-branches, 2 sites, both a ternary over two macros that are the
    same value -- the two CIA START bits, and the two TTL/HOPS limits.  Each is
    one number behind a _Static_assert that the two names still agree, which is
    what the ternary was silently asserting and the assert now says.

The -Wformat=2 hits were bounded: the four host stand-ins for ami_log() end in
vprintf; the SHIPPING ami_log() is RawDoFmt and deliberately not a printf
(%ld/%lu/%lx/%s only), so the host definitions carry
__attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3))).  That is more checking, not less --
every ami_log() call in those tests now has its arguments checked.

PORTABILITY IS PART OF THE FLAG LIST, NOT AN AFTERTHOUGHT.  Five of the
nineteen are GCC's and clang rejects them outright; under -Werror an unknown -W
is a hard error, so the first push of this branch did not build on the macOS
arm at all.  The list is the INTENT and stays whole: each flag is proved
against the compiler that is configuring, the ones it refuses are dropped BY
NAME, and the configure log names them.  Editing the list down to clang's
subset would hide the difference between "the other arm checks less" and "this
arm checks nothing".  If even -Wall will not probe, the list is used unverified
and says so -- a broken probe must not quietly disarm the gate.  GCC/m68k keeps
all nineteen.

Also here: -Werror on the LTO link (LINK_OPTIONS on the targets, not a global
add_link_options()), and a note beside the list that the intent and the
effective set are different questions.

Verified: all 29 cross arms green; host arm 558/558; a clang host build -- what
the macOS arm configures -- rc=0 with 0 warnings and 0 errors, where before it
stopped in its first translation unit; survey green; derived docs check PASS.

Two things the census missed and CI caught, both worth remembering: option-gated
files (tests/perf/prof/prof.c is compiled only under AMINETXDUO_PROFILER=ON)
are invisible to a default-preset sweep, and a single-compiler sweep cannot
tell you what another compiler does with a flag.

events.title: Βήμα 94: η γεώτρηση, και τα μονοπάτια έξω
events.message:
Βήμα 94: η γεώτρηση, και τα μονοπάτια έξω

- Ως τώρα ένα ορυχείο με ρεύμα έβγαζε 2 μετάλλευμα ανά κύκλο ροής χωρίς
  κανέναν, και η Drill υπήρχε μόνο στους πίνακες. Τώρα, όπως στο Planetbase:
  ως τρεις σε κάθε ορυχείο, εργάτες ή ρομπότ γεώτρησης, και κανείς 0, ένας 2,
  δύο 3, τρεις 4. Οσοι σκάβουν μετριούνται στο ST_OPS (το έβδομο byte της
  δομής): η άφιξη, η αναχώρηση και ο θάνατος περνούν από το νέο op_ptr, που
  κάνει και τους χειριστές του θόλου. Το bit 7 του ίδιου byte λέει ότι η
  Drill του υπάρχει.
- Η Drill δημοσιεύεται στο σάρωμα του κύκλου ροής (dr_post, src/drill.asm),
  μία ανά ορυχείο με λιγότερους από τρεις. Ο κύκλος μετρά τα ορυχεία
  (EC_MINES), και το dr_need (b6code) κάνει ένα νέο ρομπότ γεωτρύπανο όσο
  τα ορυχεία έχουν θέσεις χωρίς γεωτρύπανο· αλλιώς κατασκευής ή μεταφοράς.
- Η ανάθεση έμαθε να προσπερνά: με μία αδιάθετη εργασία έτρεχε το jb_best
  (~1 ms) για κάθε αδρανή, όποιος κι αν ήταν ο ρόλος του, και μια Drill
  που μένει ανοιχτή έκανε τη θέση 13 20-42 ms σχεδόν σε κάθε περιστροφή
  (test_sim: 70 -> 100 frames). Τώρα μια μάσκα ρόλων (jb_open) και ο βρόχος
  των πρακτόρων ξαναγραμμένος: θέση 13 χωρίς ανοιχτή 2.841 -> 2.763 us, με
  Drill ανοιχτή και αδρανείς άλλου ρόλου 6.117 -> 3.555, test_sim 34.944 ->
  32.947 us η περιστροφή.
- Ο παίκτης: «δεν χρειάζεται να σχεδιάζεις βάσεις για τους θόλους· το
  sprite για τις βάσεις χρησιμοποίησέ το για τους εξωτερικούς διαδρόμους».
  Ο θόλος μένει στο έδαφός του (μόνο η κατάληψη), η ζώνη προσγείωσης είναι
  έδαφος (GEN_VERSION 2), η αποικία δοκιμών κι αυτή. Η σύνδεση εδάφους
  ενός airlock και της πρώτης δομής ζωγραφίζεται: ένα Γ θεμελίου, χωρίς
  κατάληψη, μόνο σε ελεύθερο έδαφος που χτίζεται, μετά τους διαδρόμους, και
  ξαναζωγραφίζεται μόνο ό,τι άλλαξε (FIRE 149 -> 152 ms).
- Μνήμη: νέο b1code, 160 bytes στο #7F60 της τράπεζας 1, πάνω από τα
  εικονίδια (src/commit.asm, BANK1.BIN = bank1c.bin): η μισή τοποθέτηση που
  δεν σελιδοποιεί, 120 bytes από την τράπεζα 2. b6code 1.280 -> 1.298.
  Τράπεζα 0 383 -> 401 (49 κάτω από το πάτωμα), κώδικας τράπεζας 2 8 -> 9,
  b6code 16 ελεύθερα, b1code 7. ECON_BYTES 107, SV_VER 8.
- Χρόνοι: κύκλος ροής χωρίς ορυχεία 1.787 -> 1.577 us, με τρία 2.065 ->
  1.941 (3.841 στον κύκλο που δημοσιεύει δύο), θέση 12 χωρίς κύκλο 684,
  θέση 13 2.841 -> 2.763, ξύπνημα ρομπότ 715 -> 733 (918 με ορυχείο).
- tests/test_drill.py: οι πίνακες, ο κύκλος ροής απέναντι στην αναφορά byte
  προς byte, ποιος ξυπνά σε έξι καταστάσεις, μια ολόκληρη αλυσίδα στο
  παιχνίδι (ορυχείο στη φλέβα, εργάτης, ρυθμός ανά κύκλο, στολή, θάνατος,
  γεωτρύπανο), οκτώ ταβάνια κόστους, δεκαέξι αρνητικά. test_reach: ο
  κόσμος μετά το FIRE και πέντε αρνητικά για τα μονοπάτια. test_place,
  test_build, test_newgame: ο θόλος στο έδαφος. test_sim: κάθε ορυχείο με
  έναν, οι δομές σε κάθε φέτα κίνησης. test_save η μορφή 8, test_disc η
  τράπεζα 1.

The two receive-header words are separate Zorro cycles. Reading the length
first let the ARM publish an empty slot in between: length 0 paired with
the new serial, the frame was rejected for size and acknowledged unread.
The serial is the publication marker, so read it first, return empty on
0, then read the length. No extra bus reads.

Host test publishes the slot between the two header reads (plain and
offset 2); the old order fails 10 of its checks. Found by codex
(evidence zz-rx-header-publication-9be6b901).

events.title: M10: tape by trap (#10)
events.message:
M10: tape by trap (#10)

* M10: the tape trap in the core, against the ROMs' own routines

tap.c scans and writes the .tap format. tape.c traps four steps in each
ROM (find a header, read the data, write the header, write the data),
read off both ROMs, and resumes inside the ROM's own loop after its last
byte, so CLOAD's and CSAVE's messages, name compare, re-link and autorun
are the ROM's. The trap stands aside unless the ROM is a stock image by
SHA-1 and its page is ROM.

test_tape holds the trap to the ROM's routines on all four machines:
from a copy at the tape set-up, the ROM alone (save), the ROM with only
its byte routines hooked, and the trap leave the same RAM and registers
at the clean-up, and the same file. Fast and slow, by name past a file
with a long name, nameless, 1.1's verify, an empty deck and a short file.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* M10: the deck on the card, the Tapes page and boot_tape

tapeio serves the trap's requests from .tap files in /oric/tapes/ at a
park: the deck plays on a file at a time, passing over a file found and
not loaded; CLOAD's name chooses a file, or with the deck empty the first
tape whose first header has it; the end of a tape rewinds once. CSAVE
appends the whole file through .new and a rename. The Tapes page (eject,
rewind, new tape, the card's tapes), the deck on the main page and the
status line, and boot_tape and PICO_ORIC_BOOT_TAPE come from pico-ace.
PICO_ORIC_TAPE=OFF compiles the run loop's check out, the control for
its cost.

tools/trace-diff.py tape plays a .tap into Oricutron as a signal, its
traps off, and test_tape --write gives it the trap's own saves.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* M10: the record, §16's tape rows settled, the trap's cost

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* M10: the record's count of planted bugs

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* M10: a CLOAD the deck cannot answer returns to Ready

The owner found CLOAD"BOB", with no BOB on the tape, never stopped: the
deck rewound once and declined, and the ROM waited for a signal, as the
real machine does. Now the second end of the tape, no tape, no card or a
file cut short press the reset button (oric_tape_give_up), the program
kept, and the status line names what was not found. The Tapes page logs
its list, for checks over the UART. Archive tapes run on the board.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* M10 review: names as each ROM stores them; paths that do not fit

Codex's review of PR #10. (1) find_by_header took 16 bytes of a longer
header name as a match for both ROMs; only 1.1 keeps 16, and 1.0, which
keeps the whole name, rejects it, leaving a tape in the deck that cannot
answer. name_is now uses the ROM's own name_cap. test_tape settles the
ROMs' side by execution: CLOAD of 16 characters of a 22-character name
loads in 1.1 and is passed over in 1.0. (2) A file name too long for
ORIC_PATH_MAX was listed and searched under a cut path that opens
nothing; it is now skipped, and the list says so in the log.

events.title: dispatch: call out task-struct corruption when stack bounds read back inverted
events.message:
dispatch: call out task-struct corruption when stack bounds read back inverted

check_stack_bounds reads tc_SPLower/tc_SPUpper fresh from guest memory
on every dispatched trap (deliberately, so it stays StackSwap-aware),
but that trap-boundary granularity has a failure mode the old
diagnostic actively misdescribed: a guest that overflows and keeps
running without making a single library call can push A7 down through
the entire guest heap -- the task struct included -- before the next
trap gives the check a chance to fire. By then the "bounds" it reads
are whatever stack debris landed on the task struct, and the old
message presented that debris as the task's stack bounds and suggested
a larger --stack, a knob that can't help (and whose irrelevance was
already visible in the report: the garbage numbers don't change with
--stack).

Seen in the wild debugging a Rust/LLVM-m68k guest whose panic handler
re-panicked forever while formatting its own panic message (an LLVM
M68k backend miscompile: a CCR-clobbering MOVE between core::fmt's
DECIMAL_PAIRS bounds compare and its Bcc, so every decimal integer
format took the panic_bounds_check path): the recursion was pure
computation, so A7 descended ~16MB with no trap in between, and the
eventual report was "stack bounds [0x21900001, 0x21900000]" --
inverted, lower = upper + 1, actually two misaligned halves of a
(&str pointer, length) pair the recursion had been pushing.

Inverted bounds are recognizable precisely because no runtime code
path ever writes them: Runtime::new's layout arithmetic always yields
lower <= upper, and stack_swap_handler copies a caller-supplied
StackSwapStruct verbatim. So when lower > upper, say what actually
happened -- the task struct was overwritten, the overflow predates
this call, and --stack will not help -- instead of printing debris as
bounds with a misleading suggestion. The well-formed-bounds message is
unchanged.

events.title: fix(#7): colour-register stores follow VICE on every VIC-II
events.message:
fix(#7): colour-register stores follow VICE on every VIC-II

A CPU store to $D020-$D02E now does what vicii-mem.c:270 color_reg_store does on
every chip: regs, last_color_reg, last_color_value, nothing else. The draw takes it
through update_cregs and applies it one draw later (draw_colors_6569 /
draw_colors_8565). Before, the store was also pushed into cregs and the draw
statics (vicii_monitor_colreg_store), a draw cycle early. That path stays for host
pokes (Vic::poke_reg = vicii_poke) on every chip.

What moves: on the 6569/6567/6572 a colour change appears 8 pixels (one VIC cycle)
later; a store in raster_cycle r first shows the new colour at draw-buffer x
(r + 1) * 8 + 1 (was r * 8 + 1). The 8565/8562 change at the same pixel with the
grey dot in front.

Turbo (divider > 1 on the U64): the per-pixel slots are unchanged and still
override the resolve in the first draw; the register behind them follows the same
latch, and the slots start from a value still waiting in it. Device-measured gates
(subpixel_colour_gate, turbo_as_measured_gate, u64_turbo_gate, turbo_fastpath_gate)
pass unchanged.

Re-baselined: only two unit tests of the draw in isolation (vic_draw.rs
eight_border_values_paint_eight_pixels: no dot in the slot draw, row is 1..8;
without_turbo_the_cycle_is_one_colour: the latch is applied in the second draw).
No gate, golden, digest or 7-game result moved. New: c64c_glue_gate
a_colour_store_changes_the_colour_where_vice_puts_it_on_both_chips.

Βήμα 93: ο έμπορος

- Ως τώρα το παιχνίδι δεν είχε καθόλου εμπόριο: το SK_MERCHANT δεν το
  περνούσε κανείς στο ship_call, κανείς δεν έγραφε το EC_TRADED, και το

  της Independence ερχόταν δωρεάν.
- Ο έμπορος έρχεται μόνος του, όπως οι επισκέπτες: τα χαμηλά έντεκα bit του
  r2 ίσα με #5A5 (το μηδέν είναι επισκέπτης), μία φορά στις 1.986
  περιστροφές μετρημένα, 2,65 sol, ποτέ μαζί με άλλη ζαριά. Θέλει πίστα και
  άδειο ουρανό. Στη σειρά 2 «MERCHANT LANDED».
- Φορτίο στην προσγείωση (sm_land, src/ship.asm· land_merchant στην
  αναφορά): τρία bytes από ένα αντίγραφο του EC_RND, που δεν προχωρά.
  Κέρδος 35-65% στα δικά του, τρία ή τέσσερα από τα δεκατρία αγαθά (όχι
  νερό), ένα ως τέσσερα «πακέτα» το καθένα. Τιμές του Planetbase (Bot 120).
  Μένει EC_SOLLEN/32 περιστροφές, μισό sol.
- Η γραμμή του εμπόρου (src/lines.asm, ac_mode 3, M στη ΜΕΤΑΦΟΡΑ, κόκκινο
  χωρίς έμπορο): σειρά 3 το ζύγι, σειρά 4 ένα αγαθό με τις τέσσερις στήλες
  του Planetbase. ΠΑΝΩ παίρνει (ως το φορτίο και το 600), ΚΑΤΩ δίνει (ως όσα
  έχεις και το 99). FIRE/SPACE: δίνεις τουλάχιστον όσο παίρνεις, το
  απόθεμα ξαναελέγχεται, τα αποθέματα αλλάζουν αμέσως, το σερί σπάει, ο
  έμπορος φεύγει, TRADE DONE. Μία ανταλλαγή ανά επίσκεψη, χωρίς

- Η γραμμή του πλοίου δείχνει πια κι αυτή τη ΜΕΤΑΦΟΡΑ με το πλοίο λευκό·

events.title: debug: answer the in-flight command on either death ordering, and surface a pre-handshake death
events.message:
debug: answer the in-flight command on either death ordering, and surface a pre-handshake death

The exit notification and the socket's disconnected are both queued and
which is delivered first is not guaranteed. When finished wins, it
cleared m_haveCurrent without emitting commandFinished, so a caller
waiting on a mid-session crash (the remote-control client's
blockingDebugCommand) sat out its own timeout instead of getting its
answer. Both handlers now fail the in-flight command, so either ordering
answers the caller.

A child that dies before the handshake also surfaces as an error now
(the UI's banner and status bar key on errorOccurred, and the log-only
line was silent); the wording defers to the exit line, which names how
it ended.

Verified with a scripted fork that handshakes, answers, then dies by
signal with a command in flight: the command's completion fires on
either delivery ordering, and the death is named — plus the full
tst_hrdb suite (14/14).

events.title: netdev: ZZ9000 RX offset 2 when the firmware offers it
events.message:
netdev: ZZ9000 RX offset 2 when the firmware offers it

The payload behind the Ethernet header sits 2 mod 4 in the receive
window, the opener's IP header is longword aligned, so the bulk copy
read aligned but wrote 2 mod 4 into Fast RAM (8.5-13 us per 1512-byte
frame on a TF4060). Firmware that advertises RX_META bit 12 can place
frames two bytes further into the slot; zz_init asks for that, and
frames flagged with length bit 15 are read from ZZ_RX_PAD + 2. The
copies now peel a word only when the source is 2 mod 4, so both
layouts stay longword aligned on the Zorro side and the shifted one is
aligned on both sides. Old firmware is unaffected.

events.title: mcp: count HID holds in emulated frames, fix run-state errors
events.message:
mcp: count HID holds in emulated frames, fix run-state errors

  Key and joystick tools (input_send_key, input_send_keys,
  input_send_keys_with_delays, input_send_joystick) waited between press
  and release for the counter of *rendered* frames. At MAX SPEED a frame
  is rendered at most once per 20 ms of real time, and on a still screen
  not at all, so send_key(frames=4) let hundreds of emulated frames pass
  at MAX SPEED and ended on the safety timeout at normal speed (13-15
  frames).

  The whole sequence (key or joystick, hold, gap, landing probe) is now
  handed to the emulator thread (hid_script.c), which presses and
  releases on emulated frame boundaries. A paused emulator plays exactly
  the length of the sequence and pauses again like emu_run(frames=N); a
  running one keeps running. A breakpoint, a pause or a reset cuts the
  sequence short and releases the held key. Replies report emu_frames,
  complete and interrupted. send_keys leaves one released frame between
  keys so repeated keys register twice. The Python wrapper scales its
  request timeout with the sequence length.

  Also:
  - run_until_addr on a running emulator returns an error instead of
    only pausing it away from the target and answering running: true
  - snapshot_load and snapshot_load_buffer name the failure reason
    (e.g. "Emulator is not paused")
  - the temporary breakpoint (Run to cursor, Step over, run_until_addr,
    step_out) is removed on every pause, not only with the debugger
    window open; in headless MCP the next run used to stop on it again
  - fix the send_keys_with_delays example in tools-overview (it used an
    event format the emulator does not accept)

  New e2e test mcp_hid_frames covers exact frame counts at normal and MAX
  SPEED, interruption by a breakpoint and the run-state errors on all
  four binaries.

events.message:
fix(libretro): generate the canonical libretro-core-info entry (#2401)

* fix(libretro): generate the canonical libretro-core-info entry

RetroArch reads supported extensions, firmware and no-game support from
libretro/libretro-core-info, whose amiberry_libretro.info was written by
hand and omits m3u, m3u8, rp9, lzh, chd, zip, 7z and raw, advertises
slave and info files the core does not load, and reports
supports_no_game = false.

Generate amiberry_libretro.info from a template in that repository's
format, filling supported_extensions from retro_get_system_info() and
the version from CMakeLists.txt, so the release artifact is the file to
submit upstream. The CD32 extended ROM is listed as kick40060.CD32.ext,
a name the system-directory ROM scan recognizes; ext40060.CD32 was
never scanned.

Refs #2400

* fix(libretro): mark every listed Kickstart optional in the core info

Each run selects one model, and the core also accepts alternative ROM
names and checksum matches from the system-directory scan, so no single
listed file is required. Marking A500 1.3, A600 2.05 and A1200 3.1
mandatory would make RetroArch report valid setups as missing firmware
and block loading when it checks firmware first.
