events.title: debug: gate the cut-before-handshake message on the child's liveness
events.message:
debug: gate the cut-before-handshake message on the child's liveness

A fork that dies before the handshake has the same shape as a connection
that something cuts — !m_ready, no handshake — and the exit line printed
after the hint contradicted it. The disconnect handler now reaps the exit
notification first and only diagnoses a cut when the child is still alive;
a child that died lets its finished handler name the cause alone. The hint
also no longer prescribes a firewall fix: the listener is loopback-only,
which the macOS application firewall exempts, so the honest wording names
what was observed (a filter closed the accepted connection) and leaves the
remedy to whatever the machine actually runs.

events.title: debug: name a pre-handshake cut instead of calling it a drop
events.message:
debug: name a pre-handshake cut instead of calling it a drop

A field report from a managed Mac showed the debug connection cut before
the handshake with the emulator alive and booting — connect at the TCP
layer succeeds, because the kernel completes it against the fork's
listener before the fork accept()s, and what closed it was something
between the two processes. On macOS that is the application firewall or
an endpoint agent cutting the accepted connection of an unlisted,
ad-hoc-signed binary, which the bundled emulator is. The generic 'remote
debug connection dropped' sent the report down a transport-fault path;
the pre-handshake case now says what it is and what to allow.

main 126B、bank0 65B、bank1 93B、bank2 23B、bank3 27B。
PAINT本体はbank1の0x7C8Cから791B。目安600Bを191B超過しており、
後続GET@/PUT@に向けた容量の制約が残る。mainの追加消費はなく、
測定ROM用116B以上を維持。bank3のコードは変更していない。

作業領域（全てsrc/memmap.pyにEQU）:
- PAINT_WORK: 0xEE4E〜0xEE83、54B。境界・塗り値・区間・走査位置・上下限。
- PAINT_TILE: 0xEEB2〜0xEFB1、256B。タイル文字列の写し。
- 訪問ビット: 16000B（1画素1bit）。固定0x8000〜0x83FFの1024B、
  引数評価終了後の0xE600〜0xEDFFの2048B、HEAP_ENDから12928Bに分割。
  FREE_TOPと16bit加算のあふれを描画前に検査し、不足はERR 7。
  境界上の開始点は確保前に判定して正常終了する。
  数値・文字列・LINE等の一時域を使うのは引数評価終了後だけ。
  終了時に式スタックの位置VAL_SPを0へ戻す。
- 区間スタックを作らず、上下交互の反復走査を使う。再帰なし。
  本体のCALL深さは最大3段、局所退避を含むCPUスタック追加は最大16B
  （割込み退避を除く）。CPUスタックへ動的な区間は積まない。
  訪問した行の範囲とその隣接行だけを走査し、小領域の負担を減らす。

自作判断:
作業域不足はERR 7。仕様11.5の壁破壊異常は再現しない。
タイルの省略境界は前景色。バックグラウンド一致のERR 5は既存担当の
判断（同じ行が3行連続、1行タイルなら1行一致）を維持する。
誤りなしで返す場合の画素は、塗り前の4連結成分の規則に従う。

events.title: input.device: a handler's registers do not reach the event's writer
events.message:
input.device: a handler's registers do not reach the event's writer

On AmigaOS 3.1 input handlers run in input.device's task. lxa calls them
in the task that writes the event (IND_WRITEEVENT), so a handler that
changes a non-scratch register changed the writer's: AMOS's handler
changes d4, which AMOS uses as its event mask after the DoIO() - Fish
WhereK then jumped to 0. Handlers are now called through a stub that
preserves d2-d7/a2-a6.

Probe input/handlerregs (captured on AmigaOS 3.1). Phase 237.

events.message:
Use Ubisoft web login (WebView) instead of email/password fields

Replaces the in-app email/password login dialog with a full-screen WebView
that opens Ubisoft's official login page (connect.ubisoft.com/login). The
user logs in on Ubisoft's own page - the app never sees the password and
two-factor authentication is handled by Ubisoft.

After login the session (ticket + sessionId) is read from the page's
localStorage (PRODloginData) and renewed under the app id via
PUT /v3/profiles/sessions (UbisoftLogin.RenewSessionAsync).

Also fixes:
- WebView now fills the screen (custom top bar with title + cancel)
- Soft input mode AdjustResize so the on-screen keyboard appears
- Case-insensitive JSON deserialization of the captured session

Tested on a physical device: keyboard appears, Ubisoft login works, the
session is captured and the SPAE.PA download + game start succeed.

events.title: Add Ubisoft Connect SPAE.PA download for Android
events.message:
Add Ubisoft Connect SPAE.PA download for Android

Adds a Ubisoft Connect login flow to the Android app that lets users who
own The Settlers 1 History Edition download the copyrighted SPAE.PA data
file directly, instead of picking it via the file picker.

- UbisoftLogin: REST login (email/password, 2FA, remember-me) against
  public-ubiservices.ubi.com
- DemuxClient: TLS/protobuf demux socket to dmx.upc.ubisoft.com
- OwnershipService/DownloadService: ownership check (product 11662) and
  download URL requests
- ManifestParser/SpaeDownloader: manifest download+parse, slice download,
  decompression (zstd/deflate) and SPAE.PA assembly
- Protobuf definitions (UplayDB/Protobufs) generated at build time via
  Grpc.Tools; Google.Protobuf and ZstdSharp.Port added
- MainActivity: data import dialog with file picker or Ubisoft download
  option, login/2FA/progress dialogs
- Network security config allows cleartext HTTP to the Ubisoft CDN
  (manifest/slice URLs are plain http)

Tested on a physical device (Samsung Galaxy A13): login, ownership check,
manifest download and SPAE.PA download all work; the game starts with the
downloaded data.

events.title: Test Drive II 1.6b: Enhanced framerate option, intro car fix
events.message:
Test Drive II 1.6b: Enhanced framerate option, intro car fix

Proposed update to the Test Drive II slave (v1.5 -> 1.6b). All new
behaviour is for duel v1 (108868 bytes) only; v2 keeps the v1.5 patches.

- New option "Enhanced framerate" (CUSTOM2, off by default; the game
  icon gets the tooltype CUSTOM2=1):
  - the game logic runs at a fixed rate, independently of drawing:
    every 6 frames (the original rate) on a 68000, every 2 frames on a
    68020+, so faster machines draw more frames without changing the
    game speed; the race clock follows real time
  - after a crash or engine damage the car recovers in 240 frames with
    a 20 second penalty while the opponent and the clock keep running
    (the original blocked the game logic for a CPU-dependent time)
  - blitter bus priority, unused blitter interrupts suppressed
  - road and cars drawn at fractional positions; steering, lane
    position, mountains and hill crests move smoothly
  Measured in the first race: A500 7.1 fps (6.1 without), A1200
  16.7 fps, 68030/25 MHz 25 fps (the chip-bus limit).
- Always on: fixed the intro cars jumping 16 pixels left for one frame
  (an original bug: DDFSTOP was rewritten too late on the line above
  the car, so its first line fetched an extra word).
- The trainer (CUSTOM1) still works; slave version stays 17 (needs
  WHDLoad 17.2+ for PL_IFCx).

New sources: simulation.s (fixed-time game logic), simulation-patches.i
(its patch list), render.s (rendering), simulation-verify.s (test
fixtures, assembled only with -DVERIFY). Builds with the usual vasm
command; Makefile_windows.mak lists the new files as dependencies.

events.title: FPU: report the 68881/68882 and complete the coprocessor core
events.message:
FPU: report the 68881/68882 and complete the coprocessor core

AmigaOS 3.1 reports AFF_68881|AFF_68882; lxa's CPU core executes the FPU
instruction set but AttnFlags said there was none, so programs compiled
for the FPU took their no-FPU exit (Fish Offender, then a NULL GfxBase
call in its cleanup). With the flags set, the core needed:
- one effective-address calculation for every FPU operand: (xxx).W/.L,
  (d8,An,Xn) and full-extension forms, PC-relative and immediates of all
  sizes (fmove.d (xxx).L took a line-F in MoonTool and SManCP);
- FMOVEM.X with static/dynamic lists, the documented register order and
  all addressing modes; FMOVEM of FPCR/FPSR/FPIAR subsets;
- FDBcc and FTRAPcc (the generic cpDBcc/cpTRAPcc entries swallowed them),
  FScc with every mode;
- transcendental functions, FSINCOS, FMOD, FSCALE, FGETMAN, FINT/FINTRZ
  beyond 32 bits, FSGLMUL/FSGLDIV, the 68040 FS*/FD* forms and the
  remaining FMOVECR constants;
- exec saves the FPU context of a task (FSAVE, and FP0-7/FPCR/FPSR/FPIAR
  unless the FPU is in its reset state) on task switches.

Probe exec/fpu (instructions encoded as data, captured on AmigaOS 3.1).
Phase 237.

events.message:

The boot SSP stayed at address 0 after reset. Manx C stack checks compare
sp with the longword at 0 (cmpa.l 0.w,sp; bcc ok; jmp 0), so Fish FontEdit

cleanup) read 0x9fffff instead of 0. Vectors 12-63 were 0 where AmigaOS
points the whole table into ROM: unused exceptions now dispatch through
the task trap handler, spurious/unused autovectors return.

events.title: verify: report a startup refusal like a later disk refusal
events.message:
verify: report a startup refusal like a later disk refusal

In text mode, verify printed only the stderr error for a disk refused
at startup, while a disk refused at ACTION_DISK_INFO also prints the
"Volume: (none)" / "Filesystem responsive: NO" report on stdout. JSON
mode already matched.

Print the same report before re-raising the startup refusal.

events.title: cli: report a handler crash during startup as a crash
events.message:
cli: report a handler crash during startup as a crash

When the handler crashes before replying to the startup packet,
_run_startup_until_replies returns no replies and the deferred-flush
retry is skipped, so the user was told the handler did not reply. The
crash checks in mount and format never see this case because the
constructor has already raised.

Check for a crash first, using the message the other startup paths
use. Both cases still map to HANDLER_ERROR in JSON mode.

events.title: devbench: start / stop / restart the OS4 QEMU from the web UI
events.message:
devbench: start / stop / restart the OS4 QEMU from the web UI

The Emulator card's buttons didn't work for the qemu-os4 profile:
- the launcher path (scripts/start-qemu-os4.sh) stayed relative when the
  profile came from --profile: resolve paths after CLI overrides;
- an empty emulator_config became "." and was passed to the launcher,
  which exits on an unknown argument: keep it empty;
- devbench looked for a process named after the launcher, so a QEMU
  started another way showed as stopped (and Start would run a second
  one): new emulator_process (qemu-system-ppc for qemu-os4);
- Stop crashed on an emulator devbench hadn't started: it now stops it by
  process (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL).
Also emulator_env ({AUDIO = "1"} for qemu-os4: the ES1370 sound card) and
the card says which emulator it drives (QEMU / FS-UAE).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: Port bug fixes from C++ freeserf 0.4/0.5
events.message:
Port bug fixes from C++ freeserf 0.4/0.5

Game logic:
- Transporter no longer duplicates a resource when switching at a flag
- Serfs are only lost when a road is removed if they move along it
- Fixed deadlock of serfs waiting for each other (loop check at flags)
- Knights can be made even while a Knight0 is in the stock
- Transporter bits are cleared correctly at a crowded flag
- Fixed military score formula (overflow, as the original game)
- Pigs oink with the persistent random of the game
- Fixed DOS smelter sound (clip 62 offset and padding)

Save games keep more state so a loaded game goes on as the saved one:
- Building counts of all 24 types (gold smelters were lost)
- Burning counter of buildings
- Knight morale, castle inventory, send delays, gold, timers, messages
  and statistics history of the players
- Knight morale and inventory schedule counters of the game
- Threat levels of military buildings are preserved on load
- Serfs leaving a stock

Older save games load as before.

events.title: grm-ze06.1: PartialByte types the StoredValueScanner value channel
events.message:
grm-ze06.1: PartialByte types the StoredValueScanner value channel

A register or memory byte recovered by the scanner was a BankState, the same
record as board and mechanism state, so a mechanism-width mask (MMC3 0xFFFF,
MMC1 0x1FF) could flow into a byte scan and be rescued only by combine's
incidental & 0xFF (the grm-mej.8 incident). PartialByte is an 8-bit value+mask
that clips in its constructor and nowhere else.

- Scan.value, combine/stopped/restoredKeepingValue, forwardedStoreValue,
  callerCellValue, Hooks.resolveLoad/resolveMirrorLoad returns and RegisterEnv
  a/x/y are PartialByte; inStateAtStore stays BankState (grm-ze06.2's axis).
- Byte<->field crossings are named per strategy: verbatimFieldFromByte,
  fieldFromStoredByte (memory-latch, register-write), fieldFromDataByte,
  byteFromField, fieldFromArgumentByte; mirroredByte/byteFor return bytes.
- memory-latch's evaluateLatchScan returns LatchEvaluation (mechanism state)
  instead of overloading Scan.
- HelperArgumentRecovery scans at BankSwitchStrategy.argumentByteMask, which
  preserves today's effective stateMask & 0xFF exactly; GxROM's shifted-field
  mismatch is deliberately kept and tracked by grm-hp9s.
- CLASSIFY_ONLY names the mask-0 "stop reason only" scan.

Pure refactor: build-and-test.sh check green with no bless; ab-test.sh
--dirty HEAD --all byte-identical on 34/34 NES rows, movement=NO.

events.title: 3DO ports on classic 68k (AmigaOS 3.x, AGA or RTG) + OS4 planet fix
events.message:
3DO ports on classic 68k (AmigaOS 3.x, AGA or RTG) + OS4 planet fix

All three games now also build with ARCH=m68k for a 68020+ with AGA or an
RTG card, running the 3DO versions' own integer code:
- amiga68k.c (shared): 15-bit RGB frame to an RTG window/screen
  (Picasso96) or an AGA screen with a palette fitted to the frame
  (weighted median cut, no dithering), chunky-to-planar, double
  buffered; timer, file loading, joystick port 1 (FS-UAE maps it to the
  cursor keys).
- paula.h/paula68k.c: the 3DO sound code on the real Paula (chip RAM
  samples, channels from audio.device, the 50 Hz tick from the main loop).
- softcel.c: the 3DO cel engine in software (flat quads, scaled sprites,
  pixel-processor blends), with an optional depth buffer.
- planet_chomp: the 3DO renderer (render_cel.c, spooks/keys now culled at
  the horizon) on softcel. rolling_steel: the OS4 render.c with per-corner
  depth on a software glcels (no more side faces over the deck).
  spectral_keep: scene.c in 15-bit RGB.
- No amiga.lib on 68k: its sprintf's 16-bit %d broke the 3DO code.

OS4 planet_chomp: the planet's depth fan has six rings (was two), so
spooks round the far side no longer poke through; quits log their reason.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

project.title: volamos
project.display_title: volamos — AmigaOS CLI compatibility runtime

runtime_profiles.name: Linux x86-64 command-line runtime
runtime_profiles.notes: Current CI builds the release executable on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and executes vamos comparison and interpreter/JIT fixtures. No minimum RAM or Linux release is established.

runtime_profiles.name: Apple Silicon command-line runtime
runtime_profiles.notes: Current CI log identifies aarch64-apple-darwin and passes unit/end-to-end guest fixture execution. No minimum RAM or macOS release is established.

project.status: active
project.notes: Wine-style host runtime for classic AmigaOS m68k command-line tools: interprets guest instructions (optional m68k-crate trace JIT) and reimplements OS library calls in Rust. No Kickstart ROM is needed for normal use. It is generic development/analysis tooling, not a native reconstruction of a specific game; graphics, custom chips, Workbench GUI and games are explicitly out of scope. Linux/macOS build and guest execution are corroborated by current CI logs; published Windows x86-64 binaries compile but Windows/Wine runtime remains unverified. Interpreter/JIT parity covers six fixtures; comparison with vamos includes three documented known divergences, so it is not universal compatibility proof. The math-library shims now return comparison/test results in both D0 and 68k condition codes, matching the documented ROM calling behavior needed by SAS/C's scmieee.lib; before the fix, SAS/C double comparisons appeared equal and exp() overflow checks returned HUGE_VAL. Evidence: https://github.com/sidick/volamos/commit/de321627fd5f1c16ca6cc76020222d7f3c18d564

project.title: Rockford Patcher
project.display_title: Rockford — DOS hidden-level recovery and patcher
project.notes: Patches the DOS Rockford executable to unlock hidden levels and reconstructs additional theme tiles, values and graphics. Historical Amiga art is compared in the research, but the tool does not patch Amiga media. Version 3.0 now distinguishes ORIGINAL.EXE, which uses newly recovered original EGA SCUBA and PLAYER tiles/animations, from ADDON.EXE, whose graphics are reconstructed from Amiga screenshots. The README marks SCUBA, PLAYER and LUCK complete while MUSIC and MINER still lack end-state animations. No DOSBox run was independently performed. Evidence: https://github.com/asahala/Rockford-Patcher/commit/0e4c686000b98288c4c21ece6b958e9399210951 https://github.com/asahala/Rockford-Patcher/blob/main/README.md

project.notes: papple2 is a small Apple II reverse-engineering emulator/debugger with a completed rebuilt instrumentation layer and an IPython workbench. Its prompt_toolkit listing editor now edits labels, operand targets and comments in place, follows calls, preserves back/forward breadcrumbs, and offers a routine picker; annotations are persisted in the dossier and refreshed between terminal sessions. Lode Runner's byte-identical XekriRedmane reconstruction remains an external grading oracle, never an analysis input. Evidence: https://github.com/fschuhi/papple2/commit/99c38d0aa3838a095e09713058a598a33bb5b672 https://github.com/fschuhi/papple2/commit/71383884923cf04a022948a464fc370b65db02f3

project.title: Amiga Games — Dot Chase, Fractalus and Void Trader collection
project.display_title: Amiga Games — native games and 3DO-derived AmigaOS ports

runtime_profiles.name: Dot Chase: selected classic 68k build
runtime_profiles.notes: -m68020 build with intuition.library and graphics.library v39, four-plane LORES screen. No PPC branch is evidenced. RAM and chipset minima are unstated; not independently run.

runtime_profiles.name: Fractalus and Void Trader: selected classic AGA builds
runtime_profiles.notes: Both selected builds use -m68020, explicit AGA 320x256x8bpp and v39 OS libraries. No minimum RAM or measured performance threshold is established. 64 KiB stack requests are not RAM minima.

runtime_profiles.name: Fractalus and Void Trader: PPC OS4 variants
runtime_profiles.notes: ARCH=ppc selects -mcpu=440 and newlib with sam460ex/QEMU intent. The PPC variants use silent audio stubs; Fractalus uses graphics.library fallback rendering. Pacing/freezing limitations are author-reported. This does not cover Dot Chase or the whole collection; exact CPU/RAM minimum remains unverified.

runtime_profiles.name: Planet Chomp, Rolling Steel and Spectral Keep: PPC OS4 source ports
runtime_profiles.notes: The three source-level ports are PPC-only and build with ppc-amigaos-gcc -mcpu=440fp/newlib. Planet Chomp and Rolling Steel use OSMesa 7.8.2 software rendering; Spectral Keep renders its precomputed sprites in software. Upstream reports QEMU sam460ex performance, but no minimum physical CPU or RAM requirement is established.

project.status: Six substantive game anchors reviewed across classic 68k and PPC AmigaOS variants; independently unbuilt
project.notes: amiga_games is one source-available AmigaBridge game collection with its own canonical root, distinct from the already-tracked parent tooling. Three inspected anchors establish the bounded game collection: Dot Chase implements maze dot-eating, ghost states, power pellets, fruit, score, lives and level completion; Fractalus implements terrain flight, pilot rescue/deception, landing/airlock/takeoff, combat, fuel/shield win/loss and attract mode; Void Trader implements space combat, docking, station trading, cargo/credits, salvage and win/game-over states. Void Trader prices are fixed with 90% resale; variable-price trade routes remain future work. The complete 426-entry tree was inspected and three game anchors were read in depth; this is not a claim that every listed game or asset was audited. One subject/game collection is counted, with Dot Chase, Fractalus and Void Trader as the reviewed subjects. These are substantial native homebrew/homage implementations; no original-binary reconstruction is established. Fractalus source explicitly calls itself a Rescue on Fractalus homage. Demos, utilities and tests are outside this game scope. Hubert, although listed among games in README, is an interactive shell/REPL with LLM support and is excluded from the game anchors. No extra project is made for uninspected collection labels. The reviewed anchors are original native C/C++ game implementations and homages, not analysed historical instruction streams. source_cpu and source_language remain empty; the selected 68020 and PowerPC 440 outputs belong in target_cpu. Historical inspirations and an Amiga label do not establish an original binary CPU. Dot Chase explicitly uses m68k-amigaos-gcc -m68020 with no reviewed PPC branch. Fractalus and Void Trader have separate ARCH=m68k/-m68020 and ARCH=ppc/ppc-amigaos-gcc(-g++) -mcpu=440 branches. Their PowerPC support cannot be generalized to Dot Chase, all games, every PPC processor or every AmigaOS release. The three per-game Makefiles require the external parent AmigaBridge headers and libbridge.a at ../../amiga-bridge, so the game repository alone is insufficient without that layout, dependency and matching compiler/library architecture. Classic builds use -noixemul; the two PPC branches use newlib and architecture-specific audio stubs. Fractalus/Void Trader treat failed ab_init as optional at runtime, so a running host MCP/daemon is not established as universally required merely by README deployment instructions. Dot Chase ignores that return value; daemon-free execution remains unverified. Parent examples-pin mismatch is retained under relationships. No collection build, binary availability or playthrough was independently verified; all four build flags remain null. Requirements differ by inspected game and architecture. Dot Chase builds with -m68020, opens intuition.library and graphics.library v39, and uses a four-plane LORES custom screen; no PPC branch or chipset minimum is asserted for it. Fractalus and Void Trader default to -m68020, AmigaOS 3.x/v39 libraries and explicit AGA 320x256x8bpp. Their separate PPC builds use -mcpu=440, newlib and AmigaOS 4.1 sam460ex/QEMU intent, with silent audio stubs replacing Paula access; Fractalus also falls back to graphics.library rendering. This establishes selected compiler targets, not independently tested accelerator/RAM minima or general PPC compatibility. Source requests 65536-byte stacks in the two 3D games; stack allocations are not total-RAM minima. Upstream reports Fractalus uncapped at 150–200 fps after Delay(2) froze on OS4, resulting in very fast combat/short attract delay; Void Trader uses an explicitly temporary CPU-burn pacing loop. None of those author observations was reproduced here. Explicit game-source commit trailers attribute Fractalus attract-mode work and draw-overlay correction to Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context); the MIT copyright-line update credits Claude Opus 4.7. These are affirmative development-assistance evidence, so ai.usage is true and tools contains only Claude. The claim does not quantify generated code, cover every game, or rely on an instruction filename, provider email or the unrelated Hubert LLM feature. Latest five commit messages were freshly rechecked. The existing amiga-devbench-mcp tracker record covers the separate parent geekychris/amiga_mcp debugger/development tooling, not this game inventory. All three inspected games require its ../../amiga-bridge/include and libbridge.a in the expected layout, with matching target architecture. The parent examples gitlink at a346995a30948fff03faa3b3efbaf5a3bdb131dc pins 2dad36f1c16e158ba9e951c0a92760d25366680a and .gitmodules hints feat/initial-import, whereas this collection was reviewed at c3a23bec0328cf716fac6536f9164ea6209bf397; the recursive-parent-clone recipe does not necessarily reproduce this snapshot. Root LICENSE and inspected SPDX headers grant MIT, overriding the stale README license-TBD sentence for those files. Sampled stakattack/ptplayer.asm is Frank Wille public-domain code, so the README all-original wording is not a whole-collection provenance guarantee. Full asset/dependency licensing remains partial. Canonical root and subject/lineage aliases were screened against the 1715-project baseline f8c70d18333dad71c511eda424fadd2627c5f6fc and prior review index without an existing equivalent. Current default-branch metadata and latest commits were rechecked on 2026-10-06; snapshot c3a23bec0328cf716fac6536f9164ea6209bf397. last_activity is the latest default-branch commit date, not pushed_at; re_started remains unknown. Overall review and the broader source graph remain partial. No candidate build, execution, gameplay test, binary correspondence check or byte comparison was performed. PPC source ports derived from the author's 3DO versions: Planet Chomp, Rolling Steel and Spectral Keep. Rolling Steel retains the 3DO physics, rules, course loader and renderer maths while substituting OSMesa output; Spectral Keep retains the 3DO rules, rooms, physics, level data and voxel-sprite renderer while replacing cel output with a software framebuffer. change_details.before: Amiga Games — Dot Chase, Fractalus and Void Trader collection
change_details.after: Amiga Games — native games and 3DO-derived AmigaOS ports

change_details.before: amiga_games is one source-available AmigaBridge game collection with its own canonical root, distinct from the already-tracked parent tooling. Three inspected anchors establish the bounded game collection: Dot Chase implements maze dot-eating, ghost states, power pellets, fruit, score, lives and level completion; Fractalus implements terrain flight, pilot rescue/deception, landing/airlock/takeoff, combat, fuel/shield win/loss and attract mode; Void Trader implements space combat, docking, station trading, cargo/credits, salvage and win/game-over states. Void Trader prices are fixed with 90% resale; variable-price trade routes remain future work. The complete 426-entry tree was inspected and three game anchors were read in depth; this is not a claim that every listed game or asset was audited. One subject/game collection is counted, with Dot Chase, Fractalus and Void Trader as the reviewed subjects. These are substantial native homebrew/homage implementations; no original-binary reconstruction is established. Fractalus source explicitly calls itself a Rescue on Fractalus homage. Demos, utilities and tests are outside this game scope. Hubert, although listed among games in README, is an interactive shell/REPL with LLM support and is excluded from the game anchors. No extra project is made for uninspected collection labels. The reviewed anchors are original native C/C++ game implementations and homages, not analysed historical instruction streams. source_cpu and source_language remain empty; the selected 68020 and PowerPC 440 outputs belong in target_cpu. Historical inspirations and an Amiga label do not establish an original binary CPU. Dot Chase explicitly uses m68k-amigaos-gcc -m68020 with no reviewed PPC branch. Fractalus and Void Trader have separate ARCH=m68k/-m68020 and ARCH=ppc/ppc-amigaos-gcc(-g++) -mcpu=440 branches. Their PowerPC support cannot be generalized to Dot Chase, all games, every PPC processor or every AmigaOS release. The three per-game Makefiles require the external parent AmigaBridge headers and libbridge.a at ../../amiga-bridge, so the game repository alone is insufficient without that layout, dependency and matching compiler/library architecture. Classic builds use -noixemul; the two PPC branches use newlib and architecture-specific audio stubs. Fractalus/Void Trader treat failed ab_init as optional at runtime, so a running host MCP/daemon is not established as universally required merely by README deployment instructions. Dot Chase ignores that return value; daemon-free execution remains unverified. Parent examples-pin mismatch is retained under relationships. No collection build, binary availability or playthrough was independently verified; all four build flags remain null. Requirements differ by inspected game and architecture. Dot Chase builds with -m68020, opens intuition.library and graphics.library v39, and uses a four-plane LORES custom screen; no PPC branch or chipset minimum is asserted for it. Fractalus and Void Trader default to -m68020, AmigaOS 3.x/v39 libraries and explicit AGA 320x256x8bpp. Their separate PPC builds use -mcpu=440, newlib and AmigaOS 4.1 sam460ex/QEMU intent, with silent audio stubs replacing Paula access; Fractalus also falls back to graphics.library rendering. This establishes selected compiler targets, not independently tested accelerator/RAM minima or general PPC compatibility. Source requests 65536-byte stacks in the two 3D games; stack allocations are not total-RAM minima. Upstream reports Fractalus uncapped at 150–200 fps after Delay(2) froze on OS4, resulting in very fast combat/short attract delay; Void Trader uses an explicitly temporary CPU-burn pacing loop. None of those author observations was reproduced here. Explicit game-source commit trailers attribute Fractalus attract-mode work and draw-overlay correction to Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context); the MIT copyright-line update credits Claude Opus 4.7. These are affirmative development-assistance evidence, so ai.usage is true and tools contains only Claude. The claim does not quantify generated code, cover every game, or rely on an instruction filename, provider email or the unrelated Hubert LLM feature. Latest five commit messages were freshly rechecked. The existing amiga-devbench-mcp tracker record covers the separate parent geekychris/amiga_mcp debugger/development tooling, not this game inventory. All three inspected games require its ../../amiga-bridge/include and libbridge.a in the expected layout, with matching target architecture. The parent examples gitlink at a346995a30948fff03faa3b3efbaf5a3bdb131dc pins 2dad36f1c16e158ba9e951c0a92760d25366680a and .gitmodules hints feat/initial-import, whereas this collection was reviewed at c3a23bec0328cf716fac6536f9164ea6209bf397; the recursive-parent-clone recipe does not necessarily reproduce this snapshot. Root LICENSE and inspected SPDX headers grant MIT, overriding the stale README license-TBD sentence for those files. Sampled stakattack/ptplayer.asm is Frank Wille public-domain code, so the README all-original wording is not a whole-collection provenance guarantee. Full asset/dependency licensing remains partial. Canonical root and subject/lineage aliases were screened against the 1715-project baseline f8c70d18333dad71c511eda424fadd2627c5f6fc and prior review index without an existing equivalent. Current default-branch metadata and latest commits were rechecked on 2026-10-06; snapshot c3a23bec0328cf716fac6536f9164ea6209bf397. last_activity is the latest default-branch commit date, not pushed_at; re_started remains unknown. Overall review and the broader source graph remain partial. No candidate build, execution, gameplay test, binary correspondence check or byte comparison was performed. project.status: active
project.notes: Clean-room Dungeon Master-family engine. DM1 PC/DOS 3.4 remains playable/source-locked. v3.0.373 publishes x86-64 and arm64 host packages, verifies the authentic DM1 Amiga 2.0 F0437 title regions, RGB4 palette stages and 18 source-derived zoom steps, and the subsequent 17ce8dc change admits authentic CSB Amiga 3.3 media through the native title/menu/runtime startup path. Those bounded receipts do not establish full Amiga campaign parity. A separate isolated DM1 Amiga 2.0 M12 run still lacks first-Hall validation, while the native macOS DM2 capture reaches New/Resume/Quit without establishing physical-M5 testing, dungeon presentation, audio parity or complete gameplay. Subsequent Theron's Quest work corrects the authenticated HuC6280 bank-$1f initializer call target, aligns the bounded C decoder with the retail final-byte lookahead boundary, and hardens stale transition-queue rejection. Static US/JP media checks and synthetic algorithm vectors passed upstream, but authentic level payload decoding, runtime consumer binding and retail game start remain explicitly unproven; a cold-start input capture stayed in the System Card with no Track 02 handoff. project.notes: Emulates CPC 464/6128, Plus and GX4000 with per-model CRTC/Gate Array timing, disc and tape support, a debugger and embedded RASM. project.display_title: Amiga DevBench — serial debugger and MCP development environment
project.status: active
project.notes: Host/target bridge over serial to a real or FS-UAE Amiga, with memory/register inspection, breakpoints, remote execution, a web dashboard and MCP tools. The optional patched FS-UAE enables a separate emulator-level debugger; ordinary FS-UAE still supports the serial bridge. Docker is used for the 68k cross compiler. The environment now includes a reproducible AmigaOS 4.1 PPC/newlib build of Mesa 7.8.2 OSMesa for fixed-function software rendering, an on-guest self-test, an opt-in ES1370 QEMU audio route, and updated examples pins for three PPC ports. events.title: fix: INT 21h AH=2Ch sub-second hundredths + unplugged game port status (#2393)
events.message:
fix: INT 21h AH=2Ch sub-second hundredths + unplugged game port status (#2393)

* fix: Return sub-second hundredths from INT 21h AH=2Ch

GetTime() hard-coded DL to 0, so DOS programs measuring elapsed time through the hundredths field never saw sub-second time advance: 0.5s wait loops spun forever and per-frame movement/animation gates never fired (e.g. Pyro II hangs right after its intro and the player stays frozen on the level screen). Derive DL from the host clock as DateTime.Now.Millisecond / 10 (0-99 per the DOS API); CH, CL and DH keep coming from the CMOS RTC, which only has one-second resolution.

* fix: Report unplugged game port 0x201 status instead of echoing writes

The joystick handler stored whatever byte was written to 0x201 and read it back. Writing to the game port is how programs trigger the axis one-shots, so a trigger write also made the button bits read as active-low pressed forever, hanging games that gate progress on button release (Pyro II freezes on level entry). Reads now return the unplugged status 0xF0 (axis timers expired, buttons released) and writes only act as triggers. Note: the copilot/fully-support-joystick-types branch replaces this handler with a full Gameport (UnpluggedReading = 0xFF); this is a minimal stopgap for master.

events.title: Math libraries: extend condition codes to SPAdd/Sub/Mul/Div/Abs/Neg/Ceil/Floor (#113)
events.message:
Math libraries: extend condition codes to SPAdd/Sub/Mul/Div/Abs/Neg/Ceil/Floor (#113)

PR #112 fixed SPCmp/SPTst (and their IEEE equivalents) to set N/Z the
way the real ROM does. Verified against real Kickstart 3.1 (40.68) via
Copperline that mathffp.library's other basic arithmetic functions
(SPAdd/SPSub/SPMul/SPDiv/SPAbs/SPNeg/SPCeil/SPFloor) do the same --
N/Z always match the result's actual sign/zero-ness, not just
SPCmp/SPTst. Added set_ffp_arith_result alongside the existing
return_cmp_result to cover them, named the CCR bit constants instead
of leaving them as magic numbers, and added real regression
coverage: tests that branch on the condition codes directly (SAS/C's
own idiom, never reading D0) for every affected handler, since the
existing tests only ever checked D0/the exit code.

The IEEE single-precision arithmetic equivalents were also probed on
the same real hardware but hit an unexplained crash around
IEEESPMul partway through verification, so they're left alone here --
RKRM documents IEEE basic arithmetic (unlike IEEE Cmp/Tst) as leaving
flags undefined, consistent with what little we did observe, but
this needs its own follow-up rather than guessing.

and SAS/C's scmieee.lib branches on those without looking at D0, so every

events.title: spectral_keep: port the 3DO Spectral Keep to AmigaOS 4.1
events.message:
spectral_keep: port the 3DO Spectral Keep to AmigaOS 4.1

The 3DO version's rules, rooms, physics, level data and voxel sprite
renderer are kept unchanged. scene.c keeps its dependency sort and draws
into a 32-bit frame in software instead of building cels: the room's
walls and floor once per room, the sprites over them each frame, and the
pixel-processor effects (shadows, panel shade, flash) per pixel.
main_os4.c: window, keyboard pad, 50 Hz loop, HUD in the game's font.
sound_ahi.c: music in linked one-second chunks (gapless, can duck) and
effects through AHI. 50 fps on QEMU sam460ex.

The background copy is a loop: on the guest's newlib.library a memcpy of
>= 300 KB can leave its last 256 KB uncopied.

rolling_steel: port the 3DO Rolling Steel to AmigaOS 4.1 with OpenGL (OSMesa)

speed-pitched rumble through AHI. data/: the courses, themes and effects
built by the 3DO tools. 40-50 fps on QEMU sam460ex.

events.title: 実装: CIRCLE 文（l4-graphics 第4版 第10節、l4-s9v）
events.message:
実装: CIRCLE 文（l4-graphics 第4版 第10節、l4-s9v）

根拠: docs/spec/l4-graphics.md 第4版（c77870e）第10節 CIRCLE と、第9節 LINE（扇形の線）。測定コミットは b386e81、照合は tools/l4_circle_measure.py check と tests/conformance/expected_l4_circle.tsv。
照合: 45腕 一致45・不一致0（実装前 HEAD 6b4abf1 は6/39）。初回の全腕走査でそのまま全一致で、修正コミットは無い。

構成（docs/spec の手順どおり）
- 文の種別 49（gfxhook.asm の語の表に CIRCLE を足し、bank0 から bank1 の src/ext_bank/circle.asm へ中継）。構文・誤り番号の順・省略欄・LP・STEP・評価順・色を bank1 で処理。
- 半径の符号は丸める前に見る（VAL_IS_NEGATIVE）。N=rnd(f32(r×0.7071068))、角→点数 rnd(f32(f32(|v|)×f32(0.15915494))×f32(8N))、比率→整数 a_ は mainの MBF 乗除（窓外中継）で単精度のまま計算。定数は MBF 単精度の4バイト。
- 中点法（X=2r, Y=0, 和=0）は和を 24 ビット符号付きで持つ（半径 32767 で和が約 ±131070 になり 16 ビットを超えるため）。(a,b) 1組ごとに scale と8方向（表）・円弧の判定（sc/ec/plotf/lf）を行う。
- バンクの往復: 点は 8 組ずつ MM_CI_BUF に置き、bank2 の gx_ci_flush（→ gx_pt_begin/gx_plotxy。範囲外は点ごとに切り捨て）へ (a,b) 1組につき1回だけ渡す。点ごとには往復しない。他の往復は中心の読み取り（gx_coord）1回と扇形の線1本につき1回（gx_ci_line = LINE と同じ ln_seg。辺ごとに丸めるクリップを含む）。bank2 には入口 3 つ（0x7330〜）と本体約 42B だけ足した。
- 作業域 CIRCLE_WORK（0xEE06、72B）を memmap に追加。LINE_WORK の直後で、ディスク文・PRINT USING とは排他（OVERLAPS に理由を記載）。

自作判断（仕様で未測定のところ）
- 角の点数が 16 ビット符号付きに収まらない（半径が約 5790 を超える円弧）ときは 0xFFFF。比率の a_ が収まらない（比率が約 -128 未満）ときは 0x0100（真円）。
- 点の座標が 16 ビットを超える（中心±半径が -32768〜32767 の外）ときは打たない（巻き込みで画面内に入れない）。
- 複数の誤りが同時にあるときは引数を読む順（中心→半径→色→開始角→終了角→比率）。
- `circle(100,100),10 7`（誤りなし）は、式の評価が「10」で止まり後ろが文末検査で拾われない既存の経路のまま一致した（理由の特定はしていない）。

検証（自作ROM、全て自分で実行）
- l4_circle_measure check: 45/45。l4_line_measure check: 68/68（不変）。
- s9t の gfx 器具 83腕×2走: 判定列は HEAD と全168行で同一（差は最後の 0x32 の値が 169/171 で入れ替わる位相のずれだけ。双方向に出る=本体を通らない arm の取り込み時刻のずれ）。
- 速さ（所要フレーム、HEAD 6b4abf1 は CIRCLE 未実装）: 半径 90 の円 100 個 1709（公式 1053）、半径 10 の円 100 個 355（公式 189）。全画面BF 10、斜め線640本 2248、PSET600個 733 は不変。画素は公式と一致（check の腕と同じ規則）。
- 実描画: QUASI88 のスクリーンショットで円・楕円（比率 0.3・1・3）・円弧・負の角の扇形・開始＞終了の外側弧を確認（円が楕円の向きと縮める軸は第10.3節どおり）。
- 退行: selftest 一式（verify_l1・l3_main・l3_screen_editor・conform_l4・ext_bank・vsync_regcheck・memmap・deffn・deftype・tabspc・wrap・widthbeep・widthvram・line・gfx・circle・sincos/sqr/atnexplog の bank と endtoend・pusing・onwhile・memdyn・editinv・l4_basic・files/load/save/killname の conform と z80・m6ib/ic/ie/ig/ih の ROM 関門・check_rom_version_reserved・check_cleanroom）全て rc=0。memmap は初回に RAM 番地の直書き（0FFFFh）で止まったので 65535 へ直した（ROM は同一バイト）。
- 検査に使った ROM の SHA（先頭16桁）: N88.ROM a11f49bd32277c24（HEAD と同一）、N88_1.ROM 8da2e22d57d370a3、N88_2.ROM 03fc9f32e24ab22d（コミットのソースからの再ビルドと一致）。
- 容量: main 残126B・bank0 65B・bank3 27B は不変、bank1 1995B → 885B（CIRCLE 本体 1099B。目安 850B を超えた分は 24 ビットの和・8方向の表引き・単精度計算の窓外中継のため）、bank2 540B → 498B。0x79D7 不変。
private/ 混入なし（check_cleanroom rc=0）。
run_all はその日の最後に回す。push しない。

events.title: v0.4.0: M4 WiFi, the SYMBiFACE IDE/CF drive, LambdaSpeak 3's Epson and DECtalk speech
events.message:
v0.4.0: M4 WiFi, the SYMBiFACE IDE/CF drive, LambdaSpeak 3's Epson and DECtalk speech

### New: the M4 board's WiFi
The M4's WiFi is now your PC's internet connection.
- **Sockets:** CPC programs open TCP connections, look up host names and run their own servers. Duke's TCP and telnet examples work; the telnet client logs into telehack.com.
- **Downloads:** `|HTTPGET` saves a file from the web to the M4's card, with its `@` (quiet) and `>name` (save as) forms, the server's own file name, and redirects. `|HTTPMEM` downloads into memory, `offset=` included. Plain HTTP only, as on the real board.
- **Status:** `|NETSTAT` shows your PC's address, `|NETSET` and `|WIFI` work, and SymbOS's M4 network daemon has the board's socket interface to talk to.
- **Settings:** under Expansions → M4 board:
  - **WiFi: the PC's network** is on by default.
  - **Servers: accept other computers** is off by default, so a CPC server program can only be reached from your own PC.

### New: the SYMBiFACE II / III IDE/CF drive
Both Symbiface cards now have their IDE/CF interface.
- **The drive is a folder:** `symide` beside `cpcse.exe`, made the first time, or any folder you choose under Expansions → Symbiface.
- **What SymbOS sees:** one FAT16 partition, long file names included. It lists, reads and writes it, and its changes go back into the folder.
- **Command line:** `--ide <folder>`, `--sf3`, and `--xrom <slot>=<file>`, which fits an expansion ROM such as SymbOS's ROM version.

### New: LambdaSpeak 3's Epson and DECtalk speech
LambdaSpeak 3 now does what the board itself does.
- **Its control bytes,** with the exact ready values each mode puts on the bus.
- **Getters** for volume, voice, rate, version, mode and the clock.
- **Spoken confirmations,** like "Native Epson mode.".
- **Blocking speech** that holds the Z80 until a sentence is finished; `&DF` stops it.
- **Epson and DECtalk text** is spoken with your computer's own voices: the Windows speech voices, `say` on macOS, `espeak-ng` on Linux. The Epson chip's DECtalk firmware isn't public, so it sounds like your PC, not like DECtalk.
- **In-text commands:** the Epson parser's voice changes, whisper, pitch and speed, and DECtalk's `[:np]`-style voices, `[:rate]`, `[:dv ap]` and phoneme strings.
- **Tested with LambdaSpeak's own software:** `ENGLISH.BAS`, `WELCOME.BAS` and `MP3.BAS` from LS300.DSK, and TFM's `MP3-PLAY.BAS` with his RSX ROM, all run.

### Download
`CPCSyntaxError-win64-v0.4.0.zip`: unzip anywhere and run `cpcse.exe`. On Linux and macOS, build from source (README, *Building from source*). The YRW801 (OPL4) and SP0256-AL2 (speech) ROMs are not included; the emulator asks for them when they're needed.

events.title: 高速化: グラフィックの描画（出力は不変）
events.message:
高速化: グラフィックの描画（出力は不変）

測った時間の内訳（コア側の PC 別ステート集計。作業dir 内の一時器具で、リポジトリには入れていない）:
- 斜め線: 1画素あたり約2780ステート。番地計算 gx_addr 約720（x%8 と y*80 を毎回ループ・加算で求めていた）、3プレーンの書き込み約760、走査の和・歩進約1000。
- 全画面BF: 1バイトずつ LD/INC/DJNZ（26ステート/バイト）で48000バイト＋行ごとに gx_addr 2回。
- PSET 600個: 約67000ステート/文のうち、点を打つ部分は約1500で、残りは BASIC の文の解釈（文の語の照合・式の評価・窓外中継）。FOR/NEXT だけで約16000、代入文 x=1 でも約34000。ここは描画の外なので触っていない。

直した箇所:
- gx_addr: 範囲検査を上位バイト比較に、y*80 を (y*5)<<4 の加算に、マスクを8バイトの表に。
- 点列の入口 gx_pt_begin / gx_pt / gx_plotxy を新設（色の行 IX を1回置き、番地とマスクを呼び手が進める。CIRCLE・PAINT も使える）。1点は XOR 式でプレーンごとに読み・書き各1回。白黒も同じ入口。
- 線種なしの実線は、番地 HL とマスク B を歩進させる4通りの専用ループ（Y主軸/X主軸×x増減）。和は t=和-主軸の差 をキャリーで判定。線種ありは従来の汎用ループ（画素は同一）。
- BF・水平線: 1行1プレーンを1つの窓で、端のバイトだけマスク付き、間は PUSH DE の並びへ飛び込んで2バイトずつ書く。BF は先頭行だけ番地を求め、以降は +80。
- 窓（DI〜EI）の中はスタックにもRAMにも触れない約束を維持（SP は窓の前に退避し EI の前に戻す）。窓の最長は約600ステート。

所要フレーム（前 a3762e5 / 後。公式）: 全画面BF 28 / 10（7）、斜め線640本 5211 / 2248（1035）、PSET600個 734 / 732（194）。BF10回 270 / 93。
斜め線の残りは主に LINE 文の解釈（1文あたり約8万ステート）で、画素の描画は約半分。PSET は上記のとおり解釈が支配的。

出力が不変であること: l4_line_measure check 68/68、l4_circle_measure（自作）は CIRCLE 未実装のまま6/39で不変、l4_gfx_measure 83腕×2走は判定列が直前と同一（差は 0x5C〜0x5E に書く値だけで、値は何でもよい仕様）。速さの腕と乱数の線・BF・箱・線種・白黒・PSET・行ごとのBF各種の最終画素ハッシュが前後で全件一致。

events.message:
M9: menu and settings (#9)

* M9: menu and settings

pico-ace's settings file and its in-place rewriter, park, menu, pause and
screenshots, renamed, with the Oric's keys (rom, ram, microdisc, volume,
perf, status, backlight, layout, fast_tape, boot_tape, boot_disc) and

W: save, read back, restart into the Oric-1 16K at M7's cycle count,
screenshot, pause, About, reboot into the saved machine. A save no longer
writes the panel's own backlight unless the Setup page set it (EL §8.7).

events.message:
修正: LINE の B の辺順・線種の位相・クリップを仕様第3版と公式期待値に合わせる

根拠: docs/spec/l4-graphics.md 第3版（2055bb3）第9.3・9.4・9.6節。照合は tools/l4_line_measure.py check と tests/conformance/expected_l4_line.tsv（09d95db）。
eaf8197 は 61/68 一致だった（不一致 cp-6・cp-8・lp-c・sx-a・sy-b・sy-f・sy-n）。
- B の4辺を 下→上→右→左 の順に別の線として引き、線種の位相は文の頭で1回だけ置いて4辺を通して続ける（角は辺ごとに数え直す）。
- クリップを 左→右→上→下 の辺ごとに順に切る方式へ変更。各段で、はみ出した端点を「いまの線」とその辺の直線の交点に置き換えて整数へ四捨五入（0.5 は切り上げ）。両端がその辺の外なら棄却、最後に外が残っても棄却。
- X の差も Y の差も 65535 の線は何も描かない（第3版の「最小の実装」。境界は未確定＝自作判断）。
- 作業域 LINE_WORK を 84B に（F0・F1・K を追加）。端点の印の計算を ln_ocs にまとめた。
自作判断: 交点の丸めは「厳密な有理数に 0.5 を足して床」（32bit 積÷16bit 除数。同点は +∞ 側）。辺の順のうち上下・x/y の前後は未確定で左→右→上→下。画面外の BF の切り詰めは eaf8197 のまま。

- check: 68腕 一致68・不一致0（修正前 eaf8197 は61）。

never written.

events.title: fix(native): the watchdog acts at once when its owner's pipe ends, also when the owner's pid is reused
events.message:
fix(native): the watchdog acts at once when its owner's pipe ends, also when the owner's pid is reused

The supervisor now gives its watchdog a pipe on standard input and keeps the
writing end until it ends. The system closes that end when the owner ends,
however it ends, so the watchdog cleans up at once; a pid that another
process now uses cannot hold it back. The poll of the owner's pid stays as
the fallback. A path that the watchdog cannot remove no longer stops the
removal of the other paths and of the registry.

events.title: Accept const/volatile pointers to members in LF_POINTER (#560)
events.message:
Accept const/volatile pointers to members in LF_POINTER (#560)

* Accept const/volatile pointers to members in LF_POINTER

read_pointer checked the pointer kind against a fixed list that has the
cv-qualified forms of "Pointer" but not of "Pointer to member" or
"Pointer to member function". A type such as `int S::* const` failed the
assertion, the leaf was not stored, and the lookup that followed raised
KeyError. ATL 7.1's CVarTypeInfo<T>::pmField is such a type, so this
stopped reccmp on MFC 7.1 programs.

Replace the list with a regex. cvdump prints the optional attributes
volatile, const, __unaligned and __restrict, in that order, before the
pointer mode (see madebr/cvdump dump_tpi.py). Matching that pattern
accepts every combination, including __restrict, and still rejects
anything else. __unaligned exists only on x64 and ARM, so it never
appears in a PDB that reccmp reads, but the regex accepts it to follow
cvdump's format.

The test samples are cvdump output from programs built with MSVC 7.1
(cl 13.10.3077) and, for __restrict, MSVC 14.51 (cl 19.51) for x86.

* Remove redundant comment above LF_POINTER_TYPE_RE

events.title: M8: AY audio (#8)
events.message:
M8: AY audio (#8)

* M8: AY audio

The AY-3-8912's three tones, noise and envelope, as event times on its
divide-by-8 tick, run from event to event through only the generators
the level depends on and caught up by arithmetic otherwise; ultrasonic
tones averaged; Westcott's measured volume table; pico-ace's beeper
generalised into pcm.c; pico-ace's audio.c renamed, with core 0 paced on
its queue and PICO_ORIC_AUDIO=OFF the timer's control.

Held on the host to an independent cycle-stepped model on every sample,
random scripts and both ROMs' sounds from power-on alike; pitch, envelope
shapes and the silent keyboard scan checked; audio.c heard through a
simulated DMA. On a Plus 2 W: ten minutes without an underrun, the late
path forced, the AY at 1.8 points of core 0. By the owner's ear on a
Pico 2 W: the sound commands and a MUSIC scale work.

The record is in docs/milestones.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* M8: hardware-notes §5.3, a trigger reloads the DMA count

The note said a chain trigger reloads neither the read address nor the
transfer count. The RP2350's TRANS_COUNT description says every trigger
copies the last value written into the live counter, and only that fits
the late-refill path forced on a board (EL §6.4) and reproduced by
test_audio_port's simulated DMA. Corrected, at the owner's word.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* M8: audio.c's re-arm comment follows hardware-notes §5.3

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* M8: a new audio rate keeps the samples in place, off the stack

oric_audio_set_rate saved the samples waiting in a 2 KiB array on the
stack while pcm_init cleared the pcm, and core 0's main stack is the
SDK's 2 KiB: its frame was 2,144 bytes (Codex's review of PR #8).
pcm_set_rate now changes the rate in place, keeping the samples, the
level and the DC blocker; the frame is 40 bytes. test_audio checks what
it keeps and the new rate's count.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: Drop a held direction's queued press once a read delivers the hold
events.message:
Drop a held direction's queued press once a read delivers the hold

Saul, on the temple grund vines: press Space and an arrow together to
leap, release both in the air, and the figure lands and walks on.

When the button's press reached the queue first, the leap read took
it and stopped there; the arrow's press stayed queued while the held
arrow steered the leap.  The leap reads nothing until it lands, so the
landing read found that press with the key already up and walked it as
a tap.

A continuous read that delivers a held direction now drops that hold's
own press from the queue.  Taps released between reads still get their
one read, and button presses are untouched, so a re-tap in the air
still leaps from the landing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: planet_chomp: port the 3DO Planet Chomp to AmigaOS 4.1 with OpenGL (OSMesa)
events.message:
planet_chomp: port the 3DO Planet Chomp to AmigaOS 4.1 with OpenGL (OSMesa)

The 3DO version's rules, spook AI, sphere maze, sprite art and synthesised
sounds are kept unchanged. The cel renderer is replaced by gl_render.c:
OpenGL through Mesa 7.8.2's software rasteriser (third_party/mesa-os4 in
amiga_mcp), with a depth buffer, a lit planet, solid walls and billboard
sprites. main_os4.c adds a window, keyboard-as-pad, a 50 Hz logic clock,
the HUD drawn into the GL frame and a WritePixelArray blit. Sound goes
through ahi.device (sfx_ahi.c), with a gapless linked ambience loop.

35-40 fps on QEMU sam460ex at 320x256 doubled; HIRES renders at 640x512.

events.title: 実装: LINE 文（l4-graphics 第2版 第9節、l4-s9u）
events.message:
実装: LINE 文（l4-graphics 第2版 第9節、l4-s9u）

根拠: docs/spec/l4-graphics.md 第2版 第9節と第1版部分。測定コミット f25edfe。
置き場所は bank2（src/ext_bank/line.asm、gfx.asm の後ろへ連結）。LINE 文の語を文の表に追加（種別48）。
自作判断: クリップの交点は仕様の「交点を四捨五入して引き直す」方式で、他軸の値 = 元の第1点の値 + 四捨五入((辺 - 元の辺の値) * 他軸の差 / 辺の軸の差)（厳密な有理数に0.5を足して床）。
  根拠の腕: bx-ov・bx-p1・bx-p2・sy-c・sy-e・sy-f・mo-*・sx-a・sx-b（仕様書から別に書いた参照モデルと全画素一致）。画面外の BF は最寄り画素へ切り詰め（観測は左上のみ、他は同じ規則）。
自作照合: l4_line_measure の自作ROM記録 68腕×2走、参照モデルと一致68・不一致0。
退行: s9t の gfx 器具の自作記録83腕×2走は直前版と判定が全件同一。verify_l1・l3_main・l3_screen_editor・conform_l4・ext_bank・vsync_regcheck・memmap・deffn・deftype・tabspc・wrap・widthbeep・widthvram・line・gfx・files/load/save/killname・clearcolor/colorattr/console/crtcpix/peekpoke/strfunc/strcmp・m6ib/ic/ie/ig/ih の各 selftest・conform_files/load/save/killname・check_cleanroom すべて rc=0（memmap の直書き指摘2件は 0FFFFh を10進へ直して解消）。
速度（自作ROM）: 全画面 BF 1回 約23フレーム、640本の斜め線 約5170フレーム。
容量: main 残126B（変化なし）、bank2 残976B（LINE で1291B使用。CIRCLE 用）、bank3 変化なし、0x79D7 不変。RAM は LINE_WORK 80B（SECTOR 等と排他）。

events.message:
M7: the Oric on the device (#7)

* M7: the Oric on the device

The machine's ROM loaded from the card by SHA-1, with the page that
names a missing one and offers the other machine; core 0 running the
Oric a field at a time, paced on the timer against an absolute deadline;
core 1 presenting decoded cells in dirty bands, with the perf line; the
PicoCalc keyboard into the matrix; the heartbeat. All four machines
boot to Ready at the ROM's own pace, checked on a Plus 2 W, and the
panel checked by the owner's eye. Tier 2 is now the default.

The record is in docs/milestones.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* M7: a card put in at the missing-ROM page is read again

The owner found, on a Pico 2 W with the release build, that a card put
in while the no-card page was up left the page there until a power
cycle. The guest has not started then, so core 1 reruns the ROM job on
each card change, and core 0 claims the image with a barrier on each
side before taking it. Checked on the Plus 2 W: the card put in at the
page, and the Atmos reached Ready without a reset.

events.title: tpoff: the T425's memory zeroed after use; t425wipe; xmanx leaves the T425 to a 32-bit desktop
events.message:
tpoff: the T425's memory zeroed after use; t425wipe; xmanx leaves the T425 to a 32-bit desktop

A reset doesn't clear the ATW800/2's T425: what tpsig worked on (the
certificate arithmetic of the sites visited) or a whole Helios session
stays in its memory, and the boot protocol's peeks read it back to
anyone who can open /dev/link1.

- tls/tpwipe: a 104-byte T425 program (tp/tpwipe.py assembles it),
  booted over the link, zeroes the ranges it is sent and answers each
  with the OR of what is left (1 MB in ~0.1 s). Tested on Hatari's T425
  core (exactly the ranges, nothing else) and on a real card: markers
  inside zeroed, outside kept; 3 MB in 445 ms.
- tpoff: once tpsig has been sent, the megabyte it uses is zeroed when
  the T425 is given up, at exit, and at a SIGHUP/SIGINT/SIGTERM nothing
  else handles. On the TT: ufetch's exit and a SIGTERM mid-validation
  both left it zeroed.
- The T425's first 2 MB are the card's memory past 2 MB (measured with
  peeks and pokes against the screen): a 32-bit desktop's bottom third,
  so tpsig landed on the screen and X's drawing on tpsig. xmanx reads
  the server's _ATW_FRAMEBUFFER and leaves the T425 alone when the card
  window is 4 MB (tpoff_forbid); terminal programs need transputer = off.
- t425wipe zeroes it all (-p: only what the T425 alone sees), and
  install.sh puts tools/S04t425wipe in /etc/rc2.d where there is a
  /dev/link1, so Atari System V's boot wipes before xdm (-p if X is up).

events.title: Keyboard: F6/F8/F10 no longer arrive as Shift+F6/F8/F10 (#16)
events.message:
Keyboard: F6/F8/F10 no longer arrive as Shift+F6/F8/F10 (#16)

Shift+F5/F7/F9 on the MEGA65 are F6/F8/F10 on the ST, so the core hides
Shift. It did that in the same clock cycle in which the F key appeared;
the IKBD scans the matrix column by column and sometimes still saw Shift,
which gave the scan codes 89/91/93 (Shift+F6/F8/F10). The function keys
now follow C_SETTLE after a change of the ST's Shift state, like the
symbol keys of "Keyboard as printed".

tb_keyboard: function key cases; the monitor also fails when the key
appears within half of C_SETTLE after the wrong Shift state (it failed on
the old code, passes now).

toolchain: 16.2.4, GCC to amiga16.2 134541b3 and binutils to 2.46

GCC moves from tinic/gcc 243a0096 (bebbo 60f21496 + sibcall/a0 fix) to
tinic/gcc a5166db4: bebbo amiga16.2 134541b3 plus the same fix, rebased
onto upstream's reworked m68k_is_ok_for_sibcall, which still allows an
argument in a0.  It still reports 16.2.0b.

binutils moves to bebbo amiga-2.46 a50544a9, the commit the diffs in
tools/patches/binutils-2.46/ are written against; the branch tip has moved
on and two of them no longer apply there.  A third diff joins them:
section-already-linked-outside-link.diff, a backport of bebbo 6fa839d0.
With the archive-index patch `ar` writes an index, and indexing any C++
COMDAT object then divides by zero in bfd_hash_lookup via
amiga_slurp_symbol_table; the toolchain build stopped at libsupc++.

- build-toolchain.sh: the two pins; LC_ALL=C, because newlib archives its
  objects in glob order and an en_US.UTF-8 Linux host put libc.a members
  in a different order, moving memcpy/__udivsi3 in every shipped image;
  the GMP/MPFR/MPC probe runs after the host block, so it sees Homebrew's
  CPPFLAGS (it refused every Mac build).
- check-toolchain-malloc.py: the new compiler's malloc.o hashes.  The
  pinned newlib malloc.cpp built by the 16.2.3 compiler reproduces the old
  hashes and built by this one reproduces the new; both hosts agree.
- fix-toolchain-crt0.py: the 32-bit libb32 displacement is hex only in the
  MIT form 2.46 prints; 2.39's Motorola `(16,a4)` is decimal, and reading
  it as hex refused three libb32 crt0s of the 16.2.3 toolchain.
- fetch-toolchain.sh, package-toolchain-mirror.sh, setup-amiga cache key:
  asset series 16.2.4 and its two sha256 values.
- Comments and mirror notes that explained the 2.39 pin; 16.2.4 notes.

events.title: cmt: support UniCMT CMTSPEED headers in MZT and custom pulse lengths
events.message:
cmt: support UniCMT CMTSPEED headers in MZT and custom pulse lengths

  Tapes prepared for the UniCMT cassette replacement may contain CMTSPEED
  headers between their parts: a 128-byte MZF header of type 00h named
  "CMTSPEED" with no body, carrying four 16-bit pulse lengths in
  microseconds at offset 30h (long high, long low, short high, short low).
  Such a header changes the speed of all following parts of the tape.

  MZT playback:
  - A CMTSPEED header is not played and is not listed as a block.
  - Every following block plays with the header's pulse lengths, generated
    with GDG clock resolution (not rounded to the nearest speed ratio),
    until the next header. Blocks before the first header use the default
    speed.
  - A header with a zero pulse length is ignored with a warning.
  - A header as the first block is applied (the real UniCMT does not play
    such a tape; the cause is unknown, so it is not emulated).

  Custom pulse lengths in Virtual CMT:
  - New speed value CMTSPEED_CUSTOM (10, appended to en_CMTSPEED; the
    values of the existing ratios are unchanged). cmtspeed_is_valid()
    still means "valid ratio", cmtspeed_is_custom() is new.
  - mztape: vstream from explicit pulse lengths, pulse lengths of a ratio,
    equivalent ratio, CMTSPEED header detection. The ratio path computes
    samples as before (byte-identical streams, covered by a test).
  - Default speed and per-block speed can be custom pulse lengths.
    "Custom pulses..." item in the speed selection of the Virtual CMT
    window and of the tape file list opens an editor with four lengths in
    microseconds, UniCMT 1x/2x/3x presets, Revert and the equivalent speed.
  - Config: [CMT] mz_cmtspeed = SPEED_CUSTOM and
    mz_custom_pulse_{long,short}_{high,low}_us.
  - MCP: cmt_set_property "custom_pulses" with pulses_us, speed value 10;
    cmt_tape_block_speed accepts pulses_us; cmt_tape_list reports
    block_speed and effective pulses_us; get_periph_cmt reports
    default_pulses_us and custom_pulses_us. Python wrapper:
    emu_cmt_set_speed(pulses_us=...) and
    emu_cmt_tape_set_block_speed(..., pulses_us=...).

  Fixes:
  - The default speed 2:1 (cp/m) was saved to the config as "(null)" and
    1:1 applied after restart; the same for 3:2, 9:7 and 25:14 set via MCP.
    The missing config keywords are added.
  - Tape file list rows reacted to the mouse under a modal popup opened
    from the list (row hover now requires the window to be hovered,
    with ImGuiHoveredFlags_NoPopupHierarchy).

  i18n: 12 new strings translated into 10 languages.

  Tests: cmtspeed, mztape (pulse lengths, header detection, stream
  equality with ratios, exact GDG tick counts), cmt_unicmt (MZT index with
  headers), mcp_dispatch, and e2e mcp_cmt_unicmt_mzt: the ROM loads the part
  after a 1x header but not after a 3x header, loads it again with
  per-block 1x pulses set via MCP, and the custom pulses survive a restart
  via the config.

  Docs: Changelog (cz/en), MCP tools overview (cz/en), agent CMT workflow,
  devdoc for cmtspeed, mztape and the periph/cmt resource.

events.title: CI: fix the two failures that blocked every release build on main
events.message:
CI: fix the two failures that blocked every release build on main

Linux (werror + ASan/UBSan): mc_apply_cpu() initialised its default options with
"{0, 0}", but MachineConfigApplyOpts has three fields since mms_already_set was
added, so -Werror=missing-field-initializers stopped the build. "{0}" zeroes all
of them.

events.title: Adapt netplay delay to measured RTT
events.message:
Adapt netplay delay to measured RTT

Bump the netplay protocol to v3 and track recent round-trip times during the match. The delay now follows the measured RTT instead of staying fixed at the handshake, keeping input scheduling gap-free when it moves and shrinking it only when the line is calm enough. Echo timestamps are advanced by the hold time to avoid counting the checksum wait as network latency, and peers using the older echo behavior are rejected cleanly rather than silently desynchronizing.

events.title: Remove the fused receive checksum
events.message:
Remove the fused receive checksum

Measured on an emulated 68020, three 100 MiB downloads per arm: it cost
1.7% throughput and 42% more lost frames. Folding the checksum into the
driver's copy cuts total work but lengthens the receive interrupt, which
is what decides whether a frame survives -- and a movem rewrite of the
loop made the loss worse, not better.

ip.rx_cksum is kept as an accepted no-op: the 4.1.8 betas published it,
so a tester's ENVARC: entry or a script must not fail. M_CSUM_DONE and
pkthdr.csum stay for now; retiring them changes MHLEN.
events.author: MW0MWZ

events.title: Support point-to-point links from the interface file alone
events.message:
Support point-to-point links from the interface file alone

A SLIP or PPP link needs a peer address, and no single config surface
could express one: DEVS:NetInterfaces/ had no destination=, the legacy
interfaces file had POINT2POINT but no addressing, and only the
ConfigureNetInterface command could set a peer.

destination= and pointopoint=yes now do both from the one file. The flag
is in IFF_CANTCHANGE so it rides a creation tag; the destination is
applied before the address, or in_ifinit() installs no route at all.
Without destination=, the gateway is offered as the peer and used only if
the stack really flagged the interface point-to-point.

CheckAmiTCPNGConfig also names the setting that makes a default route
unaddable -- a gateway outside address&netmask fails ENETUNREACH, and
the only clue at boot was "errno 51".

events.title: Issue device commands from a sacrificial task
events.message:
Issue device commands from a sacrificial task

WiFi_BeginIO runs the request inline on the caller, and S2_CONFIGINTERFACE
and friends can reach a bare WaitPort on the radio -- which traps the
network task for ever and only a reboot clears it. Control commands now go
through a throwaway task: a swallowed one costs that task, not the stack.
The per-packet path is untouched.

events.title: Raise the caller to the net task's priority, never lower it
events.message:
Raise the caller to the net task's priority, never lower it

ObtainSyscallSemaphore set the caller to the net task's priority outright,
so a program running above it was DEMOTED for the length of the call --
a latent inversion since 1993. Take the higher of the two instead.

events.title: 実装: グラフィックの土台 — PSET・PRESET・POINT・CLS・SCREEN（l4-graphics 第1版、l4-s9t）
events.message:
実装: グラフィックの土台 — PSET・PRESET・POINT・CLS・SCREEN（l4-graphics 第1版、l4-s9t）

根拠は仕様 l4-graphics.md 第1版（0e39cff）の第1〜8節と、そこから参照される l1-ipl.md のポート表（第5c・5d節）・l4-program.md。測定コミットは d59af51（訂正 715a5ec）。公式ROM・notes・measurements は見ていない。

実装
- PSET・PRESET・POINT 文・SCREEN 文・CLS の引数（0〜3）・式の中の POINT(x,y)／POINT(n) を bank2 の新ファイル src/ext_bank/gfx.asm に置いた。mainに増えたのは起動時の GFX 状態の0初期化9B と CLS_STMT の入れ替え（11B→8B）だけで、増減は 0x79D7 手前の埋め草（46B→40B）で吸収した。
- 文の語の表（fn_words）を deftype.asm から bank0 の新ファイル src/l4_basic/gfxhook.asm（0x6A40、bank0.asm と deffn.asm の間の空き）へ移し、PSET・PRESET・POINT・SCREEN（種別44〜47）を足した。種別44以上は bank0 から窓外中継で main の EXT_BANK_CALL を呼んで bank2 へ渡す。式の中の POINT( は FN_TRY_NUM（0x6B10）の入口で ts_try より先に見る。
- COLOR（widthbeep.asm wb_color_stmt）に、第4引数＝前景（xor 7 で持つ。ゼロ初期化で既定7）と第2引数＝背景（ポート0x54へ出す b。省略時0）の記録を足した。ポート出力・誤りは従来のまま。
- RAM は memmap.py に GFX 領域（0xFFBC、24B）。余りが無かったので測定専用の MEASURE_REGS（M6IA）と重ねて OVERLAPS に宣言（M6IA は定常ループからだけ使い、グラフィック文を実行しない）。VRAM番地の定数（MM_GVRAM_BASE・END_HI・END_LO）は CONSTANTS。

自作判断（仕様に無い・未測定）
- VRAMの書き方は公式の OUT 0x34/0x35（ビットの意味は未測定）ではなく、プレーン選択（OUT 0x5C〜0x5E、0x5F でメインRAMへ戻す）の読み書き。第2節の「同じ画素が立つことが本質」による。選択中は C000〜FFFF（CPUスタックと BASIC のRAMを含む）がグラフィックVRAMに替わるので、レジスタだけで完結させ、前後を DI／EI で囲む（BASIC は定常状態で常に割り込み許可なので EI は無条件）。cls 2・3 は 128B ごとに EI で割り込みを通す。
- 白黒（screen 1）はアクティブページ1枚へ点を立てる／消す。screen 2（640x400）は 0x31←bit0・bit4を落とし 0x53←0xF8 まで（描画は200ライン扱いのまま）。0x31 は MM_SCR_P31（垂直同期のたびに出される。WIDTH と共用）の bit を直して即出す。WIDTH は P31 を 0x19／0x39 へ書き戻す従来の動作のまま（screen の bit を消す）。
- STEP の相対座標が符号付き16bitを超えたら ERR 6、色の省略は PSET＝前景・PRESET＝背景、COLOR 第1引数のみ（背景省略）の COLOR は背景を0にする（従来のポート出力に合わせた）。pset の構文は最後まで正しいときだけ描く（ELSE の前も可）。式の中の POINT( の入れ子は x を CPU スタックで持って MM_GFX_TX/TY の上書きを避けた。
- 既存の整数リテラル 32768 が -32768 になる件（print 32768 → -32768、HEAD から）は直していない。直接モードの pset(32768,5) は ERR 6 にならない（プログラム中の pset は ERR 6）。

検証（自作ROM。全て自分で実行）
- l4_gfx_measure（公式60腕＋追補23腕＝83腕×2走）: 関門通過。判定項目 459件中 444一致・15不一致。不一致の15は仕様書第1版が予測外れとして記録している項目だけ（−32768の受理＝co-out2 の6、pset(x,y), の ERR 22 と step の LP・lit＝ps-syn の3、cls 0 の受理、cls 1.5→2、screen ,1／,,1 が LP を戻さない、screen 引数なしの ERR 22）。初回の測定では cls の塗りの上端定数を誤っていた（FA80→FE80、16000Bの手前）ため bg 系8腕が不一致だったのを修正して取り直した。
- 実描画: pset の色0〜7が (B=1,R=2,G=4) の位置・色で QUASI88 の画面ショットに出る（7色の四角、点の消去、point の値、cls 2 で点が消えてテキストが残る、白黒のページ別、screen 0,2 で非表示でも VRAM は残る）を確認。
- 個別 selftest 一式（l4 の deftype・tabspc・deffn・wrap・strfunc・strcmp・peekpoke・s5j・onwhile・pusing・rnd・memdyn・memlimit・editinv・hexconst・widthbeep・widthvram・colorattr・clearcolor・console、ext_bank、memmap、vsync_regcheck、atnexplog・sincos・sqr の bank と endtoend、conform_l4、verify_l1、l3_main、l3_screen_editor、l4_basic、m6ib・ic・ie・ig・ih の ROM 関門、files・load・save・killname の conform と z80 selftest、check_cleanroom、l4_gfx_selftest）が全て rc=0（52本）。
- 自作照合（measure の出力を HEAD の ROM の出力と比べた。19ツール×2走）: deftype・tabspc・s5j・widthvram・rnd・clearcolor・onwhile・memlimit・widthbeep・pusing・editinv は HEAD と tsv が完全に同一（rnd・clearcolor は HEAD でも関門失敗で同一、deftype・widthbeep・onwhile・memlimit・tabspc の predicted との不一致も HEAD と同じ）。deffn・wrap・peekpoke・strfunc・strcmp・hexconst は predicted と一致。colorattr は mix80-m2・mix40-m2（HEAD でも関門失敗）のカーソル更新コマンドの個数が1ずれただけ、console は cur_n・cur_pre（カーソル更新コマンドの個数）が多数の腕で1〜数ずれ、cls 系8腕で cursor 判定が入れ替わった（agree→differ 4・differ→agree 4）。画面の中身・誤り番号・ポート値は HEAD と同じ。原因は文の語の表に4語足した分の文照合の時間で、引数なし CLS を main だけの経路へ戻しても残った（確認後に戻した）。
- この回帰の測定は、最終ROMと bank2 の定数1バイト（END_HI 0xFA）だけ違うROMで行い（gfx の腕と selftest は最終ROM）、1バイトは cls 2・3 の塗りの範囲だけに効く。
- 作業領域: ../tmp/s9t-impl-work（DO_NOT_DELETE.md）。

容量計画（docs/design/graphics-capacity.md）の要旨
- 拡張ROMバンクは4本固定（0x32 の下位2ビット）で増やせない。LINE・CIRCLE・PAINT・GET@/PUT@・VIEW/WINDOW を合わせた見積もりは約3050B（推定）。
- bank2（残り2267B）に共通部＋LINE＋CIRCLE（約1400B）、bank1（1995B）に PAINT＋GET@/PUT@＋VIEW/WINDOW（約1500B）と共通部の複製（約400B、行単位の読み書きに絞れば約120B）。bank0 は語と中継だけ（gfxhook.asm の残り27B＋末尾65B）。main は触らない。グラフィック一式は収まる（bank1 は余裕100B未満で、複製を行単位にする案を PAINT の前に決める）。
- 共通部の入口（gx_coord・gx_parse_int・gx_color_arg・gx_stmt_end・gx_plot・gx_getpix・gx_addr・gx_clear_gfx と誤り終了）は同文書の第5節。

残り容量（自作ROM）: main 末尾126B（変更なし、測定ROM用116B以上を維持。0x79D7手前の埋め草は46B→40B）、bank0 65B（77Bから）、bank1 1995B、bank2 2267B（3400Bから）、bank3 27B（使わない）。QUASI88 の 0x79D7 は触れていない。bank3 に中継は置いていない。

run_all はその日の最後に回す（未実行）。private/ 由来の混入なし（check_cleanroom.sh rc=0）。

events.title: fix(jit): keep the JIT FPU preference while JIT or the FPU is off (#2399)
events.message:
fix(jit): keep the JIT FPU preference while JIT or the FPU is off (#2399)

#2398 stopped forcing compfpu on, but fixup_cpu() still cleared compfpu
whenever JIT was off or there was no FPU. Paths that switch JIT on later
then got CPU-only JIT although the user never turned the JIT FPU off:
--model plus -s cachesize, custom input events and the debugger's
"I cachesize=..." command, and restoring JIT after the debugger's MMU
suspension once preferences were normalised. The new defaults also
required fpu_mode == 0, which excluded the native host 80-bit mode.

Treat compfpu as a preference that only takes effect with JIT and an
FPU: fixup_cpu() keeps it (AMIBERRY); avoid_fpu, the ARM FPU compile
handlers and the startup log also require an FPU (the ARM table does not
flag FScc/FBcc as FPU opcodes, so build_comp() alone would not filter
them); the softfloat conflict check ignores FPU-less configs; and
fp_set_mode() keeps its shortcut while JIT is off. The GUI checkbox and
the JIT hotkey no longer clear it when JIT is switched off. Switching JIT
on, presets and uae-configuration default it on unless softfloat

events.title: intrinsic.h: add intrinsic_label for llvmz80/clang
events.message:
intrinsic.h: add intrinsic_label for llvmz80/clang

SDCC and sccz80 use a CALL-to-extern approach which relies on the
z88dk-z80asm linker tolerating unresolved symbols. lld does not.

For llvmz80/clang, intrinsic_label(name) emits a bare asm label
__asm__(#name ":") which places the symbol directly in the z80asm
output at the correct code address. z88dk-ticks finds the label in
the .map file and uses it as the start/stop address for T-state
measurement — identical semantics to the SDCC approach.

fix(jit): respect the JIT FPU setting instead of forcing it on (#2398)

check_prefs_changed_comp() set compfpu on whenever JIT was enabled
(761b15fd2). The JIT FPU checkbox and compfpu=false had no effect, and
since JIT FPU excludes softfloat, fixup_prefs() also reset any softfloat
FPU mode.

Remove the override and default the JIT FPU on only when JIT itself is
switched on, as WinUAE does, when there is an FPU and no softfloat mode:
- uae-configuration commands that enable JIT, unless the same command
  sets compfpu (the case 761b15fd2 was fixing);
- built-in presets (quickstart, WHDLoad), whose compfpu could still be
  cleared from an earlier non-JIT configuration;
- the GUI JIT checkbox, which no longer overrides a softfloat FPU mode.

and LM stations body metres from the design eye, clamped inside the cabin's

and D shortcuts wait) and LOOK/MOVE (key V; MOVE inverts the pad and relabels
its caps: slide, forward and back, down and up, reset eye). The held-cap
repeat delay drops to 250 ms.

moved centre, an offset a window view ignores); every existing capture is

events.title: fix(jit): let the interpreter run FMOVEM EAs the ARM JIT cannot compile (#2397)
events.message:
fix(jit): let the interpreter run FMOVEM EAs the ARM JIT cannot compile (#2397)

comp_fpp_opp() called op_illg() at compile time when comp_fp_adr() had
no compiled form for an FMOVEM effective address ((d8,An,Xn), (d16,PC),
(d8,PC,Xn)). Valid instructions then raised an F-line exception in the
guest and emitted no code. Quake 3 hits FMOVEM.X (d8,A1,Xn),FP2/FP5
while loading a map and died with 8000000B on ARM64 JIT only.

Fail the compilation instead, as the x86 JIT does, so the interpreter
runs the instruction and raises any real exception itself.

events.title: Fall back to the interpreter for FMOVEM EAs the ARM JIT cannot compile
events.message:
Fall back to the interpreter for FMOVEM EAs the ARM JIT cannot compile

comp_fpp_opp() called op_illg() at compile time when comp_fp_adr() had
no compiled form for an FMOVEM effective address ((d8,An,Xn), (d16,PC),
(d8,PC,Xn)). Valid instructions then raised an F-line exception in the
guest and emitted no code. Quake 3 hits FMOVEM.X (d8,A1,Xn),FP2/FP5 while
loading a map and failed with 8000000B on ARM64 JIT only.

Fail the compilation instead, as the x86 JIT does, so the interpreter
runs the instruction and raises any real exception itself.

events.title: RTC default is wall-clock; ticks mode only on request and in unit tests
events.message:
RTC default is wall-clock; ticks mode only on request and in unit tests

The RTC time base defaulted to ticks: one clock pulse per 10550 executed
instructions, which is real time only at 0.5275 MIPS. Unthrottled on a
modern host the pulse came about 350 times a second instead of 50, and a
guest that counts 50 pulses per second ran its time of day seven times too
fast (NORD TSS: 70 s of host time became 7 min 38 s of DATE; TIME-USED
agreed, since both count the same interrupts). With wall mode, one pulse per
20 ms of host time, 60 s gave DATE exactly 1 min 0 s.

Default is now wall everywhere: the device (rtc_wall_clock_mode), the
machine config default and its .ini writer, the CLI (--rtc default, option
comment, help text), the wasm SetRTCMode comment, the glass machine form
(wall listed first and written when nothing is chosen), the project
instructions file, docs/command-line-options.md and docs/HOWTO_DEBUGGING.md.
--rtc=ticks and [machine] rtc = ticks still select the deterministic
instruction-count mode. The unit tests are the exception: test_rtc.c selects
ticks mode explicitly before its pulse counts, and test_machine_config.c
expects wall as the default. 22 of 22 tests pass.
events.author: Ronny Hansen

events.title: Drum test: put the function code in control-word bits 11-12
events.message:
Drum test: put the function code in control-word bits 11-12

The device has decoded the function from bits 11-12 since the drum fix in
b837f66 (TSS1 XDRUM builds the control word with SHA ZIN 13 octal = 11), but
the test helper ctrl_go still shifted it to bits 13-14, so every WRITE the
test issued ran as a READ and three checks failed. Shift by 11 and say so in
the comment. 22 of 22 tests pass.

events.title: LREGBL: decide "returning from a trap handler" from the C flag as well as the DIT
events.message:
LREGBL: decide "returning from a trap handler" from the C flag as well as the DIT

NDIX returns from a trap handler with LREGBL, not RETT, and LREGBL is where the
handler's ENTT-saved CALL/ENT* sequence entry is popped (nd500_trap_seq_pop_top).
53d9008 made the test "has[0] && nd500_is_in_trap_handler()", which reads the DIT's
ITH byte once a DIT is configured. The NDIX kernel stores 0 into that byte itself
(physical DITBASE+187) on its way out of the handler, so by the time LREGBL runs
the DIT says "not in a handler" while the C flag in_trap_handler is still set.
The pop was skipped at every one of 465 returns measured. A CALL whose callee's
first instruction page-faulted (demand paging) then lost its pending-call state,
and the retried ENTS raised a false Instruction Sequence Error. In vi that is
_ovbeg at 0xFC15: "Memory fault - core dumped" right after "vi file".

The test is now the C flag OR the DIT byte, so NDIX (flag only) and the octobus
lane (DIT carries the flag across a park) both work. It is made before the
register block is applied, because that block reloads CED, and the DIT byte
cleared is the handler's domain, not the resumed one's.

Found by bisecting: vi worked in the 2026-08-03 build, 952441d passes and 53d9008
fails. With this change vi starts and runs in NDIX, the nd500x test suite passes
47 of 47, and the NDIX boot still reaches login:.
events.author: Ronny Hansen
