events.title: Add experimental three-button joystick support and update documentation
events.message:
Add experimental three-button joystick support and update documentation

Add optional three-button Amiga joystick (JOY3) support and update the
documentation for it, for the CD32 pad and for the already committed shop
and scanner fixes.

Configuration (src/amiga/amiga_cfg.h, src/amiga/amiga_cfg.cpp):
- New joy3 = OFF/ON key (default OFF) plus three configurable assignments
  joy3_button1 / joy3_button2 / joy3_button3 for the physical DB9 pins
  6 / 9 / 5. They accept the same action names as the CD32 block (FIRE,
  SPECIAL_SELECT, MEGA_BOMB, PAUSE, CANCEL, NONE) and keep the safe
  built-in defaults (FIRE / SPECIAL_SELECT / MEGA_BOMB) on unknown or
  missing values. An existing cfg without the keys keeps the defaults and
  is never extended automatically; a file created from scratch gets a new
  "JOYSTICK / 3 BUTTON" block below the CD32 block.
- Documented the shared action semantics: FIRE fires the primary weapon
  together with the selected secondary weapon and SPECIAL_SELECT changes
  (cycles) the secondary weapon. This corrects the earlier, wrong
  "fire the selected special weapon" wording and is applied consistently
  in amiga_cfg.h, the generated cfg template and the examples.

Input mode and precedence (src/amiga/amiga_sdl_stubs.h):
- A session input mode (NONE / PLAIN / CD32 / JOY3) is chosen once at
  startup and kept separate from the saved preferences, so a runtime
  fallback never rewrites amiga.cfg.
- Precedence: NOJOY / JOYSTICK=OFF disables all joystick input before
  anything else; cd32 = ON takes precedence over joy3 = ON and still uses
  lowlevel.library game controller mode. A failed game controller request
  falls back to plain joystick mode for that session only and never
  silently switches to the experimental JOY3 mode. cd32 = OFF with
  joy3 = ON keeps SJA_TYPE_JOYSTK (JOY3 is never a game controller).
- Buttons 1 and 2 are read as the classic lowlevel lines (RED / BLUE);
  button 3 is read through potgo.resource on port 2 pin 5 (POTGOR,
  DATRX 1<<12 / OUTRX 1<<13). The file opens its own AmigaPotgoBase so a
  missing potgo.resource degrades to "button 3 off" instead of aborting
  startup.
- The line is requested with AllocPotBits and its pull-up driven with
  WritePotgo; only the bits actually granted are remembered. If DATRX is
  not granted the game runs in a two-button limited mode (buttons 1/2
  still active) and the startup log notes it. The allocation is released
  exactly once via FreePotBits from SDL_Quit() on the normal exit path
  only, before the gameport is reinitialized and lowlevel.library is
  closed; the setup is idempotent and an error path frees nothing. The
  first samples after the pull-up is enabled are ignored to let the line
  capacitor settle (up to 300 us).
- JOY3 buttons feed the same shared action machine as the CD32 pad, so
  FIRE / SPECIAL_SELECT / MEGA_BOMB reach the game through the action
  state, PAUSE through the pause edge and CANCEL through the synthetic
  ESC. The shared menu / store RETURN and SPACE keys are produced there
  too, giving the same actions in gameplay, menus, the shop, the pause
  window and cancel handling.

Shared controller handling (Amiga_ConfigActionActive):
- The configurable-controller predicate (CD32 or JOY3) now gates the code
  shared by both devices: the action table, the synthetic RETURN / ESC /
  SPACE keys, the PAUSE edge and the context handling. Directions keep
  flowing through the classic joystick path into AmigaJoyState (one path),
  and the legacy A/B/d-pad aliases stay disabled so they cannot bypass the
  assignment table.
- Double input is prevented: the classic RED -> RETURN and BLUE -> B
  workarounds are skipped for JOY3, and SDL_GameControllerGetButton returns
  0 for both configurable controllers. A held button is not carried across
  a gameplay / menu / modal boundary (AmigaCD32BlockedMask), the JOY3
  button-3 bit joins the debounce / phantom machinery (7 clear-streak
  entries) and an invalid port sample releases the JOY3 actions it was
  holding.

Configuration file and tests:
- Volumes saved from the in-game Options still update amiga.cfg in place
  and preserve comments, unknown keys, manual edits, key order, spacing
  and line endings, including the JOY3 assignments.
- tests/amiga_cfg_test.cpp extended: old cfg without JOY3 keys keeps the
  defaults and is not extended on save; mixed-case keys and all action
  names are parsed; missing / invalid values keep the safe defaults;
  volume save rewrites volumes only (comments, CRLF and unknown keys are
  kept, joy3 lines stay unique); a file created from scratch contains the
  JOYSTICK / 3 BUTTON block below the CD32 block with the built-in
  defaults.

Documentation:
- CHANGELOG.md, README.md, README_AMIGA.md, README_AMIGA_PL.md,
  raptor.readme, docs/amiga.cfg.example and docs/porting-analysis.md
  describe joy3, the disable precedence, the new JOYSTICK / 3 BUTTON
  block, the corrected weapon wording, the dedicated shop input context
  and the scanner endianness fix, and clearly mark JOY3 as experimental.
- Documentation of the shop controls and the boss energy scanner fix
  (the boss maximum health converted with LE_LONG, current health kept in
  native byte order) is updated only - that code is already committed in
  5739d56 ("Fix CD32 shop controls and boss energy scanner").
- Credits: thanks added for PPA user Solo Kazuki for testing on real Amiga
  hardware and suggesting CD32 / compatible gamepad and three-button
  joystick support.

Validation:
- git diff --check passed.
- The amiga.cfg configuration unit tests pass (bash
  tests/run_amiga_cfg_test.sh).
- The m68060/68881 build completed successfully before this commit; the
  source is unchanged since that run, so it was not rebuilt.
- CD32 / CD32-compatible gamepad gameplay use is reported working on real
  Amiga hardware; the dedicated CD32 shop controls and the scanner fix
  still await runtime verification on real hardware.
- Three-button joystick support is experimental: button 3 and the
  lowlevel.library / potgo interaction still need verification on real
  Amiga hardware. A successful build does not confirm that the third
  button works.
- cd32 = ON uses lowlevel.library game controller mode; the native Sega
  gamepad serial protocol is not implemented.

SEP. It now starts there before SEP and after it. A situation's own vehicle
target (in_target 0) keeps the scene's start after SEP, so the docked stack's
default view (scene 8) is unchanged.

Golden: s3-docked-ext-lm, s3-postsep-ext-csm and s8-tgt-lm (External on a
picked vehicle after SEP) change.

runtime_profiles.name: Source and upstream runtime evidence
runtime_profiles.notes: Upstream describes II+ 48 KB/DOS 3.3 for Arkabreakout/classic ports and enhanced IIe or IIc 128 KB/ProDOS for ChromaBreak, with keyboard/paddle or AppleMouse controls. The bootstrap explicitly rejects NMOS machines for ChromaBreak. These are source/author requirements, not independently verified runnable minima.

runtime_profiles.name: Pinball Construction Set adaptation
runtime_profiles.notes: The root README states Apple II+ with 48 KB or Apple //c, using mouse or joystick. This is an upstream requirement for the Pinball adaptation, not independently verified hardware compatibility.

project.status: Native game collection with bootable outputs and upstream tests; independently unbuilt
project.notes: Identity: The creator’s repository contains seven native Apple II games, including original Arkabreakout/ChromaBreak and ports of POM1 games. Reviewed concrete Arkabreakout gameplay assembly, Snake C implementation, ChromaBreak bootstrap/build, and Chess documentation. This is one repository-level collection record, not seven inflated entries. Classification: Native Apple II source collection and ports. Arkabreakout assembles a standalone BRUN binary and DOS 3.3 disk; ChromaBreak builds a ProDOS system file. The bundled a2run/a2shot emulator code serves tests and is not embedded in the games. LOGO, demos and generic dev tooling are incidental to this game-scoped record. Source CPU: The README and Snake header identify POM1 Apple-1/GEN2 versions as predecessors, and Chess documents reused POM1 rules code. Those predecessor files were not independently inspected, so no source CPU is inferred from the target assembly or Apple-1 label. Target CPU: Arkabreakout’s game.s explicitly specifies NMOS 6502 and contains native gameplay assembly. ChromaBreak’s Makefile passes --cpu 65c02; boot.s starts with a 6502 CPU probe and then selects .setcpu "65C02", rejecting an NMOS IIe. These establish separate 6502 and 65C02 outputs, not a single machine minimum. Build: The reviewed game Makefiles invoke ca65/ld65 or cl65 and construct bootable DOS 3.3/ProDOS disks. The README claims deterministic rebuilds and emulator-based tests, but those claims were not independently reproduced; byte_exact remains null. Limitations: Static primary-source review only. No candidate code, build, emulator, gameplay, hardware test or byte comparison was executed; all independent build flags remain null. Runtime profiles: Upstream describes II+ 48 KB/DOS 3.3 for Arkabreakout/classic ports and enhanced IIe or IIc 128 KB/ProDOS for ChromaBreak, with keyboard/paddle or AppleMouse controls. The bootstrap explicitly rejects NMOS machines for ChromaBreak. These are source/author requirements, not independently verified runnable minima. Limitations: Profiles preserve directly observed requirements/author claims only; no independent runtime hardware validation was performed. AI: The latest commit explicitly includes Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>; the same named tool is present in the inspected recent commit sample. This is development-AI evidence, separate from the chess opponent AI. Relationships: The README and source headers explicitly derive the classic games from VERHILLE Arnaud’s POM1 work. Chess credits cc65-Chess for board/piece art and its Apple II port, but identifies its engine as POM1 rules code; this is not another copy of the already catalogued cc65-chess-stewbc-native. GPL-3.0 code, Skinner Microban levels, CC-BY-3.0 sprites and separate Apple ROM/DOS rights are disclosed. No blanket original-authorship or permissive-license claim is made. Normalized roots were screened programmatically against prior-roots.json before file review; current catalogue titles/subjects were checked for aliases. This is bounded lineage review, not proof of complete originality. events.message:
feat(kernel): the LM station wherever an LM exists, occluded in the SLA (#70 option C)

hdr(22)'s LM-station bit now follows the LM's existence (LMEX: placed, or a
state of its own or the CSM's), so the page stops offering a station that
silently falls back. Where the scene has not placed the LM, LMSTPL places it
for the station: docked to the CSM after SEP (STKPL), the descending and
landed LM of scene 5 (LMDESC), or at its own state at any range (VEHPLD).
Before SEP the LM is stowed in the closed SLA: the frame draws only the plot
frame, the window overlay and the cabin, and letters LM IN THE CLOSED SLA,
OCCLUDED UNTIL SEP (ISLA; ours, the deck has no SLA-panel event).

Golden: hdr(22) 5 -> 7 in 49 captures; s4-lm-docked and s3-lm-eject now draw
the docked LM's station; seven LM-station cases added. New shot lm-station-sla.

events.title: fix(traj): put the ascent table's low rows on the pad's geodetic footing (#105)
events.message:
fix(traj): put the ascent table's low rows on the pad's geodetic footing (#105)

The ascent table's latitudes are geocentric, while the coastlines, the
pad's mark (DPAD) and the launch complex stand on geodetic latitudes
placed on the drawn sphere, so the vehicle lifted off 17.9 km south of
the mark. TABRV now makes each geocentric row below 50 n mi geodetic.
The latitude is taken whole rather than blended by altitude like the
radius: a blend leans the climb south 0.19 m per metre up (114 m off
the pad's axis at 10 s, 739 m at 30 s, failing the lift-off check);
whole rows put the 0.16 deg step on the 2:42 to 7:40 arc, some 1000 km
down range.

PADAX no longer carries the offset: the foot is under PADEF's place at
the lift-off state's radius less the stack's height, without holding
and turning the state Earth fixed.
events.author: aaronsb

events.title: fix(traj): square the CIRC leg's plane basis to its radius (#105)
events.message:
fix(traj): square the CIRC leg's plane basis to its radius (#105)

SNSET built the parking-orbit circle from the state card's radius and
velocity directions as they stood, so the card's flight-path angle
(Apollo 11 0.011 deg, Apollo 8 -0.001 deg) skewed the circle: its
radius wandered by about 1e-4 of itself. VORTH squares the heading to
the radius, as #80 did for LOCALVERT.

events.message:
TSS machine, Welcome window, machine pages, CDC disk type, ND-5000 pack, drum fix

Five built-in machines now: TSS joins ND-100, ND-5000, BSD 2.11 and
500 NDIX-C.

TSS - NORD Time Sharing System 3.0 (1973) on an MMS1 ND-100 with the CDC
cartridge system disc at IOX 500 and the swapping drum at IOX 540, booted
with the disc's LOAD button. C: an INI key [machine] mms = 1|2 (the
missing INI half of --mms; CLI wins), a "[boot] device = cdc" form
(BOOT_CDC, validated against [runtime] cdc, described as boot.cdc and a
runtime {cdc, drum} object), the WASM frontend installs the CDC disc and
drum from [runtime] like the native one and BootFrom type 5 presses
LOAD. JS: the TSS profile (terminals 5-10 = TSS TTY5-TTY10 - their IOX
addresses and ident codes match TSS's N10 table; TTY2-4 want idents 5-7
the ND-100 cards at 0310-0330 never answer), the disc fetched and a 1 MB
zero drum written into MEMFS before Init. images/TSS-CDC.IMG.bz2 is the
TSS repo's TEL10 jump-start disc (10 teletypes, NTY=12) built after the
clock and SET-REGISTER fixes of 08-OCT-2026, padded to 4 MB.

Drum controller: the function field of the control word is bits 11-12,
not 13-14 - TSS's XDRUM builds it with SHA ZIN 13 and a DAP stop showed
004007 for a WRITE. Decoding 13-14 ran every WRITE as a READ, which
only shows on the first process swap-out (a second TSS terminal) and
wiped TSS's context block. Verified: console + TERMINAL 5 both logged in,
WHO-IS-ON lists lines 1 and 5, in Direct and Worker mode.

Welcome window (first visit, Help > Welcome, "Show this every time" in
localStorage nd100x-welcome-show): how to start a machine, a card per
machine with "Select and start" (disabled while a machine runs) and
"Read more", the View, Help and SINTRAN menus; Help > Machines opens a
page per machine (what it is, using it, history with sources) - all from
data/machines.json.

HDD Disk Manager: fifth disk type "cdc" with its own tab, count, badge,
Import tag and catalog filter (no NDFS); Machine Setup gets a "CDC
cartridge disc" row choosing a library image for [runtime] cdc, staged
from the library at power-on.

ND-5000 boots its own pack, images/ND5000-SMD0.IMG.bz2 (SINTRAN III
VSX/500 L prepared for the ND-5000), listed in disk-catalog.json.

Fix CD32 shop controls and boss energy scanner

Add a dedicated STORE context for configurable CD32 input:
- Map SPECIAL_SELECT to Space only in the shop to toggle BUY/SELL.

- Release synthetic Space and block held inputs across context changes.

Fix boss energy percentage calculation on big-endian Amiga:

- Leave scanner ownership, rendering and save data unchanged.

Validation:
- git diff --check passed.

Checkpoint before implementing three-button joystick support.

M6: board bring-up and the card (#6)

* M6: board bring-up and the card

pico-ace's port drivers copied and renamed, brought up in HW §10's
order on a Plus 2 W, with no guest yet (design.md §15.2 M6).

- southbridge.*, kbd.*, log.*, lcd.*, sd.*, diskio.c, storage.*,
  fatfs/ffconf.h: copied from pico-ace and renamed.

  presenter comes with M7.

  names it by SHA-1; the slot is debounced, and a card put back is read
  again.

  log, busy_wait_us_32 only. main.c: core 0 logs every key event, from
  the keyboard or the UART, with its cell, and a heartbeat.

- Checked on the board: the pattern, every key, the UART's keys, the
  three ROMs recognised from the card, 655 s with zero I2C errors.

events.title: fix(kernel): make LOCALVERT's frame orthonormal off a circular orbit
events.message:
fix(kernel): make LOCALVERT's frame orthonormal off a circular orbit

LOCALVERT built its boresight and up from the radius and velocity
directions as they came. Off a circular orbit the velocity is not square
to the radius, so after TLI the frame was short and nearly degenerate:
External on the docked LM drew an empty frame (#70, patched in VIEWPT
label 21) and Apollo 8's window on the transearth coast drew nothing
(#65). VORTH now makes the horizontal square to the radius (Gram-Schmidt)
in both LOCALVERT branches and in VINIT's Earthrise azimuth, leaving a
pair already square within 1e-12 untouched so lunar-orbit frames stay bit
for bit. VIEWPT's label 21 is redundant and removed (captures identical
with and without it). Two golden cases and a shot cover the transearth
window.

Closes #80, closes #65

events.message:
feat(fusion): photographs travel with their reel as photo events (#75)

Fusion read one global table across missions and kept its fits in code, so
picking an Apollo 8 frame with Apollo 11 mounted silently switched tapes. Each
scenario reel now carries its own photo events: data/photos.tsv names each
row's reel, tools/photos.py checks the rows with a situation and tools/pack.py
packs them as page.json photos (frame, situation, g.e.t. or bracket, lens, our
fit, note, credit, source) with the photograph a media member, media/<frame>.jpg.

Media are the reel's, not the notebook's: media/ beside notebook/ in the source
folder and at the package root. The rule of #29 slice g becomes every media
member named by an attach or a photo event; pack.py, notebook.py and reelpkg.js
hold it alike and the selftest plants a fault for each rule. The packed copies
are reduced by hand (tools/photo_pack.py), so the build no longer needs Pillow;
the Apollo 8 notebook's clipped print is now the same copy Fusion lays over.

Fusion lists the mounted tape's photographs only; a pick stays on the tape and
a photo= link mounts the photograph's reel first, a fresh run. Photo events are
a third kind in the event listing, the event list and the run sheet, may be
quick views, and a notebook's print of one opens Fusion at its moment.

events.title: M5: the keyboard on the host (#5)
events.message:
M5: the keyboard on the host (#5)

* M5: the keyboard on the host

The held set, keymap and paced replay adapted from pico-ace to the
Oric's 8x8 matrix, and the matrix settled by sweeping both ROMs
(design.md §2.4, §9, §15.2 M5).

- keymatrix.*, keymap_picocalc.c: each host Shift to its own SHIFT,
  Ctrl to CTRL, Tab to FUNCT; a key pressed with a modifier, or one
  whose entry asserts SHIFT, reaches the matrix a field behind it.
- test_keyboard: all 64 cells in both ROMs alone and with each
  modifier, caught at the handler's STX #02DF; every table entry
  through the held set; hold and gap from six phases with controls;
  a typed 60-line program; type-ahead.
- test_keymap: the table's invariants and the held set, no ROM needed.
- The harness types through PicoCalc events and the held set.
- §2.4 is the sweep's table; §9.2, §9.3 and §16's keyboard rows
  settled; EL §7.1 gains two lessons.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Bind the keys the PicoCalc sends only as Shift chords

Shift+Enter, Esc, Del, Up, Down and Tab arrive as Insert, Break, End,
PgUp, PgDn and Home (hardware-notes.md §6.3). Canonicalisation paired
their presses with their releases but nothing bound them, so Shift+Enter
typed nothing. Each is now its base key's cell with SHIFT, as the Oric's
typist would press it; SHIFT changes none of those keys' codes (§2.4).
Alt+I, also Insert, still reaches nothing.

test_keymap checks every Shift alternate has an entry and drives its
cell, and fails 13 checks without them; test_keyboard types them through
both ROMs. Found in review on PR #5.

events.title: fix(rtg): never hand a zero-copy VRAM surface to the native renderer (#2396)
events.message:
fix(rtg): never hand a zero-copy VRAM surface to the native renderer (#2396)

With ZeroCopy, the amiga surface wraps the RTG screen's VRAM. lockscr() returned surface->pixels to the chipset renderer unconditionally, so any native frame drawn while that surface was current overwrote the guest's 32-bit RTG bitmap (#2392). #2393 removed the reported trigger by always suspending chipset emulation under RTG, but the native-to-RTG switch vsync still locks the draw buffer before check_nocustom() runs.

lockscr() now refuses a native lock whose surface lies inside any RTG bank. p96_is_vram_pointer() uses a range test because p96_is_zero_copy_surface() only matches the current XYOffset.

feat(notebook): finding slips, attach blocks, media members (#29 slice g2)

The binders are engineering notebooks: later understanding is added beside
the text, not written over it, and prints from the tape and photographs are
held to the page. Two fenced blocks carry that, `finding` (date, cite, text)
and `attach` (source media/<file>, figures/<name>.svg or golden=<case>;
style plate, clip, tape or insert; finish photo, film or copy; a caption;
a photograph's credit and cite), and a new reel member type `media` carries
the photographs, raster only by their own first bytes, each attached.
tools/notebook.py, tools/pack.py and web/src/reelpkg.js hold one rule; the
viewer builds slips and prints from DOM nodes and text only, photographs as
data: URLs, and page.css gives each style and finish its look.

Both notebooks use it: a finding each (TN D-6853 printed pp. 3 and 4), the
LOI figure as a plate, the Earthrise golden render as a taped film print
beside AS08-14-2383 clipped on (NASA, images.nasa.gov), the late-descent
render as a film plate, and a copy of MSC IN 69-FM-197 printed p. 152 as an
insert. The selftest plants nine faults both readers refuse and crafted
blocks that must stay inert; six shots show the styles and finishes.

events.title: M4: video on the host (#4)
events.message:
M4: video on the host (#4)

* M4: video on the host

The ULA's picture as design.md §7 describes it: ula.c decodes the window
#9800-#BFFF, the mode at the field's start and the blink phase into a
cell per byte, generates RGB565 rows from cells, and diffs decoded cells
into dirty bands. oric_run_field runs the mode scan at each field's end
and takes the next field's length from it; oric_video_take fills a frame
for the pool, copied from pico-ace. font_from_rom expands each ROM's
table, and the missing-ROM page has X.Org's public-domain 5x8 as its
fallback, generated by tools/mkfont.py.

Nine golden scenes, drawn with the fallback font so CI runs them, were
viewed before committing and are drawn identically, pixel for pixel, by
Oricutron's own ULA (tools/trace/oricutron-render.c, tools/render-diff.sh).
The dirty bands pass 400 random edits where the VRAM-byte diff, the
control, goes stale; the mode scan agrees with the decode on 2,000 random
screens; the pool passes 100,000 transitions; the ROM font equals what
both ROMs write. Eleven planted bugs caught. design.md §16's video rows
are bounded against Oricutron and MAME; milestones.md has the record.

* Blink phase: say which frame it is, and pin the boundary

oric_video_take copies the frame the ULA draws next (design.md §11.1),

The comments in oric.h said 'the frame just finished', which invites the
off-by-one Codex read into it; they now say what the code does.
test_snappool holds frame 31 shown and frame 32 hidden, and fails with
the phase taken one field later.

feat(notebook): binder reading view, light mode default (#29 slice g1)

The operator's reading view for the scenario notebooks (2026-10-07):
LIGHT, now the default, is an open three-ring binder lying on a desk,
typed pages on its rings, one page on a narrow viewer and a two-page
spread on a wide one; DARK is the viewer as it was. The look is ours,
after the typed MSC internal notes.

It is mostly a stylesheet: #libmd is a size container, the notebook
flows into CSS columns of a fixed page height, and the paper, punched
holes and binding shade are backgrounds that scroll with the columns,
one tile a view, so at rest the holes sit under the binder's rings.
Script is the paging (BACK/NEXT, PgUp/PgDn, arrows, Home/End; a jump,
no animation), the page count read from the end marker's column, a
blank last page for an odd spread, and the remembered toggle
(prefs.notebook; ?notebook=light|dark for a visit). notebook.js is
unchanged; library.js adds the two wrappers and the paging plate.

The dark viewer's rules are scoped to #libmd.dark and render the run
sheet pixel for pixel as before. The library header's buttons now wrap
on a phone. Six shots: notebook-light-page, -spread, -paged, -end,
notebook-dark and notebook-dark-url.

\s+... pattern and the element head with \s*(/?)\s*, both quadratic on a
run of whitespace: one tag of 200K spaces took 15-30 s in the page and
minutes in Python.

Each tag body is now read once, left to right: a head, then attributes
one at a time, each anchored where the last ended (sticky /y in JS,
Pattern.match(body, pos) in Python), then an end. No two parts can trade
characters, so the scan is linear. Same rule on both sides:

- whitespace is XML's (space, tab, CR, LF), not \s, which differed
  between JS and Python (U+FEFF, U+001C-1F);
- a byte order mark may lead the XML declaration, nowhere else; Python
  refused it where the page's TextDecoder drops it;
- numeric entities take ASCII digits ([0-9], not Python's Unicode \d);
- a stray / mid-tag is refused (it was accepted when attributes were
  stripped out of the tag before the leftovers were checked).

The selftest's packages line times both on six hostile figures (200K
spaces in four places, a BOM before the declaration and after
whitespace): each judged alike within 200 ms.

events.title: M3: the Oric on the host (#3)
events.message:
M3: the Oric on the host (#3)

* M3: the AY's bus, the keyboard, NMI and the field; the harness and the test ROM

The VIA wired as both ROMs drive it: CA2 = BC1, CB2 = BDIR, AY port A's
zero bits enable keyboard columns, PB3 high is a key down. sha1 copied
from pico-ace, romset by SHA-1, oric_power_on, oric_nmi, oric_run_field
with the field's length as configuration.

test/host/guest.c finds the ROMs by SHA-1 and types through the ROM's
own key table. test_boot: both ROMs reach Ready on 16K and 48K, PRINT
2+2 prints 4, T1 interrupts at 100 Hz, RND repeats from power-on, NMI
keeps the program and RESET does not, and a 16K machine without the
mirror never boots. test/asm/oric_test_rom.s proves the wiring in CI
without an Oric ROM.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* M3: the trace diff against Oricutron, and the VIA's timing it found

tools/trace/: oric-trace (our core) and oricutron-trace (Oricutron at
002279f, built from a checkout by build-oricutron.sh with a hook in its
6502 step and a headless driver), and tools/trace-diff.py.

The diff found two bugs in the core, both fixed: the VIA was ticked
through an instruction after an access on its last cycle, starting T1
three cycles early; and the IRQ was polled with the VIA at the
instruction's end rather than the penultimate cycle. The 6502 now records
which cycle a page-#03 access falls on (slow path only), the VIA is
brought to it first, and the VIA runs two cycles behind at boundaries.

It found two errata in Oricutron, corrected by name in its build:
ORICUTRON_NO_I_DELAY and ORICUTRON_BRANCH_PAGE. Boot and PRINT 2+2 then
agree line for line, cycles included, on all four machines.

design.md §5.3, §13.4 and §16 updated with what M3 settled; the M3
record in milestones.md; lessons in emulator-lessons.md; CI installs
cc65 before configuring so the test ROM is built.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* M3: the schematics, the service manual and the ULA guide in §16

Oric's BN0130 (main board), BN0138 (keyboard) and the 1984 service
manual settle the AY's wiring, the reset lines and NMI, the tape lines,
the VIA's decode through page #03, the 16K mirror (A14 and A15 ignored),
and FUNCT's cell (column 4, row 5); Mike Brown's ULA guide and
Oricutron disagree on the 60 Hz field and the blink rate, now marked.
BN0136, the Microdisc's controller, is recorded for M14. The documents
themselves stay in the gitignored reference/oric/.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* M3 done: CI ran the test ROM green

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Codex review: the AY stays deselected; GNU make's link error

A latch with a select code other than 0000 deselects the AY until a good
latch: writes and reads are ignored, where before a write after it
reached the previously latched register. test_ay8912 checks it, and
fails with the old behaviour planted.

build-oricutron.sh accepted only BSD make's form of the expected link
failure; GNU make 4 writes '*** [Makefile:NNN: oricutron]'.

The trace diff still agrees on all four machines.

  69.76% (fz 82.08 -> 90.52). Five structural fixes read off the original asm: the
  top validation loop is a for (ours was a do/while with a duplicated guard), the

- 0x42e8e0 CarPhysics_IntegrateWheelSuspension (FixedPoint.cpp, 73.53% -> exact):
  a FixVector of deltas has to be materialised component by component into an
  explicit temp (t = a - b; d = t - mid) instead of writing d = (a - b) - mid,
  which MSVC6 folds into the dependent expression; and the inline-asm helper home
  for a member operand needs a reused local (f = v.y; f = FixMul(f, k)).
- 0x465530 CarSkid_ClearWheelTrails (StageObjects.cpp, 96.77% -> exact): the
  trailing clear is a do/while that advances a SECOND pointer local (q = p; ...;
  p = q) with a signed pointer compare; one pointer local kept the anchor in edx
  with no copy chain and emitted add edx,0x30 plus an unsigned jb.
- 0x424af0 ForceFeedback_ComputeRoadNoise (StageTiming.cpp, 58.82% -> exact):
  split x = FixMul(a, b) + field; into two statements, so MSVC6 emits
  add eax,[mem] instead of homing the sum; assign the accumulator before the
  other FixMul operand so slot and operand order follow the source order.

- 窓: 下端=min(開始行+行数-1, 限界)、限界=行数-2（ファンクションキー表示あり）／行数-1（f=0）。窓の外の行は print のスクロールでも cls でも保持。窓の下の行から打つと窓がスクロールしカーソルは動かない。cls 後のカーソルは (窓の上端,0)。width が受理されると窓は全画面に戻る（f は保つ）。locate は窓の外へも書ける（限界まで）。
- カラー/白黒: モードが変わるときだけ width と同じ手順で画面を消す（白黒へ戻す手順は 0x23/0x22・P5=0x13）。同じモードなら何もしない。窓は保つ。
- 状態は1か所: 窓の下端=MM_SCR_MAXROW（既存）、上端=MM_SCR_WTOP、指定行数=MM_SCR_WN、f=MM_SCR_MODE bit1。memmap.py に CONSOLE 領域2Bを追加し CPU スタックを 386B→384B（下限384Bのまま、スタック上端不変）。作業値は SECTOR 先頭（式評価中の MM_FN_AUX 上書きを避ける）。
- main の SCROLL・CLS_SCREEN の本体をバンク0へ移し（wb_scroll・wb_cls、入口 0x7A44・0x7A48）、NEWLINE は窓の下端以降でスクロール後にカーソルを動かさない形に。窓が全画面のとき書き込みの並びは従来と同一。build_main_rom.py のスクロール範囲の故障注入は新しい形（余分に1行消す）へ更新。

検証（自作ROM）: l4-s9s 器具 191腕×2走 全て関門通過。ac 133項目は仕様どおりの誤り番号と全一致、窓・cls・スクロール・ファンクションキー・width・カラー切替の sc 99項目（ファンクションキー行の文字は自作が出さないので除く）全一致、cm 腕の port/P5 も仕様どおり（白黒復帰 0x23・P5=0x13、同モードは書かない）。実描画: console 5,10 で窓の外の行0〜4・15〜18が残り窓の中だけ上へ寄ることをスクリーンショットで確認。
退行: l4 の deftype・tabspc・deffn・wrap・strfunc・strcmp・peekpoke・s5j・onwhile・pusing・rnd・memdyn・memlimit・editinv・hexconst・widthbeep・widthvram・colorattr・clearcolor(s9q)・crtcpix(s9r)・console、ext_bank・memmap・vsync_regcheck・atnexplog/sincos endtoend・conform_l4・conform_l3・verify_l1/l2/l3・l3_main・l3_screen_editor・m6ib/ic/ie/ig/ih ROM関門・files/load/save/killname・check_cleanroom 計46本が rc=0。
残り容量: main 末尾126B（測定ROM用116B維持）、bank0 77B（以前402B）、bank1 1995B、bank2 3400B、bank3 27B。0x79D7 は埋め草のまま。private/ 混入なし。

events.title: fix(jit): keep ARM fault handlers ahead of SDL's KMSDRM keyboard handlers (#2395)
events.message:
fix(jit): keep ARM fault handlers ahead of SDL's KMSDRM keyboard handlers (#2395)

* fix(jit): keep ARM fault handlers ahead of SDL's KMSDRM keyboard handlers

SDL's evdev console keyboard code installs its own SIGSEGV/SIGILL/SIGBUS handlers when it mutes a keyboard (at video init and on keyboard hotplug). Those handlers restore the console and re-raise with raise(), so Amiberry's handler only sees the raise() context and cannot recover expected JIT faults such as Kickstart's RAMSEY size probe. A4000 configs with motherboard RAM crashed at boot under KMSDRM.

Reinstall Amiberry's handlers after SDL init and on SDL_EVENT_KEYBOARD_ADDED. Unhandled faults still restore the console keyboard through SDL_Quit() in the crash path.

* fix(jit): skip libretro keyboard hotplug and keep the JIT page guard on reclaim

The libretro SDL stub has no SDL_EVENT_KEYBOARD_ADDED, so the hotplug reclaim is compiled out there like the other device events. With JIT_DEBUG_MEM_CORRUPTION, the page-zero guard's SIGSEGV handler chains to signal_segv(); reclaim now leaves it in place instead of replacing it.

events.title: NDIX ttys through the gateway
events.message:
NDIX ttys through the gateway

A standalone ND-500 running NDIX never does an ND-100 Init, so the
WebSocket bridge had nothing to register and a telnet user saw "No
terminals available". The Worker now registers tty1..tty3 (identCode =
tty unit + 1, the mapping the page's windows use) when the ND-500 is
booted without an ND-100, routes gateway input to Nd500_SendInput(unit)
and a bound tty's output to the gateway as well as to its window, and
skips the carrier calls (an NDIX tty has none). ndix-machine.js connects
the bridge itself after the boot, since the Config window's auto-connect
waits for an ND-100 Init.

Verified headless through a test gateway: tty1 (NDIX) listed, Enter gives
the NDIX login prompt, root logs in, ls / answers, the tty1 window
mirrors it.

events.title: lists: Allocate scanned lists to fit their contents
events.message:
lists: Allocate scanned lists to fit their contents

The software, board, memory region, drive and SCSI device lists
reserved their maximum entry counts statically, about 107 KB of BSS
that a typical system never uses. On a 512 KB machine this left too
little memory to open the screen.

Grow each list in steps of 16 entries as it is filled, keeping the
existing limits. A list that cannot grow keeps the entries it has.
The memory region scan allocates before reading the free counts, and
the MUI SCSI list is cleared before a rescan frees its entries. The
first MMU list entry is now bounds checked as well.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: Gateway gets the machine's own terminals too, shared with their windows
events.message:
Gateway gets the machine's own terminals too, shared with their windows

The register message listed only the 8 gateway-only terminals that
EnableRemoteTerminals() adds (TERMINAL 12-19). SINTRAN K knows those, so
it answered; BSD 2.11's kernel has tty1-7 on TERMINAL 5-11 only
(bsd211_481 cons_mt.c), so a gateway user was always bound to a terminal
BSD has no driver for and got nothing back.

buildGatewayTerminalList() now registers every terminal except the
console: the machine's own terminals, each with a window in the page,
plus the gateway-only ones. A window terminal's output goes to its
window and, while a gateway client is bound to it, to the gateway as
well (the window mirrors the session); gateway-only terminals go to the
gateway alone. On client disconnect the terminal's carrier drops, as for
a dropped telnet line on the native build; the next key typed in the
window restores it.

Verified headless through a test gateway: BSD 2.11 multi-user, login as
root on TERMINAL 5 (tty1) through the gateway with the window mirroring
it; SINTRAN on TERMINAL 5 answers exactly what its window shows.

events.title: test(loop): judge paced sleep against measured headroom (MSVC Debug flake) (#90)
events.message:
test(loop): judge paced sleep against measured headroom (MSVC Debug flake) (#90)

test(loop): judge paced sleep against measured headroom, not an assum…

…ed one

EmuFramePacingTest.PacedFramesReportTheirSleep expected the pacer to sleep
more than 20 ms across three paced frames. That assumed each pin-level frame
finishes well inside its 20 ms period. On a -O0 Linux runner and on MSVC
x64-Debug a frame can take most of a period, so the pacer correctly never
sleeps and the test failed: once on PR #87, and on master after #89.

The test now times three unpaced frames first and requires half of the
headroom they leave. If there is under 20 ms of headroom, it says so and
checks only what does not depend on host speed: the sleep counter is sane,
take() resets it, and an unpaced frame never sleeps.

beads-6tr9

test: make the frame-turn tests independent of shuffled neighbours

MSVC x64-Debug on #90 failed EmuFrameTurnTest.OnlyTheHeadlessTurnGoesIdleWhenItEnds
(shuffle seed 39699): cpc_wait_until_idle(1) was true right after a busy turn.
That only happens when the turn refused to enter, i.e. the machine was still
paused. The fixture called cpc_resume(), which returns early when CPC.paused is
already false and so leaves a stray g_emu_paused in place (PausedFlag pins only
that flag).

- EmuFrameTurnTest::SetUp clears a desynced g_emu_paused, resumes, marks the
  runner idle, and asserts the machine runs, with a message naming the leak.
- The test asserts each turn actually entered.
- IpcServerTest's stuck-thread recovery test no longer leaves g_z80_idle false
  for whatever runs next (that suite has no per-test TearDown).

Full suite under six shuffle seeds, including 39699: 1950 passed each.

events.title: Settle garment layers and report only visible show-through by name
events.message:
Settle garment layers and report only visible show-through by name

The cover mask is read at every body corner (hidden only where hidden at
all of them) and a garment is masked only under a garment of an outer
layer (ornament, hip and head, torso, shoulder): the reverse contact is
the outer garment seen over the inner one, not a defect. The penetration
step counts an inner garment's point through the outer cloth only where
no skin drawn while both are worn hides it, measures the build pose at
every corner beside every clip pose, and names every remaining case by
garment, body part, clip and outer garment; with --baseline it lists
every garment, column and clip worse than main's.

The settle step now also pushes an outer garment out past the inner
garments it covers, cuts armholes and refines once before it, and the
motion fit measures its frames in forked workers. Pipeline selftests
cover the game-path unposing, the edge refinement and the face pushes.

events.title: fix(rtg): catch VRAM writes from direct JIT stores in the dirty tracker (#2394)
events.message:
fix(rtg): catch VRAM writes from direct JIT stores in the dirty tracker (#2394)

The emulated RTG write-watch only sees writes through the gfxmem put
handlers. The JIT decides per instruction, from one traced execution,
whether a store calls the handler or writes natmem directly. A store
traced while writing RAM stays direct when the same code later writes
VRAM, so those writes never reached mark_dirty.

rtg.library's rect copy hits this when restoring the software pointer
background after a screen mode change, leaving pointer trails in 16/32-bit
modes (#2318).

While direct JIT stores are possible, compare the visible pages against a
shadow at each drain and queue changed pages the dirty map missed.

events.message:
Size desk items to the space above the desk; one page where a spread is too small

The box, manual and foreword were sized from viewport formulas
(--box-height, --spread-page) that guessed at the room left above the
desk, and below 900px the stage was sized by its content, so whatever it
did not use went to the desk and the grey floor beneath it.

The bench stage is now a size container that always takes the height
above the desk strip, and every book sizes its pages from it.  The desk
measures the stage and sets data-pages: a spread while its pages would
be at least four fifths the size of a single page (pagesFor), otherwise
one page at a time.  Zoom still always shows one page, now filling the
screen through the same rules.  The zoomed foreword keeps a 15px floor
and widens its page to about 28em, so a phone turned sideways reads
about 45 characters a line instead of 25.

Narrow screens drop the floor's extra height and most of the desk's
back when away from the monitor; short screens (max-height 500px) get a
compact strip and a smaller banner.  The narrow strip gains bottom
padding so second-row labels are not clipped, its compact band holds
both rows, and page-turn buttons narrow to 48px to fit a 320px phone.

This replaces d950cf7's narrow two-page spread.

feat(build): the UI-free `koncepcja -H` links no SDL (beads-29zx)

Decision D5 on beads-cv2: the headless core uses the C++ standard library
and OS APIs only. KONCPC_MODERN_UI=0 (CMake: KONCPC_BUILD_MODERN_UI=OFF)
now builds without libSDL3; the GUI build is unchanged.

- KONCPC_SDL marks code that talks to SDL; only the UI build defines it.
  video_host, video_gpu, test_window and the macOS menu leave the UI-free
  build; the window, audio, joystick, clipboard and event-loop paths in
  kon_cpc_ja.cpp are compiled out, with no-op audio entry points.
- host_clock: SDL's ticks/perf counter/delay in the GUI build,
  std::chrono::steady_clock and sleep_for without SDL.
- host_surface: back_surface is SDL_Surface in the GUI build and a plain
  RGBA32 buffer without SDL. The bridge's SDL-free blit is a software
  nearest copy, byte-identical to SDL's for the headless geometry.
- savepng: a FILE*-based RGBA32 encoder; SDL_SavePNG wraps it.
- video_plugin.h holds the plugin vtable; video_headless.cpp is the
  SDL-free build's only plugin plus the IPC repaint state.
- drive_sounds uses std::recursive_mutex (SDL mutexes are recursive).
- tape line in/out has stubs that report no audio device.
- The SDL-free build keeps scr_style as read instead of clamping it to a
  one-entry plugin list.
- headless_smoke --ui-free fails on any SDL in the binary (dynamic or
  static). CI runs the macOS UI-free binary without the SDL dylib path.

fix(build): m4board_http declares back_surface as HostSurface (beads-…

…29zx)

MSVC encodes a variable's type in its symbol name, so the stale
extern SDL_Surface* declaration left the UI-free link unresolved there;
clang's variable symbols carry no type, which hid it on macOS and Linux.
The two test declarations follow.

events.title: 実装: カーソル表示コマンドの使い分けと COLOR の白黒/カラー・console ,,,1（l4-program 5.4・5.6.5、l4-s9r）
events.message:
実装: カーソル表示コマンドの使い分けと COLOR の白黒/カラー・console ,,,1（l4-program 5.4・5.6.5、l4-s9r）

根拠: l4-program 5.4.5・5.4.6・5.6.5（第14.13版 d06dd5f）、測定コミット 949492a。
- カーソル: プログラム実行中は垂直帰線の立ち上がりごと（S9C_POLL）に 0x80＋位置、INPUT 待ち（INPUT_READLINE のポーリング、CURSOR_INPUT）は 0x81＋位置。直接モード・打鍵中は従来の割り込みハンドラの 0x81（変更なし）。実行終了後は次フレームのハンドラが 0x81 に戻す。locate 時の更新は残す。割り込みハンドラ・L1 の並びは不変。
- COLOR の値: 白黒は n、カラーは 0x08|(n<<5)。カラーの既定の属性は (0x80,0xE8)（CLEAR_ROW・wb_attr が既定値で判定）。画面モードは MEMDYN+15（MM_SCR_MODE、bit0=カラー、bit5=INPUT 待ちの垂直帰線位相）。
- console ,,,1 のみ実装（文の種別43）。他の形は従来どおり ERR 2（未実装）。
自作判断（未測定）: console ,,,1 は現在の桁・行で WIDTH と同じ切替をカラーで行う（0x30=0x21/40桁0x20、画面全消去、カーソル先頭）。CRTC RESET の5つ目のパラメータに bit6 を足す（0x13→0x53。立てないと属性が色にならないことを実描画で確認。公式の CRTC 書き込みは未測定）。width 後のカラーの 0x30 値も bit1=0。

検証（自作ROM）: l4-s9r 器具 49腕×2走 関門通過、腕の判定は全て一致（st 16・px0 8・px1 8・bg/fg 16）。群の port54_distinct のみ differ（仕様どおり予測が外れた項目）。実描画: 入力待ちでカーソル■が出る・for/goto 実行中は出ない・カラーで color1〜7 が青赤紫緑水色黄白。退行: l4_crtcpix・colorattr・clearcolor(s9q)・widthvram(s9o)・widthbeep・verify_l1・l3_main(4a/4b)・l3_screen_editor・editinv・wrap・conform_l4(59項目全OK)・memmap・conform_l3 すべて rc=0。
run_all: その日の最後に回す（方針変更で今回は未実行。途中の part1/4 で conform_l3 が NG と出たが、単独実行は適合 rc=0で再現せず。要確認）。
残り容量: main 末尾 126B（測定ROM用116B維持）、bank0 402B、bank1 1995B、bank2 3400B、bank3 27B。0x79D7 は埋め草のまま。private/ 混入なし。

events.title: 889: the C64 Ultimate facade as a daemon of its own (c64re c64u-bridge)
events.message:
889: the C64 Ultimate facade as a daemon of its own (c64re c64u-bridge) The first build held the facade in each C64RE process, so the MCP server and the workbench fought over the device's one app connection and could not co-drive. The facade is now a process: `c64re c64u-bridge --device [:] [--port

]` speaks the TRX64 daemon wire protocol (JSON-RPC, the same notifications, binary 0x01/0x02 frames to A/V subscribers, ?av=0 honoured), holds the one device connection and the UDP streams, and serves any number of clients. Routing table, REST mapping, refusals by name, break_* wrappers, re-read after REST, trxmon-gone, capabilities check and the streams are the existing modules. - Gate (4b) in the bridge: project from project/set (or --project / C64RE_PROJECT_DIR); passes read per call from that project's knowledge/emulator-passes.json; no project = refused. - Lifecycle like the daemon's: started detached on select, one per device (registry + ping + lock: a second start attaches), idle exit with Spec 886's rules (requests and A/V viewers hold it, daemon/keep_alive), stream stop and device release on exit; REST password on stdin only. - Clients: "C64U selected" is a runtime endpoint. RuntimeDaemonClient gained a DaemonPolicy (its default is the emulator's code unchanged); BridgeClient is the other. One selection file per machine (~/.c64re/runtime-selection.json) that every C64RE process follows and announces. - Removed from the MCP/workbench processes: the in-process C64UBackend, lazyConnect, the /runtime-relay WebSocket. runtime_backend and /api/runtime/* stay. - Tests: smoke:889 (198), smoke:889-bridge (92, new), smoke:889-ui (122), smoke:889-streams (158), e2e:889-ue2emu (51, through the bridge with MCP + a browser-like client), e2e:889-pass (15). Revert the rigid-ornament envelope: one blend per piece measured deeper

Measured at every 7th pose on all ten body corners: skinning each ring
or string of beads as one blend and widening it left the limb rings at

moves into a neck-rigid string in the walk) and the waist beads at
0.0227 (was 0.0160; the belly folds into it in the kneel). Widening
deepens every one of them, so the depth is another body part folding
into the piece, not its size.

events.title: Provide libsocket_lazy and libos2_ses_lazy import libs
events.message:
Provide libsocket_lazy and libos2_ses_lazy import libs

These libraries allow the EXE or DLL to import functions from TCPIP32.DLL and SESMGR.DLL dynamically (the respective DLL will be loaded on the first call) rather statically (the DLL is loaded whenever EXE or DLL is loaded).

This, in turn, allows to work around indefinite TCPIP32.DLL hangs when the TCP/IP stack is not available (e.g. in Alt-F1, F2 boot mode with no PM).

See bitwiseworks/libc#141 and bitwiseworks/libcx#107 for details.

events.title: Wait for the staged lion feed to end on game frames, not a fixed 1.2 s
events.message:
Wait for the staged lion feed to end on game frames, not a fixed 1.2 s

The elephant-trampling section stages a 0.4 s carcass feed right after its
own jump to the Cairo reach. Measured on a fresh page, that jump's cold first
render draws single frames 2.5-9.5 s apart for about 30 s; the hunt clamps dt
to 0.1 s, so the feed needs 4-5 frames and ~30 s of wall time. The fixed
1.2 s wait therefore always read 'feed'. The game's no-victim feed branch
ends correctly; the check now waits for the mode to leave 'feed' (60 s bound)
and reports the wait.

events.title: tls: close without waiting, and drop what wasn't read
events.message:
tls: close without waiting, and drop what wasn't read

br_sslio_close spun for ever when a response was left part read (xmanx
stopping an image fetch for a key): the closing engine won't hand over
the application data it holds, and won't take another record while it
holds it. Seen on the TT as xmanx frozen on atari.org after Z while
images loaded. Now the unread data is dropped, our close_notify sent,
and the server's not waited for (RFC 5246 7.2.1); the socket closes
next. Closing an idle pooled connection no longer waits on the server.

feat(tools): make shots, scripted screenshots and headless checks

tools/shoot.mjs runs the committed shot list tools/shots.mjs in headless
Chromium over the DevTools protocol (Node's own WebSocket, no npm package)
and writes build/shots/<name>.png, one PASS/FAIL line per shot, exiting

for console errors and an empty #err, so 'boot' is the headless boot gate.

context per shot, labq=low, no film jitter/dust/16 fps, steady scope, no
room dust, a seeded Math.random restarted every frame, a frozen wall clock
and TZ=UTC. The profile and the in-process server live under build/ and are
removed at exit, failures and interrupts included.

tabbed-reel-mount, fusion-as08-14-2383, cabin-cm. CLAUDE.md gains a short

events.title: 実装: CLEAR の下限境界と COLOR の第2〜第4引数（l4-basic 20.9・l4-program 5.4.4、l4-s9q）
events.message:
実装: CLEAR の下限境界と COLOR の第2〜第4引数（l4-basic 20.9・l4-program 5.4.4、l4-s9q）

根拠は仕様 l4-basic 第20.9節（20.9.1 境界の式・20.9.3 文の種類・20.9.5 自作との関係）と l4-program 5.4.4（いずれも 84a5bc2）。測定コミットは a524aea。

CLEAR（strfunc.asm S9B_CLEAR）
- 上限 X < 0x8719 は誤り5（固定。従来は MM_USER_START=0x8400 を下限にしていた）。memmap.py に MM_CLEAR_X_MIN・MM_CLEAR_BOUND7 を追加（RAM 番地の直書き検査のため）。
- X < 34605+n（X+1-n < 34606）は誤り7。第3引数 n=0 は誤り5。第1引数は負が誤り5、符号付き16ビットを外れる値（65535・70000）が誤り6、それ以外は評価して無視。
- 自作判断: 自作は本文を 0x8400 から置くので、仕様の境界では受理でも 本文＋番兵＋第3引数が上限に収まらないとき（従来からの MM_HEAP_START 検査）と、n が MM_STACK_RESERVED+7 未満のときだけ追加で誤り7にする。公式と結果が変わるのは本文が長いときと n=96〜98 のときだけ（n=96 は公式受理・自作誤り7）。
- fre(0) は 20.9.5 の選択肢 (a) を採用: 誤り番号の境界だけ公式に合わせ、fre(0) は段F の自作の空きを返すまま（公式の X-(34586+n) には合わせない。本文を含めない量になり自作の空きと別物になるため）。
- 公式との差が残る点: 受理の fre(0) の値、n=96〜98、n=80・88（公式は未確定）。

COLOR（widthbeep.asm wb_color_stmt）
- 第2・第4引数は 0〜7、第3引数は 0 だけ受理、他は誤り5（誤り番号は従来から全一致。作業値の持ち方を変えただけ）。省略した引数は検査しない。
- 受理された COLOR はポート 0x54 へ必ず2回書く。1回目 0x80|(b bit0→0x07)|(b bit1→0x38)、2回目 0xC0|(b bit2→0x07)。b は第2引数（省略時 0）。第3・第4引数はポートに出さない。誤りの COLOR は書かない（文末まで確かめてから書く）。b は MM_FN_AUX+1 の bit2〜4 に同居（下位2bit は引数番号）。相対ジャンプが届かなくなった箇所は JP に変更。

検証（自作ROM）
- l4_clearcolor_measure（57腕×2走、cv・co・cp 全て採取）: 仕様の表と手計算で照合。cv: 0x8400=5・0x8800=7・0x8C00=受理、clear 65535・70000=6、clear -1=5、n=0=5、n=64・72=7、n=104〜1024=受理、32767・-1・32768=7、`clear ,,64`=7、`clear ,,128`=受理。co: 82文（参照2含む）の誤り番号が仕様 5.4.4 と全て一致（不一致0）。cp: 0x54 の値列が b=0〜7 で (128,192)(135,192)(184,192)(191,192)(128,199)(135,199)(184,199)(191,199)、bo≥1 の誤りは書き込み無し、0x52 は動かない（out &h52 は誤り2）。cl-n10: b5=0x8719・b7=0x892D・傾き1・単調（仕様と一致）。仕様と食い違う腕: n=80・88・96（自作は誤り7、公式は未確定または受理）。cl-base 等の他の cl 腕は従来どおり自作で採取失敗（ValueError。20.9.5 の「走行が崩れて採れていない」。HEAD でも同じ）。
- 関門は kn・cl 系の較正が自作の誤りメッセージ同一のため失敗（従来どおり）。
- l4_widthbeep_measure: 153腕×2走が関門通過、check --predicted-only が rc=0（照合一致）。l4_colorattr_measure: 41腕×2走の report が HEAD の ROM と完全に同一（関門失敗も HEAD と同じ）。

退行: tools/run_all_selftests.sh が NG 0 件で完走（CACHED 84本・2ロケール 12本・UTF-8のみ 132本、所要 7150秒。PC88_SELFTEST_EXCLUDE で disk2 系の2本は除外）。途中、memmap_selftest が RAM 番地の直書き（0872Eh・08718h）を検出したため memmap.py の定数へ置き換えて全体を取り直した。check_cleanroom.sh は rc=0。private/ 由来の混入なし。

残り容量（自作ROM）: main 末尾 は変更なし、bank0 507B（565B から 58B 使用）、bank1 1995B・bank2 3400B・bank3 27B（変更なし。CLEAR は 0x7300〜0x73FF の枠内に収めた）。QUASI88 の 0x79D7 は触れていない。

events.title: [PCE] a bunch of small CD fixes based on krikzz's tcd-verificator, at least the tests that work without whatever disc most of the CDD tests depend on
events.message:
[PCE] a bunch of small CD fixes based on krikzz's tcd-verificator, at least the tests that work without whatever disc most of the CDD tests depend on

* after each $1805 write, the hardware ignores successive $1805 writes until enough time has passed
* setting the ADPCM reset and play bits simultaneously in $180D causes $180C reads to have playing=1 (but I don't think the chip is actually playing sound?)
* fixed edge cases around how $180A reads and writes set the ADPCM half flag
* ADPCM length is actually a 17-bit value rather than 16-bit
* set the subchannel IRQ flag every 6 44100 Hz clocks while the drive is reading, and clear it on $1807 reads (although $1807 reads are not properly implemented yet)
* read TOC command response is always 4 bytes, regardless of which variant is selected; remaining bytes are just 0s I guess?
* fix the CD event loop always processing events immediately due to a backwards conditional (oops)

not touching any of the SCSI timing differences yet, seems like they're mostly due to not emulating the short delays on bus phase changes (and there's some timing weirdness around ADPCM DMA where it seems to run much faster than it "should" given CPU-visible delays when manually reading from $1808)

events.message:
fix(cabin): hide cabin lines behind the cabins' opaque faces (#71)

In the CM and LM station views the cabin was an outline model with no
hidden-line step, so far walls, panels and window frames drew through
one another and the view was hard to read when panning.

Each cabin's opaque faces (CM: console, couch pans, equipment bay
faces, forward bulkhead about the tunnel; LM: floor, panels, side
console tiers, engine cover, aft bulkhead about the midsection, upper
deck about the overhead hatch) are kept as triangles in /COCC/. A cabin
rides its eye, so vmask.f CBCUT cuts every cabin line once, at MLIB,
with exact plane cuts in direction space and depth, and MDRAW draws
the pieces. Per-frame cost does not grow. CBCUT(K, OFF) recomputes for
an eye offset and keeps the cut with its offset, ready for #72.

CMINT's window 2 is kept for the window mask (WKEEP) but no longer
drawn: it was the mean of CMCAB's two period outlines, one for each of
the commander's eyes, and showed as a third copy between them.

Golden: 4 of the 8 approved cabin cases change (s8-cm-cabin,
s7-cm-mask, s5-lm-cabin, s5-lm-mask); every other file is unchanged.

Closes #71

events.title: fix-toolchain-crt0: read binutils 2.46 objdump output
events.message:
fix-toolchain-crt0: read binutils 2.46 objdump output

Three gaps made the gate refuse a toolchain whose crt0 carries the
upstream fixes for all three bugs:
- instruction_details() only knew the 2.39 `addr size name:' symbol line,
  so under 2.46's `addr <name>:' no instruction had a function and no
  call to main was counted;
- the 32-bit displacement of the libb32 forms prints in hex without a
  prefix (`a4@(10)' for .bss+0x10) and was read as decimal;
- ixemul's crt0.o, a different runtime with no ____start/exit pair, was
  counted as "not understood".
With these, a toolchain built from AmigaPorts/m68k-amigaos-gcc 16.2-rc14
passes --check with all eleven crt0.o immune to all three bugs.

events.title: fix(gpu): NORMI normalises to bit 23, not 22 (#611)
events.message:
fix(gpu): NORMI normalises to bit 23, not 22 (#611)

NORMI returns the right shift that normalises an unsigned integer "as an
IEEE 32-bit floating point value" (JTRM v8 p.52), so the top set bit lands
on bit 23, the hidden-bit position: NORMI 1 = -23, NORMI $800000 = 0,
NORMI $80000000 = 8. TOM's ARITH.NET "normalisation integer generator"
encodes exactly that, and gives -32 for a zero source. The old code
normalised to bit 22 and returned one too many for every input (and 0 for
a zero source).

Club Drive clips polygons against the screen with a four-entry corner table
indexed by (NORMI(outcode) << 3) & $1F, so every inserted screen corner was
rotated by one. A polygon crossing two screen edges (common while steering)
came out non-monotonic in Y; the edge walker bailed to the command
interpreter while a span callback still borrowed its return stack (r10) as
scratch, and the interpreter's return popped a garbage address into main
RAM. From the user's mid-race savestate, holding accelerate and steering
left escaped at frame 82; with the fix all six driving patterns run 2400
frames clean.

Tests:
- test_gpu_ops: NORMI cases from the netlist decode (the old expectation,
  9 for $80000000, encoded the bug).
- test/tools/test_club_drive_611: ROM- and savestate-gated; drives from
  states/Club Drive (1994).state3 and requires the GPU PC to stay in local
  RAM for 300 frames with the picture moving. Fails on develop at frame 82.
- Retire Native Demo (bin) as a test_blitter_hung reproducer: its GPU runs
  into data at frame 1 on develop, and the corrected NORMI changes that
  garbage path so it no longer issues the never-ending blit. The non-approx
  path stays covered by the synthetic test on both engines; Music Demo
  --bios still covers the approx path.

The DSP has the identical NORMI block and off-by-one; that half is fixed
separately on fix/dsp-normi-off-by-one.

events.message:
layout: tables framing a page side by side, where there is room

A table framing a page (a column of links beside the news, tables in its
cells) went one cell after another. From 96 columns wide (em: a
terminal's column, or a "0" in xmanx's window) it is now a grid like a
table of data: the main text at least 40 em, narrow columns (a sidebar of
links, gutters) at their widest, nothing else under 12 em, its longest
words (URLs) broken at 30 em; otherwise, and on an 80-column terminal,
as before. atari.org, amigaworld.net, Paul Graham's pages and
Wikipedia's navigation boxes now read in their columns in a wide
window. Tables in a grid's cells are grids too, three deep.

Two fixes on the way, which change 80 columns too:
- A grid is placed as a block, centred or to the right as a whole, not a
  line at a time: grids in a centred cell came out ragged (Berkshire
  Hathaway's two columns of links, Space Jam's 1996 page).
- An <hr> is as wide as its line, so it no longer counts towards its
  cell's width (it made every grid with a rule in a cell fall back to
  rows), and an empty column gets no gap after it.

A framing cell is measured by its first 40 lines: on the TT's 68030 at
132 columns, atari.org lays out in 455 ms (239 as rows), amigaworld.net
in 2.0 s (1.15 s); at 80 columns nothing costs more.

events.title: anxzz9000: program the GEM multicast hash (#202)
events.message:
anxzz9000: program the GEM multicast hash (#202)

Upstream firmware (BlitterStudio PR #111) starts the GEM with an empty
multicast hash and takes bucket commands at ETH_CONFIG (0x8a). The driver
never wrote them: it relied on the fork firmware accepting every group.
On upstream firmware no multicast frame arrived, so IPv6 neighbour
discovery for the card's addresses failed (multicast in 0 on the A3000).

When the firmware reports the capability, rebuild the hash at init and on
every filter change: one bucket per joined group, or all 64 when
promiscuous or all-multicast. The software filter stays, as the buckets
collide. The hash is the GEM's, as in ZZ9000Net.device's net/mcast.c.

events.title: Fix hard disk writes: stale DMA FIFO data, driver retries (issue #11)
events.message:
Fix hard disk writes: stale DMA FIFO data, driver retries (issue #11)

acsi_ctrl took a word from the DMA FIFO in the cycle in which dma.v
raised the fill level, but dma.v's data output is a register that shows
the word one cycle later. Whenever the controller waited for the DMA
(almost always), it stored the old content of the FIFO slot: only the
first 8 words of every written sector were correct, the rest was
shifted by 16 words. TOS's sector cache hid the damage until the disk
was read again (e.g. after a power cycle).

A driver that times out during a long write and retries could also get
sectors written to the wrong place: the controller took the data of the
retry as the next sectors of the old command, and the old command's ack
was taken as the answer to the retry. Now a new command (acsi.v
cmd_start, which also clears busy) or a DMA FIFO reset after data has
moved cancels the running command; a sector in flight on the SD
interface is finished first, and a command cancelled by a FIFO reset is
not executed again.

New simulation test CORE/sim/acsi_write: a floppy boot sector writes
64 KB with one Rwabs call, check.py verifies every sector of the hard
disk image (also with slow sector writes, HD_WR_DELAY). tb: HD_WR_DELAY,
HD_TRACE, HD_OUT, MONO60, frame rate output, more ACSI_TRACE output.

events.title: fix(dsp): NORMI normalises to bit 23, not bit 22 (same off-by-one as the GPU, #611)
events.message:
fix(dsp): NORMI normalises to bit 23, not bit 22 (same off-by-one as the GPU, #611)

NORMI gives the right shift that normalises an unsigned integer "as an
IEEE 32-bit floating point value" (JTRM v8 p.52): the top set bit moves
to bit 23, the hidden-bit position, so the result is msb - 23.  JERRY's
netlist (DSP_A-5Q.NET, normalisation integer generator) encodes exactly
that and gives -32 for a zero source.  It is line-for-line identical to
TOM's ARITH.NET, the logic the GPU fix for #611 was decoded from.

The old code normalised to bit 22: every result one too high, and 0 for
a zero source.

test_dsp_ops now checks six values (8, 0, -1, -23, -32, 1); all six
fail on the old code.

Refs #611

events.title: fix(file): load $5000-linked raw binaries at $5000 (#818)
events.message:
fix(file): load $5000-linked raw binaries at $5000 (#818)

The raw-binary loader scored candidate bases only by whether absolute
JSR/JMP/LEA/MOVE targets fall inside [base, base+size).  $5000 was not
a candidate, and a $4000 window also contains almost every target of a
$5000-linked image, so such images loaded $1000 low: Chroma-Luma (bin)
ran its font data from its first JSR, the 68K hit ILLEGAL and parked at
$1000 (#800's guard), and the screen stayed black in HLE and BIOS mode
(RAM-loaded images never take the boot-ROM path, so both modes share
the failure).

Add $5000 and break overlapping-window ties on entry-point consistency:
a JSR/JMP abs.L target that is the image start or the word after an
RTS/RTE/RTR is a subroutine start under the right base and a
coincidence under a wrong one.  Among bases that clear the containment
bar, the most entry hits wins; with no hits anywhere the containment
winner stands, so images without the signal do not move.

Across the 155-title cart corpus exactly six load decisions change, all
$4000 -> $5000 and all from black/parked to running video: Chroma-Luma
(bin), JagMania (Jul 8), JagMarble (2000), FORCE Design Legion Force
intro, Joypad-TeamTap Tester [a1], and Music Demo (ScatoLOGIC), whose
#794 blitter spray in BIOS mode was this misload.  Music Demo is
therefore no longer a hung-blitter reproducer; it moves to the new
ROM-gated test_raw_binary_boot check next to the two #818 titles.

Closes #818

events.title: xmanx: a row's like cells in one request; MANX_XTRACE
events.message:
xmanx: a row's like cells in one request; MANX_XTRACE

The grid of cells (monospaced text, such as about:help's) was drawn a
character at a time: some 2000 ImageText8 requests for a screen. A row's
cells that look alike now go in one, 13x fewer requests for that page.

That was also why xmanx hung on AMIX's X2410 on an (emulated) A2410
board. X2410 hands its drawing to the board's TMS34010 in batches; with
thousands of small requests the board's queue filled and the server
stopped answering for good. With every request waited for and a pixel
read back after it, nothing hung, so each request on its own was fine.
Now about:help and Wikipedia's Atari TT030 article load there, in colour.
(Amiberry's picture of the A2410's screen lags behind its memory: xwd,
reading through the server, shows what is drawn.)

MANX_XTRACE, for finding such things: every request waited for before
the next, logged to stderr with its sequence number and, on X11R4/R5
(AMIX), its opcode, plus the events that arrive; MANX_XTRACE=N stops for
good after N requests; MANX_XGET=N reads a pixel back after each request
from N on.

events.title: fix(titledb): turn on blitter bus timing for White Men Can't Jump (#736)
events.message:
fix(titledb): turn on blitter bus timing for White Men Can't Jump (#736)

The game races its own GPU decoder against the blitter. $17BD8 starts
the GPU decoding the first logo into $0DCF00 and returns without
waiting. The fade-in at $0138AE then makes 64 pairs of SRCSHADE copies
out of that buffer, and each copy waits only for B_CMD to read idle
($015F0C).

On hardware every copy freezes the 68000. It is the lowest-priority bus
master (JTRM Rev 8 p.8), and the blitter keeps requesting the bus until
the operation completes (p.69), so the fade outlasts the decode. With
zero-time blits the whole fade ran in two fields. At that point the
decoder had finished 111 of 200 rows (RAM dumps at f19/f20/f21), and
the last copy kept 49 of them. The results:

- the Trimark logo showed only its apex (6.4% of the screen lit,
  against 43.8% for the full logo);
- the High Voltage logo never appeared;
- the spinning-ball title animation was lost.

All three happened in both HLE and real-BIOS boot.

The existing Blitter Bus Timing model charges the 68000 exactly that
bus time. This commit adds a titledb row that turns the model on for
this CRC and does not change the model itself. Fast and accurate
blitters are hash-identical on this title, so neither engine is at
fault. TOM bug 9 does not apply, because B_CMD $41802601 sets GOURZ.

With default options the frame-hash stream is byte-identical to an
explicit virtualjaguar_blitter_timing=enabled run, in both modes.
test_audio_clipping and test_audio_presence give the same result on
WMCJ before and after (RMS 1541.7, clean). A driven 6000-frame run
still reaches gameplay with no new static run.

The new test/tools/wmcj_intro_logo is ROM-gated and runs at default
options. It finds the first picture the game holds for 60 frames and
needs it to be at least 25% lit. Develop fails it at 6.4%, and so does
this build with per-title defaults disabled.

fix(ipc): pc= and mem= events fire through the bus probe (beads-uj1c) (#82)

fix(ipc): pc= and mem= events fire through the bus probe (beads-uj1c)

`event on|once pc=` / `mem=` armed with OK id=N and never fired: nothing
called ipc_check_pc_events / ipc_check_mem_write_events after the v6
rewrite. subcycle_bridge_sync_probe() now arms their addresses on the
board's bus probe next to the breakpoints and watchpoints (one atomic load
per trigger while none exist). process_probe_hit() queues a hit armed for an
event, and resumes it without a stop when no breakpoint or watchpoint shares

events.title: feat: each reel numbered on its own, one reel in the kernel at a time (#26 slice 7e)
events.message:
feat: each reel numbered on its own, one reel in the kernel at a time (#26 slice 7e)

Apollo 8's deck becomes SCENARIO ID=1 and SITUATION ID=1 (SPAN SIT=1); the
kernel holds one scenario reel's decks at a time. The page loads every
scenario reel once at boot (a deck error stops the boot), leaving the boot
reel in the kernel, and mount() reloads the decks (kernel.js useDeck,
deck_open..deck_close, about 0.6 ms in wasm) when the situation's reel is not
the one loaded (LS.deck). Old scene=N links keep their meaning (Apollo 11's
1-8, Apollo 8's Earthrise 9), as do keys 1-9 and the scene buttons.

Playlist SHOT cards name their reel (REEL=, required; SIT= an id or NAME
there) and the playlists are packed as reels of kind "playlist" (run.scn,
page.json holding the REEL object, manifest uses: the scenario reels), so
names.js loses REELS. Fusion photos name a situation (photos.tsv sit) in
their mission's reel. featInit probes the reel the kernel holds.

Native side: gen_data writes build/decks/<reel>.txt and build/decks/reels.txt
instead of build/decks.txt, and scenes.json per reel; viewsvg takes VIEW_REEL;
golden.sh cases name their reel and capture tables-<reel>.txt; make check
renders build/check/<reel>-s<N>.png. The selftest loads one reel at a time and
checks that switching reels draws the same frames as a fresh load of each.

events.title: fix(loop): pause leases exclude the frame under -H (beads-b0bj) (#81)
events.message:
fix(loop): pause leases exclude the frame under -H (beads-b0bj) (#81)

fix(loop): pause leases exclude the frame under -H (beads-b0bj)

Under -H the main thread runs the frames but never cleared g_z80_idle, so
CpcPauseLease reported the machine idle at once and IPC reset, snapshot,
disk and step commands mutated it under a running frame. An instrumented
build logged 552 leases granted mid-frame in 300 run/reset cycles.

Both loops now take each frame through EmuFrameTurn: mark busy, then
re-check the pause, seq_cst against the pauser's store-then-wait, which also
closes the check-then-mark window the Z80 thread had. -H goes idle when the
turn ends; the GUI thread keeps its old idle points.

A lease the frame runner takes on itself (an autotype KONCPC_RESET in the
epilogue) no longer waits on its own frame: on the GUI's Z80 thread it used
to stall 5 s and skip the reset.

Quitting through the macOS menu bar or Cmd-Q waited until the timeout:

events.title: docs: ledger the macOS session death as root-caused
events.message:
docs: ledger the macOS session death as root-caused

Three stacked defects: the transport losing the death cause, the workflow
never executing the bundled closure, and Homebrew's sdl2 formula being the
sdl2-compat shim whose dlopen of SDL3 no otool walk can see. The modal
NSAlert from the shim's constructor explains every symptom on both the
runner and the field machine, including the absent crash report.
events.author: idontwantyourspamthanks

events.title: release: bundle SDL3 for the sdl2-compat shim — the macOS session-death root cause
events.message:
release: bundle SDL3 for the sdl2-compat shim — the macOS session-death root cause

Homebrew's sdl2 formula is sdl2-compat: libSDL2-2.0.0.dylib is a shim whose
constructor dlopen()s libSDL3.dylib by soname. The bundling walk follows
otool -L, which cannot see a dlopen, so the bundle shipped the shim without
SDL3. The shim then failed its search (@loader_path, Frameworks, home,
/Library/Frameworks, bare soname) and called error_dialog — a modal NSAlert
no background process can dismiss, followed by an abort() that never
arrives. On a headless runner that is an infinite hang; on a user machine
it is the field report: connection dropped, no stderr, no exit, no crash
report. Every previously passing banner check had loaded brew's SDL3
through the inherited /opt/homebrew/lib rpath, which the rpath purge
removed — that is why the hang appeared exactly when the bundle became
honest.

libSDL3.0.dylib is now copied beside the shim (where @loader_path finds
it), walked by the same closure so its own deps come along, and the step
fails loudly if brew ever stops providing it.

events.title: fix(loop): -H honours the speed limiter; auto frameskip keys on the pacer (#79)
events.message:
fix(loop): -H honours the speed limiter; auto frameskip keys on the pacer (#79)

fix(loop): -H honours the speed limiter; auto frameskip keys on the p…

…acer

The -H loop asked the bridge for an unpaced frame whatever limit_speed said,
so with limit_speed=1 it ran ~1850 FPS (500 frames in 0.27 s) where the GUI
runs 50. emu_run_frame() loses its bridge_paces flag: both loops pace through
the bridge's one 50 Hz deadline, and limit_speed=0 still runs either one
unpaced (beads-gnx3).

Auto frameskip compared the clock against perfTicksTarget, which only the
long-gone EC_CYCLE_COUNT limiter ever advanced, so with frameskip=1 every frame
~20 ms after start counted as late: 198 of 200 frames were never published
(frozen display, AVI capture stopped), and sleepTimeAccum was never
incremented (beads-af0k, beads-o478: one root cause). The pacer's deadline
arithmetic moves into FramePacer (src/frame_pacer.h, unit-tested on a
synthetic clock), which reports a frame late only when it is more than a
period behind; jitter such as an oversleeping SDL_Delay is absorbed by the
drift correction. Frameskip keys on that verdict, capped at 5 skips in a row
so a machine that can never keep up still shows a picture, and a skipped
frame no longer pays for the blit. The pacer's sleep is booked to
sleepTimeAccum and taken out of the "machine" time. perfTicksTarget and
perfTicksOffset are gone.

test(loop): EmuFrameTest starts and ends with an empty autotype queue

Under --gtest_shuffle (seed 30108) a test that leaves g_autotype_queue
active ran before EmuFramePacingTest: emu_run_frame()'s autotype_frame()
then typed through CPC.InputMapper, which the test binary never builds,
and segfaulted. A leftover queue would also force real-time pacing on.

test(loop): check frameskip wiring against the pacer's own verdict

AStalledLoopSkipsWhileItCatchesUp assumed a 100 ms stall leaves the next
frames late. On a crawling CI Mac the stall ran past the pacer's 250 ms
resync, which is deliberately not late, and the test saw no skip. The
replacement asserts, frame by frame, that skip_rendering is exactly
frameskip_should_skip() applied to subcycle_bridge_frame_was_late() for the
previous frame, so it holds whatever the host's timing does. The lateness
rule and the cap stay covered deterministically by FramePacer,
FrameskipDecision and FrameskipNeverStarvesTheDisplay.

events.title: Fast start: continue where Einstein was quit
events.message:
Fast start: continue where Einstein was quit

When quitting, Einstein lets the Newton fall asleep, stops the emulator and
saves a fast start state file (FastStart.state in the data folder). If the
Newton does not fall asleep within ten seconds, no state is saved.

On the next launch, Einstein inserts the PCMCIA cards that were inserted
when the state was saved, then loads it, before the emulator thread starts.
It is only loaded if the ROM, RAM size, flash and cards did not change. Then
the Newton is woken up. If the state does not match, Einstein boots
normally and the cards stay inserted, so NewtonOS mounts them. The file is
deleted after every attempt, so an unforeseen error can't cause the same
failing start over and over. Empty slots get the cards kept in a slot.

Fast start can be switched off in the Settings dialog ("MessagePad" tab,
checked by default).

State files are now written to a temporary file and renamed when complete,
and they record the image path of the inserted cards. The state file
version is now 9.

events.title: Reset the machine through the state tree, like the reset button
events.message:
Reset the machine through the state tree, like the reset button

TStream has a third mode, resetting, and new Transfer overloads with a reset
value: TransferInt32BE(value, resetValue) and so on. TResetStream (header
only) walks the same TransferState() tree as saving and loading: every value
with a reset value goes to its power-on state, every value without one is
kept. One list per class now defines save, load and reset.

TEmulator::ResetState() resets the interrupt controller, MMU, DMA, serial
DMA registers, PCMCIA interrupt registers and card state machines, pending
pen samples, sound interrupt masks and buffers, and the platform manager
queues (with the boot lock set again, as at startup), then lets the CPU take
the reset exception. RAM, flash, the clock, the volume and the PCMCIA pin
registers are kept, like on a real reset.

Hardware Reset and Brain Wipe in the FLTK menu now go through the Monitor
(TMonitor::RequestReset()): the emulator is stopped, reset and continues.
Before, TARMProcessor::Reset() was called from the UI thread while the
emulator was running.

events.title: net: DNS asked again after a second, and answers kept
events.message:
net: DNS asked again after a second, and answers kept

A lost query, or a server slow to ask upstream, cost the whole 2.5 s
wait, and the next try came from a new socket under a new id, so a late
answer to the first was thrown away. Over the TT's WiFi DaynaPORT a
lookup took anything from 0.2 to 10 s. Now the query goes out again on
the same socket after 1 s and is waited for 2 s more, and an answer to
either will do.

Answers are kept for their time to live (at least 10 minutes, at most a
day), in memory and in ~/.manx/dns, which the next run of manx, xmanx or
ufetch starts from. When no server answers, an answer up to a week out
of date still serves. tests/test_dns.c checks the cache.

events.title: native32: callbacks under Wine (CrossOver on Apple Silicon) (#55)
events.message:
native32: callbacks under Wine (CrossOver on Apple Silicon) (#55)

native32 finds a Windows -> guest call by the fault when Windows fetches
the guest's code. Under Wine two things kept that from happening.

Wine leaves DEP off unless the process asks for it, and answers the
first fetch from a readable, non-executable page by making it
executable and carrying on. The guest's original machine code then ran:
Red Alert 2's dialog procedures did, with the menus working, and only
--callbacks showed that no guest callback ever came through the
trampoline. native32_init now calls SetProcessDEPPolicy(PROCESS_DEP_ENABLE).
On Windows a /NXCOMPAT exe already has DEP and the call changes nothing.

Under Rosetta, Wine reports a fetch from a no-access page as a read
(ExceptionInformation[0] = 0), not an execute (8). Wine calling a window
procedure in the shim page came through as "read of 0x032D0170" at
0x032D0170 and the game died creating its window. A read of the faulting
instruction's own address is a fetch as well, so the handler now takes
either.

With both, Red Alert 2 and Yuri's Revenge cross-built with clang-cl
(native32 under clang-cl, #47) pass 27 of their 30 playtest cases in a
CrossOver bottle, and the 3 that fail need IPX, which that install lacks.

events.title: Check that a state file matches before loading, fast start and debug files
events.message:
Check that a state file matches before loading, fast start and debug files

State files now come in two kinds:
- Fast start files hold a checksum of the flash instead of its contents.
  They are written when Einstein quits, and must only be loaded if the
  flash did not change since.
- Debug files hold the whole flash, so a state can be loaded again after
  the soups changed. The Monitor commands and the temporary menu items use
  this kind. "save fast <path>" in the Monitor writes a fast start file.

Before loading, the file is checked against the running emulator: ROM and
REX (checksum computed at startup, before any breakpoint), RAM size, the
flash (fast start files only), and the kind and contents of the cards in
both PCMCIA sockets. If anything differs, the reason is printed and nothing
is changed.

The ROM is no longer saved. Breakpoints in ROM are removed before loading
and set again from the loaded list. This makes debug files 16 MB smaller,
and fast start files another 8 MB smaller. The state file version is now 8.
