events.title: 実装: COLOR の属性域と40桁時のカーソル位置（l4-program 5.4・5.6、l4-s9p）
events.message:
実装: COLOR の属性域と40桁時のカーソル位置（l4-program 5.4・5.6、l4-s9p）

根拠は仕様 5.4節・5.6.2・5.6.5（9cef9f5、第14.11版）と l1-ipl の CRTC コマンド書式（第5d節）だけ。測定コミットは 2a2826f（l4-s9p）・8d6b301（追補1）。

- COLOR 文の全体をバンク0 wb_color_stmt へ（run.asm COLOR_STMT は呼ぶだけ）。n は 0〜7（小数は四捨五入）、範囲外・第2引数が範囲外=ERR 5、文字列=ERR 13、引数なし・末尾の「,」=ERR 22、第5引数=ERR 2（値の検査が先）、第1引数省略（COLOR ,3）は色を変えない。誤りは色を変えない。現在の色は MM_SCR_ZT の上位3bit（下位5bitはコンマ欄閾値÷2。RAM に空きが無いため同居。ZONE_PAD は閾値を2倍して使う）。
- 属性域: 行に組を書くのは COLOR 文ではなく印字（PRINT_CHAR → バンク0 wb_attr）。印字したセルを現在の色にし、区間 [始点,終端) を (終端桁／40桁は2×終端桁-1, 値) の組として持つ。n=0 で組が無い行は何も書かない・別の色から0へ戻した区間は組が書かれる・桁を飛ばした前の区間は (桁,0)・上書きで区間が組み直される（隣り合う同値は1組にまとめる）・20区間以上は20組目が (0x80, 最後の区間の値)・未使用は (0x80,0)・スクロールで組は行と動く。以前の「行全体を (0x80,値) で塗る」は廃止。
- カーソル: SET_CURSOR の X は 40桁で 2×桁（80桁は桁）。LOCATE のあと 0x80＋同じパラメータを出す（CURSOR_UPDATE）。QUASI88 の CRTC は 0x80 で非表示・コマンド完了後の余分なパラメータは無視するので、待機中のカーソル表示（毎フレームの 0x81）は変わらない。QUASI88 の画面ショットで 80桁・40桁とも入力中のカーソルが入力した文字の直後に見える（HEAD は 40桁でカーソルが見えなかった）。
- F5/F6 の検査（tools/l4_program_selftest.sh の case_f5_color_2・case_f6_color_7）: 位置バイトに 0x80 を期待していたが、これは 94d77f0 の自作実装（行全体を (0x80,値) で塗る）に合わせた誤りで、公式観測 l4-s5f（仕様 5.4.2・5.4.3）の先頭2バイトは (0x03,0x02)／(0x03,0x07)。期待を公式観測 (3,n) ＋続きの未使用の組 (0x80,0) に合わせ直した（検査を緩めたのではなく、公式観測へ厳しくした）。
- tools: build_main_rom.py のカーソル故障注入（l3_main_selftest 10）は、SET_CURSOR に40桁の分岐が入って COL 出力と ROW 出力が隣り合わなくなったので、ROW 出力側（直後が RET）を1ずらす形に対象を変えた。

検証（自作ROM）:
- l4_colorattr_measure（41腕＋追補1の腕、各2走）: 全腕で採取できた。cur 10腕（80桁5・40桁5）の位置パラメータが仕様の値と一致、val 8値・stmt 範囲／誤り・mix m1〜m8（80桁・40桁）・en（on error・err）が仕様の確定値と一致。事前登録の予測と食い違うのは、公式の結果も予測を外した腕（fbare=ERR 22・m2/m7 の20組目・f5b=ERR 2・f4b=ERR 5・fcomma=ERR 22）だけで、いずれも仕様の確定値どおり。器具の関門（較正）は自作の誤りメッセージが5種で同一になるため従来どおり失敗（HEAD でも同じ）。
- l4_widthbeep_measure: measure（153腕×2走が関門通過）→ check --predicted-only が rc=0（照合一致）。l4_widthvram_measure: base 11腕・color 5腕が2走とも関門通過、color 腕の属性域は80桁 (10,0)(13,3)・(20,0)(23,4)、40桁 (19,0)(25,3)・(39,0)(45,4)・(5,2) で仕様どおり。
- 実描画: QUASI88 のスクリーンショットで、80桁の色の混在（印字区間ごとの反転／通常）・40桁の混在・カーソルが正しい桁（80桁・40桁）に見えることを確認。

退行: tools/run_all_selftests.sh が rc=0（CACHED 83本・2ロケール 97本・UTF-8のみ 47本。PC88_SELFTEST_EXCLUDE で disk2 系の2本は除外）。deftype・tabspc・deffn・wrap・strfunc・strcmp・peekpoke・s5j・onwhile・pusing・rnd・memdyn・memlimit・editinv・hexconst・widthbeep・widthvram の自作照合・ext_bank・memmap・vsync_regcheck・atnexplog・sincos/sqr endtoend・conform_l4（59/59）・l3_main・l3_screen_editor・m6ib/ic/ie/ig/ih ROM 関門・files/load/save/killname を含む。check_cleanroom.sh も rc=0。途中で l3_main_selftest の L1適合 4a（初期化350件の完全一致）が崩れたため、文字出力のたびのカーソル更新はやめて locate だけにした（下の自作判断）。private/ 由来の混入なし。

残り容量: main は 0x79D7 前の埋め草 66B→約30B・末尾158B（変わらず。測定ROM用116B以上を維持）、bank0 922B→565B、bank1 1995B・bank2 3400B・bank3 27B（使わない）。0x79D7 は埋め草のまま。

自作判断（未測定）: (1) 第2・第4引数は 0〜7、第3引数は 0 だけ受理（観測は color 3,1,1,2=ERR 5 と color 3,0,0,6・color 2,3=受理だけで境目の引数は不明）。(2) 仕様 5.6.5 は「locate／文字出力のたびにカーソル位置を更新」だが、起動バナーの出力が L1適合 4a の350件に混ざるため locate だけで更新する。(3) 20区間以上の中間上書きなど仕様に無い溢れは、組19を (0x80, 現在の色) にする。(4) 同じ色の続けての印字・隣り合う同値の区間は1組にまとめる。(5) COLOR の値のビットの意味・第2〜4引数の意味・COLOR 以外の属性は未測定のまま（n をそのまま書く）。

events.title: fix: merge WinUAE drawing updates and fix RTG swap and masked NOTSRC blits (#2391)
events.message:
fix: merge WinUAE drawing updates and fix RTG swap and masked NOTSRC blits (#2391)

* fix(rtg): swap full pixels in BLIT_SWAP and honour the mask in BLIT_NOTSRC

BLIT_SWAP kept the destination in a uae_u16 or uae_u8 temporary while
the blit templates step in 32-bit words, so the source half of every
swapped word lost bits at all pixel depths; the 24-bit byte tail never
wrote its source back. The swap source rectangle is now also marked
dirty. The 8-bit masked dispatch called the unmasked BLIT_NOTSRC_8,
overwriting destination bits outside the plane mask.

Found while checking WinUAE PR #520's Unix RTG fixes against the
Windows-derived implementation.

* fix(drawing): merge WinUAE sprite LTS and display start limit fixes

Skip select_lts() when a normally armed sprite is still active, and
accept custom display limits whose start lies anywhere inside the
input buffer instead of only its first half. Ports WinUAE 09a1aa57
and 58104461 (68764eaf restores the multithreaded Denise flag that
58104461 cleared, so it nets out).
events.author: midwan

events.title: ndskit: the 2D engines, the geometry engine, an OpenGL renderer, a window
events.message:
ndskit: the 2D engines, the geometry engine, an OpenGL renderer, a window

The runtime draws. Both 2D engines run in software a line at a time, as
each line starts: every background form (text, affine, extended, the
bitmaps), 16 and 256 colours with the extended palettes, sprites in
tiles and bitmaps, affine and double-size, windows, blending, the master
brightness, the display modes. Engine A's BG0 as the 3D layer is left to
a compositor, two words a pixel saying what lies under the 3D and how
they blend, so the 3D can be drawn at another resolution than the 2D.

The geometry engine runs GXFIFO's packed commands and the ports in the
DS's fixed point: the matrix stacks, vertices, texture coordinate
transforms, lighting, strips, culling, clipping, the viewport, the
tests. SWAP_BUFFERS waits for the VBlank with the commands behind it
queued; at line 215 the rendering engine takes the lists, the 3D
registers and the texture memory.

The rendering engine is OpenGL 4.5 at any scale. The texture memory goes
up whole and the fragment shader reads it as the DS's texture unit does,
the seven formats included; colours combine in the DS's integers;
attributes are interpolated at the pixel's top left corner and texture
coordinates kept in 1/16 texel, as the DS does; translucency, the alpha
test and fog follow. A window (SDL3) composes the 2D at the DS's size
with the 3D at its own, paced by the host's clock with the vertical
sync, the keyboard as the buttons and the mouse as the stylus. Headless
runs write both screens as PNGs at given frames, through a hidden
window, and draw only the frames they photograph.

events.message:
feat(kernel): tapes as deck cards, read exactly (#26 slice 6)

A TAPE SCN= CHAN= card and rows of seven numbers (g.e.t., r, v) fill /CTAPE/
through the card reader (src/vdktap.f), so a reel can carry a ready tape.
The reader now takes 16-17 significant digits (and powers down to 10**-44)
through a double-double path, DKDD, so any double written with 17 digits
reads back to the same bits; 15 digits and 10**22 keep the old fast path.
Deck errors 28-30 cover a full tape, rows out of order, and a tape for a
scenario not read or a second scenario. A deck tape reports source 3.

tools/vtape.f writes the engine's tape as such a deck (VIEW_TAPEW), and
golden.sh's tape round trip checks 13 frames drawn from the read-back tape
against the engine's own. The selftest checks the wasm and fallback readers
against the native one on both scenarios' tapes, plus 10 planted faults.

refactor(loop): one emu_run_frame() shared by the Z80 thread and the -H loop (#77)

* refactor(loop): one emu_run_frame() shared by the Z80 thread and the -H loop

The GUI's Z80 thread and the headless main loop each carried a copy of
every per-frame duty (stats publish, bridge frame, tape wave, stop
handling, frame counters, exit-after, VBL events, recorders, session,
autotype, telnet, IPC frame step), and the -H copy had drifted. Both
loops now call emu_run_frame() (src/emu_frame.h); they keep only what
differs: the GUI thread publishes to the video ring and wakes the render
thread, -H services its drains, dock preview and screenshot inline.

Drift settled on the GUI behaviour:
- -H now relays scanned keyboard rows to the KeyboardManager, so
  BufferedUntilRead releases held keys.
- a finished step pauses through cpc_pause(), not a bare CPC.paused write.
- AVI capture skips frameskipped frames in both loops.
- audio push gates on g_emu_paused; blit/frameskip use the same limit_now.
- --fps / --debug logging now also prints under -H.

KONCPC_E2E_HEADLESS=1 makes ipc_harness run every launch with --headless.

Add amiga_gfx.s for custom-screen graphics API implementation

This commit introduces amiga_gfx.s, a new assembly file that provides a comprehensive graphics API for the Amiga platform. The implementation includes functions for initializing and shutting down graphics, opening and closing screens, handling bitmaps and sprites, and various drawing operations such as lines, rectangles, circles, and text. events.title: ndskit: the machine, threads as coroutines, melonDS savestates, discovery's new forms
events.message:
ndskit: the machine, threads as coroutines, melonDS savestates, discovery's new forms

The runtime runs a cartridge's recompiled programs as the DS does,
headless (ndsrun). Both CPUs keep their own clocks and run in quanta of
virtual time, a safe point standing for a fixed number of ticks; events
fire the lines, the timers and the card between quanta, and a run is the
same run every time. Each of the SDK's threads runs on its own coroutine
(fibers on Windows), since recompiled code nests its calls on the host
stack: the guest's own context switches, OS_LoadContext's exception
return and the IRQ handler's return with another thread's frame, name
the thread to switch to, by a marker pushed when an interrupt is taken,
by the sp a context save left, or by an entry for a new thread.

The machine has the BIOS as melonDS's direct boot leaves it and its SWIs
in C++, the interrupt entry as the BIOS makes it, both CPUs' I/O, VRAM
through its nine banks, timers, DMA, IPC, the maths unit, the
cartridge's commands and its backup memory, SPI (power, firmware,
touch), the RTC, the sound registers, and input from a script. A call
trace, breaks, a store watch, and a report of where each CPU polls and
what its stack holds show what a run does. melonds reads melonDS's
savestates and compares their memories with a run's.

The recompiler learned context saves (a function that returns twice;
its callers unwind to their landings), an entry hook, and --copy for
code a program copies elsewhere and runs there. Discovery learned
interrupt stubs, the small virtual methods and thunks of C++ vtables,
switches bounded by their first compare, holes in tables of offsets and
conditional code addresses; on the first port every function Ghidra
finds is now found, with no conflict on three cartridges.

Wacom: honour SC, the range TVPaint asks for

With "Wacom A4+ Pressure" TVPaint's init sends SC15240,15240 and maps
that range onto the whole screen. The virtual tablet ignored SC and kept
reporting 10160 x 7620, so the ink stopped at about two thirds across
and half way down — correct only near the top-left, which is why the
2026-08-25 check read as "tracks correctly". Read off the device log.

SC now sets the output range (validated to 1..65535 per axis), ~C
reports the active range, and RE / reset restore the native one.
Protocol test extended; all checks pass.

events.title: Save and load the PCMCIA controllers and card state
events.message:
Save and load the PCMCIA controllers and card state

The state file now holds the registers of both PCMCIA controllers and the
state of the inserted cards: the flash command state machine of linear
cards, and the task file registers, FIFO and state of ATA cards.

Which card is inserted is a preference. Each card's state is saved with a
tag for the kind of card and its length, so loading with a different card
(or none) skips the card state with a warning instead of misreading the
rest of the file. NewtonOS still expects the saved card in that case, so a
later step must make sure the same cards are inserted.

TMemoryStream is a small header-only stream in memory, used to measure the
card state. The state file version is now 6.

release: bound and diagnose the bundled-closure banner check

The banner check ran the rewired hatari in a $( ) substitution, which
swallows both the output and a hang: the first rpath-purged run sat there
for six hours until the job's timeout cancelled it, with hatari left as the
orphan process the runner cleanup named. The purge had made the runner load
the bundled dylibs for the first time — every earlier pass loaded
Homebrew's, because the inherited /opt/homebrew/lib rpath won the search —
so the check now runs to files under a 60s watchdog, reports the exit path
plainly, and captures a sample(1) backtrace of a hang instead of silence.

events.title: Preserve amiga.cfg contents and document CD32 controller support
events.message:
Preserve amiga.cfg contents and document CD32 controller support

Fix how amiga.cfg is written so an existing file is updated instead of
being rebuilt, and document the optional CD32 configuration the branch
already provides.

Reason for the save fix:
- The previous save path rewrote amiga.cfg from scratch whenever the
  in-game Options audio volumes changed. On a file that also carried
  manual edits, comments, unknown keys or CD32 assignments, that rebuild
  could drop everything that was not part of the hard-coded template.

Save behaviour (existing contents and keys):
- Only the value token of each volume key (music_adlib, music_mhi,
  music_wave, sfx_volume) is rewritten. The rest of the file - comments,
  unknown keys, key order, spacing, CR/LF bytes and a missing final
  newline - is copied through byte for byte.
- Missing volume keys are appended at the end using the file's existing
  EOL style. The CD32 block is not appended to an existing file; it is
  written only when amiga.cfg is created from scratch.
- Keys are matched case-insensitively, and repeated keys are all updated.

Safe replacement and error handling:
- The new contents are written to a uniquely chosen temporary file
  (amiga.cfg.tmpN). An existing amiga.cfg is first renamed aside as
  amiga.cfg.bakN, and the backup is removed only after the temporary file
  has been renamed into place.
- Any write, close, rename or backup failure aborts the update, removes
  the temporary file and leaves the previous file in place (restoring it
  from the backup when possible). This is not a full power-loss guarantee.

Added tests:
- tests/amiga_cfg_test.cpp and tests/run_amiga_cfg_test.sh cover old
  audio-only files, customized CD32 assignments, preservation of comments,
  unknown keys, unusual whitespace, CRLF and a missing final newline,
  missing and repeated case-insensitive keys, repeated saves without
  duplication, and temp-file/replace/restore failure handling.
- Run with: bash tests/run_amiga_cfg_test.sh

Documentation scope:
- Describe the optional CD32 gamepad (default cd32 = OFF), the seven
  configurable button-action keys and the allowed actions (FIRE,
  SPECIAL_SELECT, MEGA_BOMB, PAUSE, CANCEL, NONE), the in-game versus
  menu/intro action behaviour, held-button blocking across context
  changes, the plain-joystick fallback and port cleanup, the amiga.cfg
  search/save path, automatic creation, in-place save semantics and the
  temporary/backup file mechanism.
- Updated README.md, README_AMIGA.md, README_AMIGA_PL.md, CHANGELOG.md
  (Unreleased), raptor.readme, docs/porting-analysis.md, and added a
  docs/amiga.cfg.example reference configuration.

Validation and pending tests:
- git diff --check passes; bash tests/run_amiga_cfg_test.sh passes.
- The Amiga build passed in the earlier branch reports; no full Amiga
  rebuild was run for this change (a documentation plus amiga.cfg
  persistence commit).
- Runtime status is unchanged from the earlier CD32 work on this branch:
  preliminary, partial behaviour was reported with a Sega-style pad under
  WinUAE. Full validation with a physical CD32 pad is still pending and is
  expected from a second tester. The native Sega serial protocol is not
  implemented and no full CD32 validation is claimed.

This commit does not add the CD32 input implementation itself (already
present on this branch); it hardens amiga.cfg persistence, adds the
configuration tests and expands the documentation.

project.title: SunDog: Frozen Legacy — Apple II native and p-code reconstruction
project.display_title: SunDog: Frozen Legacy — Apple II native and p-code reconstruction
project.status: Upstream byte-identical native/p-code disk rebuild with explicit 488-byte data assumption
project.notes: Identity: README, source index and final delivery receipt identify reconstruction of two supplied Apple II SunDog disks. There is no license grant in the pinned root tree. The exact 488-byte unidentified-data exception remains prominently disclosed. Classification: This rebuilds original 6502 native routines and the historical SYSTEM.APPLE p-code runtime, with ca65 macros reproducing Pascal p-code and data. It does not introduce a modern embedded CPU emulator or translate the game to guessed high-level Pascal. Source CPU: The source index identifies native 6502 instructions and UCSD Pascal p-code. The 6502 is the physical processor; p-code is a virtual instruction set implemented by the historical runtime, not a second physical source CPU. Target CPU: Source-built native bootstrap/runtime components are explicitly ca65 6502, with p-code reconstructed as byte-accurate instruction macros for that original runtime. Output is two native Apple II disks; no modern host CPU is inferred. Build: Final receipt records two isolated strict builds without originals/prior outputs, byte-identical disk hashes, and 184,828 source-built, 101,404 identified-data and 488 user-assumed-data bytes. Handoff reports 180 passing tests. MAME and Apple2TS baseline checks cover play entry, disk swaps, utilities and save/fresh reload. These are upstream receipts, not independent verification by this review. All four build flags remain unknown because no candidate build, comparison or runtime test was performed here. Limitations: No candidate code was run here. The 488-byte classification is expressly an accepted assumption, not proved data; source-built totals include declarations. Combat/travel/audio/timing are not exhaustive, and final identical outputs reuse earlier behavioral baselines. Runtime profiles: MAME evidence uses an unenhanced Apple IIe with Disk II and joystick; Apple2TS used another model. These are test configurations, not an established minimum CPU/RAM requirement, so no runtime minimum is inferred. AI: The reviewed documentation, source-tree names and latest available commit messages contain no explicit development-AI attribution. Usage remains unknown; neither prose style nor lack of an instruction file establishes non-use. events.title: chore(loop): delete dead Caprice32-era paths from both emulation loops (#76)
events.message:
chore(loop): delete dead Caprice32-era paths from both emulation loops (#76)

Both copies of the emulation loop (z80_thread_main and the -H loop) still
carried paths that cannot run on v6, where the sub-cycle board is the only
engine:

- the EC_CYCLE_COUNT speed limiter: nothing produces EC_CYCLE_COUNT, so
  the sleep/deadline branch never ran and the frameskip cap it fed was
  unreachable (consecutive_skips was reset every iteration). The
  frameskip decision is kept, with its current behaviour, as one
  expression (follow-up beads-af0k);
- the EC_SOUND_BUFFER push blocks: nothing produces EC_SOUND_BUFFER;
  audio comes back from subcycle_bridge_frame(). pbSndBuffer,
  pbSndBufferEnd and CPC.snd_bufferptr were only read there;
- the VDU.scrln / CPC.scr_base / CPC.scr_pos recompute: scrln has no
  writer and scr_base/scr_pos have no reader, so the fields go too;
- the FDC.led else-branches: FDC.led has no writer, and
  subcycle_bridge_disk_leds() already reports both LEDs off when the
  bridge is down, which is what the else-branch computed;
- the non-bridge cpc_pause() fallback after a breakpoint: EC_BREAKPOINT
  is only produced by subcycle_bridge_debug_sync() inside the active
  branch;
- the !g_headless block inside the g_headless branch of the -H loop
  (OSD, topbar FPS, video_display/_b, partial audio push): g_headless is
  never cleared once set.

No behaviour change. The EC_CYCLE_COUNT and EC_SOUND_BUFFER enum values
are removed so nothing can test for them again.

events.title: Clear the JIT cache after loading a state, make save and load robust
events.message:
Clear the JIT cache after loading a state, make save and load robust

After loading a state, the JIT could keep running code translated from the
old memory: InvalidateTLB() only forgets the virtual addresses, but pages
are also found by physical address, and they point into the RAM block that
was just reallocated. TJITCache::InvalidateAll() unlinks every page, and
TMemory::TransferState calls it after loading.

TEmulator::SaveState() and LoadState() return false instead of crashing when
the file is missing or cut off, and free the stream on every path. The
Monitor reports failures. Guards resume the serial drivers and unlock the
interrupt manager's mutex even if loading throws.

events.message:
Worker chain carries the cache-bust token; remote terminals created before the boot

Worker mode on the deployed site failed with "Cannot call unknown
function DescribeMachineINI": the page's script tags carry the build's
?v= token, but the Worker was created as js/emu-worker.js, imported
../nd100wasm.js and fetched the .wasm with no token, so the Cloudflare
edge in front of the storage account handed out the 1 July emu-worker.js
and nd100wasm.js (cache HIT, max-age 14400) next to the new index.html.
Direct mode loads nd100wasm.js?v=... and worked. Now emu-proxy-worker.js
reads the token off its own script tag and puts it on the Worker URL;
the Worker passes its query string on to nd100wasm.js, the .wasm and
disk-io-worker.js. Verified headless: all four module requests carry
the token and the ND-100 boots in Worker + persistent-storage mode.

Gateway terminals: with the WebSocket bridge on, TERMINAL 12-19 are now
created between Init and the boot (remoteTerminalsBeforeBoot). Created
after the boot had started - the bridge's auto-connect did that about a
second late - SINTRAN never answered them; created before, it does.
Measured through a test gateway on ports 18777/15077.

events.title: 889: C64 Ultimate in the workbench — stream wiring, relay, selector, paused marker
events.message:
889: C64 Ultimate in the workbench — stream wiring, relay, selector, paused marker

The C64U backend owns its C64UStreams while selected (start on select without
waiting, re-arm after a reset, stop on deselect/switch with the fixed UDP ports
freed first), serves audio/start (48,003.07 Hz), session/frame_indices and the
screenshot from the stream, and emits stream/paused. The workbench server relays
JSON-RPC, notifications and the binary frames over /runtime-relay while a C64U is
selected, with a select API that asks first (409 until confirmed), device list,
start-monitor, and a REST password held in memory only. The page gets a backend
selector in the top bar, the switch dialog, a PAUSED marker on the Live tab, and
WsClient.restart(). The emulator path is unchanged.

events.title: fix(ipc): wait vbl counts real frames instead of sleeping 20ms per blank (#75)
events.message:
fix(ipc): wait vbl counts real frames instead of sleeping 20ms per blank (#75)

`wait vbl N` resumed the machine, slept N x 20ms of wall time and paused,
so the frame count was whatever the host fit in: `wait vbl 50` ran 143-182
frames unloaded and 260-275 on saturated E-cores (beads-71pg). It now rides
the frame-step counter `step frame` uses, so it ends paused N frames on,
in both the threaded GUI loop and the -H headless loop.

The deadline contract is kept (ipc_wait_vbl_default_timeout, ERR 408, then
paused); a server shutdown is still ERR 503. New: a breakpoint stopping the
machine first answers ERR 409 stopped-elsewhere and leaves the hit for
`wait bp`; a count below 1 is ERR 400; a plain pause someone else lifts
only delays the count. Only a paused machine is resumed: a running one can
finish the counted frames and pause itself before the server's resume,
which then set it running again behind an OK (caught in the -H loop).

Tests: unit (fake frame loop: exactly N, 408 without frames, ERR 400) and
e2e test_wait_vbl_counts_real_frames (firmware TIME at &B8B4, both loops,
equals `step frame 50`, 409 on a breakpoint, 408 ends paused and disarmed).
Harness comments that called it a sleep are updated.

events.title: refactor(quickdraw): share one row intersection between 68K and PowerPC (#4182 follow-up) (#4206)
events.message:
refactor(quickdraw): share one row intersection between 68K and PowerPC (#4182 follow-up) (#4206)

* refactor(quickdraw): share one row intersection with the PowerPC path

region_rows::intersect_rows now serves both rows QuickDraw produced and
rows parsed from guest region storage. It splits both rows into their
non-empty intervals, checks in one pass over each that the interval starts
never decrease, and takes the merge pass if both rows pass and the
all-pairs pass otherwise.

That check is all the merge pass needs. The pass moves past an interval
once it ends no later than the other row's current interval; every later
interval of the other row starts no earlier than that one, so its overlap
with the interval left behind lies inside an overlap the pass already
emitted. Touching, overlapping and nested intervals therefore give the
same output from both passes, as do odd trailing endpoints and empty or
inverted pairs, which are dropped before either pass. The passes part
only when a start falls below an earlier one, as in [5, 6, 0, 1] against
[0, 1, 5, 6]. A brute-force check of a model of both passes over every pair
of start-ordered rows of up to three non-empty intervals with
coordinates 0-6 found no difference.

The PowerPC path takes the function as ppc_region_intersect_rows and drops
its own all-pairs copy, so PowerPC output is unchanged on all rows.

The 68K trap path keeps the merge-only form, renamed
intersect_sorted_rows, for InsetRgn and the Intersection arm of
combine_rows, so 68K output is unchanged on all rows.

Tests: the shared function against the previous PowerPC all-pairs code on
50,000 arbitrary row pairs, 50,000 non-decreasing pairs and 50,000 pairs
with ordered starts (overlapping and nested intervals, empty and inverted
pairs and odd endpoints mixed in); on non-decreasing and start-ordered
pairs, the shared function, the previous 68K merge code and the previous
PowerPC code all agree; hand cases for the check and for the
intersection, including the unsorted counter-example.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_017DBmcphGyyAFGkZM1oyy6e

* fix(quickdraw): keep every piece when intersecting out-of-order 68K rows

The 68K trap path intersected region rows with the merge-only pass, which
drops pieces when a row lists an interval starting below an earlier one.
Such rows reach it from guest memory: SectRgn takes any pair of region
handles, CopyRgn and SetClip copy region bytes verbatim into visRgn and
clipRgn, and the region parser applies each scanline's inversion points
in the order stored, so an app-built row such as [5, 6, 0, 1] stays in
that order. SectRgn of that row with [0, 1, 5, 6] gave [5, 6].

Inside Macintosh calls the region data compact and Imaging With
QuickDraw calls it proprietary (IM I-141-I-142; IWQ 2-7, 2-29), so the
real QuickDraw result for such data is not specified. Taking the
all-pairs pass for them makes the 68K path agree with the PowerPC path,
which already did, and makes the intersection independent of the order
the intervals are listed in, as the union already is.

combine_rows and InsetRgn now use region_rows::intersect_rows, and the
merge-only intersect_sorted_rows is removed. Every row QuickDraw itself
writes has ordered starts, so the merge pass still runs on those and their
output does not change; only rows with a falling start change, and only
in what the merge pass dropped.

Tests: a SectRgn test with an app-built out-of-order row, which fails on
the merge-only path; the shared-row property tests now expect the
previous 68K intersection on rows with ordered starts and the previous
PowerPC all-pairs one elsewhere.

events.title: fix(sound): play sampled-sound instruments for PowerPC soundCmd and note commands (#4205)
events.message:
fix(sound): play sampled-sound instruments for PowerPC soundCmd and note commands (#4205)

* fix(sound): play soundCmd instruments on PowerPC freqCmd and freqDurationCmd

PowerPC SndDoImmediate decoded only bufferCmd. A sampled-sound channel
driven the classic instrument way -- flushCmd, quietCmd, soundCmd with
a SoundHeader pointer, ampCmd, rateCmd, then freqCmd with a MIDI note --
reached the process sound manager as commands it ignores, so every
effect played this way was silent.

Inside Macintosh: Sound (1994) describes soundCmd as installing a
sampled sound as a channel's voice without playing it (pp. 2-44,
2-97), and freqCmd / freqDurationCmd as playing that voice at a MIDI
note value in the range 0 to 127, middle C being 60 (pp. 2-41--2-42,
2-95--2-96). The header's baseFrequency, 1 to 127, is the note at
which the sample plays at its recorded rate (p. 2-105).

soundCmd now decodes the SoundHeader through the existing header and
codec path and keeps it as the channel's installed voice. freqCmd and
freqDurationCmd play it, transposed in equal-tempered semitones from
baseFrequency; a note or baseFrequency outside those ranges plays the
recorded rate. The book limits soundCmd to noncompressed data (p. 2-97)
and expects compressed sounds to be expanded first (p. 2-109);
compressed headers are accepted because they decode to the same
samples. SndDisposeChannel drops the channel's voice. Undecodable
headers install nothing and are reported under SYSTEMLESS_TRACE_SOUND.

Measured with the compressed AIFF-C file-playback fix also applied
(no run without it was made): on a headless PowerPC replay that
enters gameplay (5400 ticks), 14 effects start on three channels
(sound-bank headers transposed from notes 52-67).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_017DBmcphGyyAFGkZM1oyy6e

* fix(sound): loop sampled-sound voices between their loop points

A note played from a sampled-sound voice ended with the sound, so
voices meant to sustain under freqCmd played once. Inside Macintosh:
Sound (1994) specifies that a note longer than the sound replays the
frames between the header's loop points (p. 2-45), that freqCmd plays
indefinitely and changes the pitch of a note already playing
(p. 2-96), that freqDurationCmd starts at the beginning of the voice
and plays for param1 half-milliseconds (pp. 2-41, 2-45, 2-95--2-96),
and that loopStart = loopEnd = 0 means no loop (p. 2-105).

Move the soundCmd voice from the PowerPC adapter into the shared
sound channel so both command paths can use it:

- SampledInstrument holds the decoded samples, base note, and loop
  points; the PowerPC adapter decodes them from the SoundHeader.
- freqCmd and freqDurationCmd are channel commands. A freqCmd note
  repeats its loop until quietCmd; a freqDurationCmd note repeats it
  for its duration and then plays to the end of the sound. freqCmd on
  a playing note changes its pitch in place. The channel's rateCmd
  rate still applies.

Three readings go beyond the book; they are inferences from shipped
sound headers, not documented behaviour:

- Loop points are frame numbers. The book calls them byte numbers,
  which coincide for 8-bit mono data, and its Listing 2-17
  (pp. 2-45--2-46) computes byte offsets for extended and compressed
  headers; p. 2-109 says compressed loop points describe the sound
  before compression. The shipped 16-bit and compressed headers store
  frame numbers: whole-sound loops end at loopEnd ~ numFrames x
  samples per packet (within 64 samples), and a 16-bit header's
  markers sit at 5162/5163 of 5164 frames, where byte offsets would be
  about 10326.
- loopEnd is exclusive. Listing 2-17 treats it as inclusive; the
  shipped headers point both ways.
- A loop must span at least two frames. Most shipped headers carry
  loopEnd = loopStart + 1, mid-sound or on the last frames; repeating
  that one frame would cut those sounds short and hold the channel
  busy forever. Under the inclusive reading these markers span two
  frames.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_017DBmcphGyyAFGkZM1oyy6e

* fix(sound): honour ampCmd and correct the restCmd number

ampCmd was ignored on both CPU paths, and the 68K dispatcher took
command 43 for restCmd. Inside Macintosh: Sound (1994) numbers restCmd
41 and ampCmd 43 (p. 2-12); ampCmd sets the amplitude, 0 to 255 in
param1, of the sound playing and, when none is, of the next sound
played (p. 2-96).

The channel now keeps an ampCmd amplitude (full by default) that the
mixer applies on top of volumeCmd's volume, so it persists across
bufferCmd, file playback, and notes. SndDoImmediate handles ampCmd on
the PowerPC and 68K paths; restCmd (41) stays an accepted no-op.

Applications that sent 43 expecting it to be ignored now get the
amplitude they asked for.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_017DBmcphGyyAFGkZM1oyy6e

* fix(sound): queue soundCmd, note, and ampCmd commands through SndDoCommand

Only SndDoImmediate installed sampled-sound voices and played notes.
Through SndDoCommand, soundCmd reached the channel FIFO as a raw guest
pointer that the queue ignores, and freqCmd and freqDurationCmd were
ignored. The queue also waits for any playing sound, which is right
for bufferCmd, but notes must not hold the queue the way buffers do:
a queued quietCmd or pitch change behind a sustained freqCmd note
would never run.

- The PowerPC adapter decodes a queued soundCmd's SoundHeader when it
  is queued and the FIFO installs the voice in order; an undecodable
  header queues "no voice".
- The FIFO runs freqCmd, freqDurationCmd, and ampCmd.
- A note no longer holds the queue the way a sampled buffer does.
  Inside Macintosh: Sound (1994) describes freqCmd as playing
  indefinitely (p. 2-96) and pairs freqDurationCmd with a queued
  quietCmd that stops the note after its duration (pp. 2-41--2-42,
  2-95). A freqDurationCmd note therefore holds the queue for its
  duration, measured at mix-frame granularity, and a freqCmd note does
  not hold it at all. A note whose sound ends first frees the queue
  when it ends.

The 68K SndDoCommand path keeps its guest-memory queue and its own
soundCmd handling; ampCmd already reaches it through the shared command
executor.

events.message:
feat(kernel): the card reader reads run decks beside BLOCK DATA

#26 slice 4. The kernel can now read its own run decks: src/vdeck.f
(CRDOPN, CRDIN one card image, CRDEND) and src/vdkscn.f (what each card
writes) fill the scenario and situation tables from the mission and
scenario .scn cards, word for word as BLOCK DATA does. Numbers are read
exactly, as an integer mantissa (15 digits at most) and one multiply or
divide by an exact power of ten, so each double is the decimal correctly
rounded, the constant a compiler makes of the same digits. A deck fault
is refused with a numbered deck error and the card number; nothing is
truncated.

The vocabulary (card kinds, keys, code words) is generated by gen_data
from the tables it already checks decks with (src/vdvoc.f, .inc), so the
words have one source. The shell exports deck_open, deck_card(n),
deck_close and deck_sum (a hash total of the run tables, ours); the
native driver takes VIEW_DECK and VIEW_DKSUM. The page still loads BLOCK
DATA; slice 5 switches it.

generated tables); golden capture now also loads build/decks.txt through

events.title: fix(serial): IPC and the Serial Terminal drive the board's rs232 card (#72)
events.message:
fix(serial): IPC and the Serial Terminal drive the board's rs232 card (#72)

`serial send`/`send_string` queued bytes into a Z80Dart object the CPU
never addressed: its port handlers were reachable only through
io_dispatch, which nothing on the sub-cycle board calls. `serial status`
reported that object's permanently empty FIFO, and the Serial Terminal was
fed from a callback that never fired. A program polling the real card at
&FADE spun forever.

SerialInterface now holds two host-side queues. Bytes for the CPC
(IPC, the terminal's input box) wait in rx_queue until the bridge pumps
them into the card's RX FIFO, no more per frame than rs232_rx_room()
allows, so nothing overruns; the backend's bytes follow the same path and
stay in the backend until there is room (the old per-frame drain pushed
them all at once and lost all but three). Bytes the CPC sends are
mirrored by host_tx() into a monitor the terminal drains on the UI
thread. `serial status` and both UI status lines read the card's own
RR0/RR1 off the board, and add rx_fifo, rx_pending and rx_overrun.
`serial send` answers ERR 409 when the card is not on the host wire.

Z80Dart, Intel8253, dart_remap, the $FADx/$FBDx io_dispatch handlers
and serial_interface_register_io are deleted, with their tests.

events.title: Fix Android multiplayer crash and enable cross-platform play (#3)
events.message:
Fix Android multiplayer crash and enable cross-platform play (#3)

* Fix Android multiplayer crash and enable cross-platform play

The Android host never assigned a NetworkDataReceiver to the GameView, so
the multiplayer server/client had no data receiver. When a remote
participant sent data, Server.HandleData threw an ExceptionFreeserf
outside its try/catch on a background Task.Run thread, crashing the app.

Also Host.GetLocalIpAddress() used Windows-only APIs (IsDnsEligible,
PrefixOrigin) that throw PlatformNotSupportedException on Android, so
creating a client or server crashed immediately.

Fixes:

events.title: fix(dsp): indexed store after a divide writes the old data (JTRM bug 2)
events.message:
fix(dsp): indexed store after a divide writes the old data (JTRM bug 2)

Xenowings (#811) ignored all in-game input.  Its DSP joypad reader ends
with

    div   r9,r8          ; r8 = active-low joypad bits, inverted
    store r8,(r14+1)     ; -> $F1C3A8, the game's pad variable

JTRM Rev 8 p.134, TOM/JERRY bug 2 "Scoreboard Failure on Indexed
Addressing Mode Stores" ("applies to both Tom & Jerry"): the data of
store instructions 49, 50, 60 and 61 is not scoreboarded, so when it is
the result of a divide still in flight the store writes the register's
old contents.  On silicon $F1C3A8 gets the joypad bits.  This core
wrote the quotient instead, so the game read a value that did not track
the pad and the ship never moved: 600 gameplay frames with held input
hashed the same as a run with no input.

Model it for the documented pattern only: a divide immediately followed
by an indexed store whose data register is the divide's destination
(and is not one of its address registers) stores the pre-divide value.
The armed state lives in DSPExec locals and the loop runs that one
instruction past its budget, as the bug-13 load fix-up does, so nothing
outlives a slice and there is no savestate change.  The idle-loop
fast-forward rejects a loop in which it fired.  Test-ABI counter
dsp_div_store_fixups counts applications.

Not modeled: a store later within the divide latency, the external-load
variant of bug 2, a divide in a branch delay slot, and the GPU side.

test/tools/xenowings_ingame_video now also runs a forked no-input
reference arm and holds RIGHT from the first lit gameplay frame; the
frame-hash streams must diverge within 600 frames.  Before: 0 frames
differ (FAIL).  After: 835 differ, first at +366 (PASS); the ship moves,
fires and scores.

Depends on the DSP bug-13 fix (#822) and the 68000 prefetch model (#823).

Refs #811

events.title: fix(debug): a step refreshes the chip views, so rom:LO follows the ROM-switch OUT (#73)
events.message:
fix(debug): a step refreshes the chip views, so rom:LO follows the ROM-switch OUT (#73)

The IPC context line (rom:LO,...), the Gate Array / CRTC / PSG DevTools
windows and the disassembly cache read the host GateArray / CRTC / PSG
mirrors. Only subcycle_bridge_debug_sync() published them, once per frame.
z80_step_instruction() refreshed the registers alone, so while paused the
chip views kept the state from before the pause: after stepping the
firmware's ROM-switching OUT at &B9B2 on a 6128+, rom:LO stayed while the
CPU view already had the RAM paged in. The Devices themselves always
agreed: the Gate Array latch and the memory Device's latch of the same
write match on every step.

Extract the chip-view publication into subcycle_bridge_sync_chip_views()
and run it after a step and after a snapshot load as well as per frame.

Live probe, 1500 step stops on a 6128+: rom: disagreed with the CPU view
on 726 stops before (rom:LO on all 1500), 0 after.

subjects: Legends of Valour: Volume I – The Dawning
source_language: original game map/texture/sprite data and behavior
project.status: Work in progress; substantial renderer/exploration implementation
project.notes: Repository describes a Web reimplementation of Legends of Valour, with Vue/Vite and JavaScript WebGL2 code. The active src/engine/index.js has map tile decoding/collision, camera and character/sprite rendering, update logic and asset loading. useGame.js directly initializes that engine; the empty src/game/Game.js is not the only implementation. Build package has Vite dev/build/preview scripts; bundled map/texture/sprite image assets are loaded at runtime. README's reverse-engineering section is empty and does not establish the exact original edition being reconstructed. Listed original platforms describe the game's lineage, not verified separate ports. README still lists inventory, audio/music, scheduling, rendering/collision refactors and networking as TODO. No complete RPG gameplay or faithful finished recreation is claimed. Root GPL v3 does not establish rights to all original-game-derived artwork/data; no provenance blanket assumed. No local build/run performed. Empty/refactor stub files coexist with the substantial active renderer. A separate unfinished browser reimplementation of Legends of Valour. The README’s Amiga/Atari ST/MS-DOS release summary does not identify which edition supplied the analysed maps/assets. Root GPL v3 concerns code; it does not establish rights to original-game-derived art/data. Refactor stubs coexist with an active renderer. The README repeats historical release platforms, but its reverse-engineering section is empty and no exact original edition/binary is identified in the reviewed renderer. Neither source platforms nor source CPU are promoted from this lineage list. Amiga, Atari ST and DOS remain provenance context only. The active JavaScript engine and Vue/Vite package target a WebGL2 browser. They establish no native machine ISA or specific CPU requirements, so target_cpu stays null. src/composables/useGame.js initializes the substantive src/engine/index.js renderer, with map decoding, collision, sprite/camera and asset loading. Empty refactor stubs do not negate the implementation, but inventory/audio/scheduling/networking remain TODO and no successful current build or complete RPG playtest is established. All flags remain null. WebGL2/browser use is evident from the active engine, but no supported browser/GPU list, CPU minimum or RAM requirement is documented. No runtime profile is inferred from graphics APIs alone. project.title: EDOS — distribution-media analysis and extraction toolkit
project.display_title: EDOS — distribution-media analysis and extraction toolkit
source_language: binary distribution catalogue and disk data
project.status: Partial EDOS catalogue/disk-format research and extraction toolkit; tape extraction and several format/timing details remain incomplete.
project.notes: Reverse-engineers the early-1990s EDOS on-demand distribution CDs, including encrypted catalogue metadata, disk block records, flux lengths and compressed MFM/GCR bits. Actual Python implementation decrypts metadata, reads EDOS disk headers, extracts per-side/per-track blocks and computes pulse/bit statistics. It recognizes A35 Atari ST and A36 Amiga among disk platform IDs. Separate tape-controller documentation covers the 6809 controller; tape entry types are recognized but iter_blocks currently implements disk blocks only. Python command dispatch and extraction/statistics implementation are present, but no explicit successful runtime result or independently verified conversion was established. No package/build manifest was found. All build flags remain unknown. Separate repository root for EDOS format research; GitHub metadata reports fork=false, which alone does not prove originality. No repository-root match was found in the current catalogue or reviewed decisions; wider author/link research is not exhausted. Rights/provenance: No license identified. Research/extraction code, not a complete EDOS duplicator, game remake or tape converter. Sega IDs, unusual Amiga format 0x14 and accurate flux timing remain TODO. Tape-platform documentation should not be mistaken for implemented tape extraction. No license file or explicit redistribution grant identified; from_cds includes historical catalogue/controller-related material. No explicit AI-use attribution was found in the bounded reviewed material. Absence is not proof of non-use; usage stays null. Review scope: README, selected source/build/rights files and 7 latest default-branch commits; absence is not proof of no AI use. No independent compilation, installation, execution, playtest, hardware test or original-program binary comparison was performed in this catalogue review. Repository creation dates are not treated as reconstruction start dates. Evidence: https://github.com/ymgve/edos_reversing/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/ymgve/edos_reversing/blob/main/edostool.py https://github.com/ymgve/edos_reversing/blob/main/edoslib.py https://github.com/ymgve/edos_reversing/blob/main/tape_controller_system.md https://github.com/ymgve/edos_reversing/commit/c555b6c3c0949d28e6715f23c8f06cdc43aa8b32 https://github.com/ymgve Source platforms describe catalogued media families, including the README’s Spectrum tape ID; implemented block extraction remains disk-only. Tape platform recognition is not tape extraction support. CPU audit (2026-10-08): complete-tree processor/assembly/output search found no corroborated source or target ISA. The documented 6809 controller remains explicitly hypothetical and is not promoted.

project.notes: One multi-repository suite that exposes real Amiga files and floppy images to Linux over a null-modem serial link. alsfssrv.c implements a resident Amiga serial command server for filesystem listing/read/write/delete/rename, ADF floppy operations and keyboard input; amiga_operations.c uses DOS and trackdisk.device APIs. The author’s separate documentation identifies alsfsAmigaServer, alsfsNodejsServer and the Linux FUSE alsfs client as parts of one suite, not independent products. Server Makefile uses vbcc +kick13 and Amiga NDK; source says tested on an unexpanded A600 with Workbench 2.1. Suite documentation requires Workbench 2.1 for its ARexx bootstrap, a null-modem link and Linux Node/FUSE components. It reports working on a stock 1 MB Chip RAM A600, and warns that transfers are extremely slow. +kick13 build flags do not establish an end-to-end Workbench 1.3 bootstrap: upstream explicitly says the documented bootstrap needs ARexx and Workbench 2.1. Amiga server lacks a clear license in its own tree; Linux FUSE client says GPLv3, while Node package.json says GPL-2.0. Do not flatten the multi-repository licensing to a single version. Serial defaults are 19200 baud. The HTTP-facing helper and destructive filesystem operations deserve a private/trusted network; no security or reliability audit was performed. The suite can write/delete files and floppy contents; no server was executed and no disk was modified. This original filesystem transfer suite operates on Amiga files and disk images; no historical native binary is reconstructed. Data/filesystem content does not have a single source CPU. The native-server recipe uses vbcc +kick13 and the NDK but no explicit processor-selection argument, native assembly or inspected executable header establishes a target ISA independently in this bounded review. No Linux/Node host ISA is inferred. target_cpu stays empty pending stronger primary evidence. Makefile compiles the Amiga server with vbcc +kick13 and hardcoded /data paths. Linux FUSE client uses autotools and curl/json-c/crypto/zip/magic; Node serial bridge is separate. The documented ARexx bootstrap requires Workbench 2.1 despite +kick13. No filesystem operations or disk writes were performed. Author reports use on an unexpanded A600 with 1 MB Chip RAM; that successful setup is not converted into an independently verified minimum. Documented serial link uses a null-modem cable at 19200 baud. Workbench 1.3 lacks the required ARexx bootstrap. alsfsAmigaServer, alsfs Linux FUSE client, alsfsNodejsServer and alsfsdocumentation are one counted suite. Amiga server licensing is unclear, Linux client explicitly GPLv3 and Node metadata GPL-2.0. Trusted/private deployment is appropriate given HTTP exposure and destructive file/disk operations; no security assurance is implied. License/asset review: Amiga server: no explicit license found. Related Linux client: GPLv3; Node package: GPL-2.0 metadata. Preserve this mixed/unclear component status. This original filesystem transfer suite operates on Amiga files and disk images; no historical native binary is reconstructed. Data/filesystem content does not have a single source CPU. The native-server recipe uses vbcc +kick13 and the NDK but no explicit processor-selection argument, native assembly or inspected executable header establishes a target ISA independently in this bounded review. No Linux/Node host ISA is inferred. target_cpu stays empty pending stronger primary evidence. Makefile compiles the Amiga server with vbcc +kick13 and hardcoded /data paths. Linux FUSE client uses autotools and curl/json-c/crypto/zip/magic; Node serial bridge is separate. The documented ARexx bootstrap requires Workbench 2.1 despite +kick13. No filesystem operations or disk writes were performed. Author reports use on an unexpanded A600 with 1 MB Chip RAM; that successful setup is not converted into an independently verified minimum. Documented serial link uses a null-modem cable at 19200 baud. Workbench 1.3 lacks the required ARexx bootstrap. alsfsAmigaServer, alsfs Linux FUSE client, alsfsNodejsServer and alsfsdocumentation are one counted suite. Amiga server licensing is unclear, Linux client explicitly GPLv3 and Node metadata GPL-2.0. Trusted/private deployment is appropriate given HTTP exposure and destructive file/disk operations; no security assurance is implied. License/asset review: Amiga server: no explicit license found. Related Linux client: GPLv3; Node package: GPL-2.0 metadata. Preserve this mixed/unclear component status. No explicit generative-AI attribution found in the selected README, source, build, license evidence or 22 recent commit messages. This bounded review is not proof of non-use. Generic provider domains and gameplay AI are not tool attribution. events.message:
NDIX built-in boots its served root disc with persistent storage on

The 500 NDIX-C machine names a served image (diskUrl = NDIX.IMG) and no
library uuid. With persistent storage on, ndix-machine.js took "library
on" to mean "library image only" and refused to power on ("no root disc
chosen"), and the Machine Setup dropdown listed library images only, so
the locked built-in showed "(none)".

Now a profile naming a served image boots it in both modes, the way the
ND-100 built-ins fetch SMD0.IMG whether or not the library is on; only a
profile with neither uuid nor url is an error in library mode. The
dropdown lists the served image as "demo: NDIX.IMG" (selected for the
built-in), and Save keeps diskUrl while "demo" stays chosen and clears
it when a library image is picked.

events.title: Βήμα 86: τα airlock είναι οι πόρτες της βάσης
events.message:
Βήμα 86: τα airlock είναι οι πόρτες της βάσης

Τρία είδη κτισμάτων, τρεις κανόνες (link.asm, tools/reach.py):
- θόλος: διάδρομος προς κάθε θόλο ως 12 tiles και προς όποιο airlock δεν
  έχει ακόμη διάδρομο· χωρίς κανέναν, κόκκινος (το μονοπάτι του 85 φεύγει).
- airlock: ΕΝΑΣ διάδρομος, προς τον πιο κοντινό θόλο· μπαίνει μόνο κάθετα.
- δομή: μονοπάτι προς το πιο κοντινό airlock ή δομή, ποτέ προς θόλο.
Το πρώτο κτίσμα κάθε είδους στέκει μόνο του. Νέος λόγος NO CORRIDOR FITS.

Ο δρομολογητής ξέρει το airlock ως άκρο μεγέθους −1: από αυτό δεν ξεκινά
διάδρομος, και δεν παίρνει πόρτα (cr_redraw, ob_conn_scan). Το EC_FREELK
μετρά τα airlock που περιμένουν θόλο, ώστε ο θόλος να μην ψάχνει 740 µs
σε κάθε βήμα. Η αρχική αποικία έχει airlock βόρεια του θόλου οξυγόνου.

Πληρωμένα: το cr_plan πιο γρήγορο από πριν (cr_read με ldi, ο έλεγχος του
airlock 6 T), το ob_conn_scan ξαναγραμμένο με IX και πίνακα bits
(165.502 → 158.843 µs το χειρότερο ευρετήριο). Τράπεζα 0 όσο ήταν (840),
τράπεζα 2 608 → 333, κείμενα γεμάτα.

Ο φορτωτής: δεδομένα + μηχανές + κώδικας της τράπεζας 2 δεν χωρούσαν πια
στην τράπεζα 5 (16.475 bytes). Τα δεδομένα περιμένουν στη βασική τράπεζα 1,
οι μηχανές φορτώνονται κατευθείαν στη θέση τους, και το test_disc πιάνει
το επίμετρο τη στιγμή που πηδά στο #0100 και ελέγχει κάθε byte.

events.title: NetMeter: survive a Workbench screen mode change (screennotify.library) (#195)
events.message:
NetMeter: survive a Workbench screen mode change (screennotify.library) (#195)

Workbench cannot close its screen while a window is on it, and NetMeter
also held the public-screen lock for its whole run.  With
screennotify.library installed, NetMeter registers as a Workbench client
when its window is on Workbench: on 'closing' it closes the window, menus,
pens, DrawInfo and the screen lock before replying; on 'open' it opens
again at the place it had.  Sampling goes on meanwhile, so the rates are
right at once.  The library is optional and not shipped -- its licence
does not allow inclusion -- so only its documented interface is declared
here (AddWorkbenchClient 0x36, RemWorkbenchClient 0x3c, the message and
SCREENNOTIFY_TYPE_WORKBENCH); NDK 3.2 has no native equivalent.
TinyMeter does the same.  Stack frame 676 of 768.

events.title: Machines, not settings: one machine selector, built-in machines, NDIX as a machine, library-driven drives
events.message:
Machines, not settings: one machine selector, built-in machines, NDIX as a machine, library-driven drives

The browser page now boots a MACHINE chosen in the toolbar, and the
machine says everything about itself. Four built-in machines ship,
read-only and clonable: ND-100 (SINTRAN from SMD0.IMG, floppy + SMD only),
ND-5000 (the same with an ND-5000 CPU on the octobus, mms log at warn),
BSD 2.11 (the bsd211_481 port from BSD211-WD0.IMG) and 500 NDIX-C (a
standalone ND-500 booting NDIX from NDIX.IMG). The store upgrade (v4)
replaces the old "Default"/"ND100"/"NDIX C"/duplicate-NDIX leftovers.

Toolbar: a Machine selector before Power; Power builds the machine from
its INI and boots its [boot] device (new BootFrom(type, unit, image) WASM
export, honouring the unit; "device = none" powers on with nothing
loaded, in the C config, the JSON description and the native binary).
The Boot dropdown and button are gone; a BPUN is loaded from
View > Boot BPUN file. The demo boot image is fetched into MEMFS before
Init whenever nothing already holds the boot unit.

Machine Setup: boot drive chosen among enabled controllers only (or no
boot drive); an ND-5000 checkbox writing the mfbus/octobus/nd5000
sections (which the form used to drop on Save); disk slots that pick
library images of the controller's type when persistent storage is on
and are locked to the demo names in demo mode - the machine is the master
of its drives and power-on mounts them (Worker-mode SMD through the HDD
manager's post-Init OPFS sync, whose completion the boot now waits for;
booting earlier read sector 0 through a handle being re-opened); floppy
slots with an Archive picker into the Norsk Data software archive;
per-machine terminal settings (renderer, emulator, keyboard) replacing
the Config window's reload-bound rows - both renderers always load and
the console follows the selector without a reload; the section placed
with the machine's settings, above the buttons.

NDIX as a machine kind (nd500-ndix, js/ndix-machine.js): no ND-100, no
window of its own - tty 0 is terminal 1 as a VT100, further ttys get
terminals as they speak; the root disc is the served demo image (demo
mode, writable, in memory) or a library image tagged nd500. The old
ND-500 Console window and nd500-window.js are removed. Worker mode
reports the ND-500 at module ready, not only after an ND-100 Init.

HDD Disk Manager: opens in every mode (a notice when persistent storage
is off); tabs SMD / SCSI / Winchester / NDIX with image counts; Server
Catalog and Remote Images shared under every tab and filtered to its
type; no Assign and no unit rows - drives are given images in Machine
Setup; the same Rename / Export / NDFS / Del on every tab (no NDFS for
NDIX); Import on every tab preselecting the tab's type; boxed library
rows; unique names; a copy lands on its type's tab. diskType is now
passed on catalog copy, gateway copy and import (every image used to be
stored as smd); disk-types.js is loaded by the page at last (the generic
tabs had no unit counts or labels); the Winchester/floppy buffer mounts

events.title: fix(serial): keep a swapped-out backend alive until its last send returns (#71)
events.message:
fix(serial): keep a swapped-out backend alive until its last send returns (#71)

apply_config() deleted the raw SerialBackend while host_tx() on the Z80
thread could be inside its send(): the IPC `serial config set` path and
the Options dialog replace the backend with no quiesce. The Machine's
host_tx ctx is the SerialInterface, but host_tx() dereferenced the raw
pointer, so the use-after-free window was still open.

The backend is now a shared_ptr behind a mutex held only to copy or swap
it. host_tx(), the bridge's rx pump and every status reader take a
counted reference, so a replaced backend is destroyed (and closed) by
whichever holder drops it last. The staged/applied config is guarded by
the same mutex, since the Z80 thread copies it every frame.

events.title: fix(debug): register edits no longer drop or replay the instruction in flight (#70)
events.message:
fix(debug): register edits no longer drop or replay the instruction in flight (#70)

subcycle_bridge_regs_to_machine() pushed every register through z80_poke(),
which also restarts the CPU at a fresh instruction boundary. A pause or a
breakpoint parks the board mid-instruction, so any explicit edit (DevTools
field or flag, "Set PC here", IPC `reg set`) dropped the rest of the
instruction in flight, e.g. half a PUSH.

The edit now writes only the fields that differ from what the view was last
given, through a new register-file-only poke that leaves the sequencer alone.
Away from a breakpoint the in-flight instruction first runs to its end, so
edits land between instructions. At a breakpoint stop (parked after the
opcode fetch) the shown instruction has not run: edits apply in place, and a
PC edit drops it. The DevTools edit paths and IPC `reg set` now hold a pause
lease, so the Z80 thread is idle when the edit lands.

events.title: console: share the clipboard with the browser (#192)
events.message:
console: share the clipboard with the browser (#192)

* console: share the clipboard with the browser

A paste in the browser while the screen has focus arrives as `cp TEXT`: the
text, UTF-8 to ISO-8859-1 with CRLF made LF, goes onto clipboard unit 0 as a
FORM FTXT and Right-Amiga V is pressed, so it lands where a paste on the
Amiga would.  Ctrl/Cmd-V is now left to the browser (BROWSER_KEEPS) so that
its paste event carries the text.  A `cp` is read into its own 32 KB buffer
once its three bytes say what it is; every other word keeps the 48-byte one.

A change to the clipboard made on the Amiga is sent as `cb TEXT`.
CBD_CHANGEHOOK says when: the hook runs on the task that did the update,
notes the clip ID and signals httpd, whose WaitSelect() now has that bit
(http_fb_sigmask()).  This end's own pastes are known by their clip ID and
not sent back.  The page offers the text in its top bar with a Copy button:
a plain http:// page may only copy inside a click; a secure one copies at
once.

clipftxt.c holds the conversion and the FTXT build and parse, host-tested
(console_clipboard_text, 18 checks; HOST_TESTS_EXPECTED 557).  Checked on
the A3000 with two httpd instances beside the live one: a paste of "Grüße
from the console" left exactly FORM/FTXT/CHRS with FC DF on the clipboard
and was not echoed; a paste through the second instance reached the first
as `cb line one\nlínea dos ?`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* console: the side of Shift, Alt and Amiga holds for every key

qualifiers() took the side from the event's own code, which names a
modifier only on the keypress of the modifier itself: on the C of a
Right-Amiga C the code is KeyC and metaKey one bit, so it went out as
Left-Amiga C and copy could not be typed from the console.  input.ts now
keeps which sided modifiers are down, from their own key events whatever
has the focus and cleared on blur, and qualifiers() sets the bit for the
side held, both when both are, left when nothing is known.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* console: Cmd-V pastes whichever clipboard was copied to last

A copy on the Amiga followed by Cmd-V sent the browser's clipboard, which
overwrote the Amiga's copy and pasted the wrong text.  The page sees the
browser's clipboard only in a paste, so it pastes the Amiga's own (Right-
Amiga V alone, no cp) when the Amiga has copied since the last cp and the
browser still holds what that cp sent, or the Amiga's text itself (its Copy
button).  New text on the browser's side still goes as cp.

events.title: ndskit: an ARM interpreter, the recompiler, its self-test, the runtime's first lines
events.message:
ndskit: an ARM interpreter, the recompiler, its self-test, the runtime's first lines

armemu runs ARM and Thumb code as the ARM9 (ARMv5TE) and the ARM7
(ARMv4T) do: conditions, the shifter's carry, every addressing mode, the
multiplies and the DSP group, interworking, the processor modes with
their banked registers and SPSRs, exception returns, and unaligned
accesses rotated or aligned as each CPU does them. Against Unicorn's
ARM946 on 25 483 random instructions and 1 960 transfers it differs only
where QEMU reads unaligned memory as an ARMv6 would, or where the
architecture leaves the result open.

The recompiler (recomp.emit, python -m ndskit.recomp) writes one C++
function per entry and one module per program: each instruction under
its condition, the flags stored only where some path reads them, the PC
as a constant, literal pools folded, calls checked on return, calls
through registers dispatched by address with the mode in bit 0,
switches as C++ switches, exception returns, CP15 and SWI as runtime
calls, safe points for the runtime to come. Discovery now records what
each write to pc is, and learned the forms the first port needed:
constants built in two steps, tables of offsets followed through
registers, switch bounds further back, jumps into unrolled code, Thumb's
bx pc, local subroutines through lr, empty callbacks. No function opens
with a condition, which removes data read as code, and the rule of
opposite conditions is redone where it crossed a join.

recomp.selftest records vectors with the interpreter: an instruction
test of each CPU and the game's functions that run alone. runtime/
holds the context, the memories the CPUs reach directly, the modes, the
dispatch and the replaying harness. On the first port: 81 555 vectors,
no difference.

events.title: IDE: order the ide thread's interrupt handoff
events.message:
IDE: order the ide thread's interrupt handoff

Read/write and ATAPI commands complete on the ide thread, which fills secbuf, the registers and intdrq and then arms irq_delay with plain stores. The CPU thread polls irq_delay in ide_interrupt_hsync() and then builds the status from intdrq. On weakly ordered hosts (ARM64) it can see the armed delay but a stale intdrq, raise the interrupt without DRQ, and KS 3.2 scsi.device then polls for DRQ forever at priority 11. Add a release fence before arming irq_delay and an acquire fence after reading it.

events.message:
fix(ide): order the IDE thread's interrupt handoff with release/acquire (#2386)

Read and ATAPI commands complete on the ide thread, which fills the sector buffer, registers and intdrq and then arms irq_delay with plain stores. The CPU thread polls irq_delay each scanline and then builds the status from intdrq. On weakly ordered hosts (ARM64) it could see the armed delay but a stale intdrq, raise the interrupt without DRQ and leave KS scsi.device polling for DRQ forever at priority 11, freezing DOS. Arm irq_delay with a release store and poll it with an acquire load.
events.author: midwan

events.title: hardware: Require a nonzero INTENAR mirror to detect A1000 Gary
events.message:
hardware: Require a nonzero INTENAR mirror to detect A1000 Gary

The A1000 test compared JOY0DAT/JOY1DAT with their mirrors at
$DAF00A/$DAF00C. With idle ports both registers read $0000, which
is also what unmapped space returns, such as WinUAE's A1200 Gayle
window. A freshly booted emulated A1200 was therefore reported as
an A1000 and the Gayle ID was never read.

Also compare INTENAR with its mirror at $DAF01C. INTENAR is nonzero
while the OS runs, so empty address space can no longer pass as a
custom chip mirror.

events.title: NetMeter: interfaces, addresses and live rates in a Workbench window (#190)
events.message:
NetMeter: interfaces, addresses and live rates in a Workbench window (#190)

* NetMeter: interfaces, addresses and live rates in a Workbench window

The stack counts the IP bytes each interface receives and sends, 64 bits in
two ULONG halves of AmiSana2Stats, where it already counts the packets
(sana2_rx.c, sana2_tx.c).  A new selector, NETSTATUS_IFBYTES (24), answers
one NetStatusIfBytes per interface slot; NetStatusInterface and the netstatus
version are unchanged, and a library without the selector answers EINVAL.
tool_snapshot() joins the counts into ToolIfInfo (have_bytes).

NetMeter is a small, resizable Intuition window: per interface a link dot,
the name, the IPv4 address and one IPv6 address (the global one first), and
a receive and a send bar with the rate, scaled to a decaying peak.  Hovering
-- polled from the screen's pointer, so it works over an inactive window --
shows the definition file, device and link speed for a name, and the totals
for the bars.  A click on an address writes it to clipboard.device unit 0 as
a FORM FTXT, which a Shell or string gadget pastes.  The window grows to fit
a new interface or a longer address and never shrinks a size the user set.

Tests: netstatus_ifdevices covers IFBYTES (29 checks); netmeter_arithmetic
covers the rate and total text, the delta across the carry and a reset, the
scale and the bar (HOST_TESTS_EXPECTED 556).  Stack-frame budget 768 (692).
Packaged with its own icon (makeicon.py), installed into SYS:Utilities by a
system installation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* NetMeter: draw in the screen's font, proportional or not

The window, its tooltips and the layout measurement use the screen's font
(DrawInfo dri_Font, Font prefs' Screen text) instead of the RastPort default.
The rate column is as wide as the widest of the rates a proportional font can
print.

events.message:
Βήμα 85: κάθε κτίσμα θέλει γείτονα ως 12 tiles, και οι διάδρομοι μπαίνουν μόνοι τους

src/link.asm (τράπεζα 2), ο κανόνας που ζήτησε ο παίκτης, και tools/reach.py,
ο ίδιος σε Python. Εκτός από το πρώτο κτίσμα του κόσμου, κάθε κτίσμα θέλει
άλλο ως 12 tiles μακριά:

- Ένας θόλος παίρνει σκεπαστό διάδρομο προς ΚΑΘΕ θόλο που φτάνει με το πολύ
  12 πλακίδια, ως τέσσερις, χωρίς δύο διαδρόμους στα ίδια tiles.
- Μια δομή — ή ένας θόλος χωρίς διάδρομο — παίρνει μονοπάτι στο έδαφος,
  χωρίς σκεπή: ένα Γ κέντρο-κέντρο προς το κοντινότερο κτίσμα, ως 12 tiles,
  θεμέλιο με κατοχή 2 (PATH στο I), ακμή εξωτερικού χώρου.
- Αλλιώς το φάντασμα κόκκινο και ο πίνακας λέει TOO FAR ή PATH BLOCKED. Το
  φάντασμα δείχνει πράσινους τους διαδρόμους ή το μονοπάτι, και ο πίνακας το
  σύνολο του κόστους (6 μέταλλο και 3 βιοπλαστικό το πλακίδιο).
- Το bd_link δεν δένει πια τίποτα: ως τώρα κάθε κτίσμα έπαιρνε αόρατη ακμή
  προς τον κοντινότερο θόλο, όσο μακριά κι αν ήταν.

Στο FIRE το εργοτάξιο μπαίνει στη λίστα αλλαγών ΠΡΙΝ από τους διαδρόμους: οι
σειρές του έσβηναν τη γωνία όπου ξεκινά η διαγώνιος (το βρήκε το test_fit). Το
μονοπάτι ξαναζωγραφίζει μόνο τα δικά του tiles: ηλιακός 171 -> 127 ms.

ανά βήμα χωρίς σκρολάρισμα. Ο χειρότερος γύρος ενός FIRE 100-127 ms.

events.title: Thread safety fixes before the Fast start work
events.message:
Thread safety fixes before the Fast start work

Run-control and cross-thread flags are now std::atomic: the TEmulator
run-control flags, TARMProcessor::mPendingInterrupts (the timer thread could
lose an interrupt with a plain |= and &=), TMonitor::mHalted and mCommand,
and TPlatformManager::mPowerOn.

Saving and loading the emulator state:
- Run-control flags are no longer saved; the state file version is now 2.
- Serial drivers can be suspended while the state is saved or loaded
  (TSerialPortDriver::Suspend/Resume, implemented by the TCP client).
- TInterruptManager::TransferState holds its mutex.

FLTK and Monitor fixes found with ThreadSanitizer:
- TFLMonitor::DrawScreen and TFLScreenManager::PowerOn/OffScreen take the
  FLTK lock when called from the emulator thread.
- The Monitor's UI callbacks only draw the halted view while the monitor
  thread is idle (TFLMonitor::DrawScreenFromUI).
- The TCP client destructor no longer disconnects while its worker thread
  may use the socket.
- TMutex::TryLock() returns true when it got the lock, as documented.

events.title: refactor(kernel): scenario and situation tables become fixed maxima
events.message:
refactor(kernel): scenario and situation tables become fixed maxima

The scenario tables were sized to the data (NSN=2, NLEG=47, ... NSIT=9),
so a run deck read at run time could not fit a larger mission. They are
now fixed maxima with headroom (ours: MXSN 8, MXLEG 200, MXEVT 100,
MXSTRT 8, MXBURN 50, MXREF 80, MXTL 1500, MXCUE 64, MXSIT 40), and NSN,
NLEG, NEVT, NTL and NSIT become the used counts in COMMON, set by the
BLOCK DATA beside NSTART, NRF, NBN and NBR. The kernel's loops already
named those, so they now run over used rows without a text change.
gen_data refuses data that overflows a maximum, and empty tables no
longer get a zero dummy row.

Slice 3 of #26. Golden: the 129 renders, tables.txt, names.js and
scenes.json are byte-identical; the generated sources differ only in
declarations, the count DATA lines and their comments.

events.title: ncr5380: the TT's SCSI interrupt line drops when the interrupt is reset
events.message:
ncr5380: the TT's SCSI interrupt line drops when the interrupt is reset

Reading register 7 cleared scsi->irq but left the TT-MFP GPIP7 line
high (the Falcon path already clears its FDC IRQ source), so after the
first interrupt every later one made no edge on the MFP. Atari System V
waits for these interrupts and loops on "SCSI bus timedout, resetting".

events.message:
ncr5380: MODE SELECT takes its parameter list length from the CDB

scsi_emulate_analyze() starts from the previous command's
ScsiBus.data_len, and MODE SELECT had no case of its own, so a MODE
SELECT (6) or (10) with an empty parameter list asked for a DATA OUT
phase of that stale length (18 bytes after a REQUEST SENSE). The bus
then stayed in DATA OUT and the following commands never reached the
target. WinUAE's scsi.cpp has the same two cases.

events.title: fix(qd3d): sample textures with v = 0 at the bottom row (#4192)
events.message:
fix(qd3d): sample textures with v = 0 at the bottom row (#4192)

The software renderer mapped v to rows from the top of the texture
pixmap, so every texture was sampled upside down. "3D Graphics
Programming with QuickDraw 3D" (Geometric Objects, Figure 8, the
standard uv parameterization for a pixmap) puts the pixmap's integer
origin at its upper-left pixel and uv (0, 0) at its lower-left corner,
with (0, 1) at the upper left.

Character skins packed into a texture atlas showed the effect most:
regions of a model sampled the black padding of the atlas instead of
their own artwork, so half of an animated character rendered black.

events.title: fix(qd3d): cull the faces that turn away from the camera (#4191)
events.message:
fix(qd3d): cull the faces that turn away from the camera (#4191)

With kQ3BackfacingStyleRemove the software renderer removed the faces
that point toward the camera and kept the ones that point away. The
screen-space edge value is the negated cross product, and with screen y
pointing down a positive value is a counterclockwise winding as seen by
the camera, which is the front face under the default
kQ3OrientationStyleCounterClockwise. The test used the opposite sign.

"3D Graphics Programming with QuickDraw 3D" defines the front face as
the one whose vertices run counterclockwise, with the cross product of
the first two edges pointing out of the page (Orientation Styles), and
kQ3BackfacingStyleRemove as removing the shapes that face away from the
camera (Backfacing Styles).

Visible effects: closed models were drawn inside out (the far side of
the mesh, shaded as if facing away from the light), and open surfaces
seen from the front, such as a backdrop panel, vanished entirely. A
title scene that frames an animated character against a textured
backdrop showed the character inside out over a blank clear color.

The flip-style test now uses a clockwise (back-facing) triangle so it
still checks that back faces get their normals inverted, the remove
test expects the counterclockwise triangle to survive, and a new test
renders the same pair through a perspective camera from both sides.

events.title: docs: ledger the rpath purge and the absent crash report
events.message:
docs: ledger the rpath purge and the absent crash report

No hatari-*.ips on the reporting machine rules out the crashing signals
macOS writes reports for; the surviving explanations are an ordinary exit
whose stderr the old transport lost, or a SIGKILL. Both are now covered:
the transport reports the death cause, the build host's rpaths are purged,
and the seal step boots the sealed artifact.
events.author: idontwantyourspamthanks

events.title: release: purge the build host's rpaths from the bundled emulator
events.message:
release: purge the build host's rpaths from the bundled emulator

The bundled hatari and its dylibs kept every rpath they were built with:
build-tree directories and /opt/homebrew/lib, all ahead of the
@executable_path one the bundling step adds. dyld searches rpaths in order,
so on any Mac with Homebrew the bundled SDL2, libpng and the X11 chain were
never the libraries actually loaded — Homebrew's were. The runner has
Homebrew too, which is exactly why the banner check passed while a user
machine with different brew versions crashed with nothing on stderr. Every
inherited rpath is now deleted and exactly two are added: @loader_path/. for
the dylibs, @executable_path/../Frameworks for the executable. The
host-prefix assertion now scans otool -l for rpaths as well, so an inherited
one fails the release instead of shadowing the bundle.
events.author: idontwantyourspamthanks

events.title: release: arm the entry breakpoint in the sealed-emulator smoke
events.message:
release: arm the entry breakpoint in the sealed-emulator smoke

The smoke as committed could never see a stop: it armed no breakpoint, so
nothing ever entered the debugger, and it passed --control-socket with no
listener, which hatari treats as fatal at option parse. The run now writes
the bootstrap-style parse file the IDE itself writes (b pc = TEXT :once),
drops the socket option, and uses the monitor type the field report ran
(vga). Proven against a local fork build: the banner arrives, the
screenshot-able stop exists, and the wait loop's grep matches.

events.title: benchmark: Handle high-rate and coarse JIT clocks in Dhrystone
events.message:
benchmark: Handle high-rate and coarse JIT clocks in Dhrystone

A fixed 16-bit tick ceiling turns a 100 MHz E-clock into a 653 us
chunk limit. JIT clocks can also remain unchanged during short runs,
causing calibration or otherwise valid chunks to return zero MIPS.

Scale the existing 75/90 ms budgets by the reported frequency. Grow
zero-tick calibration runs within bounded limits and include sub-tick
work in accumulated measurements. Restart an overlong attempt up to
twice with shorter chunks, discarding its previous totals.

Keep rejecting invalid or changing clocks, persistent overruns and
measurements without elapsed time.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: rtg: Add P96 memory-window overlays on Unix
events.message:
rtg: Add P96 memory-window overlays on Unix

Implement feature creation, attribute access and deletion through P96
bitmap callbacks. Bound guest tag traversal and release failed bitmap
allocations before returning to the guest.

Compose scaled RGB, CLUT and YUV windows with guest-order color keys
before drawing the cursor. Match Windows YUV word order and ACCUPAK
component packing, and clip rendering to the display and VRAM bounds.

Use pixel-sized operations with format masks for logical blits. Reverse
traversal for overlapping buffers and snapshot differently pitched aliases
before writing their destination. Add full-pixel swaps and register the
transparent-copy callback, comparing source pixels against the colour key.

Exercise the minterms at every pixel size, overlap directions, partial
masks, different pitches, transparent pixels and swaps.

Workbench can supply no output handle. Writing diagnostics through

events.title: iCloud: request downloads for real-named cloud files (#3)
events.message:
iCloud: request downloads for real-named cloud files (#3)

The second device never pulled anything. Undownloaded files were only
recognised by the legacy ".name.icloud" placeholder; current iOS keeps
the real name and reports a non-current downloading status, so no
download was ever requested and every remote file was skipped as not
downloaded — the pass reported "Up to date".

Request a download for every remote entry that is not current
(including a stale local version), show "N downloading" in the panel,
and run up to four follow-up passes 20 s apart so the files are copied
once they land instead of at the next foreground.

Compile-checked only; not yet verified across two devices.

The texture-index pass walked the ten indices with the same pointer it

triangle on (an earlier fix, c11fb4d, had been lost). Like the original, a
row pointer advances by 0x13 dwords and a copy walks the ten indices.
Loop counters are unsigned, as the original's jb/jbe compares show.
