events.title: Publish GitHub Pages sections only when inputs change (#366)
events.message:
Publish GitHub Pages sections only when inputs change (#366)

Publish only the changed sections of the GitHub Pages site. Manual runs
automatically compare app and documentation inputs with the commits
recorded in the last successfully deployed artifact. Docs-only runs keep
app files and versions; apps-only runs keep docs; unchanged runs skip
deployment.

Reuse the repository's Git diff and path-filter approach. App checks
cover src, dependency/build configuration, and the production version;
docs checks cover docs, includes, MkDocs configuration, and
dependencies. Store separate docs, production, and optional test source
commits in the site artifact, updating only the sections actually
rebuilt. Preserve unselected test paths and clear rebuilt directories to
remove stale assets. Successful runs whose deployment step was skipped
cannot become the published baseline.

Replace the manual Publish apps checkbox with one **Force publish**
checkbox, disabled by default. It rebuilds apps and docs for the
selected target without consulting previous artifacts or comparisons,
providing recovery from expired artifacts or broken detection. First
deployments and artifacts without source metadata rebuild both sections.
Release tags always rebuild production apps with the release version.

Retain the archive validation, read-only artifact/deployment
permissions, serialized deployment queue, 90-day retention, and full SHA
action pins. Document automatic publishing and recovery.

Validation:
- 34 tests passed, including real temporary Git repositories for
app/docs/config changes, separate published baselines, preservation,
no-op and rerun deployment selection, version changes, initial
publishing, and force recovery; helper coverage exceeds 99% locally.
- All 14 workflow-condition scenarios passed.
- Actionlint passed for the modified workflows and docs built in strict
mode.
- Restored the actual deployed Pages artifact, verified all 950 non-doc
files match byte-for-byte, and confirmed the published docs are
retained. No live publishing was triggered.

All PR checks passed, including build/test, CodeQL, SonarCloud,
dependency review, NuGet audit, and documentation.

events.message:
Group the native sources by what they do, and list data as .byte

native/src is now app, ui, display, sound, controls, drives, slots, states,
debugger, applesoft and develop, moved with their history, and every
include names its folder. The folders avoid the core's own names (debug,
input, audio, basic, machine), so an include like debug/machine_debug.hpp
can only mean the core's. docs/NATIVE.md has the map.

The CPU debugger lists a program's data as .byte lines, text in quotes and
other bytes in hex, so a message reads as one rather than as the
instructions its bytes decode to. Where the data is comes from a ca65 .dbg:
the spans ca65 gives a type to are what .byte and its kind emitted. The
host cuts each region into lines from its start, so the listing's
alignment search walks through data as it does through code. This replaces
the text column, which only split a message across instruction-sized
pieces. A breakpoint on a program's first instruction is pinned by a test.

events.title: runtime: VDP2's special priority and special colour calculation
events.message:
runtime: VDP2's special priority and special colour calculation

SFPRMD and SFCCMD, two bits a layer (NBG0-NBG3, RBG0): the priority's
LSB from the pattern name's (or the bitmap's) special priority bit, per
character, or per dot where the dot's colour code is one of the special
function codes (SFSEL, SFCODE); colour calculation alike, or by the
colour's MSB. The runtime used to note them and use the screen's own.

A 1997 SHC game's towns set NBG0 and NBG1 to priority 2 with SFPRMD
per character: the tiles that carry the bit (table tops, tree crowns)
rise to 3, above the characters, who walked over them before.

Virtual Hydlide, a two-disc SGL game and a 1995 FMV game: byte-identical
pictures and sound.

events.title: Build and run ca65 projects in the native app
events.message:
Build and run ca65 projects in the native app

A project is a small JSON file ending .applem beside the user's Makefile,
naming the build, what it makes, its .dbg and the machine. The Develop menu
builds it in the user's login shell, lists cc65's errors (both its
file(line) and file:line forms) so a click opens the file, and starts what
was built; Watch for Changes runs any build written by anything else.

A raw binary starts from memory: MachineHost::startProgram puts it in main
RAM and enters it through a trampoline (JSR, then Applesoft's cold start),
reached through the soft entry vector and a reset on the 8-bit machines and
directly on a IIgs, whose firmware rescans on a reset during its startup.
cl65's AppleSingle output, a ProDOS program, starts from a ProDOS volume
made for it each run: PRODOS, then the program if it is a SYSTEM file, or
BASIC.SYSTEM with the program in its startup buffer. The .dbg's symbols go
to the debugger each run.

Also: the build date and time in the About panel, written into a source
file on every build; the BASIC editor refuses a line number past 63999 as
it is typed, marks one that arrives otherwise and will not write it; and
the BASIC window's status line no longer runs off the window's bottom.

events.title: tools/dataflow ranges: a run cut off by its step budget is not converged (fixes #2)
events.message:
tools/dataflow ranges: a run cut off by its step budget is not converged (fixes #2)

Ranges.run stops at self.budget steps with work still on the worklist,
but analyse() only asked whether the record invariant and the written
sets were stable - so a cut-off run could end "converged": its
invariant cached in ranges_I.json as a sound start for later runs, and
annotate.py's NOT-sound banner left off every file.

Now run() records it (self.exhausted), run_phased carries it out of
its rounds, and analyse() marks the result unconverged, with a WARNING
note, when the final game run or the loader's was cut off. The banner
and the skipped cache write then follow from the code already there.
RANGES_BUDGET sets the budget, beside RANGES_DEBUG and RANGES_CHECK
(default unchanged: 3,000,000); the README says so.

Seen on a 9,380-instruction game (puzzle-beeble): every round hit the
budget at 8,295 instructions reached, ended "record invariant stable",
and annotated without a warning. Tested here on a 557-instruction
program: RANGES_BUDGET=20000 now gives the banner on every file, the
WARNING in summary.md and no ranges_I.json; the default budget
converges as before (557 of 557 reached), no banner, the cache written.

events.title: build: refuse an assembler or linker override that is not the tool
events.message:
build: refuse an assembler or linker override that is not the tool

A real session arrived with vasmm68k_mot configured to point at hatari: an
explicit override wins outright in locate() and resolveOverridePath accepts
any executable file, so the build invoked the emulator with vasm's argument
shape, produced no object, and the run then autostarted a stale program into
a baffling half-booted screen — with nothing anywhere naming the cause. The
Browse filter is "All files", which is exactly how a mis-click lands there.

Hatari already gets an identity check (emu/HatariProbe) for the same reason:
a name is not evidence. The assembler and linker now get the cheap form of
one — an override must carry its tool's banner string ("vasm", "vlink") in
its first bytes or it resolves as not found, with a reason saying why.
Discovery of bundled and PATH tools is untouched: those are named by the
release process and by the platform, not typed by a user.

pist --diagnose prints the reason beside NOT FOUND, so a mis-filed override
is one command to identify; tst_toolfetch pins both directions (a fixture
carrying the banner resolves, one carrying another tool's does not) and
tst_settings' override fixture now carries the banner its role claims.

events.message:
tools: beebgame's dataflow analyses on a beebasm build, for Paradroid and Edge

The two shipped ports are beebasm, which baron_dbg.py cannot read: a
beebasm -v listing prints resolved operands, not source text.
py/beeb_port_kit/beebasm_dataflow.py writes the ld65 debug file from the
listing instead - code and data from it, sections from its "Saving file"
lines and address jumps, an INCBIN cut to three bytes and "..." run to
the next address, address-taken labels from a scan of the sources - and
runs the kit's vendored analyses on it. One file, forked into a
project's tools/ beside a dataflow_config.py naming LISTING, SOURCES and
ISR_ROOTS; findings point at the nearest label, not a file:line.

Measured 2026-10-06: Paradroid 22,556 instructions, 371 findings, 274
bytes; Edge Grinder 4,051 instructions, 83 findings, 106 bytes, and its
range analysis converged in 56 s - the first full game it has. Each
project carries a fork and a docs/dataflow-report.md.

The tests (both listing shapes, the SAVE split, the address-taken scan,
and the vendored model reading both ports' real listings) found two bugs
in the first version, fixed here: a label sharing a line with a
statement hid that statement's references (under-counting "taken", the
unsafe way), and a bare address line attached its label to the next
code address. py tests: 93 run, 2 skip (Paradroid's old tool paths).

fix(ppc): route InterfaceLib StdBits through CopyBits (#4145)

StdBits(srcBits, srcRect, dstRect, mode, maskRgn) is the CopyBits
bottleneck with the current port's bits as destination. The PowerPC
import table had no entry for it, so a native application that calls it
directly hit an unsupported import and halted. Shift its arguments into
CopyBits' register layout with the current port's portBits as dstBits,
run the existing CopyBits path, and restore the caller's argument
registers.

events.message:
perf(ppc): skip re-installing an unchanged screen color table (#4156)

Every PowerPC host-state sync re-installs the indexed screen PixMap's
pmTable from the host CLUT: one long and 1,026 word stores, each routed
through the attached guest address space and its sparse-overlap scan,
even when the table in RAM is already exactly that. Build the table
image once and skip the stores when RAM already holds it and every
store would have taken the unobserved fast path; the new bus helper
learns the same store-filter pages that path would have learned. Any
diagnostic, write probe, watchpoint, presentation observer, protection
or non-flat routing keeps the per-word stores.

events.title: Make the native app solid for its first release
events.message:
Make the native app solid for its first release

The fixes from a full end to end test of every native window, menu and
machine, each one pinned by a test where the code allows and the blockers
checked again in the running app.

Disks write back to the file they came from, in its own format: once the
drive is idle, on eject, before another disk replaces one, on a machine
change and on quit, exported and marked saved under one hold of the
machine. A drive remembers its disk by path and reopens it; Recent keeps
paths, not copies. A disk with no file to go back to asks to be saved, and
quitting asks only when something would be lost. Each floppy has a Lock.

Watchpoints fire on every machine: the debug state tells the MMU when it
has any, however they were added. The breakpoint list applies only what
changed, so an edit no longer makes Continue stop in place; stops are
judged by a resume count, IIgs stops are reported and counted, and the
console's s, break, G, numbering, radix and conditions behave. Step over
and out know long calls and banks.

Keys reach the machine in the order pressed, one a frame, so fast typing
keeps every key; letters and punctuation follow the keyboard layout.
Paste works on a IIgs. Dialogs and tool windows are windows of their own,
so a dialog is never drawn under another window. The BASIC window can be
opened, a long line number no longer quits the app, Write respects HIMEM,
and control characters, quoted colons in DATA and duplicate lines survive.

A IIgs memory change asks first and keeps the disks; Expansion Slots
follows a machine switch; a slot given to Your Card is remembered; a
DOS-order 2MG reads through the interleave; a WOZ's bit count is bounded.
Printer and serial cards are hidden until there is a printer.

Also: opening disks and states from the Finder, Save Screenshot, a volume
slider, the last session's autosave kept, autosave written off the UI
thread, and a run of smaller fixes the test found.

events.title: Revert three condition rewrites that changed behaviour; make the idioms safe
events.message:
Revert three condition rewrites that changed behaviour; make the idioms safe

The condition idiom accepted an operand inside grouping parentheses without
checking what the group was an operand of, and rewrote:
- (t) >= 0xb40000 in StageTiming's WRAP macro as (t != 0) >= 0xb40000
  (caught by differential_ai_telemetry),
- ((force) < 0 ? ...) in Car_UpdateCornerFriction,
- (odd != 0) + 10 in FrontendMenu_DrawProfileBestStageTimes.
All three are restored. The idiom now only rewrites an operand that is the
whole condition or an operand of &&, || or ! after stripping redundant
parentheses, never inside preprocessor directives; FixMul operand swaps skip
arguments with calls (evaluation order), and the all-occurrences variant
skips nested spots.

differential_stage_sound_reset maps each of the split 0x537568 tables at its
original arena offset, with the records' one-past-the-end address kept on
the records. 77/77 harnesses pass; 2817/3363 byte-exact.

events.title: 実装: 型宣言文 DEFINT・DEFSNG・DEFDBL・DEFSTR（l4-program 4.21、l4-s9m）
events.message:
実装: 型宣言文 DEFINT・DEFSNG・DEFDBL・DEFSTR（l4-program 4.21、l4-s9m）

根拠は仕様 4.21 節（841620c）だけ。測定コミットは c030b8f（公式111腕×2走、期待値 expected_l4_deftype.tsv）。
- 型表: 英字26文字の型（0=単精度、'%'・'$'・'#'）を memmap.py の RUN 域 50〜75（MM_DEFTYPE_TAB）に置く。0が既定なのでゼロ初期化でも単精度。接尾辞つきかの印は 76（MM_IDENT_SFX）。
- 引くのは LEX_IDENT_PEEK の1か所だけ。接尾辞（% $ # !）が付いていれば常にそれ、無ければ名前の1文字目で表を引き、IDENT_BUF[7] と IDENT_KIND を接尾辞つきと同じ形にそろえる。代入・参照・配列・FOR・NEXT・READ・INPUT・SWAP・ERASE・DEF FN（仮引数・関数名とも）は全てこの語彙経路を通る。型ごとに別の変数・配列になる。
- 数値の関数名（ABS・INT・LEN 等）は接尾辞が無いときだけ、型にかかわらず先に照合する（defint i のとき int( が配列 INT% にならない）。
- 初期化: RUN_CLEAR_STATE に1か所足した（RUN・CLEAR・NEW・行の挿入/削除/置換が共通に通る。代入・LIST・存在しない行番号・CONT は通らないので戻らない）。
- 文: 本体はバンク0（deftype.asm、tabspc.asm の後ろへ連結。固定入口 0x77C0〜0x7810）。範囲ごとに「検査→書き込み」し、失敗した範囲より前は残す。余りの文字は main の文末検査が ERR 2 にする。
- 代入の型変換をバンク0の1か所へ（単精度へは倍精度から丸め、整数は CINT の丸めで範囲外 ERR 6・変数不変、倍精度は広げる）。スカラ代入・配列要素代入・READ・FOR の初期値/上限/刻み・NEXT の加算結果（整数の制御変数が32767を越えると ERR 6）がここを通る。
- READ: 数字でない DATA を数値変数へ読むと ERR 2、倍精度の読み先へは '#' を補って倍精度の精度で読む。
- 文字列変数へ数値で始まる式を代入すると ERR 13（以前は ERR 2）。IF の左辺が DEFSTR した名前でも文字列比較になる（strfunc.asm S9E_CMP）。
- プログラム中の RUN [行番号] を実装（以前は ERR 2。4.21.6 の prog-run-line が要る）。直接モードと同じ初期化のあと GOTO と同じ移り方で入る。
- main の空き確保（測定ROM用に末尾116B以上が要る）: VAL_INTDIV・VAL_MODOP の本体をバンク0へ移し（処理は同じ）、埋め草 AEL_ROM_LAYOUT_PAD を FN 中継の後ろへ移した（0x79D7は埋め草のまま。LOGIC_OR_EXPR の JR を保つため LOGIC_OR_EXPR の後ろ）。
- RAM配置: RUN 域の使われていなかった 50〜80 に2項目を足しただけ。ROM は意図して変わるので、段Aの「10構成70 ROM のバイト一致」は今回の対象外（機能追加）。memmap_selftest は rc=0。

自作ROMで l4-s9m の111腕×2走が関門通過、deftype の check --predicted-only は照合一致（予測あり107腕が全て一致）。予測なし4腕（for-int-limit・for-int-step・for-int-edge・read-dbl）も unpredicted の観測と一致。
退行: 自己検査39本が全て rc=0（ext_bank・memmap・l4_memdyn・vsync_regcheck・atnexplog・deffn・onwhile・pusing・wrap・rnd・strfunc・editinv・peekpoke・memlimit・hexconst・s5j・tabspc ほか、m6ib/ic/ie/ig/ih のROM関門、files/load/save/killname、check_cleanroom を含む。memdyn は高負荷でタイムアウトしたため単独で再実行して rc=0）。自作照合は tabspc（--predicted-only）・deffn・wrap・strfunc・strcmp・peekpoke・s5j が一致、onwhile は期待値の全84腕×2走が一致。onwhile・memlimit・pusing・editinv・hexconst・rnd は HEAD でも照合が不一致で、HEAD と今回で全腕の観測が完全に同じ（差0）。
残り容量 main 末尾158B＋埋め草22B（測定ROM用に末尾116B以上を維持）・bank0 1511B・bank1 1995B・bank2 3400B・bank3 27B。
自作判断（未測定）: 型の大文字小文字は区別しない、ERR/ERL は DEFSTR 等の影響を受ける（予約語扱いしない）、DEFSTR した文字で始まる数値関数名（len( 等）は文字列の名前として扱われうる、プログラム中の RUN で行が無ければ初期化のあと ERR 8、READ の数字でない項目は全ての数値変数で ERR 2、FOR で単精度の制御変数は従来どおり（型変換しない）。

events.message:
chore(release): bump version to 0.11 (release date 06.10.2026)

0.11 headlines (since v0.10): Clamacs rewritten in Common Lisp — the
editor is a clamiga instance of its own now (clamacs/lisp/), shipped as a
clamacs.img heap image beside every binary plus lib/clamacs/ FASLs, with
the MUI frontend on the Amiga and a native host frontend (webview +
CodeMirror, Clamacs.app on macOS, Linux) over the new TCP development
port; the EXT.DEV layer grew DEFINE-RAW-COMMAND, COMPLETE's contains
fallback, an ASDF load/test of a system by its .asd, MP:*THREAD-DEATH-HOOKS*
and a REPL that is respawned after a heap-exhaustion death; standalone
executables — (ext:save-image f :executable t :toplevel ... :quit t)
writes one file that is the program, command line and Workbench start
included, and a SAVE-IMAGE refusal names the worker threads in the way;
the JIT — an AArch64 backend for arm64 hosts (phases 0-4, direct
native-to-native calls, &optional/&rest prologues), and on m68k direct
native-to-native calls through call-site cells with one call generation
word, &key/&optional/&rest prologues, positional arity up to 255, tail
calls into other functions, native frames with line numbers, lazy
compilation when a function turns hot (FASL v39), GC/interrupt polls in
native loops; heap images — Amiga library bases reopened after a restore
(define-library-variable, *SYSTEM-RESTORE-HOOKS*), source-file names
stored once (image v5), failed starts hand their memory back; GC —
compaction forwards through a live-granule bitmap instead of a heap-sized
table (the low-end 68020 stall), a fresh keyword no longer returns as a
stale offset, the reader's line table follows moved conses; MP — shutdown
reaps finished-but-unjoined workers, stops workers still running on
AmigaOS, exit waits bounded by the clock; a startup CPU store self-test
and the probe package that pinned the Vampire 68080 lost-store defect;
compiler fixes — DEFVAR evaluates its initial value only when unbound
(v38), &optional supplied-p vs &rest, MACROLET seen by the exit/inlining
analysis, FLET bindings protected across RETURN-FROM scans, string/vector
literal identity through COMPILE-FILE (v36), FASLs check the struct
layouts they were compiled against (v35); AmigaDOS pathnames read a
leading "/" as the parent; ~F/~$ right-justify; runtime UNDEFINED-FUNCTION
/ UNBOUND-VARIABLE are CELL-ERRORs; FOREIGN-TO-STRING reads to the NUL;
Windows builds carry :WINDOWS and native drive-letter namestrings; the
binary release packs the three builds behind six Workbench launcher
icons, one pair per binary (CLAmiga/Clamacs, -FPU, -MOS, no platform
detection), a 3 x 3 root grid, --snapshot [--with-mos] builds; and the
Amiga suite runs in 12 minutes with per-check log flushes and timings.

Permuter: idiom mutations (FixMulShift32 <-> FixMul >> 16, commuted FixMul operands, condition forms)

conditions (never inside call arguments). Each candidate rewrites one
occurrence, plus one that rewrites all of them. Run with
--mutation-kinds idiom.

Matching tools: register-blind shape score, annotated globals in fastcmp, permuter mutators

- match.py --list --shape ranks the remaining functions by similarity with

  register-allocation cases (shape 100%) are separated from structural ones;

  resort, so a global added or renamed since the last full build no longer
  reads as an unmapped symbol in the fast loop.
- scripts/permute_mutators.py: the mutator module permute_batch.py expected
  but which was never committed (moves, if/else swaps, operand swaps and

events.title: Split g_raceBlock into its separate globals: 2815/3363 byte-exact (+3)
events.message:
Split g_raceBlock into its separate globals: 2815/3363 byte-exact (+3)

The 0x537568..0x537dcc tables were one BYTE blob addressed through macros,
so MSVC6 had to assume a store into g_stageSoundUsed[i] could change
g_stageSoundCount and reloaded it after every store. The original keeps the
bound load ahead of the store, which only happens for distinct objects.
The head tables are now separate globals with their own annotations, the
per-car rows are RaceCarSoundState g_carSoundStates[8] (CarSoundSet and the
sound ids stay views into those rows), and the loaded/first pair is one
struct because the original reads the loaded byte as a masked dword.

Newly exact: CarSound_PlaySlot (98.0%), Race_MoveCarSoundBank (94.3%),
Race_MarkUsedSurfaceSoundGroups (93.1%). No function lost; datacmp clean.

events.title: runtime: VDP2's rotation screen RBG0, line scroll, raster effects
events.message:
runtime: VDP2's rotation screen RBG0, line scroll, raster effects

RBG0: rotation parameters A and B from their table in VRAM (RPTA), each
dot's map coordinates from the start, the steps, the matrix, the
viewpoint, the centre, the shift and the scale; coefficient tables (one
or two words, per line or per dot as the RAM banks are set, in VRAM or
colour RAM) giving kx and ky, one of them or Xp, and a transparent bit;
RPMD 0-2; a 4x4 map of planes or a bitmap; screen-over (repeat, a
pattern, transparent). It takes its place after the sprite and before
NBG0 among equal priorities, with colour calculation, colour offset and
windows as the other layers. RBG1 and parameters chosen by window are
still noted.

NBG0/NBG1's line scroll (SCRCTL, LSTA): an X scroll added to SCX, a Y
scroll added to SCY (the Y coordinate counting again from it) and an X
increment replacing ZMXN, every 1, 2, 4 or 8 lines.

Raster effects: while the SCU lets HBlank-IN through, the master's time
passes a raster line at a time, so that every line's HBlank is taken
before the next line starts (a poll spans about 1.6 lines, and an
interrupt raised twice before it is taken once). VDP2 register writes
made in the HBlank-IN handler are kept with their line, and each line is
composed with the registers it had: those written as they stood by then,
the others as the field ends.

A debugging aid: SATURNKIT_VDP2_HIDE=MASK leaves layers out of the
picture (1 sprite, 2 RBG0, 4-32 NBG0-NBG3).

A 1997 SHC game's title: the clouds are RBG0 (a bitmap with a
coefficient a line), the ground NBG0 in perspective by line scroll, and
the haze at the horizon colour offset B written on every line by its
HBlank handler. Its perspective frame has Beetle Saturn's colours.

Virtual Hydlide and a 1995 FMV game: byte-identical pictures and sound.
A two-disc SGL game unmasks HBlank-IN: it now takes every line's
(752 929 HBlanks in 3 000 VBlanks against 465 157), and the time spent in
its handler moves its frames slightly (964 VDP1 frames in 3 000 VBlanks
against 972; its "presents" title a few frames on at VBlank 2000); its
first room at VBlank 2900 is pixel-identical.

events.title: ci: pin the hatari-pist fork at d7e3363
events.message:
ci: pin the hatari-pist fork at d7e3363

The Windows release leg has never built: both attempts at 0.9.0-alpha died
in this action at

  hatari-src-pist/src/pistmedia.c:61:10: fatal error: sys/socket.h: No such
  file or directory

The media channel is plain TCP, so it needs no Unix-domain sockets, but it
included the POSIX socket headers unconditionally and Windows has none of
them. d7e3363 gates them on HAVE_WINSOCK_SOCKETS the way the fork's own
debug/remotedebug.c already does, and carries what follows from WinSock:
ioctlsocket instead of fcntl, no MSG_DONTWAIT, an unsigned SOCKET that makes
every `fd < 0` test a no-op, WSAGetLastError instead of errno, and
getenv+_putenv_s instead of a setenv the Windows CRT does not have.

CI's Windows leg skips the fork (matrix.emulator is false there), which is
why this only ever surfaced in the release workflow — the one place the fork
is built for Windows.

events.message:
Konami's Synthesizer: PLAY y los timbres en WAV

tools/omsx_ritmo.tcl mide en openMSX cada escritura en el DAC con la tecla
puesta a cada una de las 13 rutinas: PLAY lee el bufer de uno en uno y la
muestra dura c(r) + 16 * D ciclos (c de 67 a 82). Las 13 rutinas son el
ajuste fino de la afinacion, no voces: PLAY es monofonico. Con 0x5E29 la
afinacion es temperada de FA1 (43,6 Hz) a SI4; LA3 = 219,9 Hz.
tools/sonido.py toca cada timbre de fabrica con ese modelo en WAV de 8 bits.

events.title: discover: a pointer into code already found is an entry, however short
events.message:
discover: a pointer into code already found is an entry, however short

A table of pointers into an unrolled copy (SHC's structure copy: a
`jmp` to the entry for the number of words left) has entries whose
descents are a few instructions long, down to `rts` and its slot. The
rule that a pointer taken only for its table must descend at least 8
instructions (a data record can decode cleanly for a few) left out the
last four, and a 1997 SHC game called one of them on its first boot.
A descent wholly in code already found cannot be a data record: it is
now taken at any length.

Virtual Hydlide, a two-disc SGL game and a 1995 FMV game: self-tests
pass, their headless runs give byte-identical pictures and sound.

events.title: Overlays called and returned from; the 1st read entered with interrupts open
events.message:
Overlays called and returned from; the 1st read entered with interrupts open

A resident program may load programs one after another at one address
and call each as a function that returns, rather than start them as
programs that reset the stack. `recomp --overlay NAME,...` marks such
programs (SH2Module.flags, SH2_MODULE_OVERLAY); a call to their base
identifies the image there, activates it and calls it on the same host
stack (sh2_overlay_call, logged as "overlay N"); an image that matches
no module stops the run with its crc32. A call to any other module's
base is a program start as before.

The runtime now enters the 1st read with the CPU's interrupt mask at 0
instead of 15. On the Saturn the IP.BIN's initial program, which the
BIOS runs and the runtime does not, installs VBlank handlers, waits on a
counter the VBlank-in handler (level 15) counts, masks VBlank at the SCU
again and calls the 1st read with SR as it was: so the mask is below 15
there. A 1997 SHC game waits for a VBlank-in before it ever writes SR.
The SCU's mask stays all set at boot, so nothing is taken before a game
unmasks a source.

Virtual Hydlide, a two-disc SGL game and a 1995 FMV game: regenerated,
self-tests pass (51 542, 16 527 and 11 632 vectors), their headless runs
give byte-identical pictures and sound.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: test: compare the media panel to a rendered frame, once running
events.message:
test: compare the media panel to a rendered frame, once running

mediaDisplayFeedsThePanel failed on CI run after run while passing locally.
Two causes, both measured rather than guessed:

The panel draws its Paused badge in widget coordinates, so whenever the
fitted video reaches the widget's top-right corner the badge lands inside
the sampled grid. At the 320x200 a squeezed dock gives, that cost exactly
the four corner cells — a 60/64 pass two cells from failing — and CI
reported 34/64 and never matched in a minute of retrying. Waiting for a
later frame is no escape: after the entry stop a guest that loops forever
redraws nothing, so the one structured frame the change-gated stream
carries is delivered while the badge is still up. The comparison now waits
for the session to run again.

The expectation is rendered rather than sampled. A stride-2 walk of an
832x552 source and the panel's own nearest-neighbour downscale keep
different subsets of its pixels, so one and the same frame could disagree
in half the cells; both sides now go through the same fit and the same
drawImage, and every pixel in a cell counts. The oracle still decodes the
raw payload itself, so a wrong mask or pitch in mediaFrameImage() stays
visible.

The quiet-window gate goes with them: the widget stores a frame as it is
delivered and grab() renders synchronously, so there was never anything to
settle — only 60 s to starve on a guest that keeps redrawing.

Proved with a negative control: inverting the expectation's pixels fails
the check at 0/64 cells, worst delta 221, naming the frame, the fit and the
panel's own spread.

events.title: cpu-z80: increment R during HALT and on INT/NMI acknowledge
events.message:
cpu-z80: increment R during HALT and on INT/NMI acknowledge

Since the switch from z80ex to the cpu-z80 core (v2.0.2) the R register
was not incremented on the repeated HALT fetch (every 4 T) nor when an
INT or NMI was accepted; z80ex did both. Programs that derive a key or
timing from R broke: the tape version of Interkarate decrypts its loader
with LD A,R after a HALT waiting for the VBLN interrupt, so it looped
forever and the screen did not turn black after loading the first part.

- z80_execute.inc: INC_R in the halted path
- z80.c: inc_r_on_int_ack() for both NMI and INT acknowledge
- tests/libs/cpu_z80/test_r_register.c: HALT (per-step and batch),
  bit 7 preservation, INT ack in IM 1 and IM 2, NMI ack, internal
  interrupt handling in z80_execute

Also fix the MCP cmt_tape_block_speed command, which had no effect:
it set the block's cmt speed but not blspeed = SET, so the block was
opened at the global speed. The logic moved to the new
cmt_tape_set_block_cmt_speed() (dbgapi calls it, return codes
unchanged), covered by tests in test_cmt_state.c. The MCP docs now
state that the speed applies from the next opening of the block.

events.title: helios: HTTPS on the T425 - BearSSL and Manx built with Helios C
events.message:
helios: HTTPS on the T425 - BearSSL and Manx built with Helios C

tools/helios/bundle.py (replacing bundle.sh) lays out Manx and the
BearSSL files of tools/helios/bearssl.txt for Helios C: BearSSL's
headers renamed to unique 8.3 names (bearssl_x509.h -> br_x509.h, its
config.h -> brconfig.h) with the #include lines rewritten, stable 8.3
names for the C files (six letters and a CRC of the path when the name
is longer), and a build.csh that builds xmanx, ufetch, manxtrust and
test_sigkat. os/helios/stdint.h: Helios C has none; uint64_t is 32
bits (BR_NO_U64). The HTTP-only stand-ins (os/helios/tls.h,
tls_none.c) go.

Helios C needed two more changes in BearSSL (now all in
third_party/patches/bearssl-helios.patch): no initialiser for an
automatic aggregate (ssl_engine.c), and no declarations at the top of
a switch body - Helios C misplaces them. ec_prime_i15's run_code() and
x509_minimal's verify_signature() both kept an array there: every
prime-curve operation and every RSA certificate signature came out
wrong on the T425 until they moved. In Manx: char * casts for Helios's
read() and write(), and termios's ICANON, which Helios spells ICANNON.

tests/test_sigkat.c: known answers small enough for Helios C to
compile (BearSSL's test_crypto.c is too big for it): SHA-1/256/384/512,
RSA-2048's public operation by sig_rsa and br_rsa_i15, RFC 6979 ECDSA
on P-256 and P-384 by ecvrfy, br_ecdsa_i15 over all_m15 and over
prime_i15. All pass on the T425 (Helios in Hatari), and on the host.

ufetch on Helios in Hatari, through slirp: www.google.com, example.com,
news.ycombinator.com and letsencrypt.org load over TLS 1.2 (handshakes
about 3 s; certificate checks 10-47 s on portable C, for now).
68k.news is refused, rightly: its certificate is for another host.

events.title: tools: beebgame's dataflow analyses on a Baron build, fetched and unmodified
events.message:
tools: beebgame's dataflow analyses on a Baron build, fetched and unmodified

Eben Upton's tools/dataflow (github.com/ebenupton/beebgame) - liveness,
constants, value ranges, register ABIs and the bytes they can save - now
runs on a kit project: `python tools/analyse.py report|annotate|patterns`.

The analyses read only ld65's debug file, so baron_dbg.py writes one from
what every kit build already leaves (the -v listing, the --symbols dump,
the raw -o disc) and the tools run as they are. Baron gives no source line
per statement; the converter re-finds each by walking INCLUDE and MACRO,
and placed 573 of 573 on the template and 11,124 of 11,124 on
puzzle-beeble.

beebgame has no licence file, so nothing of it is committed here:
analyse.py fetches commit 77bbdb6 from a local checkout or GitHub and
checks all eleven files' SHA-256 before running anything (both routes
tested). Two upstream problems are patched in memory and documented: on
Windows Source.short's separators make every file "not the game's", and
a range run that exhausts its step budget is reported converged - it is
now marked NOT sound, its cache dropped, and --budget raises the limit.

Measured 2026-10-06: template report 6 findings / 11 bytes, all checked
correct; puzzle-beeble 122 findings in 4 s, its range analysis not
converging within 3M steps. docs/dataflow.md has the account and the two
Baron traps (allocator-shared zero page, constant coincidences); skill
beeb-dataflow the procedure.

Το sound.asm από 540 σε 338 bytes, και κάθε κλήση πιο γρήγορη σε κάθε
περίπτωση που δοκιμάστηκε (μέσοι όροι: snd_tick 432 -> 297 µs, snd_play

- Τα εφέ 28 bytes μικρότερα: βήμα θορύβου χωρίς hi, κανάλι και
  προτεραιότητα σε ένα byte, sn_tab με αποστάσεις ενός byte. Τα βήματα
  τα γράφουν οι μακροεντολές TONE/NOISE, με assert στα όρια.

tools: Online attaches a defined interface; ShowNetStatus says "not attached"

Since e99b7e94 the stack starts only the interfaces it is told to, so a
definition in DEVS:NetInterfaces (wifipi on the A1200) can be absent from
the running stack.  ShowNetStatus called it offline and advised "Online
wifipi"; Online then refused with "configured but the running stack has
no such interface".  Online now attaches the definition (NETCTRL_
INTERFACE_ADD, as AddNetInterface does) before bringing it up, reporting
the device's refusal if it fails.  ShowNetStatus tests "never attached"
before "offline", prints "state not attached", and says each in one line.

events.title: Fix multiple emulator bug.
events.message:
Fix multiple emulator bug.

Fixed. Replace your running copy with **`sms-game-designer-editor.zip`** (below), and do a hard refresh (Ctrl+F5) the first time so your browser picks up the patched emulator loader instead of a cached copy.

**Why it happened.** "Stopping" the emulator only emptied its container. That removed the picture but not the program: the emulator's main loop, its audio, its gamepad polling and its window listeners all kept going in the background. On top of that, every Play loaded the emulator's code again, so after three Plays there were three copies.

I reproduced both in the built editor before changing anything. After a second Play, the first emulator's gamepad poll was still ticking every 10 ms.

**The fix.**

-   **Full shutdown.** EmulatorJS has no "destroy" function. Its own Exit button stops the core's main loop and shuts the core down, so the editor now triggers that same exit. It also stops what that exit leaves running: the gamepad poll, the audio and the emulator's element.
-   **Fast double-clicks.** The emulator loads asynchronously, so if you pressed Play twice quickly, the first one could finish loading *after* it had been told to stop, and then start playing anyway. The editor now catches each emulator as it's created and matches it to the Play that asked for it. One that turns up late for an outdated Play is shut down before it can start.
-   **Code loads once.** The emulator's loader now loads the emulator's code only the first time. That's a second patch in the vendoring script, checked the same way as the update-check patch.

**How it's tested.**

-   **In the built editor:** a second Play replaces the first emulator, the old one is no longer running, and the emulator's code is loaded once.
-   **The double-click race:** it can't be triggered reliably by clicking through the editor, so it's tested directly with stand-in emulators. That covers two Plays before either loads, a Play stopped before its emulator arrives, and a Play whose loader failed. Breaking the late-arrival check on purpose fails exactly the two race tests.

The full suite is at 290 passing, nothing skipped, and the editor zip itself passes all 28 end-to-end checks after unpacking.

events.title: httpfb: back off on a still screen under the ZZ9000 encoder; input ends the wait
events.message:
httpfb: back off on a still screen under the ZZ9000 encoder; input ends the wait

The card encoder was exempt from the still-screen backoff, so an idle
/console asked the card for a frame ~28 times a second (425 of 430 replies
empty) with the 68k spinning on each.  It now takes the same ladder, from
the length of the card's reply, and an empty frame is one band instead of
five (bytes per tile row truncated to 0 fell back to 8-row bands).

Viewer input reset the backoff count but not the wait already scheduled,
so a key's echo could wait the ladder's 500 ms.  fb_write_event now makes
the next pass due at once, and a chase's empty passes no longer advance
the ladder.

A3000 (ZZ9000, 800x600x8): idle card calls 28.7/s -> 2.1/s; keystroke to
frame 68-185 ms -> 13-19 ms.  console-probe.py inflates deflated frames.

events.title: runtime: the CD drive at 2x, after a seek timed as Mednafen's
events.message:
runtime: the CD drive at 2x, after a seek timed as Mednafen's

Data sectors now come at 150 a second (double speed); the drive read
300, twice the speed its own comment gave. A Play that moves the pickup,
or starts from a pause, first seeks: status SEEK for Mednafen's drive
timing (in its 44 100 x 256 Hz clock: 255 500 to start, 12 sectors'
time, 26 a sector of distance forward or 28 back, a sector's time more
going back or 150 sectors on, one for the subcode), then the first
sector a sector's time later. A Play of mode bit 7 while playing reads
on with no seek.

A game that loads a picture file into a buffer, has SGL copy its palette
to colour RAM at the next VBlank and starts reading the next file into
the same buffer got the next file's palette: with no seek its first
sectors came before that VBlank. Loading takes longer in virtual time,
as on the Saturn; the same headless pad scripts reach their places
later, and presses timed for the old speed may fall into a loading.

events.title: Fix emulator execution.
events.message:
Fix emulator execution.

Ran 45 commands, created 5 files

Both changes work and are tested, but I ran out of tool calls one step short of the zip files. The three package folders are staged, and the downloads currently in your outputs folder are still last round's `sms-game-maker-*` archives. They contain none of this work. Say "continue" and I'll zip, check by extracting into a clean directory, and hand them over.

Compiling in the browser. Press Play and the editor now builds the ROM itself, in under half a second, then runs it. Download ROM on the Play tab gets you the cartridge.

I'd previously said this needed Emscripten, which this sandbox can't download. It turned out not to need it. CVBasic and gasm80 are plain C programs that read and write files, and Zig --- which installs from PyPI --- compiles C straight to WebAssembly. That gives `cvbasic.wasm` (213 KB) and `gasm80.wasm` (67 KB), run in a Web Worker through a small JavaScript runtime.

The proof I care about: all four sample ROMs built this way are byte-identical to the native compilers' output, including the SG-1000 one. The end-to-end test opens Bug Blaster in the built editor, presses Play, captures the ROM on its way to the emulator, and compares it to the native build.

Fixes made along the way:

-   The compiler path was hard-coded to `/wasm/`, which would have broken hosting the editor in a subdirectory.
-   The WASI runtime logged every file the compilers opened, on every build, because it treats a missing debug option as on.
-   If the emulator failed to start, the Play tab stayed silently black. It now says the emulator couldn't load and points at Download ROM, since the ROM is fine either way.
-   The Play tab had a "Show hitboxes" checkbox described as reading the emulator's memory live. Nothing read the checkbox or the emulator, so I removed it.
-   The emulator itself still comes from a CDN I can't reach from here. Building is verified; playing inside the editor isn't.

The rename to SMS Game Designer is done everywhere except 15 references to `vcs-game-maker`, the upstream project, which I left alone. Your autosave was stored under the old name, so a naive rename would have opened an empty project on next launch. The renamed editor copies the old autosave across on first launch and leaves the original in place. Old `.smsgm` project files still open; new saves use `.smsgd`. Both behaviours are tested.

The test runner forwarded a sub-suite's `FAIL` line but dropped the reason underneath it, so failures arrived unexplained. Fixed. It also caught a test that only passed on a clean disk, which I fixed too.

265 tests pass, with the full suite exiting cleanly against the final source.

The emulator now ships inside the editor, as you suggested: EmulatorJS 4.2.3, trimmed from the release's 303 MB down to the 2.9 MB the Master System needs. Pressing **Play** no longer touches the internet, so it works offline. Replace your running copy with **`sms-game-designer-editor.zip`** (3.5 MB).

**What I kept, and why.** I read EmulatorJS's own code to pick the files rather than guessing.

-   **Core:** it maps the Master System to the smsplus core, so that's the one I kept.
-   **Both builds of it:** EmulatorJS loads the *legacy* build by default, not the normal one. Keeping only the obvious build would have broken play for everyone, so both are in.
-   **No separate SG-1000 core:** SG-1000 cartridges run through the same core, which tells them apart by file extension. The core's own metadata lists both `sms` and `sg`.

**What I fixed.**

-   **Hidden network fallback:** if a bundled file goes missing, EmulatorJS quietly downloads it from its own servers. The test now records every request Play makes and fails if any goes outside the editor's folder.
-   **Update check removed:** EmulatorJS checks its servers for a newer version whenever it runs on `localhost`, which is how you run it. I disabled that one call. Nothing leaves your machine now, which is also what the README promises.
-   **The old setup was unpinned:** it loaded `emulatorjs@latest` from a CDN, so the emulator could have changed underneath the editor at any time.
-   **ColecoVision and MSX:** their cores aren't bundled, so for those consoles the Play tab says plainly to download the ROM, instead of fetching a core from the internet.

**Reproducible, not hand-assembled.** `npm run emulator` downloads the release, keeps only those files, disables the update check, and writes a manifest of file hashes. It refuses to continue if a future release changes the code it patches. Rerunning it on the extracted source archive reproduced the shipped emulator byte for byte. A test checks the folder against that manifest, and when I tampered with the bundle on purpose, the test caught it.

**Testing harness.** Bundling the emulator exposed two problems in my own tests.

-   **A crash that depended on timing:** a test run without Web Workers let the emulator throw an error that killed the run on some timings and not others. That run no longer loads the emulator, and stray errors are now reported by a test instead of stopping it.
-   **A compiler check blaming the emulator:** a check meant to catch the compiler failing was catching the emulator instead. It now tells the two apart.

All three archives were checked after zipping. The editor zip, unzipped and served as-is, passes all 25 end-to-end checks; the full suite is at 279, with nothing skipped.

**One thing I couldn't verify here:** actually seeing the game run on screen. My test environment can follow the emulator up to unpacking its core, but running the core needs WebGL, and there's no browser in this sandbox. Everything up to that point is checked, but the last step needs you to press Play.

The source archive is larger now (2.4 MB) because it includes the prebuilt compilers and the bundled emulator, so building the editor needs neither Zig nor a download. EmulatorJS and its cores are GPL-3.0; the licence is included in `emulator/LICENSE-EmulatorJS`.

events.title: perf(presentation): count retained-text cells per screen row (#4137)
events.message:
perf(presentation): count retained-text cells per screen row (#4137)

Every plain screen-row store first checks that the row span holds no
retained text by scanning one coverage flag per pixel. The PowerPC host
synchronization stores the whole front buffer this way, row by row, on
every synchronization, and the 68k plain-store paths (CopyBits
destination rows, span stores) ask the same question. Keep a per-row
count of text cells beside the global one, updated at the same single
transition point, so a row with none answers without the scan. Debug
builds recount the changed row on every transition.

events.title: perf(ppc): reuse the caller's CPU for alert modal passes (#4134)
events.message:
perf(ppc): reuse the caller's CPU for alert modal passes (#4134)

Alert, its StopAlert/NoteAlert/CautionAlert variants and StandardAlert
run ModalDialog's host loop with ModalDialog's register arguments. They
did that on a clone of the whole PowerPC CPU so the caller's registers
survived, and every idle pass re-dispatches the import, so an alert that
waits for input copied the CPU's multi-megabyte decode and basic-block
caches once per execution slice.

ModalDialog executes no guest instructions: it reads its arguments,
stages callback arguments in registers, and returns guest callbacks as
actions the run loop starts afterwards. Save the caller's registers,
run it on the CPU itself, and restore them before using its action, so
its register writes are discarded exactly as the clone's were. The time
base, reservation, native return frames and caches are never touched by
host code; a debug assertion checks the first two.

events.title: bsdsocket: a long path gets the full window until the card overruns
events.message:
bsdsocket: a long path gets the full window until the card overruns

A long path (handshake round trip at or above TCPGROWRTT) on a burst-bound
card was fitted to the card's receive memory unless the interface file set
TCPWANWINDOW: on a 3C589 (about four segments) that capped a 23 ms path
near 2 Mbit/s.  Defaults should take the throughput, so a long path now
gets the window its settle chose.  The SANA-II reader reads the driver's
overrun count once a second while a capacity is stated; an overrun while
a long-path connection runs unfitted switches that interface to the fit
until it is next attached.  TCPWANWINDOW, when set, still decides.

Earlier evidence for the default: A3000 X-Surf 100 without flow control,
a 32-frame window gave 12.9 Mbit/s over a 24 ms path against 5.7 with
the fit (test_pool_window_host.c).  Host tests: unfitted by default,
fitted after an overrun, LAN unchanged, TCPWANWINDOW over an overrun.

events.title: test: skip key injection on EmuTOS, where the guest never starts
events.message:
test: skip key injection on EmuTOS, where the guest never starts

EmuTOS abandons the autostart when a key arrives while it is still
booting, so the program never runs and no injected scancode can be
observed (docs/PLAN.md §9). Verified: injecting from t=0 left the guest on
its desktop painting neither colour; delaying the first injection ran it;
real TOS was unaffected either way. Neither a post-boot delay, a
media-frame readiness gate, nor the debugger's entry stop held up under
EmuTOS in CI, so the test skips there rather than sitting red — the
frame, mouse and panel media tests still exercise the channel.

Also read colour through the frame's own masks (the fork forwards SDL's)
instead of assuming 0x00RRGGBB, which production deliberately does not.

events.title: runtime: the CD block's Play as Mednafen's: modes, the pickup kept
events.message:
runtime: the CD block's Play as Mednafen's: modes, the pickup kept

Play Disc (0x10) now follows Mednafen's CD block. The play mode's repeat
count is taken only when its bits 4-6 are clear, so mode 0xFF changes
nothing (it was read as "repeat for ever"). Bit 7 leaves the pickup
where it is: a Play that only moves the end of the range on lets the
drive read on instead of seeking back to the start. A position 0xFFFFFF
is the last Play's; an end given in sectors counts from the start
given. The play ends when the position leaves the range (the end, or
before the start), and the status's low nibble counts the repeats done
rather than echoing the count asked for.

GFS_SGL's streams depend on it: they push the end of their play on with
mode 0xFF and issue the next file's play only once the stream's has
ended (PEND). Before, the stream never ended and the file was never
read.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: runtime: the DIVU's shadow registers; the DMAC's 16-byte units whole
events.message:
runtime: the DIVU's shadow registers; the DMAC's 16-byte units whole

Each division now also writes DVDNTH and DVDNTL's shadows at 0x118 and
0x11C (and their mirrors at 0x138/0x13C); a store there only sets the
shadow, as in Mednafen. SGL's slLookAt reads its 64/32 quotient back
from 0xFFFFFF1C; reading 0 there zeroed the camera matrix and with it
every polygon's vertices.

The SH-2 DMAC in 16-byte mode counts TCR in longwords, four to a unit.
The runtime divided TCR by four and then skipped three counts a unit,
so it moved a quarter of the bytes. The trace line now gives the source
address and the bytes moved.

events.message:
Fix dependency security vulnerabilities (#365)

Fix the vulnerable documentation, Cloudflare development/test, and VS
Code packaging dependencies behind all 37 open Dependabot alerts. The
documentation update patches search suggestions with MkDocs Material
9.7.7 and upgrades urllib3 to 2.8.0; npm lockfiles use patched undici,
sharp, Vitest/mocker, markdown-it, and brace-expansion versions. Update
qs for additional advisories found by npm audit.

Raise minimum dependency versions and add overrides for vulnerable
dependencies pinned by Miniflare. Keep the Cloudflare test integration
on its compatible Vitest 4 release line and add the extension changelog
entry.

Validation:
- All four npm projects install cleanly with lifecycle scripts disabled
and report zero audit findings; the hashed Python requirements pass
pip-audit.
- Confirmed that every one of the 37 original alert ranges excludes the
resolved dependency versions.
- Cloudflare tests: 26 CORS proxy tests and 9 SwiftLink bridge tests
passed.
- TypeScript checks and local deployment builds passed for all three
Workers.
- VS Code extension compiled and packaged successfully.
- Documentation built successfully with MkDocs strict mode.

After merge, republish the documentation through the GitHub Pages
workflow to replace the vulnerable search JavaScript. The Worker and VS
Code changes affect development/packaging tools and do not require
Worker deployment or a Marketplace release.

events.title: Fix and prevent Android type-registration crash (n_onResume/n_loadLibraries UnsatisfiedLinkError)
events.message:
Fix and prevent Android type-registration crash (n_onResume/n_loadLibraries UnsatisfiedLinkError)

Incremental builds could leave the Mono type-registration table
(libxamarin-app.so) stale relative to the generated Java stubs, crashing the
app at launch. Two .NET Android incremental-build bugs are involved: the
linked libxamarin-app.so is not relinked when the native-assembly objects
change, and regenerating the marshal methods table without a build-properties
change produces an incomplete table.

Add a ForceFreshTypeRegistration MSBuild target that deletes the
_CleanIntermediateIfNeeded.stamp before the SDK's _CleanIntermediateIfNeeded
target, forcing _CleanMonoAndroidIntermediateDir to clean the Android
intermediate on every build while keeping the C# compile output. Bake in the
reproducible build properties (PublishTrimmed=false, RunAOTCompilation=false,
Ambermoon AndroidLinkMode=None settings). Add build-android.ps1 and
test-android.ps1 as the canonical build + smoke-test workflow, and document
everything in Android.md.

events.title: Fix WASM Init() stack overflow, add Winchester boot and an Enable 5000 CPU toggle
events.message:
Fix WASM Init() stack overflow, add Winchester boot and an Enable 5000 CPU toggle

Init() trapped with "memory access out of bounds" on every browser boot.
Emscripten's default WebAssembly stack is 64 KB and InitWithConfig()'s
local MachineConfig is 75,904 bytes, so the struct alone overflowed it.
Raise the WASM link flags to -s STACK_SIZE=1048576.

Add a Winchester entry to the browser Boot dropdown: Boot() case 4 loads
WD0.IMG via BOOT_WINCHESTER, mirroring the SMD and SCSI cases, and the
toolbar checks the drive registry before booting it.

Add "Enable 5000 CPU" under Emulation in the config screen. Off by
default: the [mfbus], [mfbus.part.0], [controller.octobus.0] and
[nd5000.1] sections are appended to the INI at power-on only when the
toggle is on, so a machine with it off builds no MFbus pool and no
ND-5000 CPU, and the per-instruction MFbus tick costs four loads until
an ND-5000 actually starts. When it is on, also raise the mms log
category to WARN, since the ND-5000 mailbox/MON messages at LOG_INFO
otherwise flood the browser console once SINTRAN starts the CPU.

events.title: bsdsocket: share a card's receive capacity among a unit's connections
events.message:
bsdsocket: share a card's receive capacity among a unit's connections

ANX-018 (codex-amiga's ABI review): ANXD_CMD_RX_CAPACITY is per unit, but
every connection's window was fitted to the whole of it, so two LAN
senders could each be offered the full ring.  A connection's ring fit
now uses its part, the capacity divided by the settled, still-receiving,
burst-bound connections on the same unit (bsd_tcp_ring_sharers,
ami_bsd_tcp_window_ring_share).  A settle re-caps the others before the
new connection's data arrives; the reader re-shares once a second while
a capacity is stated, so a finished connection's part comes back.  The
two-segment floor per connection stays.

Host test: the split of a 13 KB ring for one, two and three connections.
A3000 (68060/50), X-Surf 100 with PAUSE: one stream 22.2 Mbit/s, two
simultaneous 21.7-21.9 Mbit/s in total, 0 overruns, 0 chip resets.

events.title: tls: BearSSL and Manx's TLS for a compiler with no 64-bit integers
events.message:
tls: BearSSL and Manx's TLS for a compiler with no 64-bit integers

Helios C, on the ATW800/2's T425, has no 64-bit integer type. BearSSL
gets a BR_NO_U64 setting (third_party/patches/bearssl-no-u64.patch):
uint64_t is then a 32-bit type, used only for byte counters and record
sequence numbers, encoded with a zero high word; SHA-384/512 work on
32-bit halves; the multi-hash keeps their states in 32-bit words; the
constant-time HMAC and CCM no longer shift 32-bit values by 32 or more;
x509_minimal_full and the defaults (BR_LOMUL, forced on) pick the code
that needs no 64-bit products: i15, m15, aes_ct, chacha20_ct,
poly1305_ctmul32, ghash_ctmul32.

Manx: tls.c's key exchange curves are BearSSL's m15 ones there (crypt68k
is 68030 assembly), ecvrfy sends P-521 to i15, and mont.c builds each
64-bit product from four 16 x 16-bit ones.

TARGET=no64 builds all of it on the host as Helios C would: the forced
tests/no_u64.h makes uint64_t 32 bits wide. `make TARGET=no64 test-no64`
runs BearSSL's tests of that code (tests/test_no64.c: hashes, HMAC,
DRBG, PRF, AES ct, DES, ChaCha20, Poly1305, GHASH, RSA i15, X25519 m15,
ECDSA i15 over all_m15, and P-256 m15 against prime_i15) and its 53
certificate tests: all pass. The no64 ufetch fetches example.com,
68k.news, news.ycombinator.com, www.google.com, letsencrypt.org and
geekdot.com over TLS 1.2 (ChaCha20-Poly1305, AES-256-GCM-SHA384). The
normal build's tests still pass.

runtime_profiles.name: Documented classic Amiga OCS game
runtime_profiles.notes: The generated game-world source explicitly names Amiga OCS. Exact CPU, RAM and Kickstart floors are unverified, as is a complete playthrough.

project.status: Distinct game source and scenario reviewed; draft navigation/content; rebuild and complete playthrough unverified
project.notes: Windless Bay is a distinct short interactive-fiction game set at an Antarctic research station near Mount Erebus. README identifies a classic-Amiga game built on R-Page, and game/game/world.c contains game-specific room/world state, CABLE plus COMBINE to TELEPHONE object combination, sprite associations and scenario conditions. The Makefile composes world, scene, GUI, text, assets and special-game modules with R-Page. Its world and content establish a game project beyond an engine checkout or screenshot repository. It is tracked separately from the existing rpage-resistance engine record. Classified as an original authored native-Amiga game subject, not a reverse engineering or decompilation of another commercial title. work_kinds is empty because the demonstrated work is game development and scenario generation rather than a binary-derived reconstruction. The generated world source is explicitly labeled Windless Bay for Amiga OCS and identifies the R-Page scenario toolchain. Generated C is a build/content artifact, not evidence of generative-AI authorship. Bundled engine, compression and asset tools remain dependencies within this game's single repository identity. The inspected SAS/C recipe compiles native C objects, builds an includes.gst header and links main.exe with R-Page, AmigaOS and decompression components. Resource generation is a separate asset/scenario stage. The latest five commits explicitly include draft resource toolchain, draft content and draft navigation before fixes to PNG conversion and world.json navigation. A checked-in main.exe or resource pack does not establish a reproducible source build or a completed story. No tools or candidate binary were executed, and compilable, runnable, playable and byte_exact remain null. The catalogue preserves this as substantial but draft game work. The upstream target is the classic Amiga family, with the generated game-world header explicitly specifying OCS. That is sufficient for a platform/chipset profile but not a numeric minimum. No exact processor, total or Chip/Fast RAM amount, Kickstart/Workbench version or completed-playthrough result was found in README, makefile, SCOPTIONS and the reviewed game source. The profile therefore records OCS without claiming that every stock A500 configuration meets its requirements. R-Page's independent requirements must not silently be inherited by this game without verifying the bundled version and content. Windless Bay uses ResistanceVault/rpage, already represented as rpage-resistance in the catalogue. The dependency link does not make the game a mirror of the engine: the reviewed source implements a separate named story, world and content. Engine modules, generated scenario code and packed resources belong to one game discovery. The repository LICENSE is MIT with Resistance copyright, but separately bundled dependency files should retain their own notices; this review does not assert an asset-by-asset rights audit. The root/name/alias check found no prior Windless Bay game entry. Full upstream author/content graph coverage remains partial. The checked recipe uses SAS/C sc to build an Amiga main.exe from game modules and AmigaOS-specific R-Page sources. Together with the explicit classic-Amiga target this supports m68k output. SCOPTIONS contains optimization/code/data settings but no exact CPU requirement in the reviewed text. Windows resource-tool binaries in the tree describe a development-host stage and do not make Windows a target platform for the game; neither those utilities nor Python resource scripts determine a host/game ISA entry.

project.notes: Paul Kienitz's original Amiga implementation of the remembered commercial board game Tripppples, represented by the fourth-release README and matching Tripppin 4 window title. Board.c shuffles the arrow tiles; Trip.c implements legal moves, recursive move selection and a separate thinking task; Jrdobbs.c draws the board pieces. The 8-by-8 game, configurable difficulty, suggestions and undo are substantive native game code. Canonical root and subject aliases were screened against the 1715-project baseline f8c70d18333dad71c511eda424fadd2627c5f6fc and the 2031-root prior-review index; this is a new project lineage. Current default-branch tip is b2132ac57c4be74393b1020cc8585f5fe1b77147; the complete tree contains 10 entries. This is preservation of the author's C board-game implementation, a native Amiga game subject. The author explicitly says he recreated the board rules from memory and may not have reproduced them exactly. It is not reverse engineering of a previous software binary; source-restoration is the archival work category, with board-rule implementation recorded as a technique rather than an asserted decompilation. Original classic Amiga C uses graphics.library/Intuition, Amiga Exec tasks and 68k register-call ABI pragmas. Board.c declares DrawImage with amicall register arguments a0/a1/d0/d1, and the makefile explicitly requires Amiga Aztec C 5.0+. This establishes the m68k source lineage without converting screen colors or integer widths into a processor minimum. MAKEFILE links ram:Tripppin using Amiga Aztec C and the native C library, while source uses direct classic Amiga library ABI calls and OS task primitives. The evidenced output is native Amiga/m68k. No modern host port or accelerated-CPU-only build is documented by the reviewed source, and exact minimum CPU is left unspecified. MAKEFILE says Aztec C 5.0+ only and requires custom II and INTU precompiled headers with Amiga headers, pragmas and prototypes. Trip.h includes Paul.h, which is absent from the current complete nine-file tree. The README even describes a historical omitted-Paul.h distribution issue; it does not supply the missing file today. Filenames also retain Amiga-era case assumptions. No clean modern rebuild was verified; all build/runtime/byte-exact flags remain null. The fourth-release README explicitly requires AmigaDOS 2.04 and says it no longer runs under 1.x. It launches from Workbench or CLI, optionally on a named public screen, adapting to font size/interlace and using additional screen colors when available. These are native GUI features, not evidence of an AGA/RTG or accelerator requirement. No numerical RAM or CPU minimum is documented. Trip.c's recursive PickBestMove and separate ThinkerTask are a traditional computer opponent. They establish game logic, not AI-assisted source development; the author describes writing this game for Amiga graphics and event-loop practice. Current default-branch history review covered the latest 6 commit messages returned by a 30-commit request, including tip b2132ac57c4be74393b1020cc8585f5fe1b77147; no explicit development-AI attribution or disclosure was found in these messages or the cited reviewed text. Amiga nw01/nw_light0, BeOS soeki_dev variants and sdl_port are one continuous game lineage. Reviewed SDL processing.cpp contains unit path tables, movement, attacks and deaths; Amiga source contains native screen/input/rendering work. The presence of real gameplay source is established without claiming a complete original restoration. Classified as a game subject with partial original-source restoration/preservation and a later source-based SDL backend adaptation. These are recovered authored C++ and assembly, not a decompilation of an original binary. The original Amiga material, historical BeOS code and SDL revival remain one record rather than one discovery per directory/name. The author's 2019 SDL commit explicitly calls it unfinished while reporting that the engine runs; that statement is retained as an upstream claim only. This is an incomplete recovered archive, not a complete release-ready source restoration. Amiga code depends on period compiler/API assumptions and hard-coded TEXT:Hisoft_C paths, data files and assembly helpers. The inspected BeOS makefile depends on BUILDHOME/etc/makefile-engine and period /boot libraries/headers. The SDL script compiles the platform and independent C++ modules with g++ and links SDL2/SDL2_image. The 2019 commit reports an unfinished engine that runs, followed by 2020 header/output-name fixes; it is not independent test proof. None of the variants was built or executed here and all four build flags remain null. README identifies the Amiga 1200 development origin, but does not state a complete runnable hardware minimum. Those source details preclude casually promising a stock A500 setup, yet neither an exact 68020/030 minimum nor an AGA requirement is asserted without direct requirements/testing. The BeOS display code explicitly requests 640x480 at 32 bits and checks graphics-mode support; the developer's recalled Pentium clock is not a minimum. Linux/SDL2 RAM, OS and host CPU requirements remain unknown, and every variant remains untested. Networ, Soeki and The Plague are successive names and directories of the same author/game, including the historical Amiga-to-BeOS migration and later SDL revival. They were screened as aliases against the 1715-project baseline and prior reviewed roots, with no counted match. README credits the friend who preserved some sources/assets and supplied graphics routines; this contextualizes the partial archive rather than licensing it. No root project LICENSE or clear blanket redistribution grant was found. project.notes: Darren Banfi’s AmIga Minesweeper is a distinct original native Amiga implementation, with source, screenshot and author README rather than an emulator wrapper or a mirror of another Minesweeper source release. The full minesweeper.c defines a 10-by-10 board with ten mines, adjacency counts, a queue-based empty-area reveal, flagging, mouse events, reset, win/loss handling and Amiga Intuition graphics/audio effects. It is not the same code lineage as Paul Kienitz’s Miner, despite sharing the game genre. The author’s root and title were absent from the current 1715 catalogue, source and decision indexes and 2031 prior-root union. Subject/game: native classic-Amiga homebrew written in C. This is a source-available new implementation of familiar Minesweeper rules, not evidence of disassembling the Windows game or reconstructing an original commercial Amiga executable. The Amiga APIs and actual rule/event code establish a substantive game. work_kinds stays empty rather than inventing a binary-derived reverse-engineering method; original-homebrew and AI-assisted-development nuance remains in types and notes. This is a newly authored native Amiga C game, with no separately analyzed predecessor executable or original machine code. source_platforms and source_cpu therefore stay empty; the newly authored C source is recorded under reconstructed_languages, while the explicit classic-Amiga and m68k-amigaos compiler target belongs in target_platforms/target_cpu. This avoids assigning a source ISA merely from the machine on which a new homebrew game is intended to run. The provided compiler example uses m68k-amigaos-gcc, and source calls classic AmigaOS interfaces. The output target is therefore m68k. The README’s generic classic-Amiga statement does not independently demonstrate a stock 68000 minimum, later 68020 requirements, a PPC build or an AROS target; those are not assigned. No executable was compiled or ISA-inspected in this audit. README provides an m68k-amigaos GCC command and mentions VBCC; the tree contains source and screenshot rather than a verified generated binary/release. The implementation uses C99-style loops and modern Amiga SDK declarations, so exact compiler/SDK compatibility requires a future clean build. No build, installation, game execution, gameplay or byte comparison was performed, and all four build flags remain null. README’s fully-functional description is an author assertion, not an independent test. README claims a classic Amiga with at least 1MB Chip RAM and AmigaOS 2.0+. The current source contradicts the OS floor: setPointerBusy/setPointerNormal call SetWindowPointer with WA_BusyPointer, and revealCell actually invokes these unguarded functions. Published Amiga SDK autodocs mark both SetWindowPointer and SetWindowPointerA as V39. The profile preserves the author-stated Chip RAM and marks the source-required Intuition V39 path; it does not promise OS2 compatibility. No exact CPU/chipset/RTG/accelerator minimum or measured runtime was established. README explicitly states that AI was used to make this project over seven hours, naming Amiga Guru on ChatGPT. ai.usage is true and the named tool is ChatGPT; this is affirmative author attribution, not inference from an AI-named file, a screenshot, a provider domain or gameplay logic. The current bounded latest-30 commit review found no additional explicit named AI coauthor claim. The attribution does not quantify which lines were generated or independently verify the author’s elapsed-time claim. Root LICENSE is MIT, copyright Darren Banfi 2024, and the C file names the same author. No external game-data download or commercial original binary is required by the documented code path. This distinct code is not merged with other Minesweeper homebrew merely because the rules match. The README clone command spells a different repository name; the verified canonical root is boingball/AmIgaMinesweeper and no unverified alternate URL is created. The OS compatibility contradiction is preserved for future validation rather than repaired during catalogue publication. Pinned source snapshot c825ab1055c14355816b45d688514e9d8a294cf1; bounded source/history audit. Evidence: https://github.com/boingball/AmIgaMinesweeper/blob/c825ab1055c14355816b45d688514e9d8a294cf1/README.md https://github.com/boingball/AmIgaMinesweeper/blob/c825ab1055c14355816b45d688514e9d8a294cf1/minesweeper.c https://d0.se/autodocs/intuition.library/SetWindowPointerA https://github.com/boingball/AmIgaMinesweeper/blob/c825ab1055c14355816b45d688514e9d8a294cf1/LICENSE

events.message:
xmanx: repaint only what Expose uncovers;   as a space

An Expose cleared the whole window and painted the whole page again.
With twm moving windows opaquely (Helios's twmrc does), every step of a
drag that brought a strip back from off the screen blanked the window
white and repainted it all, and on the T425 the repaints piled up. Now

A no-break space is drawn and measured as a space. X11R4's fonts,
Helios's, have no glyph at 0xA0 and give it no width, so on 68k.news
"headline  source" ran together. Layout has already kept the
words together, so a plain space looks the same.

Tested on Helios in Hatari: xrefresh over part of the window and over
all of it leaves xmanx's pixels unchanged; dragging it half off the
screen and scrolling there; the   gap. On Linux, Xvfb without

httpzz: require console service major 2; document the codec layers

From codex-amiga's ABI review (anxs2-abi-20261005/review.md):

ANX-024  The 0x8200 service was used whatever version it reported.  The
         host now requires major version 2 (the catalog's 0x00020000), so a
         firmware answering another layout falls back to the host encoder.
ANX-027  The request/reply `codec` is the outer mailbox codec (NONE in this
         version); separately the firmware may zlib-compress the inner RFB
         ops after the 4-byte header (RFC 1950, flagged by header byte 1
         bit 0), which the host passes through and the viewer inflates.

events.title: anxs2ext: v3 only; freeze the contract; one negotiation per open
events.message:
anxs2ext: v3 only; freeze the contract; one negotiation per open

Versions 1 and 2 of the SANA-II extension never left this tree, so a driver
no longer takes a v2 record: ANXD_S2_ABI_VERSION_MIN is now 3, equal to
ANXD_S2_ABI_VERSION, and every range check (netdev, the WiFiPi fork) accepts
exactly 3.  A v2 opener is ignored like any unknown version and falls back
to plain SANA-II.  The test that kept ABI 2 compatible now proves it is
refused.

anxs2ext: freeze the v3 contract; one negotiation per open; gate TxFlags

Answers codex-amiga's pre-publication ABI review (anxs2-abi-20261005/
review.md) and deepseek-v4's additions to it:

ANX-008/028  Exact v3 with a fixed prefix: ANXD_S2_EXTENSION_SIZE is the
             offset past TxFlags (24 on m68k), so appending fields never
             raises the minimum; the m68k build asserts the size and the
             TxFlags and Cookie offsets.
ANX-006      Only the first valid ANX record in a taglist is taken
             (netdev_take_extension_once); a later one is ignored and its
             Accepted untouched.  Host test.
ANX-013      TxFlags is called only when a TX feature was accepted.
ANX-015      AnxdS2RxBatch: Cookie[] under C99, Cookie[1] for C89/SAS-C,
             sized by offsetof; the header compiles with -std=c89 -pedantic.
ANX-009..012, 014, 016, 017, 018, 029  Normative text checked against the
             code: callback ABI and A4, context and blocking rules, RxDirect
             (even pointer, 14 bytes before it, NULL declines, the
             failed-copy exception to RxFilled), the SUMMED sum and
             VERIFIED scope, the TX seed and which frames an opener may
             flag, TX_QUICK and MORE/FLUSH scope, batch quick errors,
             private-command ownership and the reserved $8191, and
             RX_CAPACITY as a per-unit advisory window.

Still open: ANX-018's stack side (the window is capped per socket, not
shared per unit).

events.title: anxzz9000: TX status at 0x68, receive capacity from 0x6C, shifted-TX consent
events.message:
anxzz9000: TX status at 0x68, receive capacity from 0x6C, shifted-TX consent

The upstream ZZ9000 firmware has made 0x8a REG_ZZ_ETH_CONFIG (multicast
hash, link state).  The fork's merge with it (tinic/zz9000-firmware
af83b22) moves the asynchronous-send status to its own aligned register,
0x68.  ETH_CONFIG never reads with bit 15 set, so the driver at 0x8a only
fell back to the synchronous send there; at 0x68 it finds the async path.

A3000 (TF4060, 68060/50), firmware af83b22: receive 21.9-22.0 Mbit/s over
3 x 60 s (494 MB, no stall), send 11.9 Mbit/s, PAUSE negotiated.

anxzz9000: receive capacity from the firmware; shifted TX needs consent

From codex-amiga's ABI review (anxs2-abi-20261005/review.md):

ANX-019  The receive capacity was inferred from the async-send status (56
         frames) although an upstream build can send asynchronously with
         32 receive descriptors.  It now comes from the firmware's
         REG_ZZ_ETH_RX_FRAMES (0x6C): bit 15 present, bits 14..0 frames; a
         firmware without it reads 0, for which the ring's 32 are assumed.
         RX_STATUS bits 14..8 are a transient reservation count and are no
         longer read for this.
ANX-004  A shifted (offset-2) write carried no consent, and the firmware
         zeroed its TCP/UDP checksum field even for raw or unnegotiated
         frames.  The TX word's bit 13 (ZZ_TX_CSUM) is now set only on a
         shifted write whose TxFlags negotiated checksum offload; without
         it the firmware sends the frame as written.

Host tests: capacity from the register (present, absent, zero count), and
a shifted write with and without negotiated offload.  Pairs with firmware
that defines both (tinic/zz9000-firmware 617128a, 790f6bb and later).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: grm-mej.10 (+grm-mej.17): tmnt3 RAM bank stack and r6=r7+1 pairing hints
events.message:
grm-mej.10 (+grm-mej.17): tmnt3 RAM bank stack and r6=r7+1 pairing hints

Owner ruling (2026-10-06): absorb grm-mej.17; prove both through per-game
hints, not automatic proofs.

- New per-game keys banking.bank_stacks [{pointer, slots, provenance}] and
  banking.paired_fields [{high, low, offset, provenance}], plumbed like
  grm-mej.9's save_cells (GameCompiler, loader properties, DescriptorSupport,
  exporter, docs/SCHEMA.md, per-game-descriptors-design.md).
- BankStackBrackets: push/pop helpers recognized by shape over the hinted
  pointer/slot cells (entry stubs such as 86a5 LDA #$20 / BNE 86f9 included);
  each push must dominate the pops it reaches with no other push/pop, no
  pointer/slot write, and no outside entry into the region.
- At a verified pop the restored low field is the push-time bank only when it
  is fully known and carries a verified identity byte (tmnt3: even banks);
  the paired high field is COMPUTED as low + offset, never copied from the
  push-time high field. Otherwise unknown. 9169's pairing walk uses the same
