Generate initial version.

# SMS Game Designer

*Formerly "SMS Game Maker"; renamed because another tool already had that
name. Projects and autosaves from before the rename open as they are.*

A no-code environment for making Sega Master System games: Blockly for logic,
pixel editors for art, a compiler running as WASM, and an emulator to play
the result. Everything happens in the browser — no server, no accounts, no
install.

Ported from [`vcs-game-maker`](https://github.com/haroldo-ok/vcs-game-maker),
built on [CVBasic](https://github.com/nanochess/CVBasic) and
[gasm80](https://github.com/nanochess/gasm80), with the browser toolchain
from
[`CVBasic-emscripten`](https://github.com/haroldo-ok/CVBasic-emscripten).

## The idea

The Atari 2600 has five movable objects, so `vcs-game-maker` can name them
all: `player0`, `player1`, `missile0`, `missile1`, `ball`. The Master System
has 64 sprites, and a modest shmup has 25 things on screen at once. Naming
them is hopeless.

So this tool changes the unit of authoring:

> You author **types** — a Ship, a Bug, a Shot. The runtime owns the
> individual copies. Interactions are declared between **groups**, not
> between individuals.

Everything else follows from that. Scripts are written from the point of view
of one instance, so blocks say *set my x* and never name anything. Collision
is `on collide with enemy` on a type, and the tool derives the matrix — four
specialised tests for the worked shmup, not the 300 a named-object model
would need. Bullets and explosions can come and go, because lifetime finally
has somewhere to live.

## Why this backend

Everything must run in the browser, so the real question is not "which
console" but "which compiler can ship as a WASM blob, and which emulator can
ship next to it". CVBasic and gasm80 are two small, portable, file-in
file-out C programs — the same property that makes this kind of tool possible
at all. And the Master System needs no BIOS, so Play is one fetch lighter and
one caveat shorter than the alternatives.

The same project also builds for the SG-1000 — genuinely the same project,
with the instance counts brought inside the smaller machine and one line
changed. `examples/shmup-sg1000.json` is the worked shmup on a TMS9918: half
the pool, one 16x16 hardware sprite per actor instead of two 8x16 ones, one
colour per sprite instead of per pixel, and not a single change to any actor,
script or collision rule.

ColecoVision and MSX share that renderer and should be close. They are not
tested, so the roadmap says so.

## Getting started

```sh
npm install
npm run serve         # the compilers are already in public/wasm
```

The in-browser compilers ship prebuilt in `public/wasm/`. To rebuild them,
you need Zig, which installs from PyPI - no Emscripten SDK:

```sh
pip install ziglang==0.16.0
npm run wasm          # make -C toolchain wasm
```

To work headlessly — no browser, no WASM — you only need the native tools:

```sh
make -C toolchain native        # builds ./bin/cvbasic and ./bin/gasm80
npm run sample                  # writes examples/shmup.json
npm run rom                     # project JSON -> .bas -> .asm -> .sms
npm test                        # the whole suite: codegen, blocks, UI, playtests,
                                # and an end-to-end walk through the built editor
```

`npm test` also runs the block layer headlessly: Blockly works fine without a
DOM as long as nothing is injected into a page, so the tests build real block
trees, lower them, and compile the result to a ROM.

The suite does not stop at "it compiled". `tools/sms.py` is a headless
Master System — a real Z80 core plus enough VDP to render a frame — and
`tools/playtest.py` runs the built ROM on it and checks what a player would
notice: that the cast is on screen, that the pad moves the ship, that holding
fire spawns shots, that clearing a wave advances the room.

```sh
pip install z80 pillow
python3 tools/sms.py out/shmup.sms --frames 40 --png out/frame.png
python3 tools/playtest.py out/shmup.sms out/shmup.sym
```

That exists because the shmup once compiled cleanly, reported 91% of a frame,
passed every source-level test, and drew its entire cast as thin vertical
slivers.

`npm run rom` prints the whole accounting:

```
  out/shmup.bas  (705 lines)
  27 slots, 16/96 sprite defs, 42 collision checks/frame
  Frame 91% at worst case (sprites 34%, behaviours 24%, collision 31%)
  RAM 509/7966 bytes (6%)
  ROM out/shmup.sms  32768 bytes
```

## Layout

```
engine/          the CVBasic kernel, hand-written and versioned
  core.bas         entity pool and declarations (no executable code)
  kernel.bas       movement, animation, reaping, rendering
  terrain.bas      tile collision (only included when a room has a tilemap)

src/ir/          project model -> intermediate representation
  schema.js        project shape, target profiles, migration
  build-ir.js      slot ranges, collision matrix, VRAM and RAM planning
  lint.js          rules that run on every edit
  budget.js        frame budget, from measured cycle counts

src/generators/  IR -> CVBasic text
  blockly-lower.js          blocks -> statement AST
  cvbasic/emit-program.js   assembly and emission order
  cvbasic/emit-*.js         actors, collision, behaviours, rooms, assets

src/blocks/      Blockly definitions and the scoped toolboxes
src/components/  actor editor, sprite editor, Blockly host, budget meter
src/views/       Game / Actors / Rooms / Play / Code
src/workers/     the compiler Worker
examples/        a shmup, a platformer, an SG-1000 cut of the shmup, and a
                 coverage sample that uses every block in the language
tools/           headless build, sample generators, tests
  sms.py           a headless Master System, for looking at the screen
  playtest.py      runs the ROM and asserts what a player would see
  cycles.py        static Z80 cycle counter, for the frame budget
docs/            measurements and porting notes
```

## Budgets, not surprises

On this hardware the limits *are* the design, so they are visible while you
edit rather than after you wonder why the game crawls:

```
 Sprites  ████████░░  22/64 hw      RAM    ██░░░░░░░░   509/7966 B
 VRAM     ██░░░░░░░░  16/96 defs    ROM    ██████████  32.0/32 KB
 Slots    ███████░░░  27/40         Frame  █████████░  91%
```

Everything except ROM size comes from the IR with no compile. RAM comes
straight out of CVBasic, which prints its own accounting on every build. The
frame figure comes from cycle counts measured on the real generated Z80 —
see [docs/MEASUREMENTS.md](docs/MEASUREMENTS.md).

The same idea applies beyond performance. A platformer actor reports what its
jump actually reaches, because nobody can eyeball that from "jump strength
5":

```
 note  Hero jumps 33 px (4 tiles) and covers 54 px (6 tiles) in the air.
       Keep ledges within 3 tiles of each other.
```

When something is over budget the tool says what to do about it, with a
button that does it: *"enemy vs player_shot is 48 checks a frame. Checking it
every other frame halves that, and at these speeds it is not noticeable."* A
user cannot act on a number alone.

## Examples

**Open → Examples** in the editor offers three working games: *Bug Blaster*
(a shooter), *Cavern Run* (a platformer with tile terrain) and *Bug Blaster
SG* (the same shooter on the SG-1000). Their scripts open as real blocks you
can read and change. They are the same files the test suite builds and plays
on emulated hardware, so anything offered is known to work.

## What you get without doing anything

A new project already has the parts that make something feel like a game
rather than a demo: a title screen that waits for the button, a game over
that returns to it, five sound effects, and three tunes. Music takes two of
the four sound channels and effects take the other two, so they never cut
each other off.

None of it needs a tracker or an envelope editor. All of it is plain,
commented CVBasic in the exported source.

## Escape hatches

- **Export the ROM** and run it on real hardware or any emulator.
- **Export CVBasic source + engine** as a zip that builds standalone. The
  generated code is commented and meant to be read; that is the answer to
  every "can it also do X".
- **Export a playable HTML bundle** — ROM plus emulator plus a page.

CVBasic and gasm80 by Óscar Toledo G. (nanochess). EmulatorJS for the player.

events.title: emu: widen the owed-tail drain window to outlast scheduling
events.message:
emu: widen the owed-tail drain window to outlast scheduling

The drain that absorbs a timed-out command's late tail capped at 200 ms,
and the assertion that depends on it flaked on the macOS runner where a
shell's sleep 0.05 overshot that cap under load (the same race already
lost there once at 20 ms). The window is a cap, not a delay — the drain
returns on the first byte — so a tail that arrives promptly costs nothing;
only a genuinely late one waits it out. Widening it to 1500 ms gives the
test's 50 ms gap real margin against scheduler overshoot.

Same code passed macOS at the branch; the flake was load-induced timing,
not a regression.

events.title: fix(bdm): continue scanning after unused GPT entries
events.message:
fix(bdm): continue scanning after unused GPT entries

The GPT parser stops scanning the partition entry array when it encounters
an entry with a zero partition type GUID.

A zero type GUID marks that entry as unused; it does not indicate that the
remaining entries are unused. Continue scanning so valid partitions after
an unused entry can still be discovered.

Testing:
- Verify that a valid partition following an unused entry is discovered.
- Run the relevant PS2SDK build checks.

events.title: grm-mej.11: CalleeRegisterSummary -- per-callee A/X/Y preservation over p-code
events.message:
grm-mej.11: CalleeRegisterSummary -- per-callee A/X/Y preservation over p-code

A state-free forward fixpoint per callee entry over raw instruction p-code:
A/X/Y in {bot, Entry(R), top}, SP as Entry+k, stack slots by offset. A register
is preserved when every reachable RTS returns it holding its own entry value
with SP == Entry+2. Nested JSRs compose summaries recursively (recursion guard,
nesting cap 8, 2048-instruction cap); unresolved or banked-from-outside callees
clobber all registers. Abandons on TXS, join stack mismatch, caller-frame or
stack-aliasing stores, RTI/BRK/JMP(ind), undisassembled code, no return.

Chosen over SymbolicPropogator (does not track 8-bit parentless registers), the
p-code emulator (single concrete path) and the decompiler (runs after
BoardBankAnalyzer; no per-function unaffected inference). Design and rulings on
the bead.

Named assumptions, recorded in each Summary when relied on:
- StackDiscipline.CROSSED_CALL_IS_STACK_NEUTRAL (owner ruling O4)
- StackAssumption.INDIRECT_STORES_DO_NOT_WRITE_STACK_FRAME (owner ruling O3)

No production consumer yet (grm-mej.13 will be); full gate byte-identical.
CalleeRegisterSummaryProgramTest: 34 tests x 3 languages, incl. blmaster's real
e61b bytes (preserves X and Y, not A).

FitzBench: KB/s in 64 bits

(bytes / 1024) * E-clock rate wraps 32 bits above ~5.9 MB at 715,909 Hz,
so an 8 MB run on the A3000 printed 352 KB/s write / 532 read for runs
whose ticks give 1,316 / 2,034 (a 2 MB run in the same boot read 1,308 /
1,994).  Fixed build on the A3000, 8 MB: 1,310 / 2,002.  The CI runner's
512 KB default never reached the wrap, so its fitz-write baseline stands.

events.title: GROFRAMES: the receive-offload run length as an interface option
events.message:
GROFRAMES: the receive-offload run length as an interface option

The most TCP frames the SANA-II reader chains into one segment before TCP
sees it was AMI_SANA2_GRO_MAX, 16, at compile time.  GROFRAMES=1..16 sets
it per interface (0 or absent = 16, which stays the compile-time ceiling
and the array bound).  A shorter run reaches TCP's acknowledgment test
sooner, so a sender limited by the window is answered, and releases, in
smaller steps.

Measured on the A3000 (68060/50, X-Surf 100, switch flow control off,
RXBUFFER=49152, TCPACKMAX=2920), one build, 2026-10-05:

  GROFRAMES   LAN Mbit/s   overruns   25 ms path   overruns   burst
  16          19.1         310        4.0          77         9
  4           16.3         176        4.4          55         4
  2           13.2         127        8.2          15         2

with flow control on, defaults: 22.6 / 0 and 10.5 / 0.  The sender's
bursts shrink to the run length, but a drain's ACKs still leave
together, so the small bursts arrive as 20-30-frame trains under 1 ms
apart; this is a setting to experiment with, not a default change.

Host 554/554 with a config test (bounds, report line) and a sana2 test
that a GROFRAMES=4 run goes up at its fourth frame (fails with the
constant restored); local host and cross stages green.

events.message:
netdev: el3 claims a shared interrupt only for an enabled cause

el3_intr claimed the interrupt for any bit of EL3_S_INTS, which includes
RX_EARLY, INT_REQ and UPD_STATS.  el3_init enables only ADAPTER_FAIL,
TX_COMPLETE, TX_AVAIL and RX_COMPLETE in the interrupt mask, so the others
are reported in the status (read-zero mask 0xff) without raising INT.
UPD_STATS sets on its own as the statistics counters fill.  INT2 is shared
(the A1200's IDE, for one), and Exec stops the server chain at the first
server that claims, so the 3c589/3c556 server could claim another device's
interrupt.  Same class as the dp8390 fix.

el3_intr now loops only while an enabled cause is set (EL3_S_ENABLED, the
mask el3_init writes); masked causes are left untouched.

not acknowledged.  It fails both checks on the old code; all ok with the

events.title: netdev: dp8390 claims a shared interrupt only for an enabled bit
events.message:
netdev: dp8390 claims a shared interrupt only for an enabled bit

dp8390_intr claimed the interrupt whenever ISR was non-zero.  The IMR
enables only PRX, PTX, RXE, TXE and OVW; RDC, CNT and RST are set without
the chip asserting INT.  INT2 is shared (an accelerator's IDE, for one, on
the A3000 with a TF4060), and Exec stops the server chain at the first
server that claims, so a stale RDC made this server claim another
device's interrupt and skip the server whose device was asserting the line.

dp8390_intr now declines unless an enabled bit is set, and leaves the
status untouched when it declines; the remote DMA paths clear RDC before
they wait on it (ne2000.c:230, :332), and task-side remote DMA runs under
Disable().  The IMR is written from the same DP_INT_ENABLED mask.

test_netdev_dp8390: x_only_an_enabled_bit_claims_the_line (ISR = RDC|CNT|RST
is declined, not acknowledged, left set).  It fails 3 checks on the old
code; 152/152 pass with the fix.  netdev_dp8390_wait and netdev_ne2000 pass.

X-Surf 100 branch: PR 179 gates -- capacity hook pinned, receive helpers inlined, budgets

The PR's CI (run 37352269807 on 33bfdb15) failed four gates this branch
tripped; tools/ci.sh host stops at stage freshness locally, before them.

- check-call-abi: AmiSana2CapacityHook, a function-pointer type in a public
  header, carried no calling-convention pin.  The type, the declaration
  and definition of bsd_tcp_window_recap() and the host stub are now
  AMIGA_ASM_ARGS together.
- check-hot-calls: bsd_packet_extract(), bsd_iov_chunk() and
  bsd_iov_advance() fell out of line in the LTO image from 01000a73 on
  (main 97697d70 inlines all 18); the NetX window helpers grew their
  callers past the inliner's limits.  always_inline, as sana2_rx.c pins
  its own per-frame helpers; 18 of 18 inlined again.
- check-hotpath-budget: _nx_tcp_socket_state_data_check 493 -> 505, the
  receive pass's mark and the window-update test against the capped
  window (NetX 02604196), bought on purpose: the pass's end-of-burst ACK
  took the X-Surf's 25 ms path from 8.4 to 10.3 Mbit/s.
- check-ram-size: sizeof(AmiNetStack) +32 default (68868), +24 minimal
  (17952), +20 micro (16408): 12 bytes of receive-pass state in NX_IP and
  a 4-byte window cap per interface.

the movem drain reads (four longwords at port+0..+12), not one longword;
on the A3000's 68060 the drill passes 776/776 checks, the old fixture
failed 144.  The test_pool_window_host comment now names its figures'
source: main 97697d70 without flow control, AmiSpeedTest download, a boot
whose LAN runs overran the ring 410 times.

Host stage 554/554 and green (stage-freshness age raised to 30 days for

events.title: fix(sandbox): the harvest returns what the CPU stored into I/O space
events.message:
fix(sandbox): the harvest returns what the CPU stored into I/O space

Symptom: `trx64cli sandbox` harvested $D800-$DBE7 and $D018/$D020/$D021 as
all $00 under $01=$37, although writtenRuns listed those ranges. With $01=$34
the same stores were captured correctly. (C64RE issue #37, item 7.)

Cause: the harvest sliced the raw 64K `ram` array. A store to $D000-$DFFF with
I/O banked in lands in a chip and never reaches `ram`.

Fix: Observer gains `on_io_store(addr, value, pc)` (default no-op), fired from
the write path only when FullBus::wr_land == LAND_IO. The sandbox observer logs
the last value per I/O address (armed at entry, like writtenRuns). The harvest
overlays those values on the raw RAM slice: the CPU's value, no chip read-back,
low nibble for colour RAM $D800-$DBFF. Unwritten addresses and RAM under I/O
keep raw RAM; stores with I/O off were already right. JSON: each harvest (and
the back-compat `harvest`) gains `ioWritten: [[lo,hi],..]`; text output adds an
ioWritten note. Existing fields unchanged.

The walk, sprint, idle and the kneel transitions come from the Quaternius
Universal Animation Library (CC0 1.0, quaternius.com; pinned GitHub mirror

onto the MakeHuman A-pose. Every clip is grounded on the villager's own heel,
ball and toe-tip contact points; a gait's natural ground speed is measured off
the planted foot and the loop starts at the left foot's landing, so walk and
sprint share a phase (walk: heel first, roll, push-off over the toes; sprint:
the heel never lower than 4 cm). The UAL2 source is dropped again: it held

No freely licensed shovel clip is reachable, so dig (push in, lever, lift,
throw to the right) is authored in the pipeline: the shovel's path is keyed,
both hands are solved onto the shaft by IK — the right one lower, the tool
attached to it, the left one higher — with one smoothed lean through the
stroke. carry / carryIdle lay the shovel over the right shoulder, blade behind
and above. public/models/villager.glb holds body, morphs, skeleton and the

events.title: Name the Mockingboard's notes correctly, on PAL machines too
events.message:
Name the Mockingboard's notes correctly, on PAL machines too

Both Mockingboard windows took the AY's clock as 1,023,000 Hz, but a PAL
machine runs it at about 1.0179 MHz, so its notes, envelope ramp, noise
rate and VIA timer rate were all half a percent out and 288 of the 4,095
tone periods were given the wrong note. The native window now reads the
clock from the chip and the browser window from the machine's profile.

The browser window also named the note from the frequency rounded to a
whole Hz, which at low pitches is a large part of a semitone: 468 periods
took a neighbouring note's name (period 168 is F#4, shown as G4). It now
names it from the exact frequency. The native window shows a period of
zero as the chip plays it, as one.

events.title: Hold a button tap made in a short fall until the landing, to leap from it
events.message:
Hold a button tap made in a short fall until the landing, to leap from it

A leap that comes down lower than it took off ends with a fall of a
row or two.  The fall reads input every row, so a button tap queued
during the leap was spent on a fall read that ignores it, and the
landing walked a step instead of leaping.  On touch, a tap on the
other side during the fall was also taken as steering, which with
both sides down released the held side.

- The player step reads with a new `falling` policy while the fall
  would ignore the button: no shuba glide yet, and short of a
  knockdown fall.  It moves as `continuous` but leaves queued button
  presses for the landing read, which then leaps.  Recordings store
  what the game read, so replays are unaffected.
- SideTouch: while airborne, a finger on the other side from a held
  side is the button and the held side keeps steering.  Lifting the
  steering finger hands the steer to a remaining button finger, so
  thumb-to-thumb glide turns still work.

events.title: dat: implement C deserialization codegen, improve coverage (#3632)
events.message:
dat: implement C deserialization codegen, improve coverage (#3632)

A C library, tools/dat-cli/native, that reads the archives into the game's own types on any platform, from tables `melee-dat native codegen` writes from the DWARF. It's a port of the walk that converts as it goes, so `melee-dat native expect` and the library's trace must agree: they do for all 7048 archives on 64-bit and 32-bit little-endian and 32-bit big-endian (under qemu), and every converted object reads back against its data. The dat preset builds it with the host's compiler and runs its tests in ctest.

- the walk lays queued objects out as they were reached, so typedef tags
  apply (the CPU attack lists' DAT_TERMINATED was ignored)
- CPU attack tables typed (ftCo_AttackList); stage param types moved into
  their headers; stage param fields typed as their data
- 47 dat_symbols.txt aliases that read stage data as material animations
  removed
- generated C casts only between different types; untyped data typed from
  the fields that point to it
- `samples report --incomplete`, why units aren't complete
- a `native` dev shell with the DWARF/dat tools, qemu and a ppc32 cross
  compiler; the default shell is what CI needs
- clang-tidy's checks stay on src/: tools/ and the generated tables opt out

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* dat: native schema as descriptors per type, a file per header, enum type indices

`melee-dat native codegen` writes a directory instead of one tables.c:
each type is a named `dat_type_*` descriptor with its members, in
types/<header>.c for the header that declares it, along with what refers
to it (pointers, arrays); roots are in roots/<module>.c; DAT_TYPE_* and
DAT_NAME_* are enums. Descriptors use designated initializers, refer to
types by name and keep expressions next to their members, with the
annotation as written in a comment where it isn't plain.

- dat/schema.h: the schema's types and the macros descriptors are written
  in; DAT_NONE is 0, so every field defaults to zero
- members, expressions, scripts, binds and roots are pointers, not ranges
  of shared tables; macros expand to a depth when evaluated
- the schema is generated when configuring, again when its inputs change
- codegen split into generator.rs (the rows) and emit.rs (the C)

events.title: The OAM image is cleared at boot and at every level load
events.message:
The OAM image is cleared at boot and at every level load

Two reports off a physical DMG, one class: a byte the ROM reads before it
writes. An emulator powers OAM and WRAM up as zeros, so every check here
passed; a DMG powers them up with whatever the cells held.

BlitOam copies OAM_BYTES out of wOamShadow every VBlank and OAM_BYTES
stops at the duck, so entries 32..39 are never written on any level, and
the draws skip the slots a level does not use. OAM is in screen
coordinates and nothing scrolls it, so a leftover entry is a sprite pinned
to the screen -- the stray glyphs of the first report. wOnNotice was the
second and worse: HandleVBlank tests it with the front-end flags and skips
the whole draw pass while it is set, and the title's START reaches the
first level without going through ShowNotice, so that level ran on the
powered-on byte: no camera, no sprites, no status row.

Start now zeroes the shadow, all 40 OAM entries and wOnNotice with the LCD
off. Then the second report showed the same bug one level later and not a
power-on bug at all: only Start ever cleared the image, so a level that
used fewer slots than the one before it inherited its birds and platforms
for good -- a game over at level 3, and level 1 came up with level 3's
third hen and a lift. The clear is now the routine ClearOamShadow, called
from LoadLevel, which every level arrives through, and DrawLifts' hide path
hides both platforms instead of one (four entries, not two).

tools/verify_init.py checks all three against a machine that powered up
dirty; tools/sweep_wram.py (make sweep) is the tool for the next one of
these.

events.title: net68k: four longwords per movem in the summed 32-bit port drain
events.message:
net68k: four longwords per movem in the summed 32-bit port drain

n68k_port_in_l_sum read the mirrored window one move.l per longword and
summed it with ADD/ADDX.  It now takes four longwords per movem.l a1@ --
the back-to-back reads n68k_port_in already makes from the same window --
stores them with one movem, and sums the four data registers; the
remainder (up to three) keeps the single-read loop.  The sum convention is
unchanged: every ADD has its ADDX before the loop's SUBQ touches X, and
movem and lea leave X alone.

Why: on the A3000 (68060/50, X-Surf 100 in Zorro III) this drain was 33.6%
of a full-speed receive, averaging ~590 ns a longword against ~400 ns for
a bare read of the card (SYS:T/Z3Lat), so the instructions around each
read were a measurable part of it.

A3000, PAUSE agreed, batching on, same library, control = this tree with
the old routine:

                   control         movem
  LAN receive      22.13-22.19     22.44-22.58   (+1.5%, 6 runs)
  25 ms receive    10.44           10.50-10.51   (4 of 5 runs; one 6.31
                                                  run lost packets on the
                                                  path from its start --
                                                  sender cwnd 24 -> 5, 0
                                                  ring overruns)
  transmit         11.0-11.7       11.8-12.0
  checksum errors  0               0   (~120,000 frames VERIFIED through
                                        this sum)

events.title: feat(minigl): composite plugin frames from imported dma-bufs (#2382)
events.message:
feat(minigl): composite plugin frames from imported dma-bufs (#2382)

* feat(minigl): composite plugin frames from imported dma-bufs

When AMIBERRY_MINIGL_ZEROCOPY=1, the MiniGL plugin (companion PR
amiberry-minigl-plugin#3) exports each presented frame as a dma-buf
instead of encoding it into the Picasso96 span. The transport
registers the optional image sink after plugin load; the OpenGL
renderer imports the fd on its own EGLDisplay (resolved from libEGL at
runtime - no new build-time dependency) and composites the frame
directly, so the per-frame surface upload and the plugin's glReadPixels
both disappear.

The imported image is cached until the plugin announces a change, the
surface path remains the fallback whenever no image is live, and the
path is skipped entirely for non-RTG screens. With the flag off the
build is byte-identical in behavior; shader stacks (preset, external,
crtemu) still run for RTG screens without a live export but are
bypassed while one is showing.

Measured on the RPi4 rig (GLQuake timedemo1 640x480, same binary):
57.7 fps with the flag off vs 70-73 fps on, +22-26% guest frame rate.

* fix(minigl): review fixes for the dma-buf composite

- The imported EGLImageKHR handle was never stored, so cleanup never
  destroyed imported images; backing buffers leaked per handover.
- The registry now duplicates the dma-buf fd while the sink callback
  holds the plugin's serialization, closing the window where the next
  handover could close or recycle the descriptor between the snapshot
  and eglCreateImageKHR. The renderer imports from the owned dup.
- The sink is only registered when the OpenGL renderer is live: with a
  software or SDL backend, registration would make the plugin skip span
  updates that nothing would display.

Also removes the diagnostic back/front buffer probe used to verify the
scanout during bring-up. Re-verified on the rig: both buffers carry
live frame colors through a full timedemo, 71.7 fps zero-copy vs 57.5
flags-off on the same binaries.

* fix(minigl): renderer-published importer gate, owned snapshot dup, libretro link

Review round two plus CI:

- The renderer now publishes once, under its own current context, whether
  dma-buf frames can actually be imported (an EGL display with
  EGL_EXT_image_dma_buf_import and the entry points). Sink registration
  is gated on that flag instead of the C++ backend type, so a GLX or
  SDL-only window system keeps the plugin on the span path instead of
  exporting frames nobody can show.
- minigl_display_current() returns a fresh dup taken under the registry
  lock; the renderer closes it after the import attempt. The registry's
  own descriptor could previously be closed by the next handover between
  the snapshot and eglCreateImageKHR.
- libretro builds compile service_transport.cpp without the OpenGL
  renderer, so the old get_opengl_renderer() gate broke their link; the
  flag removes the dependency and libretro/Makefile gains
  minigl_display.cpp. Verified: full libretro core builds and links on
  aarch64 Linux again.

* fix(minigl): define destroy_minigl_import on non-Linux platforms too

It sat inside the __linux__ guard while destroy_context() calls it
unconditionally, which left FreeBSD, macOS and Windows builds with an
undefined symbol at link time. The definition now lives outside the
guard with its body still Linux-only.

* fix(libretro): compile gl_context_ladder.cpp in the core build

The ladder lookup from the KMSDRM context fix (a4efa20c) was added to
CMake's source list only. libretro's Makefile never compiled it, and
while GNU ld drops the unresolved reference with section GC (the core
never calls set_opengl_attributes), mingw's lld reports it - so the
Windows libretro job has failed since that merge. Adds the translation
unit next to the other osdep sources; the Linux core build is verified
to still link with it.

* fix(minigl): review round three - fd leaks, probe strictness, sink lifetime

- The import-failure return skipped the snapshot fd close; every retry
  leaked another descriptor. All exits from render_minigl_dmabuf close
  the owned duplicate now.
- The capability probe requires EGL_EXT_image_dma_buf_import_modifiers
  (the import attributes carry a modifier) and GL_OES_EGL_image on the
  GL context (resolved via SDL_GL_GetProcAddress, enumerated with
  glGetStringi), so a context that cannot bind the imported image never
  stops the span updates.
- Importer capability is reference counted per renderer instance and
  re-probed when the context is rebuilt: amiberry recreates the window
  context during startup, and the previous static/global flag handling
  left registration seeing no importer (observed as a silent fall back
  to span mode). When the last capable context goes away the image is
  dropped and the sink unregistered, so the plugin resumes span updates.

* fix(minigl): retryable sink install, RTG-scoped importer references

- Context recreation unregisters the sink when the last capable context
  goes, but the plugin stays loaded and the installation guard stayed
  set, leaving zero-copy off for the rest of the process. Installation
  now retries from the dispatch path whenever an importer is ready, and
  the registry allows reinstalling after the last reference drops.
- Importer references are held only by renderers presenting the
  Picasso96 screen, so a native-screen monitor staying capable cannot
  keep the sink installed while the RTG display falls back to SDL and
  the plugin keeps skipping span updates nobody consumes.

Verified on the rig: both boot contexts publish capability, the sink
installs once the RTG importer is live, 72.1 fps timedemo.

* fix(minigl): serialize install, reconcile the transport flag, probe after make-current

- maybe_install_zero_copy now runs under the plugin mutex the same way
  every other plugin interaction does; the trap workers in indirect
  UAE-board mode could previously race the first install and the sink
  state.
- The transport's sink_installed flag is reconciled against the
  registry: a release that removed the sink no longer leaves the flag
  latched, so a recreated context can reinstall.
- The capability probe moved after SDL_GL_MakeCurrent and is taken only
  by renderers presenting the Picasso96 screen: the one-shot verdict
  previously described whatever context happened to be current, and a
  capable native-screen monitor could keep the sink installed while the
  RTG display fell back to SDL.

Verified: capability published once the RTG context presents, sink
installs under the mutex, 73.0 fps timedemo on the rig.

* fix(minigl): failed-import memo, registry install/release locking

Self-review findings before merge:

- A runtime eglCreateImageKHR rejection retried and logged on every
  presented frame while the plugin kept suppressing span updates. The
  rejected export's sequence number is now remembered: no retry, no
  repeat logging, the span fallback simply stays for that export.
- Sink install/release mutated g_installed and g_set_image_sink without
  the registry mutex, and install could race the release path's
  uninstall into a dead sink with the flags claiming active (or install
  with zero importers, freezing span updates). Both now decide under
  the mutex with the plugin setter invoked outside it (the plugin holds
  its own mutex around the sink callback; opposite orders deadlock),
  and install refuses when no importer reference exists.

72.4 fps zero-copy, 57.7 flags-off on the rig.

* feat(minigl): zero-copy on by default with minigl_zerocopy option

The dmabuf composite no longer needs AMIBERRY_MINIGL_ZEROCOPY=1: the
new minigl_zerocopy config option defaults to true, and the env var
becomes an explicit override ("1" on, "0" off) for one-off runs and
troubleshooting. Registration still requires a verified importer, so
builds and window systems without one keep the span path untouched.

Closes the two blockers that kept it opt-in:

- create_screenshot() refreshes the Picasso96 span through the plugin's
  optional minigl_plugin_materialize_all before reading the surface, so
  screenshots capture current pixels while image mode holds. The
  actionable-screenshot path gets the same refresh.
- The composite is claimed by one renderer: on hosts with several
  Picasso96 monitors only the claiming monitor shows the plugin's
  image; the others keep their own span content instead of receiving
  the plugin's frame.

Verified on the rig: 72.8 fps timedemo with no environment variables,
opt-out via env yields span mode (no imports), 223-check plugin suite
green.

events.title: Declare the NDIX DIT base so the MMU knows a DIT is configured
events.message:
Declare the NDIX DIT base so the MMU knows a DIT is configured

Since 1b6582e the MMU, the trap code and the DIT accessors test
cpu->dit_configured, not DITBASE != 0, because zero is a valid DIT base. The NDIX
boot stored DITBASE directly, so the flag stayed clear and every segment fell back
to the emulator's shadow tables. The kernel then drew its page tables from the
emulator-private allocation window, which ran out ("[PHYS] out of
emulator-private memory ... window is 0x00000800..0x00280000") and stopped on
"No data capability" for segment 4 at the first read of its page-table window.

nd500_ndix_mmu_setup() now calls nd500_mmu_declare_dit_base(), which sets both.
Found by bisecting: the NDIX boot reached login: at 0d3d4d8 and failed at
1b6582e. With this change alone 1b6582e boots again.
events.author: Ronny Hansen

events.title: Give the MMU probe the same zero-capability answer as the real walk
events.message:
Give the MMU probe the same zero-capability answer as the real walk

invoke_trap_handler() checks that a trap handler is resident with
nd500_mmu_peek_space(), since 952441d (it used nd500_mmu_translate() before).
translate() maps an address through the flat-loaded kernel image when a segment's
capability is zero and the address lies inside RAM, with the I/D de-aliasing for
data; peek returned "unmapped" for the same address. NDIX's low-memory trap
handler (address 0x381, segment 0, capability 0 in the shadow table) therefore
looked "not resident", and the CPU reported a page fault on the handler instead of
dispatching it: "[STOP] page fault at PC=0x000006C4 data=0x00000381" right after
"using 344 buffers".

The fallback is now one function, mmu_flat_image_physical(), called by both
translate and peek, so a probe cannot disagree with the walk it stands in for.
It still applies only when no trap sink is attached, exactly as before.

Found by bisecting with the DIT declaration applied: 46d827f boots, 952441d
stops. With both changes NDIX reaches login: three runs out of three and the
nd500x test suite passes, 47 of 47.

events.title: Move ndmonlib to the commit where 503B DVINST reads device 0 from the command buffer
events.message:
Move ndmonlib to the commit where 503B DVINST reads device 0 from the command buffer

A bare "NC" in the monitor shell printed its banner and then swallowed every
line typed: NC reads logical device 0 with MON 503B, which had no device 0 case,
while the shell's device-0 refill (cf13652) put the typed line into a command
buffer that 503B never read. ndmonlib f77cdbd makes 503B take device 0 from the
command buffer exactly as 1B does, so NC now gets a lone CR at once and prints
"NC:". The shell is unchanged; the refill is still what feeds 1B callers.

The pin also moves past about ten ndmonlib commits that are site, documentation
and test changes plus small handler edits (317B among them). The nd500x test
suite passes at the new pin, 47 of 47, including dom_nc_compiler and
dom_nc_compile_a/b.

events.title: Merge branch 'demo-feedback': what a demo asked of the library
events.message:
Merge branch 'demo-feedback': what a demo asked of the library

A demo built on STDL measured where the library cost it frames and
what it had to write for itself; this is the library's answer, tested
in Hatari and on a real Mega STE at 8 and 16MHz.

- The gcc 4.6 multiply trap, durably: stdl_math.h (16-bit multiply and
  divide on the 68000's own instructions, and STDL_FixDiv), and the
  build's libcallcheck, which fails on any new libgcc arithmetic call.
- STDL_FillPolygon: convex polygons set, XORed, ORed or cleared into a
  colour's planes, shared edges tiling exactly; inside the clip, a
  68000 path from vertices to rows. Within 12% of the demo's own
  filler at full vertical resolution, at the same frame rate.
- Rasters on Timer B (STDL_OpenRasters and family), sharing the timer
  safely with the borders; palette staging (STDL_StagePalette); music
  from memory, seekable, with its registers readable for meters;
  STDL_BlitSprites and STDL_DirtyWholeGroups for scenes of bobs.
- Faster pre-shifted sprites, whole-group fills, aligned text, chunky
  conversion, pre-shifting and dirty restores.
- Fixed on the hardware: a program that inited without a video mode
  left the machine at 60Hz on exit (since v1.10.0).

events.title: Let the ND-5000 runner be driven from the host main loop where there are no threads
events.message:
Let the ND-5000 runner be driven from the host main loop where there are no threads

Under __EMSCRIPTEN__ ndbus_runner_start() used to refuse, so an ND-5000 could
never execute in a browser. It now creates no thread: it marks the runner
RUNNING, and the host calls the new ndbus_runner_pump(runner, max_steps) to run
the CPU on the calling thread. The state machine (IDLE, RUNNING, STOPPING,
STOPPED), the stop handshake and join behave as they do with a thread; a step
that returns false, or a requested stop, ends in STOPPED, and join returns the
runner to IDLE.

Natively nothing changes: the thread code is untouched and ndbus_runner_pump()
is a stub that returns 0, so a host may call it unconditionally.
events.author: Ronny Hansen

events.title: Make the octobus tick free until an ND-5000 monitor starts, and run the CPU on WASM
events.message:
Make the octobus tick free until an ND-5000 monitor starts, and run the CPU on WASM

The octobus card's tick runs once per ND-100 instruction. It called
mfbus_service_nd5000_mailboxes() every time, and that took the bus mutex even
with no ND-5000 present.

- mfbus_tick_work is one flag word (frame waiting for the ND-100, station scan
  wanted, a monitor started, a CPU to run). The tick tests it inline and makes
  no call and takes no lock when it is zero. A frame sent through the card sets
  the scan bit; the scan finds which stations have a mailbox (start_mess set),
  and only those are polled.
- mfbus_nd5000_armed_mask() and mfbus_nd5000_running_mask() say which stations
  have a mailbox and which CPUs are running, for any number of stations.
- The card recomputes its interrupt line only when a request is pending or the
  line is high, and counts down I/O delays only when one is in flight.
- WebAssembly has no host threads. Under __EMSCRIPTEN__ a started CPU is run
  from the tick through ndbus_runner_pump(), 8 ND-5000 instructions per ND-100
  instruction (a scheduling choice, not a measured ratio), and
  mfbus_quiesce_runner() no longer waits for a thread that does not exist.
  Natively the runner thread is unchanged and the pump mask is never set.

Release build, 100M instructions, minimum user time: no ND-5000 hardware
7.8 s, card only 8.05 s, card plus a configured idle ND-5000 8.1 s.
Needs the nd500x runner change (ndbus_runner_pump) in the same pin.

events.title: Load the floppy catalog and images from the Norsk Data software archive on GitHub
events.message:
Load the floppy catalog and images from the Norsk Data software archive on GitHub

The F12 menu, the md5:/dir: catalog mounts, tools/nd100x_expect.py and both
browser UIs read catalog/floppies.json from the RetroCoreLabs
norskdata-software-archive repository (raw.githubusercontent.com) instead of
ndlib.hackercorp.no.

The archive differs from the old catalog in two ways. The records are camelCase
with the file list as structured data (ndfs, dosFiles, backupFiles) and no
DirectoryContent text, and every image is a gzip file at
images/<md5>/<name>.img.gz, 36 of them with spaces or ampersands in the name.

- floppydb_parse_record() converts one record: name, description, product
  reference, md5, percent-encoded image URL and a generated directory listing.
  Drive type comes from imageSizeBytes (more than 1000 pages of 2048 bytes is
  SMD). Records without storage.git.imagePath are skipped. The F12 menu and
  floppydb_load_json() share it.
- New src/ndlib/gunzip.c is a self-contained gzip decoder with no zlib
  dependency, because the Windows, WASM and RISC-V builds have none. It checks
  the CRC-32 and size in the trailer. machine_mount_drive() unpacks a URL that
  ends in .gz. Output was byte-identical to gzip -dc on all 1102 archive images.
- The catalog cache is now floppies-archive.json so an old-format cache is
  never read as the new layout.
- The browser UIs unpack with DecompressionStream, and escape ' and & in the
  per-floppy attribute that carries the disk data.
- tests/test_floppydb.c uses a fixture in the archive layout and checks the URL
  encoding and the generated listing.

events.title: fix(net): gate the RX ready count on firmware 2.1 and cover review cases
events.message:
fix(net): gate the RX ready count on firmware 2.1 and cover review cases

Firmware before 2.1 maps register 0x8C to the zzdebug test counter, not
the RX ready count, so the repeated-serial rule now reads it only when
FW_VERSION reports 2.1 or later. A repeated serial 0 always waits:
firmware never starts a post-restart sequence at 0 and handshake
firmware rejects an ack of 0, so delivering it would loop on a corrupt
slot.

The status register and firmware version now come from the shared
include/zz9000_hw.h map instead of a second definition in rx.h. The
known limit of serial reuse (a restart during a payload copy can let
the ack consume the new frame) is documented at the model contract.

The firmware model now covers 2.0.x, 2.1/2.2 and 2.8 behaviour; new
tests pin the 2.1 serial-1 restart, the version gate, the re-read
mismatch, the ready mask width, serial 0, bad-size drops and the
large-gap BadData path. Also drops the unused zznet_read_word and adds
the shared headers to the device's make prerequisites.

PGCHK: a sampled default for the machine, the full run for Hatari

Hatari under fast-forward had shown 84 seconds: the reference's exact
arithmetic per row and pixel, not the fill. It now checks 30 random
polygons by default, with every fixed case, and -DPGCHK_FULL keeps the

sampled run still has the deeply clipped one - which is what catches a
broken clipped-start multiply in the sampled build, checked in Hatari.

events.title: fix(net): detect RX restarts from the firmware ready count
events.message:
fix(net): detect RX restarts from the firmware ready count

The previous rule only treated a repeated serial as new after the framer
had read an empty slot. A firmware restart and its first frame can land
between the framer's ack and its next header read, so the cleared slot
is never seen and the RX livelock remains.

The serial ack completes on the bus only after firmware handled it, so
a header still carrying the acked serial is either a stale slot on
firmware that never clears slots, or a new frame after a restart. The
ETH_RX_STATUS ready count separates them: the frame is new when
firmware reports frames waiting and the header is unchanged on re-read.
Firmware before 2.1 has neither restarts nor that register (reads 0),
so it keeps the old behavior.

events.title: STDL_Init: a program that never sets a rate leaves the sync alone
events.message:
STDL_Init: a program that never sets a rate leaves the sync alone

A Mega STE came back to its desktop at 60Hz after a test program.
stdl.old_sync is -1 for "never changed", but STDL_Init zeroes the
state and only STDL_SetVideoMode set it to -1 again, so every program
that inited without a video mode wrote 0 into $FFFF820A on its way
out: 60Hz. Games set a video mode, which is presumably why no port
noticed; probes and tools do not. In since STDL_SetRefresh (v1.10.0).

STDL_Init sets it to -1 after the memset. SYNCCHK is the check, on
the machine because tests/host does not link video.c: init and quit
alone, a video mode, and STDL_SetRefresh to the other rate, each
against the rate before. Hatari, plain ST: sync 2 before, 0 after all
three without the fix; 2 after each with it.

events.title: fix(net): deliver the first frame after a firmware RX restart
events.message:
fix(net): deliver the first frame after a firmware RX restart

Since rev 2.2 the framer keeps old_serial across empty slots. A firmware
DMA restart (Amiga reset, MAC update, TX-timeout recovery) resets the
frame serial to 2, so when the last frame consumed before the restart
was also serial 2, the next frame looked already consumed: the framer
never acked it and re-armed the IRQ, which firmware raised again for
the pending backlog, forever.

After an empty slot, the next non-empty header is a new frame even if
its serial matches: firmware clears a slot before its read cursor moves
on, so a consumed frame cannot reappear after an empty read.

The slot classification moves to net/rx.c so the host suite can drive
it against a model of the firmware backlog ring.

events.title: cp_asm.s: write the encrypted track check as decrypted code; encrypt at build
events.message:
cp_asm.s: write the encrypted track check as decrypted code; encrypt at build

checkCopyProt's 96 encrypted bytes were carried as .dc.b.  They are
now the instructions they decrypt to: the routine that scans the raw
track for the $a1 sync run and the $fe ID mark of track 79, then
counts the $ff gap bytes before it (fewer than 15 sets d3 bit 0, 80 or
more bit 1; both are needed to pass).

The key is $1567: cpsetp clears d0 and calls the cpsum chain, which
only adds constants.  The header's 'keyed by the current drive number'
was wrong and is corrected.

tools/cp_encrypt.py runs in alcyon_link.sh right after as68: it finds
cpenc..cpencend through the object's symbol table, checks the block is
the 48 words cpsetp's dbf covers, and adds the key to each word.  It
refuses to encrypt twice.  as68 reproduces the decrypted bytes exactly
(cmp.b #$4f,d6 stays the immediate cmp, not cmpi), and nothing in the
block is relocated.

events.title: feat(image): standalone executables -- (ext:save-image f :executable t)
events.message:
feat(image): standalone executables -- (ext:save-image f :executable t)

SAVE-IMAGE gains :EXECUTABLE, :TOPLEVEL and :HEAP-SIZE.  With
:EXECUTABLE T the file is a copy of the running clamiga with the image
appended and a 20-byte trailer at its end: one file that is the program,
with no lib/, no image file and no launcher beside it.

clamiga looks at its own tail before it parses its command line.  With a
trailer there the whole command line is the program's
(EXT:*COMMAND-LINE-ARGS*, verbatim), the user init file is skipped, the
:TOPLEVEL function runs after the restore hooks and its end is the
process's: 0 on return, n after (quit n), 1 after an unhandled error.
Without :TOPLEVEL the executable starts at the REPL.  A damaged
executable refuses to start instead of becoming a REPL.

AmigaOS LoadSeg reads hunks to the end of the file and refuses raw bytes
there (ERROR_BAD_HUNK), so the 68k build wraps image and trailer in a
HUNK_DEBUG; ELF (MorphOS, Linux), Mach-O and PE take them as they are.
A Workbench-started process has no program name: the executable path
falls back to the tool name of the WBStartup message, and wbrun now sets
PROGDIR: as Workbench does.

The option parser's early exits release the platform file table the
look at the tail opened (early_exit).  `make linux-test` installs
libffi-dev, without which the host build never compiled there.

Tests: tests/test_executable.sh (make test + gc-stress leg), five
scenarios in test_memleak_tracked.sh, tests/amiga/exe-save.lisp (Shell
and Workbench start, verify-amiga).  Run on macOS, Linux (Ubuntu 24.04
container), FS-UAE 68040 and the MorphOS box; Windows only by CI.

events.title: MEGA65 R3/R3A support (test): ST RAM, TOS and cartridge in block RAM
events.message:
MEGA65 R3/R3A support (test): ST RAM, TOS and cartridge in block RAM

The R3/R3A has no SDRAM. bram_m65.v replaces sdram_m65.v with the same
chipset interface and bus cycle timing (data at t = 6), using 224 RAMB36

events.title: Take a pending enabled trap when an ND-5000 process becomes active
events.message:
Take a pending enabled trap when an ND-5000 process becomes active

When SINTRAN restarts a process, a trap that is already pending in its
status and enabled is now taken before the process's next instruction
runs. mfbus_resume_runner() marks the activation; the first step of the
new host thread calls check_pending_traps() with the instruction about
to run as the trapping P, so the handler's RETT comes back to it.

ND-500 Reference Manual ND-05.009.4, status register, PRT: "If the PRT
trap is enabled, the trapped process will immediately be interrupted and
its trap handler invoked. If the process is not in the active state, as
soon as it becomes active the trap will occur."

ND-500 Loader Monitor ND-60.136.04A, MON 505B GERRCOD: "When the swapper
process detects a fatal error (e.g., outside segment), it will cause a
Programmed Trap (PRT) in the user process. GERRCOD may be used within the
trap handler to obtain the error code from the swapper."

MEASURED on LINKER-B01 under SINTRAN. Its clear loop at P=0xB00242E5
reads a never-written page (0x08602800) of the output domain file, which
it connected with MON 412B access type 1. The swapper does not serve the
read; SINTRAN restarts the linker with status bit 29 set, and the linker
has bit 29 enabled in OTE1.
- Before: the read ran again first and faulted again, the swapper counted
  ten faults at one address, and the monitor printed NO SUCH PAGE. The
  reference emulator ends the same way.
- After: P goes 0xB00242E5 -> the linker's handler 0xB005569D, the
  handler calls MON 505B, a write fault on the page follows (which the
  swapper serves), and the read is retried. The trap was taken five times
  in the C link and once in the PLANC link.

Result on a scratch pack, compiled with NC-A06 and PLANC-500-G00 and
linked with LINKER-B01, all under SINTRAN:
  ND-5000: HELLO      ->  HELLO FROM C!   program HELLO terminated
  ND-5000: PHELLO     ->  HELLO FROM PLANC!

Needs the nd500x commit "Take no end-of-instruction trap for an
instruction a memory fault aborted".

events.title: Hold the servicer's engine lock from the park mark to the answer
events.message:
Hold the servicer's engine lock from the park mark to the answer

The ND-5000 thread now takes nd500x's engine lock before it marks a
process as parked and holds it until the trap or monitor-call answer has
been written; a refused monitor call is undone inside the lock. Needs the
nd500x commit "Serialize the mailbox chain walk against trap and
monitor-call answers", which adds ndbus_engine_lock().

The lock is taken BEFORE the "leaving" mark is set. The ND-100 thread
holds the same lock while it works through a mailbox chain, and a start
inside that walk waits for a thread that is marked as leaving. With the
mark set first, this thread could sit waiting for the lock with the mark
already up, and the walk would wait for it in turn.

MEASURED without the lock: PLANC-500-G00's first page fault was declined
("no message recorded for X5CPU 1") because it arrived while the walk
that started the process was still running. With it, PLANC starts and
compiles ("11 LINES COMPILED. 0 DIAGNOSTICS.").

access type 1 (uninitialized, empty file) for the output domain, and
access type 2 for the two files it reads.

events.title: Serialize the mailbox chain walk against trap and monitor-call answers
events.message:
Serialize the mailbox chain walk against trap and monitor-call answers

The ND-100 thread works through a mailbox chain while the ND-5000 thread
may be answering a trap or a monitor call on a message. The reference
holds one lock in all three
($RETROCORE/Emulated.HW/ND/CPU/ND500/Servicer/Nd500MicrocodeServicer.cs,
_engineLock in ProcessChain, AnswerTrapStop and AnswerMonitorCallStop).
This servicer had none.

ndbus_engine_lock() / ndbus_engine_unlock() are new, in ndbus_lock.c. A
second mutex, not the bus mutex, because the servicer calls the semaphore
and queue helpers (which take the bus mutex) while it holds this one; the
order is always engine lock first. It is recursive, so a host can hold it
around "mark the process parked, then answer" while the answer functions
take it themselves.

MEASURED without it, PLANC-500-G00 started by name under SINTRAN: the
chain walk handed a 23B start to the host, the new ND-5000 thread
page-faulted on its first instruction (P=0x0800065C) and asked for the
trap to be answered BEFORE the walk had recorded the message for that
process. The log read "mailbox trap-stop DECLINED trap=46B ... no message
recorded for X5CPU 1", SINTRAN was told nothing, and the compiler never
printed its banner. With the lock PLANC starts and compiles.

test_ndbus.c: a start whose host creates a thread that faults at once
while the walk is still inside the start; the fault must be answered on
the process's own message.
events.author: Ronny Hansen

events.title: Take no end-of-instruction trap for an instruction a memory fault aborted
events.message:
Take no end-of-instruction trap for an instruction a memory fault aborted

With a trap sink attached, an instruction aborted by a page fault or a
protect violation now skips check_solo_timeout() and
check_pending_traps(). The reference returns from the step at that point:
"CheckPendingTraps must NOT run - delivering an end-of-instruction
ignorable trap for an instruction that never completed would report a
fault the hardware never raises"
($RETROCORE/Emulated.HW/ND/CPU/ND500/CpuND500.Execute.cs:716-722).
A free-running CPU (no sink) is unchanged.

MEASURED on LINKER-B01 under SINTRAN. The linker reads a never-written
page of its output file (P=0xB00242E5, address 0x08602800). The swapper
cannot serve the read and SINTRAN restarts the linker with status bit 29,
Programmed Trap, set. The restarted instruction faulted again, and
check_pending_traps() then entered the linker's own handler from inside
that half-reported fault: the page fault was never reported back to
SINTRAN, and the linker printed a register dump, "ND-500 TRAP: (7641B)
ILLEGAL INSTRUCTION CODE" and "ND LINKER abortion".

This change alone makes the lane behave as the reference does (ten faults
at one address, then NO SUCH PAGE). What the machine does instead - take
the pending trap when the process becomes active, before the instruction
- is done by the host; see the nd100x commit "Take a pending enabled trap
when an ND-5000 process becomes active".

test_fault_record.c case 6: a Programmed Trap pending and enabled, an
instruction that page-faults. No sink: unchanged. Sink: the step stops on
the page fault, P is not vectored, the trap stays pending; and
check_pending_traps() called for the activation enters the handler with
the faulted instruction as the return address.

events.title: Fix the A key: work around a Vivado synthesis bug in keyboard.vhd (issue #1)
events.message:
Fix the A key: work around a Vivado synthesis bug in keyboard.vhd (issue #1)

Vivado 2026.1 turned the first call of the process-local procedure
map_key (which wrote the process variable m and read key_pressed_n
implicitly) into a constant: the ST matrix key A (column 4, row 5) was
always pressed, so the IKBD never saw a new press of A. There was no
warning, and GHDL/Verilator simulate the code correctly. Moving another
key to the first call broke that key instead.

map_key now takes the matrix and the key state as explicit parameters.
A standalone synthesis of keyboard.vhd shows that only matrix bit 37
changes (it is a register again); confirmed on a MEGA65 R6.

Also add the JTAG keyboard probe used to find this (USER3: ST matrix,
the last bytes the CPU read from the keyboard ACIA, press counters;
tools/probe3.tcl + decode3.py) and A/S cases in the GHDL keyboard test.

events.title: hardware: Handle probe faults on 68010 and later CPUs
events.message:
hardware: Handle probe faults on 68010 and later CPUs

The existing guard assumes a 68000 exception frame and a vector table
at address zero. Extend it for hardware probes on later processors.

Use the active VBR on 68010 and later CPUs and recover through a saved
supervisor stack pointer instead of modifying the fault frame. Mask
interrupts while the handlers are installed and restore the vectors
before returning. Flush the 68060 branch cache on prediction errors,
retrying when no other fault is present.

Add a longword probe alongside the byte probe and publish results only
after successful reads have left the protected supervisor section.

events.title: Decide MOVB's direction on byte positions and read the source half with the source's bit
events.message:
Decide MOVB's direction on byte positions and read the source half with the source's bit

Two defects in MOVB (140131), both already fixed in the reference
($RETROCORE/Emulated.HW/ND/CPU/ND100/Instructions.ByteInstruction.cs,
"FIX A" and "FIX B", 2026-08-21):

A. The source byte half was selected with the DESTINATION's half bit
   ((i + d_lr) & 1), although the source word on the line above is picked
   with s_lr. Wrong whenever the two fields start on different halves.
   MOVBF (140132) had the same line and gets the same change.

B. The copy direction came from the word addresses only. With source and
   destination in the same word on different halves the branch was an
   empty TODO and the copy ran ascending, so a field moving forward had
   each source byte overwritten before it was read. The direction is now
   decided on 2 * word address + half.

MEASURED: SINTRAN's ND-500 monitor shifts the 16-byte owner name one byte
to the right, in place, at 100236B-100244B (A = X = 177663B, D = 040020B,
T = 140020B) to make room for "(". The 16 LBYTs that follow read back
Y S T S M S sp S sp S ..., and LIST-ACTIVE-PROCESSES and the ND-500 error
report printed "(YSTSMS S S S S S)TERMINAL-1".

Measured after: "1     1 (SYSTEM)TERMINAL-1".

tests/test_movb.c runs both instructions through the dispatch table: the
measured in-place right shift, its left-shift mirror, non-overlapping
moves between different halves in both directions, a same-half control,
and MOVBF from a right half to a left half.

events.title: Make the ND-100 octobus station 1, lock TSET against the ND-5000, port the card and the bridge
events.message:
Make the ND-100 octobus station 1, lock TSET against the ND-5000, port the card and the bridge

Differences between this lane and the reference
($RETROCORE/Emulated.HW/ND, the octobus card, the ND-5000 station and
Nd500CpuProcessBridge.cs), each ported as the reference has it. Needs the
nd500x commit "Port the octobus station, the mailbox servicer and the
fault record".

The ND-100 is a station on the fabric (src/machine/mfbus_bridge.c). It
was not registered, so the ND-5000's answer frame 0x8101 to station 1
went nowhere and SINTRAN found every answer only through its watchdog.
Frames for station 1 are now queued under the bus lock and pushed into
the card's receive side one per card tick.

TSET and TSETP are atomic against the ND-5000 thread (src/cpu/cpu_instr.c,
src/cpu/cpu_mms.c). SINTRAN's SLOCK takes the mailbox lock with them; the
read and the write of the word now sit inside the bus lock that the
bridge installs with mms_set_tset_lock(), and the lock is dropped before
a fault longjmps out of the instruction (src/cpu/cpu.c).

Bridge: the process is parked and its context saved BEFORE the answer is
sent, the runner thread is joined before a restart touches the CPU,
per-process state for 64 processes, the domain state loaded from the DIT
at start, reset to idle on master clear and CPURES, the host callbacks
for DMEMRD/DMEMWR and for a named process load, and one short log line
per monitor call and per answer.

Octobus card (src/devices/octobus/device_octobus.c): nine register and
interrupt differences from the reference card, the CPU-attached state and
the ACCP continue hook.

MEASURED under SINTRAN on the octobus lane:
- PLACE-DOMAIN CPU-STAT 60 s -> 4.1 s, RUN 805 s -> 0.5 s, watchdog
  messages 450 -> 6, after the ND-100 became station 1.
- "ND-5000 lock timeout" gone in twelve interactive sessions (36 rounds)
  after the TSET lock and the locked release in nd500x.
- NC-A06 runs twice in one session.

events.title: Leave I1, I2 and the flags alone when a string instruction page-faults
events.message:
Leave I1, I2 and the flags alone when a string instruction page-faults

SMOVE, SFILL, SMATCH and SCOTR each loop over string elements and then
commit the index registers and the status flags. None of the four tested
for a faulted access inside the loop. A faulted read returns 0 and a
faulted store is dropped, so the loop ran to the end on nothing, I1/I2
were committed at the element counts, and the restart after page-in
found nothing left to do.

The reference returns before the commit: Smove.cs lines 105-110
explicitly, and every instruction through the unwind of a faulted access
to the instruction boundary
($RETROCORE/Emulated.HW/ND/CPU/ND500/CpuND500.UncaughtFaults.cs,
UnwindOnAbortedAccess). Each of the four now returns on
nd500_trap_occurred() || cpu->instr_aborted with nothing committed, the
test Smvun.c, Smvwh.c and the others already make.

MEASURED on LED-CONV under SINTRAN: by smove at 0x080308D7, 20 bytes,
source 0x08046842 not present. First attempt: trap 46B, I1 = I2 = 0x14,
destination unchanged. Restart: no store. The destination kept stack
bytes (F4 08 01 20 ...), which the program then passed to MON 50B as the
file name; SINTRAN answered error 21B and the program ended in a protect
violation at 1:15052B.

Measured after: MON 50B reads the name "DDBTABLES-E'" and the type
"VTM'" and is answered K=0; LED-CONV asks for the terminal type and,
given 93, draws its screen with the "LED:" prompt.

test_string_abort.c runs each of the four twice: with the page missing
(nothing may change) and after it is mapped (the full result).

events.title: Port the octobus station, the mailbox servicer and the fault record
events.message:
Port the octobus station, the mailbox servicer and the fault record

Differences found by comparing this lane with the reference
($RETROCORE/Emulated.HW/ND/CPU/ND500), each ported as the reference has
it. A free-running nd500x (no trap sink, nd500_embedded clear) keeps its
behaviour; every change to the CPU is gated on one of the two.

Mailbox servicer (src/ndbus/ndbus_servicer.c):
- MICFU 10B DMEMRD and 11B DMEMWR are served: the bytes are read from or
  written to the ND-500 data memory of the process the message names,
  through the new host callbacks read/write_nd500_data_bytes, and the
  buffer field is taken as window-relative. They were refused before.
- The mailbox lock is released with ndbus_semaphore_release16, under the
  bus lock, instead of a plain store.
- Answers for 22B, 24B, 26B and 44B, the value-slot skip, MICFU := 23B on
  an answered start, 64 process slots, copies whose target lies outside
  the pool, and the load_named_process host callback.
- One log line with the bytes each DMEMRD returned.

Station (src/ndbus/ndbus_nd5000.c): kicks 1, 2, 3 and 6, the idle gate,
master clear and CPURES state through ndbus_nd5000_set_cpu_hooks, the
model report, end-of-mailbox, the patched control-store cells, the

acknowledge as the reference does.

Fault record (src/cpu/nd500_mmu.c, src/cpu/cpu.c), trap sink attached:
- one page fault per instruction; a later page fault of an aborted

- every protect-violation site writes the physical segment and the

events.title: X-Surf 100: receive batches for the NE2000 core
events.message:
X-Surf 100: receive batches for the NE2000 core

ne2000.c sets rx_batches, so an opener that negotiates ANXD_CMD_RX_BATCH
gets one reply per service pass instead of one CMD_READ round trip
(ReplyMsg, Signal, GetMsg, re-post) per frame.  The core's old rationale
-- "a core that raises an interrupt per frame gains nothing from a batch"
-- does not hold on a fast link: dp8390_rint() walks the whole ring per
pass, and a burst sent back to back is in the ring together, more so with
PAUSE holding the rest.  The claim, the fill and the end-of-pass flush are
the shell's, the same for every core; a pass that takes one frame answers
one, as a read would.

netdev_direct.c counts the batch replies (nu_RxBatches), published as the
special statistic "Receive batches answered", appended so every existing
record keeps its Type.  Frames over replies is the batch size an opener
actually got; 0 with frames received is an opener that never negotiated.

A3000 (68060/50, Z3, PAUSE agreed), on top of fe0896b5, the same library
and driver with ENV:ANXDRXBATCH 0 against unset:

                    batching off   on
  LAN receive       21.6           22.1-22.2   (+2.5%)
  25 ms receive     10.34          10.44
  transmit          11.30          11.76       (+4%)
  overruns          0              0
  batch replies     0              14783 (about 12 frames each)

Also measured on 28b2484e before the receive-pass fix: +1.5% receive,
+3.5% transmit.  The 68060 spends least per frame of the machines this
core runs on; a slower CPU pays more per reply.

Host: 554/554; test_netdev_ne2000 pins the opt-in.

events.title: v0.3.1: runs on macOS (Apple silicon and Intel)
events.message:
v0.3.1: runs on macOS (Apple silicon and Intel)

### New: macOS
CPCSyntaxError now builds and runs on Macs, both Apple silicon (M1 and later) and Intel. A user's build compiled, but then stopped at start-up with "Failed to initialize OpenGL loader!". macOS only gives a modern OpenGL to a program that asks for a 3.2 Core Profile context, and the emulator now asks for one. The README has a new *Building from source → macOS* section:

```
xcode-select --install
brew install cmake ninja sdl2
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja
cmake --build build
./build/cpcse
```

Other things that work on a Mac now:
- **CSL scripts window:** it runs scripts (it finds its own program file without Linux's `/proc`).
- **"Open screenshot folder":** it uses `open`.
- **GDB server and command API:** a debugger that disconnects mid-reply no longer ends the program.

If a computer's graphics driver can't provide OpenGL 3 at all, the program now explains this in a message box instead of stopping with an assert.

Windows and Linux are unchanged.

### Download
`CPCSyntaxError-win64-v0.3.1.zip`: unzip anywhere and run `cpcse.exe`. On Linux and macOS, build from source (README, *Building from source*). The YRW801 (OPL4) and SP0256-AL2 (speech) ROMs are not included; the emulator asks for them when they're needed.

events.title: X-Surf 100: acknowledge a burst's tail at the end of the receive pass (NetX 9d941cbf)
events.message:
X-Surf 100: acknowledge a burst's tail at the end of the receive pass (NetX 9d941cbf)

Review (codex-amiga 08:30/09:04Z) of a regression found measuring
batching: 28b2484e cut 25 ms receive with PAUSE from 10.4 to 8.4 Mbit/s.
Bisect on the A3000: 8437e1cd 10.37, 8437e1cd + NetX c390a9b3 10.38,
28b2484e 8.4-8.5 with batching on or off, and back to 10.44 only with both
the capped SYN-ACK and the fresh last_sent lowering removed.

An event-ring trace of one flow (diagnostic build, not in this tree)
showed the ACK ramp identical in the fast and slow runs, ACKs leaving the
instant TCP decided, no timer ACKs and no allocation failures.  The
difference was burst phase: the reader hands TCP runs of at most
AMI_SANA2_GRO_MAX (16) segments and the threshold ramps to 16 segments,
so a 32-segment window arriving as 16 + 16 was acknowledged twice per
window, and one arriving as 16 + 14 or 16 + 2 left the tail
unacknowledged a whole round trip -- the window-full sender could not send
the burst that would have pushed it over.  The capped handshake only chose
the starting phase.

- NetX 9d941cbf: the receive pass (_nx_tcp_receive_pass_begin/_complete);
  at its end a socket it took in-order data on, with two full-sized
  segments or more still unacknowledged, is acknowledged once.
- sana2_rx.c: ami_sana2_rx_drain brackets its run with the pass, the
  completion after the final GRO flush and before the input seat and the
  IP mutex are given back.
- socket.c: the fresh-connection last_sent lowering is gone; the capped
  SYN/SYN-ACK is the prevention, and the record of what was offered is
  not rewritten (codex).

A3000 (68060/50, Z3), same driver, batching held off (ENV:ANXDRXBATCH=0),
against 28b2484e:

  arm                     28b2484e   this
  25 ms receive, PAUSE    8.41       10.34   ACK every 16 segs, rtt 37 ms
  LAN receive, PAUSE      21.8       21.6
  LAN receive, no PAUSE   18.1*      17.9    (* 01000a73 arm)
  25 ms receive, no PAUSE 3.29*      3.27
  transmit                11.4       11.3
  overruns                0          0

Peer captures: no pass-end ACK on the LAN -- data ACKs all 16 (PAUSE) or 8
(no PAUSE) segments; zero-window ACKs without PAUSE 718 against main's
1310 in the same span.

Host: 554/554 (HOST_TESTS_EXPECTED 554); new test_tcp_rxpass against the
real data_check and pass functions -- 16+14 and 16+2 tails acknowledged at
the pass end and not without one, aligned 16+16 no extra ACK, one-segment
tail left to the timer, no second ACK for covered data, untouched flows
left alone, a failed ACK tried once, CLOSE_WAIT skipped, nested passes,
out-of-order data not marking; fails with the completion's ACK removed.

events.title: Polygons: a 68000 path from vertices to rows, and only the colour's planes
events.message:
Polygons: a 68000 path from vertices to rows, and only the colour's planes

STDL_FillPolygon was about 2.3x one demo's own glenz filler. Most of
the gap was per polygon and per row in how the library did it, not in
what a library has to do:

- XOR, OR and CLEAR now write only the planes the colour has. A colour
  with nothing in planes 0-1 is a pair from the third plane's word,
  and an XOR into one plane - each face of a glenz object - is eor.w
  and not.w on that plane's word alone, where it was four words a
  group, three of them XORed with zero.
- A polygon inside the clip's columns, no taller than 256 rows, SET or
  XORed onto a surface with no mask, goes through stdl_poly_fast: the
  vertex scan, the clip, the winding and the walk down both sides in
  68000, each edge stepped in 16.16 in registers inside the row loop.
  No column tables and one call a polygon. 16.16 is exact at that
  height (the step falls short by under t/65536 after t rows, and the
  true position is never within 1/dy of a column, so t*dy < 65536 is
  enough): the same pixels as the table path. test_fixed_point checks
  that for every edge up to 256 rows and the first one it gets wrong
  at 257; triangles built on such edges fail if the limit is raised.
  Anything else - clipped columns, taller, a mask, a tie in the
  winding, OR and CLEAR on the machine - keeps the column tables.
  The C walk (fill_traps) is the host's twin; PGCHK runs the suite on
  the 68000, where a broken clipped-top multiply fails it.
- The row set-up finds a column's group with a mask and one shift,
  where it took two shifts of four and one of three.

PRIMCOST, plain ST, the old polygon.c against this in one library
(A and B passes identical):
  24 one-plane glenz-like triangles   85.0 -> 49.1ms
  22-row triangle, one plane           2.29 -> 1.27ms
  22-row triangle, colour 5            2.29 -> 1.55ms (spans 2.26)
  160-row diamond, XOR                15.08 -> 12.58ms (spans 23.9)
  160-row diamond, SET                15.23 -> 12.81ms
  22-row triangle, clipped (tables)    2.75 -> 2.58ms
polygon.o is 6092 bytes, from 4172, and outside the pixel budget: only
a program that fills polygons carries it.

PGCHK had outgrown run.sh's two-minute wait with the new tests and
looked like a hang; its surfaces are filled a plane word at a time
now, 82 seconds. AGENTS.md records the ceiling.

events.title: fix: the undo ring records the byte a store overwrites, not the ROM above it
events.message:
fix: the undo ring records the byte a store overwrites, not the ROM above it

The pre-write `old` byte (undo ring + trace) came from a CPU-view bus read, only
for $0002-$CFFF, and undo wrote it back into RAM. Stores that do not land in plain
visible RAM therefore corrupted RAM on reverse-step:

1. BASIC in, STA $A000: store lands in RAM beneath; old was the BASIC ROM byte,
   rstep wrote ROM into RAM.
2. Read-only cart ROM at $8000-$BFFF: same, with the cart ROM byte.
3. KERNAL in, STA $E000: old was 0, rstep zeroed the RAM byte.
4. $D000-$DFFF with I/O off (char ROM / RAM): old was 0 and undo went to the
   I/O shadows, leaving the stored byte in RAM.
5. A store a flash cart consumes (EasyFlash, EF3, GMod2/4 ...): RAM unchanged,
   but undo wrote `old` into RAM.

FullBus::write now reports where the store landed (wr_land: RAM / port / I/O /
cart / none) and, for RAM, the byte it replaced (wr_old, read from the RAM array:
no bus read, no cart read accounting, no side effect). write_raw / write_raw_dummy
use that report; cart-consumed and dropped stores are not recorded in the ring;
restore_byte undoes a $D000-$DFFF store into RAM when I/O is off. The RMW dummy
write to $00/$01 now records the port's pre-write value too. Ring dump format
unchanged. Regression tests: trx64-core/tests/delta_ring_under_rom.rs.

Found by the TRX64-Ultimate session.

SINTRAN fills the mailbox field ABUFA with an ND-100 PHYSICAL address
(MP-P2-N500.NPL:140675), while every other mailbox address is
window-relative. The servicer in nd500x now subtracts the window base
from ABUFA, and this is where it learns that base: mfbus_add_nd5000()
passes s_base_word * 2, the ND-100 byte address of pool byte 0 that
mfbus_attach() set.

Needs the nd500x commit "Subtract the window's ND-100 base from ABUFA",
which adds ndbus_servicer_set_nd100_window_base().

MEASURED without it, PLACE-DOMAIN CPU-STAT then RUN: ABUFA = ND-100 byte
0x42D000 was used as pool offset 0x42D000 instead of 0x00D000, so
CPU-STAT's output text never reached SINTRAN's buffer and the console
showed stale bytes, and its MON 143B answer read back as zeros.

Measured with it, together with the two nd500x trap-path fixes of the
same day: CPU-STAT prints its nine-field report on the console with real
values and RUN returns to the ND-5000 prompt.
events.author: Ronny Hansen

events.title: Subtract the window's ND-100 base from ABUFA
events.message:
Subtract the window's ND-100 base from ABUFA

ABUFA is the one mailbox field that holds an ND-100 PHYSICAL address
(MP-P2-N500.NPL:140675, "% ND-100 PHYSICAL ADDR"); links, X5FIF and the
copy-family operands are all window-relative. The reference hands it to
host.WriteNd100Word / ReadNd100Word, which take ND-100 physical addresses
($RETROCORE/Emulated.HW/ND/CPU/ND500/Servicer/Nd500MicrocodeServicer.cs,
the inline-buffer arm and N5MicroFunction.WaitMonitorCall). This servicer
shifted the word address to bytes and then used the result directly as a
pool offset, with no field to say where the window sits.

MEASURED on the octobus lane, the first run in which this code executed
live. ABUFA read 0x00216800 words = ND-100 byte 0x42D000 = window base
0x420000 + 0xD000, while the copy family named the same buffer as pool
0x00D000. So:
- all 32 MON 504B output texts of CPU-STAT were written to pool 0x42D000
  while SINTRAN printed the stale bytes at 0x00D000, and
- the 24 bytes of answer data for its MON 143B were read from pool
  0x42D000, so every field it printed was 0.
SINTRAN also sent MICFU 10B 13 times in that run.

The servicer now carries nd100_window_base_byte, set by the owner through
ndbus_servicer_set_nd100_window_base(), and subtracts it in both places:
ndbus_servicer_inline_buffer_target() and
ndbus_servicer_read_wmonco_block(). An ABUFA below the window is refused
and said, not read from a wrapped offset. The default base of 0 keeps a
pool that IS the ND-100's view working as before.

Measured after, with nd100x passing the base: 39 MON 504B calls, every one
to pool 0x00D000, the report printed on the console with real values
(CPU number 100, System type 110, Sintran III VSX-500, Version L,
Generated 16 December 1988 9:34), and no MICFU 10B at all.

test_ndbus: both paths checked with the live base 0x420000, next to the
same message read with base 0, which names a place 4 MB away. 1261
checks, 0 failed.
