events.title: Take ENTT's frame page fault through the real walk, as a data write
events.message:
Take ENTT's frame page fault through the real walk, as a data write

ENTT checks its frame pages with a non-faulting peek before it changes any
register. The peek records nothing, and raise_trap copies mmu_pgf_psn and
mmu_pgf_is_write into the trap record - two fields that are deliberately
never cleared, so they still describe the PREVIOUS real fault. Raising the
page fault directly after the peek therefore reported this frame write
with somebody else's physical segment and access class.

MEASURED on the octobus lane, PLACE-DOMAIN CPU-STAT then RUN. The program's
own stack-overflow handler ENTT at 0x0800415A faulted on its frame at
0x08001800 and was reported to SINTRAN as psn=11 mms=0x8000000F: segment
11 and READ, both left over from the instruction-side fault before it.
SINTRAN was asked for the wrong page and the park repeated 156 times; the
log has no MMU line for that address at all. The real data fault at
0x08001060 in the same run reported psn=12 and was paged in after one
park.

The reference writes the frame with ordinary WriteMemory calls
($RETROCORE/Emulated.HW/ND/CPU/ND500/Instructions/CALL/Entt.cs), so its
fault always comes out of the walk. ENTT now does the same on a missing
frame page: nd500_mmu_translate as a data write, which records where,
which physical segment and that it was a write, and raises the fault
naming cpu->PC. The P handling is unchanged.

Measured after: the same fault is reported psn=12 mms=0xA000000F and is
satisfied after one park, segment 14 is reached for the first time on
this lane, and CPU-STAT goes on to make its MON 504B output calls.

This answers the psn=12 / psn=11 question in
docs/HANDOFF-ENTT-TRAP-PATH-2026-10-05.md: 11 was the previous fault's.

test_entt_frame_fault: 8 checks. With the direct trap_page_fault call put
back, two fail and print psn=11 is_write=0 - the values the live run sent.
events.author: Ronny Hansen

events.title: Report a trap to the host unless it is locally enabled
events.message:
Report a trap to the host unless it is locally enabled

raise_trap dispatched a non-ignorable trap to the program's own handler
whenever THA was non-zero and the THA slot held an address. The reference
does not: $RETROCORE/Emulated.HW/ND/CPU/ND500/CpuND500.Trap.cs RaiseTrap
("THE LOCAL-TRAP-ENABLE GATE") reads the rule out of the control store.
Trap entry builds TE from the local trap enable register, forces bits 31
and 30 on (011035), forces bits 8..0 off (011036), ANDs with the pending
bits (011037) and branches on the result (011064). Zero means the trap is
reported to the ND-100 and the handler vector is never read.

Ported as written: (OTE | MTE | 0xC0000000) & ~0x1FF against the trap bit,
registers only, no DIT read.

ONLY WITH A TRAP SINK ATTACHED. A free-running nd500x has no ND-100 to
report to and keeps its existing dispatch exactly, which the first check
of the new test pins.

MEASURED on the octobus lane, PLACE-DOMAIN CPU-STAT then RUN. SINTRAN
writes OTE1/OTE2/MTE1/MTE2 = 0 for the domain process (mailbox copies to
pool 0x08C096/9A/A6/AA). The program's install loop then fills THA[38],
and its next instruction-side page fault, P=0x08000012 on 0x08000931, was
dispatched to that handler instead of being reported. The handler's ENTT
faulted on its own frame at 0x08001800 and that park repeated 501 times
in one run - the one local dispatch of the whole run sat directly before
it. With the gate that fault is reported and paged in, and the run goes
on to four further, non-repeating parks before the next defect.

test_local_trap_gate: 12 checks. With the gate switched off 6 of them
fail, so the test can fail.

events.message:
X-Surf 100: the interface's window cap holds from the SYN on (NetX c390a9b3)

Review of 8437e1cd (codex-amiga 06:31Z): the cap reached a connection
only at the settle in the establish notification, so the SYN, the SYN-ACK
and an active open's handshake ACK offered the buffer, and the SYN's
unscaled 65535 then held the edge above the cap -- 16 frames into a card
that holds 8 without flow control.

- NetX fork c390a9b3: nx_interface_tcp_rx_window_cap, the cap a
  connection offers until its own is settled (SYN and SYN-ACK included);
  the fork's own CMakeLists lists the two new sources (the native build
  failed to link); native netx_tcp_rx_window_cap_test.
- bsd_tcp_window_recap sets the interface's cap -- the card's fit at the
  link's segment size, the LAN answer since no round trip is known yet --
  and the reader calls it once at attach (rx_capacity_changed whenever a
  capacity is known, RXBUFFER and the vendor table included) and on every
  change after.
- The settle writes NX_TCP_RX_WINDOW_CAP_NONE where the card does not
  bound the window, so a long path is not held to the interface's cap,
  and on a fresh connection lowers last_sent to the cap: the revocation
  the buffer shrink already made before the cap existed.

A3000, peer capture of the handshakes: SYN-ACK window 46720 with PAUSE
agreed, 11680 a second after the switch stopped agreeing, was 65535.
LAN receive 21.7 / 21.75 Mbit/s with PAUSE, 17.9 without -- the arms of
8437e1cd within a per cent.

events.title: windows: report installer failures and install shares from the real path
events.message:
windows: report installer failures and install shares from the real path

Under Windows PowerShell 5.1 with ErrorActionPreference Stop, the first
stderr line of pip, python or git becomes a terminating
NativeCommandError. The installer died on that line, showed only
"error: subprocess-exited-with-error", and never reached its own exit
code check. Run native commands through Invoke-Native, which streams
both streams and returns the exit code, and run git describe with
Continue so a repo without tags falls back to 0.0.0 as intended.

install.bat recorded the PowerShell exit code but returned pause's 0, so
a caller saw success. Return the recorded code after the pause.

setuptools_scm 10 lists tracked files even when the version is
pretended. It resolves them to their real path, so a checkout on a
mapped drive or behind a symlink yields \\host\share\... paths, and
relpath against a C: or U: working directory fails with "path is on
mount". Install from os.path.realpath of the checkout so both agree.
Take Resolve-Path's ProviderPath so a script started from a UNC path
does not hand "Microsoft.PowerShell.Core\FileSystem::\\..." to git.
events.author: tbdye

events.title: windows: install development checkouts with their dev version
events.message:
windows: install development checkouts with their dev version

The installer pretends the version so setuptools_scm skips its own
derivation, and it took the latest tag (git describe --abbrev=0). Every
development install therefore reported the release it descends from,
v0.6.0 thirty commits later, while pip install -e without the installer
reports 0.6.1.dev30. Derive the version as setuptools_scm does: the tag
on a clean tagged commit, otherwise the next patch release as .devN.

On a share owned by another account git refuses the checkout with
"detected dubious ownership" unless a global safe.directory entry
exists, and the installer fell back to 0.0.0 without a word. Trust
exactly this checkout for this one git call, ask git only when the
folder has its own .git so a ZIP download inside another repository
does not take that repository's version, and say so when the version
falls back to 0.0.0.

events.title: X-Surf 100: re-apply the receive window to live connections when the card's capacity changes
events.message:
X-Surf 100: re-apply the receive window to live connections when the card's capacity changes

Review (codex-amiga, 06:29Z): the capacity refresh updated only
iface->hw_rx_bytes, and bsd_tcp_window_settle runs once, from the
establish notify, so a connection settled at 32 frames while PAUSE was
agreed kept that window after PAUSE went -- and overran the ring.

- sana2: an asking that finds a different ANXD_CMD_RX_CAPACITY answer
  sets rx_capacity_changed; the reader's next drain, with nx_ip_protection
  already held, clears it and calls the registered capacity hook
  (ami_sana2_set_capacity_hook, sana2.h).
- bsdsocket: the settle's inputs (the window before the card's bound, the
  round trip) are kept on the socket; bsd_tcp_window_recap applies them
  again to every settled connection on that interface.  The settle body
  is split into bsd_tcp_window_apply, which on a live connection moves the
  cap and may grow the buffer but never shrinks it -- lowering the cap is
  all a smaller card needs, and the cap never pulls back an edge already
  sent.  library.c registers the hook before the stack starts.

A3000 (68060/50 MHz), nc -l receiving, switch port flow control turned
off 15 s into a 45 s transfer:

  build      before   after the flip            ring overruns
  01000a73   18-19    4-7 Mbit/s, window 46720  167
  this       18-19    15 Mbit/s, window 11680   1

(iperf -s cannot run this test: its server ends a stream idle for 2 s,
and the renegotiation is a 2.2 s blackout.)

Host: 553/553 ctest; sana2 device test asks a fake device for
capacity (new answer flagged, same answer not, failed asking keeps the
last, hook gets the interface and its IP).

events.title: X-Surf 100: offer 802.3x PAUSE, size the receive window to it, cap the window below the buffer
events.message:
X-Surf 100: offer 802.3x PAUSE, size the receive window to it, cap the window below the buffer

Receiving on an X-Surf 100 (AX88796B, 16 KB, no DMA) was stop-and-wait.
Peer capture on an A3000 (68060 at 50 MHz, Zorro III), main 97697d70:
8 segments back-to-back (the 11,680-byte ring-fit window), an ACK of all
8 with window 0 at +5.3 ms, a window update at +6.0 ms, 2617 such cycles
in 15 s = 16.2 Mbit/s.  A larger window overran the 13 KB ring (32 frames:
5.3 Mbit/s, 410 overruns): the PIO copy off the card runs at ~7 MB/s, about
half the wire, so the ring cannot absorb a longer line-rate burst.

- ne2000.c: the AX88796B's internal PHY (MII 0x10, ID 003b/1841) is driven
  by bit-banging MEMR (0x14).  Attach offers PAUSE (MR4 bit 10) and
  restarts negotiation -- the PHY's reset advertisement 01e1 never offered
  it, so FLWC never took effect whatever the switch was set to.  The blank
  tick (was NULL) reads BMSR/ANAR/ANLPAR once a second; while link, full
  duplex and PAUSE on both sides hold, rx_pause_capacity = 32 frames, the
  window measured best (64 was slower).  A PHY found reset is told again,
  at most three times in a row.
- ANXD_CMD_RX_CAPACITY answers rx_pause_capacity when set; the contract
  (anxs2ext.h) now says the answer can change while online and that a
  paused card answers its measured figure, not 0.  The SANA-II reader asks
  again at most once a second while traffic flows.
- Window cap (NetX Duo fork 281b077b, nx_tcp_socket_rx_window_cap): a
  window the receive bound cut to the card is offered as a cap over a
  buffer twice that (ami_bsd_tcp_window_buffer), so the ACK of a burst the
  application has not read still offers a window.
- TCPWANWINDOW=: the receive window on a long path for a card whose memory
  limits it (opt-in; 16 frames without PAUSE was +23% on a 25 ms netem path
  with 254 overruns, 12 frames still overran, so no default).

Measured on the A3000, one-shot boots, peer playhouse4, Mbit/s:

  arm                                LAN RX  25 ms RX  TX    overruns
  main 97697d70                      16.5    3.27      11.4  0
  this, switch flow control on       21.9    10.37     11.4  0
  this, RXBUFFER=13312 (cap alone)   18.1    3.28      11.3  0
  this, switch flow control off      18.1    3.29      11.4  0

Host: 553/553 ctest; new tests: ne2000 MDIO PHY mock (advertise, resolve,
half duplex, link down, PHY reset, sticky refusal, forced speed, no PHY,
non-AX card), RX_CAPACITY paused answer, capped advertisement (SWS host),
capped update step, buffer helper, TCPWANWINDOW parsing.

events.title: windows: let other accounts read files below the mount root
events.message:
windows: let other accounts read files below the mount root

WinFsp builds each file's ACL from st_mode and grants the "other" bits
to Everyone. Amiga entries rarely carry GRP/OTR protection bits, so
files report 0600 and directories 0700, and any account other than the
one that mounted (a global drive letter, a second logged-in user) can
list the 0777 root but cannot open anything beneath it.

On Windows, mirror the owner's read and execute bits into group and
other. Write stays owner-only unless the Amiga GRP/OTR write bits grant
it, and an Amiga file without the read bit stays unreadable for every
account. macOS and Linux keep the plain Amiga protection mapping.

events.title: grm-fekc: recover select-data helpers whose sites store from different registers
events.message:
grm-fekc: recover select-data helpers whose sites store from different registers

MMC3 helpers commonly write the select from a constant in one register and the
bank from the caller's argument in another (tmnt3 FUN_8705: LDY #$47 / STY $8000
/ STA $8001). findHelpers' register-agreement check nulled argReg for that, so
recovery never ran. HelperModel.recoversPerSiteWithoutArgReg() now routes such a
model (depositsPerSite strategy, null argReg) through foldDeposits under the
caller's registers, offering no face-value argument to any site.

Two latent foldDeposits defects surfaced and are fixed:
- primary (the max-address site) seeded the fold, so EARLIER sites overwrote it.
  rcransom FUN_ff29 claimed select=7 though its last write restores select from
  $fb; nesmmc3mirrortest's ModeOne/SaveRestore/VaryingWindow summaries were wrong.
- each site saw the CALL's in-state, not the state the helper's earlier sites
  built, so a mirror read inside the helper answered the caller's bank
  (nesmmc3mirrortest CrossCopy: r6 now 4, per the generator's MM4 truth).

Re-blessed: tmnt3 (instrs.inOverlay 1405->3425, bankComments 49->119, warnings
37->56 -- more code reached; remaining warnings filed as grm-mej.9, grm-mej.10,
grm-lwvc), rcransom (f21d wrong select=7 removed), megaman3 (c0b8 wording),
nesmmc3mirrortest. check nes otherwise: wizwarr (held floor) + shenlong 97
(pre-existing flap; HEAD reproduces the identical dump in ab-test).

events.title: Unmount the interpreter behind a Windows venv launcher
events.message:
Unmount the interpreter behind a Windows venv launcher

A Windows venv's python.exe and pythonw.exe are launchers that run the
base interpreter as a child with the same command line. Mount discovery
kept the launcher and dropped the child as a duplicate, but only the
child creates the PID-named unmount events, so `amifuse unmount` and the
tray failed with "cannot find the file specified" for every venv
install, including the one the installer creates. Keep the innermost
process of a duplicated chain instead.

The native cross-process unmount test signalled Popen.pid, which is the
launcher in a venv; it now uses the PID the child reports.

events.message:
boot: Reduce animation overhead during floppy loading

The loader animation competes with DOS and decompression for CPU time
and holds off task switching across a full batch of plasma blits.

Shift scrolltext with word-wide carry operations and copy precomputed
horizontal Copper WAIT bytes in groups of eight. Skip vertical plasma
updates when the phase is unchanged, and release the blitter and task
switching exclusion after each column while checking the display map.

VBlank so they continue while the foreground task is busy.

events.title: Honour the abort flag where the reference unwinds instead
events.message:
Honour the abort flag where the reference unwinds instead

Four parallel surveys compared every instruction class against
$RETROCORE/Emulated.HW/ND/CPU/ND500/Instructions/ and the engine either
side. The framing fact came out of them, and it is not what the
guard-by-guard comparison suggested:

THE C# IS ABORT-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION. A faulting access throws
Nd500InstructionAbortException (CpuND500.UncaughtFaults.cs:254), armed for
the whole instruction body and caught at the boundary
(CpuND500.Execute.cs:716), with UnwindOnAbortedAccess defaulting to true.
Its explicit InstructionAborted checks are belt and braces. nd500x has no
unwind at all, so abort safety is per access site - which means "the C# has
no guard here" never means "the C needs none", and the C must say so itself
at every site. It did not.

THE STRING DESCRIPTOR LOADER CLAIMED SUCCESS ON A FAULT.
nd500_load_string_descriptor returned true unconditionally, so all 27
`if (!nd500_load_string_descriptor(...)) return;` sites in the STRING class
were dead code. On a page fault both descriptor words read 0 and the caller
ran its copy or fill loop with element_count 0 and base_address 0, then
committed I1/I2 and the K/Z flags from it; Sfill raised a descriptor-range
trap on top of the page fault. It now reports the fault, which revives
every one of those checks.

THE DECODER'S READS NEVER CHECKED. cpu_instr.c mmu_read8/16/32 translated
and then read at the result whether or not the translate faulted - and a
failed translate returns the VIRTUAL address, so the decoder was handed a
byte from physical memory at the virtual address. mmu_write8/16/32 in the
same file have checked since the exec-argv corruption.

THE READ HELPERS TESTED HALF THE CONDITION. Seven read helpers in
instruction_helpers.c tested nd500_trap_occurred() but not
cpu->instr_aborted, while every write helper tests both. After a dispatched
handler clears the global trap state, the reads proceeded and the writes
bailed. Same asymmetry fixed in Lregbl.c and Phyladr.c.

ENTM COMMITTED TOS BETWEEN ITS GUARDS. cpu->TOS was assigned after the
old-SP guard and before the terminal one, so a fault on any of the four
frame writes left the frame half built with TOS claiming it whole. Entm.cs
has a third guard immediately before regs.TOS for precisely that reason.
TOS now commits with B and L below the terminal guard.

THE LOOP FAMILY COMMITTED THE BRANCH AFTER A FAULTED WRITE-BACK. Loop,
Loopd and Loopi guarded their operand reads but not the index write-back,
so with a memory-operand index a page fault on the write-back still set
cpu->PC to the loop target - overwriting the PC the fault handler had just
installed. The C# has a second guard inside its should-loop arm for this.

Recorded, NOT changed, because each needs its own evidence first: the
systemic case where flags are committed after a faulted DESTINATION store
(every guarded file in eight classes), the remaining raw translate-then-
access sites outside the instruction folder (nd500_fecall.c:868,
nd500_mon_sintran.c, nd500_ndix_boot.c:95, the trap-vector fetch at
cpu.c:1918 and the debugger paths), and the absence of the C#'s
one-fault-per-instruction suppression (CpuND500.MMU.cs:1646) which lets
nd500x re-fault many times inside one instruction.

events.title: Align the CALL and ENT/RET family with the C# implementations
events.message:
Align the CALL and ENT/RET family with the C# implementations

Compared all 18 CALL-class instructions against
$RETROCORE/Emulated.HW/ND/CPU/ND500/Instructions/CALL/*.cs one pair at a
time. Entd, Retd, Entb, Entf, Entfn, Entm, Ents, Entsn, Call and Callg
already matched in execution order. Six real divergences, all of the same
two shapes: a bound that does not match its array, and faulting work done
without the reference's abort guard.

OUT-OF-BOUNDS ARGUMENT LOOPS. Seven files bounded their argument loop with
ND500_MAX_OPERANDS, which is 258, while pending_call_arg_addresses holds
256 - and Call.c:121 and Callg.c:244 WRITE through that index, so a call
with 257 or 258 arguments wrote past the array into its neighbours. The C#
bounds every one of these loops at 256. Now bounded by TRAP_SEQ_MAXARG,
which cpu_protos.h already defines as "matches pending_call_arg_addresses".

ENTT MUTATED BEFORE IT WROTE. Entt.c set B to the frame base and cleared
the pending-call fields BEFORE building the frame, so a frame write that
page-faulted left the instruction half applied. Entt.cs writes the whole
frame, checks cpu.InstructionAborted, and only then assigns B, TOS, L and
clears the trap enables - the order every other ENT* variant here already
followed. Measured on PLACE-DOMAIN CPU-STAT: the first attempt ran with
B=4, the retry after the pagein with B=0x08001728, and the re-executed
ENTT raised an instruction sequence error.

ENTT AND RETT READ AND WROTE THROUGH A FAULTING TRANSLATE. 47 writes in
Entt.c and 30 reads in Rett.c used nd500_bus_write32/read32 with
nd500_mmu_translate inline, using the result whether or not it faulted,
and Rett.c had no abort guard at all before restoring registers. The C#
uses its abort-aware ReadMemory/WriteMemory throughout and guards at
AbortGuardSite.Rett. Both now use nd500_read_memory_32 /
nd500_write_memory_32, and Rett restores nothing after a faulted read.

ENTT'S GUARD IS THE INSIDE-TRAP-HANDLER FLAG. Entt.cs and Rett.cs both
test pcb.InsideTrapHandler - the DIT byte at offset 187 - not a
dispatch-to-ENTT interlock. nd500x tested trap_dispatch_pending, which a
park between the dispatch and the handler's first instruction legitimately
spends. nd500_is_in_trap_handler reads the DIT where one is configured and
the CPU field otherwise, so a machine with no DIT behaves as before.

MISSING ABORT GUARDS. Retb, Retbk, Retk and Ifkret read PREVB and RETA and
went straight on to assign B, P and L; a page fault on either left garbage
in them. Retb.cs and Retbk.cs guard there explicitly (AbortGuardSite.Retb
/ .Retbk). Chain.c guarded its operand reads but not the link read inside
its walk, which Chain.cs does guard.

Two differences left deliberately, both noted rather than changed: the
operand-count arms, where the C# returns silently and nd500x raises an
illegal-operand trap (nd500x's diagnostic is the more useful of the two
and the arm is unreachable with a correct decoder), and the own-trap-enable
clear, which nd500x does at dispatch in invoke_trap_handler while the C#
does it at the end of ENTT - ours leaves no window in which a fault between
dispatch and ENTT could be own-handled.

nd500x 38/38, conformance ALL TESTS PASSED, nd100x 21/21.

events.title: morepork conform and morepork final: an adapter's behaviour as Mammet facts
events.message:
morepork conform and morepork final: an adapter's behaviour as Mammet facts

Mammet checks the adapters, and its rules judge what a runner reports.
`morepork conform` runs an adapter through fixed probes (profile, trigger
instruction/mcycle/tcycle, boot-rom skip, version, beside itself) and states
each as adapter::honoured, refused (exit 2, with the adapter's reason) or
broke (with what differed), plus the columns the profile probe asked for and
wrote. A finer trigger whose trace has no more entries than the instruction
trace is broken even when the header claims it. `morepork final` runs an
adapter over ROMs and states each trace's last entry as adapter::ended
facts, or a failed check::outcome when the run fails. Both exit 0 whenever
they ran and keep each run's files under <result>.work/.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: ajoneil

events.title: SameBoy and missingno adapters: out-of-tree builds that refuse what they can't give
events.message:
SameBoy and missingno adapters: out-of-tree builds that refuse what they can't give

Mammet builds the adapters as checks from pinned, read-only source trees and
checks what they do. Each adapter now builds into OUT and writes nothing into
its sources, stamps its version from the build, and exits 2 naming what it
won't give instead of giving something else.

SameBoy: built from SRC (a patched tree; cloned at SAMEBOY_PIN and patched
when absent) with SameBoy's own Makefile into OUT, linked statically against
libsameboy.a, so it no longer needs LD_LIBRARY_PATH. SameBoy's boot ROMs are
assembled from SRC into OUT/boot_roms, where the adapter looks. Its
emulator_version is SameBoy's VERSION plus PIN (it said 0.16.x for v1.0.3).
It refuses --boot-rom skip (SameBoy has no skip; the panel had taken its
boot-ROM run for a skip), triggers other than instruction and tcycle (mcycle
was silently traced per instruction), columns it can't fill (they were
skipped with a warning), unknown models and unknown flags.

missingno: the Makefile copies the adapter and the crates it needs into
OUT/tree and builds there with its own Cargo.lock; with MISSINGNO_DIR, every
missingno crate comes from that tree. missingno-vcs is a git dependency like
the others, not a path to a sibling checkout. The GB adapter now honours the
profile: missingno's tracer writes its full scope to a work file, and the
adapter keeps the profile's columns (it wrote all 130 whatever was asked).
It gives the gbmicrotest block at instruction granularity, read beside each
capture, and refuses it at tcycle, where capture happens inside missingno.
Its emulator_version is missingno's version, +PIN and, for a git checkout,
the short commit. An instruction trace now ends with one more entry, the
state after the last instruction, which carries a stopping write such as
gbmicrotest's verdict. It refuses mcycle (it labelled per-instruction
entries mcycle), a boot ROM file, and unknown models.

events.title: make: build the CLI and FFI into OUT

Mammet runs morepork's builds as checks against a pinned, read-only tree, so
the build has to land elsewhere: `make OUT=<dir> cli ffi` builds with
`cargo build --release --locked --target-dir <dir>`, writing nothing into the
tree and never rewriting Cargo.lock. OUT defaults to target, so `make cli`
and `make ffi` work as before. cargo, not file lists, decides what is out of
date, and adapters get the FFI library from OUT.

events.title: dat: report and raise byte coverage, type unused data by address in dat_symbols.txt (#3630)
events.message:
dat: report and raise byte coverage, type unused data by address in dat_symbols.txt (#3630)

Archive byte coverage (matching samples and inferred data) goes from 86.98%
to 99.80%, and complete units from 106 to 345 of 838. Sample matches are
unchanged apart from the two known mismatches.

Tooling:
- `samples report` prints the archive bytes covered, and `--missing` lists
  the data the base doesn't infer by the field that reaches it.
- dat_symbols.txt lines are `name = dat:address;` like symbols.txt, with the
  dat in the section's place. `*` for the address matches a public symbol
  by name, as before; an address gives a C alias for data no public symbol
  names. Type and count are separate attributes mirroring the annotations:
  `type:T`, `count:N` and `extent` (instead of `count:*` and `T[N]`).
- `DAT_SCRIPT` takes a table (fighters) or a length expression in
  `_command` (`itCommandLength`, items); the generic commands 0-9
  (`Command_Execute`) are shared by every script. Scripts' extents count
  as typed data.
- hsd.rs keeps archive tables in file order, as the game reads them, and
  refuses malformed archives.
- Clippy comes from the flake.

Types:
- `HSD_VtxDescList::vertex` is an `HSD_VertexArray` blob; palettes are
  stored rounded up to 16 entries; collision vertices, lines and joints are
  counted; the particle banks run as far as the data does; item state
  scripts are scripts; `FtPartsDesc.vis_table` rows are
  `FtPartsVisLookup*`; `HSD_AObjDesc.obj_id` is any descriptor; every
  effect archive's table is an `EffectDataTable`.

Unused data: only names, and the pointers from them, reach archive data,
so data nothing points to is export leftovers. About 3,800 aliases type
the joint, animation and material animation trees among it whose every
part is well-formed (PlFe's and TyMcCmDs's unused models among them),
with no new walk gaps or sample mismatches.

events.title: v0.3.0: drives in the file picker, any file name on Windows, a Save dialog that browses
events.message:
v0.3.0: drives in the file picker, any file name on Windows, a Save dialog that browses

### New: the file picker switches drives
The Open dialog has a button for each drive (C:, D:, E: ...), with the one you're on highlighted. You can also type a drive (`D:`) or a folder, absolute (`D:\games`) or relative, into the name box and press Enter or Open to go there. A typed file name opens as before.

### New: the Save dialog browses
Saving (the assembler's source, DSK images, screenshots, snapshots) now uses the same folder view as Open: drives, `[..]`, folders to go into, and the files already there. Clicking a file takes its name.

### New: file and folder names in any script (Windows)
Files and folders whose names use accented letters, CJK or emoji now open. That includes discs, tapes, snapshots and ROMs you pick, drop onto the window or load from the command line, and running the program from a folder such as `C:\Users\José\Downloads`. Before, such a name could be listed but not opened. This needs Windows 10 version 1903 or later.

### New: typing the characters BASIC lines need
The command API's `type` and the headless `--type` now press the keys the CPC's own keyboard map gives. `[ ] { } ! ' `` and `@ |` all type correctly. On the French and Spanish keyboards, letters and digits now go to the right keys.

### Also in this release
A second full audit of the code. If you use the GDB server or the command API, the most important fix is this: a web page you visited could make your browser send commands to the API port. Both servers now refuse that. The audit also fixed crashes from crafted or mistaken input: symbol files, snapshots, CSL scripts, tapes, settings values and breakpoint conditions. Saves are now written whole or not at all, and the Symbiface II's clock is switched on with the board (it never was before). Unused code was removed.

### Download
`CPCSyntaxError-win64-v0.3.0.zip`: unzip anywhere and run `cpcse.exe`. On Linux, build from source (README, *Building from source → Linux*). The YRW801 (OPL4) and SP0256-AL2 (speech) ROMs are not included; the emulator asks for them when they're needed.

events.title: dat: sample each case once, show every piece of each archive, one header per unit (#3628)
events.message:
dat: sample each case once, show every piece of each archive, one header per unit (#3628)

Samples are now chosen across every archive by a `samples pick` step: for
each type and union variant, the fewest instances that together show every
case its fields take anywhere in the game (pointers null, relocated,
unrelocated or -1; float and integer classes; bitfields; nonzero padding),
preferring instances the walk found clean. Each archive's choice is
rewritten only when it changes. Sample-mode C goes from 12,130 samples
(245k lines) to 347 (13k lines), and every unit is in objdiff, samples or
not. MELEE_DAT_SAMPLES_ALL still samples everything.

Elided data is declared as the type the walk reached it as, spelled as the
pointers to it spell it (`Mtx`, `HSD_DisplayList[n]`, `u16[n]`), instead
of `UNK_T`. `MtxPtr`, `Mtx44Ptr` and `ROMtxPtr` are redeclared with
`DAT_TYPE` in dat_macros.h for the DWARF build, which uses aurora's SDK
headers.

Every piece of each archive outside the samples is now its own symbol in
the target, and the base infers each piece the walk explains on its own,
instead of only public symbols and data the samples point to, each with
everything it reaches. So what's inferred no longer depends on what's
sampled: units without samples show all their data, and 106 units are
complete in both modes. Bytes a pointer says are bytes (texels, strings,
keyframes) and command scripts up to their end command count as explained.

Each unit's C is now `src/<unit>.h`, declaring the archive's public
symbols, its samples and what they point to, and `src/<unit>.c` only for a
unit with samples, instead of a header and source per root in a folder.
A unit without samples links its base object from its inferred data alone.

Clippy is in the dev shell, and its warnings in dat-cli are fixed.

A union member condition that can't be evaluated now stops the search
instead of falling through to a later member, so `ftData_Item` uses
`DAT_IF(true)` as its catch-all.

events.title: Steer at once while falling; add stand/crouch zones to the side strips
events.message:
Steer at once while falling; add stand/crouch zones to the side strips

Side touches only skipped the 120 ms tap delay while gliding.  During
the fall before a glide, a press waited, and a quick tap became the
button instead of a turn.  SideTouch now treats any fall as airborne:
a press on one side steers that side immediately, and a tap steers
rather than fires.  A leap's held button stays held into the fall so
it can still open the glide.

The top and bottom thirds of each side strip now press up and down
without walking: a tap stands or crouches, a hold climbs.  Menus keep
the slide-to-jog behaviour.  A test overlay outlines the six zones in
fullscreen and landscape play on touch screens.

events.title: Click the 1702's power button audibly on and off
events.message:
Click the 1702's power button audibly on and off

The power button now plays a recorded 1702 push-button press.  Power-on
adds a synthesized degauss thump after the press.  Power-off plays the
same press alone: a push-push switch sounds the same both ways.

The press is iiiDIY's 1702 restoration footage (25:18.97, sources.txt),
cleaned with a time-set gate rather than spectral noise reduction, which
made it tinny.  A synthesized click was tried first and rejected by ear.
The clip lead is trimmed to 40 ms so the press is not late.

Clips play on the speaker's master gain, so volume and mute apply.
silence() and suspend() leave them ringing, which lets power-off reset
the game without cutting its own click.  They decode on an
OfflineAudioContext at startup, so no user gesture is needed to load them.

events.title: Add libc-script-launcher tool/stub
events.message:
Add libc-script-launcher tool/stub

The stub launches a script with a shebang line loaded from a file with the same name after stripping the '.exe' extension. Also, `__spawnve` can detect the stub and shortcut directly to the script file instead of creating another intermediate process that would essentially do the same operation.

The stub's own `libc-script-launcher` script acts as a tool to conveniently install launchers for other scripts from the command line.

The stub is tiny (less than 1 KB stripped and packed), it simply passes control to LIBCn to do all the work. It also detects the LIBCn version and prints an error message when the current LIBCn DLL is older than required instead of silently leaving a POPUPLOG.OS2 entry. This allows to create long-lived stubs that do not need to be updated when LIBCn updates.

Closes #187.

- forstack.asm（拡張バンク3）: FOR のフレームを19バイトにし、積めるのは（使用量＋19＋80）≦ n、GOSUB は（使用量＋7＋92）≦ n の

Review: an event jump picks the scene that suits its time; Following

A timeline jump set only the time, so the launch row left scene 1's lunar-orbit
camera at GET 0. TL_SCENES (timeline.js) cuts each scenario's time into spans,
each with the scene whose camera has a state then (scenario LEG and EVENT cards,
SP-4029 TIMELINE rows, SCNCAM/S7POSE/LMPIRO/LMDESC). A jump outside the current
scene's span sets that scene with its default look. Where no camera has a state
(Apollo 11 before orbit insertion and after entry interface, 3:00-3:15 on the
TLI coast; Apollo 8 outside lunar orbit) it opens the external view of the
Earth at 20 deg, with LC-39A marked. Each row's tooltip names the scene.

Companion, Resync and an Apollo in Real Time link start Following: as the replay
plays, the scene changes when the time leaves its span. A manual scene or time
change, or the FOLLOWING button, stops it.

events.title: netxduo: reassembly after a coalesced handshake prefix (40907d69)
events.message:
netxduo: reassembly after a coalesced handshake prefix (40907d69)

third_party/netxduo 6ba8038b -> 40907d69 (tinic/netxduo PR #11): when
a record carries complete handshake messages followed by the start of
one continued in later records, the TLS 1.2 and 1.3 client and server
state machines keep only the continued message at the start of the
record buffer, so reassembly neither overruns nor re-reads the
messages in front of it.

Pin only. nx_api.h and nx_secure/inc are unchanged between the two
commits, so the version pin stays 6.5.2. tls.library's
--wrap=_nx_secure_tls_client_handshake (src/tlslib/tls_resume.c) hands
any record holding a split message to the vendor function whole, with
the record buffer it was given, so the vendor change applies there
unchanged.

events.title: Review fixes: an empty sprite in a batch, a raster test that could not fail
events.message:
Review fixes: an empty sprite in a batch, a raster test that could not fail

A review of the follow-up commits found these.
- STDL_BlitSprites handed a sprite with no rows or no groups to the
  row loop, which counts with dbf and would have drawn 65536 of them;
  STDL_BlitSprite returns early. Only malformed bank data or a
  hand-built STDL_Sprite gets there, and it now falls back too.
- test_raster's check that STDL_ShowRasters(0) makes no copy compared

events.title: Sprites in a batch, and restores of whole groups for scenes of bobs
events.message:
Sprites in a batch, and restores of whole groups for scenes of bobs

One demo's bobs, fourteen pre-shifted 16x16 sprites restored from the
background every frame, cost about twice its own loops through the
library, and most of the difference was per call. Two additions:

- STDL_BlitSprites(spr, list, n, dst) draws one sprite at many
  places from a list of STDL_SpriteAt {x, y, frame}. What does not
  change between entries is worked out once. Each one wholly inside
  the clip, drawn by the aligned four-plane loop on the CPU, goes
  straight to that loop, now a static inline in stdl_internal.h so
  both files share it; sprite.o is unchanged at 5304 bytes. Anything
  else is handed to STDL_BlitSprite, so the pixels match
  (test_spritebatch, SBCHK). SPRCOST, plain ST: fourteen bobs 13.1 ->
  11.1ms. Its own object.
- STDL_DirtyWholeGroups(1) rounds each restore out to the groups it
  touches, a plain copy where exact edges are merged. That is right
  only where everything on the page is background or pushed, and the
  header says so. Sixteen 16x16 restores at x & 15 = 5: 12.7 ->
  7.9ms.

A bob is now about 10.6k cycles drawn and restored, against 14.9k on
the version the demo tried and 7.5k for its own loops.

events.title: Polygons: an edge's columns stepped in 68000, when nothing needs clamping
events.message:
Polygons: an edge's columns stepped in 68000, when nothing needs clamping

Profiled on a glenz-sized triangle, about 30 rows, the side walkers
cost about 150 cycles a row a side, more than the edge set-ups: two
clamp compares every row, in a loop gcc kept in C. A polygon whose
vertices all lie within the clip's columns cannot have an edge
outside them, so it needs no clamping. One that is also under 32768
rows tall keeps every edge value in sixteen bits. Such polygons now
step their edges in a five-instruction 68000 loop (C twin on the
host); the rest keep the clamped C.

PRIMCOST on a plain ST:
- the 22-row triangle 2.71 -> 2.29ms, level with STDL_XorHSpans
  (2.27);
- the 160-row diamond 17.3 -> 15.1ms, against 23.9 as spans.
PGCHK passes on the machine.

Also tried and dropped: a direct path for triangles, sorted into two
trapezoids sharing the long edge, with no walk round the vertices.
It came to the same 24k cycles a triangle as the general path. The
walk was not the cost; calls and set-up spread through the function
were, and the extra path was a kilobyte for nothing.

events.message:
FixDiv: the divisor's sign folded into the dividend, 424 -> 334 cycles

Tried for one demo's polygon slopes, STDL_FixDiv cost about 175
cycles a call more than the demo's own two-divu.w function. The
difference was the generality: both operands narrowed to 16 bits, and
both signs tested and applied. It now folds the divisor's sign into
the dividend once, leaving one sign to handle, and splits the first
quotient with a mask. MATHCHK on a plain ST: 424 -> 334 cycles,
against 314 for a form that takes only positive divisors (now a
comparison line in MATHCHK) and 630 for the C. Its cases, negative
divisors included, pass on the target.

events.title: Rasters: a fixed-address handler per second register, and an optional copy
events.message:
Rasters: a fixed-address handler per second register, and an optional copy

Tried in place of one demo's own raster handler, two costs showed.
- The general two-register handler fetched the second register's
  address and saved a register to hold it, a third dearer an
  interrupt than the demo's handler with the address written in.
  With colour 0 first, each of the fifteen possible second registers
  now has a handler of its own with both addresses as operands.
  RASTCHK on a plain ST, colour 0 plus 15: every second line 15% ->
  12% of the machine, every line 29% -> 25%.
- STDL_ShowRasters copied the shown table into the next one every
  frame, about 2.9k cycles, for a demo that rewrote every entry
  anyway. It now takes `keep`: 1 for the copy, for a program that
  changes a few entries, and 0 for none. The API is unreleased, so

events.title: Review fixes: polygon edges at int16_t's ends, staged SDL palette, and more
events.message:
Review fixes: polygon edges at int16_t's ends, staged SDL palette, and more

Three reviews of this branch (the asm, the C, the docs against the
code) found these.

Polygons:
- A column off either end of int16_t wrapped when it was narrowed into
  the edge tables, and a row drew 32000 pixels (ASan reproduced it on
  the host). Each side is now held within the clip plus one before it
  is narrowed.
- The divs.w fast path took edges up to 32767 columns wide but any
  height, so an edge taller than 32767 rows divided by a negative
  number on the target.
- Orientation comes from the top vertex's cross product, compared
  rather than subtracted; the signed area it replaced overflowed for
  big polygons.
- A clipped top from the far ends of int16_t steps in 64 bits.
- The fill now ignores the surface origin, as the contract says draw
  primitives do. SET takes STDL_TRANSPARENT as STDL_FillRect does.
- test_polygon gains these extremes, and PGCHK on the target fails
  without the divs.w fix.

Palette staging: SDL_SetPalette(SDL_PHYSPAL) wrote through
STDL_SetColour, which is never staged, so TPALETTE -stage did nothing.
A raw-word hook now stages it. Staging marks registers one by one, so
a staged physical write changes only the register it names, and
leftover state cannot reach a later STDL_Init.
tests/hatari/palstg.c, counted by palsplit.py, measures 99 and 100
frames of 100 split unstaged, through STDL_SetColours and the SDL
shim, and 1 and 2 staged (the switch-over frames).

Music:
- A voice handed back by an effect during a pause stays silent; it
  used to drone the held note.
- A seek is playing again before it writes the state, so an effect
  ending meanwhile restores its voice rather than muting it.

Rasters: reopening after a later Timer C hook no longer saves the
prefix as its own successor, which would loop on the first tick.

libcalls.sh:
- It stops when objdump fails or yields no disassembly. Before, it
  passed on anything.
- It now finds the float conversions (__floatsisf, __fixdfsi) and the
  64-bit helpers.

Docs: corrected wherever the reviews found them wrong, and every
measured figure now has a probe in the repo:
- PRIMCOST gains polygon and aligned-text cases;
- IXCHK times the pre-shift;
- RASTCHK measures the general handlers too and, built
  -DRASTCHK_NOPREFIX, the hold without the Timer C prefix, counted by
  rstill.py: 2 of 144 frames late with it, 16 without.

POLYDEMO's star is now a fan of triangles that really share edges.

events.title: Rasters: STDL_OpenRasters, Timer B shared safely with the borders
events.message:
Rasters: STDL_OpenRasters, Timer B shared safely with the borders

Programs wanting rasters (colour registers changed every few lines)
wrote their own Timer B handler. Two things went wrong that the
library can prevent. Nothing stopped it running while an open border
also used Timer B. And the terminate path did not know about it, so
an abnormal exit left the Timer B and Timer C vectors pointing into
freed memory.

STDL_OpenRasters(lines, reg1, reg2) changes one or two colour
registers every `lines` lines from a table:
- STDL_RasterTable is the table to fill and STDL_ShowRasters shows
  it from the next frame.
- There are three tables, so the program never writes one that this
  frame or the next VBL reads. A new one starts as a copy of the last
  shown.
- A VBL callback restarts Timer B from entry 0 before each picture.
- A Timer C prefix, as the borders use, lets Timer B in during TOS's
  200Hz handler.
- Colour 0, which is also the border, has its own quicker handlers.
- stdl_timerb_owner in video.c makes rasters and borders refuse each
  other.
- The teardown is vectors and registers only, on the terminate path.

Measured on a plain ST:
- with colour 0 first, every second line costs 11% of the machine
  (15% with a second register) and every line 22% (29%);
- with a fixed table and the program idle, a stripe edge is a line
  late in 6 frames of 186, 13 with the general handler, and 184
  without the Timer C prefix;
- RASTCHK aborted with rasters open, and the desktop came back in its
  own colours.

test_raster covers the refusals, the open state, the VBL arming, the
tables (never the shown or the armed one handed out) and both
teardowns, against host stand-ins for the MFP and vectors. RASTCHK
measures the cost and checks the two refusals on the machine. The
new RASTERS example draws copper bars in colour 0 and a gradient in
colour 15. AGENTS.md records the ownership lesson.

events.title: Polygons: STDL_FillPolygon, set, XOR, OR or clear into a colour's planes
events.message:
Polygons: STDL_FillPolygon, set, XOR, OR or clear into a colour's planes

A filled polygon meant building a span list for STDL_HSpans or
STDL_XorHSpans, which clip and find the row for every span on its
own. One demo measured over a thousand cycles a span drawing a glenz
object. STDL_FillPolygon fills a convex polygon directly:
- each side's edges are stepped exactly (an integer and a remainder,
  so nothing drifts) into a table of clipped columns;
- 68000 fills the rows from the two tables, for SET and XOR at either
  plane pair;
- OR and CLEAR use the C, which is also the twin.

Coverage follows the rectangle's rule, top and left edges in, bottom
and right out. Faces sharing an edge then tile with no seam, which
XOR needs, and a rectangle's corners fill exactly STDL_FillRect's
rectangle. The ops take a colour's planes, so a glenz draws each
face into a plane of its own.

Measured on a plain ST:
- a 160-row diamond XORed: 16.8ms, against 23.9 through
  STDL_XorHSpans;
- a 22-row triangle: 2.6ms against 2.3. Each edge's set-up is a
  divide, about 1000 cycles, so faces of a few rows are cheaper as
  spans, and the header and skill say so.

test_polygon checks random convex polygons against an exact rational
reference (every op, budgets 4/2/3, clips, origins, masks), plus
split polygons XORed seamlessly and the rectangle case.
tests/hatari/pgchk.c runs it on the machine; it passes, and a broken
XOR fails it. The new POLYDEMO example XORs three turning shapes into
three planes, its rotation through STDL_MulS16. Its own object, so
programs that never call it do not carry it.

only check of the asm, and times the conversion. On st:

events.title: Text: 8-pixel fonts on their own grid through movep
events.message:
Text: 8-pixel fonts on their own grid through movep

An 8-pixel glyph at x & 7 == 0 is one byte of each plane per row,
the bytes two apart, and movep.l reads or writes all four in one
instruction. stdl_glyph8_rows doubles the row out to a long mask and
merges with d ^= (d ^ c) & m. Its gain is less in the row than
around it: five asm operands where the general glyph rows take nine,
which gcc reloaded for every character. That overhead was about 135
instructions a character, measured with the profiler, against about
140 for the eight rows themselves.

STDL_DrawText takes it for a whole line when the font is 8 wide and
x is on the byte grid; glyphs cut by the clip still take the general
rows. STDL_DrawChar takes it for an uncut cell. Each lives in its own
out-of-line function, because as a test inside the general loop it
made unaligned text 5% slower through register allocation. Measured
on a plain ST, 8x8 font, colour 5:
- a 39-character line at x = 0: 13.9 -> 9.55ms;
- one character at x = 0: 552 -> 520us;
- STDL_DrawChar at x = 8: 497 -> 447us;
- unaligned text: +1-1.4%, the cost of the test that chooses.

The C twin works in plane words, since the host keeps them in its
own byte order. PIXCHK full passes on st, test_text_model included.

events.title: Fills: whole groups as rows of stores, four groups to a movem
events.message:
Fills: whole groups as rows of stores, four groups to a movem

A fill of whole groups that was not a full-width block went through
the edge-merge row loop. That loop read and rewrote the first and
last group of every row, about 100 cycles each where a store costs
24. fill_groups stores each row from its end down, four groups to a
movem.l of eight registers and the rest a group at a time, or at a
plane budget of 2 a long a group with planes 2-3 left alone. Full
rows still take the single memset or fill_longpairs.

The branch sits where fill_block was called for those fills, and
nowhere else. Written in ahead of the other paths, or moved out of
line with them, it changed fill_rows' register allocation and made
a 1x1 fill 2-3% dearer (148 instructions became 165). As it is, the
1x1 path is the same 148 instructions it was.

SPRCOST on a plain ST against the previous commit:
- 64x32 whole-group fills 0.54 (2031 -> 1089us);
- 16x16 0.87;
- unaligned fills and the 1x1 fixed cost unchanged;
- 86 cases 0.973, floor 1.002.
BLITCHK on an STE passes at every budget, and its CPU timing at
budget 2 goes 1330 -> 1260ms. PIXCHK full passes on st. Pixel-path
text 34412 -> 34620.

events.title: Dirty: restore by offset when the background is the page's shape
events.message:
Dirty: restore by offset when the background is the page's shape

STDL_DirtyRestore replayed each rectangle through STDL_BlitSurfaceEx.
That set-up clips both surfaces, asks the BLiTTER's rules and
dispatches on phase and masks, and it was most of the cost of a
sprite-sized restore. Restoring a page from a background of the same
size and stride, with no origins and no masks, a rectangle is an
offset into both, two edge masks and a run of whole groups. With no
BLiTTER and the default plane budget, DirtyRestore now does exactly
that:
- the rectangle is clipped to the page's clip;
- the edge groups are merged as longs;
- the rest goes through the asm row copy;
- nothing is rounded out.
Anything else takes the general path as before.

SPRCOST on a plain ST, 16 restores of 16x16:
- at group edges (a new case), 9.9 -> 6.3ms;
- at x & 15 = 5, 18.6 -> 14.9ms; the edges' merges, about 160 cycles
  a row each, are most of what is left.
Over all 86 cases 0.993 (floor 1.002). test_dirty compares the
direct path with STDL_BlitSurfaceEx byte for byte over random
rectangles and random page clips, and breaking its clip or its right

events.title: Sprites: the aligned four-plane loop in 68000
events.message:
Sprites: the aligned four-plane loop in 68000

A pre-shifted sprite away from the screen's edges, or an unshifted
one at phase 0, ran through the C row loop, which gcc 4.6 compiles a
plane word at a time and reloads around every store: about 300
cycles for a mixed group. Written out, each group's mask is doubled
into a long and the planes go a pair at a time, an and.l and an or.l
each, with transparent groups skipped and opaque ones stored as
before. That is about 160 cycles a group. A clip cover or a plane
budget of 2 keeps the C, which is also the asm's twin on the host.

SPRCOST on a plain ST (Hatari), against the previous commit:
- pre-shifted sprites 0.69 of their time (16x16 1333 -> 952us,
  32x32 3115 -> 1982us);
- phase-0 sprites 0.61-0.74;
- everything else unchanged.
Geometric mean over all 85 cases 0.948, same-binary floor 1.002.
PIXCHK full passes on st. Pixel-path text 34272 -> 34412.

events.title: Music: play from memory, position, seek and register read-back
events.message:
Music: play from memory, position, seek and register read-back

STDL_MusicFromMemory plays an STM linked into the program in place,
so a demo can be one file. STDL_MusicFrame is the music's own clock
to sync to, STDL_MusicLength the range, and STDL_SeekMusic jumps
there. STDL_GetMusicRegisters copies out the stream's 14 registers
for VU meters without reading the chip.

The stream is delta-coded. A seek replays the deltas from the
nearest key, and the loader keeps a key every 256 frames: the frame's
offset and the registers before it. It then writes the whole state
to the chip, every voice rather than just what the next frame
changes. The keys replace an offset per frame, 4 bytes a frame (21KB
for a two-minute song), of which the player only ever used the
loop's.

Resuming after a pause now writes that state back too. Before, pause
silenced the voices, and a note held across it stayed silent until
the stream next changed it.

test_music replays a 700-frame stream alongside the player, checking:
- the clock;
- the chip and the read-back;
- seeks either side of each key;
- resume, the loop, file against memory;
- a truncated stream refused.

Breaking the resume or the keys fails it. PLAYMUS records the same
in Hatari as on main (spectral correlation 0.999). The new MUSICVU
example draws a VU meter and a position bar and seeks with the arrow
keys.

events.title: Palette: STDL_StagePalette, and STDL_HW444 for constant tables
events.message:
Palette: STDL_StagePalette, and STDL_HW444 for constant tables

A palette written from the main loop lands wherever the beam is, and
that frame shows the old colours above it and the new below.
STDL_StagePalette(1) converts each change when it is made and writes
it in the next vertical blank. The changes it covers are
SetPalette, SetColours, the SDL shim and FadeTo. Measured in Hatari
with a colour switched at mid-screen every frame: 300 of 300 frames
split unstaged, 0 of 305 staged.

Overscan already staged its writes while a border was open. It now
shares the mechanism, in a new palstage.c, each user holding a bit,
so opening and closing a border no longer clears a program's own
staging. The pending flag drops before a stage is converted, so a
VBL landing midway cannot write half a palette, which the border's
copy could. release_hardware clears the hook with the VBL slots, so
staging reinstalls if the program inits again. STDL_SetColour stays
immediate for raster tricks.

STDL_HW444(0xRGB) converts a constant with four bits per channel to
the rotated hardware word at compile time; a raw 0xC72 shows green.

TPALETTE gains -stage. test_palette covers the staging cases (both
users, off writing what waits, a full queue, reinstall after release)
and HW444 against the run-time conversion.

events.title: Arithmetic: stdl_math.h, and the build fails on a new libgcc call
events.message:
Arithmetic: stdl_math.h, and the build fails on a new libgcc call

gcc 4.6 turns any multiply or divide it cannot prove 16-bit into a
__mulsi3 or __divsi3 call, and what it can prove moves with the code
around the expression. Measured, the calls come from mixed widths
(two bytes, s16 by int, s16 by u16), from a loop counter that ivopts
rewrites as a 32-bit variable whatever its casts, from every product
at -O1, from any divide or % by a non-power-of-two, and from a
difference of pointers to a 6-byte struct. On a plain ST a call costs
about 350 cycles against 40 for muls.w, and 630 against 140 for
divs.w (MATHCHK).

stdl_math.h makes the instructions public as STDL_MulS16,
STDL_MulU16, STDL_DivS16 and STDL_DivU16, inline asm with C twins.
It adds STDL_FixDiv, a 16.16 (a << 16) / b in two chained divu.w
(420 cycles against 630). test_math checks them against wide
arithmetic, and tests/hatari/mathchk.c runs the same cases on the
target and times them.

tools/libcalls.sh lists every libgcc arithmetic call per function
from the objects' relocations. With an allowlist it fails on any
that is new or more frequent. The cross build runs it as
libcallcheck against tests/libcalls.allow, where each of the 59
remaining sites says why it is not hot. Ports can run the same
script on their own objects.

Four per-frame sites are fixed:
- the music tick's volume scaling (u8 * u8);
- STDL_FrameLimit's 200 / fps;
- the ring pump's half offset;
- STDL_FadeTo, which spent 48 multiplies and 48 divides a step after
  the blank. It now works each step out before the blank and writes
  it straight after, with test_palette checking every step against
  the old formula.

The skill's profiler recipe gains a demo's Hatari findings:
- `symbols prg` loads the program's own symbols;
- a save must happen while profiling is on;
- the saved call graph carries per-function cycles, and is where the
  libgcc calls show up.

events.title: v0.2.7: external debugging with DeZog, a tape deck, assembler syntax colours
events.message:
v0.2.7: external debugging with DeZog, a tape deck, assembler syntax colours

### New: external debugging and code loading
Work in VS Code (or any editor) and let the emulator follow your build. Everything is off until you turn it on in *Settings → External debugging* or on the command line. The servers listen on `127.0.0.1` only.

- **GDB server** (`--gdb`, port 12000) for [DeZog](https://github.com/maziac/DeZog)'s `mame` remote: source-level debugging with breakpoints (conditional ones too), step into/over/out, pause and continue, watchpoints, and memory and register views and edits. DeZog's breakpoints also show in the emulator's Debugger window. Plain gdb clients work too, along with MAME's `monitor` commands.
- **Command API** (`--api`, port 6128) and the new **`cpcse-ctl`** program beside `cpcse.exe`, for build scripts. It can load a `.bin`, `.dsk`, `.sna`, `.cpr` or tape and run it, type on the keyboard, press keys, read and write memory and registers, set breakpoints and watchpoints, disassemble, step, wait for a stop, and take PNG or BMP screenshots. Requests are one line each, as JSON or a short form (`cpcse-ctl load build/game.bin 0x4000 entry`).
- **Auto-reload** (`--watch`): your build's output is loaded again and restarted every time it changes. That works for a `.bin`, or a `.dsk` with a command typed after it.
- **New command-line options:** `--gdb[=port]`, `--api[=port]`, `--load file[@addr]`, `--watch file[@addr]`, `--run entry|addr`, `--reset`, `--command "RUN\"GAME\n"` and `--symbols file`. Symbols can come from RASM, sjasmplus, pasmo or WinAPE files, or `EQU` lists, and addresses can be given as labels.
- **Documentation:** `docs/external-debugging.md` has a DeZog `launch.json`, a VS Code build task, and every option and command.

### New: tape deck
In the Media window, *Media → Tape* and *Debug → Chips → Tape*:
- a **tape counter** with a reset button
- the tape's time position, and which block it is in out of how many
- **rewind to the start, back a block, play, pause, stop, fast forward, eject**
- a list of the tape's blocks to jump to
- a MOTOR light

### New: assembler syntax colours
The assembler's editor colours each part of the code in its own colour: instructions, registers and conditions, directives, numbers, strings, comments, label definitions and the labels they use. **Colours...** lets you change each colour or switch the colouring off, and your choice is saved.

### New: Eject for cartridges and snapshots
Cartridges and snapshots now have an **Eject** button in the Media window and the Media menu, like discs and tapes. Ejecting restarts the same machine without it. The Snapshot section shows which snapshot is loaded.

### New: windows that fit when they're narrow
Rows of buttons, toolbars and text now wrap to the window's width in every window, so a narrow or docked window shows everything instead of cutting it off. This covers the Machine, Media, Settings, debugger, Chips, Memory, GFX9000, DSK editor, assembler, CSL and printer windows.

### New: GFX9000 VRAM image as the display shows it
*Debug → GFX9000 → VRAM image* now colours VRAM the way the picture does: each layer uses its own palette offset, sprite patterns use their sprite's palette, and transparent dots show the backdrop colour. In P1, **layers A and B are shown side by side**, and hovering over a dot shows which layer it belongs to.

### Download
`CPCSyntaxError-win64-v0.2.7.zip`: unzip anywhere and run `cpcse.exe`. `cpcse-ctl.exe` and `docs/external-debugging.md` are in the zip too. On Linux, build from source (README, *Building from source → Linux*). The build includes `cpcse-ctl`. The YRW801 (OPL4) and SP0256-AL2 (speech) ROMs are not included; the emulator asks for them when they're needed.

events.title: fix(kmsdrm): GLES-first context ladder and runtime-matched ImGui GLSL (#2379)
events.message:
fix(kmsdrm): GLES-first context ladder and runtime-matched ImGui GLSL (#2379)

* fix(gui): pick the ImGui GLSL version from the runtime GL context

The backend's hardcoded desktop default (#version 130) does not compile
on GL 2.1 contexts, so opening the GUI with F12 while emulation ran
aborted with a shader-compile IM_ASSERT on Raspberry Pi 3 (vc4 via
KMSDRM, where the context ladder lands on its GL 2.1 Compatibility
tier). The startup GUI was unaffected because it renders through the
SDL renderer path; only the F12 re-entry routes ImGui through the
emulation GL context.

Derive the version from the live context instead: GL 2.x gets
"#version 120", GLES2 "#version 100", GLES3+ "#version 300 es", and
desktop GL >= 3.0 keeps the backend default (130/410, 150 on Apple).
The overlay's duplicated version detection now uses the same helper.

* fix(gfx): match SDL3's lowercase kmsdrm driver name and keep desktop GL as the KMSDRM ladder fallback

set_opengl_attributes() classified KMSDRM with a case-sensitive
strcmp(drv, "KMSDRM"), which never matches SDL3's lowercase "kmsdrm",
so KMSDRM silently walked the plain desktop ladder. Fixing the
comparison alone would regress RPi3: the ES-only ladder tier requests
GLES 3.0, vc4 only has GLES 2.0, and both attempts failing demoted the
monitor to the software renderer.

The ladder selection now lives in a pure, unit-tested table
(gl_context_ladder) with three profiles: Desktop (unchanged),
GlesPreferred (KMSDRM: ES 3.0 first, then desktop Core/Legacy tiers so
vc4 keeps hardware GL 2.1), and GlesOnly (Android/iOS/USE_GLES3,
unchanged strict ES ladder).

events.title: fix(log): keep startup migration messages in the log file (#2378)
events.message:
fix(log): keep startup migration messages in the log file (#2378)

* fix(log): keep startup migration messages in the log file

Legacy layout migration runs before logging_init() opens the log, so its
write_log() output was discarded and the log was then truncated. The
"Migration Review Needed" notice told users to check a log that held
nothing about the failure.

Buffer messages logged before logging_init() and replay them into the
log once it opens. The notice now names the log file path, or explains
how to enable logging when it is off.

* fix(log): re-arm startup log capture on every amiberry_main run

libretro can run amiberry_main() again via retro_load_game() without
reloading the core. Capture was disabled after the first logging_init(),
so a second run lost its migration messages again. Re-arm the capture at
the start of each run, and end it on the logging_init() restart path.

* fix(log): reopen a closed log and report when it cannot open

logging_init() skipped reopening the log on its third and later calls,
even when logging_cleanup() had already closed it after a libretro core
run. Only skip while the file is still open.

The migration notice pointed at the log file even when fopen() failed
and the buffered details were discarded. Say the log could not be opened
in that case.

events.title: feat(crash_detect): inframe_hang signature for absurd blits (#740)
events.message:
feat(crash_detect): inframe_hang signature for absurd blits (#740)

The blitter runs synchronously inside one register write, so a garbage
B_COUNT can keep retro_run from returning for hours -- the per-frame
watchdog never gets a turn and the frontend sees a hung core with no log
line. Check at blit dispatch (both engines, memo and compare paths):
when B_COUNT asks for more than 2^24 pixels, log [CRASH-DETECT]
inframe_hang with the counts, the command, A1 base and all three
processor PCs, then run the blit as before. Log-only, latched like the
other signatures, one multiply per blit.

Pixels are counted the way the accurate (default) engine runs them:
outer 0 = 65536 lines (JTRM BLIT_COUNT), inner 0 = one step (<= 64 px;
BlitterMidsummer2 stops on the bit-15 crossing). Counting inner 0 as
65536 per the JTRM flagged Troy Aikman, Double Dragon V and Brutal Sports
Football, which write B_COUNT=0 at boot and run fine.

Reproducers: Music Demo (ScatoLOGIC) --bios writes B_COUNT=$2710826D
(334M pixels) at frame 158; DEMO1 (bin) in HLE freezes at frame 400 on
the accurate engine.

The issue proposed sampling PCs in the JaguarExecuteNew slice loop. That
loop advances emulated time on every iteration, so the frame always ends
unless a single call inside it never returns -- and a sampler there never
runs during such a call. Every in-frame hang sampled (Music Demo, DEMO1,
DEMO1B, Painter) was inside BlitterMidsummer2.

cart_boot_matrix.sh now lists inframe_hang among a timed-out row's
signatures (cd_boot_matrix.sh already reports the first CRASH-DETECT line).

events.title: debugger: route debugger window writes through the emulation thread
events.message:
debugger: route debugger window writes through the emulation thread

Debugger windows changed emulator state directly from the UI thread,
concurrently with the running emulation (risk of crashes or corrupted
data). All such changes now go through the dbgapi command queue and are
executed by the emulation thread:

- I/O Ports: history capacity/clear, Reset Activity, per-port reset
- Breakpoints: Delete All, load from file, reset hit counter
- Memory Heatmap: mode, Reset, region reset, import Add/Sub
- Memory Map: banking (set/clear masks), DMD
- Event Viewer: mode, categories, import, Pause/Auto-mark on match
  triggers (new eventlog_trigger module)
- Memory Browser Freeze Bytes, Callstack Active/Reset, Ctrl+R refresh
- MemExt Map: own request mechanism (works without the debugger too)

Bug fixes (present in 2.0.5):
- MemExt Map (PEHU): Apply without changes remapped the banks
- I/O Ports: saved history capacity and recorded-port mask were ignored
  after start
- DMD from Memory Map and --run-mzf bypassed the OUT (CEh) path, leaving
  CTC0 GATE0 blocked after --run-mzf in MZ-800 mode
- MCP debugger_activate/deactivate did not recompute CPU callbacks

Also: removed unused debugger_change_dmd/debugger_mmap_*, corrected
heatmap docs (sizes, region counts), 5 new i18n strings in 10 languages.
Each change has a regression test.

events.title: grm-rr5p: RUNTIME_SOURCE for loads of RAM cells nothing in the program stores to
events.message:
grm-rr5p: RUNTIME_SOURCE for loads of RAM cells nothing in the program stores to

StoredValueScanner.neverStoredTo: a load of a writable, non-volatile cell is
RUNTIME_SOURCE (honest NOTE) only when no write reference and no plain-operand
store targets it, no absolute-indexed store's base..base+$FF window covers it,
and -- for zero page -- no indexed/indirect store exists anywhere in the
program. A cell with ANY store is a parameter latch and stays ANALYZER_LIMIT.
One cached store census per program modification number.

Phase 1 measurement (bead comment): the naive writable-block rule flipped two
latches (nesmirrortest c102, dbz_datach cc2a); this rule keeps both WARNING.

Goldens: banktest2 0816 and nesmirrortest c034/c107/c142 WARNING -> NOTE
(untouched cells); criteria banktest2 C3 and nesmirrortest M6 updated, M5
(c102 latch) unchanged. 8 RuntimeSourceNoStoreProgramTest cases.

Also: retire contra's grm-akiv question in human-research-todo (owner: 849f is
7 entries, 86cd a separate table) -> follow-up grm-t223.

During HTMLM_Export and HTMLM_PrintBegin the gadget holds its lock for

from other tasks are ignored.

events.title: Add a debugging console, over one shared breakpoint list
events.message:
Add a debugging console, over one shared breakpoint list

Debug > Console (Cmd-Shift-K) is a command line onto the machine. It reads
the Apple II monitor's own syntax (300, 300.3FF, 300: A9 00, 300L, 300G, and
E1/2000 on a IIgs) and a debugger's words: m, w, f, l, find for memory; g,
s, n, finish, pause, until for running; r, ?, sym, stack, trace for looking;
reset and reboot; and bp, bl, bd, be, bx for breakpoints of every kind,
soft switches and the beam included. Addresses are numbers or names, and
values may be expressions. An address in the output opens the CPU debugger
there, Tab completes commands and names, the history is kept, and a stop
the debugger judges is reported in its words. The parser
(console_command) touches no machine and is tested on its own; the console
is tested by typing into a real //e.

Every window's breakpoints are now one list the App owns and applies to the
core when it changes: execution, access and stack, soft switch and beam. The
CPU debugger lists switch breakpoints with the rest, so they gain conditions
and hit counts, and its beam breakpoints are no longer a list of their own.
Settings from before are read into the one list. The console applies a
change itself before anything it runs, since the machine runs on its own
thread and a breakpoint set one command before a go was otherwise missed.

events.title: fix(display): correct smart horizontal centering offset (#2377)
events.message:
fix(display): correct smart horizontal centering offset (#2377)

* fix(display): correct smart horizontal centering offset

Compute the display window position from the line renderer's own pixel origin and use the correct sign and scaling for the offset. Keep the previous offset only when the whole window stays visible with it. Mirrors tonioni/WinUAE#518.

* fix(display): undo the line's centering shift when latching the origin

internal_pixel_start_cnt is latched after get_line() applied linetoscr_x_adjust, so on shifted lines it already contains the previous offset. Feeding it back into center_image() made offsets beyond the hysteresis alternate between frames (e.g. 9 and 49). Record the shift each line was drawn with and remove it; ignore lines whose origin never latched.

events.title: fix(native): zombies do not count as running; a stop waits for the leader's exit; unknown monitor output is an error
events.message:
fix(native): zombies do not count as running; a stop waits for the leader's exit; unknown monitor output is an error

In a container whose PID 1 never reaps, as GitHub's job containers, an
orphan stays a zombie, and kill(pid, 0) and kill(-group, 0) called it
running: stops waited out their grace period and then failed. On Linux the
supervisor now reads the state from /proc and treats Z and X as ended. A
group of zombies counts as gone before Node reports the leader's exit (macOS
too), so a stop now also waits for that exit: right after a c64_window move
the old VICE was still listed as running.

A profile or memory map that VICE prints in another form read as empty
(found on macOS); it is now an error that quotes the lines.

Tested: the process tests and the full live suite in a Debian 13 container
with tail -f /dev/null as PID 1 (448 pass, 50 skipped); full live suite
here, 498 of 498.

events.title: Header cache: ignore the screen witness during the race
events.message:
Header cache: ignore the screen witness during the race

The witness (8 bytes of the blue lap digit) told hupd whether the
screen had been repainted. When blue leads, its column blinks, and
cars plus the shared background and priority mask change those
bytes: every call then reset all four columns, which never finished
before the next blink, so the other scores stayed blank. In the race
the header is only repainted at the start, where hlab already clears
the cache, so the witness is skipped there.

events.title: Open one Ensoniq oscillator in full
events.message:
Open one Ensoniq oscillator in full

Clicking an oscillator's row (anywhere but its mute) replaces the list with
that oscillator alone: its state and mode, pitch, frequency, resolution,
volume, interrupt and channel, its table, pointer, position, accumulator and
last byte read, and its seven registers by their numbers in the chip. Its
table fills the rest of the card as a wave that zooms and pans as the sound
RAM does, down to 16 bytes with each byte's value, and can follow the
playhead a screen at a time. All oscillators, or Escape, goes back to the
list, and the arrows step to the oscillators either side.

The sound RAM and the table share one set of wave helpers: the view and its
clamping, zooming about the pointer, panning, the zoom buttons, the drawing
and the address ticks.

events.title: Break on soft switches, on every machine
events.message:
Break on soft switches, on every machine

A breakpoint can now stop the machine when a soft switch changes, or when
it turns on or off; on a IIgs, when one of its registers changes or its
bits under a mask hold a value. MachineDebug checks them after every
instruction while any exist, against the state rather than the switches'
addresses, so a change made by a read, by STATEREG or by the machine itself
counts. Both conditions fire on entry, a step only notes a change, and a
reset starts each one afresh. A stop names the instruction that moved the
switch: "PAGE2 on, by $2003".

Which switches a machine has comes from one catalog in the core
(soft_switch_catalog), so a II+ no longer lists the //e's memory switches
and only a IIgs lists its registers. A hasCassette capability drops the
cassette switches from a //c and a IIgs. A IIgs's registers are read from
bank $E0, where the I/O page always is, and its pushbuttons are reported.

The native app has a Soft Switches window with a breakpoint menu on every
row, and the CPU debugger says why it stopped. The browser's Soft Switch
window is built from the same catalog and gains the same breakpoints.

events.title: fix(jit): handle shift counts 32-63 in ARM register shifts (#2376)
events.message:
fix(jit): handle shift counts 32-63 in ARM register shifts (#2376)

A 68k register shift count is taken modulo 64, but the ARM64 32-bit
variable shift uses the count modulo 32, and LSL_wwi/LSR_wwi encode only
five bits. With flags not needed, LSL/ASL Dx,Dy therefore kept bits it
should have shifted out: for .w, counts 32-47 left the low word
unchanged or partly shifted (VirusCheckerII crashed with a Line-A error).

- jnf_LSL_{b,w,l}_reg: shift in 64 bits, so every 6-bit count is exact;
  .l clears the upper half afterwards.
- jnf_LSL_l_reg, jnf_LSR_l_reg: the constant-count shortcut compared the
  register number with 31 instead of the count, so constant counts
  32-63 reached the immediate shifts and were encoded modulo 32.
- jff_LSR_l_imm: clear the result for counts 32 and above instead of
  encoding them modulo 32.
- jnf_LSL/LSR_{b,w}_imm: limit the count before folding a constant
  operand, which shifted a 32-bit value by up to 63 bits in C.
- jff_ASL_{w,l}_imm: CLS cannot exceed 31, so for constant counts of 32
  and above V was set even for a zero operand. V is now set when the
  operand is non-zero.

The ARM32 midfuncs had the same constant-count and folding mistakes and
get the same fixes; their register shifts already use eight count bits.

Fixes #2375

events.title: Fix Android in-game menu crash (KeyNotFoundException)
events.message:
Fix Android in-game menu crash (KeyNotFoundException)

The in-game menu (SettlerMenu) crashed the app when opened on Android.
Root cause: TextureAtlas.GetOffset threw KeyNotFoundException for sprite
indices missing from the texture atlas (game data does not contain every
sprite the SettlerMenu box draws). The exception propagated out of the SDL
run loop and closed the app without logging.

- TextureAtlas.GetOffset: use TryGetValue, return atlas origin (0,0) for
  missing sprites instead of throwing.
- TextureAtlasManager.AddGuiElements: add a 1x1 placeholder sprite for
  missing sprites so the sprite index space stays contiguous.
- Interface.OpenPopup: log the full exception before rethrowing.
- MainActivity: log exceptions from the run loop and the touch-event drain
  so future SDL-thread failures are visible in logcat.
- Add game-data import via the system file picker for first start without
  bundled SPAE.PA (copyrighted data is never shipped).
- Document the fix in Android.md.

events.title: fix: what two real Bruce Lee releases found in DXA, Ghidra, BASIC and the unpacker
events.message:
fix: what two real Bruce Lee releases found in DXA, Ghidra, BASIC and the unpacker

The whole workflow ran on two releases of Bruce Lee from corpus/, through
the MCP and every skill script.

- dxa prints a two-byte .word line with spaces instead of a tab, so every
  real 64 KiB image was refused. The listing parser accepts both.
- Ghidra can give one generated name to two thunks, and the importer refused
  the whole result. A repeated generated name now gets its address.
- "SYS2073 TCS-CRUNCH!" was reported as computed. BASIC ends the expression
  at the first byte that is no operator, so it is $0819.
- The unpacker's "unlikely" and c64_keyboard's reach are now described
  honestly: a simple cruncher can look like code, and typed keys reach only
  programs that read them through the KERNAL.

Tested: unit tests for each case; full live suite with real VICE and
Ghidra, 491 of 491.

events.title: fix(host): complete drive stops at the computer's next instruction (D22); fix Windows CI
events.message:
fix(host): complete drive stops at the computer's next instruction (D22); fix Windows CI

A drive 8 checkpoint makes VICE enter the monitor from inside the drive CPU,
with the computer's CPU halfway through an instruction, and makes drive 8
the text monitor's default device. A computer register write was then lost,
the first frame count ended one frame early, and load, disassemble, search,
memmap and the stopwatch acted on the drive. The session now runs the
computer to its next instruction after such a stop, and every
device-dependent text command selects the computer first.

The Windows CI job failed because the fake Ghidra installation in the test
had no analyzeHeadless.bat, which discovery looks for on Windows.

Tested: a new live regression test fails without the fix; full live suite
with real VICE and Ghidra, 489 of 489.
