events.title: test(e2e): two whole-game runs through play(), scripted by outcome (U30)
events.message:
test(e2e): two whole-game runs through play(), scripted by outcome (U30)

tests/test_full_game_e2e.py drives play() with a ScreenPlayer that reads
each screen and picks the next key; no key list is fixed in advance.
Both start states are built in the test under all-faithful house rules
and loaded from a save.

- Early win (AE4): a rank-9 solo boss with no tip and no flag buys pub
  tips until 3 and 5 come up, walks to cell 569 and wins the transport
  (x5, rank 10), then to 861 and wins the mayor hit (x6). The next turn
  start shows the victory screen and the ranking, with no turn menu
  after it. Fights are aimed from the board, without rigging the RNG.
- Jail: a rank-6 boss is stopped at a roadblock, surrenders, refuses
  the lawyer and is sentenced to 3 months. Exactly three jail screens
  follow (3, 2, 1), with upkeep on each skipped turn, then a free turn.

Each run takes under a second and fails fast on a step budget when its
feature is broken. Both passed across seeds 0-99.

Refs #144

project.status: active
project.notes: Clean-room, source-faithful engine for Dungeon Master, Chaos Strikes Back, Dungeon Master II, Dungeon Master Nexus and Theron's Quest. Dungeon Master 1 PC/DOS 3.4 is playable/source-locked; a 2 October original-media regression reaches and defeats the first map-1 group, while 3 October Atari ST checks carry authenticated SND1 data through a live food-swallow event into the SDL queue on English, German and French editions. Audible output, overlap arbitration and PSG parity remain unverified. A persisted authenticated collection root now reaches source-owned startup state for DM1 PC 3.4, CSB FM Towns and DM2 DOS through the normal menu handoff, without establishing later gameplay, every edition or physical desktop input. DM2 Macintosh work remains bounded to source-backed controls, big-endian wall actuators and viewport hitboxes. Theron's retail JP route now reaches Akutuba and the first-person dungeon view, but its native BRAM remains an empty save and the emulator autosave does not restore a usable viewport. Nexus remains active real-data bring-up.

project.title: papple2
project.display_title: papple2 — Apple II reverse-engineering emulator/debugger
project.status: active
project.notes: Small Apple II emulator deliberately built as a reverse-engineering/debugging instrument rather than a general player. Its ApplePy-derived core now has a completed rebuilt instrumentation layer (tag core-complete): memory access by kind, hook lists, after-instruction callbacks and method-attached experiments. The next phase is an IPython workbench using dynamic analysis first and static disassembly to fill unexecuted holes. Lode Runner's byte-identical XekriRedmane reconstruction is explicitly an external grading oracle, never an analysis input.

project.title: 2.5vibePlus4
project.display_title: 2.5vibePlus4 — Plus/4 TED raycasting SDK
project.notes: Standalone native Plus/4 TED 2.5D SDK derived solely from the 3Dvibe64 2.5D pipeline, not its polygon engine. Python builder, native assembly, bitmap/double buffering and four original/optimized automatic/interactive demos. Assembly guide describes 6502-compatible instructions; exact native CPU variant merits follow-up. Upstream documents VICE xplus4 testing; physical hardware has not been tested. Code/data are PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. The project is original Commodore Plus/4 / TED SDK/homebrew work, so source CPU is not applicable; its checked-in 6502-compatible assembly and 64tass build establish 6502 output without implying a narrower chip variant or RAM minimum.

project.title: UnifiedFloppyTool
project.display_title: UnifiedFloppyTool — Amiga/Atari disk preservation
source_language: floppy disk formats and flux data
project.notes: Forensic floppy toolkit covering Amiga, Atari and other disk/flux formats. Current work raises A2R from T2 to T1, fixes Apple 5.25-inch seam/checksum handling, pairs verification sectors by ID, and wires effective settings into the conversion plan: retry count reaches SCP→D64 and clock correction reaches the SCP→ADF flux decoder only when advanced options are enabled. Encoding remains visibly unconnected because no live conversion path reads its carrier. The earlier G71 bridge and documented real-hardware bench gaps remain open.

project.title: NESRecomp
project.display_title: NESRecomp — 6502-to-C static recompilation framework
project.notes: Translates NES/Famicom 6502 ROM code into C with a hardware runner. Beyond its FDS LLE/HLE support, the cycle backend now exposes opt-in game-mod packages with instruction-boundary hooks, isolated guest-routine calls, mod save-state records, presented-width control and game-owned frame rendering. Generated C alone is not a playable game, hooks are disabled by default, and unsupported BIOS/disk or renderer routes still fail closed.

project.status: active
project.notes: Clean-room, source-faithful engine for Dungeon Master, Chaos Strikes Back, Dungeon Master II, Dungeon Master Nexus and Theron's Quest. Dungeon Master 1 PC/DOS 3.4 is playable/source-locked; authenticated-media regressions verify bounded Atari ST, Amiga and FM Towns startup/menu-to-runtime handoffs without claiming complete campaign parity. CSB requires a nonzero source-rendered viewport hash after authenticated handoff, proving renderer execution rather than pixel/audio parity. DM2 Amiga reaches its initial real-GDAT M11 frame with zero core fallbacks while broader input, save, display/audio and dungeon parity remain open. Theron's current labeled suite passes 53/53 tests, but public status was corrected to keep original presentation, stair/exit, pickup/use, combat and chapter-completion consumers explicitly open. Captured controller input was observed only in the System Card poll loop, not the title/menu route. Nexus remains active real-data bring-up and full-suite parity is not claimed.

project.title: Fairlight II
project.display_title: Fairlight II — ZX Spectrum completion-bug reverse engineering
project.status: active
project.notes: Active investigation of the ZX Spectrum 48K Fairlight II completion bug. Current work maps the C0-FF room-bytecode opcode table, direct and lookup-based operand encodings, room-renderer flags and dynamic-object formats. The E1-E6 flag interpretation is explicitly attributed to ChatGPT in the analysis and remains documented as such rather than silently treated as established original intent.

project.title: ghidra-retro-machines
project.display_title: Ghidra Retro Machines — bank-aware loaders and retro CPU languages
project.notes: Ghidra extension configures banked memory maps, ROMs, hardware registers and symbols for C64/C128/PET PRG and NES iNES analysis, and bundles explicit SPC700 and 65C816 language variants for SNES code. The SPC700 language is decode-capable with p-code still under rewrite; the 65C816 language is disassembly-oriented while its p-code is verified against exhaustive vectors. Current NES work resolves proven constant-pointer indirect jumps and bounds table-after-code jump tables by their switch window; Mega Man and Life Force rows were re-blessed, while Contra, Final Fantasy and TMNT changes remain held for owner review. Its exhaustive 65C816 vector baseline now reports 500 PASS, 8 N/A and 4 FAIL rows after isolating one named SBC (dp,X) test-vector oracle defect. The exception is guarded by tripwires that fail if the case starts passing or disappears, so it cannot mask wider regressions. Build and real-ROM gates therefore demonstrate bounded progress rather than universal correctness claims.

project.status: active
project.notes: Clean-room, source-faithful engine for Dungeon Master, Chaos Strikes Back, Dungeon Master II, Dungeon Master Nexus and Theron's Quest. Dungeon Master 1 PC/DOS 3.4 is playable/source-locked; authenticated-media regressions verify bounded Atari ST, Amiga and FM Towns startup/menu-to-runtime handoffs without claiming complete campaign parity. CSB now requires a nonzero source-rendered viewport hash after authenticated Atari ST, Amiga and FM Towns menu handoff; this proves the viewport renderer ran, not pixel parity, native display or audible output. DM2 Amiga now reaches its initial real-GDAT M11 frame through the normal launcher with zero core fallbacks and source movement, while broader input, save, native display/audio and dungeon parity remain open. Current Theron evidence includes authenticated US and JP Track 02 boots with source-backed early runtime, scripted movement and bounded in-memory title-audio handling. Its registered Theron selection passes 71/71 tests on the documented authentic-media host, with eight optional media/capture tests skipped. Authentic regressions verify 93 approachable closed doors per region remain fail-closed and 71 Akutuba item transactions per region, including all six type-zero records, preserve exact source occurrence and property records. They do not prove original door, T900 pickup/UI, quest-item or complete campaign semantics. A fresh-start DM1 C37 save round-trip is verified, while authentic Atari v1.0 resume remains fail-closed pending an Atari-specific tail/champion/queue adapter. Nexus remains active real-data bring-up and full-suite parity is not claimed.

project.title: NESRecomp
project.display_title: NESRecomp — 6502-to-C static recompilation framework
project.notes: Translates NES/Famicom 6502 ROM code into C with a hardware runner. The cycle backend now supports Famicom Disk System images through LLE BIOS execution and an opt-in HLE tier for disk-ID requests, side changes and fast loading; synthetic-BIOS/multi-side tests and owner-ROM traces bound those claims. Generated C alone is not a playable game, and unsupported BIOS/disk routes may still fail closed.

events.title: Project metadata updated
events.message: notes: Translates NES ROM 6502 machine code into C and provides a PPU/APU/mapper runner; generated C alone is not a playable game. project.title: ghidra-retro-machines

project.notes: Ghidra extension configures banked memory maps, ROMs, hardware registers and symbols for C64/C128/PET PRG and NES iNES analysis. Current NES work resolves proven constant-pointer indirect jumps and bounds table-after-code jump tables by their switch window; Mega Man and Life Force rows were re-blessed, while Contra, Final Fantasy and TMNT changes remain held for owner review. Build/real-ROM gates therefore demonstrate bounded progress rather than universal mapper or analysis correctness.

project.status: active
project.notes: Clean-room, source-faithful engine for Dungeon Master, Chaos Strikes Back, Dungeon Master II, Dungeon Master Nexus and Theron's Quest. Dungeon Master 1 PC/DOS 3.4 is playable/source-locked; authenticated-media regressions verify bounded Atari ST, Amiga and FM Towns startup/menu-to-runtime handoffs without claiming complete campaign parity. CSB and DM2 retain bounded verified real-media routes. Current Theron evidence includes authenticated US and JP Track 02 boots with source-backed early runtime, scripted movement and bounded in-memory title-audio handling. Its registered Theron selection passes 71/71 tests on the documented authentic-media host, with eight optional media/capture tests skipped. Authentic regressions verify 93 approachable closed doors per region remain fail-closed and 71 Akutuba item transactions per region, including all six type-zero records, preserve exact source occurrence and property records. They do not prove original door, T900 pickup/UI, quest-item or complete campaign semantics. A fresh-start DM1 C37 save round-trip is verified, while authentic Atari v1.0 resume remains fail-closed pending an Atari-specific tail/champion/queue adapter. Nexus remains active real-data bring-up and full-suite parity is not claimed.

project.title: ZX Spectrum game disassemblies

project.notes: Independent reproducible disassemblies of six ZX Spectrum games. project.title: NESRecomp
project.display_title: NESRecomp — 6502-to-C static recompilation framework
project.notes: Translates NES ROM 6502 machine code into C and provides a PPU/APU/mapper runner; generated C alone is not a playable game. The opt-in cycle-accurate compiler/runtime uses bounded interpreter fallback and trace-parity verification. Its 27 September generated catalog reports 57 of 458 known mapper IDs supported, covering 6,682 of 10,632 known dumps; every supported mapper has contract/fixture checks, while title validation is explicitly bounded rather than exhaustive. README describes Windows x64 as mature, macOS as experimental and Linux as less tested; no minimum host CPU/RAM is stated.

project.title: STM32 USB Floppy Tracer
project.display_title: STM32 USB Floppy Tracer — Amiga/Atari physical disk imaging
project.notes: STM32F407 firmware plus Rust host CLI/GUI reads ADF and ST and writes ADF, IPF, ST and experimental patched STX. The firmware configuration explicitly selects Rust's thumbv7em-none-eabihf target for Cortex-M4F/M7F; the documented working board is STM32F407, so ARM is recorded as an output CPU without assigning CPUs to the disk-image inputs. Written tracks are verified; weak-bit and some STX protections remain experimental.

README describes Windows x64 as mature, macOS as experimental and Linux as not fully tested; no minimum host CPU/RAM is stated.

project.title: BeerMon v0.45 — reconstructed Amiga monitor

project.notes: Carnivore / BeerMacht / TRSI is credited for the historical BeerMon v0.45 monitor and debugger. Volker Schwaberow's reconstructed Moni.s explicitly selects mc68030, uses the 68020/68030 MSP/CACR/CAAR control-register path, and contains guarded 68040 and FPU probes. The source is therefore recorded at the explicitly documented m68k family level while m68030 records the reconstruction/output assembler mode, not a claimed minimum runnable Amiga. No original-binary comparison, successful build or runtime test is established.

project.status: in progress
techniques: shared Atari ST and Amiga regression testing
project.notes: The repository root builds an enhanced Atari ST version from the corrected historical source and a separate native Amiga port, sharing gameplay changes but keeping independent source trees. It also contains an independent preserved-original Atari ST build in src_orig, catalogued separately. The enhanced Atari output uses a TOS launcher and disk image; the Amiga version supplies native bitplanes, input, Paula audio and AmigaDOS handling. The documented Amiga baseline is PAL OCS/MC68000, Kickstart 1.3 and 512 KB Chip plus 512 KB expansion RAM; an explicit 68020-only variant is available. The original build is explicitly not byte-identical; do not infer byte identity for the enhanced versions. Real Amiga hardware remains unverified.

project.title: ZX Spectrum game disassemblies
project.display_title: ZX Spectrum game disassemblies — reproducible SkoolKit archaeology
project.status: active
project.notes: Independent reproducible disassemblies of six ZX Spectrum games: Atic Atac, Manic Miner, Fairlight, Knight Lore, The Hobbit and Ant Attack. Build scripts take user-supplied original media, generate commented/source-level-debuggable disassemblies and snapshots, and verify reassembly against the original bytes. Ant Attack is documented as 100% covered (41,984/41,984 bytes), with every routine named and every instruction but three observed to execute; its build reassembles byte-for-byte. The Hobbit also has an optional verified-source fast-draw patch whose 22 pictures are compared against the original run with whole-memory equality checks.

project.title: ZX Spectrum game disassemblies
project.display_title: ZX Spectrum game disassemblies — reproducible SkoolKit archaeology
project.status: active
project.notes: Independent reproducible disassemblies of five ZX Spectrum games. Build scripts take user-supplied original media, generate commented/source-level-debuggable disassemblies and snapshots, and verify reassembly against the original bytes. The Hobbit now also has an optional verified-source fast-draw patch: only plotting code is replaced, all 22 pictures are compared against the original run, and whole-memory equality is checked after each picture.

project.title: beebjit
project.display_title: beebjit — BBC Micro JIT emulator, debugger & preservation test bench
source_language: BBC Micro disk and tape images
project.notes: BBC Micro/Master emulator focused on very fast 6502 JIT execution while retaining enough hardware fidelity for original protected media. The README documents FSD/HFE handling, 8271/1770 emulation, deterministic capture/replay, experimental rewind and a built-in 6502 debugger, including preservation-oriented protected-media examples.

project.title: Disassemblies
project.display_title: Atari 2600 disassemblies — Dennis Debro exact-ROM reconstruction collection
project.notes: Large Atari 2600 reverse-engineering collection by Dennis Debro. The title READMEs identify the sources as analyzed, labeled and commented reverse-engineering projects and state that the code assembles into the exact game ROM. The tracker treats the collection as one record rather than fabricating separate activity histories for each title directory.

runtime_profiles.name: Atari ST / STE / Mega ST 68000 build
runtime_profiles.notes: The shipping ST/STE binary is compiled for a bare 68000 and is explicitly described as the safe run-on-anything Atari build; a stock non-e ST is verified.

evidence.excerpt: Atari ST / STE / Mega ST — openua-atari-st-*.zip, 2 MB, colour monitor; tested on TOS 2.06, EmuTOS and TOS 1.04.
A 68000 build runs on any Atari, and a stock non-e ST is verified too.

runtime_profiles.name: Atari Falcon030 / TT030
runtime_profiles.notes: One -m68020-60 binary serves both Falcon030 and TT030; the standard target machines documented here are 68030 systems.

evidence.excerpt: Atari Falcon030 / TT030 — openua-falcon-*.zip, 4 MB, TOS 4.04 (Falcon) or 3.0x (TT). One binary serves both.
The Macintosh 68k code is retargeted to machines including the target 68020/030 family; Falcon030 and TT030 are supported backends.

runtime_profiles.name: Accelerated Atari ST / STE 020+ build
runtime_profiles.os: No extra TOS floor documented; TOS 2.06 tested
runtime_profiles.notes: On an accelerated ST/STE the Falcon/TT -m68020-60 binary detects ST hardware and selects the native ST display backend. The documentation explicitly states an 020 or better is required for this variant.

evidence.excerpt: Run the Falcon/TT zip's binary; the Falcon/TT zip is -m68020-60. Requirements are just the accelerator: an 020 or better.

runtime_profiles.name: Amiga ECS/OCS
runtime_profiles.notes: Bare-68000 ECS/OCS build; Kickstart 1.3 will not launch it. The documentation describes 7 MHz as playable, with acceleration improving comfort.

evidence.excerpt: Amiga ECS/OCS (A500+ / A600 / A2000, bare 68000) — Kickstart 2.0 or later, 2 MB; playable at 7 MHz.

runtime_profiles.name: Amiga AGA / RTG
runtime_profiles.notes: One -m68020 Amiga binary serves AGA and Picasso96/CyberGraphX RTG, selecting the display path at runtime. The hardware guide describes memory as about 4 MB, so no exact minimum RAM value is asserted here.

evidence.excerpt: Amiga AGA (A1200 / A4000) and RTG — Kickstart 3.0+, about 4 MB; one frua serves AGA and Picasso96/CyberGraphX RTG.
The codebase is already GCC -std=gnu99 -m68020 C.

project.title: PCE Analyser
project.display_title: PCE Analyser — PC Engine/HuC6280 reverse-engineering toolkit
project.status: active
project.notes: Branch-resident PC Engine analyser in the 8-Bit Analysers repository. The PCE branch defines a PCEAnalyser executable for Windows, Linux and macOS and contains HuC6280-aware execution/code analysis, assembler-export validation, ROM/CD-ROM analysis, bank/memory mapping and graphics/VRAM inspection. It is tracked separately from the master-branch Spectrum/C64/CPC suite so branch activity can be attributed to the correct project.

CHANGE: A bug was found in the Unicard uc3 (Unicard3) firmware - in the binary directory listing it does not fill the long file name (LFN) field. In this point the emulator deliberately behaves CONTRARY to the accurate-emulation principle: it emulates uc3 the way we believe it should behave IF the bug were not there (i.e. filling the LFN correctly). For this reason, uc1 (which is faithful to the real HW) is now the default Unicard firmware for MZ-800.
